62545.en:
Writer: John Kastronis

Mission Objective: Destroy the Gallente ships; bring the informant back to your agent

Mission Briefing: As you well know, the Serpentis are notorious pirates across the galaxy. They are particularly troublesome here, pushing their drugs and committing all sorts of crimes against the Federation. Of course, they're not all bad all the time.

It just so happens that a Serpentis captain is ready to turn himself in. Of course, he can't just dock in one of our stations and surrender. He'll be dead before he exits warp. That wouldn't be a big deal, except this captain has information that can help bring down several higher-ranking Serpentis members.

We've agreed to send someone over there for a show, to fight and destroy his ship. At the last second, he'll eject so you can pick him up and bring him back safely. Are you up to it?

62546.en: An incompetent executive will be passing through a transfer station in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. In order to eliminate this problem for the company and keep it from hurting our stock price, you will need to intercept the executive and his security detail at the transfer station and eliminate the executive's ship. You may engage the security detail if you wish, but it is not strictly necessary.

62547.en: Kill the Amarrian traitor and her bodyguards

62548.en:
Writer: Sean Twist

Mission Objective: Investigate the distress beacon and rescue the lost miners

Mission Briefing: {[character]player.name}, we recently lost contact with a small group of industrial miners at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Outside of the miners' distress beacon being activated, we've heard nothing from them for two days. Just... silence.

Normally, we'd just write them off and hire new crews. But we spent a fortune on implants for those miners, and we're not ready to write those off. So would you please go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and see what's what?

Whatever the case, you'll need to bring those miners back here for examination and questioning.

62549.en:
Writer: Travis Heermann Mission Objective: Destroy Gallente ships; bring Admiral Queel back to agent Mission Briefing: This is a communiqué directly from the Intelligence division of the Ministry of War.

An admiral in the Gallente navy has seen the light of true faith and experienced a true religious conversion. He no longer believes in the never-ending Gallente quest for money and prestige. Having a high-ranking Gallente officer suddenly join our side could cause tremendous damage to their ability to wage war against us. The knowledge he holds regarding their systems and tactics would be staggering. But he needs a way into Amarrian space without being captured.

Retrieve Admiral Queel from the rendezvous point in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, near the edge of Gallente space. And be very, very careful. You should probably bring associates, because if the Gallente navy shows up, they will take no prisoners.

62550.en: Crooked cop allowing Amarrians to ship slaves through Gallente territory. Mission is being revised, so no more detail provided here as it is still up in the air.

62551.en:
Writer: Anthony Pryor Mission Objective: Destroy or drive off Mordu's Legion vessels Mission Briefing: Now that things are heating up between us and the Caldari again, Mordu's Legion is in the thick of things. They've been engaging in raids and reconnaisance, harassing merchant traffic and generally making a nuisance of themselves. In this sector, at least, they're doing just what the Caldari want them to – keeping our fleet elements tied down so those greedy bastards can martial their own forces in relative peace.

We might have an ace in the hole, however. We have good intelligence that many Intaki inside the Caldari State are growing impatient and restless, suffering discrimination and unemployment. Many blame the Caldari for their woes, and with the right incentive might even be persuaded to join their fellow Intaki here in the Federation. An incident involving the State-sanctioned Mordu's Legion may be just enough to tip the scales.

We've been monitoring subspace chatter, and we think that the Legion may be planning on hitting one of our bases in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We're planning on spreading the story that the base is full of Intaki refugees, but it would be best if some heroic pilot caught the Mordus in the act and drove them off before the base was completely destroyed.

What we'd like you to do is get your ship over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take up position near the station. When the Legion ships arrive, destroy them or drive them off. We'll be monitoring things and will have definite evidence of the attack. Bring back the evidence and you'll be well rewarded.

So, what do you say? The Legion may be coming in strength, so you might want to bring some friends along.

62552.en:
Dungeon Description

1. The room contains several large asteroids and half-finished mining facilities. The miners are going about their business, and continue to do so, unless they are attacked.

2. When the first mining ship takes damage, the rest of the miners attack. An automated defense platform becomes active and begins to fire upon the character.

3. One of the miners drops a big portion of ore when the ship is destroyed. This ore must be returned to the agent.

Completion

Destroy all enemy ships; bring their cargo back to your agent (drop on completion).

62553.en: I've been asked to help the Customs Authority apprehend a group of smugglers trying to get some military-grade sensor components out of the State where they can sell them to the highest bidder. They've sent us a list of possible targets and we've been tracking them; one of the suspect vessels has just entered our jurisdiction. I'd like you to intercept this ship; once you're there, we'll let you know if that's the one we're looking for. If it is, you'll need to disable the vessel, apprehend the crew, and confiscate the sensor components, which are being carried in small secure containers. Can you handle that for me?

62554.en: Eliminate the Blood Raider smugglers and recover their slave cargo.

62556.en:
Mission Objective: Destroy all enemy ships; rescue the miners

What I had in mind for the dungeon was a small transfer station, made up of a few LCOs like a control tower, a cargo platform, a station hangar, and maybe a docked Badger at the center of the area. When the player first arrives, that's all there is. 

1. When player warps into first room, a significant force of Gallente privateers blocks the way to the acceleration gate. They attack after the following chat text appears: "So, they've finally sent someone to investigate. Too bad for you. You should have brought more ships." 

2. When the player warps into the second room, the mining colony is a large facility with several intact and damaged structures, choked with asteroids and Amarrian wrecks (the destroyed escort ships). As the player warps in, the Gallente privateer leader says in chat, "How did you get through our advance picket? Bah! No matter! We'll add your salvage to our stockpile. We're going to make a killing." 

3. The surviving miners can be found in the Habitat. However, the chat message comes up when the last privateer is destroyed: "We sealed ourselves inside the habitat to keep those bastards from looting us, but now we're stuck in here. You'll have to blow the place apart to get us out!" (Thus they can drop on completion.)

62557.en:
Level 2 Basic Encounter

Writer: John Kastronis

Mission Objective: Investigate the asteroid belt; kill any enemies

Mission Briefing: Some of our explorers have just located a hidden asteroid belt that is apparently full of rare ore — here in local space. That's more than a little suspicious. The signature the belt is giving off is also so obvious that it seems nearly impossible it hasn't been found and mined out before now. We're afraid it might be a trap of some sort. We want you to warp over there, check it out, then come back with a report.

62558.en:
Ah, politics. I never get tired of them. Oh, wait. No. I hate politics.

But without politics, our great democratic and free society would collapse. It's the nature of the beast, I'm afraid. And, well, the Federation has numerous laws to prevent politicians from being abusive with their politicking. A local political office is up for grabs after the incumbent died of a heart attack after a night at a pleasure hub. The Vice Commissioner of Waste Management for the County Council or something unimportant like that.

Normally, we wouldn't even bother with something this trivial. Those silly planetside dirthuggers and their governments aren't much to look at. But one of them had to go and break some laws and now it's our job to clean it up. You see, someone has hijacked some broadcast waves and is sending out a 24/7 message denouncing one of the candidates. And because it's a space-based satellite doing the broadcasting, we're the ones that have to deal with it.

Now, we don't know who it is that's making the broadcasts, and frankly, I don't care. As long as they're stopped, I'm happy with it. We've pinned down the offending satellite, so I want you to fly over there and blow it up. There might be some automated defenses, but it's some mud dweller's, so they can't be that great.

mission text: Jack Holt
developer: Orrin Loria

62565.en:
The Cartel has a pretty good thing going in Curse – we're able to strike into the heart of all the other empires and remain relatively safe from retaliation. Now that the conflict between the Amarr Empire and the Republic is heating up, we're getting pressure from both sides. The Minmatar have been pushing hard in some places, and now we've decided that it's time to push back.

We've been working with representatives of the Khanid Kingdom to give the Minmatar a surprise. The Republic has been building up forces in (system); in exchange for some generous financial compensation we've agreed to help the Khanids push the Minmatar out. We need a pilot to fly out there to keep the light Minmatar escorts busy while we help the Khanids destroy the larger vessels. We've loaded the location into your Neocom. We'd like you to fly there and destroy any Republic vessels you encounter.

62566.en:
What Agent says to offer this mission: As a matter of fact, I do. As I'm sure you're aware, even in times of conflict with an external enemy we still find ourselves in competition with other “friendly” corporations. One such corporation is providing security for a repair outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They got that security contract by underbidding us. I want you to head out there, destroy their entire security force, then destroy the repair outpost. With such an abyssmal failure on their record, they'll never get another security contract in this sector again.

And who knows, maybe we'll get the reconstruction contract for the replacement outpost as well.

So what do you say? Do you think you can handle this job? I can make it worth your while.

62567.en:
In the heinous world of spaceship piracy, only the worst — or best, depending on your outlook — rise to the top and stay there. The Angel Cartel is among the very few pirate organizations that can claim this dubious honor. 

The Cartel is the most widespread criminal organization blackening the space lanes. There are many reasons for this, chief among them being that the Angels fully embrace the sound business policy of diversity. Outside of common piracy, the Angels have their fingers in most illegal pies, be they protection rackets, industrial blackmail, or murder for hire. There are also rumors the Cartel is involved in even more despicable operations — yet attempts to investigate these claims have only produced numerous law enforcement corpses. 

Most spacers know that to cross the Cartel is tantamount to suicide. Without mercy, without compassion, and allegedly armed with long-lost Jovian technology, the Cartel is best avoided by those with a fondness for breathing. 

But sometimes even pirates can go too far....

62568.en:
What Agent says to offer this mission: A hefty reward, if you're successful.

For a some time now there have been rumors of Caldari citizens who are unhappy with the way the State is run. Some of them are no doubt Gallente sympathizers, and we're certain the Gallente are giving them aid through third-parties. Either way, they're traitors to the State, and we must be vigilant to keep them from disrupting our operations.

In recent days, we believe one of our repair and resupply depots has been under surveillance by suspected members of one of these traitor groups, and we think they're going to attempt some kind of sabotage. We could quadruple our security, but that might tip them off. Instead, I want you to go there and keep an eye out for them. If you see anything suspicious, you are authorized to destroy the vessel in question immediately. We don't want to take any chances.

Once you've destroyed the transport, recover any cargo and bring it to me. We might be able to use it as evidence of Gallente involvement.

62569.en: Mission completion triggers when you are within 2500m of Cartographer's Quarters.

62570.en:
From the author: Mission Objective: Destroy the Caldari monument. Mission Offer: There is a monument where a battle in the Gallente-Caldari war occurred within Gallente space. We once tolerated pilgrimaging Caldari, but with this war we cannot allow the Caldari any excuse to proceed this deep within our space. Such leniency would only invite terrorism. I need you to destroy the monument, and any witnesses to the event. We will release a statement that the site was attacked by pirates. The Caldari won't believe this, of course, but it will provide us with plausible deniability.

Undoubtedly there will be an uproar about this. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} will disavow any involvement. You will be best served by remaining silent yourself.

62600.en:
Mission Objective: Pick up the damaged tools from the mining colony

Mission Briefing: A Mannar mining colony has recently been attacked by rogue drones. Unfortunately, this mining colony supplies us with a good deal of cheap minerals we use for our defense initiatives. We can't wait for them to repair the damage done by the drones, so we've decided to fix their equipment for them, free of charge. The sooner we can get them back to work, the better.

All you need to do is pick up the parts from their mining colony and bring them back here. Good luck!

62605.en:
The Angel Cartel has established a firm presence in this deadspace complex. While they use it as a naval construction base, reports claim that they perform some testing of shield prototypes deep inside. These rumors remain largely unconfirmed. The area is extremely dangerous and the inner pockets are off limits to everyone but the key players in the Angel Cartel.

DED Threat Assessment: Critical (10 of 10)

62606.en:
The Centus Assembly T.P. Co. deadspace complex is run by Sansha's True Power corporation. Mineral storage facilities and naval shipyards are hidden behind powerful defenses in the outer pockets.

Commander Chelm Soran is responsible for security in the Assembly, although he is rarely present himself.

DED Threat Assessment Level: 10 of 10

62607.en:
This deadspace complex is the fleet shipyard headquarters of the Serpentis Corporation. It is defended by a massive battle fleet, manufactured by the corporation and assisted by elite mercenaries trained by the Angel Cartel.

DED Threat Assessment: Critical (10 of 10)

62608.en:
This deadspace complex contains a heavily guarded prison facility of the Angel Cartel. It is here that kidnapped enemies of the Cartel are held for ransom or brutal interrogation and torture.

DED Threat Assessment: Perilous (8 of 10)

62609.en:
The Pith's Penal Complexes are run by an Amarr captain called Dewak Humfry, commonly referred to by his previous prisoners as "Dewak the Insane" or "Dewak the Screaming." He is a fiercely disciplined tactician. After a prolonged stint of service in Imperial Navy forces, he decided to go into business in the private sector.

Threat Assessment Level: 8 of 10

62610.en:
This military complex belongs to the Angel Cartel. The Cartel sent a crew of their finest engineers and military personnel here to establish a mining complex. Unconfirmed DED reports state that the Angel Cartel plans to use this complex to develop new weapons and practice combat maneuvers and strategies away from prying eyes.

DED Threat Assessment: Major (7 of 10)

62611.en:
According to reliable sources within the Imperial Navy, this deadspace complex is currently occupied by a large contingent of Crimson Hand cultists. Intelligence indicates that the Crimson Hand, a militant splinter group of the Blood Raider Covenant, is currently engaged in a massive military buildup. While their continued alliance with Omir Sarikusa is in question, they do seem to be planning something big.

DED Threat Assessment: Serious (6 of 10)

62612.en:
Sansha's War Supply Complex was built as a direct countermeasure to CONCORD's increased emphasis on curbing the influence of Sansha's Nation. The compound contains a lot of basic armaments and supplies. It is sturdy and well defended.
DED Threat Assessment Level: 6 of 10

62613.en: This is an A-Class repair and resupply post, operated by the Serpentis. Not only is it important to their operations, it has also been rumored to be one of many hideouts utilized by their resistance movement. They are supposedly planning a revolt against the vicious oppression of the shadowy ruling body, the Furies, and will defend themselves and their compatriots with vicious fervor if attacked.

62614.en:
This is a den for those who value instant worldly pleasure above all other things. It is a popular stopover for overworked Angel pirates and members of secret guilds or groups.

DED Threat Assessment: Dangerous (5 of 10)

62615.en:
This deadspace complex once held a great naval installation, but after a strain of rogue drones attacked and seized the complex, little remains from any human inhabitation. The sector has now been taken over for an outgrowth hive of the strain, though it is not developed enough to count as a true mother hive.

DED Threat Assessment: Dangerous (5 of 10)

62616.en:
This small outpost acts as a monitoring and coordination hub for the Sansha forces in the area as well as a comms relay between neighboring battle towers.

DED Threat Assessment: Unsafe (3 of 10)

62617.en:
This deadspace complex was built by the Serpentis Corporation to protect and store narcotic and military supplies for their members. The complex also acts as a temporary storage area for the corporation's traffic of illicit substances. While the entrance check-in sectors of the complex are not known to be heavily guarded, certain sections house experienced security staff who use top-of-the-line equipment funded by the Serpentis Corporation's income from illegal activity.

DED Threat Assessment: Unsafe (3 of 10)

62618.en:
This deadspace field appears to have been infested with a strain of rogue drones. Rogue drones are a self-replicating "life form" controlled by artificial intelligence, often in the form of a lucid communication hive mind or centered inside one of their dreaded rogue drone mothers. This particular complex is the construction site of a new hive, far away from its maternal headquarters.

DED Threat Assessment: Minor (2 of 10)

62619.en:
"Old Meanie" is a mining relic in the possession of the Amarr Empire. Previously it was a small mining outpost, but was raided so frequently by Serpentis pirates that it was abandoned. Today it contains some experimental biodomes, and further inside the complex Amarrians are creating a spiritual center. Security has been contracted to renegade Blood Raider pirates.

DED Threat Assessment: Training (1 of 10)

62620.en:
This deadspace complex is under the control of the drug-dealing Serpentis Corporation. This particular branch is a drug dealing outlet, containing narcotic supermarkets and local storages for illicit substances.

DED Threat Assessment: Training (1 of 10)

62621.en:
The Mul-Zatah Monastic order has for a long time maintained close links with Omir Sarikusa and the Blood Raider Covenant. The order is considered by most law enforcement agents to pose a limited threat to security since they seem to keep to themselves for the most part. They are however notoriously intolerant of trespassers near their Monasteries and it is not advisable to approach lightly armed.

DED Threat Assessment: Risky (4 of 10)

62622.en:
The Mul-Zatah Monastic order has for a long time maintained close links with Omir Sarikusa and the Blood Raider Covenant. The order is considered by most law enforcement agents to pose a limited threat to security since they seem to keep to themselves for the most part. They are however notoriously intolerant of trespassers near their Monasteries and it is not advisable to approach lightly armed.

62704.en:
You are currently able to change your attributes without delay using a bonus remap. This perk is only available a limited number of times.

After your bonus remaps are exhausted, you will not be able to change your attributes again until the remap timer has elapsed.

62706.en:
These agents will introduce you to their respective careers, guiding you into one of the many paths to glory in New Eden and equipping you, as you progress, to face the rigors of your chosen profession.
You may visit and learn from any or all of these agents at any time.

62712.en: The specified application text is too long ({[numeric]length} characters). The text can be a maximum of 1000 characters long.
