129464.en:
I'll explain the situation. Some time ago, I was taking one of my weekly vacations in my resort here when we were attacked by Blood Raiders. It was during the early morning, before most of my staff arrives for work. I was quite incredulous at the time, after all I have the entire Kador fleet at my disposal. But when I ordered my security personnel to send a distress call, they noticed that all of our communications systems had been tampered with, even the backup! Someone had been going through an extreme effort to cripple us. Even the warp drives of our ships had been disabled, preventing us from leaving that way as well. This sort of operation would require extensive knowledge of our security system, which is quite disturbing.

To cut the story short, our security forces have been fighting for their lives for the past few days. Only due to the exemplary bravery of my security personnel am I still alive. The Blood Raiders have cornered us here in the last pocket of my complex, and we're slowly running out of supplies. Our ships may be bigger, but the Blood Raiders just keep on coming, and for some reason not a single squadron of Kador ships has arrived to aid us.

If you could lend us a hand, I would be eternally grateful. I realize that I could leave this area with you on your ship, but I would only do such a thing as a last resort. I want control over my Mansion back, and the scoundrels who dared attack it destroyed! Every last one of them! I'll be the laughing stock of the Kador family if I flee from such low-life criminals with my tail behind my legs. Please do this for me, {[character]player.name}, I dare not risk any more of my own men.

129468.en: <font color =FFCC11>Start with destroying the weaker Blood Raider ships, and bring 10 of their tags to Lord Manel.</font>

129469.en: Now it's time to take care of their cruisers and higher-echelon frigates.  That should severely cripple them and pave the way for you to take out their leaders.  Get me 5 of their tags and I'll consider the job done.

129471.en: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}.  Now there's just the leaders left to take care of.

129472.en: The targets have been destroyed, as you requested, Lord Manel.

129473.en: Now the only assignment left for you to complete is taking out their leaders.  Instead of just getting their insignias, I want their heads on a platter.  This will serve as a reminder to all pirates that I am not a man to be trifled with.  Once I have two of their heads, I will relieve you of your duties.  I will also give you a message which you might want to bring to Odan Poun, if he has become concerned with my well being.  In it I will recommend that he give you a reward for a job well done.  But you won't get anything until I have those heads!

129476.en: You can take these severed disgusting heads now, Governor.

129479.en: Yes, I have some work.  But it's pretty risky, and involves fighting some pretty nasty mercenaries.  If you think it's over your head, then back out now.

129480.en: Don't worry, I'm up for it.

129481.en:
Well then, to your first assignment. One of the major guilds of Maphante, Giraka, has been a thorn in my side for quite some time. I made a deal with them a few years back which entailed that I had full rights on importing a certain commodity into Garisas. But because of my political feud with Lord Methros and Arachnan, who by the way think they have some kind of authority here when in fact Lord Manel occupies the Governor's seat, I've lost a great deal of power over the local guilds. So Giraka have decided to abandon their business relationship with me and have turned to Lord Methros instead. This of course is unacceptable, Garisas is mine and I won't have that sniveling fool Methros poking his nose where it doesn't belong.

I want to teach Giraka a lesson. That will also send a message to the rest of the guilds that I'm not to be trifled with. But I'm afraid that my own forces are simply not adequate to take on Giraka, and I'd rather not get Lord Manel involved in this dispute. He has enough on his mind already, what with Methros and Arachnan fighting over Araz as if it were their own.

Your first task is to assault a supply station that Giraka owns, in Garisas. They are expecting a shipment of this commodity I told you about, and I want their transport vessels destroyed. The only problem is that the convoy carrying the goods has an escort, and the supply station has a sizable security force as well. So I would suggest that you take care of the guards at the supply station before the convoy arrives. I estimate that the convoy will arrive soon, so I suggest you hurry and take care of those guards right now. Then wait for the convoy to show up and finish your business there. Report to me when your task has been accomplish.

129483.en: Not bad, not bad.  I didn't expect you to make it out of there alive, {[character]player.name}, much less complete the assignment.  But you proved me wrong.

129484.en:
After your last mission, you should have realized by now what I meant by 'the commodity' which me and Giraka have been disputing over. With the convoy destroyed, this gives me an excellent opportunity to get an edge over Giraka on the black market.

The client that was expecting the shipment of drugs by Giraka has in fact come to me to get his fix. He now wants 5 units of crash, which I have managed to acquire in Chanoun. The problem is delivering the crash here, those customs officials at the gate can be quite nasty when it comes to drug transports. I would suggest that you use a fairly cheap ship to get the job done, just incase the gate officials get trigger happy.

Make it here on time and you'll even get a bonus.

129487.en: I have the crash as you requested, {[character]agentID.name}.

129488.en: Apparently Giraka's council have become furious at the destruction of the Blood Raider convoy that they were expecting.  They know I was behind it, which leads me to believe we have a traitor in our midst.  But two can play that game, heh heh.  I have my own insiders in Giraka's compounds in Port Maphante, and they inform me that Giraka are planning a strike against my astrofarm plantation in retaliation for the drug convoy incident.  I expect their strike force to be split into waves, which is their general tactic.  But this gives you an excellent opportunity to prevent them from ganging up on you.  Destroy the first waves fast enough and you should have no problems.  But be wary of the mercenary overlord, he's no small fish to fry.

129490.en: Great work, {[character]player.name}, workers at the astro farm inform me that there were no casualties and the structures are still intact.

129491.en:
With the increasing hostilities between Garika and myself I've had to increase the number of personnel in my security forces considerably. It's costing me a fortune by the way. The problem is we are running kind of low on arms for the ground forces, because it so happens that the merchant guilds control most of the small arms trade here in Garisas and Garika has made it very hard for me to find a willing supplier.

But that got me thinking, why settle for standard small arms when I can have something much more effective? Something that will give my ground troops an edge if my enemies here decide to strike at my quarters within Maphante. It so happens that I know exactly where to find such high-tech weaponry. An agent of the Blood Raiders, which I have had extensive dealings with, informed me of a stash of elite laser-pistols which is hidden somewhere in the Mire Keep complex in Garisas, probably within the Grey Barracks. It's being guarded by powerful Blood Raider ships, and will be quite difficult to approach. Bring a few units of those pistols to me and I will reward you generously.

Since you've been so helpful to me I'll let you have something that will earn you plenty of favor points with the Governor of Araz. Well, as long as he's still alive anyway. One of my agents working inside the Governor's Audience Chamber in Chanoun overheard a conversation between Nossa Farad and some other individual. He took the liberty of recording this conversation. It should offer evidence enough that Nossa Farad is planning an assassination attempt against Lord Manel.

I haven't been able to locate Manel, but if you can then give him this message. It will explain everything.

129494.en: I have the elite laser pistols that you requested.  Here you go.

129495.en: I have this message from Bartezo Maphante ...

129496.en:
I hear you may be offering a message from Bartezo Maphante...

[Do not accept this mission if you have not already spoken with Bartezo Maphante, in Port Maphante in Garisas.]

129497.en: One minute, let me find it in my cargo hold... [Do not accept this mission if you have not spoken with Bartezo Maphante in Garisas already.]

129500.en: Bring Bartezo's message to Lord Manel.  Bartezo is located in Port Maphante in Garisas.

129501.en:
Incredible! I knew Nossa disliked me, but I never thought she'd go this far. The only reason I haven't sacked her is due to the political ramifications, since she is closely related to Moranour Kom. With this evidence, I will be able to take care of Nossa Farad for good. She will lose her position in the Kador family, get thrown in jail, and possibly even be made a slave. Delightful, no?!!

I'm very grateful for your help, {[character]player.name}, and I hope you can make good use of your reward. Take care.

129502.en: Message? I don't know what you're talking about.

129503.en: Well, then, quit wasting my time.

129504.en: Lai Dai Corporation has requested a batch of data sheets for their researchers on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Deliver them on time and you'll be rewarded with a bonus.

129505.en:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. You can continue working for various corporations in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} as long as you like. I suggest finding an agent that has a more variety of tasks available, simply search the stations that are owned by a corporation within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} and you are bound to find an agent to your liking. You can also search for agents which will speak to you by checking the database information for the corporation of your choice. To do that simply open the People and Places menu through your NeoCom and search for the corporation name. Right click on it and choose 'show info'. There you should find a list of all of its agents that are available. Their division should give you a hint as to what type of mission they are associated with.

Take care!

129513.en: We have a trade agreement with the Caldari Navy, where they request a large amount of robotics each day from our factory here in Airkio to supply their assembly plant in Maurasi.  If you would be so kind, you could make a delivery of robotics for us in exchange for {[numeric]rewardQuantity} ISK as well as a bonus if you're fast. 129516.en: We just finished producing a batch of antibiotics that I want you to deliver to the Caldari Navy station in Maurasi.  Do this quickly enough and I'll even reward you with a bonus.

129517.en: Thanks for the help, {[character]player.name}. Before you run off, though, I suggest you speak with Jeka Vantoh at the Chief Executive Panel Bureau in New Caldari. Apparently she's looking for a hand with something. Until next time!

129518.en: Kaalakiota Corporation has promised us some construction blocks for the extension we're building to the CEP station here in New Caldari. I've been on the lookout for people willing to make the deliveries for us, and you seem to fit the profile. If you're faster than the last guy who made the run, I'll even give you a bonus. Deal?

129519.en: Kaalakiota Corporation has promised us some construction blocks for the extension we're building to the CEP station here in New Caldari. I've been on the lookout for people willing to make the deliveries for us, and you seem to fit the profile. If you're faster than the last guy who made the run, I'll even give you a bonus. Deal?

129520.en: Now that that's taken care of, there's something else I'd like you to do for me. Just give me a minute here, would you?

129521.en: Kaalakiota requires a progress report on our work here every now and then. I think you're the right man for this job as well. And remember, if you're fast, then you get a bonus.

129522.en: Good work. By the way, could you pay Onmi Mara a visit? I believe she's looking for a freelancer like yourself to do a quick courier job. Right, good day.

129523.en: A couple of our personnel here in Nonni require a lift.  They need to be at {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} for a meeting at the Mercantile Club.  Please, don't be late!

129524.en: Talk to Yrmek Penola at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} if you haven't already.  I think he's in need of a hand.

129525.en: Hey, you're an Amarr aren't you?  What brings you to these parts.

129526.en:
So? Are you perhaps offended by the fact that I'm not Caldari? We are allies you know, no need to be rude. I'm just working here as a contractor for Mercantile Club.

Anyway, I need some tobacco transported to {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}. Some State And Region Bank executives requested them, and they made a point in requesting them delivered ASAP. So hurry up with your answer, will you. Yes or no?

129528.en: Sorry, but I don't like Amarrians.

129529.en: What!?  How dare you ...  I'll ... I'll ... I'll demand your CEO send me an apology!  Yes that's what I'll do.  You better get ready for a demotion, because he won't like what I've got to say about you ...

129530.en: Bring some tobacco to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, the State And Region Bank employees will pick up the shipment from your hangar there once it has been delivered.

129531.en: Good job, {[character]player.name}.  Now I suggest you speak with my colleague, Irsen Alaja, at the Mercantile Club Bureau in Kaimon.  He has more work for you.

129532.en: I'd like you to move a few tourists to {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  They are stopping by the entertainment facility at the Nugoeihuvi Development Studio.  It's quite popular with the locals, and we're always open to cheaper labor than the horribly expensive standard transportation services here.

129533.en: Thanks for the help, {[character]player.name}.  I suggest you speak with Enanato Imeri at {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, she's been looking for someone with your enthusiasm to work for the State.

129534.en: I'd like you to move a stack of holoreels to our publisher in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  Take care not to lose the cargo, the holoreels contain thousands of hours' worth of video data!

129535.en: I know that a colleague of mine, Hann Najus, is looking for work, so I suggest you pay him a visit in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.

129536.en: I have a job for you, {[character]player.name}.  Demand for silicon is getting out of hand, and our convoys can't keep up.  Could you help them out by transporting this batch of silicon to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}?  It would be much appreciated.

129537.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}.  I know Samora Miven, at the station you transported the silicon to, has some work to offer, you might want to pay her office a visit.

129538.en: The Caldari Navy has requested more ammo, and we're looking for someone to make the run for us.  Take this batch of hybrid-charges to the Navy assembly station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} and I'll give you a reward.

129539.en:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. You can continue working for various corporations in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} as long as you like. I suggest finding an agent that has a more variety of tasks available, simply search the stations that are owned by a corporation within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} and you are bound to find an agent to your liking. You can also search for agents which will speak to you by checking the database information for the corporation of your choice. To do that simply open the People and Places menu through your NeoCom and search for the corporation name. Right click on it and choose 'show info'. There you should find a list of all of its agents that are available. Their division should give you a hint as to what type of mission they are associated with.

Take care!

129540.en:
Although you managed to prevent more Eggs from falling into the hands of the Blood Raiders, we currently do not have enough supplies to cope with the royal household's demands. Therefore i need you to collect me some more. 

I have already located a sufficiant supply from a neighbouring constellation. 

Be quick we do not have much time before the Emperor's Household runs out of their most valued delight.

129541.en: I would be honoured to carry out such a vital task for the Empire.

129542.en: I am far to busy to haul junk food to those lazy royals.

129543.en: I have delivered the vital shipment of Eggs to ensure a constant supply for the Emperor and his family.

129544.en: I can't be bothered anymore, these eggs are really starting to smell out my ship.

129545.en: Your assistance is greatly appreciated in serving the Emperor and his family.

129546.en: Your services are duly noted and appreciated. Take pride in knowing that you have carried out an important duty to the Empire.

129547.en: I have a mission of great importance to the Empire, can you assist me?

129548.en:
Your services are duly noted and appreciated. Take pride in knowing that you have carried out an important duty to the Empire. 

Don't go anywhere i have another important mission that i need you to assist me with.

129549.en: I am ashamed to know you. You may very well have damaged the constant supply line of Yorak Eggs to the royal family. For that i can never forgive you.

129550.en: I am ashamed to know you. You may very well have damaged the constant supply line of Yorak Eggs to the royal family. For that i can never forgive you.

129551.en:
I am ashamed to know you. You may very well have damaged the constant supply line of Yorak Eggs to the royal family. For that I can never forgive you.

P.S Those Eggs will have already started to go bad. If you still have them on you I suggest you don't open them as you may not recover from the exposure to the toxins they produce (although that might not be a bad thing).

129552.en: I cannot wait anymore on you. I have lost faith in you, you are no longer as reliable as i once believed.

129553.en: You took to long to deliver the Eggs, the supply line to the royal family has been disturbed. My head may very well be on the line.

129554.en: I would be honoured to carry out such a vital task for the Empire.

129555.en: Your assistance is greatly appreciated in serving the Emperor and his family.

129556.en:
What an outrage!

The Emperor's House requires the finest delicacies from around the region to be delivered to its local office for the royal lineage to feast upon. As their humble servents we are tasked with the timely delivery of Nidupadian Yorak Eggs from this system.

Those blasted Blood Raiders have attacked our main processing plant in this system, we believe that there are still some Blood Raider pirates in the vacinity of the plant lead by a skilled mercenary called 'Keron Vandafelt' who is looking for left over Eggs and killing incomming vessels unaware of the recent attack.

These pirates must be eliminated once and for all. I am sending you the co-ordinates to the attack site now. I want Keron's head on my desk before the end of the day!

129558.en: Your services are duly noted and appreciated. Take pride in knowing that you have carried out an important duty to the Empire. Don't go anywhere i have another important mission that i need you to assist me with.

129559.en: I am far to busy to haul junk food to those lazy royals.

129560.en: I am ashamed to know you. You may very well have damaged the constant supply line of Yorak Eggs to the royal family. For that i can never forgive you.

129561.en: I can' no longer wait for your decision. I have lost faith in you, you are no longer as reliable as i once believed.

129562.en: I can't be bothered anymore, these eggs are really starting to smell out my ship.

129563.en: Those royals can go without those pesky eggs, i've had enough.

129564.en: Gah! those blasted pirates are still running rampant throughout the complex. There is no way we can re-establish supplies before the royal family runs out of Yorak Eggs.

129565.en: You Failed Me. For that i cannot forgive.

129566.en:
What an outrage!

The Emperor's House requires the finest delicacies from around the region to be delivered to its local office for the royal lineage to feast upon. As their humble servents we are tasked with the timely delivery of Nidupadian Yorak Eggs from this system.

Those blasted Blood Raiders have attacked our main processing plant in this system, we believe that there are still some Blood Raider pirates in the vacinity of the plant lead by a skilled mercenary called 'Keron Vandafelt' who is looking for left over Eggs and killing incomming vessels unaware of the recent attack.

These pirates must be eliminated once and for all. I am sending you the co-ordinates to the attack site now. I want Keron's head on my desk before the end of the day!

129573.en: Our generals in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} have requested an enormous amount of ground troops in preparation for a possible encounter with the Caldari Navy.  They're basically bolstering the front lines in case of an attack, and Unel seems to be one of the weak points in our defensive perimeter.  Would you be so kind as to transport some of these troops to their destination?  You'll be rewarded of course.

129574.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}.  I suggest you speak with Ansa Vanonari, she's an agent of Chemal Tech which might have some work for you.

129575.en: {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} has requested another batch of silicon, to be used in the manufacturing process at their factory.  If you would deliver this shipment to them, I would be very grateful.

129576.en: You've certainly earned your reward, {[character]player.name}.  Now I suggest you speak with Ihanani Oksen, she might have something to offer you that's worth your time.

129578.en:
With political relations between the Ammatar and the Minmatar Republic quickly deteriorating, things look dire for our citizens across the border. There are thousands of Nefantar inhabitants stuck in the Tartatven constellation, some who are working there on official business, others who simply settled there years ago. The Republic government refuses to let the majority of them leave their sovereign space and, in fact, has many under constant surveillance.

We fear that their lives may be at risk should the Ammatar declare war on the Republic and invade Audesder. There's already a huge buildup of military forces here in Kenobanala, and many fear that war is inevitable. So it's my task to ensure the safe return of as many Nefantar to Ammatar space as possible.

What I need you to do is deliver a group of Nefantar refugees from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} to Fort Kumar. I will then relocate them to one of our settlements in Joas.

May God light your path.

129580.en: You have done well, {[character]player.name}. But our task is not finished. There are still thousands of Nefantars that need to be moved. If you have more time on your hands, I'd like you to make a few more runs to Aedald for me.

129581.en: Duvolle Laboratories is building an extension to its research laboratory in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, and purchased a crap-load of construction blocks from our warehouse. If you would be so kind, can you transport some of these blocks to the station? You'll find all the details you need in the mission details in your Opportunities interface.

129582.en: Nice work.  I suggest you speak with Ossa Blaus at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; she wants your help with something, I think.

129583.en: The Quafe Corporation Factory in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} is in constant need of more hydrogen batteries, which they use for some of their reactors.  If you're up for it, then I'd like you to transfer some of the batteries to them before our deadline runs out.  Be on time!

129584.en: Well done.  I heard Lorchaert Brounave in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} has something to offer you, so stop by his office will you?

129585.en: Federal Administration has requested another shipment of Quafe Ultra to their Information Center in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  We're always on the lookout for cheap labor to get these transportation jobs done, so if you have time could you take care of this {[character]player.name}?

129586.en: I believe Ley Serene was looking for you at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} ...

129587.en:
I assume the smell of battle drew you here to Araz. This constellation may be a backwater of the Empire, yet interesting things are taking place here. I will not try to deceive you, so let me come clean right from the start. I'm here as a supporter of Lord Methros. Not as an official of Imperial Armaments, but as more of a personal friend; though Lord Methros has been a cherished customer of Imperial Armaments for years.

I do not know how much you know about the situation here in Araz, or what you think you know. Things are a bit complicated here at the moment, and the rumor mill is spinning like crazy. I'd advise you to take any information you get with a grain of salt. The hottest topic is the presence of the Blood Raiders in the constellation, or more precisely, why are they here and what are they up to? Idle tongues have spewed forth the rumor that Lord Methros invited the Raiders here, but heed not the black lies of these mouths. Lord Methros is just as anxious to rid Araz of the Blood Raider plague as everyone else. He even asked me personally to aid him in the matter.

Which finally allows me to answer your question regarding whether I have a job for you. Indeed I do. The Blood Raiders have taken over the ancient imperial fortresses that litter the night sky here in Araz. One of these fortresses lies close by, in the system of Koona. Travel there and enter the forsaken ruins. A group of Blood Raider cultists resides somewhere in there, taking blood from innocent travelers. We must put a stop to this vile practice. Locate the cultists in the fortress and retrieve the blood fund they've accumulated. Return with it to me, and we'll be one step closer to purging Araz of the Raiders' foul presence.

Be warned, though: The fortress can not be entered in anything larger than a cruiser-class ship.

129589.en: Well done. I will return the blood fund to the rightful authorities. Meanwhile, I have another assignment lined up for you.

129590.en: Killing cultists is my second-favorite pastime. I like it so much that I'd be willing to do it for free, if my all-time favorite pastime wasn't spending money. And lots of it.

129591.en:
I'm still trying to find out what the Blood Raiders are up to here in Araz. All I can say with certainty is that they're putting in a lot of effort into causing havoc here, presumably to further their own gains. Their agenda may be as simple as taking over the constellation. Simple, if megalomaniacal. But it may be that they're searching for something. We can't be sure. Whatever it is they're after, the Blood Raiders are out in force.

Moreover, I just recently discovered that they've sent some of their top scholars here, hiding them in a long-forgotten mining station in the middle of nowhere. These scientists are up to no good, and God knows what they're brewing in that alchemist's tower of theirs. We must put a stop to this operation before their plan unfolds. You took good care of those cultists, so there's no doubt in my mind that a few alchemists shouldn't pose too much of a problem for you. Blow up their tower and bring me back whatever concoctions they were making there.

129593.en:
Excellent job, {[character]player.name}. You are obviously in God's favor. Those plague spores seem destined for some evil purpose; good thing we got them before the Blood Raiders could unleash them on some unsuspecting planet. I can't wait to dispose of them.

I do have another small mission for you, if you're interested.

129594.en:
We have to divert our attention away from the Blood Raiders for a moment, {[character]player.name}. I've been perhaps overly eager to help out my friend Lord Methros and as a result have been neglecting my duties here in Araz. The constellation is seeing a lot of black market activity, mainly in the guise of the so-called Giraka merchant guild. The Girakas have been attempting to undermine my business deals here, and my superiors are getting restless.

One of my most important clients is Lady Eroza Arachnan, sister of the despicable Lord Arachnan. Lady Eroza is an important political figure, and we must ensure that she remains a loyal client of Imperial Armaments. She's requested a rather curious item from our catalogue to be brought to her, called the Truthteller. While I won't go into details on how it works ― trade secrets and all that ― I will say that it's a torture device of the most ingenious sort, guaranteed to make anyone spill his beans, and probably his guts too. I've no idea what exactly the good lady intends to do with it, but let's just assume it's for a good cause. I need someone fast and reliable to deliver the device to the ACN station over in Aphi, where a representative of Lady Eroza is waiting for it.

129596.en: I know I can rely on you to deliver it quickly and efficiently.

129597.en: Great job as always, {[character]player.name}. Now we can get back to business dealing with those pesky Blood Raiders.

129598.en: What are you trying to do?! These Girakas will be the end of me!

129599.en:
Now we can get back to taking care of those damned Blood Raiders. You've already visited one of their outposts here in Araz, the old imperial fortress over in Koona, the Bastion of Blood. The Blood Raiders are refurbishing the old keep and intend to make it into an impregnable stronghold. Needless to say, that won't do. We must foil their efforts now before the fortress's defenses come online. Mind you, the Blood Raiders are as hard to get rid of as cockroaches, so I don't intend for you to wipe them out for good. But if we strike them enough times, they might give up eventually.

There's a foreman overseeing the reconstruction of the old keep. If we can take him out, we'll at least delay them until a new foreman has been appointed. Bring me back that foreman's head.

129601.en:
I've been in contact with Lord Methros, keeping him up to date on what I've been doing to aid his cause. He's happy with your efforts and would have you take care of an important matter for him. This a personal request from Lord Methros himself: I don't have to tell you what an honor that is.

As you know ― better than most by now, I'm sure ― the Blood Raiders are a plague here in Araz. With so many of them nearby, it's only to be expected to find some of their more gruesome forms of entertainment here. They like blood sports, and they've set up an arena to indulge themselves. It's called "The Cauldron," and many good Amarrian souls have lost their lives there. One such soul is a cousin of Lord Methros, who was kidnapped a few weeks ago. Nothing was heard from him, or his kidnappers, for a long time, but now Lord Methros has finally learned the fate of his cousin: He died as an "entertainment" for a crowd of raucous Raiders. While Lord Methros mourns his fallen family member, he must mind the honor of his family. As do other members of House Methros, the young cousin bore the coat of arms of his noble family. Lord Methros wants that back, as the thought of some hideous Blood Raider wearing his sacred coat of arms is unbearable.

Make your way over to the Cauldron and locate the Blood Raider chapel there. The coat of arms is inside the chapel. Bring it back and you will have the eternal love of House Methros.

129603.en: The grace of God be with you.

129604.en: You have done House Methros a great service, {[character]player.name}. Lord Methros wants you involved in his plans for Araz. There's an ACN reporter over in Koona who is a close confidant of Lord Methros. I'm giving you a holoreel depicting some of the worst atrocities committed by the Blood Raiders in Araz; as a reporter, this fellow will be thrilled to get his hands one something so juicy. Go talk to him, and he will let you in on the ingenious schemes Lord Methros is hatching. I believe the fellow's holed up in what is called "The Ravelin" in the contested Bastion of Blood in Koona.

129605.en:
Dakumon tells me you're a resourceful pilot. Let's see if he's right. As you perhaps know, the Arachnan family is the biggest rival of Lord Methros in the constellation. You might say the two families are duking it out to see what family is the most powerful in Araz. Lord Arachnan has a younger brother, Thyram Arachnan, who was a gifted fighter pilot. Sadly, Thyram was also what is commonly known as the black sheep of the family.

A few years back, shortly after he succeeded his father as head of the family, Lord Arachnan had had enough of Thyram's uncouth ways and disowned him, exiling the young scoundrel from the family estates. But Thyram didn't go far; he and his shady friends joined the local pirates and have been roaming the asteroid belts around Araz since then.

Lord Methros wants to send a clear message to the Arachnan family that none of them is safe, while at the same time ridding the habitants of Araz of a pesky pirate threat. And you're the person to deliver that message ― by killing Thyram Arachnan. The only problem is, Thyram discarded his identity long time ago. The only information I have on him is that he has the rank of a warrior with the local pirates. You need to track him down, move between the constellation's asteroid belts, and kill all the warriors you can find until you find the right one. How will you know you got the right one? Thyram still holds some sentiments for his old family, it seems, for it's said that he always wears his dynasty ring. Find the ring, and you know you've got the right guy. Return with the ring to me once you have it.

Oh, and in case you were wondering what a journalist is doing working under cover, let's just say that Amarrian journalism has never been plagued by impartiality and that the stories you instigate yourself are always the most interesting.

But Thyram didn't go far; he and his shady friends joined the local pirates and have been roaming the asteroid belts around Araz since then.

Lord Methros wants to send a clear message to the Arachnan family that none of them is safe, while at the same time ridding the habitants of Araz of a pesky pirate threat. And you're the person to deliver that message ― by killing Thyram Arachnan. The only problem is, Thyram discarded his identity long time ago. The only information I have on him is that he has the rank of a warrior with the local pirates. You need to track him down, move between the constellation's asteroid belts, and kill all the warriors you can find until you find the right one. How will you know you got the right one? Thyram still holds some sentiments for his old family, it seems, for it's said that he always wears his dynasty ring. Find the ring, and you know you've got the right guy. Return with the ring to me once you have it.

Oh, and in case you were wondering what a journalist is doing working under cover, let's just say that Amarrian journalism has never been plagued by impartiality and that the stories you instigate yourself are always the most interesting.

129607.en: Yes, excellent, this is the right ring. Congratulations on finding it! Now, on to your next task.

129608.en: It might take a while to find him, but have a bit of patience {[character]player.name}. I'm sure I can turn this into a good story for ACN, and you'll be at the center of it!

129609.en:
We Amarrians are nothing if not civilized. We were eating off of gilded plates while the other races were still using their hands to wipe their arses. We have traditions older than sin and customs more ingrained (and sometimes more disgusting) than overgrown toenails.

The feud between House Arachnan and House Methros is getting serious, and in accordance with traditions, there's protocol to be followed. But there's a bit of a twist, you see. Lord Arachnan succeeded his father not many years ago. But while he is the eldest son of his line, he does have an older sibling, a sister. I believe you've already heard her name from me: Lady Eroza Arachnan. She is disputing her brother's claim as the head of the Arachnan family.

Lord Methros, in his infinite wisdom, has decided to throw his lot in with Lady Arachnan. Lord Methros' best and brightest archivists and scholars have been poring over old documents looking for precedents, and it seems they've found one. Some thousand years ago, apparently, when the head of the Arachnan family passed away, he was succeeded not by his eldest son, who by all accounts was frail of mind and body, but by his eldest daughter. She was a most capable administrator and disciplinarian, I understand, as is her descendant, the admirable Lady Eroza Arachnan. Lord Methros passed these records into my hands, and I will make sure they're well broadcast over the ACN netword in the next few days. But protocol calls for this information also to be delivered, by hand, to the lord of the region.

That's where you come in, {[character]player.name}. I want you to deliver the ancestral records to Kador Prime, where an associate of mine will accept them from you and deliver the package to the Kador household. The package is waiting for you in the ACN station over in Aphi, so you have to pick it up there first. This is hot news: Hurry so I can send out my report of the goings on through the ACN network.

129611.en: Good job. Now I can broadcast this sensational news to the rest of the Empire. Talk to me again soon; Lord Methros is nowhere near through with Lord Arachnan.

129612.en:
Predictably, Lord Arachnan is not amused by his sister's actions. I believe "treacherous" and "bitch" were the words he used when describing his feelings. And of course the fact that his arch-rival Lord Methros has intervened on Lady Arachnan's behalf aggravates him even further. But Lord Methros stands by his allies, and he has allied himself with Lady Arachnan. He has know made it his mission in life to depose Lord Arachnan and instate Eroza as the rightful head of the Arachnan family. If he succeeds, the Arachnans will undoubtedly be very grateful and, more importantly, less belligerent toward our lord and master.

With Lord Arachnan declining to step down voluntarily, more drastic measures are called for. (Incidentally, we already started down this path when we killed Lord Arachnan's younger brother. And by "we," I mean "you," of course.) Don't you sometimes just marvel at Lord Methros foresight?

Now all that stands between Lord Arachnan and his sister in the hereditary ladder is Lord Arachnan's son. With him out of the way, the path is clear for Lady Arachnan. The son goes by the name Aradim Arachnan, and he is a real hot-head. The boy fancies himself a knight of the olden days, and his foolish father indulges his fanciful dreams. Aradim and his friends like to duel in their shiny cruisers. Or joust, as they call it. They think so highly of themselves that they've declined protection from Lord Arachnan's household guards, against the better wishes of the lord's chief of security. So taking them out shouldn't be too much of a problem. Just don't fall into the same trap as they likely will and get overly confident. Overconfidence is ugly at best and lethal at worst, so keep your head screwed on straight.

Bring me the head of Aradim Arachnan, as intact as possible. Lord Methros wants it to be quite recognizable by Lord Arachnan when it's presented to him.

129614.en: Brilliant work, as always. Lord Arachnan must know what is coming by now. Talk to me again when you're ready to thicken the plot a bit more, ok?

129615.en:
Things are heating up now, {[character]player.name}. We've put things into motion that we cannot have perfect control over; I have little idea where it will all lead. Isn't it exciting?

Lord Methros is very pleased with your efforts so far; we have seized the initiative in the struggle against Lord Arachnan, and it will be interesting to see how he'll react to us slaying his son. Lord Methros himself is putting the final touches on the coup de grace for Lord Arachnan, and my editor and I are already quivering in anticipation of what he will do. But in the meantime, I have an interesting assignment for you.

I do not know how familiar you are with Amarr high society, but I can tell you that appearance and prestige are critical. For the Amarrians, you must appear powerful and strong to be prestigious, regardless of your birth. Bloodline alone is not enough. And I have the perfect mission for you to humiliate Lord Arachnan and take him down a peck or two.

The ancestral armor of House Arachnan is back in Araz, after being on display on Kador Prime for the last six months. Needless to say, the armor represents the dignity and ancestry of House Arachnan, so losing it would be a huge blow for Lord Arachnan, as the head of the house. The armor is usually stored in the Black Barbican, an ancient and impregnable fortress over in Chanoun owned by the Arachnan family. They keep many of their most valuable and prestigious items there. But the armor is not yet in the Barbican itself, it's still lying in the Outer Keep. Experts are inspecting it to see if it received any damage on the journey, and the armor won't be transferred into the Barbican for a little while. So if we hurry, we can catch the armor before it's locked away for good in the Barbican.

129617.en: And so the world crumbles around the great Lord Arachnan. Oh, the irony! Lord Methros is ready to close the matter now for good by killing Lord Arachnan himself! Talk to me when you're ready.

129618.en:
The Arachnan family owns a manor out in deep space. The grandfather of the current lord of the house built it as a reclusive summer vacation spot for the family. While its location is no secret, its tight security means it receives few visitors. Thus it's an ideal location for secret negotiations. Lord Methros has set Lord Arachnan up beautifully. Using one of his own lieutenants as a decoy, Lord Methros has manipulated Lord Arachnan into thinking he has a spy placed highly in the Methros household. And now a meeting has been arranged between Lord Arachnan and the double-agent in the aforementioned manor.

All we need do is invade the place and blast everything to pieces, including Lord Arachnan himself, allowing Lady Eroza to assume her rightful place as the head of the Arachnan family. You, a dedicated and superbly talented supporter of Lord Methros, are to be given the honor of killing Lord Methros' greatest foe.

Go and blow up the manor house. Lord Arachnan is in it and will surely die with the destruction of the manor. Now here's the only tricky part: Lord Methros wants the surveillance tapes from the internal security systems in the manor. They will serve not only as a proof of Arachnan's death, but will also allow Lord Methros to see with his own eyes the final moments of his arch-nemesis. The internal security system is called Perpetual Chamber Warden. Bring it back to me and your job is done.

129620.en: Go blow that bastard up, {[character]player.name}! Did I mention I have an exclusive on the surveillance tapes you're bringing back? This will make my career!

129621.en: Fantastic results. No doubt we'll soon see Eroza Arachnan assume the leadership of House Arachnan. Oh, happy days!

129622.en: I'm a very busy person, so unless you possess something of interest for me, then don't bother talking to me.

129623.en: I'm a very busy person, so unless you possess something of interest for me, then don't bother talking to me.

129624.en: I have a special holo reel I received from an agent in Munory. I'm sure it's of interest to you.

129625.en: Ok, lets see this holo reel then.

129626.en: I have nothing of interest for you. Let me get back to you when I have.

129627.en: Don't bother me again until you have a scoop of some sort. With all the goings on in the constellation us journalists are quite busy.

129629.en: Here's the holo reel, full of Blood Raider atrocities.

129630.en:
Oh, this is interesting. And there's a encrypted note in here too.

Ah, you have proven yourself as a worthy champion of the cause of House Methros. I have some interesting jobs lined up for someone of your calibre.

129631.en: I'd like you to transport a few State officials to the Federation Navy station in Luminaire.  They've got important business to attend to, so don't be late.  Just drop them off at your hangar in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

129632.en:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. You can continue working for various corporations in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} as long as you like. I suggest finding an agent that has a more variety of tasks available, simply search the stations that are owned by a corporation within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} and you are bound to find an agent to your liking. You can also search for agents which will speak to you by checking the database information for the corporation of your choice. To do that simply open the People and Places menu through your NeoCom and search for the corporation name. Right click on it and choose 'show info'. There you should find a list of all of its agents that are available. Their division should give you a hint as to what type of mission they are associated with.

Take care!

129645.en: The Core Complexion Inc. Factory in {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name} informed us that they have another shipment of ammo ready to be transported here.  Our transportation services cannot handle the load of these constant courier jobs so I'd be very grateful if you could take it on yourself to bring one batch of Carbonized Lead ammo here.

129646.en: Thanks.  Don't go anywhere though, I have one more assignment I'd like you to complete.

129647.en: A friend of mine, Hakar Ogok, apparently is in need of some work.  He resides on the Core Complexion station in Arlek which I sent you to earlier.  Since you're probably heading there anyway to speak with Hakar, you might as well bring a batch of Enriched Uranium with you.  They need it for their factory there.

129648.en: Nice work.  And don't forget to speak with Hakar before you leave.

129649.en: The Urban Management station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} is getting low on medical supplies.  It's located very close to the border with the Ammatar territories, and due to the current hostilities between our nations, the sick and wounded keep the medical staff there busy.  If you could make a quick run to {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} with a batch of antibiotics, I would be very grateful.

129650.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}.  Keep helping the Republic like this and you'll definitely make a name for yourself.  By the way, Eslin Stein was looking for someone like you.  He's located at the Urban Management station in Odatrik.  Good luck.

129651.en: The Vherokior Tribe Treasury station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} is in constant demand of coolants.  They're a pretty wealthy bunch out there, and they keep needin' more cooling devices to keep the engines of the shuttles and planetary vehicles, which they use on their expeditions, from overheating.  If you're up for it, you could take a batch of coolants over there and earn a reward.

129652.en: The Vherokior Tribe Treasury station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} is in constant demand of coolants.  They're a pretty wealthy bunch out there, and they keep needin' more cooling devices to keep the engines of the shuttles and planetary vehicles, which they use on their expeditions, from overheating.  If you're up for it, you could take a batch of coolants over there and earn a reward.

129653.en: Good stuff.  Speak with Vilhara Vit at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} if you need more work.  Cheers.

129654.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}.  Don't forget to pay Benur Errus a visit.

129655.en:
I have a batch of Dairy Products that need to be shipped to the Native Freshfood Warehouse in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} today, {[character]player.name}. They are used in creating the traditional Native Freshfood Special, which is a highly sought after meal. Our executives love it, and so we have this extremely lucrative deal with Native Freshfood corporation where we supply them with the ingredients almost for free and they make the product. To cut our losses we try to hire cheap labor to transfer the goods over to their factory.

So you up for it, {[character]player.name}? You could stop by my friends office, Benur Errus, for a treat if you want. He's located at the very station I'm sending you to.

129656.en:
Hello, {[character]player.name}. I'm on the lookout for someone who can handle a combat ship, if you know what I mean. You see, there is currently a trade agreement between Native Freshfood and Vherokior Tribe: They supply us with dairy products, and in return we sell them our meals for a very low price. Usually we get many convoys each day from their station in Teonusude, but there has been a problem recently. There is apparently a rogue drone hive somewhere in that system, and the security forces haven't been able to locate it. Our convoys have been attacked occasionally when they are passing through.

Fortunately, our last convoy that was attacked managed to escape, giving us the exact coordinates of where it was ambushed. These drones don't have any common sense, so they're probably still there. Apparently they have taken control over a warp disruptor device near a research outpost and are using it to "capture" passing ships. We've already managed to disable the device remotely, but we need someone to take care of the drones. And that's where you come in. You up for it?

129657.en: Nice job, {[character]player.name}.  I couldn't have done it better myself.

129658.en:

129659.en: A friend of mine, Vilhara Vit, is expecting a shipment of our famous Native Freshfood Special.  I'd like you to make the delivery for me.  I'll pay well, of course ...

129660.en:
Your next job is a little more risky, it will send you into 0.5 security space. I doubt you'll encounter any pirates on the way, but you never know.

What I need you to do is transport a few tourists to the Krusual Tribe station in Hek. Hek is a popular tourist area these days and we always have people on the lookout for cheap flights there. If you're up for it, I'll let them know.

129661.en: Thank goodness you arrived there safely.  And by the way, Evika Deng was looking for you.  You'll find her at the Krusual Tribe station in Hek.

129662.en:
The Republic Fleet keeps demanding more troops due to the current hostilities with the Amarr-Caldari alliance, and we're forced to comply. I don't know where this will end; so many youths lost in battle... I just hope this won't be like the Great Wars, when an entire generation was almost lost. Ah, tragedy.

Anyway, we cannot avoid our duty. Could you transport a few of these troops to the Republic Fleet station in Lustrevik? I would be very grateful; good, reliable independent transport is hard to find these days.

129663.en:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. You can continue working for various corporations in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} as long as you like. I suggest finding an agent who has a more of a variety of tasks available; simply search the stations that are owned by a corporation within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} and you are bound to find an agent to your liking.

You can also search for available agents by checking the database information for the corporation of your choice. To do that, simply open the "People and Places" menu through your NeoCom and search for the corporation name. Right-click on it and choose "show info." There, you should find a list of all of that corporation's agents who are available to you. An agent's division should give you a hint as to what type of mission he or she is likely to give you.

Take care!

129670.en: I need a hand with a courier job.  The Emperor Family has ordered the movement of millions of foot soldiers to Saidusairds, which is on the Federation - Empire border.  Since {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} is one of the chief suppliers of these troops, our local transportation service is currently flooded.  What I'd like you to do is take one small group of light marines to {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, and drop them off at the Carthum Conglomerate station there.  I'm not authorized to send someone like you into low secure space, so unfortunately I can't pay you for making the entire run.  But it will at least save us half the journey.

129671.en: I need a hand with a courier job.  The Emperor Family has ordered the movement of millions of foot soldiers to Saidusairds, which is on the Federation - Empire border.  Since {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} is one of the chief suppliers of these troops, our local transportation service is currently flooded. 129672.en: Nice work, {[character]player.name}.  I suggest you speak with Ilia Abazen at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, she has a job or two for you.  Good luck.

129673.en: I'll take it, but does this mean we're invading the Federation?

129674.en: No, we're just strengthening our position there in case of an attack.  With the political climate as bad as it is today, we need to be prepared.

129675.en: One of our executives needs to be delivered to the Sarum station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} for a meeting.  He's running pretty late and we haven't managed to find suitable transportation for him in time.  Could you make a quick run to {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} and deliver him to this destination?  I would be very grateful.

129676.en: One of our executives needs to be delivered to the Sarum station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} for a meeting.  He's running pretty late and we haven't managed to find suitable transportation for him in time.  Could you make a quick run to {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} and deliver him to this destination?  I would be very grateful.

129677.en: Good job.  I suggest that you pay a visit to Korini Nakan, at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  He has some work that you might be interested in.

129678.en: I need you to make a standard shipment of robotics to the Sarum Family station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, {[character]player.name}.  Just drop off the shipment there and Sarum personnel will pick it up.  You up for it?

129679.en: I need you to make a standard shipment of robotics to the Sarum Family station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, {[character]player.name}.  Just drop off the shipment there and Sarum personnel will pick it up.

129680.en: I suggest you speak with the Sarum agent Korini Nakan, he's always on the lookout for someone like yourself.

129681.en: I have a shipment of goods to deliver to the Ministry of War in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, and I was wondering if you could make the run for me, {[character]player.name}.  You'll be paid in full, of course.

129682.en: I suggest you visit Kanori Agored's office while you're at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. He just might have a job for you. Good luck.

129683.en: I need to get another shipment of small arms to our troops in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, {[character]player.name}.  Could you make a trip to the Imperial Navy station there and drop them off at the docking bay?  You'll be rewarded ...

129684.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}.  If you're still looking for work, I know Utaka Orasa at the Navy station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} has been looking for someone like you.

129685.en: We just received a shipment of arms cache, which means another group of our slave troops has been equipped and is ready to move out.  If you have spare time on your hands, {[character]player.name}, I would like you to help us move them to {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  Drop them off at the Imperial Navy station there, and my colleagues will take care of the rest.

129686.en: We just received a shipment of arms cache, which means another group of our slave troops has been equipped and is ready to move out.  If you have spare time on your hands, {[character]player.name}, I would like you to help us move them to {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  Drop them off at the Imperial Navy station there, and my colleagues will take care of the rest.

129687.en: Good work.  But it seems that your captive is no longer of use to us.  My guess is that he injected himself with a deadly viral agent before you arrived.  But don't worry, we expected as much, and we have an antidote ready for you in the infirmary.  However, this will complicate matters a bit.  Now we have to wait for them to make the next move ...

129688.en: I'd like to do some more investigating on the Thukker mercenary incident.  It would help a great deal if we knew the true identity of the pilot you captured, but to do that I need professional help, since our database here has very limited records of Thukker citizens.  I know of a private investigator residing in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} who might be able to identify the scoundrel.  Bring a DNA sample taken from his body to this acquaintance of mine and we'll see what he comes up with.

129689.en: I'd like to do some more investigating on the Thukker mercenary incident.  It would help a great deal if we knew the true identity of the pilot you captured, but to do that I need professional help, since our database here has very limited records of Thukker citizens.  I know of a private investigator residing in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} who might be able to identify the scoundrel.  Bring a DNA sample taken from his body to this acquaintance of mine and we'll see what he comes up with.

129690.en: Nice work, {[character]player.name}, but I need you ASAP for another mission.  Something dire has come up.

129691.en:
As I said earlier, something dire has come up. One of our biggest research outposts in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has been attacked. Its location is a secret, so someone must have been snooping around; I'm gonna take a shot and guess that it was those Thukker mercs you took care of.

We've identified the attackers as agents of the Minmatar-Gallente alliance. They've certainly got balls if they've come this far into our territory, I'll give them that. But they must be eliminated before they board the outpost. We'll destroy it before we allow them to get their filthy hands on the stuff our scientists have been researching there.

From the data I've received, there is a large force of Minmatar fighters at the doorstep of our research outpost already, fighting their way in. We are expecting reinforcements to arrive soon, as we spotted two separate groups of Republic ships heading their way already. So you must hurry before the reinforcements arrive, or you'll never be able to take them out.

129693.en: Great, now make haste!  Destroy the Republic forces before their reinforcements arrive, then take care of the extra ships.

129694.en: You've done us a great service, {[character]player.name}, I can't thank you enough.  I hope you enjoy your reward, you've certainly earned it!

129695.en:
We've had increasing reports of hostile activity within our borders in the past months, and I've been ordered to take a look into the matter. One of these reports came from a group of miners scouring the Veldspar belts in the outer regions of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They claimed to have seen a large ore convoy heading away from one of the belts, consisting of ships which appeared to be of Gallentean origin. Their escort attacked them immediately, but they escaped unharmed. My best guess would be that these hostiles are in fact pirates, but what intrigued me is that their ships did not appear to match the description of any pirate organization known to infest {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

I want you to take a look into this, {[character]player.name}. Fly to the asteroid belt where the miners were attacked. Wait there for a while, and see if any hostiles show up. If they do, destroy them but try to take back someone from their ranks alive for questioning.

Dismissed.

129697.en: Interesting.  The pilot you managed to capture is a Federation marine.  This will undoubtedly raise a few eyebrows in central command.  Please wait a bit while I get our next orders.

129698.en: Take care out there.  I've no idea what to expect, so be prepared for the worst.

129699.en:
Something came up while you were off on your reconnaissance mission. A group of slave traders traveling through {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} stumbled upon a strange anomaly that caught their attention. It's a cloud of gas that somehow acts as a shield against long-range scanners, which is probably why our surveillance forces haven't detected it yet. These slave traders couldn't scan what was inside and weren't going to take any chances by approaching the anomaly, so they left and informed the authorities.

I would like you to investigate this strange cloud, and see what's inside. I'll upload a bookmark to the mission details in your Opportunities interface that should send you close enough to the anomaly for your scanner to detect what's inside. If you encounter any hostiles, destroy them. Then report back to me with your findings.

129700.en:

129701.en: More Federation vessels?  This smells very fishy indeed.  We'll have to investigate this acceleration gate more thoroughly ...

129702.en: I've been to the anomaly and this is what I discovered ...

129703.en: Now be careful out there, who knows what you'll find in that gas cloud.

129704.en:
Since you found the acceleration gate in your last mission, I believe you're the most suited to take a look at what's at the other side. I've received reports of Gallente convoys traveling to and from the area you discovered, but never realized there was a connection until your discovery. So this might be a hidden base of some sort, who knows. But it's for you to find out.

When you arrive at the warp-in point after using the acceleration gate hidden inside the anomaly, I want you to neutralize any hostiles you find. I'm especially keen on finding out what these convoys have been transporting, so if you see one then destroy it. I'll send someone else to pick up the pieces after you're done, so don't leave any survivors.

129706.en:

129707.en: Incredible. You've done extremely well, {[character]player.name}, but from here on in this investigation is in someone else's hands.  The case has been taken over by someone higher up the chain of command, so from my point of view this investigation is closed.

129708.en:
There is a rumor afloat that the ruins of the Mire Keep in Garisas is currently being used as a Blood Raider stronghold. We've known this for many years, but this is the first time rumors such as this have spread so far within the civilian populace. It's causing quite a stir, and the people demand action. With the limited funding we have, a direct assault will hit our wallet quite hard. Not to mention the Blood Raider forces will simply come back in a few months and reclaim the area, or build another base of operations elsewhere in Araz. We also do not want to start a full fledged war with those pirates, not when our military is busy with the Republic and Federation scum.

But even so we need to prove that we're doing something about them. And for that we have you, {[character]player.name}. Your first task is to infiltrate the Keep and retrieve some of their bio-engineers within the infamous Blood Factories. I want to know more of what is actually transpiring in there. With knowledge comes power.

We're under a huge amount of pressure, even from the Emperor Family, to rid all of our territories of the Blood Raider religion and the gruesome ritualistic murders committed by it's followers. So don't screw this up, we might not get another chance at this if they know what we're after.

129710.en: Good to know you're ready for this assignment, {[character]player.name}.  I suggest you thoroughly search the Mire Keep complex for any Blood Factories, you'll probably find the scientists inside.  Good luck.

129711.en: You did good out there, {[character]player.name}.  My men have already started interrogating the prisoners.  I'll let you know when we have some results.  In the meantime, I have some other work for you so listen up ...

129713.en: Find Blood Factories in the Contested Amarr Mire Keep complex in Garisas, and capture Blood Raider scientists from their laboratories inside those structures.  Return to your agent once you have captured 5 scientists.

129714.en: I want you to enter the Slope and kill a few Corpse Dealers for me. Bring me back some of these inactive bug-ridden corpses; I want to investigate further what these bug devices can do.

129715.en:
Welcome, capsuleer. Your presence here in the Ravelin indicates to me that you are interested in stemming the tide of Blood Raiders into Koona. The Blood Raider cult is out in force in this constellation, and here in Koona they've made this old Imperial fortress their own. Thankfully, they've not been here all that long, so there's still time to do something about it.

The local authorities seem either unable or unwilling to deal with the Blood Raiders once and for all. I've even heard rumors that Lord Methros, ruler of Koona and the nearby Munory, is secretly dealing with the Blood Raiders, or with some part of the cult at least. Be that as it may, all of my attempts to get help from the lord have fallen on deaf ears, and even my pleas to the Imperial Navy went unanswered. I guess it's all up to me.

Amarr Constructions has poured a lot of ISK into building up its infrastructure here in Araz, and we're not about to let some murderous scumbag fanatics ruin it all for us. My superiors have given me full rein to deal with the problem, including a vast warchest to reward those willing to aid me in this endeavor. If you're interested, I might have several assignments for you.

The Blood Raiders are strengthening their defenses all the time. We will deal with that later, but for now we must put an end to a particularly devilish little scheme of theirs. For all their fanaticism, the Blood Raiders are no fools, and they know they will be resisted. So they're expecting a lot of visitors in the Bastion of Blood. They'll fight with every means at their disposal, and not just firepower alone. One of their more cunning plans, our spies have discovered, is to fill bodies they've already drained of blood with bug devices and Trojan horses. They disperse the bodies around the complex in the hope that someone compassionate (or foolish) enough will pick it up. Once the bug-ridden corpse is inside the ship, it can wreak all kinds of havoc.

Fortunately, the plan is still only in its infancy. The Blood Raiders have started littering the first room in the complex with corpses, but the bug devices in them remain inactive. That gives us a chance to clean some of them up before they come online, plus kill some Blood Raiders in the process. I want you to enter the Slope and kill a few Corpse Dealers for me. Bring me back some of these inactive bug-ridden corpses; I want to investigate further what these bug devices can do.

129716.en: Welcome aboard, {[character]player.name}. The Corpse Dealers shouldn't be too much of a problem as they're not expecting anyone to engage them just yet, but be careful nevertheless.

129717.en: Excellent job. Now we can start doing some serious damage to the Blood Raiders here in the Bastion.

129718.en: Go into the fortress and hunt them down. Once you've collected a sizeable amount of antiseptic biomass, return to me with it. Perhaps some bereaved families will at least be able to bury their loved ones, instead of having to anxiously wait for years for any news of them.

129719.en:
I doubt your actions against the Corpse Dealers were enough to scare the Blood Raiders off from carrying out their macabre plan. But at least it tells them that we're on to them. Once I've analyzed the bug-ridden corpses you brought me, we'll have a better idea how we can foil their plan further. In the meantime, we're ready to strike the Blood Raiders at the heart of their operation. The cultists have been busy ambushing innocents around the constellation, and every day dozens of corpses are taken to the Bastion of Blood to be drained in their horrid rituals. Most have been processed with antiseptic agents to hinder rot. The bodies, or what remains of them, are brought in by special couriers called simply Corpse Collectors.

Enter you: Go into the fortress and hunt them down. Once you've collected a sizeable amount of antiseptic biomass, return to me with it. Not only are we putting spikes in the Blood Raiders' operation, but we're also saving the remains of those they've killed from a fate worse than death. Perhaps some bereaved families will at least be able to bury their loved ones, instead of having to anxiously wait for years for any news of them.

129720.en: Well done. I'm all ready to run a DNA test on the biomass you brought me. I hope we get some positive results. Talk to me again soon; you've been of great help to me so far, and I have several jobs earmarked just for you.

129721.en: Bring the remains of Daryd Kador to his family for proper burial.

129722.en:
Most of the biomass you brought me is too mixed for DNA analysis, but fortunately some pieces were more or less intact. In fact, my analysis shows that one of the bodies you brought back is that of a member of a minor branch of the Kador family, one Daryd Kador. Now, Daryd was not part of the ruling branch of the Kador family and thus stood a long way from the Kador throne. Nevertheless, I feel it is my duty to have his remains brought to the Kadors for proper burial.

Of course, since it was you who found him, I feel it's only right that you finish the job and bring Daryd Kador's remains home. It's not much of a job, but I can use the time while you're gone to put the final touches on the next step in my personal crusade against the Blood Raider heretics. Just so you know, I have acquired a passkey to the innermost sanctum of the Bastion of Blood, and once you've returned, I aim to put it to good use ... in your hands. Just don't take too long getting back, or I'll be forced to give the passkey to someone else to do the job.

129723.en: Good job as always, {[character]player.name}. Now we can strike the Blood Raiders were it really matters. I have to step out for just a moment; talk to me again when you're ready.

129724.en:
The passkey I gave you, the Bastion Master Key, was built by Amarr Constructions centuries ago, which explains how I got my hands on it. It will give you access to the Treasure Chamber and allow you to bring some friends along. But be very careful because the gate reconfigures its access algorithms each time it's used, so you can use the passkey only once ― which means you get only one shot at completing this assignment. Fail and we're through.

Before you panic, I've done some research to help you prepare. Most likely you'll be confronted by a squadron of Blood Raider destroyers the moment you enter the chamber. The generator building is guarded by a few battleships, supported by several battlecruisers and a few elite frigates. Be careful of the frigates, as they can warp scramble you. I want you to destroy the generator building, but otherwise I leave the planning of this operation in your capable hands.

129725.en:
The Blood Raiders have centered their operation on what they call the "Treasure Chamber," the innermost sanctum of the Bastion of Blood. There they are constructing a massive power generator; once operational, it will generate enough power for the Blood Raiders to operate an insane number of defensive structures around their station. Destroying the unfinished generator now would be a huge blow to the Blood Raiders, plus it would allow us to continue harassing them in the Treasure Chamber because their mega-defense systems would remain inoperable.

129726.en: Tough luck, {[character]player.name}. I thought you were made of sterner stuff. Clearly I overestimated your talents. I guess I'll have to scramble our ships to deal with the Blood Raiders en masse. God knows what we'll do about the generator and their uber-defenses now, though... Maybe I should look into evacuation parameters.

129727.en: Outstanding job, {[character]player.name}! Your success fills me with confidence. Talk to me again soon. With you at my disposal, I'm raring to have a go at the top-echelon Blood Raiders in Araz. With you on our side, I'm sure we'll have no problem dealing with them.

129728.en:
The Blood Raiders have a massive command outpost in Garisas. It is very well defended, so don't even think of entering it unless you have backup and are packing a lot of firepower. The Blood Raiders have a battle station there that acts as their command outpost, but that is not our concern. Instead, head for the innermost room in the outpost, the Commander Keep. There you should find the leader of the Blood Raider operation here in Araz, Archpriest Hakram.

Bring me the Archpriest's head to complete this assignment and you will have done not only Amarr Constructions, but the whole Amarr Empire a great service.

129729.en:
Thanks to you, the Blood Raiders have been dealt severe blows here in Koona. Maybe that will set their timetable back some weeks and even make them abandon the Bastion all together. I feel there's little to be gained by harassing them further here in Koona, though. If we really want to hurt the Blood Raiders, we must attack higher up the chain of command.

The local lord over the Garisas system here in Araz, Baron Bartezo Maphante, has long since lost his autonomy in the system. It is now run by criminal elements and merchant guilds. Thus, it was easy for the Blood Raiders to establish themselves in force there. Now, pretty much the whole Blood Raider operation in the constellation is run from Garisas. That is were we must hit them.

The Blood Raiders have a massive command outpost in Garisas. It is very well defended, so don't even think of entering it unless you have backup and are packing a lot of firepower. The Blood Raiders have a battle station there that acts as their command outpost, but that is not our concern. Instead, head for the innermost room in the outpost, the Commander Keep. There you should find the leader of the Blood Raider operation here in Araz, Archpriest Hakram. He is a close friend of Omar Sarikusa, the supreme leader of the Blood Raiders, and is acting on Sarikusa's behalf here in Araz. If we take Hakram out, their whole operation will be thrown into disarray, which might allow us, and those local authorities actually willing to do something, the chance to drive the Blood Raiders out for good.

Bring me the Archpriest's head to complete this assignment and you will have done not only Amarr Constructions, but the whole Amarr Empire a great service.

129730.en: I'm a happy man, {[character]player.name}, for I know this tough assignment is in the hands of the very best.

129731.en: Great job. Of course, I expected nothing less of you. Your talents are unquestioned, and I´m honored to call you friend, {[character]player.name}.

129732.en:
Welcome, weary traveler. Are you here to visit the holy spa? Araz holds a special place in the hearts of true believers, for it was here that the great prophet Angitus Omira had his divine visions. Every year thousands of pilgrims make their way here to visit and pray at the spa.

Alas, lately is had become very dangerous for pilgrims to enter Araz. Blood Raiders are everywhere and the ongoing feud between the most prominent noble families in the constellation destabilizes things even further. And Kador does nothing but watch, but that is to be expected as he likes his underlings to fight each other. That way, they're too busy trying to choke each other to harbor any thoughts of uniting against their liege lord. What is more, it allows Kador an easy way to determine the strengths and weaknesses of his feudal lords. He's a clever man, but as is so often the case it is us lesser persons that suffer.

But enough of that. Let's get back to the business at hand. For many years I have aided pilgrims on their voyage to the Prophet's Spa. With the volatile situation I've had to take extra precautions to make sure nothing untoward happens on their way over here. One such precaution is to have experienced pilots ferry the pilgrims the last stages of their journey. Your presence here tells me you're interested in work, so that is what I'm offering you. It's not much fun, but for the pilgrims it's quite vital. And if you do well I have another job for you that might more to your taste. I take it you have nothing against killing Blood Raiders? Never mind, we worry about that later. For now, I want you to fetch a few pilgrims and bring them to Munory. I will then guide them on the last part of their sacred journey.
