129968.en: Good work.  I've notified our engineers which were on stand-by near the deadspace area to warp inside and start modifying the gate which leads to the Drone Hive.  After the modifications it should lead you to the Amarrian complex instead ...

129969.en:
These Blood Raiders are a determined bunch, I'll give them that. There has been a coordinated strike against our production facilities at various key locations throughout the constellation. I'll admit that we don't know for sure that the Raiders were behind the attacks, but given our recent activities, not to mention theirs... Anyway, due to this unforeseen occurrence, we're going to need to relocate some of our resources. This is a tremendous logistical undertaking, one that will require much manpower to execute quickly and efficiently.

One of our most important products is an infantry-borne anti-tank laser we're currently in the final stages of developing. Much of our stock was destroyed in the series of attacks, but fortunately we have a few crates of parts in Munory that were still due for the assembly line. Since you've proven yourself to be a trustworthy and effective pilot, I'm assigning you the task of relocating these parts to safer facilities, so we can continue to produce this weapon.

Head over to the Ducia Foundry Mining Outpost in Munory, grab those crates, and bring them to the Amarr Constructions Production Plant in Chanoun. Your work, and your silence in this matter will be much appreciated.

129970.en:
The Blood Raiders have come down hard on us for what happened, {[character]player.name}. They don't like people stealing their technology any more than might be expected of a bloodthirsty cabal of ruthless cultist freaks, it appears... A shipment of explosives en route to a contingent of Lord Arachnan's armed forces has been intercepted and all our personnel killed. It's beginning to look like we have to show these bloody-minded creeps a thing or two.

I want you to head down to Zimse, where rumor has it they have a small outpost. Eliminate all opposition you find there. One hopes your actions will send them the message that Imperial Armaments are not to be trifled with. Report back to me when you're done and it may be that I will have found some more work for you.

129971.en:
We've found out for certain who was behind the strike on our production facilities, {[character]player.name}. No surprise, really. The Blood Raiders have their tendrils everywhere, it seems.

Imperial Armaments is not known for anything less than a full-throated response. There is a Blood Raider outpost in Aphi. The thing is heavily fortified, but we will not let that deter us. Currently residing there is a Blood Raider Arch Deacon by the name of Toran Degartat. We have it on good authority that he's the one who orchestrated the attacks on our factories. Degartat makes his temporary residence in a small munitions depot, located underneath the Cathedral at the deadspace location I'm about to send you to.

Destroy the munitions depot and kill every living thing you find there. It's time we show these bastards what it means to mess with Imperial Armaments. Return to me for a substantial reward: We value good service highly here at Imperial Armaments.

129972.en:
Our engineers have just about finished modifying the gate that used to lead to the drone hive. It's far enough into the deadspace area to be usable for our little project of connecting it to the Amarr complex. I'm a little worried that it might not send you to the correct location, modifying these gates is always risky, and there's no time to test it.

Your assignment is simple. Get as far into the Amarr complex as you can, and bring back any important info to me. Knowing their positions and strength before we launch our assault would really help.

Oh and one other thing, when you arrive there one of our agents will probably have already gone through the gate. His task was to move the navigational beacon in the Amarr complex room. This will cause the acceleration gate from the slave compound, where we believe most of the Amarr armada is located, to fail. This should give you some extra time to finish your task before reinforcements arrive. But regardless, please complete this mission as fast as possible, or you risk being overwhelmed.

129975.en: I'm afraid I can't decode the information inside the data chip you recovered from the Amarr complex earlier.  You'll have to deliver it to an old friend of mine in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, he has the necessary tools to crack the code.  Check the mission details in your Opportunities interface for further information.

129978.en:
The data you retrieved earlier has some very important information. I don't know if the Amarr forces have guessed that the data chip you recovered had survived the explosion of the control tower, but either way we need to move fast while we still have the advantage.

This data directs us to two areas in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. One is the deadspace area that you must be familiar with by now, the other area is not in deadspace. I would like you to investigate area two. I will add a bookmark to the mission details in your Opportunities interface of course.

129979.en: A Caldari stargate hidden inside a man-made ion field?  This is an amazing discovery, {[character]player.name}.  But we must keep this quiet.  If the general public hears about this, it may cause mass panic.

129980.en: What is this place and who are you?

129981.en:
The Museum Arcana is a private establishment were connoisseurs of all things old and arcane can pursue their interest. Within you will find many collectors from all over, but I must warn you that they are fervent followers of their chosen hobby and do not suffer fools or over eager treasure hunters.

We do not let just anyone enter the museum. You have proved that you possess at least rudimentary knowledge of archaeology, but to pass into the museum proper you must first complete a little task I will set you. My formal title is the Doorkeeper, but I seldom use it. All you have to do to pass this little test is analyse the little casket beside me. There is a runic inscription hidden there somewhere, and I want you to bring it to me. You can also find the key to the gate leading to the museum, so look closely. The key you can keep, and it grants you full access to the museum. Just to make this a little interesting I will give you a good bonus reward if you manage to complete your assessment of the casket in less than 5 minutes.

129982.en: I consider myself a proficient archaeologist, so this will be a trivial matter for me.

129983.en: If you say so. Show me there's more to you than just your big mouth.

129984.en: I'm not interested in visiting the museum at the moment.

129985.en: Suit yourself. I will not test you again, but you can analyze the casket whenever you want.

129986.en: I told you this would be easy for me. Here's your inscription.

129989.en:
In your last mission for me you discovered a Caldari stargate inside {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. This must be taken care of, before the Caldari fleet manages to bypass our entire defense system. So far they seem to be content with laying low and getting on with their business in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, but that could change when they find out they have been discovered.

So don't screw this up, {[character]player.name}. You have one shot to get this right. The Caldari Fleet could be coming through that gate any minute now, so you need to work fast. Destroy the stargate before the Caldari manage to send more ships through. Our scanners have already detected some activity around the gate, so you will probably have to fend off a few fighters to get the job done. If you can't handle it, then let me know ASAP so I can find someone more suitable. Good luck out there, soldier.

Those Caldari gates can usually take more of a beating.  But anyhow, you did good, and saved us a heap-load of potential trouble.  But here is where our involvement in this case ends.  Dealing with the remainder of the Amarr slave complex is for someone higher up the chain of command.

129992.en:
It has come to my attention that another agent within {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} revealed a sizable deadspace area inside {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} that has apparently been claimed by the Amarr - Caldari alliance. Apparently what he found in there was more than he could handle, so it has fallen to us to resolve this critical matter of national security.

Your first task is to infiltrate the Amarr slave compound and destroy the fleet guarding it. The previous agent with this assignment had discovered a secret entrance into the complex. However due to his bungling the Amarr forces now know about this 'hidden' route and therefore it's pointless to use it. Instead I want you to fly in there through the main gate and attack them head-on. You should be experienced enough to handle 'em, although I do of course recommend bringing some backup with you.

But our job isn't over yet, I noticed that you captured some of the Amarr light marines which were on board one of their vessels.  They will need to be interrogated, just in case we missed something.

129995.en:
The Amarr troops you captured in your previous mission are unwilling to reveal any information. In fact we've nearly lost a few to suicide. So as a last ditch effort I want them brain scanned, we can 'fetch' images from their brain which may reveal something to us. It's a difficult and risky process, but then again these are the enemy and in war one must make decisions which would otherwise be deemed unethical.

The equipment which is needed to do the brain scan is located at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Drop off the marines there and my associates will take care of the rest. Dismissed.

129997.en: Get back to me when you're ready for another combat mission.

129998.en:
A brain scan of the marines you captured revealed images of a third entrance into the Amarr slave compound deadspace area. However getting through the first acceleration gate requires a key. Fortunately one of the marines knew its location.

You must once again venture to the slave compound. There you will find an armory which was hidden by a cloaking field emitter. Since we know of its exact location now, we will modify your ship's computer to ignore the cloaking field. This should make the task of retrieving the key quite easy.

Once you have the key report back to me, and I will give you the coordinates to the third entrance.

130000.en: Great, now that we have the key it's time to use it.  Let's see what lies at the other side.

130001.en: I have the Imperial Navy Gate Permit and I have destroyed the targets.

130002.en:
Now that we have the keycard it's time to send you to the third gate. Make sure you're well equipped and ready for anything the Amarr or Caldari might pit you against, because I have absolutely no idea what lies beyond the acceleration gate.

I will fit your ship with some high tech sensors of my own, just in case I'm able to spot something that you miss. Don't worry, it won't fill a module slot. Now get going!

130004.en:
Another stargate located inside our jurisdiction! Thank goodness you managed to destroy it. No wonder the Amarr forces had such an easy time bringing in reinforcements.

Now only the final assault on their headquarters is left. This will truly test your mettle, so get ready!

130005.en: Find TakmahlLore 3 in Takmahl Digital Mezzotint containers

130007.en:
This is the Museum Arcana, where you'll find the finest collection of rare and beautiful items from all over. But what we are most famous for is our collection of Takmahl artefacts. The Takmahls were once part of the great Amarr Empire, but were exiled from the empire a long time ago, only shortly after us Amarrians took to space again. The Takmahls were heretics of the worst sort, some call them the predecessors of the Blood Raider cult.

For centuries nothing was heard from them, but not long ago relics were found here in Araz that show that the Takmahls had a thriving culture for many centuries after their departure from the glorious Amarr Empire. Yet at some point they died out, for what reasons I do not know. Archaeologists and treasure seekers from all over have since convened here in Araz, dreaming of uncovering the secrets of the Takmahls, or more precisely, their fabled treasures.

Yet my job here is not just overseeing the museum, but more importantly I am here as a member of the Theology Council. It is our job to make sure the despicable scriptures and rituals of the Takmahls are kept well under wrap. The last thing the Empire needs right now is another religious schism.

Your presence here means that you are an archaeologist of some merits. I have use of someone with your talents, rooting out those seeking false enlightenment or harbingers of discord. Help me out a bit and I will give you the key to the hidden treasures of the Takmahls. But only if you first prove yourself to be a champion of the Amarr faith.

There is a certain item to be find among the relics you see here scattered around. I want you to use your archaeological skills to unearth for me a Centrifugal Primer. It's advanced theoretical texts that I hope will give us rare insights into the rise and fall of the Takmahls. Bring me one of them, from past experience I know that your best bet of finding one is in a Digital Mezzotint. It's a rare item, so don't be too discouraged if you don't find it right away. If you haven't realised already this is a test of your mettle. If you manage to find me one I'll reward you well later down the line, but even if you fail I still have some use for you. Talk to me again when you have the Primer, or when you have given up the search.

130010.en: I'm not interested in hunting down heretics or thieves.

130011.en: Here's your Primer. This wasn't all that hard.

130012.en: I'm so sick looking for this rotten Primer that I could throw up. Have someone else do your dirty work.

130013.en: Ah! You have proved yourself to be an archaeoligist of exceptional talents! Talk to me again soon, I have another job for you with some juicier rewards.

130014.en: Take care amongst all the collector sharks out there.

130015.en: Yeah, I knew this was a tough one. But I'm willing to give you a second chance. Talk to me once you're ready for something different.

130016.en: You said you had something of interest for me. What is it?

130017.en:
Yes, I want to enlist your aid in an effort of mine. I've been scourging what Takmahl ruins I've come upon for statues and idols made by the Takmahls. These statues and idols depict our deity and are a grave affront to our religion. It is my duty to find and destroy these heretical symbols before they spread to the world.

What I want you to do is simple. I know that somewhere buried among the rubble you find here you can find these holy statues if you only dig long enough. It seems that your best bet of finding one is in one of the striking curiosities around here. Search them and see if you can come up with a holy statue. If you do, bring it to me. If you manage this within the next 3 hours I will even reward you with a rare implant.

130021.en: Excellent. As before, don't let the fanatical collectors get to you.

130022.en: Your vanity ill suits your limited talents, young one.

130023.en: I finally found that statue. Hope it's the right one, doesn't look much like god to me.

130024.en: It's the right one alright. You are proving to be quite an asset. If you tackle one more problem for me you'll get the key to the whereabouts of Takmahl relics beyond your wildest dreams.

130034.en:
We're doing a good job protecting the Empire from the foul influences that the Takmahl theology might impose. But more is needed and I want you to show me one more time your dedication in rooting out these blaspehmous religious artefacts of the Takmahl. Once you've done that then you truly are an honorable pilot worthy to learn where the true treasures of the Takmahls lie.

The Arcana Patrons seek the potentially most dangerous items of the Takmahls, their holy scriptures. But we must tolerate them for they are important clients of the museum, vital for its survival. Yet you are not bound by the same restrictions I am, so you can move against them without putting the future wellbeing of the museum in jeopardy. Hunt down the Arcana Patrons and bring me back the ritual texts they are collecting. Those texts could cause severe disturbance in the Empire if revealed and the Theology Council is not about to let some uncouth art collectors hoard them.

You were not born yesterday, so I shouldn't have to urge caution, but yet I feel I must do so as the Arcana Patrons are a dangerous lot. Do not lose faith if you don't find the texts right away, in this assignment as so many others patience is a virtue worth practicing. But if you do manage to get the texts quickly, say within the next 3 hours or so, I will be a happy man and will reward you accordingly. And as promised, the moment you bring me those texts the key to the Labyrinth, wherein the hidden treasures of the Takmahls await, will be yours.

And as promised, the moment you bring me those texts the key to the Labyrinth, wherein the hidden treasures of the Takmahls await, will be yours.

130037.en: Those Arcana Patrons don't frighten me, the texts will be in your hands before you know it.

130038.en: I have no interest in tackling those Patrons. Keep the key yourself.

130039.en: Here are those ritual texts you asked for. They sure make for a nice bedtime reading.

130040.en: I knew you wouldn't balk at the last hurdle.

130041.en: It's your loss, the Labyrinth will now be closed forever to you.

130042.en: Those texts are going on the pyre, for your information. But thank you very much, the Empire is grateful for your efforts. The key to the Labyrinth is yours. You'll find the Labyrinth in the Aphi system. It's located pretty close to the sun, so bring your suntan lotion.

130043.en: Great work in your last mission.  But now it is time for the final attack, to completely eliminate the Amarr presence within the troublesome deadspace area in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  The sensors I had implanted onto your ship detected a gate leading towards their headquarters, within the room where you destroyed the stargate.  It is time for you to access this gate and confront the remainder of their forces.  I will again implant the sensors onto your ship, so expect me to contact you once you warp through the acceleration gate leading to their headquarters.

130045.en: Incredible job, {[character]player.name}.  I was afraid there for a minute that you might not be able to handle them, when you warped through the acceleration gate.  But you made it, and I'm proud of you.  Enjoy your reward!

130046.en:
Nice of you to drop by, {[character]player.name}. And what an uncanny coincidence...

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has a slight problem on its hands. One of our agents sent a certain mercenary on a very important courier mission to deliver an item of great value to our headquarters. This was a few weeks ago, and this mercenary never showed up at his destination. At first we thought he had simply run off with the goods, but upon further investigation that proved not to be the case. His ship had been destroyed, though, we received no transmissions from him, and we found clues at the site linking the crime to a certain pirate who also happens to work as a bounty hunter. I have no doubt that some pirate organization put him up to it, but that is of little importance compared to retrieving the item that was stolen.

Now we looked up this bounty hunter and we discovered something that will interest you, no doubt. What we found was that he is currently on an assignment to kill none other than you, {[character]player.name}. Who hired him we do not know, but considering your past I'm sure you have a few suspects in mind who might pull something like this off. Now that we have a mutual target, I thought, "Why not ask {[character]player.name} to take care of the job?" And then suddenly here you are.

By doing this assignment, you'll not only rid yourself of a rat who's on your tail, but you will retrieve the item that we're after. I'm sure you're willing to get the job done, eh? I'll upload the pirate scumbag's current location into your NeoCom; he's out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} hanging around a casino. He's a pretty tough nut to crack, I hear, so you may want to bring backup with you just in case.

130054.en: Alright, what is my first task?

130056.en: There were Mordu ships awaiting you?!  This is outrageous, those slimy worms actually went so far as to hire the Mordu's Legion for assistance.  For this they will pay dearly!  And I'm counting on you to make it happen, {[character]player.name}.  Get ready for your next assignment.

130058.en:
We have discovered a fleet of Legionnaires heading towards the rebel forces in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Apparently they have split themselves into 5 groups, and we want you to eliminate all of them. They must not be allowed to reach the militia base inside {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, that would seriously undermine any attack we attempt on their position there. Once you have destroyed all 5 groups, then return to me.

We've discovered their gathering point, which should simplify this mission quite a bit for you. You must fly to the gathering point and destroy all 5 groups of Legionnaires when they arrive.

130061.en: Excellent!  This should leave their base weak enough for us to launch a direct assault on it immediately.

130062.en:
Now comes a critical stage in our operation. We must assault the headquarters of the rebels, and destroy their pitiful forces. I want you to lead the assault, {[character]player.name}. Their base will be well guarded by filthy Mordu, but with your superior combat skill you should be able to take them out.

Also if you find any survivors, bring them back here for interrogation. We would also like to retrieve the leader of the traitors holed up at that base, for public execution. That should teach them a lesson they won't forget.

130097.en:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} recently sacked one of its employees after a routine inspection revealed a large amount of indecent pictures stored in his personal database.  Sadly, this ex-employee wasn't all too pleased with our 
decision, and has resorted to camping outside of our headquarters and harassing our customers.  Fortunately though, we dug up some old offenses this guy made and revealed them to the authorities, who promptly lowered his security rating quite a bit.  In effect, he's fair game.  Please warp over to the location on the bookmark I'm about to give you and squash this little pest.  I doubt he will survive for long, as some of our customers are 
heavily armed.  So hurry up and take him out if you want your reward.

130098.en:
I knew you were up to it. Now, the story behind this mission is actually rather complicated, but you just need to know the basics. The reason I'm telling you this at all is because I don't want you finding about this later and getting it into your head that I betrayed you, because I'd never do that *smile*. Anyway, two years ago one of the new recruits within our marketing department started to show an incredible amount of promise, making decisions that generated an enormous amount of revenue for us. Needless to say, he quickly rose up the ranks within our corporation as well as earning a place within the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} government, and we owe our recent successes largely to his 'efforts'.

However quickly some of us became suspicious, especially those within our ranks which were jealous of his success. After a lot of research and investigation, we came to the conclusion that he had a contact within the Guristas Pirates which was supplying him with sensitive information which they had acquired through illegal means. As you might know, these pirates are infamous within the Caldari territories, and have even spread to neighboring regions. For this reason we must not allow this to reach the ears of ANYONE affiliated with the authorities, or it will have dire consequences. I hope I have made myself perfectly clear on that matter. I expect your full discretion. I'll add more information to the mission details in your Opportunities interface once you get started. Good luck.

130099.en:
I have a job for you this time which I would not have given to just anybody. I know that I can trust you, your faithful service to me in the past has proven that. Now to cut the story short, what I need is a ship destroyed. But there is a 'slight' problem, which I'll get to. You see, this ship isn't just any old pirate ship, it contains a high ranking official within {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, who also happens to be a member within the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} government. This isn't a rescue mission, this is a destroy mission. But don't worry, this mission is completely confidential. If you're interested, then I'll give you more details, otherwise this conversation never happened. Just take note of the fact your target is very powerful, do not attempt this unless you have a powerful warship at your disposal, or friends.

The ship you are supposed to destroy is actually a Guristas Emissary vessel, which is used as a secret meeting place between the person which must be killed, and his Guristas contacts. You will probably also notice his own ship nearby, which may or may not be unmanned at the time. You must also destroy this vessel, whether your target is inside it or not, to make it look like he was ambushed by pirates. And take care of anyone else nearby, none may escape. I hope I have made myself clear.

Oh and please note, you can keep whatever you find in the wreckage of these ships, it is of no concern to us. We will of course reward you as well when you have finished the task. The bookmark I gave you will show the exact location of the meeting place so getting there shouldn't be a problem.

130100.en: I'm up to the job, and don't worry, you can trust me with keeping this under the table.

130101.en: Your problem has been solved.  Both the pirates and my primary target were destroyed.

130102.en: I understand.  Just don't tell anyone about what I said, you hear?

130103.en: Marvelous.  You really did good out there, and I am absolutely certain I can trust you with keeping quiet about this.  However, let this be an educated warning to you:  don't mess with the system, because in the end you WILL regret it!

130105.en: We have a rather nasty problem on our hands.  You see due to the nature of our business, we tend to make a lot of enemies.  Usually this is not a problem, but it seems we pissed off someone with money where his mouth is.  To get straight to the point, we have a bounty hunter on our tails.  To make matters worse, this happens to be an infamous bounty hunter who is NOT to be taken lightly.  I'm not sure who he is after, but it's probably someone within our ranks who isn't expenda ... err who is important.  I want you to head out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take care of this threat once and for all.

130201.en:
Recently, we started noticing an increased presence of Amarr military drones in the area. Our fears were just confirmed a few hours ago when one of our members stumbled upon a transport ship with an Amarr logo on its hull parked in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. A ship scan revealed a hoard of construction blocks in its cargo hold. This means they must be constructing something in the proximity, which is of course unacceptable. Their project must be stopped in its infancy at all costs. I want you to warp to a remote stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} which we believe the latest transport ship we spotted was intending to use. Wait for a few minutes until it arrives. But hurry before it's too late!

And remember, do not reveal your identity to anyone nearby, as we want to keep a lid on this operation. We do not want to ignite the spark of a full fledged war with the Empire.

You have the full authority of the government to shoot to kill, we do not expect any prisoners. And please do not confuse these low-lifes to the legit slave-users we sometimes do business with. 130244.en:
Ok, you're now all set to speak with Aviekko. You'll probably find her at her desk in the Echelon Entertainment Development Studio in Autama. And don't forget to bring your graduation certificate when you pay her a visit!

If you forget the location of this agent, you can always look it up by opening the 'show info' window for the graduation certificate.

130246.en: I was sent to speak with you, Aviekko, and I have this certificate to prove it.

130247.en: Ah, so you're a qualified pilot eh.  I have some work for you after all.  Just give me a minute to go over my files, I'll have something for you to do in a jiffy ...

130248.en: Ok, show me the certificate.  You better not be pulling my leg ...

130250.en:
Before you begin I should get you acquainted with my current assignment. I am Aviekko Ta, agent of Atoa Issa. I am one of many agents which were dispatched by Atoa to search for leads of the missing relics, which were stolen from the 13 Achur temples. So far I've had little luck, but I believe my venture in hiring graduates from the prominent aerospace aviation schools, like yourself, will pay off in the long run.

Your first task is to retrieve a few starmaps of mine from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}. I just ordered them from our archives on our home-planet Achura in Saisio. They should lead us Kikko Roisen, who I've suspected for quite some time to have been involved with the infamous heist.

Anyway, get going. I need those starmaps asap.

Anyway, get going. I need those starmaps asap.

130252.en: Excellent.  I'll have a look at these starmaps immediately and compare them to the data I already have about Kikko.  I'll let you know when I've found something ...

130255.en:
The sacred pieces believed to be from the Rod of the Creator were stolen from under the watchful gaze of the Achur religious order. This any true Achur would know. The State has pledged enormous resources to tracking down the thieves. But even so the Elder Visionaries of Achura are not satisfied. They do not trust the State government, and they cannot sit idly by as their religion is ridiculed for its failure to protect the icons of its faith.

And so the Celestial Imperative was devised. Atoa Issa, a proud Achur himself, took leave of his prominent position within the Caldari Navy to oversee the search for the scoundrels who dared insult the Achur religion and people of Achura. By his side stands Seer Chakai Potan, representative of the temples of Achura. Together they control the enormous wealth the Achur government and the temples have supplied to fund this investigation. And to quote Atoa, 'no stone shall remain unturned, no world shall elude our probing gaze. I vow to you, people of Achura, that I will spend every fiber of my existance from here after to track down these vile, wretched thieves and restore the honor of our people!'

130256.en:
These starmaps are indeed interesting. They point to virtually hundreds of locations in Autama where Kikko has been sighted. Visionary Atahari has had him tracked ever since his bungled burglary attempt at the temple a few years ago, so that should come as no surprise. But I've managed to narrow down these locations to 3 settlements, where he has been spotted very frequently. These are the most likely locations where we will find him.

I truly hope he hasn't left the system, but at this stage we can only cross our fingers. The mercenary tracking Kikko on Atahari's command disappeared when he tried to confront Kikko on my behalf, and that may have triggered him to think about relocating himself. Fortunately rumor still has it that he hasn't left Autama, but you never can be too sure.

Your first task is to investigate a small settlement next to the ruins of an old Caldari station. It's been rumored to be inhabited by pirates in league with the Guristas organization. You might encounter some resistance when you start poking your nose around there, but I'm sure you can take care of it.

Your goal is to find any trace of Kikko. If you find nothing, then return back to me and we'll continue the search.

130262.en: So you found nothing?  Well, at least we've narrowed down the search a bit.  Let's continue on.

130263.en:
Your second objective is to storm a habitation module in Autama where Kikko Roisen has been seen multiple times. If you find him inside, then bring him to me. Either way, report back to me immediately after the operation has finished.

Again you will receive a bookmark into your NeoCom, so this should be simple enough. There may be guards there, so be prepared for a fight.

130267.en:
Luck has not been on our side so far, {[character]player.name}. And I'm becoming less convinced we will ever find Kikko *sigh*. The third hotspot which I want you to investigate is a bit different from the last two. It's a small mining colony situated at Autama VII's moon. I won't give you a bookmark this time, as you should find it very easily on any standard map of Autama.

Search the place thoroughly. If you can't find Kikko there, then I don't know what to do.

130270.en: Incredible!  You did it!  You found Kikko!  I'll get to analyzing the data you brought back immediately, if it's what I think it is then we finally have a lead on the missing Achur relics!

130272.en: Warp to Autama VII – Moon 1 and find the mining colony there.  See if it leads you to Kikko.

130274.en: Ok ok, you can have the damn data chip.  I was going to sell it to her anyway, but since it's my life I'm bargaining for then just take it!  I've had it with trying to escape that wretch, even the Guristas can't save me.  Now please leave me alone.

130275.en: If you're not here to kill me, then do you mind sparing my life?  Kill the Guristas guards here if you want, take the loot, just don't kill me.

130276.en: If you're not here to kill me, then do you mind sparing my life?  Kill the Guristas guards here if you want, take the loot, just don't kill me.

130277.en: I found this data sheet in your stash, Kikko.  It has some pretty incriminating evidence about your dealings with the Guristas organization.  Either cough up whatever you're hiding, or I'll take this straight to the authorities.

130278.en: So, what brings you to such a dangerous place?  The Guristas are not to be trifled with ...

130279.en: Well, erm, they told me I'd be safe if I gave them access codes to some corporation hangars at the Echelon Entertainment station here in Autama.  Hey wait, you aren't recording this are you? ...

130280.en: You sure you don't have any work for me?

130281.en:
Hmmm, actually there might be something you can help me with. My corporation, Echelon Entertainment, has a long standing rivalry with Nugoeihuvi Corporation. We're competitors in the entertainment industry, and it always gives you an edge if you know what your adversaries are planning.

It so happens that I know of the location of a hidden Nugoeihuvi station in Autama. It's called Station Yxtara, and I'll supply you with a bookmark to it. What I want you to do is retreive the access codes I need to break into their central computer mainframe inside Yxtara. And I believe that I know of a person who has those access codes and should in fact be orbiting around a lookout post next to the station.

His name is Havatiah Kiin and he's the captain of Yxtara's security. He normally flies a condor right outside of the station, and should be an easy target. Now considering the station is supposed to be hidden, I'm quite confident that the station manager will want to keep it that way, hence I doubt they will call in CONCORD. However Nugoeihuvi will have their own guards defending the station. So don't say I didn't warn you!

130299.en: Since you are so eager to work for me, {[character]player.name}, I would like to start off our relationship by explaining a few critical details.

130300.en:
I am Avrue Auz, agent of Beizan Picholen. I came to Chandeille (Lirsautton V) eight years ago, during the height of the Picholen-Auboure family feud. Deni Picholen hired me as Beizan's secretary and financial manager. The Picholen family is quite wealthy, having long owned a number of franchises connected with Kaalakiota and their wares.

Anyway, the feud was quite draining on the Picholens, especially their wallet. But the biggest disaster the family had ever faced came only a few years ago. It was a dreadfully cold afternoon during the height of the Chabash winter on Chandeille when I received the news that a Picholen industrial had been caught by planetary security forces, trying to smuggle a troop of slaves and illegal combat boosters into Namin City. Speculation had it that the slaves were to be used as cheap manpower in a secret military operation directed against Auboure, named after its ancient ruling family.

To me, this siezure of assets was bad enough, but to make matters far worse, my employer, Beizan, was directly implicated in the deal, for the industrial smuggling the contraband had been rented in his name. It was a debacle. Kaalakiota canceled their multi-million ISK deal with Picholen, and the Governor of Chandeille placed a huge fine on the family that has basically crippled its financial status. In other words, the Picholens lost everything other than their name and sovereignty over Namin City. Most of their lands were confiscated, as well as their overseas bank accounts. I'm a bit surprised you haven't heard this story, in fact; it was all over the Federation media at the time.

But anyway, to cut the story short, Beizan was imprisoned in Pinmouth, an infamous Federation prison facility in Lirsautton, and resides there still. It is my firm belief, however, that Beizan is really innocent, and that is why I sent for someone like you.

130302.en:
Your first task is to raid a merchant operating a small trading hub in Meves. He is known to have dealings with the Auboure family; he was in fact their first contact when they started expanding their trade relations outside of Lirsautton to compete with the Picholens. It is my firm belief that the Auboures have something to do with the smuggling incident that resulted in Beizan's arrest ― yes, I believe he was framed.

The merchant's name is Kelmiler Delbone. Interrogate him for me, find a way to make him reveal what he knows about the incident. Once you have something, report back to me.

130303.en: These documents will have to do.  Let's see if we can find anything in here that connects Kelmiler to the crime.  One minute ...

130304.en: So what is it I need to know?

Interrogate him for me; find a way to make him reveal what he knows about the incident that resulted in Beizan's arrest. Once you have something, report back to me.

130306.en:
The documents you retrieved reveal nothing about the industrial. However, what interests me is that Kelmiler appears to have sold a large number of illegal boosters to a member of FedMart, located in Jel. Interestingly, these boosters are identical to the ones found inside the industrial that was caught by the planetary security forces on Chandeille. Yes, a very interesting find indeed.

I want you to fly to the FedMart station in Jel. I have an acquaintance there who will supply me with records of transactions at that station. Perhaps they will lead us to whoever bought those boosters from Kelmiler Delbone.

130307.en: Fly to the FedMart station in Jel and return with records of FedMart transactions at that station. Perhaps they will lead us to whoever bought those illegal boosters from Kelmiler Delbone.

130308.en:
Thank you. Alright, let's see... Hm. Interesting. Hmmm. Oh, my goodness! These records explicitly mention a man by the name of ... Mamo! No, surely it can't be. Mamo Guerre!? The Mamo Guerre? Amazing, even if this clue turns out to be a dead end. At the very least, we have uncovered evidence of criminal activity on one of the most powerful men in {[location]agentRegionID.name}.

Good work, {[character]player.name}. Very good work!

130310.en: I'd like you to pay Mamo Guerre a visit near the moon of Lirsautton VI. See if you can scrounge up evidence linking him with the incident Beizan's rotting in jail for.

130311.en: I'd like you to pay Mamo Guerre a visit. You might find him near the moon of Lirsautton VI; my sources claim that he frequents that place. See if you can scrounge up evidence linking him with the incident Beizan's rotting in jail for. If Mamo's playing any part of this ... why, I'll drag his name so far through the dirt he'll move to Fountain and live as a hermit. But let's give him something Beizan certainly could have used during his trial ― the luxury of being innocent until proven guilty.

130312.en: Aha! According to this message, Eilard Ansti purchased the boosters from Mamo Guerre. Eilard is a long-time associate of the Auboure family. Now I think we're finally getting somewhere...

130313.en: I don't have time for simpletons.  Either leave me be or show me a good reason why I should waste my time on you ...

130314.en: I was sent to speak with you, Mamo.  Do you have a minute?

130315.en: Find something of interest to Mamo Guerre ... Avrue Auz might have something in mind.

130316.en:
Ok, you have my attention. But don't think for a moment that your little plan has any chance of success. In these parts, I am practically above the law. You can go right ahead and report your findings to the authorities, little good it will do you ...

But before you leave, you might want to consider a proposition I have. If you do a certain job for me, then I will give you what you seek. The choice is yours.

130319.en: I believe this might interest you ...

130320.en:
So let me get this straight. You want me to tell you what I did with the boosters that I supposedly bought through my connections in FedMart? No problem, as long as you do something for me. You rub my back, I rub yours.

There is a certain commodity I am after, which is extremely hard to acquire. It's virtually undetectable with the current sensors used by the customs officials, and is highly illegal if you get my drift. It so happens that I know where a few units of this commodity are stashed. In fact I've configured the gateway located behind my ship to send you there. It's being guarded of course, but that's why I need you.

Bring me what I need, and I'll give you the information you've been looking for.

Just a word of advice before you leave, the spot you're about to warp to is located in a phenomenon we call deadspace. Since we are also currently located inside deadspace, you won't be able to warp directly back here without the use of an acceleration gate. Instead you'll have to warp outside of the deadspace bubble and then back to me.

130322.en: Good job.  Now for the information Avrue Auz was after, one moment.

130323.en: I have the 'commodity' you are after, now cough up the info.

130325.en:
Don't be so hasty, {[character]player.name}. There's always a catch you know. All you have to do is transport the commodity to the FedMart storage facility in Jel. I need it analyzed there in our lab, plus you'll make a good test dummy to see if it actually works against the customs officials at the stargates.

Once the item is in your hangar there, then I will reward you with the information you seek. And I do hope you'll never show your face in my territory again after this is over, comprende?

130327.en: So, what's the deal?  You said you'd cough up the info after I got you the crash ...

130328.en: I'll do what you ask, but if you try and play me like that again I'll ...

130329.en: Alright, here you go.  Bring this data chip to Avrue, it will explain everything I know about her situation.

130330.en: I'd like you to bring Eilard Ansti here; he must know something about the crime, and it's essential that we acquire this information. You may use any means necessary. I will supply you with a bookmark to Ansti's whereabouts within a deadspace pocket in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. You'll have to navigate through a few checkpoints due to the warp disruption, but I'm sure you can "convince" the guards to let you through...

130331.en:
Ok, it's time to pay Eilard Ansti a visit. I'd like you to bring him here; I really need to have a ... chat with him. He must know something about the crime, and it's essential that we acquire this information. You may use any means necessary ― you'll receive a sizable reward for your efforts, of course, and I'll see to it that the authorities don't get involved.

I will supply you with a bookmark to Ansti's whereabouts. Fortunately for us, he owns a small piece of space here in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, set within a deadspace pocket. You'll have to navigate through a few checkpoints due to the warp disruption, but I'm sure you can "convince" the guards to let you through...

I won't pull any punches here, {[character]player.name}. This may be quite dangerous. Good luck.

130332.en:
You found Serpentis there along with Eilard's corpse?! Oh, my. It's getting very hot in here, suddenly, don't you find...? Ahem.

Give me a few minutes while I'll have the computer in our medlab perform a quick scan of Eilard's remains.

130333.en: I think we can assume Govarde is alive until we receive evidence to prove otherwise: The Navy database has no record of his death. I have a bookmark that should lead you to a luxury resort in Lirsautton where Govarde is known to hang out. I want you to snoop around and search for any clues that might lead us to him.

130334.en:
The data you retrieved revealed that this Govarde is indeed a member of the Serpentis organization and is wanted by CONCORD for a number of offenses. He was last seen in Lirsautton, which would explain his meeting here with Eilard. Now we can only hope that he wasn't one of the Serpentis you killed during your retrieval of Eilard's corpse, but I think we can assume Govarde is alive until we receive evidence to prove otherwise: The Navy database has no record of his death.

I have a bookmark that should lead you to a luxury resort in Lirsautton that has been under investigation for quite some time as a secret drug-manufacturing op. Not yet proven, of course, but the interesting part is that Govarde has been sighted there frequently by civilians staying at the resort. I want you to snoop around and search for any clues that might lead us to him.

130335.en: So, what did you find out?

130336.en: Pay a visit to {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} and pick up a package for me from an acquaintance of mine who's Navy data technician there.

130337.en:
The results of the autopsy scan show that Eilard was killed by a blaster at close range, most likely by the Serpentis goons who were waiting for you when you arrived. However, I did find an interesting bit of data in his ComPlant. The Serpentis probably hadn't gotten to extracting it when you showed up, so I was able to recover his datajournal entries.

Most of the information was useless (if mildly entertaining...), but one very recent bit of mem-script reads, "Meet Govarde at 1800h." Now, I might be reaching a little here, but perhaps this "Govarde" was one of the Serpentis you killed earlier? Maybe he was the person Eilard was due to meet? Certainly a difficult theory to prove, but I have an idea.

I want you to pay a visit to {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} and pick up a package from a Navy data technician there. The records are off limits to non-Navy personnel, for they contain extensive data on the Serpentis, but I have a contact working there who should be able to do the research for me. He owes me one, and this is as good a time as any to pay up.

130338.en: Excellent.  One minute while I take a look at this data ...

130339.en: What's the word from the medical lab?

130341.en:
The Khanid Insurgency are rebels who want to topple the Khanid government and install one that'd be more inclined to start a war with the Amarr. They are led by an old, crazed hag going by the name of Deza Yobili. She claims to have been 'wronged' by the Khanid Monarchy, because as part of an exchange deal we handed her husband to the Amarr authorities in return for a group of Khanid citizens that had been illegally held in Amarr prisons. Her husband was nothing more than a murderer, and yet some misguided souls within the Kingdom view him as a martyr. It's a rather sad ordeal, all in all.

We are doing everything we can to stop Deza and her cronies, but she keeps eluding our grasp. And their numbers refuse to drop, which is why we have started taking extra measures to quell this uprising attempt before it gets out of hand.

Now here is where you come in. One of my servants, Ziona Koon, went missing while she was posing as a student for the Royal Amarr Institute in Emrayur. The last I heard of her she was on to something. She left a report in her quarters in Emrayur, and I would like to retrieve that report to figure out what happened to her. Please retrieve this report for me.

130343.en: Excellent.  Please wait a minute while I run over the report ...

130347.en:
The Khanid zealot, Deza Yobili, nicknamed ‘the black widow', runs a guerilla army whose aim is to enact a coup against the current regime. She has captured the hearts of many hardline Khanids due to her heart-wrenching story. Her husband, Jabil Yobili and 3 of her sons were executed by Amarr Imperial forces after they had been handed over by the Khanid Navy as a part of an exchange deal for Khanid POWs. Jabil and his sons had been accused by the Empire of slaughtering many Amarrian citizens during an insurgency in Gousoviba.

Deza's youngest son, Abarak Yobili, was imprisoned by the Khanid government for ‘causing civil unrest', when he led a demonstration against the newly rejuvenated Khanid – Amarr alliance.

Deza is the figurehead in a persistent movement to oust the current monarch of the Khanid Kingdom, and to sever their ties with the Empire once more. They are still greatly outnumbered and opposed by the majority of the Khanid nobility, but even so they are considered a threat and the Khanid monarch is eager to eradicate this thorn from his side.

130348.en: So, have you finished reading the report?

130349.en:
I've briefly skimmed over it. The report mentions that Ziona had found a suspicious fellow who claimed to offer her a job inside the Khanid Kingdom. He told her to meet her at a rendezvous point in Emrayur, where he would go over the details. She was to bring all of her credentials along with her. This certainly sounds like an undercover operation of some sort. Maybe we've hit the jackpot!

I want you to fly to Emrayur and investigate the rendezvous point. I am afraid something may have happened to Ziona, since she hasn't been in contact with me for many days. Perhaps she left some clues as to where they took her.

130351.en: You brought back a Khanid marine I see.  The rookie fighters that attacked you must have been some of the new recruits this rogue agent has been gathering.  Well, at least we don't need to worry about them in the future.

130352.en:
Turn out that the marine has certain weaknesses, and has received very little anti-interrogation training. The clock is ticking, but there may be a way for us to extract data from him in a rather more humane way than I had originally intended.

I'd like you to look for some ... helpful products on the market, as I haven't the time to see to those matters. Think of it as some time off from the more dangerous tasks that I have in store for you.

130355.en:
I think I've found our lead. According to the prisoner, the man we're after is Mamin Choonka. He runs a diner in Ashab, somewhere near the moon of Ashab II. It offers a hefty discount to students of the academy, hence it's quite popular among their ranks.

I want you to pay him a visit. But don't go in with guns flaring, I want you to get to know him. Tell him you just graduated from the academy, and let's hope he tries to convert you to his cause. If all goes well, he will offer you a place within the Khanid insurgency. Perhaps that will lead us to one of their bases, or even better Deza Yobili.

It's hard to pin Choonka down, so I won't give you a bookmark. Instead, I want you to fly to his base at the moon of Ashab II and find him on your own. I'm sure you won't have any trouble.

I think I've found our lead. According to the prisoner, the man we're after is Mamin Choonka. He runs a diner in Ashab, at the moon of Ashab II to be exact. It offers a hefty discount to students of the academy, hence it's quite popular among their ranks.

I want you to pay him a visit. But don't go in with guns flaring, I want you to get to know him. Tell him you just graduated from the academy, and let's hope he tries to convert you to his cause. 130357.en: Amazing!  This operation has gone more smoothly than I had expected, even in my wildest dreams.  I will report back to the Royal Family immediately, but before I leave I have one more task to give you.

130359.en: Find Mamin Choonka at his diner in Ashab, near the warp-in point of Ashab II's moon.  See if you can acquire the coordinates to the Khanid insurgency from him.

130360.en: I heard you had work available.  Was my source correct?

130361.en: Now that depends entirely upon the source, {[character]player.name}. But yes, I might have something available. It depends on whether you're willing to risk your neck or not. My assignments involve fighting ... lots of it. If you're looking for something more on the lines of dung-hauling, I suggest you look elsewhere.

130362.en: Then I am definitely what you're looking for. I am well prepared for combat.

130363.en: Ah, I was hoping you had something safe and easy. I'll have to decline.

130364.en: Your first job involves taking on a group of rogue drones that have for some god-forsaken reason decided to infest my storage facility in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. Destroy all of them, and then report back to me.

130365.en: Your first job involves taking on a group of rogue drones that have for some god-forsaken reason decided to infest my storage facility in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. Destroy all of them, and then report back to me.

130366.en: A job well done, {[character]player.name}.  Take your reward, but don't leave yet.  I have more tasks in store for you.

130367.en:
You did well against artificial intelligence, I'll give you that. But can you cut it against living opponents? Your next assignment is to destroy a pirate convoy carrying illegal goods into {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. You might ask, "how did you find out about this convoy?" The answer is that I ordered the goods myself. Through a contact, of course ― I would never reveal my true identity to those bastards.

Destroy the convoy, and bring the database from one of the ships to me if you manage to find one intact. I need to present it to the authorities so that we might trace their travel route to its origin and eliminate their drug factory for good.

130369.en: Your third and final mission for me is to eliminate a group of rogue Khanid pilots in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. I entrusted them with some very confidential information, and they've repaid my trust by trying to blackmail me. Once you've reduced their ships to slag, report back to me. But don't forget to search the wreckage of their ships just incase they leave something behind, such as notes or any data concerning me. I don't want the authorities to trace their deaths back to me. That would cause some, er, unfortunate complications.

130371.en: The Khanid pilots are no more, {[character]agentID.name}.

130372.en: Magnificent!! You passed the test, {[character]player.name}. Nice work. Not only have you shown that you can handle yourself in combat, but you've also proven yourself to be reliable under ... "difficult" circumstances. I now truly believe I can trust you.

130375.en: Yes, in fact. One last errand for you, {[character]player.name}. I'd like you to pick up some potential new recruits from the academy in Chaven. Once that has been completed, I'd like you to meet a very special person in the Khanid Kingdom. You'll find her at the coordinates listed in this data disc. Once she has gotten to know you better, you might have a very promising career ahead of you within the ranks of the Khanid Traditionalist Movement.

130377.en: You've done well, {[character]player.name}. I think you'll fit into our ranks very nicely. But I'm afraid I've nothing more to offer you, so I must bid you fare well. Good luck in the future.

130378.en: Anything else you need me to do, {[character]agentID.name}?

130379.en:
I've had a sinking suspicion for quite some time now that I'm being followed. I kept seeing the same mysterious man behind the corner whenever I turned my head. It was getting quite antagonizing. I work for the Khanid secret-service, so I notice these things quite well ...

Anyway I had the man's ship bugged, and we tracked him down to guess where ... Mamin Choonka's diner. Obviously Choonka has somehow gotten a hold of my identity, and probably wants me killed. I suspect they will strike after I leave the station. Which leaves me in a sort of a dilemma, as I have to meet with my superiors soon for a meeting in Khanid space.

To make things easier for me, I would like you to take care of these pests. That should clear the way for me to leave the station for a while. I will give you the exact coordinates for their ships, as we still have one of them bugged.

130381.en: Excellent.  You've done well, {[character]player.name}.  I'll definitely recommend you to his Highness.  Take care!

130383.en: The colleague that I mentioned, Arizam Gimit, requires your graduation certificate before he'll offer you work.  I suppose you've left it behind at your hangar somewhere?  If not I can easily have a copy of it made on {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}.  Just pick it up there and bring it to me.  Once I've signed it then you're all set to speak with Arizam.

130387.en: Ah, so you're a qualified pilot eh.  I have some work for you after all.  Just give me a minute to go over my files, I'll have something for you to do in a jiffy ...

130390.en: I was sent to speak with you, Pinala, and I have this certificate to prove it.

130391.en: Ah, so you're a qualified pilot eh.  I have some work for you after all.  Just give me a minute to go over my files, I'll have something for you to do in a jiffy ...

130396.en:
Ok, you're now all set to speak with Pinala Adala. You'll probably find her at her desk in the Eram IX - Moon 4 - Sebiestor tribe Bureau. And don't forget to bring your graduation certificate when you pay her a visit!

If you forget the location of this agent, you can always look it up by opening the 'show info' window for the graduation certificate.

130400.en: I have an important job for you, {[character]player.name}.  Because of your good standing and the fact you have successfully completed a number of missions for {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} we have decided you are worth the trust of a very important courier job. It entails bringing a large cargo of transaction and salary logs to this station from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} where they have been stored for the last few weeks for a routine inspection by the authorities.  This data holds information of sensitive nature on our recent business dealings, earnings and expenses and wages that we pay our staff members.  Under no circumstances may any of these reports be lost, or worse yet fall into the wrong hands.  Pirates have a tendency to want this information so they can sell it to our rivals.  They used to have easy access to this information by hacking our transmission calls, but now that we send these reports via freight this is no longer as serious of a problem.  I trust you on this, {[character]player.name}, don't let me down.

130403.en: Thank you. Be careful out there, those logs must not fall into the wrong hands.

130405.en: I have an important job for you, {[character]player.name}.  Because of your good standing and the fact you have successfully completed a number of missions for {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} we have decided you are worth the trust of a very important courier job. It entails bringing a large cargo of transaction and salary logs to this station from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} where they have been stored for the last few weeks for a routine inspection by the authorities.  This data holds information of sensitive nature on our recent business dealings, earnings and expenses and wages that we pay our staff members.  Under no circumstances may any of these reports be lost, or worse yet fall into the wrong hands.  Pirates have a tendency to want this information so they can sell it to our rivals.  They used to have easy access to this information by hacking our transmission calls, but now that we send these reports via freight this is no longer as serious of a problem.  I trust you on this, {[character]player.name}, don't let me down.

130406.en: I am very disappointed in you.  This failure might result in catastrophic consequences, should the logs you were supposed to transfer fall into the wrong hands.  If this happens I will hold you fully responsible.

130407.en: Thank you. Be careful out there, those logs must not fall into the wrong hands.

130432.en: The Republic bastards just launched a daring but foolhardy attack on our outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They killed every man, woman and child residing there, taking no prisoners. This was probably a retaliatory attack after we killed one of their commanders, but it matters not. We must intercept them before it's too late. I have reliable information that the leader of this attack was none other than Warlord Ixon Kruz, so you will undoubtedly have a very tough fight on your hands. Prepare yourself well, but don't tarry too long or you won't get there in time!

130434.en:
We need you for a very important assassination mission, {[character]player.name}. The Caldari State military has set up a base in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, intent on flushing out pirate activity here. We cannot afford to launch a full scale attack on it at the moment, so we have been forced to resort to scare tactics to drive them away. We planned to assassinate their commander, who is their highest-ranking official at the military outpost, but so fair all of our attempts have been foiled. You are our last hope, {[character]player.name}.

Now is the perfect time to undertake this mission. We know that the Commander is traveling through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} at this very moment, and we can supply you a bookmark to his approximate location. Should you strike immediately, then you may catch them by surprise. He is traveling with a small troop from his armada occupying the military base, so the fight may be difficult for you if you go in alone.

130436.en:
That blasted priest, Karmone Tizmer, is at it again. He has set up base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and is busily trying to convert and kill our brethen there in the name of his false religion. With him are a troop of Amarr ships, being piloted by Cult of Catechization activists. We need someone competent to take them out of business before they cause too much damage. You are the perfect man for the job, {[character]player.name}.

But do not take this mission too lightly. They are quite dangerous, and their ships are of the highest quality. You will probably need backup for this one.

130440.en: Now that I know you have the skills to pull through, it's time to test your loyalty.  So I'll get straight to the point.  I work for a Matar citizen, who wishes to remain anonymous, who was wronged by a certain Vherokior shaman.  My client wants revenge, and this requires the capture of this Vherokior individual.  If you don't have the guts to take part in this endeavor, then I suggest you leave now.

130441.en: So, what do you need me for?

130442.en: I'm up for the job, as long as it doesn't involve breaking the law.

130443.en:
Oh don't worry about that, you won't be breaking any laws. Or in other words, no one will know that you are breaking any laws. We dug up some dirt on the shaman in question, and soon he will be a wanted man in the Republic. We won't reveal it to the authorities until we have him though, just to make sure we get there before the police do. We need him alive, he's of no use to us dead.

Once our allegations of him are proven, he will be executed. It will matter little to the authorities if we do the honors for them. Therefore you have nothing to fear.

Now for your task, I want you to apprehend a member of the Angel Cartel. The Cartel is the biggest criminal organization in the known universe, so finding a few of their members shouldn't be very difficult. I'll even upload a bookmark to one of their hideouts for you, you can view it in the mission details in your Opportunities interface.

130444.en: Warp to the coordinates that Pinala gave you, recorded inside the mission details in your Opportunities interface.  Destroy the Angel Cartel ships at their hideout and capture one of their pilots from the ejected container (if one survives).  Bring this person back to your agent, as long as the captive is still alive.

130445.en: Here is the prisoner you asked for.

130446.en: Excellent!  He will do nicely.  But there's more to be done, so stick around.

130448.en:
The Brutor, Hnarlir Afer, has been an outcast from his home-world, Matar, ever since his Voluval ritual. The mark it left behind was so shameful even his loving father disowned him. He moved to the Gallente Federation, where hardly anyone recognized the mark or paid it any attention. There he began a life of a mercenary, having been bred as a space pilot by his military veteran father.

He quickly made a name for himself, before becoming a freelancer. Using the wealth he garnered from that profession, he started up his own corporation, The Markoni Dragons. It has been quite successful, earning Hnarlir a small fortune.

But even with his change of fortune, Hnarlir greatly misses his homeworld. He desperately wants to return and reclaim a position within his nation of birth. But he dares not return with the mark on his cheek as visible as ever. His family has suffered enough shame on his behalf already.

Yet Hnarlir still has hope. Hope that his ‘condition' can finally be modified. Even though it goes against everything the Minmatar consider holy, Hnarlir is just desperate, and wealthy, enough to pull it off. He wants to learn the method which the Vheriokor shamans use to perform the Voluval ritual and modify the mark so that it no longer resembles the symbol of the Ammatar Mandate.

130449.en: Now I would like you to drop off these reports I have to the Vherokior Bureau in Gelfiven.  An associate of mine will retrieve it from the hangar there.  These reports and the Angel Cartel prisoner you brought me will be enough to convince any jury of the Vherokior shaman's guilt.  That should set us up nicely for capturing him.

130450.en: Now I would like you to drop off these reports I have to the Vherokior Bureau in Gelfiven.  An associate of mine will retrieve it from the hangar there.  These reports and the Angel Cartel prisoner you brought me will be enough to convince any jury of the Vherokior shaman's guilt.  That should set us up nicely for capturing him.

130453.en: This sounds a bit too suspicious to me.  I'm out.

130455.en: Bah, I knew you didn't have it in you.  Get lost then, bud.

130457.en:
Before we make our attempt at capturing Logut Akell, the Vherokior shaman I was referring to earlier, we need to find him. He is currently meditating somewhere in Eram, but I haven't been able to track him down. If you didn't know, this meditation process of the Vherokior shamans can take months or even years, and frankly I'd rather not wait that long.

There is one link to Logut that I haven't pursued ... yet. His name is Matique Karani, and he's an associate of Loguts. I want you to pay Matique a visit and force him to reveal the whereabouts of Logut. Use any means necessary.

Oh and you'll probably have to deal with a few guards Matique hired. If it weren't for them, I'd have done the dirty work myself a long time ago.

130459.en: So he's at one of Eram IV's moons eh?  I hope you 'took care of Matique' in your last mission, otherwise I'm afraid he may have notified Logut about our plans already.  But either way we can't waste any more time, it's time to finish what we started.

130462.en: Well, what are you waiting for then?

130464.en: I already told you, go get Logut!  Matique said he was located near one of the moons of Eram IV, so go get him!  Now!

130465.en: Great work!  My men are taking care of his 'accommodations' as we speak.  You'll be rewarded well for your efforts, of course.

130468.en: I'm tired of your insults, Pinala, go find someone else to do your dirty work.

130469.en: I need to have a chat with Logut Akell.  It's personal.

130470.en: I'm sorry but he explicitly told me to prevent anyone from disturbing him today.  Maybe some other time?

130471.en: No, you either hand him over now or I blow this place up.

130472.en: Right-e-o, I'm sorry to disturb you.  Silly me.

130473.en: Obtain something of importance to Logut, to force him to come with you.  A wise choice would be to use the gateway beneath Logut's abode, perhaps it leads to somewhere interesting.  The key to the gateway must be around here somewhere ... I suspect a Data Analyzer may come in useful.

130474.en: How dare you!?  I will not 'hand him over', and I am perfectly fine with laying down my life for Logut.  We also have a very nice security system in place, so I'd think twice about attacking our home or trying to sneak in ...

130475.en: I have someone here with me that might 'interest' Logut ...

130476.en:
No, this cannot be! Touch a strand of hair on Dari's head and we'll have the Republic Fleet so far up your ass they'll hear your screams on Amarr Prime. But I will speak to Logut, as long as Dari is unharmed.

*long pause*

Logut has agreed to your terms, he will cooperate as long as Dari remains safe with me. He would do anything for his daughter, even surrender to treasonous scoundrels like yourself. But be warned, if he is not returned safe and sound within the month, we will contact the Minmatar secret service and they will hunt you down like the dog you are. Be-gone!¨

130479.en: The key to the gateway is hidden inside the blasted neon sign near Logut's Abode, so bring along a Data Analyzer.

130480.en: Actually, I was sent here by a person named Pinala Adala.  I was supposed to kidnap Logut, but I've had a change of heart.

130481.en:
Ah, is that so? I will relay this information to Logut immediately, one minute ...

*long pause*

130483.en: Sorry but I don't have time to wait for you, I have business elsewhere.

130484.en:
I have spoken with Logut. He says that he will come with you under the pretense that you have 'kidnapped' him for Pinala. He will be wearing a bug attached to his garments, which will send his exact coordinates to me. I will then inform the government of his kidnapper's location, and hopefully they'll be taken care of by the Republic Fleet.

However before he can commit himself to such a dangerous task, he wants you to do him a favor. His daughter, Dari Akell, lost her husband to the Angel Cartel. He was a miner, working as a contractor in Elgoi for Core Complexion inc, when a gang of Cartel thugs struck. They had threatened to 'cause grievous harm' to the mining operation if the foreman would neglect to pay them tribute, but he had refused. So they made an example of some of his subordinates, including Dari's husband. The Cartel got what they wanted, and Logut's son-in-law is now dead.

Needless to say, Logut wants revenge. I will supply you with a bookmark to the mining operation where Dari's husband was stationed, a few Angel goons should be located nearby. Destroy them. Do not return until this task has been accomplished.

130486.en: Alright, Logut will see you now.  Take him to Pinala, we will take care of the rest.  Fare well.

130487.en: I have done what you asked, Hlebnar.

130488.en: As your final task for me, I would like you to help with delivering the reports of our success to Hnarlir Afer.  His agent in Eystur will pick them up and deliver them the rest of the way.  Hnarlir is a very secretive man, and would not want his whereabouts known to just anyone, even a trusted accomplice such as yourself.  Good luck.

130538.en:
We've spotted an unauthorized Guristas personnel transport ship flying through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Cargo scanners revealed a load of militants on board, no doubt a part of a ground force intended to strike a target near here. We don't know where they are headed or what they're up to, but we definitely want to find out. I request that you intercept the transport and capture the men on board. Bring them back to us for questioning.

We believe the escort team is split up into a few groups. If you strike fast and hard, you'll probably avoid getting swarmed by them all at once. Just keep a look out for any stray ships, we don't want them escaping back to their homebase to report the incident.

Our spies discovered that a few convoys of Blood Raider ships carrying a heap load of viral agents are heading to one of the planets in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, with the intention of carrying out a biological attack on the populace! They must not be allowed to release the biohazard into the planet's atmosphere! I desperately need you to head over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and intercept the convoys.

Be careful though, we suspect that they have an interceptor or two guarding the convoys as well as other nasties. But I'm sure that's no problem for a seasoned pilot like yourself.

Our convoys have been attacked, as well as some outlying outposts; they seem to be intent on causing as much damage as possible. I'd like you to take care of them as quickly as possible. And be aware that they may not all be gathered together when you arrive... if so, you will be able to pick them off as they warp in to the rendezvous point.

130627.en: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}.

130628.en: It appears that the Federation Navy has been gathering en masse inside {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}.  Obviously they have been trying to keep a low profile, as they have split their armada into multiple groups.  But nonetheless my superiors are extremely nervous at these tidings.  We'd like you to remove their presence from {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} for good, before they manage to gather enough ships here to launch a massive offensive against one of our strongholds.  I'll supply you with the bookmarks that you need to find them.  Just remember, do not let them know under any circumstances who you are working for, we do not want to receive a retribution attack should you fail.

They are using some sort of scrambling device to deactivate our sentry guns as well.  We request that you gather a group of battle-hardened pilots and take them on.  If you don't then I'm afraid we'll have to negotiate our way out of this or keep our fingers crossed that backup arrives in time.

130654.en: I'm looking for some work, as long as it's for the greater good of the State ...

130655.en:
Ah then I have something for you. I'm in charge of security for the Minedrill expedition forces stationed here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. As you probably know this is risky space, but even so we've been harassed by the same pirate far too many times for it to be coincidence. Also upon investigating the matter further, I discovered that this pirate is in fact called 'Black Jack', a notorious felon who terrorized Molden Heath not too long ago. There was a documentary about him released by The Scope ...

Anyway, if you find him then kill him for me, please. He's been the bane of too many of my colleagues and has been making quite a fool out of my security division in fact. There are many stories floating around which tell of his greatly exaggerated 'victories' over my men and those of the Navy guarding the civilian excavators, which are often completely false and unjustified. Now if you could bring me something to prove he's dead, his DNA would probably do, then I'll be able to vindicate the reputation of the security division here in Kois City.

Now as for finding Black Jack, I have absolutely no clue. You could try searching for him with your scanners, but that's about all I can tell you. I've tried looking for him near the habitation module they call 'Black Jack's Shack', but he's never there.

Finding Black Jack is about as hard as finding a needle in a haystack. I suggest you refrain from accepting this mission unless you have some idea of his whereabouts.

130658.en: Somehow I doubt you'll find him, but good luck regardless ...

130659.en: Great news!  With Black Jack out of the way, our expeditions should be a lot less risky.  This will most definitely boost morale, and all thanks to you.  Enjoy your reward.

130660.en:
Now on to the big fish. As you undoubtedly know, our biggest threat in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} has been the Guristas organization. Although they seem to be quite disorganized, as you would expect for a pirate organization, their top man here is rumored to be Airkio Yanjulen, a commander residing in O-LR1H. Killing him should weaken them considerably ... at least I hope so.

Bring me proof of his death and I'll reward you generously. The last I heard he was stationed in the Guristas War Installation in one of their outposts within O-LR1H. You will have to use your system scanner in that system and search for the 'Iacta Space Plain' to find him.

130663.en: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}.  A rather gruesome sight, but his corpse will do.  I will notify the admiral immediately.   You may go.

130667.en: Aye I do, {[character]player.name}. We got reports of an Ammatar patrol in this sector. Our surveillance patrol reports they are scouts providing intel back to their leaders for a much larger raiding party. We cannot have them discover our weak points or gather any intel on our convoy travel routes. Teach them a lesson for us, {[character]player.name}.

130668.en: Great job {[character]player.name}! You did good out there, here's your reward.

130669.en: Now head out there and do your job, {[character]player.name}. Don't make me regret giving you this assignment.
