130674.en: Looks like you could use a hand out here ...

130675.en:
Is it that obvious? Well, since you had the guts to fly out here into no-mans land you might be of some use to me.

We've been holed up here for days, unable to complete our objective. I was sent here along with the rest of my division to set up a blockade around the O-LR1H gate, to prevent the Guristas from continuing to flood this system with their fighters. Unfortunately we're simply outnumbered and outgunned, there's no way for us to hold that position and the admiral was very clear when I left that he could not spare any reinforcements for quite some time.

So we've been forced to do nothing more than monitor the gate, alerting our forces of any possible threat. It's rather embarrassing to say the least, but here's where you come in ...

130677.en:
During my research of the Guristas movements through {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, I discovered that most of the Guristas squadrons flying through {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} originate from a certain outpost within O-LR1H. I believe that's where their command post in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} is located. Not only that but local rumor has it that many of the Guristas ships currently stationed in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} have only recently arrived to the constellation.

So my conclusion naturally is that a large portion of the Guristas forces that have been harassing us here lately are part of an assembly of fighters recently allocated here by the Guristas central command in 6NJ8-V. With this in mind I would also assume they are acting on specific orders and not randomly attacking us when the opportunity arrives, like is often the case with pirates in these parts.

Now if I could only get a hold of their plans, I would have some good news finally to present to Admiral Aurobe Kois. Knowledge of their next move would give us a huge advantage. Acquiring this knowledge is of course easier said than done.

This is where you come in. Your job, obviously, is to acquire this data. And I know of two ways to do it. Your first option is to befriend one of their leaders within the Iacta Space Plain in O-LR1H and somehow acquire the information through him. This is of course highly difficult and only possible if you are in good standing with the Guristas organization. Your second option is to rescue the last agent I sent on the very same task, Otsalen Mano. He found something, but before he could return to me his identity was discovered. He's currently being held in one of their prison facilities near the Iacta Space Plain in O-LR1H. And there's nothing I can do about it until I get more firepower ...

Anyway, don't return until you have the Guristas war plans!

130679.en: You have the plans?  Most excellent!!  I'll have this delivered to the Admiral immediately.  But if you have some spare time on your hands, I could use a hand with a couple other tasks ...

130680.en: I have the war plans, as you requested {[character]agentID.name}.

130682.en: Search for the Iacta Space Plain in O-LR1H.  A system scanner will probably be necessary.  From there infiltrate the prison facilities and rescue the prisoner Tomi requested or find some way of acquiring the Guristas War Plans.

130684.en: I saw the armory disintegrate from a distance.  What a sight indeed.  Nice work.

130685.en: The armory has been destroyed, as you requested.

130686.en: The last thing I want you to do for me is to intercept a squadron of Guristas fighters who recently came through the stargate from O-LR1H.  They've been following a certain expedition of ours, no doubt waiting for the right time to attack.  Little beknownst to them we've been tracking their every move.  Now I expect them to show up at a certain point in G5ED-Y any moment now, and I want you to be waiting there for that to happen.  Once they appear, shoot them down immediately.

130689.en: Just remember to be patient.  I don't know exactly when they will show up, so keep your guard up.

130690.en: Is there anything else I can do for you?

130693.en: I heard you might have some work available ...

130694.en:
You heard right, {[character]player.name}. We've been plagued by Caldari agents trying to infiltrate our operations here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. One such agent, Tantima Areki, managed to fool us for weeks, pretending to be a Guristas loyalist. When we finally discovered his true identity, he fled to somewhere within {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. We haven't found him yet, but I'm hoping you will succeed where my lackeys failed. Bring me Tantima Areki, preferably alive, and I will reward you well.

Use a system scanner and look for deadspace signatures. He will most likely be orbiting a Caldari Tactical Outpost.

130697.en: Ah, you brought him back alive.  Excellent.  I will have him interrogated immediately, and then executed.  You have done well.

130699.en: Destroy the long range scanner near the stargate to O-LR1H in G5ED-Y, and bring back its contents to your agent.

130701.en: The Caldari have erected a base of operations close to the stargate we use in G5ED-Y.  Not only that but they are closely monitoring our movements from a static long range scanner.  They use this information to send in reinforcements to the Caldari Navy positions before we attack, among other things.  I'm tempted to launch a major assault against their outpost, but perhaps you can spare me the manpower by doing the job yourself.  You will be adequately rewarded of course.

They use this information to send in reinforcements to the Caldari Navy positions before we attack, among other things. 130703.en: Good work.  Now I have another job for you, I want you to bring these documents to an agent of mine in G5ED-Y.  His name is Knaaninn Aranuri and he currently resides in a habitation module near the fifth planet in G5ED-Y.  You'll have to use a system scanner to find him.  Make haste.

130706.en: Bring {[character]agentID.name} the Guristas War Plans.  You should have received these plans from agent Airkio Yanjulen in O-LR1H.  {[character]agentID.name} resides near the fifth planet of G5ED-Y.

130707.en: I was supposed to bring this data to you, {[character]agentID.name} ...

130708.en: Give it to me then so I can take a look at it ...

130712.en: Ah.  My orders, finally they have arrived.  My men have been getting quite restless, ever since Airkio sent us here to spy on the State scum.  It seems that we get to launch a major offensive against the Caldari Navy positions here in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}.  But don't leave just yet, I have a job for you.

130714.en:
I've started readying the troops for battle, but there is one critical threat looming on the horizon. My sources tell me that a massive weapons convoy is en route to {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, all the way from Caldari Navy compounds in their sovereign space. It is scheduled to arrive here any minute now.

If it arrives at Kois City in one piece, it will give our enemies a huge boost. They've been low on ammunition and equipment for the past few weeks due to our relentless guerilla attacks, but that will be a thing of the past if that convoy arrives at its destination.

You probably guessed it by now, but I want you to stop it from getting to Kois City. I have a bookmark to the stargate they are using to get here. Warp to the location and eliminate every Caldari ship you see. Once they have all been reduced to floating debris, report to me.

130716.en: Now that the weapons convoy is out of the picture, we can continue our preparations.  All thanks to you, of course, {[character]player.name}.  Enjoy your reward.

130718.en: I hope you have what it takes, {[character]player.name}.

130720.en: You came to the right place, but he isn't here.  Left quite some time ago on a reconnaissance mission and hasn't been heard of since.  I'm actually becoming quite worried, he and his men are a vital part of our expedition, and if something happened to them I'm afraid we might have to go empty handed back to base.

130721.en: I might be of some assistance, if you need help.

130722.en: As a matter of fact, I could use a hand in finding out what has actually become of Black Jack.  A colleague of mine in UL-4ZW, Gue Mouey, might know something.  He's one of the overseers of the Syndicate Trade Hub in that system, you'll find it near UL-4ZW IX.  He has had extensive dealings with agents of the Guristas and Caldari Navy, if anyone is qualified to scrounge up information on what happened to Black Jack, it's him.

He's one of the overseers of the Syndicate Trade Hub in that system, you'll find it near UL-4ZW IX.  He has had extensive dealings with agents of the Guristas and Caldari Navy, if anyone is qualified to scrounge up information on what happened to Black Jack, it's him.

130724.en: I have this message from Gue.

130725.en: This is terrible news.  Black Jack possibly dead?  This changes everything.  But before we pack our bags and head back to Syndicate space, I want to make sure our information is correct.

130726.en: Hello, {[character]agentID.name}.  Isana Dagin sent me to you, she ...

130727.en: Aha!  I knew that broad liked me.  Whatever kind words she has for me, tell her it's mutual.  Or better yet, I have some flowers I'd like you to give her ...

130728.en: Err, actually she needs some information on Black Jack.  You heard anything from the ranks of the Guristas lately, relating to him?

130729.en: What?!  That's all she wants?  Some information?!   Well, if that's the case then it'll cost ya.  Getting my hopes up like that wasn't very nice ...

130730.en: I have these tags if you'd like, I heard they fetch a good price in these parts.

130731.en: Well ... ok, that will have to do.  Now as for the information, I have something on Black Jack, yes.  This guy, Tikui Makan, a prominent member of the Guristas I might add, has been boasting lately of killing Black Jack in a duel which supposedly took place in Y5J-EU.  I don't have any more information on the matter, but I can give you Tikui's location.  I'll upload it into this data chip, take it back to Isana.  And when you do that, put in a good word for me, will ya?

130732.en: Get something for {[character]agentID.name} that will convince him to give you the information Isana wants.

130734.en: As you heard from Gue, Tikui Makan recently boasted of killing Black Jack.  We need to confirm this statement before we abandon our assignment.  Gue lists the coordinates to Tikui's hideout in his message, and I want you to take a closer look.  See if you can find Tikui there, and if you do tell him to give you the exact coordinates of the encounter he had with Black Jack so that we may identify his corpse, if there is one.  Just make sure he's telling the truth.

130735.en: As you heard from Gue, Tikui Makan recently boasted of killing Black Jack.  We need to confirm this statement before we abandon our assignment. Just make sure he's telling the truth.

130736.en: Oh and another thing, I think Gue has the hots for you.

130737.en: You can tell that rascal that I'd rather take a trip out of the nearest airlock than start up a relationship with him.

130738.en: You can tell that rascal that I'd rather go skinny dipping in an active volcano than have anything to do with him that isn't strictly business related.

130739.en: You can tell that rascal that he has a bigger chance of winning the Legends Trials than he has with me.

130740.en:
This information changes everything. I cannot believe we almost fell for Black Jack's ploy. This matter will be dealt with when I arrive back to Syndicate space.

The Syndicate forces under my command are not well equipped enough to take on the assignment without Black Jack and his men. So I must rely on you, {[character]player.name}, to finish the job.

130741.en: You have established yourself as a trustworthy client of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. I have some corporate documents for you to deliver to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. You have 24 hours to get this done; that should be no problem for someone as yourself, right? I assure you the reward will be well worth the effort.

130742.en: Great!  Your achievements for us have not gone unnoticed.

130743.en: You said you still needed some help.

130744.en:
Quite right, {[character]player.name}. I think it's time for you to know the objective of my mission here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. We were to infiltrate Kois City, the central administrative complex in G5ED-Y, from where the Caldari send all of their expeditions, and answer the question that has been nagging my superiors back home, "Why are they here?".

Now getting into Kois City will be no easy task. It's heavily fortified. But on the bright side I think I know exactly what we're looking for. My sources tell me that the expeditionary forces store most of the data they have collected in a computer within the city's science labs. Backup data is also stored in data chips within their storage facility in the civilian sector of the city. Therefore your task is to somehow get into the civilian quarter and acquire at least one of those data chips. From this data we will hopefully be able to piece together their objective, and find out if it's worth our time to get involved.

This used to be Black Jack's task, but I assume he discovered something that convinced him to cut ties with us and go solo. But I will tell you this, it is in your best interest to complete this task at any cost. Should you fail, or decide to 'keep' the data for yourself, the Syndicate will hunt you down like a dog and force you to watch your own family executed in the cruelest of ways. Is that clear?

130747.en: Good.  Now you'll find the storage facility I referred to in the civilian sector of the city.  You will probably have to destroy it to access the data chips due to the heavy security of the structure.  So just keep your fingers crossed that the data isn't destroyed with the building!

130748.en: Infiltrate Kois City, find the storage facility in the Civilian Quarter and destroy it.  Loot the Expeditionary Data from the wreckage and return to your agent.

130750.en:
You have the data! Incredible, I truly thought the mission I gave you was close to impossible. Yet here you are.

Enjoy your reward, {[character]player.name}, you've certainly earned it. As for myself, I'll be heading back to Syndicate space soon enough with my findings, have a nice day.

130751.en: What brings you to this dangerous place, {[character]agentID.name}?

130752.en:
Ah, it's nice to see a friendly face around here for a change, {[character]player.name}. But to answer your question, I came here to investigate Constellation E-8CSQ, which has been reported to contain massive gas clouds full of material used in booster manufacturing. There have been a lot of rumors about it within {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, and I thought I'd take a look for myself. Unfortunately, the number of rogue drones and outlaws here has me quite worried, so I dare not go looking for the clouds myself. Hence, I might have a job for you...

However, I suggest you refrain from accepting my task unless you have access to a gas cloud harvester module. Without that, you will just be wasting my time.

130753.en: I'll take anything you got as long as it's worth my time.

130754.en:
Okay, what I need you to do for me is find one of the famed E-8CSQ gas clouds. Now of course I'm referring specifically to those gas clouds containing the materials I need for booster manufacturing. You must tell me where the cloud is and get me a sample from it. If you do this for me, I'll give you a booster blueprint copy, plus a little extra cash if you're fast. And you'll learn something in the process. Sounds useful, huh?

You will find information on how to find and access the clouds in the message I uploaded to the mission details in your Opportunities interface.

130755.en: I found one of the gas clouds you've been looking for, {[character]agentID.name}, and it's at these coordinates ...

130756.en: Excellent work!!  Now I just need to find a station where I can manufacture the boosters and I'm all set.  Thanks a bunch, {[character]player.name}.

130757.en: A Brief Guide to Booster Manufacturing

130758.en: Greetings, Rakka.  I hear you call the shots here in Makeinu?

130759.en: I am the mayor, yes. But you might find the inhabitants to be a bit ... independent. Anyway, I assume, from looking at the database information on you, that you're a freelancer. Looking for a job, perhaps?

130760.en: As a matter of fact, I am. Anything I can do for you or this fine station?

130761.en:
Makeinu has a thorn in its side that I want drawn out, the sooner the better. As you might know, some of our residents have had a fairly violent history. And it so happens that DED felt the urge to send assassins all the way out here to settle the score with a couple of my people who had some run-ins with the law some time ago. Or this could be a private vendetta by an angry DED commander. Who knows? But either way, they need to be dealt with before they find us. We're ill equipped to deal with an encounter like that, and quite frankly most of us are too old and worn out to fight.

I've had the DED squadron tracked for some time now. I'll upload a bookmark for their current location to the mission details in your Opportunities interface. Find them and take out their leader ― that should be enough to send them crawling back to their homeland with their tails between their collective legs.

130763.en: I have completed the task, Rakka.  Now for my reward ...

130764.en: Excellent. Yes, you will receive your reward, don't worry. But before you leave, I have one more task for you. The competence you showed in your last assignment has given me an idea ...

130765.en: You said you had some more work for me?

130766.en:
Yes, your next assignment is a little more personal in nature. You see, I was born and raised in the Venal system, and during my teens I joined the Guristas militia. I never knew my parents, but I assume they were loyal to the Guristas. I did have a few comrades that I could call friends, and my life was relatively stable. But then came the assignment that would change everything.

I was sent to E-8CSQ to find and apprehend a traitor, Akkeshu Karuan. My orders were specific, to bring him back dead or alive to Jirai Laitanen at the Guristas headquarters. I was not to return, not ever, until and unless this task was accomplished. I never questioned my orders, and frankly I don't give a damn what Akkeshu was accused of. For my entire life, I have known nothing other than the Guristas, the organization that fed and clothed me during my darkest of times, and I owe them my life.

But unfortunately the mission did not go as planned. I fought Akkeshu and his men inside what is now known as "Cadaver Reef." I was victorious in that battle, but Akkeshu still slipped through my grasp. He and what remained of his gang fled deeper into the deadspace pocket, and of course I followed with the fleet under my command. That action turned out to be a terrible mistake. Akkeshu knew the area like the back of his hand, and he managed to use that knowledge to his advantage. Once he warped away from our targeting systems, all we could find was an acceleration gate. When we activated it, it propelled us deeper into the rock-filled deadspace complex. But somehow Akkeshu had managed to reconfigure the gate, and instead of finding him on the other side, we were sent straight into a massive drone hive. We put up a brave fight and managed to destroy the hive, but at enormous cost. The fleet was shattered, and I was left with a force so small we could not hope to face Akkeshu again.

So here I am, all these years later, rotting in a town filled with hopelessness and depression. I so yearn to return to my roots, but I know that if I do so, I will be promptly executed for my failure.

I am now too old and out of practice to attempt to find Akkeshu again. But considering how well you dealt with your last mission, I have hope that perhaps you can succeed where I failed. All I ask for is evidence of Akkeshu's death; with that, I can return to my homeland and hopefully redeem myself, dying in peace among my own people. I do not have many years left, and you cannot imagine how much I wish to spend them in the land of my birth instead of a place like Makeinu Town.

Find Cadaver Reef. Use scan probes. Bring me proof of Akkeshu's demise, and I will give you my most prized possessions.

130771.en: Incredible! I simply could not bring myself to believe you would succeed, {[character]player.name}, but here you are. I owe you more than I can ever repay, but I hope this meager reward will have made it worth your time. Take care.

130773.en: To finish this mission, you must first find Cadaver Reef via system scanning. It lies somewhere in this constellation. Akkeshu might be located inside; destroy his ship and return with his DNA for your reward.

130774.en: So what brought you all the way out here, {[character]agentID.name}?

130775.en:
I came here to investigate Constellation 09-4XW, which has been reported to contain massive gas clouds full of material used in booster manufacturing. Unfortunately, the number of rogue drones and outlaws here has me quite worried, so I dare not go looking for the clouds myself. Hence, I might have a job for you...

However, I suggest you refrain from accepting my task unless you have access to a gas cloud harvester module. Without that, you will just be wasting my time.

130776.en: I'll take anything you got as long as it's worth my time.

Okay, what I need you to do for me is find one of the famed 09-4XW gas clouds. Now of course I'm referring specifically to those gas clouds containing the materials I need for booster manufacturing. And you'll learn something in the process. Sounds useful, huh?

However, I suggest you refrain from accepting my task unless you have access to a gas cloud harvester module. Without that, you will just be wasting my time.

130809.en:
Okay, what I need you to do for me is find one of the famed OK-FEM gas clouds. Now of course I'm referring specifically to those gas clouds containing the materials I need for booster manufacturing. You must tell me where the cloud is and get me a sample from it. If you do this for me, I'll give you a booster blueprint copy, plus a little extra cash if you're fast. And you'll learn something in the process. Sounds useful, huh?

You will find information on how to find and access the clouds in the mission details in your Opportunities interface.

130810.en: I found one of the gas clouds you've been looking for, {[character]agentID.name}, and it's at these coordinates ...

130830.en: We've been encountering a tremendous amount of pirate activity in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name} lately.  Our convoys are constantly under threat, and our CEO demanded that we do something about the situation.  We are to hire trustworthy and competent mercenaries to help us out, as the security forces in this constellation are swamped with work.  So I ask you, {[character]player.name}, will you help us out this time?  If your answer is yes, then I have a difficult assignment for you.  I need you to eliminate a heap load of pirates at a few coordinates.  You will receive bookmarks to these locations, all of them within the system {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}.  Hopefully this will put a dent into their plans, and relieve our security forces a bit of their workload.

130835.en:
Alright, I'll tell you a little story. My expedition had discovered an area filled with gas clouds thicker than I had ever witnessed in my life, and we were ecstatic. For days we harvested the gas fields, with no end in sight. At that time I was already starting to daydream about where I would retire when I finished this job. It was probably the greatest moment of my life. Unfortunately, followed by the worst.

Once we had filled our cargo holds, we started to align our ships for warp. It was then that they hit us. They came from nowhere and warp scrambled our industrials and jammed the two merc ships escorting us. They demanded over half of our cargo. We debated. But before we could give an answer, they attacked. Half the expedition was wiped out, including some of my closest friends. The ones who survived were told to go back to camp and relay our story to the rest of the miners and harvesters, so that the next time one of our expeditions runs into the Guristas we follow their orders immediately.

Now I just want to leave this dreadful place, I knew I took a huge risk by coming here but now that I've seen the face of death ... I just don't think I have it in me anymore.

130836.en: I'm sorry for your loss.  Perhaps I can help.

130837.en:
I know some of the families of my colleagues who perished on that fateful day, and I would like their bodies returned to me so that I can bring them back to Caldari space for proper burial. If you're up for the job, I'll give you a bookmark to the deadspace area where they lost their lives. You should be able to find the wreckage of their ships there.

You'll probably have to navigate through at least two pockets though to find all of them, once the Guristas attacked we tried to flee via the acceleration gates there, some of us only made it past one gate before being mowed down.

130839.en: You're some fighter, I didn't expect you to come back alive.  But I'm happy you did, here's your reward.

130841.en: Your success in the last mission has given me some hope.  Perhaps my comrades can be avenged.  The captain of the Guristas gang which attacked us is still at large.  But some of my people have tracked him down, and I have the coordinates to his hideout.  I will give you these coordinates, if you promise to destroy him and anyone under his command.  You will receive a reward, of course.

130843.en: Although the loss of my friends can never be replaced, you have certainly gone far to ease the burden of their deaths.  For that I will be forever thankful.  Take your reward, and be safe.

130845.en: You're observation is correct, I AM frustrated!  And it's rather embarrassing to tell you the truth ... but if you're a merc for hire then I'll spill the beans, as long as you promise to help me.

130847.en:
Ok, just promise you won't laugh. You see, before I came here I was a computer programmer. I specialized in creating and maintaining artificial intelligence for Kaalakiota, probes and drones and that sort of stuff. Well after I got here, I realized I needed some heavy duty protection considering the relative lawlessness of this place, and the mercs here were just way too expensive.

So I used my expertise to set up a self-maintaining drone facility, which provided me with enough backup to safely harvest the gas fields around here. It worked like a charm to begin with ... until hardware failure wiped out the secret password I've been using to access the mother-drone computer's mainframe.

Now I can't even get into my own home! I've been sitting around here for days but none of these good-for-nothing mercs have the guts to face my drones. Maybe you've got it in you?

Anyway first I want my stash of extracted gas chemicals. You'll find a few containers full of it in my storage facility. I'll give you the coordinates, all you have to do is warp there, take out the drones guarding the stash, loot it, and bring it back here.

130848.en: I brought back the stash.  Some advice though, carry a backup of that damn password!

130849.en:
Hey! Don't tell me what to do! If I didn't have another job for you, I'd keep the reward for myself. Learn some manners!

Besides, you have no idea how much CPU a complex password like that takes. Hacker-proof passwords are no laughing matter these days.

130851.en: You said you had another mission.

130852.en: Yes, that is correct. I need you to clean up the mess I left behind, before things spiral out of control. I don't want to have any civilian deaths on my hands. To do this, the drone mother-computer must be taken care of. It is located near the place I just sent you. I have opened the acceleration gate leading into an adjacent deadspace pocket, which is where you'll find the target. Destroy it and return to me.

130855.en: Don't come back until the Drone Creation Compound has been destroyed, that's where the drone mother-computer is stored.

130856.en: Not bad, not bad.  You'll do quite nicely here, {[character]player.name}, I know there's a bunch of people looking for someone of your caliber.  Take care.

130857.en: I'm looking for some work, you got any?

130858.en:
Have I got any? Are you mad? I've been sitting here all day looking for contractors with some combat experience. Now I need someone I can rely on for this job, and I have to say I'm impressed with the way you've dealt with some of your previous assignments for Caldari agents. So maybe you're cut out for this ...

Anyway, I've been informed that a few gangs of Guristas scoundrels have decided to attempt a full scale assault on our little town here. Inside sources tell me that they are not working for the core Guristas leadership in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, so they won't be as deadly and organized as I first feared. But they're still a major threat, and as such I need someone to take care of 'em. If you can do the job, in other words take 'em out before they reach Pioneer's Sanctuary, then I'll reward you generously.

It so happens that I know where one of their stopping points will be, I will give you the coordinates of course.

130860.en: Just a word of advice before you leave, they will arrive at the rendezvous point in waves, so I suggest shooting them with all you got to prevent them from overwhelming you.

130862.en: Excellent work!  You saved us from a nasty encounter, and for that I thank you.  But there's more, so stick around.

130863.en: You mentioned you had some more work for me.

130864.en: Now I'd like you to target a Guristas Relay Station in ZH3-BS which has been transmitting orders to dozens of pirate gangs in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}.  They're the top dogs in this system, and get their information directly from the Guristas high command.  By taking them out we will be dealing a serious blow to their plans.  I will give you the coordinates, of course.

130868.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}.  You've just given us hope that we might actually win after all!

130869.en: I'm looking for work, you got any?

130870.en: I'm in a bit of a dilemma at the moment.  I managed to find an area of deadspace filled with lucrative gas clouds, but as always there was a catch.  The Guristas had apparently erected an outpost next to an acceleration gate leading directly into the deadspace pocket containing the clouds.  I haven't detected any signs of them actually harvesting the gas, but I dare not try to enter the area with them nearby.  Could you please remove their presence for me?

130872.en: The pirates are gone?  I'll have to take a look myself.

130873.en: Anything else I can do for you?

130874.en: Hmmm, yes there is one more thing.  I have a long range scanner in I1-BE8 which I use to look for promising sites which may harbor harvestable gas clouds.  The problem is I'm afraid of going back there and retrieving the data, the last time I tried I noticed a couple pirates nearby who I thought might be waiting in ambush.  Anyway I don't want to take any chances, but if you're willing then I'll pay you for getting me the data.

130876.en: Thanks for retrieving the data, {[character]player.name}.  Hopefully this data will lead me to gas clouds far away from those pesky pirates.

130877.en: You're the mayor of Pioneer's Sanctuary, aren't you {[character]agentID.name}?

130878.en:
Your observation is correct. And I've been watching you, {[character]player.name}, for a while now, and you seem to fit the criteria I've been looking for.

Now I have a task for you that may prove to be extremely dangerous. As you probably know already we've had a long standing quarrel with the Guristas forces in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. And it's really showing a toll on the settlers here. But I want to propose a truce, and I want you to be the one that brings them the offer. I will supply you a bookmark to the Guristas Headquarters in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, all you have to do is warp in there and bring it to their leaders.

130879.en:

130880.en: It's as I expected, they won't listen to reason.  Then I guess it's time for us to face the cold hard facts, the town must be abandoned.  Unless someone is brave enough to stand up to those scoundrels and teach them a lesson ...

130881.en: I'm willing to help you fight the Guristas

130882.en:
You are, huh. Unfortunately there is only one way to truly stop the Guristas from enslaving us, at least temporarily. And that is to annihilate their high command in 1QH-0K. I know it sounds foolhardy and it probably is, but it's the only way ... if we don't strike them down at the root they will just keep on coming.

I'm probably getting way ahead of myself here, I really can't ask you to try something insane like assault their most powerful stronghold in the entire constellation. But if you do, I will give you a very nice reward for the insignia from their leader.

130883.en:
Unfortunately there is only one way to truly stop the Guristas from enslaving us, at least temporarily. And that is to annihilate their high command in 1QH-0K. I know it sounds foolhardy and it probably is, but it's the only way ... if we don't strike them down at the root they will just keep on coming.

130884.en: I will do it.  The Guristas will fall before me.

130885.en: I fear for your life, but on the other hand you are our only hope.  So I wish you good luck.

130886.en: The Guristas high command in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} is no more.

130887.en: You have managed the impossible once again, {[character]player.name}.  But this time you surprised even myself.  Pioneer's Sanctuary owes you a great debt which can never be repaid in full.  But hopefully your reward will at least repay your expenses.  Good luck in whatever the future holds for you.

130897.en: I'm lookin' for some work. You got any?

130898.en: Sure, {[character]player.name}. Something up your alley just hit my desk this morning, in fact. I need someone to investigate a distress signal in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It was sent from an industrial registered to a group of harvesters that recently came to Fatimar Outpost from Amarr space. It's probably just an engine failure or something, but I don't have spare mechanics to deal with that problem just now. So I'd like you to fly them back here to safety, and we'll fetch the industrial later.

130899.en: I need someone to investigate a distress signal from an industrial registered to a group of harvesters in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I'd like you to fly them back here to safety, and we'll fetch the industrial later.

130900.en: From your report, I can only assume that the hapless harvester expedition was beset by Sansha pirates and murdered; the distress signal must have been sent by the enemy to lure us in. Clever, I suppose, but I feel bad for the harvesters' families. They were simple, hard-working men and women, and they'll be missed here in Fatimar.

130902.en: Deliver the bad news to the slain workers' colleagues. They reside in a small outpost in a nearby system; I'll upload the coordinates directly into your NeoCom. As usual, all you have to do is fly close to the outpost structure and the message should automatically be uploaded into their communications database.

130903.en: Your an observant one, {[character]player.name}. You'll go far, I imagine. Now that we know of the harvester's fate, it's time to deliver the bad news to their colleagues. They reside in a small outpost in a nearby system; I'll upload the coordinates directly into your NeoCom. As usual, all you have to do is fly close to the outpost structure and the message should automatically be uploaded into their communications database.

130904.en: So what's next? You seem like you have something on your mind.

130905.en: Yes, thanks for the help, {[character]player.name}. Wish I could find more for you to do right now, but most of the jobs around here are beneath a capsuleer like you.

130906.en: I guess my work here is done.

130908.en:
Yes I do. I'm the leader of a small gang of harvesters, and I'd like to hire you to clear a rogue drone infestation near a gas field we've been working on. They have been continually harassing us, and it's come to a point where my gangmates have refused to venture back there. Armed escort would cost a fortune over a long period, so we believe the most cost effective approach is simply eradicating the threat all-together.

Your first mission is to clear the area of rogue drones. Once that is done then report back to me immediately.

130909.en:
Yes I do. I'm the leader of a small gang of harvesters, and I'd like to hire you to clear a rogue drone infestation near a gas field we've been working on. They have been continually harassing us, and it's come to a point where my gangmates have refused to venture back there. Armed escort would cost a fortune over a long period, so we believe the most cost effective approach is simply eradicating the threat all-together.

Your first mission is to clear the area of rogue drones. Once that is done then report back to me immediately.

130910.en: Excellent.  But there's one more thing to be done to completely end our drone problem.

130912.en: Now it's time to strike at the root of the problem, the Drone Hive.  The drones are manufactured there, so as along as it's around they will just keep coming.  Destroy it and report to me for your reward.

130913.en: Now it's time to strike at the root of the problem, the Drone Hive.  The drones are manufactured there, so as along as it's around they will just keep coming.  Destroy it and report to me for your reward.

130914.en: You've done us a great service, {[character]player.name}.  I'll notify my crew immediately, they'll be ecstatic.  Take care.

130915.en: Who are you, if I may ask?

130916.en:
Who am I? WHO AM I? I am Kushan Horeat, Baron of Dagamar. I came here with my forces when Nimpor requested my assistance. And perhaps you are curious as to why a prestigious Imperial lord would waste his time answering a peon like yourself...?

The answer is that I need a little help. I have a dangerous mission that needs doing, and I would rather not risk my own men if possible. So, on behalf of the Amarr Empire, I desire you to help me.

130918.en: How dare you speak to me like that, you whey-faced monkey! Out here, you're a nobody, just like me, so sit down and mind your manners ― before I give you something to curse about... Stupid windbag.

130919.en: You... you, you worthless, impudent fool! If I wasn't so busy looking for servants to do my bidding, I'd strike you down right now! Get out of my sight, worm!

130920.en: I see you've done my bidding in a timely manner.  Maybe after all this is over I'll hire you as my wine steward.

130921.en:
That's more like it.

Your task is simple. There is a stargate in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} that I had built recently, to transport my troops secretly past the Sansha louts. Somehow, though, one of my incompetent commanders managed to reveal himself ... and the stargate ... to a Sansha patrol. Now they're all over it, probably scavenging the place for spare parts.

I want you to destroy it. Completely. Don't even leave the debris behind. There is data in the computer systems inside the stargate that might reveal the location of all our positions to the Sansha, including Fatimar Outpost. This data must not fall into the hands of the enemy.

Dismissed.

130924.en: Yes, there's one more thing I want done. Immediately, you understand? We've been preparing for a major assault against Sansha positions in 3GD6-8, but our intel of the system is very limited. I would like you to conduct a simple recon mission through a few deadspace pockets there that may contain Sansha activity. If you stumble upon a complex of theirs, then return to me immediately and give me the exact coordinates.

130926.en: Sorry, but I don't have time for arrogant louts like yourself. Later, mouthpiece.

130927.en: How DARE you speak to me like that! I'll have your head on a platter! I'll, I'll ... why, I'll have your whole family thrown into slavery! I'll tear down your ship and build my vacation resort out of it! Just you wait and see!

130928.en: Excellent, servant. Get to work, then, and be quick about it or I'll lower your reward.

130929.en: Now that wasn't so hard, was it? Perhaps you really aren't as stupid as you look. Maybe there's hope for you yet...

130932.en: I'm not just angry, I'm bloody furious!  I was just minding my own business in an asteroid field in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, when an extra group of miners show up.  I ignore them and continue mining my roid.  Then one of them jams me and threatens to blow my ship up if I don't leave.  Talk about being rude!  And to top it off, they're from a rival Minmatar mining colony in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}.

130934.en: Really?  Thanks!  I'll reward you well for your effort.  What I need you to do first is warp to my asteroid field and take out the louts who stole it from me.  When that's done, we'll take care of the pesky Minmatar mining colony.

130935.en: I've taken care of the criminals.

130936.en: Excellent.  Now we must strike fast against their colony, or I might have to worry about reprisal attacks when I get back to work on the asteroid field.

130937.en:
I'm not just angry, I'm bloody furious! I was just minding my own business in an asteroid field in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, when an extra group of miners show up. I ignore them and continue mining my roid. Then one of them jams me and threatens to blow my ship up if I don't leave. Talk about being rude! And to top it off, they're from a rival Minmatar mining colony in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}.

What I need you to do first is warp to my asteroid field and take out the louts who stole it from me. When that's done, we'll take care of the pesky Minmatar mining colony.

130938.en: I'm ready for the next mission.

130939.en:
Ok, now it's time to finish the job we started. The expedition you faced in your last mission hails from a colony in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and they'll probably not be happy when they find out what happened to their colleagues. I want you to completely obliterate their outpost and any ships nearby, that way I can safely venture back to the asteroid field without worrying about reprisal attacks. This will also rid Fatimar Outpost of a long standing competitor, so we'll effectively be killing two flies in one blow.

Good luck.

130942.en: I'm looking for work, you got any?

130943.en:
You know who you're speaking to, right? I'll educate you regardless. I am {[character]agentID.name}, protector of Fatimar Outpost. Basically I run this place, and have ever since Frolo died.

Now I have a mission that would require you to be extremely meticulous and discreet. From looking at your accomplishments here in Fatimar Outpost you probably have what it takes to get it done. And oddly enough I trust you to keep a lid on this more than Kushan Horeat and his men.

If you're still interested, let me know.

130945.en: Sounds too risky for me.  I'd rather do garbage hauling missions.  Wait ... what on earth am I doing in 0.0 space?!!

130946.en:
I'll start from the beginning. I joined Frolo's crew many years ago, when I was a young lad, and served under him right up to his death. Those were some good times, and we made a fortune from harvesting gas clouds in this area and neighboring constellations. Dorim, Frolo's second son, also served under his father and we became the best of friends.

Now life here was simple, until Frolo died. He was a great man, a remarkable leader. The pioneers out here all looked up to him and followed the rules while he was around. But soon after his death that was about to change.

A few months after Frolo passed away, his firstborn, Jamur Fatimar, arrived in Fatimar Outpost. He had lived all his life with his mother in Amarr space, far away from the grueling life we have here in no-man's-land. Basically he was fed with a silver spoon his entire life, and that rubbed off on him.

As soon as he arrived he claimed ownership of the Outpost. We decided to play along with his little game, as neither I nor Dorim had any real ambition to take on the leadership role. But people quickly started to despise him. He was much harsher than Frolo ever was, and was very detached from the local miners and harvesters here who Frolo used to work along-side. He was a strict, traditional Amarrian ruler who had zero tolerance for any difference of opinion from his own. He implemented a hefty tax which was largely used to pay for his extravagant lifestyle. Needless to say, things got hairy around here. Some of pioneers split away from Fatimar Outpost and founded their own colonies elsewhere, and there were rumors of a rebellion.

When I saw everything that we had built virtually crumbling beneath us, I was forced to intervene. I claimed leadership over Fatimar Outpost. A power struggle ensued, which I eventually won. As you might expect, Jamur was not very fond of losing his title and decided to split away from us, forming his own colony elsewhere in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. But I've always had the impression that he was out for revenge, and therefore I've had his little colony under surveillance for quite some time. And that's what alerted me to an extremely worrying turn of events. Jamur had been in contact with someone from outside {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, who my sources tell me has promised to help him in 'his war with Fatimar Outpost'. I can't imagine what a bitter, power hungry man like Jamur would do to reclaim his title. I want you to find out for me. I will upload the coordinates of the meeting point into your NeoCom, all you have to do is warp there and disrupt the meeting. Bring this 'agent' to me for questioning.

130948.en: Jamur escaped?  Too bad, but at least you got someone.  I'll have them interrogated immediately.

130949.en: Are you done with the interrogation?

130950.en:
Yes, they coughed it up immediately. Apparently they aren't very loyal to their former master. The leader of the group has been in close contact with Jamur and claims he's gone mad. His hatred of me has clouded his judgment, and he's done the unthinkable. The secret agent in your previous mission was in fact an agent of the Sansha's Nation! Talk about striking a deal with the devil ... he's gone way too far this time.

The good news is that we can trace Jamur's exact whereabouts. The bug I had implanted into his ship is still functional, and I can see his location on our scanner. I want you to find him immediately and take him out. Every minute that passes is crucial, he must not be allowed to reveal our location to the Sansha's Nation. If that happens then all may be lost.

130955.en: Amazing job, {[character]player.name}.  We owe you one.

130956.en: I want these elite troops delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for inspection. We hired them recently from an Amarrian security firm to work as guards on our transport vessels. Standard procedure requires that they be inspected for any possible diseases or mental disorders before they're allowed on board.

130957.en: I need you to help out. There is fierce fighting going on in a nearby system and we have militants here that need to be moved out there as soon as humanly possible. Are you willing to help our cause?

130959.en: I want these elite troops delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for inspection. Standard procedure requires that they be inspected for any possible diseases or mental disorders before they're allowed on board.

130960.en: We were ordered by high ranking officials in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} to deliver a batch of Zemnar to the inhabitants of {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Their supplies are low and they need some backup incase of a viral outbreak.

130961.en: We were ordered by high ranking officials in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} to deliver a batch of Galeptos Medicine to the inhabitants of {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Viral outbreaks have been common in outlying settlements within {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} and they need more drugs to combat the infections.

130962.en: A relative of mine in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} just requested a special order of genetically enhanced livestock. I'd like you to deliver them to him in person; he'll meet you on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. And keep a lid on this, will you? Some consumers, especially religious Amarrians, would boycott his wares if word got out he uses genetically enhanced animals.

130964.en: A group of lads from {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} have been requested by {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} army to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  I've agreed to their request, and I'd like you to carry it out.  Deliver them to their destination, the faster the better.

130965.en: A group of battle-hungry lads from {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} have been requested by officials within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} army to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  I've agreed to their request, and I'd like you to carry it out.  Deliver them to their destination, the faster the better.

130966.en: Our friends in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are worried their oxygen supplies won't last until the next shipment from their supplier.  They've requested an extra batch, and we've promised to deliver.  You'll find the goods in your cargo hold if you agree to this task.

130967.en: Our friends in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are worried their oxygen supplies won't last until the next shipment from their supplier.  They've requested an extra batch, and we've promised to deliver.  You'll find the goods in your cargo hold if you agree to this task.

130968.en: One of our transports flying through {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} broke down and requires immediate repairs.  We've agreed to send him the spare parts he needs to complete the operation, and I'd like you to deliver the goods.  If you're fast he might even make it on time, so don't tarry!

130969.en: One of our transports flying through {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} broke down and requires immediate repairs.  We've agreed to send him the spare parts he needs to complete the operation, and I'd like you to deliver the goods.  If you're fast he might even make it on time, so don't tarry!

130970.en: To eliminate the depressive mood of our hangar staff, cargo bay workers, janitors and other laborers we decided to throw them a party at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  I'd like you to do the honors of delivering the spiced wine to the gathering.  And don't forget, a quick delivery will get you a bonus!

130971.en: To eliminate the depressive mood of our hangar staff, cargo bay workers, janitors and other laborers we decided to throw them a party at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  I'd like you to do the honors of delivering some of the personnel to the gathering.  And don't forget, a quick delivery will get you a bonus!

130972.en: A spate of engine failures and system crashes at a client firm in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} has forced them to come to us for more coolants.  We have some extras available, which I'd like you to deliver.  Get it done in time, before their manager suffers a nervous breakdown, to earn your bonus.

130973.en: A spate of engine failures and system crashes at a client firm in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} has forced them to come to us for more coolants.  We have some extras available, which I'd like you to deliver.  Get it done in time, before their manager suffers a nervous breakdown, to earn your bonus.

130974.en: The local news recently aired a story on poor immigrants in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  Apparently some of the families have fallen on hard times and lack the funds to even buy the most basic necessities.  A few concerned citizens in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} asked me to have these polytextiles delivered to the needy in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, which they can make use of.  I'd like you to make the first leg of the trip, which is to drop off the goods at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Officials at the station will take care of the rest.

130975.en: I've been ordered by the government to have these fertilizers delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, from where they'll be dispersed to nearby bio-domes.  Quite a mundane job but one that needs to be done.  Obviously I'd like you to do the honors of making the delivery, so here you go.

130976.en: I've been ordered by the government to have these fertilizers delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, from where they'll be dispersed to nearby bio-domes.  Quite a mundane job but one that needs to be done.  Obviously I'd like you to do the honors of making the delivery, so here you go.

130977.en: Bio-engineers and farmers in nearby settlements, which have been supplying us with foodstuffs, have had good fortune recently.  Their supplies of frozen plant seeds are overflowing, and they would like to sell some of their excess products.  Obviously we took advantage of a good opportunity and bought the goods for silly prices, those people are so gullible.  I'd like you to deliver the goods to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, where we've found a buyer.

130979.en: Miners stopping by {[location]agentStationID.name} for supplies is a common occurrence.  It so happens that a few of them left off in a hurry, and forgot a load of drill parts in the cargo bay.  Fortunately for them the containers were marked, which allowed us to trace the owners quickly enough.  When we contacted them they requested we send the parts to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, for a fee of course.  If you'll do the honors of transporting the goods, a part of that fee will be yours.

130981.en: Apparently some unruly locals got into trouble while visiting {[location]agentStationID.name}, and we've pressed charges.  The authorities requested we send footage from our security cameras to a specialist in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, to ascertain their authenticity.  Once he's gone through these holoreels, we'll hopefully be able to get this through court without a lengthy trial.

130983.en: A few colleagues of mine are on an assignment in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and requested a batch of transmitters which they need for a particular task.  I need them delivered there A.S.A.P.  You're up for the job, I presume?

130984.en: A few colleagues of mine are on an assignment in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and requested a batch of transmitters which they need for a particular task.  I need them delivered there A.S.A.P.  You're up for the job, I presume?

130985.en: A friend is in need of some new hardware.  We have begun mining operations on a planet nearby, and our logistics officer thought it would be a brilliant idea to buy old Amarrian transport vehicles to save us some ISK.  Oh, well.  Looks like we bought the cat in the sack, as we used to say back home.  So now it's my responsibility to fix the situation so we can continue to get minerals for our building projects.  Take these planetary vehicles and bring them out there, so the lazy gits can get back to work.

130986.en:
The security in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} has been getting worse and worse.  I'm telling you, those guys are in someone's pocket.  I have put in a formal request for their termination, but the powers above don't seem to be in agreement.  Which, of course, only reinforces my opinion that they are all corrupt.  Seeing as we can't throw them out of the nearest airlock, I'm going to do the next best thing

I'm sending you out there with a new security officer and some guards to back him up.  It's your responsibility to make sure they make it to the station safe.

130987.en: Our cargo area and lower-tier decks are overflowing with vagabonds and tramps.  It has almost reached epidemic proportions.  These people simply refuse to leave, some are laid off workers of ours while others are simply outsiders who think they can come and live off our hospitality indefinitely.  Since there are strict regulations against sending them out the airlock for no reason, and since we can't simply frame every single one of them for a crime worthy of such a fate, we've no choice but to forcibly move them somewhere else.  Another station will do.  In fact I'd like you to move a heap-load of them to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  I never liked those bastards over there anyway, let them deal with this 'human problem'.

130988.en: One of the local warlords is coming to this area.  We're going to be needing his assistance in the coming weeks, so to make sure we have his backing I'll need you to get me some spirits to make sure everything goes as smoothly as possible.

130989.en: As you know, much of our business consists of gun running. I just made an accounting error which means that a shipment of our guns wasn't sent.  So, to keep the buyer happy, I'm gonna send you over his way with a sample of our high-quality slug throwers.  Hopefully this will buy me an extra day to get it sorted.

130991.en: An old friend of mine runs a strip club in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Some strange flu seems to be striking his strippers pretty hard, so he's gonna be needing new girls.  I need you to take these ladies over to his station.  And if I find out any of them got pregnant along the way, you'll never work for me again.

130992.en: Well, once again the techies in the armament production department have screwed up and installed faulty guidance systems into the new batch of Widowmakers, so now our missiles are flying all over the place. This is not good for our reputation.  I'm sending you over there with new equipment so this can be solved, and fast.

130993.en: We just got information relayed from a nearby listening post.  This info is way too valuable to be sent by local channels, so I'm making you responsible for this data.  Make sure it gets to the right location intact.

130994.en: One of our station reactors is running under threat of melting down, so I'm sending you with some coolant to get the situation under hand. If the reactor goes haywire because you didn't make it in time, I will be very disappointed.

130995.en: I have some very important merchants here that need to be ferried to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can start securing a deal with them.  As you can understand, these people do not want to be known, so we are sending you to fly them around.  Make sure no passenger manifests of these persons are kept.  Thank you.

130996.en: Once again we are out of food.  You'd think they would learn, and just eat a little less, but no.  The big bosses want me to fix this problem, so I'm delegating the task to you.  I want you to ferry these dairy products to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

130997.en: I need you to run over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop off these electronic parts. The Chief Technical Operator there contacted me regarding the discovery of a major defect in their primary reactor, and they don't have the parts on hand to repair it.

Take these planetary vehicles and bring them out there, so the lazy gits can get back to work.

130999.en: Homeless people are everywhere, littering the streets.  I've gathered up a whole bunch of them, and I want you to go and dump them at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Make it somebody else's problem!

131000.en: My superiors over at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are waiting for these reports.  I'm swamped with work so I need you to deliver them for me. Don't mess this up. Both our jobs are on the line here.

131001.en: The greenhouses at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} need a delivery of fertile soil. Take these crates and deliver them, would you? Thanks. Have an excellent day!

131010.en: Garbage is something I have an intense dislike of, and our supplies right now are unfortunately enormous.  Take these crates to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and stash them in an empty hangar there.  They will never suspect us and we'll be rid of this problem for now.

131011.en: I have some very important merchants here that need to be ferried to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can start securing a deal with them.  As you can understand, these people do not want to be known, so we are sending you to fly them around.  Make sure no passenger manifests of these persons are kept.  Thank you.

131012.en:
Several years ago on my daughter's birthday, she begged me to get the newest Andorandy doll set for her. Unfortunately, I couldn't find even one of the popular dolls, even though I ran market database searches repeatedly in this region for several weeks. Well, I'm happy to say I turned all that effort into a lucrative business; today, I sell Andorandy dolls and many other sorts here from my offices in {[location]agentStationID.name}. Maybe you've heard of us? My Little Girl, we´re called.

Anyway, right now I have a problem: I have a shipment of dolls awaiting delivery, but some inventory problems in one of my warehouses are interfering. Can you pick up the dolls for me and deliver them to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}?

131013.en: We've been having problems with some of the local miners lately, and it's time for them to be relocated. Take them to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and tell them they've received a raise. They should be pretty surprised by the end of the month.

131014.en: We've been getting reports of unrest among a garrison of ours on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  I have a devious plan to quell this little hubbub without the use of force.  We just got a shipment of high-grade holoreels with the biggest female stars of the Federation – and no, you may not ask where.  Just head over to that station and make sure the cinema manager gets them.

131015.en: We've engaged in a terraforming project on a nearby planet.  It's going as planned, but we need to make sure the greenery will flourish, so I think some fertilizer would be well in order.  I know this isn't what you had in mind when you became a pod pilot, but someone has to take care of the crap.  And I know you would be perfect for the job.

131016.en: I need you to run over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop off these electronic parts. The Chief Technical Operator there contacted me regarding the discovery of a major defect in their primary reactor, and they don't have the parts on hand to repair it.

131017.en:
As you probably know by now, not all of our operations are conducted during daylight hours. The big bosses have just given me a job that needs a reliable pilot, and seeing that you have such an excellent track record with us, I think you'd be perfect for the job. Move this package to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Don't try to open it. In fact, don't even look at it. Seriously. It's in your best interest.

And you were never here. Wait, who are you? I don't know you. Capiche? Now get going.

131018.en: Homeless people are everywhere, littering the streets.  I've gathered up a whole bunch of them, and I want you to go and dump them at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Make it somebody else's problem!

131019.en: As you know, we have a reputation for being a rowdy bunch and not the most civilized organization in the cluster, but sometimes my own men amaze even me. Yesterday the lads were responsible for showing a VIP a good time and making sure he was entertained, but just now I got a call from a local station manager who's refusing to clean up the mess they made. I'm sending you over there with an army of janitors. No, I don't want to hear about it. Just get going.

131020.en: My superiors over at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are waiting for these reports.  I'm swamped with work so I need you to deliver them for me. Don't mess this up. Both our jobs are on the line here.

131021.en: As you know, keeping the grunts happy is one of my most important jobs.  If they stop working, everything breaks down and we don't want that.  So, for the sake my head and yours, please ferry this shipment of tobacco to the {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}  station.

131022.en: The greenhouses at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} need a delivery of fertile soil. Take these crates and deliver them, would you? Thanks. Have an excellent day!

131023.en: As you know, water is one of the most important commodities around. Without it, we would all die. More importantly, though, the station manager in a nearby station is well-connected with the powers that be. This guy has a thing for bathing in fresh water from the planet below. Yes, yes, I know, and yes, I agree, but when the big bosses ask you to jump, all you do is ask how high.  So I'm asking you to jump, and be fast about it.

131024.en: We are launching one of our new listening posts nearby. Everything is ready and we have a Go signal from the authorities, but the idiots next door forgot to make sure they had the necessary supplies for the launch.  We need you to ferry some rocket fuel so these baboons don't lose their heads to the management.

131110.en:
I've been looking for someone of your talents. It has come to our attention that an armada of Amarr crusaders has arrived in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. According to our sources, their primary objective is to destroy the Pagera Manton, which they view as being a sacrilegious icon of the Blood Raider faith. They believe the Blood Raider organization is defiling the graveyard of their ancestors, and their aim is to 'give them rest'.

These sorts of incursions are nothing new, but this time they mean business. I've never seen such a huge armada threaten our beloved holy site, and to top it off it's being led by one of the Amarrian High Priests, Heftah Nekmar, which is of some concern to us. He has recently led a campaign of propaganda against the Blood Raider religion from inside the Amarrian territories, and the destruction of the Pagera Manton would certainly be viewed as a mighty victory by his people.

131111.en: Ok, what do you want me to do?

131117.en:
One of the most revered holy sites of the Blood Raiders is located in the constellation OK-FEM, called the Pagera Manton. The Pagera Manton was a giant space-ship that was at the head of a massive Amarrian exploration team that had ventured into unknown lands hundreds of years ago. A malfunction in its warp-drive stranded the ship, far away from the rest of the fleet. During that time space-communication was not as sophisticated as today, and it had no way of contacting other vessels of the expedition. Years passed and the crew had finally lost all hope of survival. Food supply was running dangerously low, and it seemed that starvation was inevitable. It was then that one of the officers, an Ammatar by the name of Kalorr Makur, took matters into his own hands. He staged a successful coup against the commanding officer of the ship and had his most loyal followers bind and gag the dissidents inside a secure chamber under his control. These unfortunate souls became the crews new food supply, unbeknownst to most of the crewmembers. For over a year this plan worked, although Kalorr did have to turn to his own followers eventually to replenish his stock of human meat.

Over a century later the ship was discovered by Blood Raider pioneers scouring the distant solar-systems of OK-FEM. They found the remains of the crew, and more importantly a few dozen gigantic tanks encasing millions of liters of blood. Unbeknownst to them the blood had been collected by Kalorr who dried the human meat before consumption. The blood had been meant as a final foodsource after the meat supply had run out, but was never actually consumed as the machine responsible for recycling the air supply malfunctioned which caused the remaining crew to slowly suffocate. Fortunately the blood containers were kept in sub-freezing temperature, which despite over a centry of decay were still up and working when the Pagera was found. And not only that, Kalorr Makur's body was discovered in its very own container, along with his closest allies.

News of the find quickly spread through the Blood Raider territories, and their revered High Priest at the time declared it a 'gift from God'. The blood was stripped from the tanks and brought back to the Blood Raider headquarters for examination and ritualistic purposes. Kalorr was cloned, using genetic material retrieved from his body taken from the Pagera, and he was immediately instated as an officer of the Blood Raiders. Years later he was even made into a saint.

And to this day the Pagera is closely guarded by Kalorr and his small army of clones, extremely loyal to the Blood Raiders. Drugs, many generations of cloning and a terrible history has rendered the former Amarrian expeditioner completely insane. And despite the Pagera being a popular point of pilgrimage for the members of the Blood Raider organization, few venture there outside of large, heavily armed groups. Kalorr is known to pick off stragglers for his sinister rituals, no matter to which religion or organization they belong to.

Their comrades are still in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, probably looking for any traces you left behind to track you down.  Please remove this threat before they trace your movements here, we'd rather not lose this outpost because of your blunders.

131124.en: Excellent.  I'll have them interrogated immediately.  Then maybe I'll have them sacrificed on the altar.  Yes that will do.

131126.en: A fine job, {[character]player.name}.  We need more people like you around here.

131128.en: I will do as you command.

131129.en: Be on your way then.  I've already updated your NeoCom with the coordinates.  Do not leave any survivors.

131131.en: Uhm, there were a little more than just a "few" clones out there, you filthy liar. I quit.

131133.en:
Unfortunately, we discovered a few stragglers who avoided the fate of those rebels you took care of in that last assignment. Worse, we think they're about to make an attempt to reach an old abandoned stargate in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. Their getting away would be a huge embarrassment, so I want you to get to that stargate first in order to foil their plans.

There's something that will work in your favor though: This particular stargate is a very old model, and it needs to be powered up for a while before it will work. Therefore you'll have a few minutes to destroy the escapees before the stargate is completely powered up. Don't bother to attack the stargate itself ― if you destroy it they'll just warp away, and then who knows when we'll have another chance to catch them.

131134.en: A fine job, {[character]player.name}. And good riddance to those traitorous clones. We'll have to take extra precautions so that this doesn't happen again.

131149.en:
One of the most revered holy sites of the Blood Raiders is located in the constellation OK-FEM. The original Pagera Manton was a gigantic battleship, flagship of a massive Amarrian exploration team seeking unknown systems roughly 200 years ago. However, a malfunction of the then newly built jumpgate into OK-FEM caused an explosion in the Pagera Manton's tachyonometry, resulting in the destruction of its subwarp drives. The ship was stranded in a distant and uninhabited system, and space communication not being as sophisticated as it is today, the Manton had no way of contacting other vessels of the expedition.

Years passed and the crew eventually lost all hope of survival. The food supply running dangerously low, starvation was imminent. Then, one of the senior officers, an Amarr Holder (and secretly a Sani Sabik adherent) by the name of Lieutenant-Commander Kalorr Makur, took matters into his own hands: He staged a successful coup against the ship's commanding officer and had his most loyal followers bind and gag the dissidents within a secure chamber. These unfortunate souls became the new leadership's food supply, although Makur apparently managed to keep this fact secret from most of his followers. According to the ship's logs, maintained by Makur, this plan worked for several years... although there is evidence that Makur did occasionally turn to his own followers to replenish his "stock," hiding his motives behind the guise of executions for crimes supposedly committed against the commander. Eventually, the ship's air supply malfunctioned, and the sixty or so remaining crewmembers slowly suffocated.

Over a century later, some time before the Amarr invasion of the Minmatar homeworlds, the ship was discovered by Amarr outlaws. They found the remains of the crew, and more importantly a few enormous tanks holding thousands of liters of human blood; it seems Makur had dried his human meat before consumption. The blood had been intended as a final food source after the meat supply had run out, but was never actually consumed before Makur and his crew died. Fortunately the containers were kept in cryo-vaults, which despite over a century of decay were still up and working when the Manton was found. And Kalorr Makur's body was discovered in its very own cryo-tank, along with those of his closest allies.

News of the find quickly spread throughout the pirates in the region and thence into the territories of the nascent Blood Raiders, whose revered High Priest declared the Manton a "gift from God." The blood was brought back to the Raider headquarters. Kalorr Makur was cloned using genetic material retrieved from his body, and immediately instated as an officer of the Blood Raiders. Several years later, he was beatified and sainted.

To this day, the floating wreck of the Pagera Manton is closely guarded by Makur and his small army of clones, all extremely loyal to the Blood Raiders. Drugs, many generations of cloning, and a terrible personal history have rendered the former Amarrian capsuleer completely insane. And despite the Pagera being a popular point of pilgrimage for the members of the Blood Raider organization, few even of that cult venture there outside of large, heavily armed groups, for Makur is known to pick off stragglers for his sinister rituals no matter to what religion or organization they belong.

131150.en: Do you have any more tasks for me?

131151.en: I believe it's time to turn our eyes towards the defilers, led by the vile High Priest Heftah Nekmar. He's been a problem for years, and now he has the audacity to venture into our territory to attack our beliefs! He must be punished! An example must be set! And you shall be the deliverer of our wrath.

131154.en: Your destiny obviously lies with the Blood Raider Covenant. And this day is a further testament of that fact. May your reward serve you well.

131155.en:
Welcome to Yakura Harvesting Depot, {[character]player.name}. I have use for someone like you. You see, I'm not the typical Serpentis member, in fact I never took up the stereotypical practice of piracy. Instead I've devoted my life to creating a business which specializes in harvesting gas and rock from the Pegasus constellation. I still work for the Serpentis of course, but I've more interest in finding lucrative roid and gas fields than bullying the passersby.

Anyway, I have a small job for you. Our scanners have indicated that there is a large quantity of gas clouds in a certain area in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We think the source is pretty close to a certain asteroid belt, which has been claimed by an Astral Mining Inc. expedition. I want you to warp over to this asteroid belt and take a sample from one of the asteroids there, bring it back to me for inspection. We're hoping to find gas residue on the rock which would indicate the presence of gas clouds nearby.

131161.en:
The results of our tests indicate that vast swaths of gas clouds should be located not far from where you retrieved the sample. Since we expect the profits of harvesting these clouds to be extremely profitable, we're willing to risk a possible confrontation with Astral Mining Inc.

But first I want you to take care of their current expedition in the area. I want you to go back to where you found the sample and wait for the expedition to arrive. Destroy as many of their ships as you can, but it's imperative that you at least take out their commanding officers. That should cripple them long enough for us to move in and set up our defense perimeter before any reinforcements arrive.

131165.en:
Hey there, {[character]player.name}. I have a task I want you to complete. If you do it right, I might have a small reward for you.

The next Legends Trial battle starts at midnight tonight, and as head of security around here, my job is to make sure it goes as smoothly as possible. However, there is a small problem. The documents detailing the fighters and their ships were scheduled to be delivered to me from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} this morning. However, the courier assigned to the task has obviously failed us, and as such I need you to step up and fill his place. Go get the documents and bring them to me. Do it quickly and I will have a little something extra waiting for you.

Fly safe.

131166.en:
Precisely one week from today, the Gallente Gaming Commission will have another Legends Trial tournament. The famed contestant, Kuroki Tselmi, will be going up against his long-time rival, Hadni Riiuto. Now, everybody loves to see two fighters face each other when they also have a personal dislike for each other. It makes the entire fight that much more intense. Of course, given the nature of mankind, everybody and their pet has placed some money on the outcome of this fight.

Acquaintances of mine also placed money on this fight and we are all hoping that Kuroki Tselmi will win. He usually does, but it probably won't hurt if we try to give fate a little nudge, here. This is where you come in.

I need you to go to Riiuto's agent. When you meet him, have a word with him about this whole business. He'll know what to do next, and we'll all be able to sleep a little easier at night knowing important people won't lose a lot of money on the match.

Now, I have spoken to Riiuto's agent and he sounds fine with it, but keep your wits about you; don't go thinking this is going to be a walk in the bio-dome. This needs to go precisely as planned with no screw-ups, otherwise the Betting Commission will be on top of this like a Gallente escort, and they'll ride this thing for all it's worth if they find out.. I suggest you bring some friends to make sure the agent doesn't feel like telling anyone about this. What do you say, do we have a deal?
