132898.en:
Some years ago, the great Emperor Doriam, in the spirit of co-operation and generosity, allowed some Minmatar refugees to set up home in a former Ammatar station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They were not enslaved, but have been allowed to live free folk, as long as they maintained an excise quota on all of their trade. We have allowed them to continue thus in order to honor the reforms undertaken by Emperor Doriam, but recently one of their number took it upon himself to resist an Imperial customs inspection of their homes, killing the officer in question.

The Minmatar attempted to cover it all up, of course, but we soon got to the bottom of the matter. As they have thrown aside our goodwill and struck down one of the Chosen, the Navy has been ordered to dispense God's judgment upon the heathens. The Admiralty, however, feels that this job is best undertaken by a loyal but independent pilot, rather than official Navy forces, and we have chosen you to dispense with our punishment.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any resistance, so that I can send transports in there to bring back the entire population of the habitats, women, children, and all. After that, destroy all the colony structures, and we will then, in our divine mercy, place any survivors into slavery ― if any are innocent ― and begin them on their path to glorious enlightenment through proper service to the Empire.

Now, we have had reports of Minmatar Republic ships in the area, likely attempting to evacuate the inhabitants: If you are fired upon, you have all authority to defend yourself by any means necessary … and by that, I mean kill them all. God's will be done.

132902.en: Well done. Let us hope they can serve the Empire better now, as do we all.

132903.en: Hm. And here I was under the impression that we all served the Empire. You may be a capsuleer, but you are no emperor.

132904.en: Very kind of you, {[character]agentID.name}. I understand you have some work for me?

132905.en: Perhaps you'd best send in the Navy after all, {[character]agentID.name}. The task is beyond me.

132906.en: Surely this task is beneath me. Spend my time against some piddling Minmatar fleet? I, who destroy battle stations as a matter of course?

132907.en: The Minmatar defenders are no more, {[character]agentID.name}. You can send in your ship to gather the new slaves there.

132908.en: Given freedom, Minmatar will always show their true colors. Yes, I'll happily help to reclaim these infidels for you.

132913.en:
Some years ago, the late Amarr Emperor Doriam ―probably the only enlightened Amarrian to ever have lived ― built an Amarr habitation station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} as a gesture of goodwill. Minmatar were welcomed there and were not enslaved, but have been allowed to live free folk. However, recent governors in that station started to levy outrageous excises on all Minmatar tradesfolk and goods there. Things quickly turned ugly, and recently one of our people got in a fight with an Imperial customs agent; things escalated, and our man ended up killing the officer in question. Knowing what was coming, we managed to evacuate the rest of our people, but the situation is far from resolved.

As you might have guessed, the Amarr have taken this event as cause for military action. They've sent in a number of heavily armed ships, and we fear they're going to try to use the colony as a base of operations for surface raids on nearby planets, taking whatever Minmatar they can as slaves when they leave. We can't let that happen. The Republic Fleet has its hands tied, since any action on their part would result in open war, and we're just not ready for that yet. I need you to get in there!

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any resistance, and then destroy the colony structures so the Amarr can't use them. We have had reports of many Amarr ships in the area: If you are fired upon, as is likely, you have all authority to defend yourself by any means necessary … and by that, I mean kill them all.

132916.en: Good, then. Be careful out there: The Amarr ships in the area are reportedly numerous and powerful.

132917.en: Well done. Let's see the Amarrians try to cover up their political machinations now that their ships were destroyed by “unidentified pirates,” eh? Ha!

132918.en: Hm. And here I'd been given the impression you feared nothing. Hm, indeed.

132919.en: Very kind of you, {[character]agentID.name}. I hear you might have some work for me?

132920.en: Perhaps you'd best send in the Navy after all, {[character]agentID.name}. The task is beyond me.

132921.en: Amarr may not declare open war against the Republic, but they'll certainly send their assassins after a lone captain. No thanks ― no targets on my head!

132922.en: The Amarr ships are no more, {[character]agentID.name}, and their colonies are floating scrap.

132923.en: Of course, {[character]agentID.name}. I'll happily clear out the Amarr scum for you.

132928.en:
Some weird disease has spread through a civilian colony out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We quarantined it and sent some scientists in there to study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Gallente businessman caught wind of this and has figured out that he can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. Now, our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing, which is already underway. But we sure as hell don't want the Gallente getting their hands on this stuff.

Trouble is, this Gallente person, or corporation, or whatever, has already moved on it, paying off some government official and thus getting permission to send in mercenary ships to secure the area. We can't send in our military for fear of political repercussions, so I need someone like you to deal with this matter for me.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any Gallente ships there, and then destroy all the colony structures so no one else gets any ideas about collecting samples of this biological weapon. Now, we've had reports of some tough ships in their fleet: Be careful out there, but be sure to kill them all. We don't want any of them escaping with this virus.

132929.en: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. What can I do for you?

132930.en: I think you'd better hire one of the big mercenary companies for this one. Mordu's, maybe, or some other goons?

132931.en: Biological warfare? Incurable diseases? Uhhm, I think maybe I'll pass on this one. Thanks anyway.

132932.en: All done, {[character]agentID.name}. The enemy ships are destroyed, along with the colony itself.

132933.en: Sure, sounds easy enough. Blow some stuff up. I can do that real well. I'm in.

132938.en: Well, you'd have been at no personal risk, I assure you. But fine, suit yourself.

132939.en: I knew I could trust you to get the job done. Good work. Now let's keep this whole matter between you and me, okay?

132940.en: Good. But I must repeat: The Gallente ships in the area are reportedly numerous and powerful. Be careful.

132941.en: Are you saying you can't do it? Alright, alright, fine. I'll get someone else.

132942.en:
Well, we seem to have a bit of a situation here, and I'm hoping you can help me out. You see, some civilian living in a colony complex out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} brought some creature home from a nearby planet ― I guess he was part of a work detail there or something ― and apparently it was a carrier for some weird disease that quickly spread through the colony. We quarantined the colony and sent some scientists in there to contain and study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Gallente businessman ― we haven't found out who yet ― caught wind of this and has figured out that he can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. Now, the idea had crossed our minds too, of course, but our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing, which is already underway. But we sure as hell don't want the Gallente getting their hands on this stuff.

Trouble is, this Gallente person, or corporation, or whatever, has already moved on it, paying off some government official and thus getting permission to send in mercenary ships to secure the area. We can't send in our military for fear of political repercussions, so I need someone like you to deal with this matter for me.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any Gallente ships there, and then destroy all the colony structures so no one else gets any ideas about collecting samples of this biological weapon. We'll cove the whole thing up as an act of piracy, and it'll soon be forgotten. Besides, we already have samples of the virus for ourselves.

Now, we've had reports of some tough ships in their fleet: Be careful out there, but be sure to kill them all. We don't want any of them escaping with this virus.

132943.en:
Some weird disease has spread through a civilian colon complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We quarantined it and sent some scientists in there to contain and study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Caldari corporation caught wind of the problem and has figured out that it can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. However, our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing. And we sure as hell don't want the Caldari getting their hands on this stuff.

Trouble is, this Caldari corporation has already moved on the civilian complex, no doubt bribing some government official to get permission to send in mercenary ships and thus secure the area. We can't send in our military for fear of political repercussions, so I need someone like you to deal with this matter for me.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any Caldari ships there, and then destroy all the colony structures so no one else gets any ideas about collecting samples of this biological weapon. Be careful out there, but be sure to kill them all, and leave no colony structures intact. We don't want anyone escaping with this virus.

132944.en: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. What can I do for you?

132945.en: I think you'd better hire one of the big mercenary companies for this one. I might just be out of my league here.

132946.en: Biological warfare? Incurable diseases? Uhhm, I think maybe I'll pass on this one. Thanks anyway.

132947.en: All done, {[character]agentID.name}. The enemy ships are destroyed, along with the colony itself.

132948.en: Sure, sounds easy enough. Blow some stuff up. I can do that real well. I'm in.

132953.en: Well, you'd have been at no personal risk, I assure you. But fine, suit yourself.

132954.en: I knew I could trust you to get the job done. Good work. Now let's keep this whole matter between you and me, okay?

132955.en: Good. But I must repeat: The Caldari ships in the area are reportedly numerous and powerful. Be careful.

132956.en: Are you saying you can't do it? Alright, alright, fine. I'll get someone else.

132957.en:
Well, we seem to have a bit of a situation here, and I'm hoping you can help me out. You see, some civilian living in a colony complex out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} brought some creature home from a nearby planet ― I guess he was part of a work detail there or something ― and apparently it was a carrier for some weird disease that quickly spread through the colony. We quarantined the colony and sent some scientists in there to contain and study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Caldari corporation ― we haven't found out who exactly ― caught wind of this and has figured out that it can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. However, our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing. But we sure as hell don't want the Caldari getting their hands on this stuff.

Trouble is, this Caldari corporation has already moved on the civilian complex, no doubt bribing some government official to get permission to send in mercenary ships and thus secure the area. We can't send in our military for fear of political repercussions, so I need someone like you to deal with this matter for me.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any Caldari ships there, and then destroy all the colony structures so no one else gets any ideas about collecting samples of this biological weapon. We'll cove the whole thing up as an act of piracy, and it'll soon be forgotten. Especially by you and me. Right? Okay.

Now, we've had reports of some tough ships in their fleet: Be careful out there, but be sure to kill them all, and leave no colony structures intact. We don't want anyone escaping with this virus.

132958.en:
I recently sent a capsuleer out to investigate disturbing reports from the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system: The number of missing persons cases on some outlying planets there has risen sharply and there have even been reports of lost ships. My capsuleer returned, unfortunately in his pod, but my suspicions were confirmed. What he reported is very disturbing, and we need someone with resources such as you possess to deal with it.

It appears an unprincipled Amarrian Holder has set up a heavily guarded slave breeding facility there. {[character]player.name}, go to this facility, rescue as many of my people as you can, and then reduce the place to cinders! Kill every Amarrian there ― make them pay for what they have done. Leave nothing intact, nothing ― the facilities least of all, lest some other Amarrian come in and occupy them!

132959.en:
This type of breeding facility produces Minmatar children ready to assume their place as servants to the Amarr; rumors abound that the slaves in these places hail from other races as well, including even fallen Amarr who are sent here rather than to penal colonies. 
Brood slaves are held within breeder colonies for years for the sole purpose of increasing a slaver's stock. Discarded when they have outlived their usefulness, these poor people have a terribly short life expectancy, although that fact might be a blessing when one considers the misery of their existence. Slavers who use such methods tend to be secretive about it, anchoring their breeding centers in low-security space; these facilities, however profitable, are looked down upon even in Amarrian society (especially since the Doriam reforms).

132961.en:
I recently sent a capsuleer out to investigate disturbing reports from the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system: The number of missing persons cases on some outlying planets there has risen sharply and there have even been reports of lost ships. The locals are a superstitious lot, so they blame it on angering some spirit or other, but I have no such beliefs ― I suspect foul play. My capsuleer returned, unfortunately in his pod, but my suspicions were confirmed. What he reported is very disturbing, and we need someone with resources such as you possess to deal with it.

It appears an unprincipled Amarrian Holder has set up a heavily guarded slave breeding facility there. You cannot know the sheer horror of these places, our people penned and bred like cattle; the men sold or sent to work camps, the women used mercilessly. The owner no doubt felt that the place would remain undetected in unregulated space, so close here to a ready supply of … well, what I'm sure they would refer to as “livestock.”

{[character]player.name}, go to this facility, rescue as many of my people as you can, and then reduce the place to cinders! Kill every Amarrian there ― make them pay for what they have done. Leave nothing intact, nothing ― the facilities least of all, lest some other Amarrian come in and occupy them!

132962.en: That's truly unfortunate. Now what am I supposed to do?!

132963.en: See to it. Get those poor people out of that hellhole!

132964.en: Ah, wonderful. I knew you wouldn't fail. Justice has been done.

132965.en: Well, I see where your priorities lie…. Good day.

132967.en: I feel bad about those poor people, but the defenses at that compound are beyond me. I give up.

132968.en: I sympathize with the plight of those people, of course, but take on an entire slaver complex by myself? That's suicide. Clones are too expensive for that.

132969.en: I've rescued the slaves and destroyed the facility.

132970.en: Don't worry, I'll make every one of them pay in blood.

132974.en:
{[character]player.name},

Scouts inform me that the station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has been evacuated and disassembled. No doubt the Holder who owned the place caught wind of our efforts, and your tardiness has allowed him time to remove his operation to another system.

May the fates of those slaves weigh on your soul.

{[character]agentID.name}

132975.en:
A couple of years ago, the Serpentis Corporation built a station out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and everyone in the constellation has been worried about it since. At first, as always with the Serpentis, things were fine ― they kept up a clean front and acted like a legitimate corporation. More recently, though, they've been pirating nearby gates and causing all kinds of problems for the local police forces. CONCORD intervention is minimal, of course, in low-sec, and they're always careful to make things seem like some other pirate group is responsible.

These raids must be stopped. And here's an interesting thing: Interstellar law states that an unoccupied station can be freely commandeered. And that Serpentis station apparently has some state-of-the-art tech that we'd like to get our hands on. So that's why I need you: {[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and destroy every damned Serpentis you find there so we can go in and claim the station for our own.

132976.en: Many thanks. I came as soon as I got your message. Is there something I can help you with?

132977.en: I've reconsidered your offer, and I've found it wanting. Sorry, I‘m out.

132978.en: A Serpentis battle station, and you want me to go in there? Are you mad?! Uh... no! As if...!!

132979.en: The Serpentis station is defenseless. Good fight, that was.

132980.en: Oh, yeah, take out some Serpentis? For sure! I hate those guys!

132985.en: Wow, take it easy. I just asked. No harm in asking, is there?

132986.en: Ha! Well done! I knew you wouldn't let me down, {[character]player.name}.

132987.en: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}. Do be careful, though. It won't be an easy job.

132988.en: {[character]player.name}, this was our first real opportunity to strike back at those bloody pirates. I can't believe this!

132989.en:
Yes, indeed. I think the job I have here requires someone of your unique talents.

132991.en:
The Serpentis Corporation was founded a few decades ago by V. Salvador Sarpati. At first a legitimate corporation, it was engaged in hi-tech research, but with time its ties to organized crime grew and the Serpentis research stations, scattered around in remote areas, became infamous pirate havens. Sarpati made a deal with the Angel Cartel early on to gain protection for his stations, and the duty was taken on by the Guardian Angels. Both sides have prospered enormously from this deal ― Serpentis can operate in peace, and the Angel Cartel gets access to the illegal research efforts of the Serpentis.

It is strongly believed that Serpentis is the largest developer and manufacturer of illegal neural boosters, especially since Sarpati's father was a renowned specialist in that field. The home of the Serpentis criminal organization is the Phoenix constellation in the Fountain region.

These raids must be stopped. Like all pests, though, the only way to be sure you're rid of them is to exterminate them entirely, right at the source; if you just kill the ones you see crawling about, you're not accomplishing much. And that's why I need you: My scouts reported just yesterday that a large force of their ships left the base, off to raid nearby systems, so we can make a sudden strike at their home station while their defenses are down, and then clean up the rest later.

{[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and destroy the Serpentis station, along with every damned Serpentis you find there. I imagine you're going to want a few good allies ships along with you, though; I'm sure their base will have reasonably strong defenses.

132993.en: Many thanks. I came as soon as I got your message. Is there something I can help you with?

132994.en: On second thought, you‘d need a squad of dreadnoughts and assault frigates to take down a battlestation! I quit.

132995.en: A Serpentis battle station, and you want me to go in there? Are you mad?! Uh... no! As if...!!

132996.en: The Serpentis station is toast. And I loved every second of it.

133003.en: Ha! Well done! I knew you wouldn't let me down, {[character]player.name}.

133004.en: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}. Do be careful, though. It won't be an easy job.

133005.en: {[character]player.name}, this was our first real opportunity to strike back at those bloody pirates. Well, so be it. Their time will come.

133043.en:
Some of the top cybernetics experts in the region were recently here at {[location]agentStationID.name} for a conference, and they made me a proposal that I found quite intriguing. These scientists theorize that the Sansha mindslave technology is leaps ahead of anything we currently have in the realm of cerebro-emission communications. You might call what they've got a sort of limited telepathy, I suppose. Anyway, these scientists were having heated arguments about the risks and benefits of toying with Sansha tech. And that's where it gets interesting.

A handful of them approached me after the conference and spoke of a Sansha base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that they had learned of. They asked if I knew any ships' captains who might be interested in “acquiring” a few Sansha mindslaves for them to experiment on. Now, a friend in the Admiralty tells me the Navy is apparently planning to move against this station very soon, so our window of opportunity is narrow. We'd be doing the authorities a favor, and getting a little something on the side.

Destroy a Sansha tower and pick up some prisoners. What could be easier?

133044.en: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. I trust you are well. You have some work for me?

133045.en: I think I'd rather not finish this mission. Sorry, second thoughts: Sansha are too creepy.

133046.en: I don't think I care to bring Sansha aboard my ship, thanks very much. No, find someone else.

133047.en: The Sansha Battletower is no more, {[character]agentID.name}, and the prisoners are here in station.

133048.en: Sansha prisoners, eh? Well, I can set my cargo bay to keep them in cryo-containment, I suppose. Sure, I'm in.

133053.en: I understand your reticence, but think of the ISK! Ah, well, your loss.

133054.en: Well done. I'll send the reward directly to your Interstellar account.

133055.en: Excellent. I'll await your return with bated breath … and a heap of ISK.

133056.en: Blast it! Oh, fine. I'm sure I can find someone else to share the reward with me.

133058.en:
{[character]player.name}, an employee of ours, Solen Sagul, has been acting a little odd lately; he comes and goes at strange hours and doesn't say where he is going or where he's been, but he often takes company ships and disappears for days at a time. We are lucky if he shows up for meetings, and when he does appear he utters the strangest things, completely inappropriate and ... well, just unsettling. We could deal with it if we thought he was just insane, but we are afraid it's more than that.

You've heard those stories about people taken alive into rogue drone hives? Well, one of Sagul's co-workers claims he heard the man muttering something about “the hive mother” and “the song of the drones.” We need to be sure that Sagul has not been ... taken by the drones. We had security look around in his logs and they found this location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that he's visited several times in the past months. It's a dark, nasty part of space, though, and I can't send just anyone: Maybe you can take a look and tell us what you find.

Oh, and if you do find anything remarkable there, I need you to get in close and have a good look before you report back to me.

133059.en:

133060.en: You know, a quitter is just another kind of loser.

133061.en: Yes, of course. You might run into some trouble out there, so be careful.

133062.en: Well, that's good news. But I have bad news too. Just give me a moment to finish up here and I'll explain...

133063.en: Fine, be that way. But I assure you, there's more to these stories than most would care to admit.

133064.en:
{[character]player.name},

Unfortunately, Solen Sagul has disappeared entirely. Because I hadn‘t heard anything from you, I hired a recon ship to go check the location I told you about in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; there were signs of drone activity there, but little else. I guess, if there was something more there, it‘s gone now.

I‘m sure you have good reason for not getting this job done on time, but in the future ... do try to be a little more prompt.

{[character]agentID.name}

133068.en: Sure, seems easy enough. I assume the ISK's good, as usual?

133069.en: Well, you were certainly right about the drones: There were a ton of them out there, along with some kind of huge structure. I cleaned the place out, though, so no worries.

133070.en: People taken by drones? Yeah, right. No, I think I'll pass on this one.

133071.en: This is crazy, {[character]agentID.name}. I can't finish this job for you.

133072.en: Good day, {[character]agentID.name}. A pleasure to be back here at the {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} offices. Anything new?

133073.en:
It seems some cybernetics experts among the Caldari and the god-fearing Amarr have recently made efforts to acquire Sansha mindslave technology. Now, we don't know what they're after, specifically, but we can't afford to let them jump ahead of us. We have a couple of sympathizers among them who we think we can convince to defect, so maybe they can keep us up to date on what has transpired with this Sansha research.

Anyway, we know of a Sansha base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and a friend of mine in the Admiralty tells me the Navy is apparently planning to move against this base very soon, so I've devised a plan. Our window of opportunity is narrow, so you'd need to be ready to move fast. We'd be doing the authorities a favor, and allowing our people to remain abreast of the most current scientific theory.

You seem a little confused. Oh, I guess I haven't really filled you in on my little brainstorm… Heh. Ok, here it is: Go out there, destroy the Sansha tower, and pick up some prisoners to bring back here. Easy enough, right?

133074.en: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. I trust you are well. You have some work for me?

133075.en: I think I'd rather not finish this mission. Sorry, second thoughts: Sansha are too creepy.

133076.en: I don't think I care to bring Sansha aboard my ship, thanks very much. No, find someone else.

133077.en: The Sansha Battletower is no more, {[character]agentID.name}, and the prisoners are here in station.

133078.en: Sansha prisoners, eh? Well, I can set my cargo bay to keep them in cryo-containment, I suppose. Sure, I'm in.

133081.en:
Sorry, {[character]player.name}, but I had to hire some mercenaries to get the Sansha prisoners from {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} before the Navy got in there. My apologies, but you were simply taking too long.

{[character]agentID.name}

133082.en:
{[character]player.name},

Unfortunately, the Navy moved in and obliterated the Sansha Battletower in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I guess there are always more Sansha, though.

Oh, that's an awful thought…

{[character]agentID.name}

133083.en: I understand your reticence, but think of the benefit to science! Ah, well, forget it, then. I'll find someone…

133084.en: Fine work. I've managed to scrape together a suitable reward for your work. Thanks, my friend.

133085.en: Excellent. I'll look forward to your victorious return.

133086.en: Blast it! Oh, fine. I'm sure I can find someone else to assist me in this.

Solen Sagul found a way to sneak back into the research facility here in {[location]agentStationID.name}; he got the help of some old friends in the corporation who had no idea he is ... changed. The problem is that he managed to slip out with copies of some preliminary design documents for a prototype battleship that's going to be built here in the station next year. I take it I don't have to tell you how valuable these documents are, nor what would happen if they fall into the wrong hands.

Now, we managed to get a tracking beacon painted onto Sagul's ship as he blasted out of here, and one of our scanning engineers was then able to track him to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We sent a recon pilot out there, and she was able to pick up some heavy drone activity. We need those copies of the design documents destroyed, {[character]player.name}, along with Sagul and all of his “friends.” If you get out there and he isn't around, don't worry: He's bound to show his face out there eventually.

{[character]agentID.name}

{[character]player.name}, an employee of ours, Dimitri Ulanus, has been acting a little odd lately; he comes and goes at strange hours and doesn't say where he is going or where he's been, but he often takes company ships and disappears for days at a time. We are lucky if he shows up for meetings, and when he does appear he utters the strangest things, completely inappropriate and ... well, just unsettling. We could deal with it if we thought he was just insane, but we are afraid it's more than that.

You've heard those stories about people taken alive into rogue drone hives? Well, one of Ulanus's co-workers claims he heard the man muttering something about “the hive mother” and “the song of the drones.” We need to be sure that Ulanus has not been ... taken by the drones. We had security look around in his logs and they found this location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that he's visited several times in the past months. It's a dark, nasty part of space, though, and I can't send just anyone: Maybe you can take a look and tell us what you find.

Oh, and if you do find anything remarkable there, I need you to get in close and have a good look before you report back to me.

133253.en:
Recent advances in station design among the Minmatar, particularly the Sebiestor tribe, have resulted in frighteningly powerful battle stations capable of withstanding tremendous punishment. They are not to be underestimated.

{[character]player.name}, these Minmatar rebels, as you know, are always causing problems, so their raids in outlying systems don't normally draw too much notice. Not normally. Recently, though, we've been hearing rumors about some kind of “super” battle station they're building in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, supposedly with a full capital ship maintenance array. I don‘t really have the resources at hand to investigate these rumors, but just to be safe, maybe I could pay you to check things out for me?

So, could you fly out there and investigate these rumors for me? I'll pay you handsomely. And if you do encounter any Minmatar, or any kind of enemy station, just take care of it for me, won't you? We can't afford that kind of trouble around here. As is standard these days, do it quickly and I'll throw in a substantial bonus. What do you think?

133254.en: Actually, I'm not here for pleasure, but thanks.  I was wondering if you have some work for me. I'd heard you might?

133255.en: I've changed my mind. You'll have to find someone else; I'm vacationing after all.

133256.en: A simple recon mission? No, thank you. I had expected something a little more ... meaningful.

133257.en: There was truth in those rumors. Now, what business do the Minmatar have building a battle station so close to our territory...?

133258.en: I hope there is indeed a station there.  If so, I shall summon my allies and strike at once.

133263.en: Life can't always be blasts and battleships. Who knows what you might have found out there?

133264.en: Good question, {[character]player.name}. And I fear we won't like the answer.

133265.en: How lucky that you arrived here when you did, {[character]player.name}.

133266.en: Well, convenient, that is. And me just having heard that the rumors are true. Guess this is a job for the Navy after all.

133267.en:
“All work and no play,” you know. But I can see that you're determined. Yes, well, there is something I had planned to hand over to the authorities, but maybe you can handle this one without us having to get them involved. In fact, that might be best, now that I think about it.

133269.en: The Sebiestor tribe hails from the inhospitable steppes of the Mikramurka continent in the northern arctic region on the Minmatar homeworld of Matar. The Sebiestors are the most technically inclined of the Minmatar tribes; they were at the forefront in the tentative space exploration program the Minmatars were undertaking just before the Amarrians arrived to subjugate them. Today, most Minmatar ships, and especially stations, tend to be engineered by Sebiestors.

133270.en:
Recent advances in station design among the Minmatar, who have shared their designs through treaty with their Gallentean allies, have resulted in frighteningly powerful battle stations capable of withstanding tremendous punishment. They are not to be underestimated.

We've been hearing rumors about some kind of ultra-powerful battle station the Gallenteans are building, using Minmatar designs, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Supposedly, it's fitted with a full capital ship maintenance array. Now, I don‘t really have the resources at hand to investigate these rumors, but just to be safe, maybe I could pay you to check things out for me? I'll pay you well, of course.

And if you do encounter any hostile Gallente out there, or any kind of enemy station ― how shall I put this...? Eh, take care of it, will you? We can't afford any Gallentean capital ships being built or serviced so close to our territory. Of course, as is common these days, do it quickly and I'll throw in a substantial bonus.

133271.en: Thanks. I hear you might have some work for me. That true?

133272.en: I've changed my mind. You'll have to find someone else. Sorry.

133273.en: A simple recon mission? No, thank you. I had expected something a little more ... meaningful.

133274.en: There was truth to those rumors of a station, that's for sure. What's, or rather who's behind it, I wonder?

133275.en: I'll head out there at once. This just might get interesting.

133280.en: I'm sorry you find things too dull for your liking here, {[character]player.name}.

133281.en: I don't like to think about it, {[character]player.name}. But it bears thinking about.

133282.en: How fortuitous that you arrived here just now, {[character]player.name}. Good luck!

133283.en: Sorry? Sorry?! Hmph. I knew I shouldn't have offered this to a freelancer.

133284.en:
Yes, I do. Good timing. {[character]player.name}, we've been hearing rumors about some kind of ultra-powerful battle station the Gallenteans are building, using Minmatar designs, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Supposedly, it's fitted with a full capital ship maintenance array. Now, I don‘t really have the resources at hand to investigate these rumors, but just to be safe, maybe I could pay you to check things out for me? I'll pay you well, of course.

We can't afford any Gallentean capital ships being built or serviced so close to our territory. Of course, as is common these days, do it quickly and I'll throw in a substantial bonus.

133302.en:
The oligarchic Caldari State stands for corporate capitalism in its purest form. There are eight great “mega-corporations” that together own more than 90 percentage of all property within the State. Each corporation is made up of thousands of companies of various sizes, each with any number of specific market interests, ranging from simple mining companies to powerful security companies. There is no single, unified government as such; each megacorp rules its territories like a kingdom with little or no interference from the others. 
The eight major corporations are Kaalakiota, Sukuuvestaa, Nugoeihuvi, Ishukone, Wiyrkomi, Hyasyoda, CBD, and Lai Dai.

133303.en:
Recent advances in station design among the Caldari, who have shared their designs through treaty with their Amarrian allies, have resulted in frighteningly powerful battle stations capable of withstanding tremendous punishment. They are not to be underestimated.

{[character]player.name}, our scouts have just discovered an extremely powerful battle station the Amarrians are building, combining their efforts with top Caldari military designers, out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The truly frightening part, though, is that the damned thing is apparently pretty much fully operational ― who the hell knows how they've managed to keep the entire project hidden for the months it must have taken to build! ― and worse yet, it's tricked out with a massive capital ship maintenance array.

Now, I don‘t really have the resources at hand to investigate these rumors, and I‘m afraid that it‘s going to take the Navy too long to get out here to deal with the thing. So I imagine you can see where this is all going by now: I need someone to head in there and take that station apart, and it has to happen right now. You think you can handle this one? Needless to say, we can't afford any Amarr capital ships being built or serviced so close to our territory.

133408.en:
A few months ago, a relative of one of the executive officers of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} disappeared for a while. I won't name any names, because we want to avoid tarnishing any valuable reputations. You get me? Okay. We now know that she was involved with some shady fellows, one guy in particular who's known for his close ties to people in the Blood Raiders. I understand he's a pilot who's trying to get accepted into the Raiders' organization, actually.

Now, the girl doesn't want to talk about what happened, but she was pretty messed up and she's now with child. I think she had a crush on this guy for some time, or at least that's what her friends told me. Poor kid. This guy needs to be brought to justice. Terminal justice, if you take my meaning. The beauty of it is, we know he's currently hiding out at a Raider recruitment station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so if we take out that whole station, then we make points with the authorities and we clear up this personal issue at the same time.

So here it is: I want you to go out there and take out that recruitment station ― I mean reduce it to scrap ― along with any Blood Raiders you might find guarding it. Sound good? The reward, as always, will be commensurate with the risk.

133412.en:
The Amarr Empire has had its share of religious cults and fanatics in the past, but few have been as successful, or as much feared, as the Blood Raiders. The Raiders are a corrupted sect of an ancient cult called Sani Sabik, which historically used human blood in its rituals. The Blood Raiders believe that cloned bodies have “purer” blood than other bodies, and this explains their penchant for operating mainly in space, attacking unwary spacefarers and draining their bodies of blood.

The Blood Raiders are led by the fearsome Omir Sarikusa, who has remained on top of the DED most wanted list for many years now. Under his leadership, the Raiders have become more organized, and they have firmly established several bases in the Bleak Lands region.

133428.en:
Formed by two former members of the Caldari Navy who go by the names “Fatal” and “The Rabbit,” the Guristas are a constant thorn in the side of the Caldari State. The Guristas are traditional pirates in the sense that their operation is not based around some creed or ideology, but rather a plain and simple motivation: greed.

The Guristas have starbases close to Caldari space, and from them they embark on daring raids, often into the State itself. Though Guristas pirates are considered more honorable than many of their counterparts, they are still extremely dangerous and not to be tampered with.

133445.en:
The Serpentis Corporation was founded a few decades ago by V. Salvador Sarpati. At first a legitimate corporation, it was engaged in hi-tech research, but with time its ties to organized crime grew and the Serpentis research stations, scattered around in remote areas, became infamous pirate havens. Sarpati made a deal with the Angel Cartel early on to gain protection for his stations, and the duty was taken on by the Guardian Angels. Both sides have prospered enormously from this deal ― Serpentis can operate in peace, and the Angel Cartel gets access to the illegal research efforts of the Serpentis.

It is strongly believed that Serpentis is the largest developer and manufacturer of illegal neural boosters, especially since Sarpati's father was a renowned specialist in that field. The home of the Serpentis criminal organization is the Phoenix constellation in the Fountain region.

133461.en:
Operating from the heart of the Curse region, the Angel Cartel is today the largest and best organized of the space-based criminal factions. The Angels are divided into several groups, each with a very special function; the organization as a whole is commanded by the “Dominations.” In the century they've been lurking in deep space, they have stolen, plundered, or sabotaged countless ships and kidnapped, harassed, or murdered thousands of people.

The Angels recruit members from all races, and are thus not bound to any one area of operation; their touch reaches almost the entire known EVE universe. Many believe that the Angels got their power by uncovering Jovian technologies hidden in their ancient homes, now infested by the Angel Cartel.

133475.en:
One of our patrols spotted a Mordu's Legion strike force not far from here. We have since received intelligence confirming that the Legion has been hired to assassinate one of our high-ranking officials. We can't let this happen, of course, so we need someone of your caliber to destroy them all. Make sure no one survives.

Of course, we ourselves have used the Legion in the past for … well, for various things. So we don't want to make a big political scene out of this if we ever have to hire them in the future. That's why we mustn't send one of our own ships out to confront them. No, you're the right one for this job. Leave no trace behind; I don't want this biting us in the ass later on.

Oh, and one other thing: Our spies inform us that Taisu Magdesh might actually be part of the Mordu strike force, so be extra careful if he appears ― his reputation is hard won.

133476.en:
The origin of Mordu's Legion is an indirect result of the Gallente-Caldari War, during which a group of Intaki military personnel sided with the Caldari. The Intakis were placed into a separate unit commanded by a Caldari officer named Mordu. After the war, the Intakis settled in Caldari space, but unwillingly became embroiled in a battle against Caldari locals in what is now known as the Waschi Uprising. Mordu's Legion formed at that time as a mercenary fighting force, and after the uprising it stayed active, working for the highest bidder ― but, it is said, acting always with integrity and honor.

Mordu's Legion is loosely associated with the Caldari Navy, but remains independent. The Legion is commonly hired by companies to protect valuable assets in low-security space, most often near the Caldari State; for instance, Outer Ring Excavations pays the Legion handsomely to patrol the Outer Ring region.

133501.en:
The Angels have a “research station” out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. That‘s bad enough. Now, last week, a friend told me that a couple of scientists who work for his pharmaceutical corporation were kidnapped by the Angels and taken to their glorified floating drug lab. Their ruffians have been showing up in stations all through the system, and in nearby systems too, pushing some new, experimental drug they're making by the shipload in this station of theirs. “Wrath,” they're calling it. Well, that's the last straw.

I want something done about this, and the Navy doesn't seem to care about what's going on. So I've arranged for a nice little reward for the first captain who's willing to go out there and take out that station. I'm serious. Destroy the whole place, and take out all the pirates you see flying around there. And if you can, bring those scientists back here, too; they have families to feed, for god's sake!

133503.en: I've changed my mind. I‘m sure you can find someone else crazy enough to tackle an Angel battle station.

133504.en: An Angel battle station? Are you nuts?! Uh, ah no...

133505.en: The Angel station is destroyed. And I earned every bit of that reward!

133506.en: Angels? For sure! I hate those guys!

133507.en: Well, it was a long shot. I just hope some other semi-suicidal starship captain is up for the reward...

133508.en: Oh, excellent! I knew you could do it, {[character]player.name}.

133509.en: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}. Be careful out there. It won't be easy.

133511.en:
Ha! Upset!? That‘s an understatement. How would you feel if you had just learned that the Angel Cartel had just taken possession of a battle station in the same constellation you live in with your family?! Bad news, I tell you. And it gets worse. Angel ruffians have been showing up in stations all through the system, and in nearby systems too, I hear, pushing some new, experimental drug they're making by the shipload in this station of theirs. “Wrath,” they're calling it. It's too much, I tell you. I need a drink.

Okay, that's a little better. Now, let me fill you in: A couple of years ago, the Serpentis Corporation built a research station out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and that was bad enough. Things were alright at first, despite the Serpentis‘ reputation, but then rumors started spreading that they were making drugs there, not doing any kind of real research.

And then some local freight-runners reported seeing cargo ships pouring in and out of the place, and the station started expanding, adding sentries and missile batteries, and, inevitably, Angel and Serpentis ships started frequenting the place. Piracy ramped up in local shipping lanes. And now this: We find out that the Serpentis have moved on and pretty much left the place in the hands of the Angels.

Now, last week, a friend told me that a couple of scientists who work for his pharmaceutical corporation were kidnapped by the Angels and taken to their glorified floating drug lab. That's the last straw. I want something done about this, and the Navy doesn't seem to care about what's going on. So I've arranged for a nice little reward for the first captain who's willing to go out there and take out that station. I'm serious. Destroy the whole place, and take out all the pirates you see flying around there. And if you can, bring those scientists back here, too; they have families to feed, for god's sake!

{[character]player.name}, are you the capsuleer for this job?

133513.en:

The Salvation Angels are the least combative division of the Angel Cartel. They are responsible for building and maintaining the Angels' stations and space ships. To this end, they frequently travel with Angel raiding parties in support ships, salvaging what they need from the wrecks their fellow Angels have left in their wake.

Okay, that's a little better. Now, let me fill you in: A couple of years ago, the Serpentis Corporation built a research station out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and that was bad enough. Things were alright at first, despite the Serpentis‘ reputation, but then rumors started spreading that they were making drugs there, not doing any kind of real research.

And then some local freight-runners reported seeing cargo ships pouring in and out of the place, and the station started expanding, adding sentries and missile batteries, and, inevitably, Angel and Serpentis ships started frequenting the place. Piracy ramped up in local shipping lanes. And now this: We find out that the Serpentis have moved on and pretty much left the place in the hands of the Angels.

Now, last week, a friend told me that a couple of scientists who work for his pharmaceutical corporation were kidnapped by the Angels and taken to their glorified floating drug lab. That's the last straw. I want something done about this, and the Navy doesn't seem to care about what's going on. So I've arranged for a nice little reward for the first captain who's willing to go out there and take out that station. I'm serious. Destroy the whole place, and take out all the pirates you see flying around there. And if you can, bring those scientists back here, too; they have families to feed, for god's sake!

{[character]player.name}, are you the capsuleer for this job?

The Salvation Angels are the least combative division of the Angel Cartel. They are responsible for building and maintaining the Angels' stations and space ships. To this end, they frequently travel with Angel raiding parties in support ships, salvaging what they need from the wrecks their fellow Angels have left in their wake.

Lately, our scouts and agents have been reporting increasing numbers of rogue drones, not just here, but throughout civilized space. We think they are building up for a massive attack in all the empires. Who knows what their goal is, really. Honestly I don't care about what the drones do elsewhere, but I want our sovereign space cleared of these machines.

Some recon scans I received yesterday indicate there's a sizeable drone colony being built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Go out there, {[character]player.name}, and clean that hive out. I hate vermin, maybe even more than I hate the idea of those damned Jovians ― at least they are somewhat human.

133639.en: Very well. But I think you gravely underestimate the threat these drones represent.

133640.en:
Just in time for a job that requires a capsuleer of your skill.

You've been working for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} long enough that I think I can trust you with this ... situation. You know we try to keep our eyes on pretty much everything and everyone. Lately, our scouts and agents have been reporting increasing numbers of rogue drones, not just here, but throughout civilized space. We think they are building up for a massive attack in all the empires. Who knows what their goal is, really.

Now, honestly I don't care about what the drones do elsewhere, but I want our sovereign space cleared of these machines. You know how it is with vermin ― once they get a foothold, there is no stopping them. Well, some recon scans I received yesterday indicate there's a sizeable drone colony being built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Hopefully you can deal with them in time before we are overrun by those infernal things and no ships are safe.

Go out there, {[character]player.name}, and clean that hive out. I hate vermin, maybe even more than I hate the idea of those damned Jovians ― at least they are somewhat human.

133661.en:
Quafe has been secretly developing a new soft drink called Quafe Unleashed that they say will revolutionize the entire soft drink industry. But only hours ago, the formula was stolen. Security records show that a Quafe employee, an Amarrian named Galin Famis, has just left the station with the top-secret formula in his possession. Quafe representatives believe that he might be on his way to try to sell or deliver the formula to one of Quafe's competitors, and have offered a reward for the recovery of the formula.

Now, the Amarr government has spoken out against this act of corporate terrorism, but so far they haven't taken any overt actions to deal with it. We could make big points if we could find Famis. We were able to track him for a while, and we've just heard that he's now in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. I'll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom. Stop him before he meets his contact, and bring back the formula.

We're not expecting you to go to war for this, but you should be prepared to meet some rough customers.

Let me make it clear: I want you to go in there and wipe them out. You knocked them off balance with your previous attack. Now you must finish them off.

I've uploaded the location of their hideout in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} into your databank. Now, get going, and don't come back until you've destroyed them.

Do not go into this mission unless you are fully prepared for combat!

133699.en:
Good, my friend. Good. The prisoners you procured for us on your last assignment provided ample information on the Flame of Peace organization. Some of them succumbed admirably to our interrogation techniques, and they have since become newly reformed, docile slaves. But before we wiped their minds, they gave us clues to the location of their leader.

The leader is a woman calling herself simply "Chosen." Apparently she had some sort of delusional religious vision and in a fit of inspiration and creativity, wrote their "sacred text" over the course of a pleasure cruise through the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. And what emerged was the Fellowship of the Flame of Peace.

Let me make it clear: I want you to go in there and wipe them out. You knocked them off balance with your previous attack. Now you must finish them off. I've uploaded the location of their hideout into your databank. Now, get going, and don't come back until you've destroyed them.

133712.en:
This new "religion" is one of the most twisted travesties of faith we have ever encountered. They talk much of peace and love, and all such nonsense, but according to their text, they kill and eat one of their members during their most sacred rituals. After the ritual slaughter, they roast their victim's flesh in the so-called Flame of Peace and share it among the congregation. Now you see how dangerous these deranged fanatics are!

This is highest priority. The data crystals gave us a clue to the location of one of their major enclaves. It lies deep in some rugged deadspace area, and they are likely guarding the entrance. Go there, destroy their habitat, and crush all resistance. Capture some of them alive and bring them back for interrogation.

We know that the cultist have members from all walks of life, civilians and otherwise. Some of them are likely to be experienced combat pilots, though. Don't go out there without fitting your ship for a fight.

We cannot crack the encryption on these odd data crystals you discovered, but the contents appear to be some kind of heretical religious text. Of course, there is only one true religion, so this upstart cult must be stamped out wherever they can be found. However, now that you've destroyed that nest, we need to look for more until these vermin are eradicated.

Deliver the data crystals to the Theology Council's chief cryptographer at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. He has an incredible talent for this sort of thing, and we hope that he can crack the encryption. Perhaps the data inside will offer some clues about this cult's plans and locations.

133737.en: Amarrian theocracy is millennia old and traces its roots back into ancient times, perhaps even before humans ever set foot among the stars. Religion is the backbone of Amarrian society. Countless wars have been fought and lives lost over the proper interpretation of the Amarrian Scriptures.

133738.en:
The Theology Council has caught wind of a religious colony, whose leaders are gathering followers on a remote station in this system. They apparently call themselves the Flame of Peace. Their outpost is in the heart of a deadspace pocket, which is more than a little suspicious. The Council wants to know what these people are up to out there. Of course, we cannot allow the slightest deviation from the practices and beliefs of Holy Scripture, so you must determine if they are gathering a following for some strange new heresy.

If you determine that they are indeed heretics, destroy them without mercy and bring back any evidence you can.

The frigate Sunhammer was recently attacked by Angel Cartel pirates; the captain called for reinforcements and managed to warp away, but the Angels scanned him down and pursued him, and the ship was lost... yet not before the fast-thinking captain jettisoned his cargo to avoid the risk of its being destroyed in the firefight. The captain's pod made it back in one piece, and the cargo's mostly expendible, but for one thing: Among the junk they had to ditch was a Brutor Tribe roster with all the history and lineage of tribal members in this sector from over a century ago.

The roster is absolutely unique; it can't be replaced. We need someone to get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and find the roster. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed. What do you say, {[character]player.name}?

Oh, of course there's a good chance the Angels will still be lingering in the vicinity of the cargo, so be prepared for a fight.

133755.en:
You look pretty green to me, youngster. But we've got a situation here and maybe you can help us out.

The frigate Sunhammer was recently attacked by Angel Cartel pirates; the captain called for reinforcements and managed to warp away, but the Angels scanned him down and pursued him, and the ship was lost... yet not before the fast-thinking captain jettisoned his cargo to avoid the risk of its being destroyed in the firefight. 133757.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}. I'll know who to turn to next time I have a job that needs doing.

133758.en: Don't worry! I'll get the roster back!

133760.en: I'm no rookie. I'm a capsuleer. What do you have for me?

133761.en:
The transport Santaros had a bulkhead failure in a nearby system and was forced to jettison its cargo. Its crew barely made it back in one piece, and the cargo's mostly a dead loss, but among the junk they had to ditch was a relic from Old Amarr, an item of little value to you or me, but vital to Lord Kendron Horowan, a noble who is friendly with House Tash-Murkon. We need someone to get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and find the relic. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed, as well as the gratitude of an important nobleman.

I've uploaded the location of the Santaros's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the relic, get it back to me here.

133763.en:

The transport Santaros had a bulkhead failure in a nearby system and was forced to jettison its cargo. Its crew barely made it back in one piece, and the cargo's mostly a dead loss, but among the junk they had to ditch was a relic from Old Amarr, an item of little value to you or me, but vital to Lord Kendron Horowan, a noble who is friendly with House Tash-Murkon. 133766.en: Don't worry. I'll get the relic back.

133768.en: I'm no rookie. I'm a capsuleer. What do you have for me?

133769.en: Relations between the Federation and the Caldari have never been good in the best of times, and now, with the region arming for war, there is every possibility that the old hatreds between Gallente and Caldari will be reignited. If the Caldari are indeed massing a fleet nearby, it's the job of every patriotic Gallente fighter to stop it.

133770.en: About an hour ago, we received a distress call from one of our scouts in a damaged escape pod; there's a lot of subspace interference, but we were able to make out his location and ID. It sounds as if he was ambushed by Caldari ships. We need someone to head out here and pick him up before the enemy finds him. I've bookmarked the pilot's last known location for you.

133772.en:
You may have been hearing some scuttlebutt about Caldari fleet movements in the area. We suspect that they're up to something big, something that might presage a general conflict. Needless to say, this constellation's been a powder keg for years, and a single spark will set the whole region alight. We're shorthanded here at {[location]agentStationID.name}, but we've got a number of scouts out combing the region looking for signs of enemy activity.

About an hour ago, we received a distress call from one of our scouts in a damaged escape pod; there's a lot of subspace interference, but we were able to make out his location and ID. It sounds as if he was ambushed by Caldari ships. We need someone to head out here and pick him up before the enemy finds him.

Now, I know it's a big task for a newbie like you, but if you're up to it we're ready to offer generous compensation for your time. I've bookmarked the pilot's last known location for you. So, what do you say?

133773.en: Thanks! You don't know what a service you're doing for us!

133774.en: Thank god! We're sending him in to intensive care even as I speak; come back in a little while and I'll let you know if there's anything else we need.

133776.en: He's in bad shape, but he's still alive, {[character]agentID.name}.

133778.en:
Seems the pilot you rescued in your last mission had jumped a couple of Caldari couriers and hacked a data chip containing information on enemy fleet movements from one of their ships. On his way back here, he ran into an enemy destroyer, but was able to warp away and jettison the data chip before the Caldari captain tracked him down and destroyed his ship. Our man gave us the location of the chip he jetted, but now we need someone to go retrieve it.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your ship's database; the data chip is at that location. But I'm afraid there may be enemy fighters about looking for the chip as well. Be careful!

133779.en:
I certainly did. Good timing on your part. That poor devil you brought in didn't make it - his injuries were too severe. But he was able to provide us with some information before he died.

Seems he had jumped a couple of Caldari couriers and hacked a data chip containing information on enemy fleet movements from one of their ships. On his way back here, he ran into an enemy destroyer, but he was able to warp away and jettison the data chip before the Caldari captain tracked him down and destroyed his ship. Our man gave us the location, but now we need someone to go retrieve it. You did well in finding and bringing our guy back, may he rest in peace, and I want you for this job too.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your ship's database; the data chip is at that location, but I'm afraid that there may be enemy fighters about as well looking for the same item. Be careful!

133780.en: Good work! I've handed the chip over to the lab boys for decoding. If it contains what I think it does, I'll have more work for you shortly.

133781.en: I'm ready to do my duty!

133783.en: You asked me to come back for an update on the situation...?

133784.en:
The data on the chip you recovered for us earlier is heavily encrypted, and we think it contains some telemetry data regarding enemy ship movements. We just don't have the right personnel here to get at it, though, and some recent subspace interference is preventing us from communicating with our friends over at the {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} facilities. Deliver the chip for us for decryption.

Make sure the data chip is in your cargohold before you undock.

133785.en:
Yes, and thanks to you, our pilot didn't die in vain. The data on that chip is heavily encrypted, and we think it contains some telemetry data regarding enemy ship movements. We just don't have the right personnel here to get at it, though, and some recent subspace interference is preventing us from communicating with our friends over at the {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} facilities.

Time is of the essence; we need to have this chip delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for decryption. Are you fueled up and ready to go, {[character]player.name}?

133788.en: I dropped off the data chip, {[character]agentID.name}.

133789.en: Oh? Have you retrieved the information on that chip?

133790.en: I thank you, {[character]player.name}. You're a real patriot.

133791.en: Excellent! With your help we'll see to it that those Caldari have a hell of a surprise coming.

133792.en: This report is as good as delivered.

133793.en: Here's my report, {[character]agentID.name}. There's definitely something fishy going on out there.

133794.en: I take it we had some progress in analyzing that telemetry data?

133795.en:
We're organizing a pre-emptive strike to take out their fleet, but the thing is, we can only get so many Navy ships in here to do the job in the short time we have available. More importantly, we need someone we can trust to take out one of their communications tower arrays in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} so the Navy ships can get into position for the attack. We need you to take the array out for us.

This will be a tough fight, so make sure your ship is fitted for a full-scale assault! A shield booster or armor repairer is essential, and you should be prepared to warp out for repairs if you're anywhere near taking hull damage.

133796.en:
We've got those Caldari bastards right where we want them. We're organizing a pre-emptive strike to take out their fleet, but the thing is, we can only get so many Navy ships in here to do the job in the short time we have available. More importantly, we need someone we can trust to take out one of their communications tower arrays in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} so the Navy ships can get into position for the attack.

We need you to take the array out for us. Are you up to this job?

133798.en: Your service is an example to all capsuleers, {[character]player.name}. Here's your reward; you've earned it!

133799.en: Those Caldari are an arrogant bunch of bastards. It'll give me pleasure to pay them back in kind.

133800.en: The com array is down, {[character]agentID.name}. They had some serious defenses out there, but the deed is done.

133801.en: What do you need me to do, {[character]agentID.name}?

133802.en:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places and go to "Bookmarks." Then right-click on the objective item (the corporate records) and choose "Set Destination." Then go to your ship's control panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate star system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click on the corporate records, and select "Warp to within 0." Once you've arrived at the location, look at your Overview and find the cargo container; right-click on it and select "Approach." Once you've approached to within 1500 meters, right-click the cargo container and select "Open." A window will now open, displaying the container's contents. Click and drag the corporate records into your cargo hold. Now return with them to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name} for your reward.

133806.en: Don't worry, I'll get those records back for you.

133808.en: Why, sure. What do you have for me?

133809.en: Your agent has given you the task of locating some lost records. Once you have accepted the mission and undocked, view your mission details by selecting the 'Agent Missions' icon at the top left of your HUD. Then select the 'Lost Records' entry and then 'Warp to Location'. Once you've arrived at the location, proceed onwards until you locate the cargo container; then right-click on it and select "Approach." Once you've approached to within 2000 meters, right-click the cargo container and select "Open." A window will now open, displaying the container's contents. Select the 'Loot All' button to place the records into your cargo hold. Now return with them to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name} for your reward.

133813.en: Don't worry. I'll get those records back.

133815.en: That's why I'm here. Guess I timed that one well...

133816.en:
The famed Dr. Lamia Calus is one of our top nanite research specialists. She has entered a requisition for 47 units of Green Arisite for her research. If you can procure this mineral, I'm sure you'll be adequately rewarded. I have coordinates here to a mining site of ours where a bit of this rare substance can be found.

Green Arisite is related to Gneiss, which is itself rare and is typically found only in low-sec space; pirates and mercenaries of all stripes are often found in its vicinity. Don't go out there in a defenseless mining scow.

133817.en: Excellent. The famed Dr. Lamia Calus is one of our top nanite research specialists.  She has entered a requisition for 47 units of Green Arisite for her research. If you can procure this substantial quantity of mineral, I'm sure you'll be adequately rewarded. The sooner, the better.

133818.en: Scientific progress grinds to halt, thanks to your lack of initiative.

133819.en: Excellent. I've downloaded the coordinates to your NeoCom. Come back soon.

133820.en:
How on earth did they find our secret mining site, I wonder? And who are they working for? Hm.

Well, that's why I needed someone as capable as you to go out there. Listen, I just need a few minutes while I finish entering this data: Come back and see me in a bit.

133821.en: That is unfortunate. Ah, well, I'm sure I can find someone else for this lucrative opportunity.

133822.en: No need to bother with the ore any longer.  You took too long, and our scientist found other resources.  I hope you know that you have missed a golden opportunity.

133823.en: No need to bother with the ore any longer.  You took too long, and our scientist found other resources.  I hope you know that you have missed a golden opportunity.

133827.en: Here's your ore. Some mercenaries had set up a mining op there, but I dealt with it. Now, you mentioned some other work after this?

133828.en: Hm. Okay. Mining doesn't get me in my happy place, but if it's just this one mission and such a small amount...

133829.en:
Dr. Lamia Calus' former mentor was the famous particle physicist and AI specialist, Professor Kajurei Delainen. A number of years of ago, though, Delainen disappeared. He was supposed to report to his laboratory at the appointed time, but he simply never appeared. His living quarters were cleared out and his bank accounts emptied and closed. Yet no evidence of criminal wrongdoing was ever found.

In any case, evidence has just surfaced that he in fact still lives ... and in this very system! Now Dr. Calus has reached a critical stage in her research, and Delainen was once the galaxy's foremost expert on both quantum particle physics and artificial intelligence. He claimed that the two fields were more closely related than anyone realized. His expertise would be invaluable to our current research.

Your mission is to bring him back here. One hitch, though: It is very possible that he will not come willingly. Don't take no for an answer.

133830.en:
You might remember the preeminent scientist, Dr. Lamia Calus, from your previous mission. Her mentor was the famous particle physicist and AI specialist, Professor Kajurei Delainen. Perhaps you've heard of Delainen's "Seven Pillars of Artificial Intelligence"? No? Well, no matter.

A number of years of ago, Delainen disappeared. He was supposed to report to his laboratory at the appointed time, but he simply never appeared. His living quarters were cleared out and his bank accounts emptied and closed. Yet no evidence of criminal wrongdoing was ever found. In such a vast universe, it can be easy for a person to disappear.

In any case, evidence has just surfaced that he in fact still lives ... and in this very system! Now Dr. Calus has reached a critical stage in her research, and Delainen was once the galaxy's foremost expert on both quantum particle physics and artificial intelligence. He claimed that the two fields were more closely related than anyone realized. His expertise would be invaluable to our current research.

Your mission is to bring him back here. One hitch, though: It is very possible that he will not come willingly. Don't take no for an answer.

133831.en: It seems that apprehending a helpless old man is too much for you.

133832.en: Excellent. Do be prompt about this one... and don't hurt him! We need that man unharmed!

133833.en: Oh? Well, nonetheless, splendid! Dr. Calus will be pleased.  Stick around, {[character]player.name}; I'll have some more work for you shortly, I imagine.

133834.en: It seems that apprehending a helpless old man is too much for you.

133835.en: You failed. You won't find Delainen at that location anymore. He sent us a note saying he'd caught wind of your coming and relocated. He has disappeared once again.

133836.en: You failed. You won't find Delainen at that location any longer. He sent us a note saying he'd caught wind of your coming and relocated. He has disappeared once again.

133837.en: Your lack of initiative has cost us

133838.en: Your lack of initiative has cost us

133839.en: Bring back some helpless old man? Piece of cake. Be right back.

133840.en: I have Delainen with me. Uh, just a word of warning, though: He's completely insane!

133841.en: As long as it's not retrieving more ore, I'm good with that.

133842.en: Acceleration gates are not an uncommon sight for most pilots. Like warp gates, each acceleration gate can only be configured for one point in space; unlike warp gates, they can only be used for travel to other points within the same solar system. Acceleration gates can also be locked, preventing pilot from using them. Such locking mechanisms can be based on ship type, on the presence of active guard units in the area, or on appropriate codes/keys.

133843.en:
The letters of Bishop Dalamaid, currently on tour through the Empire, have been stolen by Minmatar terrorists. There's a media lockdown; attention is the only thing the Minmatar could reasonably expect to gain from such a heist. Still, the letters are of extreme importance to the Empire, even if they aren't grounds to mobilize a large force. That's where you come in: I want you to recover the letters for us.

The terrorists were recently spotted in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They're likely using a series of acceleration gates to disguise the true location of their base, a not uncommon tactic. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Follow the terrorists, destroy any resistance, and return the letters to me.

133845.en:
As you may have heard, the letters of Bishop Dalamaid are currently on tour through the Empire. Not only are they of doctrinal significance, but sections dealing with the various scandals of the flesh among the clergy of Dalamaid's time have always been popular. It's a little embarrassing to admit, but these tawdry details are usually the bigger draw, a fact that the Empire has rarely been too ashamed to take advantage of. This tour was one such attempt to use the controversial nature of the letters to get more citizens interested in the Scriptures.

However, the plan has misfired. Minmatar terrorists recently broke into the station where the letters were being kept and have stolen them. There's a media lockdown on the whole thing, for attention is the only thing the Minmatar could reasonably expect to gain from such a heist. Still, the letters are of extreme importance to the Empire, even if they aren't grounds to mobilize a large force. That's where you come in: I want you to recover the letters for us.

The terrorists were recently spotted in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They're likely using a series of acceleration gates to disguise the true location of their base, a not uncommon tactic. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Follow the terrorists, destroy any resistance, and return the letters to me.

133846.en: This will not do, not at all. Now I'll have to find someone else to take care of this.

133848.en: Excellent. More Minmatar terrorists have been sent to their Judgment, and the letters have been returned to Imperial hands. Good work, {[character]player.name}.

133849.en: Oh, sure. Maybe rescuing doctrinal works isn't as sexy as rescuing exotic dancers, but I expected better.

133850.en: You have taken too long in recovering the letters of Bishop Dalamaid. The Minmatar terrorists have escaped; it will take weeks to track them down. I only hope we will be able to recover the letters safely.

133851.en: I can't hold off on the search anymore. I was hoping you could retrieve the letters of Bishop Dalamaid discreetly, but now I have to mobilize an entire force, attracting exactly the sort of attention the terrorists wanted.

133854.en: I'll give those Minmatar terrorists exactly the sort of attention they deserve.

133855.en: I've returned with Bishop Dalamaid's letters.

133856.en: I'm not going to risk my ship against Minmatar fighters just for some stupid old papers.

133857.en: The Minmatar can have the stupid letters. I quit.

133859.en: Acceleration gates are not an uncommon sight for most pilots. Like warp gates, each acceleration gate can only be configured for one point in space; unlike warp gates, they can only be used for travel to other points within the same solar system. Acceleration gates can also be locked, preventing pilot from using them. Such locking mechanisms can be based on ship type, on the presence of active guard units in the area, or on appropriate codes/keys.

133860.en:
The Achuran White Song bird has been sacred to the Achura throughout their recorded history. The creature mates only in the mountains of Saisio III, and naturally is exceedingly rare. Recently, the remnants of the old Achuran government made a gift of two such birds to the State, a male and a female. These particular birds are quite special, in that they have been genetically modified to mate off-planet. This is a matter of tremendous importance for us, from both a diplomatic and an ecological standpoint.

Twelve hours ago, the birds were stolen. Gallentean eco-terrorists hijacked the diplomatic courier mid-transit. Now, I don't think anyone ever needs an excuse to gun for the Gallente, but these guys are more worthless than the Federation Navy. The terrorists were last spotted at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's likely they are using a series of acceleration gates to hide the true location of their base. You'll have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Track down the terrorists, and recover the White Song birds.

133862.en:
