The Achuran White Song bird has been sacred to the Achura throughout their recorded history. The creature mates only in the mountains of Saisio III, and naturally is exceedingly rare. Recently, the remnants of the old Achuran government made a gift of two such birds to the State, a male and a female. These particular birds are quite special, in that they have been genetically modified to mate off-planet. This is a matter of tremendous importance for us, from both a diplomatic and an ecological standpoint.

Twelve hours ago, the birds were stolen. Gallentean eco-terrorists hijacked the diplomatic courier mid-transit. They released a statement claiming that the Caldari State is-- hang on, let me get this right... ah, here it is: "incapable of doing what is best for the longevity of this beautiful species, as demonstrated by their abhorrent destruction of the natural qualities of these rare and fragile..." blah, blah, blah, you get the point.

Now, I don't think anyone ever needs an excuse to gun for the Gallente, but these guys are more worthless than the Federation Navy. The terrorists were last spotted at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's likely they are using a series of acceleration gates to hide the true location of their base. You'll have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Track down the terrorists, and recover the White Song birds.

133863.en: You have no idea what a PR nightmare this will be for the State.

133865.en: Only one survived? Damn it. Well, I'm sure there was nothing you could do. It was those damned Gallente. We won't be able to populate another world with just one bird, but I suppose we can always engineer more.

133866.en: I'm not going to waste time explaining to you what a mistake this is.

133867.en: The Gallentean terrorists escaped from the system and disappeared. Best intel suggests there was a complication, and that both birds will have died while in their "care." If you had acted faster, all this could have been avoided.

133868.en: We lost track of the terrorists. If you'd given me an answer, a more timely response could have been put together to prevent this.

133871.en: I understand my duty. These terrorists will pay. Dearly.

133872.en: The Gallenteans are no more. Sadly, only one of the White Songs survived.

133873.en: Gallente or no, I have more important things to do than rescue a couple of birds.

133874.en: I've had it. This mission is for the-- well, you know.

133875.en: I am ready for whatever you need.

133876.en: Acceleration gates are not an uncommon sight for most pilots. Like warp gates, each acceleration gate can only be configured for one point in space; unlike warp gates, they can only be used for travel to other points within the same solar system. Acceleration gates can also be locked, preventing pilot from using them. Such locking mechanisms can be based on ship type, on the presence of active guard units in the area, or on appropriate codes/keys.

133877.en:
You've heard the legends of King Rouvenor, yes? Founded the kingdom of Garoun, reigned for a hundred years of peace, killed the fabled Giant Long-Limb of Lyace? Everyone knows these tales. Well, most believe them only to be tales. However, a recent archaeological dig has found what could be the old city of Amatore itself! Nothing is certain yet, but this could be the biggest find in the history of the Federation. Already artifacts from the dig are being sent around to scholars across the universe.

Enter the Caldari. An artifact we believe to be the armor of Rouvenor himself was on its way to the University of Caille when it was hijacked by Caldari terrorists! They've issued no demands, but it is clear they wish to do harm to this piece of our cultural heritage.

We've tracked the terrorists to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It is likely they are using a series of acceleration gates to conceal the location of their base, as so many pirates are wont to do. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Track down these despicable terrorists, and restore the Armor of Rouvenor to its people.

133879.en:
Those damned Caldari aren't content to raze our borders and sabotage our economic concerns abroad. Oh, no! Now the bastards are attempting to defile our cultural history!

You've heard the legends of King Rouvenor, yes? Of course you have -- every Gallentean who went to primary school has. Founded the kingdom of Garoun, reigned for a hundred years of peace, killed the fabled Giant Long-Limb of Lyace? Everyone knows these tales. Well, most believe them only to be tales. However, a recent archaeological dig has found what could be the old city of Amatore itself, the wondrous capitol of King Rouvenor! Nothing is certain yet, but this could be the biggest find in the history of the Federation. Already artifacts from the dig are being sent around to scholars across the universe.

Enter the Caldari. An artifact we believe may be the armor of Rouvenor himself was on its way to the University of Caille when it was hijacked by Caldari terrorists! They've issued no demands, but it is clear they wish to do harm to this piece of our cultural heritage.

We've tracked the terrorists to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It is likely they are using a series of acceleration gates to conceal the location of their base, as so many pirates are wont to do. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the terrorists' base. Track down these despicable terrorists, and restore the Armor of Rouvenor to its people.

133880.en: You are spitting on our heritage. All you unpatriotic swine will get yours someday.

133881.en: It is good the Federation can still count on pilots like you.

133882.en: You have the thanks of the entire Federation. With heroes like you, we shall soon bring the peace and glory of Old Gallente to every corner of the universe.

133883.en: I had hoped for better from a citizen of the Federation. Get out of my sight.

133884.en: The Caldari terrorists have absconded with the Armor of Rouvenor, and we do not know where they have gone. The Gallentean people have lost an important part of their history because you did not succeed in your mission.

133885.en: Not only did the Caldari terrorists escape with the Armor of Rouvenor, but now they are publicly decrying it as a fake. The lows they will stoop to in the pursuit of discrediting the Federation are limitless, but the damage is done. Had you decided sooner, this could have all been avoided.

133888.en: I will do this thing, for the glory of what Gallente was and will be again.

133889.en: I have done it. I give you the Armor of Rouvenor.

133890.en: I will risk neither my ship nor my life against these children's stories.

133891.en: The Caldari can have that hunk of rusted metal. I quit.

133893.en: Acceleration gates are not an uncommon sight for most pilots. Like warp gates, each acceleration gate can only be configured for one point in space; unlike warp gates, they can only be used for travel to other points within the same solar system. Acceleration gates can also be locked, preventing pilot from using them. Such locking mechanisms can be based on ship type, on the presence of active guard units in the area, or on appropriate codes/keys.

133894.en:
The Republic needs your help. Twelve hours ago, an Amarrian spy attacked and destroyed a prison convoy in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Most of the guards and prisoners are dead, but one prisoner was rescued: a suspected Amarr sympathizer.

Fortunately, they haven't left the system yet; we've learned that the spy has some sort of forward base established here. He's likely using a series of acceleration gates to disguise the true location of the base, a not uncommon tactic. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the base. Follow the Amarr agent, destroy any resistance, and bring back the sympathizer.

133896.en:
Excellent. Because the Republic needs your help. Twelve hours ago, an Amarrian spy attacked and destroyed a prison convoy in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Most of the guards and prisoners are dead, but one prisoner was rescued: a suspected Amarr sympathizer.

I wish I could say Amarr sympathizers were uncommon. We like to tell ourselves that we cleaned house when we expelled the Nefantar tribe – the Ammatar – from the Republic. But of course life is not so simple. For every ten Minmatar we have fighting to free our brethren from Amarrian captivity or to restore some bit of our displaced old ways, there is one who will sell out his brother for a few ISK. And it only takes one dissenter, one cowardly traitor, to undermine the efforts of hundreds. This is why it is always a top priority for the Republic to ferret out the weak or the corrupt from positions of power. And why the corrupt must be instantly and decisively exterminated.

The prisoner who was rescued is one such figure, formerly a local politician of some influence. He had everyone fooled with his historical conservation initiatives, until an anonymous tip led to his arrest. He was on his way to the Tribunal when the Amarr spy took him ― bastard probably had a deal worked out with the Amarr the whole time.

Fortunately, the Amarr agent hasn't left the system yet; we've learned that he has some sort of forward base established here. He's likely using a series of acceleration gates to disguise the true location of the base, a not uncommon tactic. You will have to approach and activate each acceleration gate you find to progress further to the base. Follow the Amarr agent, destroy any resistance, and bring back the sympathizer.

133897.en: On the contrary, there is no better use of a Minmatar's time than chasing down a traitor. Be gone.

133898.en: Go with the blessings of the tribes.

133899.en:
Good work, {[character]player.name}, I'll just transfer him to— oh, look, I seem to have accidentally opened the airlock he was being kept in! What a tragedy. And the Republic is safer for it.

Remember this lesson well. The true justice of the Minmatar is swift and uncompromising.

133900.en: On the contrary, there is no better use of a Minmatar's time than chasing down a traitor. Be gone.

133901.en: We've lost track of the Amarr agent. Had you acted more quickly, proper justice might have been served. In lieu of direct action on the traitor, the Republic has performed his sentence on his immediate family, both back and forward one generation. Whatever further Minmatar lives are lost as a result of this are on your head.

133902.en: Justice cannot wait for your decision to act. In lieu of direct action on the traitor, the Republic has performed his sentence on his immediate family, both back and forward one generation. You left the Republic with no other choice.

133905.en: I will bring the traitor back to face justice.

133906.en: I have sent the Amarr spy back to his God, and I've brought the traitor back to you.

133907.en: Chasing down a single traitor is not the best use of my time.

133908.en: Chasing down a single traitor is not the best use of my time. I quit.

133909.en: I am always ready to serve the Republic.

133910.en: We need you to go pick up a unique Mechanical Engineering datacore put together for the project by one of Dr. Calus's colleagues not far from here and bring it back as soon as possible. You will be rewarded, of course, as usual.

133912.en: Now, now: I always pay my debts. And now the project can move into the final stage. I hope you're still willing to help out?

133913.en: Scientific progress grinds to halt, thanks to your lack of initiative.

133914.en: Dr. Calus has informed me that your delay in procuring the datacore has put her research irrevocably behind schedule. As such, your involvement is no longer welcome.

133915.en: Dr. Calus has informed me that your delay in procuring the datacore has put her research irrevocably behind schedule. As such, your involvement is no longer welcome.

133918.en: I'd be happy to help. Money's money, eh?

133919.en: I have the datacore. You owe me.

133920.en: Interesting. But how can I help?

133921.en:
Somehow Delainen subverted Calus's research. They inserted the nanites, programmed by Prof. Delainen, into a battlecruiser's systems, but the things immediately began to malfunction. In less than ten minutes, they had changed the structure of the ship to ... something else. It blew a hole through the wall of the station into open space and blasted out of there. Everyone in the lab was killed, including Calus.

We believe that the nanites somehow merged Delainen into the ship they had created, making it some sort of bizarre biomechanical symbiote. But we need to know what happened for certain, and this ― well, this Delainen-ROM symbiote, I guess, for lack of a better name ― is the only thing that can give us the answers.

We want you to go out there and confront it; we've tracked its location, and it's still in this system. I've sent the coordinates to your NeoCom. Destroy it if you must, and then sift through the wreckage to find its central AI core. Bring that back for further study.

133922.en:
Well, that thing is gone, so the station is safe for now. The breached districts have been sealed off until repair crews can get in there. But I suppose you're wondering what happened. Let me back up for a moment.

Dr. Calus's original goal was to create a ship energy system that used advanced nanites to harvest the energy that binds subatomic particles together. The amount of energy that could be produced would be staggering. Think of it. The offensive potential of our ships and weapons systems could be increased a hundred-fold at least, maybe a thousand-fold.

But somehow Delainen subverted Calus's research. He spent years living in close proximity to a nest of rogue drones; he even claimed to have struck up a beneficial relationship with them. Who knows what that does to a person?

They inserted the nanites, programmed by Prof. Delainen, into the battlecruiser's systems, but the things immediately began to malfunction. In less than ten minutes, they had changed the structure of the ship to ... something else. The security 'reels show a flash of light, almost like a jump gate activation, and then Delainen just disappears. Then, immediately, the metallic beast begins to move. We have heard of massive rogue drones, but this is different.

The ship actually spoke to Calus, who was injured during the ship's violent transformation. It said its name was "ROM." Then it blew a hole through the wall of the station into open space and blasted out of there. Everyone in the lab was killed, including Calus.

We believe that the nanites somehow merged Delainen into the ship they had created, making it some sort of bizarre biomechanical symbiote. But we need to know what happened for certain, and this ― well, this Delainen-ROM symbiote, I guess, for lack of a better name ― is the only thing that can give us the answers.

We want you to go out there and confront it; we've tracked its location, and it's still in this system. I'll send the coordinates to your NeoCom. Destroy it if you must, and then sift through the wreckage to find its central AI core. Bring that back for further study.

133923.en: You're just letting that thing loose upon the galaxy! Imagine the havoc it will cause!

133924.en: Good, but move quickly, before it jumps elsewhere. It's hiding in an asteroid field in this system.

133925.en: That is a tremendous relief. You have done well; now we must study this thing for clues about what went wrong. Stick around.

133926.en: You're backing out now? Cowardice does not look good in such an experienced ship commander.

133927.en: You waited too long. The symbiote has somehow slipped away and eluded us. This is on your head. Who knows the havoc that thing will create, who knows how it will evolve!

133928.en: You waited too long. The symbiote has somehow slipped away and eluded us. This is on your head. Who knows the havoc that thing will create, who knows how it will evolve!

133932.en: I have the AI core right here. And it's dripping green goo all over my cargo hold! And the goo is moving!

133933.en: I must've missed it, sorry. What happened?!

133934.en:
Delainen apparently formed some sort of bond or relationship with the rogue drone colony near his previous home. But it's worse than that. Even now there are ongoing subspace transmissions taking place between these drones and the AI unit you recovered ― the thing's intelligence core is most certainly not dead.

The drones have moved around several times, but they're remaining near, for whatever reason. Go to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and destroy that rogue drone colony once and for all. The hive mind CPU and construction center is in the central hive structure. That is your target.

These drones are very, very advanced, and they've had time to build. You might even wish to take some help with you. Once they are all destroyed, salvage the hive mind CPU and return it to us.

133935.en:
Yes, I did. The good Dr. Calus ― whose value to us necessitates our keeping a clone in place for her ― is studying the Delainen-ROM's AI "brain" as we speak. But there's something else we'd like you to do.

Delainen apparently formed some sort of bond or relationship with the rogue drone colony near his previous home. But it's worse than that. Even now there are ongoing subspace transmissions taking place between these drones and the AI unit you recovered ― the thing's intelligence core is most certainly not dead.

The drones have moved around several times, but they're remaining near, for whatever reason. Go to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and destroy that rogue drone colony once and for all. The hive mind CPU and construction center is in the central hive structure. That is your target. Once the drones there are all destroyed, salvage the hive mind CPU and return it to us.

133936.en: If we had thought you a quitter, we would never have hired you in the first place.

133937.en: Of course, my friend, yes. Of course. Just be careful out there!

133938.en: We have little choice, {[character]player.name}; we must understand what has gone on. But we have made progress here as well. Come back when you have time and I'll explain.

133939.en: You're backing out now? Cowardice does not look good in such an experienced ship commander.

133940.en: You waited too long. Apparently, the Delainen-ROM AI core warned them that we were coming: The drones have disappeared and moved. Now, it is unlikely we will ever have the opportunity to fully understand what happened.

133941.en: You waited too long. Apparently, the Delainen-ROM AI core warned them that we were coming: The drones have disappeared and moved. Now, it is unlikely we will ever have the opportunity to fully understand what happened.

133944.en: More weird drones? Yeah … okay, fine. But this had better be worth it!

133945.en: The drone colony is destroyed. I have the hive mind CPU on board. But do you think it is wise to have it so near the AI core? Weren't they communicating somehow?

133946.en: Look, I don't need any weird nanites taking over my ship. I'm done with this.

133947.en: Look, I don't need any weird nanites taking over my ship. I'm done with this.

133948.en: Yeah, it's all cleaned up. But thanks for the concern. You mentioned that I should stick around, though?

133949.en:
We've completed Dr. Calus's study of the Delainen-ROM symbiote's AI core and the CPU you got for us. They're like nothing we've ever seen before. A strange combination of human thought patterns, atomic-scale nanites, and constantly evolving neural networks. And the thing wouldn't stop telling bad jokes! But if those nanites were ever loosed, they could easily latch onto the nearest ship and reconstitute themselves. We just can't risk that happening … again.

But it's also too valuable to destroy. We have placed the items in a special cryogenic container for temporary cold storage. The closest station with an adequate facility for long-term cryogenic storage is in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, though. Please take the container over there for safekeeping.

133950.en:
We've completed Dr. Calus's study of the Delainen-ROM symbiote's AI core and the CPU you got for us. They're like nothing we've ever seen before. A strange combination of human thought patterns, atomic-scale nanites, and constantly evolving neural networks. And the thing wouldn't stop telling bad jokes! But if those nanites were ever loosed, they could easily latch onto the nearest ship and reconstitute themselves. Er, itself. Well, whatever. We just can't risk that happening … again. Which is why it's too dangerous to study further ― the chance of a breakout is just too high.

But it's also too valuable to destroy. We have placed the items in a special cryogenic container for temporary cold storage. The closest station with an adequate facility for long-term cryogenic storage is in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, though. Please take the container over there for safekeeping.

133951.en: You're quitting now, {[character]player.name}?! After everything you've been through? But this is just a courier mission!

133952.en: Excellent. Come back when you're finished.

133953.en: Another job well done, {[character]player.name}. But I need to talk to you again right away ― this isn't over!

133954.en: You're quitting now, {[character]player.name}?! After everything you've been through? But this is just a courier mission!

133955.en: Forget it. We'll find someone else to carry this. We can't just leave it lying around. Such a lack of initiative looks poorly on such an experienced ship commander.

133956.en: You waited too long, so we found someone else to do this. Such a lack of initiative looks poorly on such an experienced ship commander.

133959.en: Yeah, sure. At least I won't have to worry about any green goo this time if it's all frozen.

133960.en: No, thanks. I'm about done with this stupid drone business.

133961.en: On second thought, I'm about done with this stupid drone business. Count me out.

133962.en: Sure. Makes sense. How can I help?

133963.en:
That green goo in your cargohold was far more dangerous than we first realized. Some nanites – perhaps even the very ones from your cargohold – somehow made their way onto a battleship called Solar Cinder, which blasted out of its hangar just a few minutes ago. We don't know what to call this thing now, but it is sentient, and shows many similarities to the Delainen-ROM symbiote. But this is a battleship. An uncontrolled battleship with human-patterned AI ... and capable of self-replication!

We need you to get out there and destroy it! The military is on the way, but they will not be here in force before it has time to escape, if that's what it intends.

This won't be easy. That ship was heavily armed, and the symbiote's drone technology is very advanced. Furthermore, we believe that it can actually "heal" itself. You just might want to get some assistance on this one.

133964.en:
Yes. Very astute, {[character]player.name}. Do you recall that green goo in your cargohold a while back, when you returned with the drone AI core? That material was far more dangerous – and far more cunning – than we first realized. The nanites in the symbiote's AI core were the size of molecules, with atomic-scale manipulator arms. And because they are so small, they are practically undetectable. A billion of them could hide in the crevices of a speck of dust.

Are you frightened yet? You should be. Because they are loose.

Those nanites – perhaps even the self-same ones from your cargohold – somehow made their way onto a battleship called Solar Cinder, which blasted out of its hangar, with no crew, just a few minutes ago. We don't know what to call this thing now, but it is sentient, and shows many similarities to the Delainen-ROM symbiote. But this is a battleship. An uncontrolled battleship with human-patterned AI ... and capable of self-replication! Given time, it could lay waste to an entire planet!

We need you to get out there and destroy it! The military is on the way, but they will not be here in force before it has time to escape, if that's what it intends.

133965.en: You just let that thing loose upon the galaxy! Imagine the havoc it will cause!

133966.en: Good. But move quickly. It's hiding in a deadspace location not far from here.

133967.en: Your assistance has been invaluable, {[character]player.name}. You are a courageous commander. Enjoy your rewards and my personal gratitude. You've more than earned them.

133968.en: You're backing out now? Imagine the havoc that thing will cause!

133969.en: The Solar Cinder drone entity escaped, thanks to you. I must say, I've never been associated with such a shiftless coward.

133970.en: The Solar Cinder drone entity escaped, thanks to you. I must say, I've never been associated with such a shiftless coward.

133973.en: Solar Cinder, huh? How apt: That thing's as good as cinders, now.

133974.en:
Mission accomplished at last. The entity is destroyed. The galaxy is safe.

But I have some repair bills to cover, so... about that reward?

133975.en: This could go on forever. Nah, I'm gonna let the military deal with this one. It's out of my league now.

133976.en: This is crazy. I'm just gonna let the military deal with this one. It's out of my league now.

133977.en: Don't tell me. You mean there's more rogue nanites out there?

133978.en:
Quitting missions (or ignoring them until they "time out," which amounts to the same thing) invariably results in a loss of faction standing; it is almost always in a character's best interest to complete all missions he or she accepts.

However, a character may freely decline a mission when it is first offered, as long as it isn't one of those rare "storyline" missions; after that, declining another mission within four hours of the first does result in a loss of standing. Still, in general, a pilot's career is usually long and eventful enough that a few such minor hits to standing may not be too large a price.

133979.en:
We've been getting a few reports of strange activity in this system. Now, I bet it's just smugglers. And honestly, I'd rather not create too much of a fuss over it ― but it's making the civvies nervous, and they could raise just as much hell for us as any smuggler. So, just go out to these coordinates, poke around a bit, and come back. If anything pokes back, just run.

Or don't do it at all. I mean, what the hell do I care, really? It may be I can find some other work for you if you'd rather not play scout…

133981.en:
We don't stand much on formality here: This isn't a post people seek out to advance their careers. Most of us are content to not be noticed. People start making noise, the hard-asses start remembering we're here, and that means more work for everyone.

But speaking of work, I've got some for you. We've been getting a few reports of strange activity in this system. Now, I bet it's just smugglers. And honestly, I'd rather not create too much of a fuss over it ― but it's making the civvies nervous, and they could raise just as much hell for us as any smuggler. So, just go out to these coordinates, poke around a bit, and come back. If anything pokes back, just run.

Or don't do it. I mean, what the hell do I care, really? It may be I can find some other work for you if you'd rather not play scout…

133982.en: Yeah, I don't blame you. Still, my superiors aren't going to like it. But that doesn't mean I might not have something else for you…

133983.en: Ah, nice. Thanks. My favorite holovid show's about to come on, and I really don't want to miss it.

133984.en: Gallente? Here? You've got to be kidding. Okay, let me set this show to record… gimme just minute and come back, will you?

133985.en: Something else? Yeah, I've got something for you. Come back in a bit.

133986.en: Things are quieting down, so I'm calling off the recon. Any activity now and people will get suspicious.

133987.en: Things are quieting down, so I'm calling off the recon. Any activity now and people will get suspicious.

133990.en: Sure thing. Consider the area poked.

133991.en: Yeah, about this whole scouting thing? Seems you've got Gallente out there. And I don't mean a few.

133992.en: I think I'll pass. You suggested you might have something else?

133993.en: I'm just having so much fun with this mission that I think I should let someone else do it instead. What else have you got?

133995.en: Sometimes a mission might not turn out the way you anticipated. You might have incomplete information from your agent, and conditions can change during the mission. Such changes are generally communicated to you directly, either through a direct pop-up window when using an acceleration gate or by means of a text message appearing in your local chat channel.

133996.en: Okay, here's what I need you to do. I have a few friends in the Intaki Syndicate who owe me for looking the other way during a few local business deals. I need you to hop over to their base and get their support. Do whatever you can. But be sure you're armed. You can never tell what's going on with the Syndicate.

133998.en:
Yeah, slow, right. It's only the Gallente. No big deal. They're just going to turn this whole place into a libertine drone-lover festival, that's all!!

Okay, think, think.

Alright, we know they're building a jump gate in this system, right? And we can't take on both the guards at that gate and the forces they presumably have building up elsewhere in this system. I'll call in the Navy ― they should be here in a matter of hours, I hope ― but we need to occupy these free-loving jerks in the meantime. We need some sort of a distraction....

Okay, here's what I need you to do. I have a few friends in the Intaki Syndicate who owe me for looking the other way during a few local business deals. I need you to hop over to their base and get their support. Do whatever you can. But be sure you're armed. You can never tell what's going on with the Syndicate.

133999.en: I don't think you know quite how hairy things are going to get around here. Fine, alright. Get lost, then.

134000.en: Good. Oh, and if their leader mentions anything about anything like… oh, say, a few outstanding debts? Just tell him he's thinking of the wrong {[character]agentID.name}.

134001.en: The Federation is moving faster than I thought. Still, with the Syndicate's help, this should be a lot easier.

134002.en: Damn it! You and your stupid ethics. Alright, fine. Give me a minute to think of something else and then come back, okay?

134003.en: Took your sweet time, huh? Okay, whatever, I know how it is. Anyway, chatter's coming through that the Intaki Syndicate is moving out. In fact, it sounds like someone pushed them out. If it was the Gallente, our job just got harder. Come and see me right away.

134004.en:
Listen, the Intaki Syndicate is moving out, and so are we. The Navy has arrived to deal with this, finally, and called for a wholesale civilian evacuation, so it's all out of our hands now.

Thanks for nothing.

134007.en: The Intaki Syndicate, huh? Okay, I'll do my best.

134008.en: I found the Intaki. The Gallente were giving them some trouble, but I gave the Gallente more. The Syndicate said they'd help us out.

134009.en: I'm not getting mixed up in criminal affairs. Give me some other option.

134010.en: This is getting too hairy for me. I'm out.

134011.en: Calm down. Take it slowly. We can deal with this.

134012.en: Sometimes agent missions will require you to destroy large structures such as space stations, wrecks, bunkers, or even jump gates. In general, structures can take a serious beating. In fact, some are altogether impervious ― but luckily, this jump gate isn't one of them. Get to it.

134013.en:
Fly to the Gallente jump gate and destroy it. I won't lie to you: The gate is almost certainly more heavily fortified than it was before. The gate itself will probably take a crapload of damage before it's disabled. However, there should be fewer enemy pilots to deal with this time, since they'll all be tied up in the larger battle. Once the jump gate is down, not only will the main Gallente force be without reinforcements, but they won't have a clean exit, and they should flee or surrender.

We've picked up some local chatter from the Gallente saying that only frigate-class ships can get to that jump gate.

134015.en:
Yeah, it would. That's what we're using. Between my few ships and my friends in the Intaki Syndicate, we have enough to occupy what's over here now until the Navy gets here. The problem is that damned jump gate you found.

I can see you sweating already. Calm down. I know you aren't ready for a major fleet op, not yet. And I want to use that to our advantage. We're staging our battle on the other side of the system ― close enough for the Gallente to take the bait, but far enough that that gate will be beyond their sensor range, especially against a frigate-class ship the size of the one you'll need to be flying.

Fly to the Gallente jump gate and destroy it. I won't lie to you: The gate is almost certainly more heavily fortified than it was before. The gate itself will probably take a crapload of damage before it's disabled. However, there should be fewer enemy pilots to deal with this time, since they'll all be tied up in the larger battle. Once the jump gate is down, not only will the main Gallente force be without reinforcements, but they won't have a clean exit, and they should flee or surrender.

134016.en: Damn you! We've risked so much on this operation. The Gallente are pulling out, yeah, but they're mostly escaping with no losses… using the gate you didn't take out. I don't think anyone is going to be calling this a sound victory by any means.

134017.en: That's the spirit. Show those self-righteous Gallente the price of trying to occupy Caldari space.

134018.en:
Terrific news, {[character]player.name}, terrific news. Reports are coming in from the battle. The Gallente are being routed. Their entire formation is broken. And even better, we've captured their command ship. That's going to be one hell of a bargaining chip for us here at {[location]agentStationID.name}.

I have to admit, I was not sure we were going to make it through that alive. Of course, the politicians are probably going to cover all of this up; this sort of event could trigger all out war. But we know what happened, and we know we kept the State safe. And you were instrumental in this victory: You have our deepest thanks, {[character]player.name}.

134019.en:
You know, the universe is big. It can be dangerous. But sometimes things need to get done, even if you'd rather just be lying back with a nice cold rum and Quafe.

I only hope we can pull this off. And you― you can leave. Coward.

134020.en: The battle's over. The Gallente are pulling out. They know that we know where their gate is, and they seem content with having destroyed a good chunk of our forces in this system. They left their gate on a self destruct. It's going to be almost impossible to prove the Gallente were even here. All we have as proof is our dead.

134021.en: The battle's over. The Gallente are pulling out. They know that we know where their gate is, and they seem content with having destroyed a good chunk of our forces in this system. They left their gate on a self destruct. It's going to be almost impossible to prove the Gallente were even here. All we have as proof is our dead.

134022.en: It's all over – you can come out of hiding now

134023.en: It's all over – you can come out of hiding now

134024.en: The Gallente are in for a nasty surprise. I am going to destroy their precious gate, and their ships along with it.

134025.en: Jump gate destroyed. The Gallente are cut off ― and still stupid to boot.

134026.en: This is too big for me. I can't do this. Sorry, but I'm out.

134027.en: Hope for a miracle, because I can't take that gate out.

134028.en: End this? It would take a small fleet to handle these Gallente!

134029.en: At first glance, courier missions may seem a waste of a capsuleer's valuable time. After all, a standard crewed (i.e., non-capsule-controlled) ship could ferry material just as well. The difference is in the security capsuleers bring to a shipment versus standard ship crews. As well, a capsule ship requires a far smaller crew, meaning fewer potential leaks regarding shipping schedules, routes, and cargoes. Further, the capsuleers themselves are more reliable and easier to work with than most other ship command structures, making them a favorite for agents throughout the EVE universe.

134030.en: Our good friends over at CBD have been picking up some strange chatter for the past few days. According to them it has some bearing on what's going on in our system. Go get the intelligence report from the Spacelane Patrol station I've added to your bookmarks, and bring it back here.

134032.en:
Our good friends over at CBD have been picking up some strange local chatter for the past few days. According to them, this chatter has some bearing on what's going on in our system. But I still had to buy the intel from their Spacelane Patrol... I didn't have quite enough favors built up get them to deliver it, and it apparently isn't the sort of thing you just transmit across open space.

Anyway, go get the intelligence report from Spacelane Patrol and bring it back here, would you?

134033.en: Listen, I know I said some stuff before about quitting missions, but it still makes folks uneasy. I mean, it's not a huge deal, but don't make a habit of it.

134034.en: Try to be quick about it. The faster we get things settled around here, the better.

134035.en:
Good work. Let's take a look, here…

Wha―?! Damn! Damn… damn, damn… This isn't good, {[character]player.name}. I'm gonna need your help again.

134036.en: Just so we're clear, you probably shouldn't pass on every mission. Oh, well, your loss.

134037.en: CBD has taken down their intel offer. Somehow they got the impression we weren't that serious about it. If you had acted a bit faster, we'd have it by now.

134038.en: CBD has taken down their intel offer. Somehow they got the impression we weren't that serious about it. If you had acted a bit faster, we'd have it by now.

134041.en: This sounds more to my liking. Sure, I'll do it.

134043.en: No, I think I'll pass on this one too.

134044.en: I've decided I don't want to play space taxi. Thanks, but no thanks.

134046.en: Sometimes agent missions will require you to destroy large structures such as space stations, wrecks, bunkers, or even jump gates. In general, structures can take a serious beating. In fact, some are altogether impervious ― but luckily, this jump gate isn't one of them. Get to it.

134047.en:
Fly to the Gallente jump gate and destroy it. I won't lie to you: The gate is almost certainly more heavily fortified than it was before. The gate itself will probably take a crapload of damage before it's disabled. However, there should be fewer enemy pilots to deal with this time, since they'll all be tied up in the larger battle. Once the jump gate is down, not only will the main Gallente force be without reinforcements, but they won't have a clean exit, and they should flee or surrender.

We've picked up some local chatter from the Gallente saying that only frigate-class ships can get get to that jump gate.

134049.en:
It's not war yet, but it could be soon. I mean, skirmishes aren't that uncommon. The bloodier ones are usually covered up, with neither side gaining much ground. This time, though, might be different. Either way, we have a hell of a fight before us. We damn well could have used some help... Ah, well. Nothing for it. I've put together a small force to try to counter the Gallente, but it does not look good. We're going to have to try something absolutely crazy.

I can see you sweating already. Calm down. I know you aren't ready for a major fleet op, not yet. And I want to use that to our advantage. We're staging our battle on the other side of the system ― close enough for the Gallente to take the bait, but far enough that that gate will be beyond their sensor range, especially against a frigate-class ship the size of the one you'll need to be flying.

Fly to the Gallente jump gate and destroy it. I won't lie to you: The gate is almost certainly more heavily fortified than it was before. The gate itself will probably take a crapload of damage before it's disabled. However, there should be fewer enemy pilots to deal with this time, since they'll all be tied up in the larger battle. Once the jump gate is down, not only will the main Gallente force be without reinforcements, but they won't have a clean exit, and they should flee or surrender.

134050.en: Damn you! We've risked so much on this operation. The Gallente are pulling out, yeah, but they're mostly escaping with no losses… using the gate you didn't take out. I don't think anyone is going to be calling this a sound victory by any means.

134051.en: That's the spirit. Show those self-righteous Gallente the price of trying to occupy Caldari space.

134052.en:
Terrific news, {[character]player.name}, terrific news. Reports are coming in from the battle. The Gallente are being routed. Their entire formation is broken. And even better, we've captured their command ship. That's going to be one hell of a bargaining chip for us here at {[location]agentStationID.name}.

I have to admit, I was not sure we were going to make it through that alive. Of course, the politicians are probably going to cover all of this up; this sort of event could trigger all out war. But we know what happened, and we know we kept the State safe. And you were instrumental in this victory: You have our deepest thanks, {[character]player.name}.

134053.en:
You know, the universe is big. It can be dangerous. But sometimes things need to get done, even if you'd rather just be lying back with a nice cold rum and Quafe.

I only hope we can pull this off. And you― you can leave. Coward.

134054.en: The battle's over. The Gallente are pulling out. They know that we know where their gate is, and they seem content with having destroyed a good chunk of our forces in this system. They left their gate on a self destruct. It's going to be almost impossible to prove the Gallente were even here. All we have as proof is our dead.

134055.en: The battle's over. The Gallente are pulling out. They know that we know where their gate is, and they seem content with having destroyed a good chunk of our forces in this system. They left their gate on a self destruct. It's going to be almost impossible to prove the Gallente were even here. All we have as proof is our dead.

134056.en: It's all over – you can come out of hiding now

134057.en: It's all over – you can come out of hiding now

134058.en: The Gallente are in for a nasty surprise. I am going to destroy their precious gate, and their ships along with it.

134059.en: Jump gate destroyed. The Gallente are cut off ― and still stupid to boot.

134060.en: This is too big for me. I can't do this. Sorry, but I'm out.

134061.en: Hope for a miracle, because I can't take that gate out.

134062.en: Moving against us? This is war!

134063.en: I've been hearing about a rogue drone hive nearby. The Theology Council has been searching for more information on the issue of these… "awakened" drones. Such a matter has a certain interest to those who are given to the study of doctrinal matters. Will you do me the courtesy of investigating the situation and, if possible, bringing one of these strange creatures' AI cores back for study?

134064.en: I've been hearing about a rogue drone hive nearby. The Theology Council has been searching for more information on the issue of these… "awakened" drones. Such a matter has a certain interest to those who are given to the study of doctrinal matters. Will you do me the courtesy of investigating the situation and, if possible, bringing one of these strange creatures' AI cores back for study?

134066.en: That is the most any of us can do, no? It's always good to find someone else with a well-developed moral sense. Do be careful.

134067.en: That is for the Council to decide, of course. Go with God, child, and know that your assistance is appreciated.

134068.en: I will keep you in my prayers.

134069.en: Next time you are called upon, assuming you are called upon, perhaps you will act with appropriate haste.

134070.en: Next time you are called upon, assuming you are called upon, perhaps you will act with appropriate haste.

134071.en: I will do all I can.

134072.en: I found an AI core, but I'm not sure if it will do you any good.

134073.en: I don't think I'm up to that right now.

134074.en: Rogue drones are too weird for me. I'm done.

134075.en: Got any work for a capsuleer, Your Eminence?

134076.en: I've been hearing about an abandoned drone hive nearby. We have yet to find any viable explanation for its presence. I need someone to go investigate and make sure there aren't any rogue drones still hanging around: We need to be certain this is not a threat.

134077.en: I've been hearing about an abandoned drone hive nearby. We have yet to find any viable explanation for its presence. I need someone to go investigate and make sure there aren't any rogue drones still hanging around: We need to be certain this is not a threat.

134078.en: That's a damn shame. I'll have to send out someone who can handle it.

134080.en: That's the Caldari spirit, all right. Well done.

134081.en: Or maybe something. That structure's been dismantled, picked clean. Try to act a little faster next time, huh?

134082.en: Or maybe something. That structure's been dismantled, picked clean. Try to act a little faster next time, huh?

134086.en: I destroyed all the drones in the area. Should be no further threats from that quarter, at least.

134088.en: Sorry, I'm just not up for this.

134090.en:
I've been hearing about an abandoned drone hive nearby. These creatures are undeniably strange, and at this point, any information we can get about them is a boon. Trust me, the university will be happy to have the chance to examine anything you can find, once they know there's no threat of active drones out there.

I need someone to go peruse the area, if you take my meaning? Confirm that it is the "real deal," as it were, and make sure there are no rogue drones still in the vicinity. Does this task seem agreeable to you?

134091.en:
Well, perhaps… Yes. Yes, I've been hearing about an abandoned drone hive nearby. These creatures are undeniably strange, and at this point, any information we can get about them is a boon. Trust me, the university will be happy to have the chance to examine anything you can find, once they know there's no threat of active drones out there.

I need someone to go peruse the area, if you take my meaning? Confirm that it is the "real deal," as it were, and make sure there are no rogue drones still in the vicinity. Does this task seem agreeable to you?

134092.en: That's truly a shame. I knew I needed a first-rate capsuleer for this one, not just some riff-raff pilot.

134093.en: "Up for it." How quaint. You do seem quite the pedestrian. Still, not all covers belie the contents. And it's always good to find someone else with a healthy sense of intellectual curiosity, whatever their manners.

134094.en: Well, that is good news. I'll put the grad students to work on it; maybe we'll be able to come up with a way to use this location for further study.

134095.en: Or perhaps something. That structure has been dismantled in its entirety. Do try to act a little more quickly next time, won't you?

134096.en: Or perhaps something. That structure has been dismantled in its entirety. Do try to act a little more quickly next time, won't you?

134100.en: I found drones out there, but it's all clear now. Send those egg-heads on in there!

134101.en: Nah, I don't think I'm up to that right now.

134102.en: This shit's too weird for me. I'm out.

134103.en: Yeah, there is. You got any work?

134104.en: I see. Well, I cannot say I'm surprised. One look ought to have told me to send you packing.

134105.en: I' been hearin' 'bout this abandoned drone hive nearby. These things are weird, right, but they're also huge ― and really advanced, techonologicalically, you know ― and I'm always on the lookout fer spare parts. I need someone to go check it out, see, confirm it's abandoned; make sure there aren't any rogue drones still hangin' around. See if there's anything useful there ya can bring back fer me.

134106.en: I' been hearin' 'bout this abandoned drone hive nearby. These things are weird, right, but they're also huge ― and really advanced, techonologicalically, you know ― and I'm always on the lookout fer spare parts. I need someone to go check it out, see, confirm it's abandoned; make sure there aren't any rogue drones still hangin' around. See if there's anything useful there ya can bring back fer me.

134107.en: That's a damn shame. I really coulda used those parts.

134108.en: It's always nice to find a like-minded indy-vidual. Careful out there, huh?

134109.en: I'll get this sent down to the shop right away, see what my boys can put together.

134110.en: Oooh. Hoity-toity, eh? Well, fine, suit yerself then.

134112.en: I found some stuff, but I don't know if it will do you any good.

134114.en: I'm not in the mood to go junk-hunting. See you later.

134116.en:
I've got some confidential mining survey reports here I need hand-delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I suspect that there are some fairly valuable mineral deposits nearby and they may need help mining them. Deliver this and I'll see to it that you're suitably rewarded... and put in a good word for you with the station manager. I've entered the station location into your Neocom.

The reports have been placed in your station hangar. Remember to put them in your cargohold before you set out!

134117.en:
I've got some confidential mining survey reports here. There has been a lot of Angel Cartel activity in this area recently, though, and I'm not going to take the risk of sending this over an open channel or even via common courier. I need it hand-delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Deliver this and I'll see to it that you're suitably rewarded... and put in a good word for you with the station manager.

What do you say?

134118.en: Ha. Good. Contact me as soon as you get there, alright?

134119.en: Thanks for the assist. Come back soon and we'll have more work for you.

134120.en: I say… I'm on my way.

134122.en: Thanks, {[character]agentID.name}. What sort of work did you have in mind?

134123.en: Excellent. You had better move. We cannot afford to lose her.

134124.en: What would you have me do?

134125.en:
A slave named Jaliti has escaped from the house of the one of the five Heirs to the Imperial Throne. We don't know why or how, but she has commandeered a luxury transport and is still on the run. The Heir in question, who will of course remain anonymous, demands her return, for he greatly enjoys her beauty and company. She is also privy to a great number of personal secrets that could cause great embarrassment to the Heir, and perhaps even to the Imperial Council.

We intercepted a transmission indicating that she intends to meet a contact in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. We don't know whom she will meet, but you must stop her and bring her back, any way you can. Alive if possible, but dead if necessary. I'm sure if you're successful, the rewards will be substantial. We are dealing with an Heir, after all.

The ship Jaliti commandeered is known to be well-armed. You might need a battle-ready frigate to bring her back.

134126.en: I have the slave in custody and her Minmatar lover is floating ash.

134127.en: Splendid! In custody. Splendid! The Heir will be pleased.

134128.en: I didn't think you were up to this challenge. Perhaps you should go do something less meaningful.

134129.en: Most of the difficult labor in the Empire is performed by legions of uneducated slaves, who serve at the beck and call of those who are both clearly and naturally above their station. From conquered races to hereditary servants, Amarrian slaves are diverse and numerous, and they spend their entire lives working toward enlightenment under the guidance of their rightful masters.

134131.en:
I'm not entirely sure you're ready for an important task like this, but time is of the essence. This may well be the most important mission you have ever undertaken.

A slave named Jaliti has escaped from the house of the one of the five Heirs to the Imperial Throne. We don't know why or how, but she has commandeered a luxury transport and is still on the run. The Heir in question, who will of course remain anonymous, demands her return, for he greatly enjoys her beauty and company. She is also privy to a great number of personal secrets that could cause great embarrassment to the Heir, and perhaps even to the Imperial Council.

We intercepted a transmission indicating that she intends to meet a contact in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. We don't know whom she will meet, but you must stop her and bring her back, any way you can. Alive if possible, but dead if necessary. I'm sure if you're successful, the rewards will be substantial. We are dealing with an Heir, after all.

134132.en: Alas, the window of opportunity through which you might have proven yourself has passed. Fortunately for the Empire, someone else stepped up to challenge instead of you. Your failure will not sit well with those in power, and certainly does not bode well for your future.

134134.en: I think the slave is better off where she's going.

134135.en: You were not paid to think, fool! Your rashness will not sit well with those in power, and certainly does not bode well for your future.

134136.en: Alas, Jalita has surely escaped by now and is lost to us forever. Your failure will not sit well with those in power, and certainly does not bode well for your future.

134138.en: The Vitoc Method is fundamental to the Amarr slave market. The Method has two key components: a deadly, highly toxic drug with a seemingly viral ability to mutate, and its carefully-guarded antidote: Vitoc. The subject infected with the chemically engineered virus will suffer an agonizing death without regular doses of Vitoc; his daily dose, however, will react with the toxin to bring him several hours of euphoria in addition to keeping the virus inert for a short time.

134139.en: Go pick up the Vitoc shipment in its warded container and bring it back to {[location]agentStationID.name}.

134141.en:
Well, some good, some… Heh. Just kidding. No, folks are saying good things about you.

Anyway, listen, I have a lead on a Vitoc shipment not far from here. I've arranged a buy, but I need someone to make the pick-up under the radar. We've arranged for special packaging that will keep the authorities from being able to scan the stuff in your hold, since the stuff is normally highly illegal around here, so you don't need to worry about that.

{[character]player.name}, this could provide the breakthrough our researchers need. Can I trust you to handle it?

134142.en: I'm sorry I entrusted you with something so sensitive.

134143.en: Work fast. We're counting on you.

134144.en: So my source was right about you. Nice. Listen, I should have more work for you soon. I've arranged for a Civilian Relic Analyzer to be placed in your hangar in station; come and see me once you have it fitted on your ship.

134145.en: I understand. Please excuse me; I've no time to waste.

134146.en: Someone bought the Vitoc out from under us. When you're working with smugglers, you work fast, and you don't take anything for granted.

134147.en: I have to find someone who can get this done before our contact sells that Vitoc to someone else. Don't contact me again unless you have the time to do the job.

134153.en: I'm not dealing with drug-runners. I quit.

134154.en: Oh, yeah? All good, I hope. So what's going on?

134155.en:
Hack the wrecked Amarrian science vessel's computers and bring whatever you find back to your agent. Be sure to have some weaponry fitted as well: There's a good chance some pirates have already caught wind of this wrecked vessel as well.

Make sure you fit out the Civilian Relic Analyzer that your agent gave you before you leave the station. You may have to run it for a few cycles before you find anything on the wrecked ship.

134156.en:
Well, I've got a job you can do to prove it. We're always looking for information. After the last job you ran, I think I can trust you with something a little more sensitive.

I just got a tip that there's a wrecked Amarrian science vessel nearby that is likely to contain something useful; apparently it was here on some kind of "goodwill incentive program" devised by some clown in CONCORD, but the ship was jumped by Brutor Tribe radicals before it landed in station. Heh. Stupid CONCORD, and pathetic Amarrians ― no doubt they were using this program to scout for slave-ship raids anyway.

Point is, though, that I need you to get in there and hack it; take whatever data you can from it before the pirates rip the whole thing to pieces for salvage. This is more important to us than you can understand right now. Matari lives may well be at stake here.

134157.en: My source was wrong about you.

134158.en: Your loyalty is in the right place.

134159.en: So my source was right about you. I'll pass your name along. Come back and talk to me again in a while, will you?

134160.en: I see. Don't come back until you're ready to prove yourself worthy of my trust.

134161.en: The pirates beat you to it. There's nothing left of that science vessel.

134162.en: The pirates beat you to it. There's nothing left of that science vessel.

134164.en: I have the information you asked for.

134165.en: This is all a little too dull for me. I'm more of a straightforward, shoot-em-up kind of capsuleer. Good luck finding someone else.

134166.en: Guess I can't be trusted after all. I quit.

134167.en: I can. And I'm glad you feel that way.

134168.en:
The Nefantar go by many names, but Ammatar is the most common ― though their former Minmatar brethren sometimes refer to them as “the Lost Tribe” in pity, but more often “the Fawning” or “the Yoked” in scorn. The Nefantar have left behind their tribal heritage and taken up many (but not all) aspects of the Amarrian religion, a movement that has resulted in a unique blend of cultures.

The Ammatar Mandate and the Minmatar Republic have been locked in a state of cold war for years now; since the Vindication Wars, there hasn't been a large-scale battle between them, mainly due to former Prime Minister Karin Midular's diplomatic efforts. However, after Midular's passing, the animosity between the two peoples cannot be denied.

The old, traditionally aristocratic bloodlines of the Nefantar see themselves as the rightful rulers of all the Matar tribes; for their part, most Minmatar hold little more than bitter animosity toward the tribe that long ago betrayed its cousins, and a widespread hatred of the Ammatar is still common among all other Matari.

134169.en:
One of our research stations has been compromised, and we believe that the Amarr and their allies, the traitorous, mongrel Nefantar, will attempt to destroy it. We need you to get in there and defend the station, for I can't be sure I can mobilize local military forces in time.

The Amarrians will go to any lengths to prevent us from reverse-engineering a treatment that could invalidate the Vitoc Method. If we can make it costly enough for them, though, they may just be forced to give up on this station, with it being so deep in our sovereignty.

134171.en:
One of our research stations ― the very one where I sent the information from that science vessel you hacked for us ― has been compromised, and we believe that the Amarr and their allies, the traitorous, mongrel Nefantar, will attempt to destroy it. As you know, we Minmatar have many small research stations scattered throughout space to better avoid Amarr detection, but as a result, our resources are necessarily splintered.

The loss of this research station would be a tremendous setback to us. We need you to get in there and defend the station, for I can't be sure I can mobilize local military forces in time. The Amarrians will go to any lengths to prevent us from reverse-engineering a treatment that could invalidate the Vitoc Method. If we can make it costly enough for them, though, they may just be forced to give up on this station, with it being so deep in our sovereignty.

134172.en: We will not take this betrayal lightly.

134173.en: You will do what you must.

134174.en: Though this battle was small, it is still a great victory. And already it bears unexpected fruit. Return to me when you are ready to take on a great labor.

134175.en: I hope, for your sake, that you do not come to regret this choice.

134176.en: The station has been destroyed by Nafantar raiders. The Matari lives lost are on your head.

134177.en: We are sending someone who understands the importance of speed. Stand down.

134181.en: The station is safe, and the Ammatar have learned a painful lesson.

134182.en: I don't think I can do that.

134183.en: I can't fight a war by myself! I'm outta here.

134185.en:
This type of breeding facility produces Minmatar children ready to assume their place as servants to the Amarr; rumors abound that the slaves in these places hail from other races as well, including even fallen Amarr who are sent here rather than to penal colonies.

Brood slaves are held within breeder colonies for the sole purpose of increasing a slaver's stock. Discarded when they have outlived their usefulness, these poor souls have a terribly short life expectancy, although that fact might be a blessing when one considers the misery of their existence.

Slavers who use such methods tend to be secretive about it, often anchoring their breeding centers in low-sec or unclaimed space; however profitable, these facilities are generally looked down upon even in polite Amarrian society (especially since the Doriam reforms).

134186.en: Destroy the Amarr Breeding Facility, kill any enemy ships there, and return any enslaved Matari you find to {[location]agentStationID.name}.

134187.en: Amarr Breeding Facilities – Even Death Is Better

134188.en:
We have tracked down an Amarr "breeding facility." {[character]player.name}, I was held in one of these places once, when I was young, and it is only thanks to the efforts of one such as yourself that I find myself a free person today. They're hellholes.

You will find only women and children there; the boys are shipped elsewhere before they turn nine. Most of these facilities don't even bother with Vitoc; they prefer cheaper, more primitive methods of control. After all, the work is hardly complicated: Where humane restraints don't work, brute force and fear often will.

Destroy this place. Rescue as many Matari as you can, but be certain that even those who die are better off.

134189.en: I hope that you are haunted for the rest of your days by the angry spirits of those you refuse to save.

134190.en: Steel yourself, and do what must be done.

134191.en: You have done our people a great service. No reward can be enough, though our means are limited ― still, go with our gratitude.

134192.en: Well, not everyone is capable of such a thing. But a capsuleer is supposed to be made of sterner stuff.

134193.en: The Amarr have swift counter-intelligence. They have moved their operations, and we don't know where.

134194.en: I pray there is still time to rescue those unfortunates. Clearly, that rescue will fall to someone else.

134196.en: You are released from your obligation

134197.en: I understand. I'll do what you ask of me.

134198.en: I've brought back as many as I could.

134199.en: I can't condemn innocent victims to death, even in the face of such an atrocity.

134200.en: I'm not doing this. I'm done here.

134202.en:
When mining for specific minerals, use the Overview to help. Click the small white arrow beside the word “Overview”; from there, select “Load default,” and then “Mining.” Then, you can right-click any type of asteroid in your overview and select “Remove from Overview”; keep doing this until only the type you want is left in your overview.

Now, if you plan to mine this type of ore regularly, you can click the Overview arrow again and select “Save current type selection as…” and put in whatever name seems appropriate. Now you can return to this setting anytime you want to simply by using the Overview arrow to select “Load [type].”

134203.en: Scouts we hired from Minmatar Mining found that there are some significant amounts of Augumene nearby. That's not normally a very valuable substance, but we're using a fabrication process here that utilizes Augumene as a catalyst, so we'll take all we can get. We need 400 units.

134205.en: Well, as we had projected in that report you delivered for me, scouts we hired from the Minmatar Mining Corp found that there are some significant amounts of Augumene nearby. That's not normally a very valuable substance, but we're using a fabrication process here that utilizes Augumene as a catalyst, so we'll take all we can get. We need 400 units. You good for it?

134206.en: Well, get to work then! We'll see you on your return.

134207.en: That's a great help to us, friend. Come back and see me, okay?

134208.en: Doesn't sound too exciting, but I'll do it.

134211.en: First, you'll need to locate Veldspar, Scordite, or other ores that produce Tritanium. Next, mine the ore and transport your cargo back to the station. Open your cargo hold and right-click on the ore, then select "To Hangar and Reprocess." In the next window, you'll see how much Tritanium you'll receive. Once you've reprocessed enough, return with it to your agent to complete the mission.

134212.en: Our production here is going into high gear and we're experiencing shortages of just about everything. We expect everyone to pitch in. I need you to obtain 750 units of Tritanium and deliver them here. You've been reliable so far: care to help out again? You'll get fair compensation for your efforts, plus our gratitude… which isn't worthless, I assure you.

134214.en: Our production here is going into high gear and we're experiencing shortages of just about everything. We expect everyone to pitch in. I need you to obtain 750 units of Tritanium and deliver them here. You've been reliable so far: care to help out again? You'll get fair compensation for your efforts, plus our gratitude… which isn't worthless, I assure you.

134215.en: See you when you get back!

134216.en: Thanks a million, {[character]player.name}. We'll be needing some help on another matter, so come back soon.

134219.en: Sounds good to me. What do you need?

134220.en: If you take too much damage in battle, be sure to warp out to a nearby station for repairs; also be sure to replenish your ammunition if you're running low. Pirates can be pretty tough, so you'll need to be on your toes to deal with them.

134221.en:
It seems that our activity in this system has attracted unwanted attention. Mercenaries and pirates of a variety of allegiances have been preying on our unarmed miners and transports. This can't go on! The industrial production of this sector is vital to our military effort.

Hunt these bastards down. I've uploaded their current location to your NeoCom.

134223.en:
It seems that our activity in this system has attracted unwanted attention. Mercenaries and pirates of a variety of allegiances have been preying on our unarmed miners and transports. This can't go on! The industrial production of this sector is vital to our military effort.

Are you willing to hunt these bastards down? We have lots of pilots who are good mining operators, but only the rare few are also capsuleers capable of taking on pirates and raiders like you can. There's a generous reward in it if you're in, not to mention the bounties and loot on the enemies themselves.

134225.en: I knew we could count on you, {[character]player.name}. We're planning to finish those raiders off once and for all, so stick around, huh?

134226.en: I won't leave one pirate vessel intact.

134229.en:
It looks as if there was some organization behind all the recent pirate activity. We've just learned that they maintain communications in adjacent systems via a communications tower network in this very system! We need someone to take out the pirates' tower array. That someone is you.

I'll enter the locations into your bookmarks. If you leave now, there's every chance you'll catch 'em napping. We'll offer a decent reward plus a bonus if you hit them fast.

134230.en:
It looks as if there was some organization behind all the recent pirate activity. You hurt them in that last mission, but they're still out there. We've just learned that they maintain communications in adjacent systems via a communications tower network in this very system! If one of their scouts is forced to flee, the others maintain contact with him via FTL communications made possible by this com network.

We need someone to take out the pirates' tower array. There's been a lot of subspace chatter over the past few days, and we have a pretty good idea that they're planning something big. We need to hit them hard before that happens, throw a wrench in their plans.

So, would you like to be the one who goes in there and finishes them off? I'll enter the locations into your bookmarks. If you leave now, there's every chance you'll catch 'em napping. We'll offer a decent reward plus a bonus if you hit them fast.

134232.en: Happily, I I consider it well spent. You've proven yourself admirably. This system is a safer place because of you.

134233.en: I'll head out there right away. They don't stand a chance.

134234.en: Those tower arrays are history. Now, about that reward?

134235.en: Hey, {[character]agentID.name}. Alright, tell me about this idea of yours.

134236.en: When you reach your destination system, right-click in open space, and you will find a submenu for this mission. One of the options there is to dock at the desired station: This menu makes it easy for you to go straight there without having to search through the overview list for the destination station.

134237.en: I have a fresh shipment of slaves here that need to be vaccinated, prepped, and properly indoctrinated. Please take them to our facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

134239.en:
Well said, well said.

{[character]player.name}, I have a fresh shipment of slaves here that need to be vaccinated, prepped, and properly indoctrinated. Please take them to our facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Let us not make their keepers wait.

134240.en: You cannot complete a simple mission like this? Hm. That does not bode well for your future in the Empire.

134241.en: That is precisely what I wanted to hear.

134242.en: Well done, {[character]player.name}! But there is indeed something else: You won't believe what has happened! Give me just a moment to finish reading this report and then come speak to me again.

134243.en: That is unfortunate. I'm sure I can find someone else for this lucrative opportunity.

134244.en: I found someone else to take care of this. No need to bother. I should add that your lack of spirit disturbs me…

134245.en: I found someone else to take care of this. No need to bother. I should add that your lack of spirit disturbs me…

134250.en: Thank you. The Empire deserves no less of us.

134251.en: You can usually find the items your agent requires by sifting through the wreckage of destroyed ships or structures, or by looking inside floating cargo containers.

134252.en: A woman named Zira started an uprising among those new slaves almost the moment they arrived at the indoctrination facility. It was a bloody affair, and several guards and innocent citizens were killed or wounded. You are to hunt down Zira, terminate her with extreme prejudice as a lesson to them all, and recapture the other escaped slaves.

134254.en:
Oh, they have their uses, I assure you. Just rule them with an iron hand, my friend.

Anyway, it seems a woman named Zira started an uprising among those new slaves almost the moment they arrived at the indoctrination facility. It was a bloody affair, and several guards and innocent citizens were killed or wounded. This insubordination cannot be tolerated. You are to hunt down Zira, terminate her with extreme prejudice as a lesson to them all, and recapture the other escaped slaves.

Don't waste any time. We've tracked them to a deadspace location, but they may be planning to jump out of the system even as we speak. I've uploaded their location to your NeoCom.

134255.en: What, scared away by the thought of facing a few miserable sub-humans? This does not look good on you. Not good at all.

134257.en: Nice work. These escapees will be severely punished. Now, don't go far; I'm sure I can find something else for you.

134258.en:
Who's paid you to think?! Your job is to do!! Ach!

I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

134259.en: You allowed those filthy, disease-ridden slaves to escape. Now they will carry their pestilence to the rest of the galaxy!

134260.en: You allowed those filthy, disease-ridden slaves to escape. Now they will carry their pestilence to the rest of the galaxy!

134264.en: Slaves in custody. Zira is dead.

134265.en: Let them go. They're not worth the trouble.

134266.en: On second thought, I think we should just let these slaves go. They're just not worth the trouble.

134267.en: More trouble than they're worth, slaves. Alright, what can I do?

134268.en:
You can make multiple consecutive jumps through stargates much more quickly manually than you can relying on Autopilot (because the Autopilot brings your ship out of warp 15 km from the stargate each time you warp, forcing you to then fly at sub-warp speed to within 2,500 m of the gate before jumping).

First, set your destination by right-clicking on the location in the mission details or in your bookmarks. The correct stargate icon will now be highlighted in yellow, both in your overview and in space.

Now, right-click on the stargate (either in space or in the overview) and use the "Warp to within 0 km" option… and then turn on Autopilot; you will drop out of warp directly beside the stargate and, because Autopilot is on, jump immediately. As soon as you begin to jump, turn your Autopilot back off; once you've jumped, simply repeat the whole "Warp to 0 km" process with each stargate along the route until you arrive at your destination system.

134270.en: You cannot complete a simple mission like this? Oh, dear. Oh dear, oh dear, oh dear. This does not bode well for your future in the Empire.

134271.en: It didn't take them long. We were right about this Zira Cobalus. Return immediately so we can discuss the next step.

134272.en: That is unfortunate. I'm sure I can find someone else whose loyalty is not so plainly in question. Keep one eye over your shoulder, my friend.

134273.en: You waited too long. Someone erased all the data we had on this "Zira." Now we will never know the truth.

134275.en: I'll get this over there right away.

134277.en: Oh, I've had enough of this business, I think. Not interested. Sorry.

134278.en: I think I'm going to pack it in after all. I'm tired of being your errand-runner.

134280.en: If your ship is badly damaged and in danger of destruction, you should consider warping away from an encounter. You can repair your ship at most stations, for a cost dependent upon the amount of damage, or you can use Hull Repairers and Armor Repairers to fix the damage yourself while you are in space. But before you try to fit those items to your ship, you should make sure you have the correct skills.

134281.en:
We did intercept an encrypted transmission from Zira's contact. (We sent a recovery team to pick up Zira's remains, and we discovered that she had a cybernetic transceiver implanted in her brain.) Her contact identified himself only as "Helter."

We don't know who he is, but we think, from examinations of his speech patterns, that he is Amarrian. The coordinates of the rendezvous were included in the transmission, and I've uploaded them into your data bank. Go out there and see who we're dealing with. But be careful.

134283.en:
I think you can, yes. Are you ready for another mission, a truly important one? Good.

We did intercept an encrypted transmission from Zira's contact. How could a naked slave with no possessions receive a transmission, you ask? We sent a recovery team to pick up Zira's remains, and we discovered that she had a cybernetic transceiver implanted in her brain. Not a simple cybernetic implant, but something bio-electrical, beyond our current technology, deep in her cerebral cortex.

Her contact identified himself only as "Helter." We don't know who he is, but we think, from examinations of his speech patterns, that he is Amarrian. The coordinates of the rendezvous were included in the transmission, and I've uploaded them into your data bank.

Go out there and see who we're dealing with. But be careful.

134284.en: I was afraid this was too much for you. From now on, we'll have to keep you busy elsewhere... maybe hauling trash or something.

134286.en: Excellent! So, a double agent working with the Minmatar... No surprise, really. Those mindless sub-humans will do anything to stick a thorn in the side of the Empire, and true loyalty is at a premium these days. Now, we do have a chance to finish this before it goes any further: Come see me as soon as you can.

134287.en: I was afraid this was too much for you. From now on, we'll have to keep you busy hauling garbage or something.

134288.en: You waited too long. We have missed an opportunity to thwart the rendezvous and discover the identity of the Amarrian double agent. Your lack of initiative puts your loyalty in question, {[character]player.name}.

134289.en: You waited too long. We have missed an opportunity to thwart the rendezvous and discover the identity of the Amarrian double agent. Your lack of initiative puts your loyalty in question, {[character]player.name}.

134292.en: Sounds more like my kind of work. Sure, I'm in.

134293.en: The contact is an Amarrian, and his name is Garmasi Jowai. He is definitely working with the Minmatar.

134294.en: This sounds too dangerous to me. I don't want to be a spy; just give me some pirates to fight or something.

134295.en: This is too dangerous. Bring in the Navy or something, okay?

134296.en: That's frustrating. Is there some way I can help?

134297.en:
Some deadspace acceleration gates are locked so that you cannot use them until all the enemy ships in the area have been destroyed. If you warp into a deadspace area and you become surrounded by enemies, consider warping out again to repair or to try a different tactic rather than running for the next acceleration gate.

When you warp to an encounter area that you expect might be swarming with enemies, do not use the "Warp to 0 km" option if you can avoid it.
