Instead, warp to 50 km or so, and force your enemies to come to you. This is a useful option particularly if you are outgunned or seriously outnumbered, especially if you use long-range weapons. (Unfortunately, this tactic isn't available in many deadspace locations, but it should be used whenever possible.)

134298.en:
Now is our chance to apprehend Garmasi Jowai. Intel has determined that he is meeting his Minmatar handlers in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Get out there and catch him, and bring him in to face the Emperor's justice.

The strength of the Minmatar force is unknown, but you can bet they'll be heavily armed. You should not attempt this mission without a well-armed ship, and you should be prepared to warp out for repairs if necessary.

134300.en:
Excellent. This is our chance to apprehend Jowai and make him pay — as well as getting some useful intelligence from him. Intel has determined that he is meeting his Minmatar handlers in a remote pocket of deadspace in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Our ships are too far away, and you've shown great courage and resourcefulness up till now.

Get out there and catch him, {[character]player.name}, and bring him in to face Imperial Justice. Our interrogators are quite... skilled. And you will be well rewarded, of course.

134301.en: It seems the Minmatar frightened you off after all. From now on, we'll have to keep you busy hauling garbage or something.

134302.en: Excellent. Glad to have you working on this one.

134303.en: You have done the Empire a great service, {[character]player.name}. You will be handsomely rewarded.

134304.en: It seems the Minmatar frightened you off after all. From now on, we'll have to keep you busy hauling garbage or something.

134305.en: You waited too long. Garmasi Jowai escaped from the rendezvous point with his Minmatar handlers. Your lack of initiative puts your loyalty in question, {[character]player.name}.

134306.en: You waited too long. Garmasi Jowai escaped from the rendezvous point with his Minmatar handlers. Your lack of initiative puts your loyalty in question, {[character]player.name}.

134309.en: You bet. And I'll enjoy every nano-second.

134310.en: Garmasi Jowai is in custody, and his Minmatar flunkies are destroyed.

134311.en: This is too dangerous for me. I think I'll go find something else to do.

134312.en: This is too dangerous. I quit.

134313.en: Yes, I can. And I will.

134314.en:
The Empire has been studying the ships flown by the Minmatar for some time. Though they mostly fly variants of standard Minmatar ships, the Thukkers usually have specific load outs: They favor Explosive and Thermal weapons, and their ships have a low heat tolerance, making Thermal weapons the best to use against them. If you are using laser weapons, X-Ray or Gamma lenses could be good to equip. If you feel like bringing the fight in closer, Multifrequency lenses do even more Thermal damage, but at the cost of range.

Remember, whatever weapon you use to destroy their ships, Thukkers decompress explosively, just like any other Minmatar...

134315.en:
A group of Thukker raiders has taken residence in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. So far they've only hit soft targets, passing industrials and the like. They haven't gotten brave enough to try for a station. And, thanks to you, we won't let them live that long.

Head out to their hiding spot. Wipe the savages out. All of Creation will be a safer place for their deaths. And remain wary. I smell the Minmatar "government" behind all this.

134317.en:
Yes. Minmatar heathens, and pirates as well. As if we don't have enough to worry about with Blood Raider pirates, Gallente political maneuvering, and our own houses trying to screw each other over. We don't need a bunch of bloodthirsty savages coming in here and causing more trouble.

The Thukker raiders have taken residence in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. So far they've only hit soft targets, passing industrials and the like. They haven't gotten brave enough to try for a station. And, thanks to you, we won't let them live that long.

Head out to their hiding spot. Wipe the savages out. All of Creation will be a safer place for their deaths. And remain wary. I smell the Minmatar "government" behind all this.

134319.en: Spoken like a true crusader. Godspeed.

134320.en: Take joy in the knowledge that you have preserved the Empire's peace, and that more damned have been sent to the eternal purgatorial furnace.

134321.en: The Empire was not forged by the timid, my friend, nor can the timid preserve it.

134322.en: The Thukkers attacked a local outpost. Though the savages themselves died in the ensuing battle, the civilian losses were great. Had you acted more quickly, perhaps fewer souls would be awaiting their judgment now.

134323.en: The Thukkers attacked a local outpost. Though the savages themselves died in the ensuing battle, the civilian losses were great. Had you acted more quickly, perhaps fewer souls would be awaiting their judgment now.

134326.en: I will make these Thukkers regret ever coming to this system.

134327.en: Those Thukkers will no longer bother the living.

134328.en: I have no desire to engage these violent beasts. Do you have any idea what it costs to replace a ship like mine these days?

134329.en: I cannot wipe out the Thukkers.

134330.en: What's the problem? Specifically, I mean.

134331.en: A small group of Serpentis pirates has taken up residence in a deadspace pocket here in our system. I want you to fly out there and take these clowns out. Use whatever means you need to. And be careful: I have a feeling that they wouldn't be here this deep into our space unless Gallente agents were behind it.

134333.en:
Great, 'cause we have a slight problem: A small group of Serpentis pirates has taken up residence in a deadspace pocket here in our system. They've been mostly harmless until recently, when the dumbasses actually tried to hold up a Rorqual. As you can imagine, they didn't hurt anybody, but they raised enough ire from high up in the corporation that now we have to do something about them.

I want you to fly out there and take these Serpentis clowns out. Use whatever means you need to. And be careful: I have a feeling that they wouldn't be here this deep into our space unless Gallente agents were behind it.

134334.en:
You know that and I know that, but my boss will not get off my back about it.

Alright, alright, fine. I'll get someone else.

134336.en: Great. Maybe my boss will ease up on me for a while now.

134337.en: You are going to tangle with the Serpentis at some point. Better to tangle with them when they're small and stupid.

134338.en: The Serpentis pulled off a heist on a freighter full of rare ores. That pissed the Navy off something awful. Subsequently the Serpentis thieves had a little run-in with a Navy Raven. The idiots are dead, but we have no idea what they've done with the minerals. If you had acted faster, the State would not have lost these resources.

134339.en: The Serpentis pulled off a heist on a freighter full of rare ores. That pissed the Navy off something awful. Subsequently the Serpentis thieves had a little run-in with a Navy Raven. The idiots are dead, but we have no idea what they've done with the minerals. If you had acted faster, the State would not have lost these resources.

134343.en: Those Serpentis are not coming back… ever.

134344.en: I'm not about to tangle with the Serpentis just because some haulers got spooked.

134345.en: These Serpentis aren't worth the effort.

134346.en: That's me, always willing to help.

134347.en: The Federation Navy and FIO have been investigating the Guristas for years, seeing as they're primarily a Caldari organization. Most of the information is classified, but what is public knowledge is their usual load out: Guristas prefer weapons that do Explosive and Kinetic damage, so watch out for that. Luckily, their ships tend to have poor Kinetic resistance; using pretty much any hybrid charges should work fine, or use Hornets if you're into drones.

134348.en:
What's the matter is the Guristas, of all things; there's a group of them in this system harassing industrials and civilian vessels alike. They don't seem particularly effective as pirates go, but they're brazen enough.

The big concern is that filming for the holo Tears of the Sky is taking place in the same area. Smart money would bet that the Caldari mega-corps are funding these guys; the State is desperate to keep this holo from coming out.

Anyway, the best solution is to just take these Guristas out.

134350.en:
What's the matter is the Guristas, of all things. Yeah, I know, when have Guristas ever caused trouble in these parts, right? It's weird. But nonetheless, there's a group of them in this very system harassing industrials and civilian vessels alike.

Now, they don't seem particularly effective as pirates go, but they're brazen enough. The big concern is that filming for the holo Tears of the Sky is taking place in the same area. It's set to be the best selling version of the Caldari Uprising yet, with a quarter of the Federation's biggest companies all sponsoring it. If the Guristas mess it up, there is going to be a storm of bad press.

Smart money would bet that the Caldari mega-corps are funding these guys; the State is desperate to keep this holo from coming out. They claim it "misrepresents history." Heh, well, whatever else you want to say about 'em, it's a fact that they have no respect for artistic license...

Anyway, the best solution is to just take these Guristas out. You interested?

134351.en: I can understand if you don't want to mess with the Guristas, but I never want to hear you besmirch the holoreel industry again.

134353.en: No, not of the year. Of the century.

134354.en: I know you're young, so you may not fully understand it yet, but believe me when I tell you that nothing is more important than holoreels.

134355.en: The Guristas made a move on the set of Tears of the Sky. Security ships took them out, but this is going to push back the shooting for at least another quarter. Not only is this going to hurt the Gallente economy, but you've disappointed holoreel fans everywhere.

134356.en: The Guristas made a move on the set of Tears of the Sky. Security ships took them out, but this is going to push back the shooting for at least another quarter. Not only is this going to hurt the Gallente economy, but you've disappointed holoreel fans everywhere.

134360.en: The Guristas are… dealt with. Tears of the Sky is still on track to be the best holoreel of the year.

134361.en: I think I have more important things to do than safeguard the filming of a holoreel.

134362.en: To hell with the Guristas, and to hell with this holo.

134364.en: Between our records and CONCORD's, we have a ton of data on the Blood Raiders. They're about what you'd expect from one of the only religious pirate organizations in existence. But what we're most interested in, of course, is how to destroy them, should we need to: They seem to favor Electromagnetic and Thermal weapons; their ships are tough, but vulnerable to EM-based attacks… so EMP ammo would be a good choice for guns, Mjolnir if you are using missiles.

134365.en: A group of Blood Raiders has been seen in this system. This deep in Minmatar space, you can bet the Amarr government is behind it. I need you to go out there and wipe them out, and make it as violent as you can. We want to make sure this hit is noticed. But be careful on this one.

134367.en:
Yeah, Blood Raiders. Never heard of them? The Raiders are a corrupted sect of an ancient cult — I forget the proper name — that historically used human blood in its rituals. Today, they believe that cloned bodies have "purer" blood than others… which is why they operate mainly in space, attacking unwary capsuleers and other rich folks who can afford clones and draining their bodies of blood.

Anyway, a group of Blood Raiders has been seen in this system. Yeah, weird, huh? This deep in Minmatar space?! You can bet the Amarr government is behind this. I need you to go out there and wipe them out. Make it as violent as you can. We want to make sure this hit is noticed. But be careful on this one.

134368.en: It may seem like just a few whacked out pirates, but if we let them escape without punishment, what message are we sending our enemies?

134370.en: That's exactly what I wanted to hear. Good work.

134372.en: The Blood Raiders took out one of our patrols. The Raiders themselves were destroyed, but at considerable loss of life. Had you exterminated them when you were asked to, our dead pilots would still be around.

134373.en: The Blood Raiders took out one of our patrols. The Raiders themselves were destroyed, but at considerable loss of life. Had you exterminated them when you were asked to, our dead pilots would still be around.

134376.en: I will exterminate these Blood Raiders in as bloody a manner as I can.

134377.en: The explosions of the Blood Raider ships could be seen from Athra, I imagine. Boy, did I make a mess of them!

134378.en: I'm busy enough as it is, thanks. But no thanks.

134379.en: I'm not too keen on facing down these Blood Raiders. I quit.

134381.en: Medical doctors being in such short supply, and thus in high demand, few of them are willing to risk their lives for a less lucrative practice than the one they can run comfortably planet-side. On stations, robotic AI Medical Doctors (AIMEDs, more commonly known as "AI Docs" or just "AIDs") are much more common than human medical practitioners, and much more affordable.

134382.en: Pick up the shipment of AIMEDs and deliver them to {[location]agentStationID.name}. Keep in mind that pirates and other unsavory elements are always looking for AIMEDs since medical staff among them are virtually non-existent, so you should be prepared for interference of some kind.

134384.en: I can hardly blame you. I'll have to find someone else to fix those morons' mistake.

134385.en: Good for you. The morons barely deserve the help, but it's my ass if someone goes and dies.

134386.en: Well done. Not a single unnecessary death. And the reward's pretty generous, so it should cover any additional hassle, I think. Sorry for the trouble, though.

134387.en: I can hardly blame you. I'll have to find someone else to fix those morons' mistake.

134388.en:
Those fools went and let ships dock with no medics to give the okay. Turns out one of 'em was carrying some kind of plague, and the whole station ended up sick before they figured out what was going on.

Anyway, you don't need to take the AID parts over anymore. They'll take care of that when they refurbish the place after the hazmat team finishes sterilizing it and incinerating the bodies.

134389.en:
Those fools went and let ships dock with no medics to give the okay. Turns out one of 'em was carrying some kind of plague, and the whole station ended up sick before they figured out what was going on.

Anyway, you don't need to take the AID parts over anymore. They'll take care of that when they refurbish the place after the hazmat team finishes sterilizing it and incinerating the bodies.

134392.en: Yeah, I'll give it a shot.

134393.en: Got the AIDs here. Turned out to be a bit trickier than expected, I might add.

134395.en: Well, that's fortunate! I came to see if you had any work for me.

134396.en: The Prophecy is built on an ancient Amarrian warship design dating back to the earliest days of starship combat. It was originally intended as a full-fledged battleship, but Imperial Navy engineers determined after mixed fleet engagements with early prototypes that the Prophecy would be more effective as a slightly smaller, more mobile Battlecruiser-class.

134397.en: One of our covert ops pilots managed to scan a badly damaged Amarrian Prophecy down in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, but of course he couldn't take her on, even if she was badly damaged; he figured her captain was hiding out until we eased off on stargate security so he could sneak through and get back to Amarr space. Go out there and blow that damaged battlecruiser to hell.

134399.en:
It looks as if the Amarr are getting a little too ballsy. We encountered a small Amarrian skirmish fleet a couple of jumps away and chewed 'em up pretty bad. Their leader was in a Prophecy, which was damaged in the fight, but he managed to warp her away when we demolished his squad. She was nearly hulled, and we want someone to make sure she doesn't make it back to Amarr territory.

One of our covert ops pilots managed to scan the ship down in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, but of course he couldn't take her on, even if she was badly damaged; he figured her captain was hiding out until we eased off on stargate security so he could sneak through and get back to Amarr space. I want you to get out there and take out that damaged battlecruiser, blow her to hell.

Now, I know you'd be willing to do this just to take down some of those arrogant Amarr bastards, but I've arranged for a decent reward anyway. You in?

134400.en: Well, I'll just have to find someone else with the guts to finish the job!

134402.en: Those Amarrians will rue the day they messed with us! We're analyzing the enemy fleet's communications — come back if you're interested in more action.

134403.en: I guess I misjudged you, {[character]player.name}. I'll have to seek help elsewhere.

134404.en: The Amarrian battlecruiser has escaped, possibly with valuable information regarding our force dispositions and capabilities. Your failure to complete this mission is a stain upon both your honor and mine, {[character]player.name}.

134405.en:
{[character]player.name},

Your delay in responding to my request for assistance with the enemy battlecruiser in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has forced me to revoke my offer of employment. I will be seeking assistance from more reliable pilots in future.

134407.en: That battlecruiser's dead, mark my words!

134408.en: The battlecruiser's destroyed. It wasn't alone, and it must've had both hull and armor repairers fitted, 'cause there wasn't a scratch on it when I got there.

134409.en: Hm. No. Not worth my time, one lone battlecruiser. Thanks, but no thanks.

134410.en: That battlecruiser isn't as badly hurt as you claimed, and it sure as hell isn't alone out there. Take your mission and shove it!

134413.en:
The Amarrians were busy out here, I guess — they were up to a lot more than just scouting, it seems. One of their missions was apparently to place mines along some of our major shipping routes. {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, in particular, is full of the blasted things, and we've got a convoy coming through within four standard hours. We need to get someone to both systems and clear out those mines!

These "mines" are quite something, though. They are highly explosive proximity charges built into structures, but when they blow, they also launch a bunch of drones into space to finish off anything not torn entirely apart by the explosion. It's a tough job, but if they're not cleared by the time the convoy gets there, our people are in serious trouble.

You up for it?

134414.en: You think this is a joke, don't you? Good men and women may die because you don't have what it takes to finish a simple job!

134415.en: Well, what are you waiting for? Get out there and get those mines!

134416.en: Good work, kid! Those convoys will get through now. Come on back soon and I'll have some more work for you.

134417.en: Don't ask if you're not serious about wanting work. You've wasted my valuable time.

134418.en: You've delayed too long; our convoy struck a mine and had to turn back. Lives have been lost and our forces in the region have been dealt a serious setback. Well done.

134419.en: I don't like being kept waiting. We've had to abort two convoy missions now and I've had to hire a team of minesweepers to go in there and clear it out. If you're going to treat all my offers this way, don't bother coming back.

134422.en: I'll do it, sure — sounds a little more interesting than your typical shoot-em-up.

134423.en: The convoys are safe. I've dealt with the mines — cunning idea, those. Too bad we didn't think of it first!

134424.en: Surely you must have some cheap ships you can throw away on these mines, right? I mean, why risk my ship?!

134425.en: Sorry, I decided I don't want to risk my ship to clear those mines.

134426.en: I'm back. What do you need? Those Amarr ships were up to no good, I'm sure.

134427.en: We need a fast, competent courier to get these documents for a modified EMP Smart Bomb over to the research wing at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; they need them as a model for the new prototype. I imagine I'll have more work for you as soon as you get back, since they're going to want to start producing these right away. You up for the job?

134428.en:
That convoy you helped get through was more important than you know. In addition to their normal cargo, they were transporting a sealed diplomatic container containing research blueprints for a new EMP Smartbomb II. The next time those Amarr decide to swing through this sector and leave drones for us to find, our boys'll be waiting for them with a few racks of these babies. Those fanatical SOBs won't know what hit 'em.

Anyway, we need a fast, competent courier to get these documents for a modified EMP Smart Bomb over to the research wing at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; they need them as a model for the new prototype. I imagine I'll have more work for you as soon as you get back, since they're going to want to start producing these right away. You up for the job?

134430.en: Excellent work. See me again as soon as you get a chance.

134431.en: Well, it's not the most glamorous job around, fine, but it was vital. Guess I'll find someone else.

134432.en: Those techies over in research are still waiting to create the new smart bomb, {[character]player.name}. I've given the job to someone else.

134433.en: Research needed the docs for that smart bomb yesterday, {[character]player.name}! While you were busy screwing around, I hired someone else for the job.

134437.en: I delivered those smart bomb design documents as requested.

134438.en: I'm not your errand boy. I'm a capsuleer. Find someone else!

134439.en: What's up? Any more minefields need clearing?

134440.en:
Thanks to your help, we've built a number of the advanced EMP smart bombs. We've scheduled testing in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but it looks as if Amarrian intel has realized that something is up: Amarr is dispatching recon ships to all our surrounding systems.

{[character]player.name}, we can't let them observe this weapons test! We need to hit any Amarrian recon ships in the system and destroy them before they can get word back to the enemy. And I have a plan.

We've tracked down a small gang of Amarrian ships nearby. Go in there and attack them so they call for backup, luring their recon ships in to assist; then you can pick them off once they arrive.

134442.en:
Yes, of course. We waste your talents in such banalities, I realize. Still, thanks to your help, we've managed to build a number of the advanced EMP smart bombs. We've scheduled a live test in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but it looks as if Amarrian intel has realized that something is up: Our spies tell us Amarr is dispatching recon ships to all our surrounding systems.

We can't let them observe this weapons test! We need someone to keep the gate closed. We need to hit any Amarrian recon ships in the system and destroy them before they can get word back to the enemy. And I have a plan.

We've tracked down a small gang of Amarrian ships nearby. If you were to go in there and attack them, they would call for backup, luring their recon ships in to assist; then you can pick them off once they arrive.

What do you say? This a little more up your alley? If not, well, I might have something else you can do to help.

134443.en: Good! Now for all that's holy, be careful out there!

134444.en:
The test went without a hitch, thanks to you and our other recon pilots! Now we're ready to take the fight to the enemy.

Come back and see me as soon as you can.

134445.en: Alright, that's fine — not every capsuleer develops recon skills, I know. Let me peruse these files and I'll see what else I can offer.

134446.en: Since you dawdled for too long, the enemy has observed our smart bomb test. They'll be coming here in force any time now, I'm sure. If you want to make up for this failure, come see me.

134447.en: We needed help sooner than this, {[character]player.name}. I've gotten help elsewhere.

134450.en: Definitely! This sounds like something I can sink my teeth into!

134451.en: Not a single enemy ship escaped. The secret testing operation is secure.

134452.en: Sorry, no can do. Sounds like maybe you have something else for me, though?

134453.en: Sorry, this was more than I could handle.

134454.en: Absolutely. Uh, something a little more challenging, though? I mean, any rookie can mine Kernite…

134455.en:
You've been with this assignment since the beginning, so you know we're involved in producing new high-tech EMP smart bombs. Our intel tells us that the enemy fleet is fielding a good number of electronic warfare frigates that like to orbit at close range. Fitting a smartbomb or two would counter this tactic of theirs quite effectively.

{[character]player.name}, it's up to you now.

134456.en:
You've been with this assignment since the beginning, so it's only fitting that you be the one to take the fight to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, where our scouts have detected part of an Amarrian fleet. The Navy will engage the main Amarrian force elsewhere, but we are confident that a capsuleer such as yourself, having proven your skills time and time again, can be trusted to deal with this smaller force.

Be careful out there, {[character]player.name}. I mean it: This one is not going to be easy.

134457.en: You've come this far only to quit? I expected better of you.

134458.en: Prepare for launch then, captain. Good luck!

134459.en: You've done us an invaluable service! Let us hope this reward for a job well done, along with our eternal gratitude, will suffice.

134460.en: You've come this far and now you're backing out?!

134461.en: I'll blow those bastards back to hell!

134462.en: Enemies destroyed. Smart bombs or otherwise, they didn't stand a chance.

134463.en: That sounds suicidal. No offense, but I'm not the pilot for this one.

134464.en: Sorry. There's no way I'm going to be able to complete this mission.

134465.en: Reporting back for more work — you said you might have something big this time?

134466.en: As a result of your failure, the Amarrians now know that we're manufacturing high-tech EMP smart bombs in this vicinity. They can't attack this station — it's too well defended — but they also know we need Mexallon to produce the bombs, and they are trying to cut off our supply. We need someone to deliver some more Mexallon to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. You good for this job, at least?

134467.en: I knew you couldn't hack it, {[character]player.name}. You've just proven it… again.

134468.en: Ha! Some spirit after all. Good! We might make a decent pilot out of you yet!

134469.en: Yes, you've erased that black mark on your record, {[character]player.name}, at least as far as I'm concerned. But do keep the insolence to a minimum from now on, hmm?

134470.en: Coward! I knew you weren't up to it!

134471.en: The enemy has successfully shut down our advanced EMP smart bomb production. Your repeated failure to act has caused considerable damage to this sector.

134472.en: The enemy has successfully shut down our advanced EMP smart bomb production. Your repeated failure to act has caused considerable damage to this sector.

134475.en: Spare me the sarcasm, {[character]agentID.name}. Let's see you go out there and face down an Amarrian fleet! Just give me the stuff and I'll get it there, okay?

134476.en: Okay, your precious minerals are safe. Are we even now?

134477.en: Er, no thanks. I may not have been able to defeat the Amarrian fleet single-handedly, but I'm not some stupid courier.

134478.en: On second thought, I don't think I will deliver the Mexallon. Your insolence is just a bit too… insolent.

134479.en: Uh, "failure" is such a strong word…. Anyway, what can I do?

134481.en: Thanks, youngster! We'll make a real miner of you yet!

134482.en: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you simply won't find it on the market.

134484.en:
We recently found a number of new mining fields in adjacent systems, and the usual assortment of pirate trash has come out of the woodwork to exploit it. We'll need them mined soon because even those thieving bastards have friends in places high enough to put the legal status of these sites in doubt. For some reason they've taken an interest even in Banidine, too, and we'll need to find out why; all my workers are busy with the more profitable fields, but I'm not taking any chances.

I'm uploading a bookmark to your People & Places databank; it shows the location of a Banidine mining operation. I need you to head out there and mine all the Banidine — should be 18,000 units, my foreman tells me. Once we've made an undisputed claim, we're free to mine there again without interference, and I'll provide you with a little something for your trouble.

134486.en: Here's the Banidine ore, {[character]agentID.name}. Seems like a waste of time to me, but hey, you're paying.

134487.en: Listen, just leave the logistics of it all to me, okay? You mine, I plan, you mine some more. That's all you need to know.

134488.en: I'm young, but I'm no rookie – I'll get your ore for you.

134489.en: Thanks, youngster. You may prove yourself yet.

134490.en: Yeah, I'm looking for work. Whatever you've got.

134493.en:
The easiest way to travel to a destination system quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group; once you have selected "Stargate" there, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in the mission details and choose "Set destination." You will notice that the next stargate along your route, both in space and in your Overview, is now yellow.

Next, right-click on the yellow stargate (in space or in the Overview) and select "Warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot, then sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

After you have completed the mission, if you have problems finding your way back to the agent, simply open the "People and Places" window from your NeoCom and check the Agents tab; the agent you are working for should be displayed there. Right-click on the appropriate agent and select "Set destination," then turn on your Autopilot to make your way back to the agent's system.

134495.en:
Damnation, they're sending them out younger and younger. Are you sure you're old enough to fly a starship? Oh, well, we have to play the hand we're dealt, and if you're the best I can get, I suppose you'll do.

We'll start simple, youngster. Banidine is normally all but worthless, so real miners don't usually bother with the stuff. Still, I've found a buyer who's willing to take whatever we can mine. So, get me 20,000 units of Banidine and I'll make it worth your while. It should be easy, even for a pup like you, but it will show me that you're serious.

There's an asteroid field near here that's lousy with the stuff – I've bookmarked it for you. Get back as soon as you can and I'll arrange a little bonus.

134496.en: Twenty thousand Banidine? That doesn't sound too tough. Sure, I'm good for it.

134497.en: Great, great. Maybe now I can get some work done.

134498.en: You look preoccupied. Something I can help you with?

134500.en:
Excellent! Maybe I'll finally get that raise.

Oh, uh, good job. Here's your payment.

134501.en: Uhh... nah. Sorry. That's a little too pedestrian for me.

134502.en: Dammit, don't make me mine this crap myself. I hate mining.

134503.en: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother putting it into their mining packages when they produce ship scanners. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in the mission details and select "Add to Overview."

134505.en:
Well, maybe, yeah. Have you ever heard of Banidine? Doesn't matter, you have now. Anyway, my boss wants the stuff. Why? I have no idea — something to do with manufacturing cheaper parts, refrigeration units or something. I don't know. Point is, he's made it my job to get the ore. And now, if you're interested, I'm makin' it your job.

There's a few Banidine rocks out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enough for 20,000 units, the scouts tell me. Go out there, mine it, bring it back. Should be easy enough, right?

134506.en: I can't wait around here forever. I'm getting someone else to mine the Banidine.

134508.en: The mining isn't done... but I'm done with it.

134509.en: Oh, for the love of... fine. Whatever. I'll get someone else to do it.

134510.en: Look, if you can't point a beam at a few derelict Banidine rocks in a timely manner, I'm just gonna give the mission to someone else. Make sure you're ready to do some work next time you see me.

134513.en: Get it quick. I don't like waiting.

134515.en: Mine 18,000 units of Banidine at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring it to {[character]agentID.name}.

134516.en: I've got your Banidine right here, pal.

134518.en: I don't work for crazy people.

134519.en: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in your mission details and select "Add to Overview."

134521.en:
Look, I need some… ah, building materials, but I've got a client who's a bit particular. He wants it special, from some asteroids that already destroyed a shuttle of his, I guess. He gave me a location; you just go there, mine all 18,000 units of the Banidine that's there, and bring it back. Now, you won't find this stuff anywhere else, so don't go looking to bring me back something similar and easier to come across — you try and rip me off on this, and I'll know. Got it? Alright.

So, you game?

134522.en: I got no time for games. I'll find somebody who can get it done.

134524.en: I'm done with this weird stuff. Banidine? It's worthless! So I get to wondering… who the hell wants this stuff, and for what? And I decide, maybe I ought not to do this, huh?

134525.en: Thanks a bundle. I didn't pay ya to think. That's my job. Remember that next time.

134526.en: I need this done yesterday. I found someone else who can do the job faster.

134529.en: Excellent. Get out there as soon as you can.

134531.en:
A huge asteroid has crashed into one of our stations. The station itself and most of the inhabitants are lost. This asteroid is particularly deadly in that it contains a huge quantity of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene so rescue crews can go in there and retrieve the survivors.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site. Mine it all and bring the ore back to me.

134533.en: Great work! I'll send in the rescue crews. I'm sure the families of the survivors will be delighted that you helped save their lives. And we might even find some way to use the Augumene.

134534.en: I don't have time to save a few station-dwellers' lives.

134535.en: Nice. Well, hopefully someone else will see the value in saving some civilian lives.

134536.en:
When mining for specific minerals, you can often use the Overview to help. Click the small white arrow beside the word “Overview”; from there, select “Load default,” and then “Mining.” Then, you can right-click any type of asteroid in your overview and select “Remove from Overview”; keep doing this until only the type you want is left in your overview.

Furthermore, if you plan to mine this type of ore regularly, you can click the Overview arrow again and select “Save current type selection as…”; type in whatever name seems appropriate. Now you can return to this setting anytime you want to simply by using the Overview arrow to select “Load (name).”

134538.en:
We need your help right away! We're calling on all ship commanders in this region. A huge asteroid has crashed into one of our stations. The station itself and most of the inhabitants are lost. This asteroid is particularly deadly in that it contains a huge quantity of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene so rescue crews can go in there and retrieve the survivors.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site. Mine it all and bring the ore back to me.

134539.en: I don't have time to save a few station-dwellers' lives.

134540.en: Hundreds more people will die now, thanks to you.

134541.en: I understand. For the good of all, I'll clear out that Augumene.

134542.en: Good. Get this done. I do not envy you your task.

134544.en:
We've determined that the asteroid that collided with the station was composed of Augumene, which is particularly deadly in that it is a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene safely from a starship.

More than that, others may be coming for the Augumene. We can't recover all the sensitive material from the wreckage of the base in time, and a blockade would tip our hand. The only solution is to mine out the Augumene ourselves. We want you to go out and retrieve all of the Augumene from the site. And hurry.

I've uploaded a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to find the crash site and then mine all the Augumene and bring the ore back to me.

134545.en: I have done it. The remains of the station should now attract no unwanted attention.

134546.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}. I wish we had not needed this to be done at all, but you did well.

134547.en: I'm afraid I cannot do such a thing. It's… well, so many lives lost…

134548.en: I understand. It's just this side of grave robbery. Still, desperate times, desperate measures, and all that.

134549.en: Space stations are ideal research locations for most governments. Station crews can perform dangerous experiments that could endanger the civilians near a terrestrial base. Another advantage to the isolation of these stations is that they are harder for enemy factions to find, making espionage or outright destruction more difficult... usually.

134551.en:
Something terrible has happened. An asteroid has collided with a research station at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. There's no official death-toll yet, but it's expected to climb into the tens of thousands. Some of our brightest were there, working out the very technologies that would enable us to better defend our way of life from Gallente and Minmatar agressors. Now they're all gone....

I'm sorry. I lost myself there. We've determined that the asteroid that collided with the station was composed of Augumene, a rare and extremely toxic ore. We need someone to mine out the Augumene safely from a starship.

More than that, others may be coming for the Augumene. We can't recover all the sensitive material from the wreckage of the station in time, and a blockade would tip our hand. The only solution is to mine out the Augumene ourselves. We want you to go out and retrieve all 3,600 units of Augumene from the site. And hurry. If we don't get that ore, looters might follow its signal and stumble on what's left of our base.

134552.en: We cannot wait around forever. The task has gone to someone else.

134553.en: This task is too urgent for your pace.

134554.en: I can't do this anymore. It's too much.

134555.en: Disappointing. I thought you seemed reliable.

134556.en: You moved too slowly, {[character]player.name}. A recent recon shows that not only is the Augumene gone, but approximately 20 tons of material and data sheets are missing from the wreckage. We can only hope the thieves were merely scavengers.

134558.en: I'll see what I can do.

134560.en: I'm ready, I think.... Get started at what?

134561.en: We've found a conglomeration of Augumene asteroids nearby. The ore's not much good to anyone due to the exorbitant cost of reprocessing, of course, but a couple of our scientists are interested in doing some research on such a rare substance. In any case, hopefully you've been around the block enough times that you can find the ore and bring it in.

134563.en: Not bad! Perhaps I was wrong about you.

134564.en: Well, I'm sure I can find someone else to handle this.

134565.en:
We've found a conglomeration of Augumene asteroids nearby. The ore's not much good to anyone due to the exorbitant cost of reprocessing, of course, but a couple of our scientists are interested in doing some research on such a rare substance. In any case, hopefully you've been around the block enough times that you can find the ore and bring it in.

You think you're up to this? I've uploaded the location to your People & Places databank.

134566.en: I didn't think you could handle it. Too bad I was right.

134567.en: Most people don't go looking for Augumene: It's virtually worthless, so you simply won't find it on the market.

134569.en: If it will help, I'll do this.

134570.en: Thank you. We need to get this thing settled, and quick.

134571.en: What is it? Have I done something wrong?

134572.en: A commercial station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} was destroyed in a freak accident. They're saying it was some sort of rogue asteroid, and it's fallen to us to analyze the thing. We're going to need all of it. Most of the asteroid is still at the site of the accident. It's a grim task, I know. But we need to do this if we're going to figure out how this happened.

134573.en: I've retrieved all the ore samples.

134574.en: Thanks. We'll get this to the boys in the lab immediately.

134575.en: I'm not going to do this just to save your job.

134576.en: You know, if you aren't part of the solution....

134577.en:
No, no, not at all—

Listen, it's just coming over the news channels now. There, see? A commercial station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} was destroyed in a freak accident. They're saying it was some sort of rogue asteroid. Investigators are reporting over ten thousand confirmed dead so far. Naturally, people are demanding answers. The government wants answers, the media wants answers, the people want answers... you get the idea. And nobody seems to have any answers.

To put it simply, this shouldn't have happened. {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and its surrounding systems were cleared of rogue asteroids years ago, or so we thought. In fact, the station's position and orbit were chosen specifically to ensure its safety from collisions with celestial objects. If we don't find out how this asteroid got there, the finger pointing is going to start. Nobody's job will be safe once that starts happening.

It's fallen to us to analyze the asteroid. We're going to need all of it, {[character]player.name}. The asteroid is still at the site of the accident, though it's busted up some, I imagine.

It's a grim task, I know. But it's one we need to undertake if we're going to figure out how this terrible thing happened.

134578.en: Never mind about the investigation. It's been handed off to someone else.

134580.en: I can't continue on with this. Sorry.

134581.en: Damn it, do you want me to lose my job?

134582.en: About that asteroid collision: Don't worry about it. One of my coworkers just got sacked for it, and he was an idiot anyway. Looks like the whole thing is blowing over. Still, would have been nice to put solving this whole mess on my résumé.

134584.en: Sure, I think I can help you out.

134585.en: Excellent! I'll get my lab ready.

134587.en: I've just gotten word about a deposit of Augumene in this system. Now, we're not really sure what use we might make of it, but a number of our competitors seem to want it for research, so that means we need to move on it too. Go out to the bookmark I'll provide for you and mine every unit of the stuff you find there for us to study… before anyone else gets their hands on it.

134588.en: I found your mystery rocks. Enjoy.

134589.en: Wonderful! I'll get to work on this right away.

134591.en: You're on their side, aren't you?

134592.en: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions — which more than negates any profit to be made from reprocessing the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

134594.en: I've just gotten word about a deposit of Augumene in this system. Now, we're not really sure what use we might make of it, but a number of our competitors seem to want it for research, so that means we need to move on it too. Go out to the bookmark I'll provide for you and mine every unit of the stuff you find there for us to study… before anyone else gets their hands on it.

134595.en: I've got to get going on this research. I'll get someone else to find me some Augumene before it's too late to finish my dissertation.

134597.en: I'm too busy to go looking for your mystery rocks. Sorry.

134598.en: Oh, great! There goes my entire thesis. Four years of preliminary research, all brought to an end by you. Thanks.

134599.en: I'm working under a deadline here. I'm never going to get my research finished now! I have to find a new topic for my dissertation because of your procrastination.

134601.en: I can do that. Sure. Where to, again?

134602.en: Excellent. Go quickly. I've uploaded the location to your NeoCom.

134603.en: Heard…? I hear lots of things. Which thing are you talking about?

134604.en: I've procured the Mercium for our cause.

134605.en: {[character]player.name} , you are a credit to your people.

134606.en: That sounds lame to me. No thanks.

134608.en: Ah, you haven't heard, apparently, or you'd know what I meant. Well, that's a relief. The fact is, we've gotten word of the location of a bunch of Mercium ore here in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but we believe that our information has also been leaked to other factions — including the Gallenteans. It's vital that you collect all the Mercium: It cannot be allowed to fall into enemy hands.

134609.en: We can wait no longer. I will seek out someone else to recover the Mercium before it is captured by our enemies.

134611.en: I'm not going to all that trouble over some worthless rocks. Sorry, but I quit.

134612.en: If enemy factions get their hands on that Mercium, it's on your head, not mine.

134613.en: You are too late. The Mercium is now in the hands of our enemies.

134615.en: I understand. I'll get that ore in no time. No worries.

134616.en: Go quickly, then. Time is precious!

134617.en: Why? Work quickly on what? I'm in the dark here.

134618.en:
One of our sources obtained information on the whereabouts of a significant deposit of Mercium ore. It would be disastrous for our cause if this Mercium were to fall into Amarrian or Caldari hands. Unfortunately, we're certain that they already know about it, so as I said, we must work quickly.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

134619.en: I got there first, I guess. Here's the ore.

134620.en: Well done! Glad to have had you on board for this one.

134621.en: I can't take that kind of pressure. Sorry.

134622.en: If they find it first, it's on your head. Not mine.

134624.en:
Oh, right. I was thinking I'd already sent you a com-chat about this. Heh. Sorry.

One of our sources obtained information on the whereabouts of a significant deposit of Mercium ore. It would be disastrous for our cause if this Mercium were to fall into Amarrian or Caldari hands. Unfortunately, we're certain that they already know about it, so as I said, we must work quickly.

Remember, they want that Mercium, so that means we need it more. Get it? You do whatever you have to to get this done quickly, alright?

134625.en: I couldn't get the Mercium, and I'm not about to do it now. Sorry, but I quit.

134626.en: If they find it first, it's on your head. Not mine.

134627.en: Sounds like a good deal. I'm in.

134628.en: Remember, move fast. Time's of the essence, huh?

134630.en:
Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

134631.en: Here's your Mercium. So, where's my cut?

134632.en:
Here you go. Oh, this is gonna be just like hacking into that SCC station computer and making ISK for myself!

Uh, I mean, not that I've ever done that....

134633.en: I'm not interested in getting caught in a four-way crossfire just to mine some rocks that might be worth something to someone at some point.

134634.en: Not everybody's got what it takes. I knew that when I first looked at you.

134636.en:
This thing: Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Alright? You gotta get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

134637.en: I don't have this kinda time, {[character]player.name}. I gotta move on this Mercium before it's gone.

134639.en: Selling to all four of the big empires? Uh... even I don't want to piss off that many people. Nah, I quit.

134640.en: Don't worry, I'll find someone who's willing to make some decent ISK.

134641.en: Somebody else already beat you to that Mercium, bonehead. Way to go.

134643.en: If it needs to be done, it needs to be done. I'll get you the Lyavite.

134644.en: Take care of yourself out there. The investigator I sent out is still having nightmares.

134645.en: Whatever it is, you know I'm up for it.

134646.en: I'm back from the ghost station, ore and all.

134647.en: You made it back? You got the Lyavite okay? You didn't... see anything, did you? No? Okay. Good.

134648.en: Something weird is going on here, and I'm not touching it. No thanks.

134649.en: I'm not going to force you. But someone has to go.

134650.en:
Abandoned posts and stations aren't as uncommon as you might expect. Most are actually only half-built, victims of insufficient funding; often pirates or other drifters move in and patch holes just well enough to prevent decompression. Other times, the stations just aren't profitable or inhabitable, for any number of reasons, and it actually costs less to just leave the station floating there rather than to dismantle it.

But even then, there are usually records, people... something....

134652.en:
Well, we've got a bit of a weird one here. We've found an old mining post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. But, the thing is, we can't find who used to own it: There are no records of its being built or even existing. It's simply empty. No sign of anyone left there, dead or otherwise. Our initial investigation found extensive fire damage, gas leaks — you name it, it went wrong. Lots of explosive damage, though we can't tell if that was accidental or intentional. And some marks... well, we just don't know what could do that to metal. It's damn creepy, that's for sure.

Anyway, near as we can tell, the miners were working on a large Lyavite deposit. They didn't finish, because there's still about 5,000 units of it at the site. Now, I know Lyavite isn't the most popular rock, but nobody just leaves that much ore lying around. And besides, the brains at the lab figure they can use the stuff for some of their research, so this opportunity is too good to pass up. That's where you come in. Warp in, mine the Lyavite, and warp out. It's that easy.

134653.en:
You are not going to believe this. Remember that abandoned mining post I told you about? The one with the Lyavite? It's gone. I don't mean someone else mined it, or it was raided or anything. It's just gone. We've sent five different scouts out there, and they all confirm that the location where the post used to be is just dead space.

Even the dust is gone.

134655.en: I've seen all sorts of crap as a pilot, and this is too creepy even for me. I'm out.

134656.en: I'll not ask why. I'm sure you have your reasons.

134657.en: Look, I know the mission sounded a bit off, but it needed to get done. My superiors are really putting the pressure on now, and I have to give this to someone else. I'm sorry.

134659.en: You're a little twisted. And I'm okay with that. Yeah, I'll get you your Augumene.

134660.en: Excellent. Go get me some of that magnificent ore.

134661.en: You seem happy. What is it?

134662.en:
I was talking to some blowhard in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} when his station was destroyed. So, I'm thinking raiders, right? But no, it's even better. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh!

It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me! I want you to go out there, and bring me back all of that Augumene.

134663.en: Here's the Augumene. Where's my ISK?

134664.en: Ah, it even feels like providence. And cold, hard kredits. Speaking of which, here's yours.

134665.en: You seem entirely too happy with all this. And that troubles me. I'm going to decline, I'm afraid.

134666.en: What? You don't like free ISK?

134667.en: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes very expensive safety precautions. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

134669.en:
I'm on the comm, talking to this blowhard I knew back from my days at the academy, right...? So he's going on and on about how his corporation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is going to make ISK hand over fist mining some rare ore, blah blah blah. Then all these alarms start going off on his end. And I'm thinking his stupid corp is getting raided or something. Then, all of a sudden, the wall behind him disappears and he's ripped away from the screen! The blowhard got spaced right in front of my eyes!

Now, here's the best part. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh! It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me!

So, anyway, I want you to go out there and bring me back all of that Augumene. Do that, and I'll have a nice reward here for you when your come back, alright?

134670.en: I don't have time to wait for you to decide whether you like ISK or not. I'll get someone else to mine my lucky rock. So you can just get lost, okay?

134672.en: This is more than a little weird. I'm not mining this Augumene anymore.

134673.en: Don't tell me you're scared of a little rock?

134674.en: Great. You took just long enough for some other vultures to get all the Augumene. That rock was meant for me, but no, you had to prance around until it was too late. Thanks for nothing.

134679.en: There's a rich deposit of Mercium in this system. Bring me 1,800 units and we might both end up rich.

134681.en: Well, looks like the research guys have shot several holes in my Mercium reprocessing theory. Son of a… Well, you did your part, anyway: Here's your payment.

134684.en: Most people don't go looking for Mercium, as it doesn't do so well out on the open market. If you are having trouble finding it, you can right click the "Mercium" icon in your mission log and add it to your overview.

134686.en:
To be part of the future you need to help build it first. That's what I'm asking you to do.

There's a rare ore called Mercium, similar to Omber, but it's much more difficult to reprocess. Current methods render the ore unusable. It's maddening to no end. I think I might have solved the problem, though. I can't tell you my whole theory, but it's a variant on the standard electrolysis method used by planetside miners. All I need is some Mercium to try it on.

There's a rich deposit of Mercium in this system. Bring me 1,800 units and we might both end up rich.

134687.en: I quit. Sorry, but I have better things to do with my time.

134689.en: Furriers are small animals commonly found as pets among the Amarrian higher class. They resemble rabbits in size and temperament, although they can turn vicious from time to time; many royals, the Tash-Murkons in particular, find this trait quite endearing. The creatures are largely mammalian, although they do exhibit some reptilian qualities: They lay eggs rather than giving live birth, and they have distinctly bird-like, scaly facial features.

134690.en:
It seems that some rogue scientists just could not leave Creation well enough alone. One man in particular, one "Vilus Seermal," has apparently been performing genetic experiments on the fuzzy little critters, in a hidden laboratory not far from here. While this is not illegal, the ethics of his experiments are certainly in question. He has, for whatever reason, apparently turned the things into cute, cuddly killing machines.

I shudder to think of it. I'm sure all those scientists are dead, but we can't allow those mutated furriers to mix with the general furrier population. Yet there are environmentalists out there who would protect those little beasts. In fact, I have word that some eco-terrorists might be on their way at this very moment: Get out there and destroy that laboratory before someone does something incredibly rash. And don't let anyone stop you!

134692.en:
It seems that some rogue scientists just could not leave Creation well enough alone. One man in particular, one "Vilus Seermal," has apparently been performing genetic experiments on the fuzzy little critters, in a hidden laboratory not far from here. While this is not illegal, the ethics of his experiments are certainly in question. He has, for whatever reason, apparently turned the things into cute, cuddly killing machines.

Well, we just received an emergency transmission from the laboratory. Listen.

"We need help immediately! The coordinates are attached within the carrier wave of this frequency. You must help us. They have us trapped in the communications room, and they're chewing through the door as I speak! Hurry! (grinding sounds) No! They're coming through! They've gnawed through! Oh, no! NOOOO... (crashing, squealing sounds, human screams)..."

You get the idea, I think. But there's the most disturbing part. After all the screaming and crashing stops, this comes at the end of the message.

"(Hissing static, distant slurping, and then a small, impish voice) Fooood! Good. Food good! Bring more foooood!"

I shudder to think of it. I'm sure all those scientists are dead, but we can't allow those mutated furriers to mix with the general furrier population. Yet there are environmentalists out there who would protect those little beasts.

Get out there and destroy that laboratory before someone does something incredibly rash.

134693.en: Well, let us pray to all that's holy that those vicious vermin die of starvation before anyone finds them.

134695.en: Nice work. I was afraid overzealous animal rights people might get word of this.

134696.en: I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

134697.en: The furriers must die. And I love playing exterminator.

134699.en: I can't do this. Whatever those scientists did, these are still innocent creatures.

134700.en: On second thought, I can't do this. Whatever those scientists created, these are still innocent creatures.

134701.en: Oh? Try me. I've heard some crazy stuff in my time...

134703.en: Thanks for your help! Now get out there and capture that fugitive, {[character]player.name}.

134704.en: You have our thanks for a job well done.

134705.en: Dinner engagement, eh? I see. Going to be wearing any yellow, by chance...?

134706.en: That crook won't escape me. I'll leave immediately.

134707.en: I've captured the fugitive as ordered.

134708.en: Well, I'd be happy to help, but I'm afraid I have a dinner engagement elsewhere...

134709.en: What do you need me to do?

Fortunately, we've tracked the ship he stole and located its signal at a suspected terrorists' outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Fly out there and retrieve him. There's a significant reward.
