Once you have arrived in the correct star system, simply right-click anywhere in space. In the drop-down window that appears, your current mission information appears at the bottom. From there, select the "dock" option and your Autopilot will bring you into the station momentarily.

Once the courier item is delivered, return to your agent's home station (also available via the drop-down simply by right-clicking anywhere in space) to collect your reward.

135013.en:
No doubt you've see that little furrier that's been bouncing around the station for the last few days, {[character]player.name}? You haven't? Well, I certainly have — nasty little creature. It bites, you know.

In any event, it was part of a shipment of exotic pets intended for delivery to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, but it got left behind because I spilled a drink all over the cargo manifest. We need someone to take this furrier, special delivery, over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and get it the hell out of our hair.

Remember to move the "special delivery" container into your cargo hold before you go.

135015.en: You'll do it? Hey guys — he says he'll do it!

135016.en: So the little monster didn't ruin your upholstery? Good job, my friend. You may have a future in the animal transport business! Check back to me in a while.

135017.en: Okay, I'll take the damned furrier.

135018.en: The furrier's delivered. Man those things stink.

135019.en: Hi. I'm looking for some gainful employment.

135020.en: That furrier you delivered was carrying some kind of disease, and it's running rampant since the thing bit a few folks here. We haven't got the right vaccine here. Since you were the one who brought the damned furrier that started it all, I think it's only fitting that you get the vaccine and bring it back here for us.

135021.en:
Ha. Good one…

Listen, about that furrier? Things have gotten a little complicated, {[character]player.name}. That thing was carrying some kind of disease, and it's running rampant since the thing bit a few folks here. We haven't got the right vaccine here, and god the place is in bad shape — people turning green and swelling up like balloons everywhere. Since you were the one who brought the damned furrier that started it all, I think it's only fitting that you get the vaccine and bring it back here for us.

Oh, yeah — we'll vaccinate you before you leave, too. What do you say, champ?

135022.en: I knew you'd want to help. Please make it snappy.

135023.en: Great job, {[character]player.name}. Come back later and I'll see if I can scrounge up another job for you.

135024.en: I'll deliver the vaccine, but only if you stop calling me a furrier-hauler.

135026.en: Who are you calling a furrier-hauler, drink-spiller?

135027.en:
It seems that the folks at one of our other offices can't find the proper paperwork about this last pet shipment, and they need this manifest. Or at least what's left of it after I spilled my drink on it. They're begging us to send it over. So, can you run this manifest over there so we can put this entire sordid affair behind us?

Remember to put the manifest in your cargo hold or you'll have to come back and relive the whole, sad incident all over again.

135028.en:
Ha! Smartass! No, nothing like that {[character]player.name}. Er, well, sort of…

It seems that the folks at one of our other offices can't find the proper paperwork about this last pet shipment, and they need this manifest. Or at least what's left of it after I spilled my drink on it. They're begging us to send it over. So, can you run this manifest over there so we can put this entire sordid affair behind us?

135029.en: Here's the manifest. Now get going.

135030.en: Thank goodness. That's the last furrier we'll be transporting out of this station, let me tell you.

135031.en: Okay, but just this one more time.

135033.en: You are? Why? Spill another drink and you need me to get some wipes for you?

135034.en:
One of the functions of my job is to ensure things operate smoothly in this region. I have a number of informants that keep me in the loop of the less visible happenings. They tend to be skittish by nature, but recently one of my informants was noticeably shaken. He won't send the information, and he won't meet me in person. He's insisted that I send a third party to pick up the data.

Normally I'd just find another informant, but this one was on the trail of a particularly virulent heretic. The man can't be anything but mad—he calls himself The Crackpot, for one thing—but it's damned hard to track a madman. He's been attracting attention, even followers from among the weak-minded, and it's long past time to put a stop to his nonsense.

If you'll go and pick up that data, it could help us track this menace down.

135036.en: Go quickly. I can't afford to lose this lead.

135037.en: Well done. Once I get this decrypted, I may have more work for you.

135039.en: Something spooked the snitch and he ran off. Now we'll have to find a new source for intel on this heretic, and who knows where he'll be by then.

135040.en: Something spooked the snitch and he ran off. Now we'll have to find a new source for intel on this heretic, and who knows where he'll be by then.

135043.en: That sounds simple enough. I'll get the data for you.

135046.en: I don't like the sound of this. I quit.

135048.en: From the publisher's description: "This is the most remarkable book published in the last century. Here, the great Emperor Heideran VII records his dreams for peace throughout the galaxy; it is this vision that propelled him into becoming a champion of interstellar relations. His relentless struggle toward this goal has brought unparalleled harmony among the empires; his constant search for peaceful solutions to any problem having many times quelled the storms of hostilities on the horizon. His determination and his powers of persuasion have compelled his own people and others to sacrifice many things they thought sacred to ensure that tranquility will prevail, now and forever."

135049.en:
The Crackpot has been hiding his heretical nonsense in copies of the Pax Amarria! This is absolutely intolerable! Needless to say, we've been seizing copies as they're found, and of course those in possession of such an insulting piece of work have been detained for questioning. Still, that leaves us with a pile of gilded filth on our hands.

I want you to go pick up the copies that are being held and bring them back here. We're having the Pax Amarria covers stripped off before we send them along for the ceremonial burning.

135051.en:
That Crackpot has been hiding his heretical nonsense in copies of the Pax Amarria! This is absolutely intolerable! Needless to say, we've been seizing copies as they're found, and of course those in possession of such an insulting piece of work have been detained for questioning. Still, that leaves us with a pile of gilded filth on our hands.

I want you to go pick up the copies that are being held and bring them back here. We're having the Pax Amarria covers stripped off before we send them along for the ceremonial burning.

135052.en: I thought you were better than that.

135053.en: Remember, we can't get rid of this trash fast enough.

135054.en:
We'll get these stripped down and shipped out as quickly as possible. They'll be burned at a more appropriate location.

By the way, some of our detainees have proved… most informative. I should have more work for you soon.

135055.en: I thought you were better than that.

135056.en: I'll find someone who understands that, and can help us dispose of this garbage in a more timely fashion.

135057.en: I'll find someone who understands that, and can help us dispose of this garbage in a more timely fashion.

135060.en: I'll go and get the books immediately.

135061.en: I have the heretical nonsense you requested.

135062.en: I'm not helping with any book-burning.

135063.en: I don't like the sound of this. I quit.

135065.en: We've finally got The Crackpot. I need you to go pick him up and bring him here. We've made sure to keep him anonymous. Go and get him before some other loon tries to break him out.

135066.en:
We've finally got The Crackpot. It turns out his real name was Russell. I need you to go pick him up and bring him here for transport. We want him there when his books burn—he'll need to recant publicly, throw the books on the fire, that sort of thing. After all, we wouldn't want him martyred.

He's in confinement a few jumps away. We've made sure to keep him anonymous. There are still some crazed sympathizers on the loose, and we don't want them endangering themselves any further. Go and get him before some other loon tries to break him out.

135067.en: Well, I'm sure I can find someone who will properly appreciate the honor of this assignment.

135068.en: I thought you would be. Remember, this must be done quickly, before word gets out.

135069.en: The Empire thanks you for your assistance in disposing of this trash.

135070.en: I thought you'd be pleased at the chance to finally bring this menace in.

135071.en: Someone broke that madman out. Now we'll have to start the hunt all over again.

135072.en: Someone broke that madman out. Now we'll have to start the hunt all over again.

135075.en: I'm honored to be of service the Empire.

135077.en: I don't like the sound of this. I think I'll pass.

135078.en: I don't like the direction this is going. I quit.

135080.en: The problem is information networks. Our soldiers are well cared for and would normally be content, but they find that pictures and holoreels all tend to be from Gallente producers. They see the decadence and excess of our enemies. Our men are revolted by the excess of the Gallente, yes, but there is jealousy among them as well. And this jealousy is eating away at the core of our efforts.

135082.en: The State should support its soldiers not out of concern for the soldier, but for the services he renders.  Remember this in your future travels.

135083.en: And do hurry.  Our chefs are grumpy and impatient.

135084.en: Not very appetizing, is it?  I have faith our chefs will be able to make ...something... out of it.  But come, there is still more to do.

135085.en: The State should support its soldiers not out of concern for the soldier, but for the services he renders.  Remember this in your future travels.

135086.en: You have taken too long.  Our chefs have quit in disgust.  This will delay SPLET for weeks.

135087.en: You have taken too long.  Our chefs have quit in disgust.  This will delay SPLET for weeks.

135092.en: To hell with food delivery.  The soldiers should be happy simply serving the State.

135093.en: I tire of trafficking food.  The soldiers should be happy simply serving the State.

135094.en: How can I aid the mighty State?

135095.en: Sure, no problem. I'm on it.

135097.en: Yep. As usual, I'm the right one for the job, {[character]agentID.name}.

135098.en:
Our miners have just reported a bunch of rogue drones in the system. Between them and the damned ore thieves, I'm almost ready to give up. They're worse than Gallentean greenroaches – if we don't show them that they're not welcome here, we'll be up to our eyeballs. And I can't send my guys out there if I know they might be in danger. No, we need a capsuleer on this job, someone capable of defending a ship and mining at the same time.

I've bookmarked a mining site for you. Go on out there and, if you see any drones, take 'em out. You know the risks. Then mine whatever Banidine you find out there so I can find out what the damn things are so interested in.

135099.en: Here's the ore you asked for. Seems like a waste of time, but hey — anything the drones want, it's a safe bet we shouldn't let them have it, right?

135100.en: Agreed, {[character]player.name}... can't be a good thing. Thanks for the assist!

135101.en: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market.

135103.en:
Yes, I think you are. Listen, our miners have just reported a bunch of rogue drones in the system. Between them and the damned ore thieves, I'm almost ready to give up. They're worse than Gallentean greenroaches – if we don't show them that they're not welcome here, we'll be up to our eyeballs. And I can't send my guys out there if I know they might be in danger. No, we need a capsuleer on this job, someone capable of defending a ship and mining at the same time.

I've bookmarked a mining site for you. Go on out there and, if you see any drones, take 'em out. Be caref— well, I don't need to tell an experienced starship captain like you. You know the risks. Then mine whatever Banidine you find out there so I can find out what the damn things are so interested in.

135104.en: According to recent studies, the typical foot soldier's sense of humor tends towards the ironic, with a particular fondness for satire and gallows humor. Yet to hear Command tell it, these types of humor are the most dangerous to morale.  As a result, most government-sponsored entertainment is consciously light-hearted, even if nobody really enjoys it.

135105.en: There is a man awaiting pick-up at a nearby station-- I'll upload the coordinates to your Neocom. The man is a comedian of a specialized sort.  You‘ll know him when you see him.  Bring him back here for me.

135107.en:
No, the State cannot afford the lofty prices of professional entertainers of such caliber. We have booked far worse, I'm afraid.

There is a man awaiting pick-up at a nearby station-- I'll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom. The man is a comedian of a specialized sort. You‘ll know him when you see him. Bring him back here for me.

135108.en: Inane or not, this job posed no threat to your safety.

135109.en: Trust me, this isn't any less weird on my side.

135110.en: I share your misgivings, but if this is the worst thing we do to our men, then we will be well on our way to perfection.

135111.en: Indeed he could, but the State wants him here now, and if you will not get him, I will have someone else do it.

135112.en: Our prop comedian is dead.  He was reportedly beaten and stabbed to death by citizens who were simply "annoyed into a murderous rage."  Had you acted faster, we might have acquired his services before he was brutally killed at the hands of a vengeful mob.

135113.en: Our prop comedian is dead.  He was reportedly beaten and stabbed to death by citizens who were simply "annoyed into a murderous rage."  Had you acted faster, we might have acquired his services before he was brutally killed at the hands of a vengeful mob.

135116.en: This is getting slightly weird, but okay.

135117.en: Though it may constitute some form of war-crime, here is your prop comedian.

135118.en: I will not bother with this.  The comedian can take a transport like everyone else.

135119.en: I have delivered many inane objects in my time, but I will never deliver a comedian.

135120.en: What are we talking about?  Musical acts?  Stunts?

135121.en: A race against the drones, huh? Sure, I'll do it.

135122.en: Get this done, {[character]player.name}. We don't really need that Banidine, but better we get it than those drones.

135124.en:
A recent survey scan of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} reveals a big deposit of Banidine ore. We were content to leave it alone at first, but then we saw swarms of drones in the area. They seem to be making their way through the asteroid fields there in a hurry. They haven't stumbled on the Banidine yet, but it's only a matter of time.

We want you to get to the ore before they do. I won't lie to you; it's going to be close. You may even have to fight a few of them off, so be careful.

135125.en: Got your Banidine here. No drones were going to stop me.

135126.en: Got your Banidine here. No drones were going to stop me.

135127.en: Good work. Those drones are making life difficult for everyone hereabouts.

135128.en: No. I'm not scared, I'm just sick of mining and popping drones.

135129.en: If we don't get that Banidine, those drones will. I hope someone else can do it.

135131.en:
A recent survey scan of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} reveals a big deposit of Banidine ore. We were content to leave it alone at first, but then we saw swarms of drones in the area. They seem to be making their way through the asteroid fields there in a hurry. They haven't stumbled on the Banidine yet, but it's only a matter of time.

We want you to get to the ore before they do. I won't lie to you; it's going to be close. You may even have to fight a few of them off, so be careful.

135132.en: I'm giving the job to someone else. The universe isn't going to stop and wait for you to make up your mind.

135134.en: I decided I'm not really into this job.

135135.en: What? A few drones too much for you to handle?

135137.en: Sure. I'll see what I can do.

135138.en: Don't waste any time. Our people are waiting.

135140.en: I have your mountain of Augumene right here.

135141.en: Nice work. I'll keep you in mind when something else comes up.

135142.en: I hope I can find someone else to handle this.

135144.en: Maybe next time, huh? In any case, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} will manage. It's your loss.

135145.en: If it will help us defeat those bastards, I'll do it.

135147.en: Sure. Uh, how do I do that?

135148.en: Acquire the 20,000 units of Augumene at the location I've given you. Now, there may be other folks looking to get this stuff too, so don't go out there unprepared to defend yourself, okay?

135150.en: Good. You've helped make the universe a safer place.

135151.en: I don't want to be a part of this. It's just not right.

135152.en: "Conscientious objectors" like you are going to destroy this government.

135154.en: I'm starting to think this is a bad idea. I quit.

135156.en: The Nugoeihuvi Corporation, or NOH, is the only Caldari mega-corporation that has focused on the entertainment industry. They have always been suspected of strong ties to the Caldari underworld, mainly because many of their products cater to that social element or are on the borderline of legality.

135157.en:
We are working closely with several bathhouses through Nugoeihuvi to acquire the large number of companions required for SPLET. We are close to completing the contracts. All that is required to finalize is a final inspection, to be performed by the SPLET organizer.

Pick up the NOH prostitute-- I'll upload the station address to your NeoCom-- and return her here. After this last mission, I believe the program will be ready to launch.

135159.en:
Originally, we were going to be hiring the best dancers in Caldari space. It was to be a dazzling performance, with custom arranged music and specially choreographed numbers. It would have been a show both tantalizing and tasteful. But such things are expensive.

We found the best cost-effective solution by working with NOH's bathhouses. Traveling with SPLET will be a "companion army." We are close to completing the contracts. All that is left is a final round of...negotiation by the SPLET chairman.

Pick up the NOH prostitute-- I'll upload the station address to your NeoCom-- and return her here. After this last mission, I believe the program will be ready to launch.

135160.en: Damn it, the chairman will have my head for this.

135161.en: Good.  Although SPLET has not become what was originally envisioned, I doubt the soldiers will complain too loudly...

135162.en: Excellent.  Thanks to your help, SPLET will soon be making its way through the Caldari ranks.

135163.en: But we were so close to finally being done with this!

135164.en: The chairman has grown impatient with the negotiator's delayed arrival.  He has cancelled SPLET, citing a “personal insult” on the part of NOH.

135165.en: The chairman has grown impatient with the negotiator's delayed arrival.  He has cancelled SPLET, citing a “personal insult” on the part of NOH.

135168.en: I will do this last thing.

135169.en: I have brought the— uh— negotiator.

135170.en: This task seems to favor the chairman more than the Caldari soldiers.  I will not do it.

135171.en: I will not continue this mission.

135173.en: Take out drones, mine Mercium. Got it, chief.

135174.en: Glad to hear it. I'll leave you to it, then.

135175.en: You know me. I'm always interested in work.

135177.en: I knew those drones wouldn't be that big a deal for you.

135178.en: I don't want to mess with someone else's failed experiments.

135179.en: They're still just drones. What's the big deal?

135180.en: Since their invention sometime around the Gallente-Caldari War, drones have become commonplace in nearly all facets of life. Drones vary in size from that of a human eye up to those that rival the largest frigates, and they have been built to fill the roles of fighters, miners, and repair vehicles, as well as household cleaning units and tiny children's toys — not to mention their various military uses in space stations and on planetary surfaces alike. New uses for drone technology are being developed constantly.

135182.en:
You ever try mining with drones? Useful little guys, huh? Yeah, well, to a point…

Turns out someone got the bright idea that if mining drones mine more ore, bigger drones would mine even more ore. This guy's team slapped some mining drone's AI into non-regulation heavy combat units and threw some mining lasers on. He even hacked the firmware so that the mining brains could control the weaponry, making some sort of self-sufficient mining machines. But of course the genius didn't test the things properly before sending them out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to mine Mercium. And of course now he's made himself scarce.

You can probably guess what happened. Now there's a bunch of haywire drones zipping about this rare mineral that we want — our guys in the lab need it for research, I guess. The drones aren't even mining the rock, last I heard, but they have tried to bore through any ship we send out there....

It's getting ridiculous. If you can, get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, neutralize the drones, and bring back all the Mercium; we'll pay you well for your efforts.

135183.en: I can't just sit on this contract. I'm sending this off to someone with more initiative.

135185.en: I don't have time to mess with this crazy drone business.

135186.en: Really, {[character]player.name}, I expected more from you.

135191.en:
I've just discovered a sizable deposit of Pithix out by an old mining station. The station's been abandoned for a while now, but there are still working sensors in the area; that's how we picked up on the Pithix. Problem is, the transmission's hardly secure. I need you to get out there and bring me back that rock before someone else cleans the place out.

Oh, there might also be some rogue drone activity in the area. Fair warning.

135192.en: I've got your rocks here. Seems like a waste of time, but it's your ISK…

135193.en: Alright. Now I just have to find a buyer…

135196.en:
Pithix is virtually worthless, due to the terrible inefficiency of reprocessing it; one is far better off to mine for Jaspet instead. As a result, you won't find the former ore on the market. In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother giving it a unique listing in their mining packages when they produce standard ship scanners.

If you're having trouble finding the Pithix at the mission location, simply right-click the "Pithix" icon in the mission details and select "Add to Overview."

135198.en:
I've just discovered a sizable deposit of Pithix out by an old mining station. The station's been abandoned for a while now, but there are still working sensors in the area; that's how we picked up on the Pithix. Problem is, the transmission's hardly secure. I need you to get out there and bring me back that rock before someone else cleans the place out.

So, are you game?

135199.en: I don't want to do this anymore. Sorry.

135200.en: Great, now there's no way I'll get someone there in time. Thanks a bunch.

135201.en: This sounds easy enough. I'm in.

135204.en:
There's an abandoned mining station not far from here that still has a bunch of Pithix 'roids floating around. There's about 4,500 units of it out there, and we want all of it. Don't worry, we'll pay you.

Oh, and keep an eye out for rogue drones. There might be a few roaming around.

135206.en: No deal. Sorry. I'm a lover and a fighter, but I'm no miner.

135208.en:
There's an old mining station not far from here that hasn't been used in months. The mining company gave up their claim when they thought they wiped the area of all valuable materials. About all they left was a bunch of Pithix.

But it just so happens that a couple of scientists who do some work for us want Pithix for some of their research projects. There's about 4,500 units of it out there, and we want all of it. Don't worry, we'll pay you.

135209.en: I'll take that, and here's your pay. Pleasure doing business.

135210.en:
Most people don't go looking for Pithix. It doesn't do so well out on the open market. That's why a lot of sensor manufacturers don't even bother to give it its own unique entry in the mining packages they produce for standard ship scanners.

If you are having trouble finding the Pithix 'roids in this mission, you can right-click the "Pithix" icon in your mission log and add it to your overview.

135211.en: I'm pretty bored of this already. See ya.

135212.en: Not motivated enough? This was almost free money!

135216.en:
There's an old mining station not far from here. When they pulled out, they took everything they could with them; about all they left was a bunch of Pithix.

Now, it just so happens that I know a couple of scientists who want Pithix for some of their research projects. There's about 4,500 units of it out there, and they're willing to pay a good price for all of it. Go get it for me. I'll give you your fair share.

Oh, hey, make sure you fit some guns or something - we spotted some rogue drones around here recently.

135218.en: I'll take that, and here's your pay. Pleasure doing business.

135219.en: No deal. Sorry. I'm a lover and a fighter, but I'm no miner.

135220.en:
Most people don't go looking for Pithix. It doesn't do so well out on the open market. That's why a lot of sensor manufacturers don't even bother to give it its own unique entry in the mining packages they produce for standard ship scanners.

If you are having trouble finding the Pithix 'roids in this mission, you can right-click the "Pithix" icon in your mission log and add it to your overview.

135222.en:
There's an old mining station not far from here. The mining company that owned it hasn't been around for months. Something about repeated attacks by "blood thirsty raiders." Heh. When they pulled out, they took everything they could with them. About all they left was a bunch of Pithix.

Now, it just so happens that I know a couple of scientists who want Pithix for some of their research projects. There's about 4,500 units of it out there, and they're willing to pay a good price for all of it. Go get it for me. Don't worry. I'll give you your fair share.

135223.en: I'm pretty bored of this already. See ya.

135224.en: Not motivated enough? This was almost free money!

135226.en: Please hurry back with the space ice.

135227.en: You do? Great, when can I start?

135229.en: Oh, thank you. I was about ready to strangle that guy.

135230.en: I'm not much of an "art" person. So no.

135231.en: You're gonna leave me to deal with a disappointed artist? Oh, that's real nice. Thanks so much.

135232.en:
Right away. But look, this one's a little weird. Just a heads up.

There's this guy who's making these really, truly gigantic ice sculptures — some kinda artsy shit, I don't know. I said, buddy, that much ice, it's gonna melt before you can finish carving it, or it's gonna break under its own weight. He says he knows that, says that's why he's gonna build it in space! Crazy…

Anyway, he's got the money, so what am I gonna say but "how much and how fast?" So, can you get 20 units of Crystalline Icicles over here ASAP? I got a location for you.

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Crystalline Icicles ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

135233.en: Now he doesn't want that ice! He wants a different kind of ice because now it's a different phase of the moon and the colors don't match anymore! And he won't stop talking about this stuff! Next time, move a little quicker, huh?

135234.en: I don't like art anymore. Not when it takes effort. I quit.

135235.en: You're gonna leave me to deal with a disappointed artist? Oh, that's real nice. Thanks so much.

135236.en: Now he doesn't want that ice! He wants a different kind of ice because now it's a different phase of the moon and the colors don't match anymore! And he won't stop talking about this stuff! Next time, move a little quicker, huh?

135237.en: One order of Azure Ice, coming up.

135238.en: You and me, we're gonna go far.

135239.en: Could be. Let me hear more, my friend.

135240.en:
There's a field of Azure Ice at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I want to sell it to some less-than-brilliant colonists. It's not as good as Blue Ice, but the they won't know the difference. Bring me back, oh, 20 blocks of it. I'll split the profit with you.

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Azure Ice may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

135242.en: Excellent. I've already got your share of the money ready. This should keep their colony running just well enough so that they can make more orders.

135243.en: Maybe I'll ruin the lives of unsuspecting colonists some other time, but not today.

135244.en: Those colonists already ruined their lives. What's the harm in making some ISK off of that?

135245.en: The open market doesn't bother with Azure Ice. Everyone and their grandmothers know it's not nearly as useful as Blue Ice. Planetary water ice has more demand. Any deal that gets you ISK for Azure Ice is a good sell. And if you ever get stuck with Azure Ice and no mission to turn it in... well, just be glad your docking bay has no volume limit.

135247.en:
Alright! You ever been out to some of those backwater colonies? You know the ones I mean. Barren wastelands of rocks and dust where some nut got the bright idea to try to build the agricultural community of tomorrow? Kind of place where the main export is despair? That kind of place?

Well, so happens I know of one that's just starting up. Poor bastards need some fuel. They're willing to pay good money, too. Now, I could sell them the good stuff, but seriously, these jokers wouldn't know good ice if it fell out of the sky and crushed their pet furrier.

There's a field of Azure Ice at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's not as good as Blue Ice, but the colonists won't know the difference. Bring me back about, oh, 20 blocks of it. I'll sell it to the colony goobers and cut you in. Sound good?

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Azure Ice may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

135248.en: You moved too slow. Someone else got the sell. Not only that, but they got the right stuff for the job. How is anyone supposed to get repeat business if customers keep getting what they need?

135249.en: Maybe ripping off colonists isn't the best use of my abilities.

135250.en: As far as I'm concerned, there is never a better use of one's skills than exploiting the ignorant. Go figure.

135251.en: You moved too slow. Someone else got the sell. Not only that, but they got the right stuff for the job. How is anyone supposed to get repeat business if customers keep getting what they need?

135252.en: I can harvest the cloud for you.

135253.en: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good pilot capable of using a gas harvester.

135255.en:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting these wild drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. So the best solution is to just remove the cloud: no cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. Of course, you'll also need to deal with whatever drones are there.

135256.en: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.

135257.en: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.

135258.en: I'm afraid I can't do this.

135259.en: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Thanks for being honest, though.

135262.en: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good gas harvester around here.

135263.en: You know me, ready for anything.

135264.en:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. And you also gotta deal with any drones there. Fair enough?

135265.en: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.

135266.en: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.

135267.en: I'm afraid I can't do this. So... "no thanks."

135268.en: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Hey, thanks for being honest, though.

135270.en:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. I don't know why. It's like insects to a flame or somethin'. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. It's annoying as hell.

I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. If you don't or ya can't, just say "no thanks." You can decline one mission about every 4 hours without pissing me off, so no worries.

135271.en: I'm on it. Back in a bit.

135273.en: You know I do. What have you got?

135274.en:
We've located some asteroids that contain substantial amounts of Polygypsum — that's a comparatively rare mineral, and almost completely unknown in this system. Our guys want to have a look at the stuff and see if they can figure out some way to make use of it; however, we don't have anyone who wants to deal with it. So guess who I thought of first?

You'll need to grab all 2,800 units of the stuff and get it back here. See you then.

135275.en: It was awfully dull, but the reward should make some amends. Here's your ore.

135276.en: You've earned your reward as far as I'm concerned, {[character]player.name}, that's for sure.

135277.en: Hm. No, I think I'm going to go, oh… watch some paint dry, actually. Thanks for the offer, though.

135278.en: I see. Well, I guess I can find someone else willing to make an easy few ISK.

135280.en: Sure, I'll see what I can do.

135281.en: Don't waste any time. These guys are waiting for their ore.

135282.en: We do? Or I do? Either way, I'm ready. What's up?

135283.en:
We need a big shipment of Geodite crystals for a client of ours, some gemology lab. These gemologists figure they might be able to get some decent stones out of it and make a bit of profit that way. Whatever. They want to pay for it, so it's all good by me. And you'll get your cut, don't worry.

Geodite takes up a lot of room: You're going to need a big cargo hold, or you'll have to make several trips.

135285.en: Nice work. I'll keep you in mind when something else comes up.

135286.en: That's one boring scenario you've worked out there, my friend. I think I'm gonna pass.

135287.en: Man, I hope I can find someone else to handle this.

135288.en:
Geodite ore is pretty much worthless because of the poor-quality Nocxium it produces; one is far better off to look for Crokite instead... although that's no easy job. In any case, you won't find Geodite on the market anywhere.

If you're having trouble finding the Geodite at the mission location, you can right-click the "Geodite" icon in the mission's details and select "Add to Overview."

135290.en:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has an unusual request for the right miner. We need a big shipment of Geodite crystals for a client of ours, some gemology lab. Maybe you've heard of Geodite, but if not, it'd be no surprise — the stuff's pretty much worthless. But these gemologists figure they might be able to get some decent stones out of it and make a bit of profit that way. Whatever. They want to pay for it, so it's all good by me. And you'll get your cut, don't worry.

Anyway, if you're interested, I'll send the coordinates over to your ship's NeoCom — the field's in this system.

135291.en: Hm. This is a pretty boring scenario you've worked out here, my friend. I think I'm gonna cut out.

135292.en: Maybe next time. Once again progress grinds to a halt.

135293.en: You know I'm never one to shy away from my patriotic duty.

135294.en: Be quick about it. We don't want to let anyone else beat us to that Oeryl.

135296.en:
It's the sound of war! It's been too long since the blaring of military marches has been heard, the stockpiling of weapons undertaken, the murderous idealism of a young generation inveigled. And to me it all seems like the clinking of ISK.

War is one of the biggest boons to business you could hope for. It's a hungry giant that will eat anything you can throw at it. And the thing is, if you don't feed it, it will just eat you…. But if you feed it well? Oh, the rewards. Public recognition, sure, but the contracts, the contracts, {[character]player.name}! That's where the real ISK is. And we're going to get those contracts. Oh, yes. But first we need minerals.

Right now, it seems the giant on our doorstep wants Oeryl, and we're going to give it to him. There's a deposit out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Bring back all 5,600 units of the stuff and I'll make sure you get your share of the reward.

135297.en:
War is one of the biggest boons to business you could hope for. It's a hungry giant that will eat anything you can throw at it. And the thing is, if you don't feed it, it will just eat you…. But if you feed it well? Oh, the rewards. Public recognition, sure, but the contracts, the contracts, {[character]player.name}! That's where the real ISK is. And we're going to get those contracts. Oh, yes. But first we need minerals.

Right now, it seems the giant on our doorstep wants Oeryl, and we're going to give it to him. There's a deposit out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Bring back all 5,600 units of the stuff and I'll make sure you get your share of the reward.

135298.en: Here's the Oeryl. Uh, for the war effort.

135299.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}. Just remember, you're not a profiteer — you're securing the financial stability of the homefront.

135300.en: I'm not comfortable with the moral implications of this job.

135301.en: I knew you were one of those spineless sympathizers.

135302.en: It has been nearly a century since the Caldari-Gallente War, the last major war between any of the Great Empires, came to a close. Though skirmishes have broken out here and there, the distractions of the ever-expanding "lawless" space and the efforts of organizations such as CONCORD have helped maintain an uneasy peace. But no peace lasts forever.

135304.en: While you were puttering around, deciding whether you were going to do the Oeryl job, the government went and got its ore from another seller. Nice effort. Or rather, lack thereof.

135306.en: I can't continue doing this. Sorry, but I quit.

135307.en: Do you want the enemy to win? Do you?

135308.en: In the time it took you to fail this mission, nearly 250 brave pilots lost their lives. You also failed to make a load of money. You need to do better.

135310.en: Yeah, okay, I'll get your rock…

135311.en: Well, get going then! I need that rock!

135313.en: I hear there's some Green Arisite that a bunch of people are looking to get their hands on. Now, I don't know why they want it, but if they want it, I want it. You may have to hunt for it a bit; I hear the belt's got a lot of big broken-up old asteroids floating around. Might be a little creepy, but it shouldn't do you any harm, and I want that damn rock!

135314.en: I got there first! Here's your stupid green rock.

135315.en: Hah! Who's the stupid one?! Now I can sell it for a fortune to those other jerks!

135316.en: I think I'll pass. Also, you might want to cool off a bit.

135317.en: If I cooled off, I wouldn't have a business. Now move along.

135319.en:
Look, I hear there's some Green Arisite that a bunch of people are looking to get their hands on. Now, I don't know why they want it, but if they want it, I want it.

You may have to hunt for it a bit; I hear the belt's got a lot of big broken-up old asteroids floating around. Might be a little creepy, but it shouldn't do you any harm, and I want that damn rock!

Go get it before those other bastards get their grubby hands on it!

135320.en: On second thought? I'm out of here. And I think you're a little crazy.

135321.en: Yeah — like a fox! Suit yourself, it's your loss.

135322.en: If the pay is good, I'm there.

135323.en: Indeed. And paid you will be.

135324.en: Why is that? You got something for me?

135325.en:
Demand for minerals is skyrocketing. Which is good for us. More demand means more profit.

To fill that demand, though, we're having to turn to some unorthodox ores: Green Arisite, for instance. I know of a large field that's full of the stuff. If you can get it for me, I'll make sure you're reimbursed. We just may be able to make some use of it, with the right tech. Who knows?

135326.en: Your Green Arisite. But I think you're gonna lose your shirt on this one…

135327.en: Good job. Nice working with you

135328.en: Not today, sorry. Uh, my cousin just asked for help moving some furniture…

135329.en: I guess I'll find someone who likes ISK, then.

135330.en: Green Arisite is relatively worthless because of the high costs of reprocessing; one is far better off mining Gneiss instead. As a result, you won't find the former ore on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Arisite at the mission location, just right-click the "Green Arisite" icon in  this mission's details in your Opportunities interface and select "Add to Overview."

135332.en:
I do. And it's going to be a big haul.

Demand for minerals is skyrocketing. All the big empires are stockpiling for the coming fight. Oh, come on, you've seen the signs! Ships, rockets, drones, fortifications — all these things take material. The skirmishes out in 0.0 aren't lessening the demand any, either. Which is good for us. More demand means more profit.

To fill that demand, we're having to turn to some unorthodox ores. Green Arisite, for instance. I know of a large field that's full of the stuff. If you can get it for me, I'll make sure you're reimbursed. We just may be able to make some use of it, with the right tech. Who knows?

135333.en:
Too. Many. Rocks. Uhhhh…

I quit.

135334.en: What kind of miner are you?

135335.en: I can harvest the cloud for you.

135336.en: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good gas harvester around here.

135337.en: Gallente? I'll take care of them.

135338.en:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. The best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. Of course, you'll also need to deal with whatever drones are there.

135339.en: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.

135340.en: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.

135341.en: I'm afraid I can't do this.

135342.en: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Thanks for being honest, though.

135344.en: Take the reporter from {[location]agentStationID.name} to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, then report back.

135346.en: Well, not everyone has the stomach to do what must be done. Do you think you could manage to carry a reporter from point A to point B, or will that strain your moral sensibilities?

135347.en: I've had just about enough of you anyway.

135348.en: Don't forget, we are making sure that the blame for this action falls where it truly belongs: on the Amarr.

135349.en:
Good enough. Since someone else took care of that job you couldn't handle, things should still work out alright.

Come back to me when you're ready to do some more work for the cause... assuming you can handle it.

135350.en: Some people just aren't ready to serve the greater good.

135351.en: I think I can manage that.

135353.en: I don't want to be involved with anyone who thinks that your methods are acceptable.

135354.en: I don't want to be involved with anyone who thinks that your methods are acceptable.

135355.en: Something a little less morally objectionable, yes.

135356.en: Go pick up the reporter at the location I've given you and bring him back to me.

135357.en:
Weak moral constitution, I suppose. Very well, then.

Go pick up a reporter waiting at a nearby station -- I'll give you the location -- and bring him back to me. Will that be supportable?

135358.en: I gave you every opportunity to help our cause.

135359.en:
Sure, chief. Whatever.

Oh, I suppose: At least you're doing something halfways useful.

135360.en:
While you were ferrying that reporter over here, someone else took out that CONCORD committee, so there's still some real progress being made.

Come see me again when you're ready for real action.

135361.en: I gave you every opportunity to help our cause.

135362.en:
The ship was still destroyed, but the Empire managed to dodge the blame again. I've been hearing stories ranging from pirates to equipment failure. If you had done as I originally asked, at least some good would have come of this destruction.

Instead, you couldn't even move a reporter within a reasonable timeframe. Hold your head up high, {[character]player.name}.

135363.en:
The ship was still destroyed, but the Empire managed to dodge the blame again. I've been hearing stories ranging from pirates to equipment failure. If you had done as I originally asked, at least some good would have come of this destruction.

Instead, you couldn't even move a reporter within a reasonable timeframe. Hold your head up high, {[character]player.name}.

135366.en: Um, okay. You could be a little less of a jerk about it, though.

135368.en: I'm not interested in this busy-work.

135369.en: You know what? I'm tired of being insulted by a crazy person. I quit.

135370.en: That sounds potentially less crazy, yeah.

135371.en: It just so happens I am trained in Gas Harvesters. I'll do it.

135372.en: Thank you. Get back as quickly as you can.

135374.en:
I need pain medications badly. I can't just wait for the next delivery. I need to produce my own drugs. For that I'm going to need Gamboge Cytoserocin. I heard a smuggler say there was a pocket at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Go there, and bring back everything you can. I'll try to make it worth your while.

You need to fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission.

135375.en: Here's your gas. Do some good with it.

135376.en: More good will come from this than you know.

135377.en: I'm afraid I cannot do this.

135378.en: Okay, that's fine. It's better that you're upfront with these things than not.

135379.en: Although the compounds that are popularly called "boosters" are illegal in empire space, other legal derivatives of gas cloud materials are used in the medical community. These medicinal drugs are highly controlled, but are often the difference between life and death for many citizens.

135381.en:
The government says we're prepared for war. You wouldn't know it by looking at our wounded. Space makes everything worse. Just look through the medical bay. Second-degree burns and frostbite are both alarmingly common, and are usually in conjunction with other serious injuries.

I need pain medications badly. I can't just wait for the next delivery. I need to produce my own drugs. For that I'm going to need Gamboge Cytoserocin. I heard a smuggler say there was a pocket at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Go there, and bring back everything you can. I'll try to make it worth your while.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.

135382.en:
I have a friend in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I'd better go lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

Your agent's datapad has given you the coordinates to one of the competitors of your agent's "friend" in the Gallente Navy. Your "mission" once you arrive there should be abundantly clear.

135383.en: Strange, isn't it.... how someone can just completely forget about a conversation? Though some conversations are best left forgotten, right, {[character]player.name}?

135384.en: Oh, you will? That's so very kind of you, {[character]player.name}. Perhaps we can talk again later, after I've had a little nap.

135385.en: Is that so? Dear me... that's quite unfortunate. I am terribly sorry to hear it, {[character]player.name}. Here, take this compensation for the concern you must also be feeling; hopefully it will ease your mind somewhat.

135386.en: Yes, of course, please forgive me. I'll just get some rest now. Do close the door on your way out. <sigh>

135387.en: You seem to have forgotten what I was talking about too, {[character]player.name}! Ah well, perhaps it was a conversation best left forgotten.

135390.en: Yes, just get some rest {[character]agentID.name}. Don't you worry, I'll take good care of your friend's problem for you.

135391.en: It's good to see you so well rested, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm afraid I have some bad news: I've lost your datapad, the one with the coordinates on it? Oh, and I fear that a certain Gallente lieutenant may have run into some trouble as well.

135392.en: What the hell are you yammering on about?! I 'm going to go wash down a few Starsi and leave you to your rest. You apparently need it.

135393.en: I just wanted to let you know that I too forgot everything you were talking about. Seems that now we both forgot, hmm? Guess I'll come back for a real mission later.

135394.en: I'm ready to serve in any way I can.

135395.en:
Gallente Navy ships are not often allowed inside State borders – at least not officially. Conditions determined in the Iyen-Oursta Treaty at the end of the war place strict conditions on the manner in which each nation's fleets enter the other's sovereign space.

One of the current laws allows such deployments, though, if they are hired by a third party as part of usual trade business. Additionally, they must meet stringent size and composition requirements that greatly limit any damage they could potentially cause. Since official search and rescue missions are, by treaty, conducted exclusively by the nation that owns the space, further "hostile" forces cannot legally be sent to recover hired navy forces that go missing.

135396.en:
There has been an ongoing situation in the entertainment industry, the gambling sector in particular. We've started to see Gallente companies buying out the smaller ones here and reaping profits from our own citizens. Worse, they've offered Navy vessels as security for these companies' spacebound offices, many of which are located here in our own regions.

Make no mistake, {[character]player.name}: This is in all likelihood just their first step. Their intentions are nothing short of an economic war with us over one of our key industries, followed by a direct assault in our own backyard once we're sufficiently weakened.

So, we're getting loyal pod pilots like you together and sending them off to as many of these "company sites" as we can find. A local recon force recently found such a Gallente Navy headquarters nearby in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Get out there and deal with them. This is a standard office complex; an outer layer of security with the offices behind them. Take out all of the guards, then go for their headquarters.

135398.en:
There has been an ongoing situation in the entertainment industry, the gambling sector in particular. We've started to see Gallente companies buying out the smaller ones here and reaping profits from our own citizens. This isn't entirely new, of course — they've been trying to do it for decades — but it's actually seeing widespread success now.

What concerns us is that the Federation is officially starting to play an active role in all of this. They've offered Navy vessels as security for the companies' spacebound offices, many of which are located here in our own regions. Since these security forces come at a greatly subsidized cost, we're starting to see a few troubling things. First off, the companies obviously have more ISK to fund further acquisitions. More important, however, is this slow build-up inside our space of Gallente military units. They may be relatively inexperienced and poorly equipped, for the most part, but it's the quantity that concerns us, not the quality.

Make no mistake, {[character]player.name}: This is in all likelihood just their first step. Soon the Federation will forge these various companies into a more unified and organized conglomerate, and then we'll see them pushing to allow larger military escorts with better equipment. Their intentions are nothing short of an economic war with us over one of our key industries, followed by a direct assault in our own backyard once we're sufficiently weakened.

So, we're getting loyal pod pilots like you together and sending them off to as many of these "company sites" as we can find. They were supposed to have registered their offices with our officials, but a combination of lazy State bureaucrats and Gallente scheming means there are currently numerous sites out there that we don't have exact coordinates for. Our mistake in part, yes, but we're fixing it now. It's easy enough to disclaim any official involvement in this little removal operation too, since we have your kind doing the work for us.

Anyway, a local recon force recently found such a Gallente Navy headquarters nearby in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Are you ready to act?

135399.en: You disappoint me, {[character]player.name}. Next time you take up a mission, understand that we will expect you to see it through — no matter the cost.

135400.en: Excellent, I'm sure you will, {[character]player.name}. I'm sending the location now.

135401.en: You did? Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. On behalf of the countless Caldari whose jobs you have saved, I thank you.

135402.en: The State does not ask much of its people. Your lack of loyalty will not be tolerated for very long around these parts, {[character]player.name}.

135403.en: You promised to deal with that company I needed removed, remember? Well, now too much time has passed and they've relocated their headquarters after noticing our scouts. You have let me down, {[character]player.name}, and countless other Caldari as well.

135404.en: My offer of work is withdrawn. I can't wait for you to consider the mission forever, {[character]player.name}. I've given the task to another pilot who can act more speedily.

135407.en: I can't believe this is allowed to happen! Give me the coordinates. I'll show them the fast route back to Gallente space: via clone replacement.

135408.en: My work is done. You won't be seeing any new acquisition bids from that company.

135409.en: I don't think I care enough about your economic concerns to risk my ship over it.

135410.en: You know, upon reflection, I'm less sure about this mission now. They're not breaking any laws, so if you want them gone you'll have to find someone else.

135412.en:
Over the years, the Caldari have seen various citizens desert their posts in search of better futures elsewhere. The Guristas have always recruited disgruntled ex-State pilots into their ranks, while Mordu's Legion has taken in those who were unhappy with their place in the State, but who remained patriotic or were otherwise obligated to maintain good relations.

Recently, however, there has been an increase in defections to various Gallente corporations, usually in the research and security sectors, and even to the Federation Navy. While such a thing was virtually unheard of in the past, the Federation is increasingly becoming the home to a certain class of Caldari: those skilled pilots and technicians who have come to disagree violently with the State, but who, for various reasons, do not want to enter the seedy underworld of galactic piracy. Such people have found the Federation most sympathetic and welcoming.

135413.en:
One of our people has betrayed us and is planning to defect to the Gallente. This particular traitor is fairly high-profile, you see, which makes it difficult for us to act more openly. I need this situation sorted. We have to send a message that any treacherous behavior against the State will have truly dire consequences.

We have been able to locate the traitor's temporary living quarters, which are still in State space and therefore under our jurisdiction. Can you head over there and deal with this, {[character]player.name}? I don't want this fool making it to Gallente space alive. Oh, and bring what's left of him back to me, just for certainty's sake.

135415.en:
We have a serious matter to deal with, {[character]player.name}. Very serious. One of our people has betrayed us and is planning to defect to the Gallente.

It's not as if he knows anything particularly important. Nor does he pose much of a threat. It's the principle of the thing. And the example this sets for others. This particular traitor is fairly high-profile, you see, which makes it difficult for us to act more openly. We've already lost enough people to the Guristas and the Legion, and if we start losing people to the Federation, who knows where it will end.

I need this situation sorted. We have to send a message that any treacherous behavior against the State has consequences. We have been able to locate the traitor's temporary living quarters, which are still in State space and therefore under our jurisdiction. We have a small window of opportunity to act before he leaves for the Federation. Can you head over there and deal with this, {[character]player.name}? I don't want this fool making it to Gallente space alive.

135416.en: Let him?! And let the Federation propaganda machine turn him against us entirely? A very foolish stance, {[character]player.name}. Your failure to act will only encourage more problems of this kind.

135417.en: Good to hear. One less leech, we can do without.

135418.en: Ha! Impressive work, {[character]player.name}. I heard you made a real mess of those traitors. Here is your reward — take it with my thanks.

135419.en: Excuse me? You want to encourage this behavior?! Your lack of loyalty is disconcerting, {[character]player.name}. Not to mention the lack of foresight....

135420.en: I made it explicitly clear to you that there was only a small amount of time to stop that traitor from defecting to the Federation. The opportunity has passed. Mend your ways, {[character]player.name}, or you will find yourself without friends very quickly.

135421.en: I cannot keep waiting for an answer, {[character]player.name}. If we cannot deal with this traitor quickly, he will vanish into Federation space. Since you seem unable to help me battle this problem, I will find another pilot with the courage and the initiative to do so.

135424.en: Yes, it's a distressing trend, I agree. I'll see to it he never makes it to Federation space.

135425.en: It's done: Add one more traitor to the body count... and some ISK to my account, please.

135426.en: What a pointless job! I want to make a difference, maybe get rich along the way... not chase down people who just happen to like Intaki wine. Get back to me with some real work, ok?

135427.en: You know what? I've changed my mind. If this guy wants to run to Gallente so bad, let him.

135428.en: I might be. What did you have in mind?

135508.en:
The Gallente have somehow discovered one of our secret cloning facilities, and I'm told their orders to attack it have come from the most senior of Federation military officials.

I can't stress enough the importance of this mission. If those clone bays go down, we'll have a huge problem on our hands. I don't have the clearance to know exactly whose clones are being stored where, nor if they are the only copies. All I know is that they are holding important people, very important.

Fly over there immediately, and destroy any and all hostiles you see. Once the facility is secure, we can send in the relocation fleet and move it all safely away. You must move quickly, though! This initial force is undoubtedly just the scouting party since they're not attacking the facility yet. We need them cleared out before we have a fleet of Navy Moros besieging the facility.

135510.en: Well… then why did you accept it in the first place?! Damned podders. Where is your loyalty, your commitment!? Get out of here.

135511.en: Ha! Yes… yes indeed. You're a source of inspiration for us all, I assure you. I'll have the transport fleet on standby; report back to me immediately after the area is secure.

135512.en: You truly are an asset to the State, {[character]player.name}. I honestly don't know what we would have done without your help. Be proud of the work you have done today.

135513.en: Suicide missions!? You have a clone, do you not, {[character]player.name}?! Unlike the many important Caldari whose clones are in peril…! A true Caldari would give anything to serve the State in such an important matter. Clearly you are no such thing.

135514.en: Because of your inaction, thousands of Caldari lives were lost retaking the cloning facility. I can barely describe the level of profound disappointment I have in you, {[character]player.name}. Do not offer your services in the future unless you truly intend to provide them.

135515.en:
It should not take anywhere near this long to decide on a mission of such importance. I cannot wait for you any longer; I've arranged for a more reliable party to secure the facility.

I suggest you fix your attitude.

135518.en: Okay, relax. I've got this one in the bag. That's why you asked me, remember? I'll get my people together and we'll have a barbecue, Caldari-style.

135519.en: I told you I had it covered. You can send your fleet in now.

135520.en: Wait… you're actually serious about asking me to do all this? I'm not standing between a Gallente fleet and a target like that! Find someone else for your suicide missions!

135521.en: It's a hopeless situation, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm afraid you're going to have to find another solution. I can't involve myself any further in this; I just don't have the resources to deliver the results.

135522.en: Born ready, {[character]agentID.name}. But, uh, what the hell is going on? You look about ready to slit someone's throat.

135573.en: They should do both, {[character]player.name}! We first have to remove them; then and only then will we have proof of what they were up to. I now regret my faith in you; you are capable, no doubt, but short-sighted.

135574.en: I thought you would agree with me on this. I'm uploading you the location of the memorial site now. Just be prepared for a fight: They won't take kindly to being forcibly removed.

135575.en: Disgusting, isn't it? I can only wonder about a nation that cares only for material gain. No doubt it won't be the last time you have to do this sort of thing for us… but at least we have reliable people like you to count on.

135576.en: I admire your humanity. This is, however, exactly what they're expecting us to do. They'll just withdraw before the media storm hits and we'll still look like brutal imperialists.

135577.en: Did you forget what you promised me, {[character]player.name}? I asked you to clear that memorial site of Caldari presence, and still no word back from you. I'm tired of waiting; I'm going to hand the job over to someone more reliable and deserving.

135580.en: Of course. If the Caldari are going to exploit such sacred places for profit, then I'll be the first one to get in their way.

135581.en: The area has been cleared of foreign personnel and structures. They defended it surprisingly well, so I think it's safe to say we haven't seen the end of this matter.

135582.en: That's pretty sickening, I agree, but I don't think we should remove them. Just expose what they're up to and the situation will resolve itself, I'm sure.

135583.en: I've changed my mind about this one, sorry. If they want to make a profit out of their own memorials, then they can answer to their own conscience, not to our guns.

135584.en: You do? Alright, then, let's hear it.

135585.en:
I have a friend in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I'd better go lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

Your agent's datapad has given you the coordinates to one of the competitors of your agent's "friend" in the Gallente Navy. Your "mission" once you arrive there should be abundantly clear.

135586.en:
The corporations of the State have many friends, as you know... many friends in many interesting and useful places. Why is this relevant, you ask? Well, it's not at all… it was merely an idle thought I had today that I wanted to impart upon you.

But actually, now I come to think about the topic of friends… I am reminded of a particular friend of mine in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them. But it would be very, er, helpful... for me — for us — if this friend of ours were to get what he wants.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, with all the random third party violence these days, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Right. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I better go and lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

135587.en: Strange, isn't it.... how someone can just completely forget about a conversation? Though some conversations are best left forgotten, right, {[character]player.name}?

135588.en: Oh, you will? That's so very kind of you, {[character]player.name}. Perhaps we can talk again later, after I've had a little nap.

135589.en: Is that so? Dear me... that's quite unfortunate. I am terribly sorry to hear it, {[character]player.name}. Here, take this compensation for the concern you must also be feeling; hopefully it will ease your mind somewhat.

135590.en: Yes, of course, please forgive me. I'll just get some rest now. Do close the door on your way out. <sigh>

135591.en: You seem to have forgotten what I was talking about too, {[character]player.name}! Ah well, perhaps it was a conversation best left forgotten.

135594.en: Yes, just get some rest {[character]agentID.name}. Don't you worry, I'll take good care of your friend's problem for you.

135595.en: It's good to see you so well rested, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm afraid I have some bad news: I've lost your datapad, the one with the coordinates on it? Oh, and I fear that a certain Gallente captain may have run into some trouble as well.

135596.en: What the hell are you yammering on about?! I 'm going to go wash down a few Starsi and leave you to your rest. You apparently need it.

135597.en: I just wanted to let you know that I too forgot everything you were talking about. Seems that now we both forgot, hmm? Guess I'll come back for a real mission later.

135598.en: I'm ready to serve in any way I can.
