135609.en: What the hell are you yammering on about?! I 'm going to go wash down a few Starsi and leave you to your rest. You apparently need it.

135610.en: I just wanted to let you know that I too forgot everything you were talking about. Seems that now we both forgot, hmm? Guess I'll come back for a real mission later.

135611.en: I'm ready to serve in any way I can.

135629.en:
Amarrian society, a religious oligarchy, relies on slaves to do nearly all of its manual labor and servant work. Of course, Gallenteans despise this practice. Honest workers should be given an honest wage, not kept in bondage.

Amarr's slaves are often taken wherever they can be found. Citizens of the Gallente Federation, as any other nation, sometimes find themselves locked in Amarrian slave collars. Most of the time, there is little to be done about it, especially if the slaves were kidnapped in low-security or otherwise lightly policed areas of space.

135630.en:
An Amarrian Holder we've suspected for some time of black market slave trading has overstepped his bounds and nabbed a few Gallente citizens for his slave pens. You must stop him. He thinks he's getting away unnoticed, but I want you to prove him wrong.

Destroy this scumbag's ship and bring those slaves back to me, {[character]player.name}. We'll make sure they are returned to their homes. After they pay back their transport fees, that is.

You will need a well-armed frigate to accomplish this mission. The slave ship is probably armed, and might have escorts as well.

135632.en:
Alright, then. An Amarrian Holder we've suspected for some time of black market slave trading has overstepped his bounds and nabbed a few loyal Gallente citizens for his slave pens. You must stop him. He thinks he's getting away unnoticed, but I want you to prove him wrong.

Destroy this scumbag's ship and bring those slaves back to me, {[character]player.name}. We'll make sure they are returned to their homes. After they pay back their transport fees, that is.

135633.en: Good, good. I like your spirit. That's why I asked you to do this job.

135634.en: Excellent. I'm sure those poor, unwashed people would shower you with gratitude. But first, let's see that they have showers of their own, eh?

135639.en: I'll bring back those citizens, don't you worry.

135640.en: Alright, I'm back. One less slaver to worry about, assuming he didn't have a clone, and a bunch of Gallenteans happy to be home.

135642.en:
Pisharpar Corilian is one of the most renowned Amarrian poets of all time. He is also a spy. He has been on a "book tour" of Gallente space for several months now, and our suspicions were confirmed when we tracked a coded transmission coming from his pleasure yacht. We believe he has had secret data chips implanted within his massive rolls of flesh, where he can hide all sorts of sensitive information.

We cannot tolerate this blatant abuse of the arts! We want him terminated immediately… but it must look like piracy. That's where you come in. He is currently traveling to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Warp in, blast him and his entourage to smithereens, and warp out. Simple.

Now, it's likely that a man this respected in Amarrian society has a clone, but at least we'll have destroyed whatever information he's gathered into his data-ridden body. Take care of him, and you'll be doing us all a great favor.

135643.en:
This, {[character]player.name}: All the great nations in the galaxy have long allowed each other to travel freely in pursuit of commerce, but I've just heard a story that makes me think this time of freedom is near its end.

Pisharpar Corilian is one of Amarr's most renowned poets of all time. He is gifted, but a typical example of a poet. He's effete, arrogant, and overly sensitive — always with his head in the clouds and his feet floating half a meter off the floor. In Corilian's case, this is literal: So obese that his legs can no longer support his weight, he uses a hoverchair to get around.

He is also a spy. He has been on a "book tour" of Gallente space for several months now, and our suspicions were confirmed when we tracked a coded transmission coming from his pleasure yacht. We believe he has had secret data chips implanted within his massive rolls of flesh, where he can hide all sorts of sensitive information.

We cannot tolerate this blatant abuse of the arts! We want him terminated immediately… but it must look like piracy. That's where you come in. He is currently traveling to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Warp in, blast him and his entourage to smithereens, and warp out. Simple.

Now, it's likely that a man this respected in Amarrian society has a clone, but at least we'll have destroyed whatever information he's gathered into his data-ridden body. Take care of him, and you'll be doing us all a great favor — both politically and artistically... (If you've never read his work, you'll have to take my word for it.)

135644.en: You can't handle one pitiful, overweight poet? What kind of capsuleer are you?

135646.en: Nice work. When news gets out, of course, it will be a "terrible act of piracy"… but in the meantime I think we can drink a toast to that whining bastard's bloated, frozen corpse.

135647.en: Wow, I would never have thought…. Well, I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

135652.en: Very well. It ain't over till... well, er, till the fat man is dead.

135653.en: Chalk up one large, whiny poet. Clone or no, that was a surprising pleasure, I must admit.

135654.en: But I myself am a great patron of the arts! I love his work!! I can't kill him!

135655.en: Find somebody else to do this. I have better things to do than hunt down some stupid poet, even if he is a spy.

135656.en: Uh, okay. Fair enough. Care to explain what's on your mind, though?

135657.en:
The toxic chemical known as Vitoc is the preferred method Amarrians use to control their slaves. The drug is injected into the slaves, and the slaves must work to retrieve a periodic dose of antidote to the poison. Gallente scientists, among others, have been chasing the formula for Vitoc for years, but without success. The drug behaves in many ways like a virus.

If one could find the cure, the entire Amarrian economy might be crippled… assuming that cure could somehow be supplied to a sufficient number of their slaves.

135658.en:
An informant within the Amarrian Empire has given us a break in our long quest to find the cure for the slave drug, Vitoc. A sample of their most recent version of the drug has been ... diverted to be transported on an industrial ship passing near Gallente space. If we move quickly, we can intercept the industrial ship, steal its top secret cargo, and it will all be blamed on pirates.

Destroy the industrial ship and bring the Vitoc to me.

Amarrian convoys are well guarded when they pass near Gallente space. Be prepared for a fight.

135660.en:
An informant within the Empire has given us a break in our long quest to find a counter for the slavers' drug, Vitoc. A sample of their most recent version of the drug has been… diverted, to be transported on an industrial ship passing through Gallente space. If we move quickly, we can intercept the ship and steal its cargo, and — the best part? — it will all be blamed on pirates.

Destroy the industrial ship and bring the Vitoc to me. Can you do it?

135661.en: This was a golden opportunity to strike a serious blow against Amarr slavery! Have you no guts at all?

135662.en: I'm uploading you the coordinates as we speak. Your target will not be in this area for long, though, so don't dally.

135663.en: Excellent work. I'm glad we can depend on you. Our scientists will want to see this stuff as soon as possible.

135664.en: I see. Showing your true colors, eh? Well, I just hope I can find a pilot with a sense of moral propriety for this job.

135669.en: I'm the capsuleer for this job. Just tell me where to find that ship.

135670.en: Alright – those Amarr creeps never knew what hit them, and I've got the Vitoc samples right here.

135671.en: I don't care all that much about any Amarrian slaves. I mean, sure, slavery's bad… but risk my ship over it? No, thanks.

135672.en: I just don't have time for this Vitoc mission. You'll have to find someone else.

135673.en: Wow, great news! How can I help?

135689.en: Sometimes a mission might not turn out the way you anticipated. You might have incomplete information from your agent, and conditions can change during the mission. Such changes are generally communicated to you directly, either through a direct pop-up window when using an acceleration gate or by means of a text message appearing in your local chat channel.

135690.en:
We have a research scientist currently in a small, secret outpost near here; he's originally Caldari, but he recognized the error of his upbringing and came over to our side after the war. More importantly, though, he's on the verge of a breakthrough in a high-priority weapons technology project. And likely as a direct result of that research, we think someone's trying to kill him. He has requested secure transport out of there, and we can't risk losing him.

Head over to the location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring him back here to me, will you? This mission requires the utmost secrecy, so don't tell anyone where you're going or say anything about your passenger. Got it? He's an important man, and there will be a decent bonus if you get him here discreetly and quickly.

135692.en:
We have a research scientist currently in a small, secret outpost near here; he's originally Caldari, but he recognized the error of his upbringing and came over to our side after the war. This mission requires the utmost secrecy, so don't tell anyone where you're going or say anything about your passenger. Got it? He's an important man, and there will be a decent bonus if you get him here discreetly and quickly.

135693.en: You can't be serious…!? Such a lack of initiative looks quite bad, my friend. Quite bad indeed.

135695.en: Well done. You're a resourceful capsuleer. And yes, never fear — we take care of our own.

135696.en: Oh, I see. Matters of national importance are too dreary for you, eh? I see it all too clearly…

135702.en: Looks like your scientist has had, er, a… bit of a setback. Too bad about that.  Hope he had a good clone ready.

135703.en: Let him find his own ride. My time is too valuable to spend it ferrying around some egghead.

135704.en: You know, on second thought, let this lapdog scientist of yours find his own ride.

135705.en: Okay, sounds good. What is it?

135707.en: That's precisely what I wanted to hear. I'm glad we understand one another. Don't waste any time.

135708.en: Ha! Nice work, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your reward — you've earned it.

135709.en: You would allow a madman to harm our beloved monument? What kind of patriot are you? Gods, I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

135710.en:
{[character]player.name},

Your lack of initiative has allowed that insane Amarrian terrorist to detonate a bomb on the Crystal Boulevard! Where the hell were you?! Thousands are dead, and the repair costs will be astronomical. But you capsuleers never seem to think in such terms. Sickening, really.

I pray, for all our sakes, that you will learn to let your conscience guide you in the future.

{[character]agentID.name}

135712.en: This madman will never plant his bomb. Or see another sunrise, for that matter.

135713.en: The terrorist is now a grease smear on his battlecruiser's smoking wreck.

135714.en: What do I care about the Crystal Boulevard? I never shop there.

135715.en: Okay, I'm officially intrigued. What's up?

135716.en:
There's been an increase in Caldari activity in surrounding systems. We think those self-righteous bastards might be up to something. Of course, that's nothing new.

We've placed passive reconnaissance units in several nearby locations, but we don't want any direct transmissions from them for fear of attracting Caldari attention. So we've decided to dispatch "unofficial" vessels like yours to pick up the data chips from their base and bring them back here. The Caldari are less likely to suspect — or at least less likely to interfere with — a capsuleer, so they should leave you alone.

If you do get jumped, however, remember that the recon unit is the top priority. Get it out of there if you can. Do it fast and there'll be a substantial bonus.

135717.en: I knew you were good for it, {[character]player.name}.

135718.en: Good job, capsuleer. You show some promise, I must admit.

135719.en: I can't say I'm too surprised, {[character]player.name}.

135721.en: Here are the data chips from your recon base, {[character]agentID.name}.

135722.en: Sorry. I don't want to get involved.

135723.en: Yeah, I'm interested in helping out.

135724.en: Acceleration gates are one of the main means of intrastellar travel. They can propel space craft great distances without the need for a large gravitational body as an end point.  If the enemy has found a way to quickly and properly configure an acceleration gate to be used as a weapon, the consequences could be dire indeed.

135725.en:
We've found what appears to be a large collection of acceleration gates surrounded by Minmatar ships. These gates have apparently been modified to act as "simple" mass drivers. Theoretically, they could propel asteroids or similar celestial bodies at Amarrian targets. The combination of mass and velocity produced by such a gate could easily destroy a station; I don't even want to think what the results would be for a planetary impact.

We need you to stop the Minmatar before they get a chance to use these devices. Destroy any enemy ships you find. But do not destroy the gates: We do not know how dangerous that would be… and in any case, our scientists want to take a closer look.

135727.en:
We just received intel from one of our patrols. They were following up reports of strange gravimetric fluctuations in a small region of space. What they found—

It appears to be a large collection of acceleration gates. And they're surrounded by Minmatar ships. The gates have apparently been modified to act as "simple" mass drivers. If they actually work, they could propel asteroids at Amarrian targets. The combination of mass and velocity produced by such a gate could easily destroy a station. I don't even want to think what the results would be for a planetary impact.

We need you to stop the Minmatar before they get a chance to use these devices. Destroy any enemy ships you find. But do not destroy the gates. We do not know how dangerous that would be… and in any case, our scientists want to take a closer look.

135729.en: Remember, only destroy the enemy ships. The gates are not to be harmed.

135730.en: Good work. Our agents are over there now, dismantling the gates for study. This technology could go a long way to helping us destroy the Minmatar threat once and for all.

135731.en: We'll see how sorry you are when the Minmatar start throwing asteroids through your house.

135732.en: We've detected several large explosions coming from the enemy mass driver cluster. Apparently their experiment failed. We simply lucked out on this. Had you responded faster, though, we might have secured the technology and developed it properly for ourselves.

135733.en: We've detected several large explosions coming from the enemy mass driver cluster. Apparently their experiment failed. We simply lucked out on this. Had you responded faster, though, we might have secured the technology and developed it properly for ourselves.

135736.en: The Minmatar will be driven from the system.

135737.en: The system is safe.  The Minmatar have been destroyed.

135738.en: I'm sorry, but I'm not going to go against the Minmatar over some supposed super-weapon that probably won't work anyway.

135739.en: I'm sorry, but I can't clear the Minmatar from the acceleration gates. Don't ask me why. I just can't.

135741.en: Acceleration gates are one of the main means of intrastellar travel. They can propel space craft great distances without the need for a large gravitational body as an end point. 135753.en: The Gallente will be driven from the system.

135754.en: The system is safe.  The Gallente have been driven out.

135755.en: I'm sorry, but I'm not going to go against the Gallente over some supposed super-weapon that probably won't work anyway.

135756.en: I'm sorry, but I can't clear the Gallente from the acceleration gates. Don't ask me why. I just can't.

135758.en: Acceleration gates are one of the main means of intrastellar travel. They can propel space craft great distances without the need for a large gravitational body as an end point.  If the enemy has found a way to quickly and properly configure an acceleration gate to be used as a weapon, the consequences could be dire indeed.

135759.en:
We've found what appears to be a large collection of acceleration gates surrounded by Caldari Navy. These gates have apparently been modified to act as "simple" mass drivers. Theoretically, they could propel asteroids or similar celestial bodies at Gallente targets. The combination of mass and velocity produced by such a gate could easily destroy a station; I don't even want to think what the results would be for a planetary impact.

We need you to stop the Caldari before they get a chance to use these devices. Destroy any enemy ships you find. But do not destroy the gates: We do not know how dangerous that would be… and in any case, our scientists want to take a closer look.

135761.en:
We just received intel from one of our patrols. They were following up reports of strange gravimetric fluctuations in a small region of space. What they found—

It appears to be a large collection of acceleration gates. They're surrounded by Caldari ships. The gates have apparently been modified to act as "simple" mass drivers. If they actually work, they could propel asteroids at Gallente targets. The combination of mass and velocity produced by such a gate could easily destroy a station; I don't even want to think what the results would be for a planetary impact.

We need you to stop the Caldari before they get a chance to use these devices. Destroy any enemy ships you find. But do not destroy the gates. We do not know how dangerous that would be… and in any case, our scientists want to take a closer look.

135763.en: Remember, only destroy the enemy ships. The gates are not to be harmed.

135764.en: Good work. Our agents are over there now, dismantling the gates for study. This technology could go a long way to helping us quell the Caldari once and for all.

135765.en: We'll see how sorry you are when the Caldari start throwing asteroids through your house.

135766.en: We've detected several large explosions coming from the enemy mass driver cluster. Apparently their experiment failed. We simply lucked out on this. Had you responded faster, though, we might have secured the technology and developed it properly for ourselves.

135781.en: Good work. Our engineers are over there now, dismantling the gates for study.  This technology could go a long way to helping us obliterate the stain of the Amarr once and for all.

135782.en: We'll see how sorry you are when the Amarr start throwing asteroid through your house.

135783.en: We've detected several large explosions coming from the enemy mass driver cluster. Apparently their experiment failed. We simply lucked out on this. Had you responded faster, though, we might have secured the technology and developed it properly for ourselves.

135788.en: The system is safe.  The Amarr have been driven out.

135789.en: I'm sorry, but I'm not going to go against the Amarr over some supposed super-weapon that probably won't work anyway.

135790.en: I'm sorry, but I can't clear the Ammarr from the acceleration gates. Don't ask me why. I just can't.

135792.en: Ah, {[character]player.name}, good to see you. To business. We've just detected a hidden Amarrian reconnaissance outpost nearby. I don't need to explain the threat to you, do I? We must wipe them out before they are able to expand their operations further into our territory. If you can take care of this problem for me, you will be well rewarded.

135793.en: Good job. We should be receiving the tracking data shortly -- be sure to check back in soon.

135794.en:
We've decrypted the data and analyzed the telemetry, and the Caldari are definitely amassing near this sector for some reason. Worse still, we suspect that our communication problems aren't the result of excessive ionization after all: We think the Caldari are jamming our transmissions. We sent out some scouts to track down the source of the interference, and they've traced the jamming signals to a location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I've added it to your bookmarks.

It's vital that we figure out just exactly what the Caldari are up to as soon as possible. Enemy scouts may be interdicting any traffic in that system as well, so be on the lookout for enemy vessels. Avoid or destroy them, as you see fit.

There's bound to be a structure of some kind out there that's causing the signal interference, and I need you to see what exactly it's doing; access the structure and bring me whatever Communications Logs you find inside.

135795.en:
We did, yes. This is big, really big. We've decrypted the data and analyzed the telemetry, and the Caldari are definitely amassing near this sector for some reason. Worse still, we suspect that our communication problems aren't the result of excessive ionization after all: We think the Caldari are jamming our transmissions. We sent out some scouts to track down the source of the interference, and they've traced the jamming signals to a location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

Here's the report with all pertinent information; I've added it to your bookmarks. It's vital that we figure out just exactly what they're up to as soon as possible. Enemy scouts may be interdicting any traffic in that system as well, so be on the lookout for enemy vessels. Avoid or destroy them, as you see fit.

There's bound to be a structure of some kind out there that's causing the signal interference, and I need you to see what exactly it's doing. Get a report on whatever you find out there back to me as soon as possible.

135796.en:
Even with the best of equipment and space superiority, any long-term military engagement has to rely on ground and station personnel. And personnel are only as reliable as their morale. I won't lie to you, the morale of our soldiers could be better.

To fix this, a number of the mega-corporations have joined together to produce SPLET—the State Personnel Life Enrichment Tour. This program will tour to various parts of the State, providing entertainment and other morale services for our soldiers.

The first thing we need is food, and there are crates of frozen food waiting not too far from here. Bring the food here so our chefs can start to figure out how to stretch it into an appropriately festive-- but still economical-- dish.

135797.en:
The courier ship Swiftsure had a warp drive mishap in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and was forced to jettison its cargo lest it be damaged or lost if the core blew. Eventually they managed to make it back in one piece; however, the cargo they had to ditch was a set of important Federation court records. We don't have backups available, so those records are irreplaceable.

{[character]player.name}, we need someone to head out there and find those records. There's a healthy reward in it for you if you succeed. I've uploaded the location of the Swiftsure's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and get it back to me here.

135798.en:
So it would seem.

Listen, the courier ship Swiftsure has just had a warp drive mishap in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and was forced to jettison its cargo lest it be damaged or lost if the core blew. They're crawling back to their home station as we speak; however, the cargo they had to ditch was a set of important Federation court records. We don't have backups available, so those records are irreplaceable, and they can't get another courier out there until tomorrow sometime. Bloody couriers. Can't get good help these days.

{[character]player.name}, we need someone to head out there and find those records right away. There's a healthy reward in it for you if you succeed. I've uploaded the location of the Swiftsure's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and get it back to me here.

135799.en:
My suppliers can't keep up with all this demand for their excellent moonshine. So I've taken the liberty of modifying the booze a little bit. Yes, yes, I admit it, I'm adding water to it. To make certain the drunkards I deal with won't notice, I've come up with a devilish little scheme.

An old schoolmate of mine is a janitor on the School of Applied Knowledge over in Sakkikainen. Some graduation students there have come up with a strange little mixture they call Rotgut. I don't know the scientific mumbo-jumbo for how it works, all I know is that it increases the intoxication effects of alcohol many times. That's exactly what I need for my watered-down wares. I need someone discreet to pop over there and get me a bit of this Rotgut. Then, once the new concoction is ready, all I have to do is lay back and watch the dimes roll in.

135800.en:
My suppliers can't keep up with all this demand for their excellent moonshine. So I've taken the liberty of modifying the booze a little bit. Yes, yes, I admit it, I'm adding water to it. To make certain the drunkards I deal with won't notice, I've come up with a devilish little scheme.

I need someone discreet to pop over there and get me a bit of this Rotgut. Then, once the new concoction is ready, all I have to do is lay back and watch the dimes roll in.

135801.en:
Good day to you. I was sent out here to this constellation to compile a comprehensive dossier about the political situation. The recipient of the dossier is none of your business. I must admit I underestimated the difficulty of this mission. After all, how much can be going on in a remote, unimportant constellation such as this? But the political situation here is in a constant motion. It seems lot of people are taking a sudden interest in this place.

Fortunately, I have found a solution to my problems here. The Angel Cartel has a strong presence here in Ani and they are even more anxious than I am to keep a tab on the goings on here. What I need to do is get my hands on some of the information they've collected. Then, finishing my report should be a breeze. Or that's what I hope, at least. The constant fluctuations in the political climate makes me fear my task here will be endless. Just remember to fit your Relic Analyzer into your ship before you head out.

135802.en:
Good day to you. I was sent out here to this constellation to compile a comprehensive dossier about the political situation. The recipient of the dossier is none of your business. I must admit I underestimated the difficulty of this mission. After all, how much can be going on in a remote, unimportant constellation such as this? But the political situation here is in a constant motion. It seems lot of people are taking a sudden interest in this place.

The constant fluctuations in the political climate makes me fear my task here will be endless. Just remember to fit your Analyzer into your ship before you head out.

135803.en:
The Crystal Boulevard is indeed one of the great monuments of the Gallente Federation. It is perhaps the most stunning sight in the galaxy, a sea of gleaming crystal spires and sparkling lights, teeming with inhabitants and tourists. As such, it is a symbol of pride for the Gallente, a symbol of wealth, a symbol of freedom.

That makes it a wonderful target for enemies of the Federation as well.

135804.en: Excellent. Now get to it, before that bastard gets away.

135805.en: Good job! We'll analyze the data right away. Come back in a few hours and we may have some more work for you.

135807.en: I've eliminated the traitor and obtained his log book.

135809.en:
Turns out the traitor was on his way to meet up with his contact, a Caldari spy, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. With luck, the contact is still out there waiting for the traitor's arrival.

Head out there and take him down.

135810.en:
We've analyzed the data you brought back from the traitor's ship. He was on his way to meet up with his contact, some Caldari spy, in the asteroid fields of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. With luck, the contact is still out there waiting for the traitor's arrival.

Can you head on out to that system and take him down? His ship is likely to be pretty powerful, but if you can capture him alive we'll provide you with a substantial bounty.

135812.en: Excellent job! You've helped deal a major blow to the Caldari spy network.

135813.en: I'll get him and bring him back.

135814.en: The contact has been dealt with, {[character]agentID.name}.

135815.en: Not really interested. Seems like this should be something for the Navy, anyway, no?

135816.en: I'm always ready to help. What's going on?

135817.en: See you when you return, my friend.

135818.en: You're a hell of a pilot, {[character]player.name}. Come back in a bit and I'll let you know if there's more work for you.

135819.en: I'll do it. Send me the coordinates.

135820.en: I've defeated the raiders and found the information you requested.

135821.en: Sounds good, {[character]agentID.name}. What do you need?

135822.en: Alright, then, capsuleer, go take some Caldari names.

135823.en: Great work! I suspect we won't be seeing anymore Caldari raiders in this sector for a while.

135827.en: I can't believe this! And here I was just going to pick up an Egonics headset for each of my cousin's kids… Okay, don't worry, just get me that ship's coordinates.

135828.en: I can't believe this! And here I was just going to pick up an Egonics headset for each of my cousin's kids… Okay, don't worry, just get me that ship's coordinates.

135830.en: All of the kidnapped citizens are safe at home now. They seem a bit groggy, but otherwise none the worse for wear.

135831.en: Magnificent, {[character]player.name}. Their families will be so happy to have them back. You've done a great deed today, my friend.

135832.en: What do I care about a few numbskull music freaks? Not worth my time.

135833.en: Not worth…?! Wha—? I can't believe you can say that! Get out of here, will you? I have to find someone else to save those kids.

135834.en:
Egonics, Inc. is unique in the Gallente music industry. Extremely popular among young citizens of virtually every star nation, Egonics produces the only entertainment headset that transmits music directly into the user's brain. The company's contracted musical artists tailor the music to the individual tastes of every listener.

The technology's growing popularity has caused it spread across the galaxy, except in the Amarr Empire, where possession of Egonics tech is outlawed.

135836.en:
What's wrong? Listen to this. Egonics headsets: They're the fashion, right? All the kids have to have them. But some people, including me, have always been afraid that something like this could happen.

Apparently some Amarrian slaver has found a way to hack the Egonics signal, at least at short range. Security cameras in a nearby station show hundreds of people — all of them wearing Egonics devices — simply walking into the cargohold of an Amarrian Bestower. This strange exodus went unnoticed because, other than their destination, the people seemed to be behaving normally. It wasn't until after the ship had departed the station and the missing persons reports starting coming in that we realized anything was amiss.

Security found that this Amarrian "citizen" had inserted subliminal commands into the Egonics signals at the station. Of course, they thought their network security was iron-clad, but now I can assure you they're rethinking their assumptions. This is a catastrophe of the highest order, {[character]player.name}!

Just imagine what a tragedy this would be if it wasn't Federation policy to put a tracking beacon on every Bestower that docks in our sovereignty!

If you can get all of those Gallente citizens back, there's a big reward for you. And if you can keep the Egonics corporate name out of it, so much the better… If you see any Scope reporters nosing around as you leave, pray, ignore them.

There are over 1,000 people missing. You will need a large cargo capacity to carry them all at once, unless you intend to make multiple runs to the deadspace location where the Amarrain ship is located.

The slaver ship likely has escorts, as well.

135837.en:
{[character]player.name},

Fortunately, the Navy was able to catch that Amarrian monster as he tried to leave Federation space with those kids. No thanks to you, of course. I can't believe you just sat on this mission! Over a thousand young lives were at stake!

I think maybe you need to take a deep look at what really matters to you in this life, friend. Obviously, something's not quite right in your head.

{[character]agentID.name}

135839.en: Forget it. I've changed my mind. Let the Navy deal with this.

135840.en: You're just going to let that slaver get away with a thousand kids? What kind of person are you? Perhaps you should work out of Amarr space from now on!

135843.en:
These pirates in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} are well funded, well equipped, and commanded by some canny ship commanders. In fact, we believe the Gallente government has sanctioned these "pirates" as privateers.

Go out there and wipe them out. Yes, this is a “terminate with extreme prejudice” matter. The bounty on the pirate commander is sizeable, but you'll need proof of his death to collect it: Bring back his head and you'll be well-rewarded for your efforts.

You're going to face a sizable force of pirates. You'll likely need at least a battlecruiser, and maybe even a few allies.

135844.en:
A gang of pirates has been terrorizing the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system for some time. And they've been using their base in that system as a launching point to strike out into neighboring systems as well. Of course, pirates are to be expected these days, but these pirates are different. They are well funded, well equipped, and commanded by some canny ship commanders.

A survivor of the pirate raids told us that at least two of the ship captains — including the pirates' leader himself — were once high-ranking officers in the Gallente Navy. In fact, we believe the Gallente government has sanctioned these pirates as privateers. The damage they have already caused to Amarrian interests is incalculable. Go out there and wipe them out. Yes, this one's a “terminate with extreme prejudice.”

The bounty on the pirate commander is sizeable, but you'll need proof of his death to collect it. Bring back his head and you'll be well-rewarded for your efforts.

You're going to face a sizable force of pirates. You'll likely need at least a battlecruiser, and maybe even a few allies.

135845.en: Don't have the stones? I'm sure there are plenty of ship captains courageous enough to grab this bounty.

135846.en: Good. But move quickly. These "pirates" could disappear at any time.

135847.en: Thank you for your assistance. You are a courageous pilot, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your rewards. You've earned them.

135848.en: Don't have the stones, huh? Well, I'm sure there are plenty of ship captains courageous enough to grab this bounty.

135849.en: Don't have the stones? Good thing there are plenty of ship captains courageous enough to grab this bounty. Consider yourself un-hired.

135851.en: This Gallente pirate is a dead man.

135852.en: Mission accomplished. The pirates are dead, and I have the commander's filthy gob in a jar in my cargo.

135853.en: You know, this sounds pretty risky. And I just had my ship cleaned and repainted. Nah, I'm gonna pass, thanks.

135854.en: Hey, I'm all about dealing with pirates. What's the problem?

135855.en: I guess you can't take the heat. There are others who will.

135857.en: Excellent work! That'll put the fear of their bloodthirsty god right into them.

135858.en: I'm sorry to hear that, {[character]player.name}. I'll find someone else, I suppose.

135859.en: Sounds like quite a challenge. Sure, I'll help.

135860.en: I took out the enemy vessels. Good fight, just like you said.

135861.en: Sorry, but I can't do it, {[character]agentID.name}. Pressing business elsewhere.

135862.en: I've changed my mind — these odds are too uncertain. I quit.

135863.en: Good day, {[character]agentID.name}. What can you offer me?

135864.en: Be prepared: I'm sure he has a few of his deputies along for the ride; together they are deadly.

135865.en:
Now that I have your attention, I'll tell you my story. I am a prominent salesman sent to Otitoh on a special assignment from Expert Distribution. Well… I was.

I was born and raised in New Caldari, and I wasn't prepared for the harsh life of this run-down system. My first few months here were quite difficult, and I often thought about abandoning my work here and running back to my family.

In my depressed and lonely state, I needed a companion: someone to ease the tension of everyday life here. My wife refused to leave our home in New Caldari, so I had no one. So, I was completely helpless when I stumbled upon a beautiful young woman who seemed to be caught up in the same situation that I was. There was no one around who gave a damn.

I found her in a bar in the Lai Dai station in Otitoh. She actually started the conversation— considering how I was brought up, I'm not used to a woman taking the initiative in such matters. Anyway, next thing I knew, I was waking up the next morning in her bedroom with a terrible hangover. Before I had time to fully clothe myself, I discovered my mistake: the door to the apartment opened and a short, gnarled old man came in. As soon as I saw him, I knew I was in trouble.

That man was Eteri Tazaki, an officer of the Lai Dai Protection Services. He was furious, but— fortunately for me—unarmed. He chased me out of the apartment, calling for the guards. I managed to escape into a nearby alley, and, with my heart about to explode, I ran as fast as I could to the hangar bay.

I've been running ever since. The fact is, every law enforcement officer in this system seems to be corrupt, and by the virtue of his position alone, Tazaki has managed to convince the authorities that I raped his wife. I'm now a wanted man, hunted by those I once trusted with my life. I'm still trying to come to terms with what has happened, but it's hard. I just hope my family doesn't hear about this until I have time to explain everything in person.

What I need from you, {[character]player.name}, is help to escape this constellation. I can't risk trying to make the jump out of here without adequate preparation; if I'm caught, I could end up in prison for the rest of my life. That's something I want to avoid at all costs, especially in these parts.

Your first task will be a difficult one. The sheriff of Otitoh, Togany, has been snooping around the area looking for me. I think he must have been tipped off by one of the locals, because he's currently scouring the asteroid belts near here, where I usually run at the first sight of law enforcement officers. You must take him out— destroy his ship or whatever; just prevent him from finding me. I fear that if he's not taken care of soon, I will be caught. If he catches me, he'll call in back-up, and there'll be no stopping them. He's currently located near one of the moons of Otitoh VII. Bring me proof of his demise and you will be rewarded.

135866.en:
Amazing stuff, {[character]player.name}. I didn't expect you to bring him here alive, but I'm quite pleased; this won't go over as badly with the authorities as killing him would've. I'll keep him prisoner on my ship until I've managed to get away from Okkelen, then I'll release him. Now we have to move fast: once the authorities figure out their sheriff is missing, they'll send out search teams, and then I'll be in serious trouble.

Get ready for your next assignment.

135867.en:
The Caldari are helping the Amarrians plan an offensive in this sector by deploying subspace beacons deep in obscure star systems. We need to destroy the beacons and strand some of the Caldari in this sector.

The most powerful of these beacons are located in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system; go there and destroy them quickly. There will be ships guarding the beacons, and they'll no doubt put up a very strong resistance.

135868.en:
So glad to hear it. Good, good.

Okay, we believe that the Caldari are helping the Amarrians plan an offensive in this sector; the Caldari are deploying subspace beacons deep in obscure star systems to support it. We're developing a plan to destroy the beacons and strand some of the Caldari flotillas in this sector.

The most powerful of these beacons are located in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, and since you're the best commander we've got involved, we want you to go there and destroy them quickly. There will be ships guarding the beacons, and they'll no doubt put up a strong resistance.

What do you say? Do you want the mission?

135869.en: Your loyalty and bravery continue to astonish us all.

135871.en: I see. Well, I suppose this is a difficult job I've offered you. Still— Oh, well, I'll find someone…

135872.en: I will destroy the beacons, never fear.

135873.en: The beacons are all destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. Along with the Caldari bastards who put them there.

135874.en: This sounds pretty dangerous, going up against the Caldari. No, I think I'll pass.

135875.en: I think so, yes. Sounds like you need the help.

135876.en: You've really let the Republic down, {[character]player.name}. Don't expect to keep up this sort of behavior without some lasting effect.

135877.en: I knew we could count on you, {[character]player.name}. Please hurry.

135878.en: Good job! We've scored a major victory here, thanks to you!

135879.en: Damnation, {[character]player.name}! You were our best hope. I just pray I can find someone else.

135880.en: It sounds like a very difficult job. Of course I'll do it!

135881.en: I like to stay out of political squabbles. Find yourself another capsuleer.

135882.en: This mission isn't worth the risk. I'm sorry, but I have to withdraw.

135883.en: An emergency? Sure, how can I help?

135884.en: The Sansha recently began a campaign of expansion. Our forces have contained them so far, but every day it gets harder. A new Sansha base has recently been discovered on our side of the line. We don't have the men to spare to handle it right now. I need you to take care of it. Destroy the station and any Sansha craft that may be defending it.

135885.en: Sansha's Nation was founded more than a century ago. Sansha was a Caldari tycoon who set out to create a utopian state. He started experiments, combining capsule technology with the human mind, creating zombie-like creatures that had the cold, calculating minds of computers, but the ingenuity of humans. When this became public knowledge, Sansha was condemned and his forces were decimated, but remnants still remain.

135887.en:
Understand that what I'm about to tell you is classified. If word of this got out, there would be a system-wide panic.

The Sansha recently began a campaign of expansion. Our forces have contained them so far, but every day it gets harder. The Sansha do not sleep. They do not flinch. They do not run. They have our guys running triple shifts just to keep up. The cracks in our line are already starting to show.

A new Sansha base has recently been discovered on our side of the line. We don't have the men to spare to handle it right now. I need you to take care of it. Destroy the station and any Sansha craft that may be defending it.

135888.en: I'm not about to force you to go back, but I am disappointed.  We trusted you to do this.  You've made life a lot harder for my boys.

135890.en: Thanks to your efforts, we've been able to focus on pushing the Sansha back. We've driven them back to where they started, but the fighting is still hard. You've done well, {[character]player.name}.

135891.en: Fair enough. I can't order you.

135892.en: Things are going badly. Because you were slow to act, the Sansha station we found launched a raid against one of our facilities. Now I have to pull people off the line to handle the mess.  Next time, make sure you can do what needs to be done.

135893.en: The situation with the Sansha station cannot wait any longer. I need someone who can decide and commit, not lollygag.

135896.en: That station is as good as dust.

135898.en: I'm not ready for an operation on this scale.  Not against the Nation.

135899.en: There were Sansha everywhere.  I'm not going back out there, man.  You can't make me.

135900.en: I am a dedicated problem solver.

135901.en:
Excellent. Now, first off, I must stress that this is all strictly confidential. If any word of this matter were to get out, it could tarnish our appearance in the public eye, not to mention damage Federation morale.

It looks as if one of our public confidence operatives has turned. What's a public confidence operative? A person whose job it is to spread good news and make sure the general public doesn't lose faith in the government. Yes, I guess you could call it "propaganda management"… but hell, what's a government without propaganda?

Anyway, it seems those fascists in the Caldari State have managed to turn the guy, and he's heading for enemy space with a computer full of our public confidence procedures. He's met up with some Caldari warships, and they're escorting him to the frontier. We need to stop them, destroy that ship, and get back the computer with the... public confidence procedures.

Keep it on the sly, {[character]player.name}, and you'll be well rewarded. What do you think?

135902.en: Excellent. Alright, get moving, then — that bastard's getting away!

135903.en: Thanks to you, our people will remain happy now!

135904.en: Your loss, {[character]player.name}. Remember: Keep your mouth shut about this.

135905.en: Always happy to help, but especially when there's ISK involved.

135906.en: Here's that data chip you wanted. And don't worry, there's no one left to talk about this matter.

135907.en: You want me to help you lie to the people of our fair and just Federation?! You're crazy.

135908.en: Thanks for your consideration, {[character]agentID.name}. And yes, I believe I am.

135909.en: Sansha's Nation was founded more than a century ago. Sansha was a Caldari tycoon who set out to create a utopian state. He started experiments, combining capsule technology with the human mind, creating zombie-like creatures that had the cold, calculating minds of computers, but the ingenuity of humans. When this became public knowledge, Sansha was condemned and his forces were decimated, but remnants still remain.

135910.en: The Sansha recently began a campaign of expansion. Our forces have contained them so far, but every day it gets harder. A new Sansha base has recently been discovered on our side of the line. We don't have the men to spare to handle it right now. I need you to take care of it. Destroy the station and any Sansha craft that may be defending it.

135912.en:
Understand that what I'm about to tell you is classified. If word of this got out, there would be a system-wide panic.

The Sansha recently began a campaign of expansion. Our forces have contained them so far, but every day it gets harder. The Sansha do not sleep. They do not flinch. They do not run. They have our guys running triple shifts just to keep up. The cracks in our line are already starting to show.

A new Sansha base has recently been discovered on our side of the line. We don't have the men to spare to handle it right now. I need you to take care of it. Destroy the station and any Sansha craft that may be defending it.

135926.en:
A few hours ago, an Amarrian strike force hit a refugee convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have gone now, but we've picked up a distress transmission that claims there are survivors. It could be a trap, or the Amarrians may be planning to return and capture the survivors for sale as slaves in the Empire.

Warp over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and investigate. If there really are any survivors, get them before the Amarrians do; you'll need to move quickly. And if it proves an ambush, then take out any Amarrian bastards who show themselves.

135927.en:
You may already know that Amarr is preparing for war. It seems that they want to take back what they feel was once rightfully theirs and make us all slaves in the process. It will be the Day of Darkness all over again, if they have their way.

But they will not. We Minmatar will not kneel to that sociopathic, god-mongering cult run by feeble cybernetic monstrosities. The Amarrians will either perish or slay us to the last — either way, they will never again make us their slaves.

We've not come to open warfare yet, but the Imperials have been raiding along the frontier, trying to provoke us into a fight. A few hours ago they hit a refugee convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have gone, but we've picked up a distress transmission that claims there are survivors. It could be a trap, or the Amarrians may be planning to return and capture the survivors for sale as slaves in the Empire.

So, we need a good, capable captain who's willing to warp over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and investigate. If there really are any survivors, get them before the Amarrians do; survivors may not last long out there, so you'll need to move quickly.

If it proves an ambush, then take out any Amarrian bastards who show themselves. Will you do it?

135928.en: On your way, captain. Death to Amarr!

135929.en: Thank god! We'll see to the refugees' comfort. Take your reward and my personal gratitude.

135930.en: I'm… shocked. My reports have you a fearless, dedicated veteran. I am supremely disappointed, both in you and in my intelligence.

135931.en: I will help you to the best of my ability. The Republic!

135932.en: The refugees are safe and the Amarrian ships are destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}.

135933.en: I know it's important, but the danger sounds too great. I can't risk my ship over a few civilians.

135934.en: I'll serve the Republic any way I can, {[character]agentID.name}. What is needed of me?

135935.en:
We've been having problems with a Sansha outpost for a while now. I've finally received clearance to sponsor a raid on the facility. I guess someone got tired of paying for new haulers.

So how about it? Get some of your capsuleer buddies together and destroy every Sansha you find. You'll be a hero; and since the Sansha are all unholy mockeries of all that is human, you don't even have to feel bad about killing them!

135936.en: Sansha's Nation is just this side of rogue drones-- in some ways the Nation is worse. At least drones are machines acting like they're alive. Sansha were people; now they act like machines. Best thing about both is that you can blow the hell out of them and still maintain a clear moral high ground.

135939.en: Do you have any idea how much these Sansha are costing us on a weekly basis? Never mind. I guess I'll have to contract one of the mercenary companies to take care of it.

135940.en: Glad to hear it.  Happy hunting.

135941.en: I wish I was there to see it.  There's nothing quite as satisfying as watching the explosive decompression of an enemy ship.  Hope you had fun.  Oh, and thanks for saving all the civvies in system from the Sansha threat, or whatever.

135942.en: Not diving in?  What, are you afraid of a few explosions?

135943.en: I can't wait for you to finish off those Sansha.  Too much pressure from above, you understand.  I have to pass the contract along to a professional mercenary corp.  You just weren't fast enough.

135944.en: You can't make up your mind in a timely fashion; I can't just sit on this offer.  The job's moved on to a merc corp.  Now you'll have to watch someone else have all the fun.

135947.en: Sansha, huh?  Yeah, I think I know some people who might want to space a few.

135948.en: It's done.  We wiped every one of the Sansha out.

135949.en: Moral high ground or not, I'm not diving into a nest of Sansha.

135950.en: I was all for clearing out the Sansha, but there were just too many of them.  I have to quit.

135969.en: Take this soil to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so our science weenies can figure out how to grow stuff for us to eat. No lollygagging.

135970.en:
Some egg-heads we hired've been analyzing a nearby planet for "sustainable food resource population." Heh, yeah. Anyway, looks like our plans to terraform it are moving forward.

Now, a big part of this project is good, fertile soil. Yeah, soil. Think about it.

But before the project can move full ahead, we need someone to transport sort of a small amount of the stuff to test out the growing conditions. And that means someone with a big enough cargo hold and a desire to make a bit of ISK for the effort.

So, what do you think? Are you interested?

135971.en:
Hey, don't give me that look. It might be mud, but it's important mud!

Oh, just get going.

135972.en: Alright, alright, wiseguy. Here's your ISK. Pleasure doin' business, and all that.

135973.en: Uhh, well… yeah, sure, I guess. I mean, ISK is ISK, right?

135974.en: Okay, your name is mud. Or, rather, your mud is delivered. So pay up.

135975.en: Dirt transporting, huh? You do realize that I'm a capsuleer, right? Not some common industrial pilot?! Thanks, but no thanks.

135976.en: Uh, it's "pod pilot." So what's going on?

135977.en: Take this soil to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so our science weenies can figure out how to grow stuff for us to eat. No lollygagging.

Now, a big part of this project is good, fertile soil. But before the project can move full ahead, we need someone to take a small amount to their lab to test out the growing conditions. And naturally, I can't think of anyone I'd rather pay for such an easy job but you.

So, what do you think? Are you interested?

135985.en: A few unfortunate members of our corporation were kidnapped yesterday. I have reliable information that their kidnappers are close by. If you find the kidnappers, then deal with them appropriately and return their captives to me, dead or alive.

135986.en:
Alright, here's a job you might be ready to tackle. A few unfortunate members of our corporation were kidnapped yesterday while on duty near the edge of this very system. I have reliable information that their kidnappers are nearby. I'll upload the coordinates into your NeoCom: You should use them to find a series of gateways which should lead you to these enemies of the state.

Sound like something you'd be interested in? If you succeed I will reward you handsomely.

135987.en: Good, good. I'll trust that you know what you're doing, then. See you soon.

135988.en: Excellent.  The victims' families will be pleased that their loved ones are still alive.

135989.en: Fair enough, if inconvenient. Always refreshing to meet someone who knows his or her place in the scheme of things.

135990.en: Absolutely, I'm interested. This one's right up my alley.

135991.en: The kidnappers are dealt with, and I've returned with the victims.

135992.en: Uh, I'm not really much of a combat pilot, actually. Maybe someone else would be a better choice.

135993.en: A few of our senior officials were kidnapped yesterday. I have reliable information that their kidnappers are close by: I've uploaded the coordinates into your NeoCom. If you find the kidnappers, then deal with them appropriately and return our people to me, dead or alive.

135994.en:
Correct. A few of our senior officials were kidnapped yesterday while inspecting one of our sites in this very system. I have reliable information that their kidnappers are nearby.

Can you help?

135995.en: Good — I'm certain you know what you're doing. See you soon.

135996.en: Excellent. We are forever grateful, and their poor families will be pleased to hear the news.

135997.en: Fair enough, if inconvenient — it's always refreshing to hear someone who acknowledges his or her place in the great scheme of things.

135999.en: The kidnappers are dealt with, and I've returned with the officials.

136000.en: Uh, I'm not really much of a combat pilot, actually. Maybe someone else would be a better choice.

136002.en: Transport a unit of hired marines over to the {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} station so it can be brought under ... er, new management. Do not get involved personally. Just get the soldiers into the docking area and then look the other way.

136003.en: I figured I could count on you. My thanks.

136004.en: Indeed, they are. I'm expecting further communications any minute. Again, my thanks.

136005.en: Well, suit yourself. No risk, I assure you. But have it your way. Your loss.

136006.en: Sounds… interesting. Well, no, actually it sounds a bit tedious. But ISK is ISK. I'm in.

136007.en: I delivered your marines. Things ought to be well under way by now.

136008.en: Uh, sounds a bit risky. I mean, what if the station guards attack my ship? No, no thanks.

136018.en:
Well, lemme tell you: A warlord who's been visiting my people in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} station for a while now has a thing for long-limb roes, and I need to get some over there for him. This man is very important and very dangerous, {[character]player.name}, and I want him on my good side, so let's make every effort to get his needs fulfilled.

Can you help me out?

136019.en: Do I look like a putz? Of course I'll pay you. Just get the stuff over there as fast as you can.

136020.en: Fantastic. Your ISK has been deposited to your account. And don't worry, my friend, I won't forget you when I rise to higher places.

136021.en: I can help you out, sure. I can't do it for free, though.

136022.en: Alright, delivery completed. You mentioned payment?

136023.en: I do, yeah, and I am… depending on what you need.

136046.en: Yes, yes, already taken care of. Now, if you'll excuse me?

136047.en: I'm interested, I'm interested. No need to be hasty. Just give me the coordinates and the batteries, and I'm off.

136048.en: Done. Batteries delivered, crisis averted. So, about my pay...?

136049.en: I might be, yeah. What's the deal?

136050.en: The {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} station manager has reported a lack of hydrogen batteries in their supply depot, a situation that could result in a temporary shutdown of the entire station. Deliver the batteries to them as quickly as possible.

136051.en:
Just this: The station manager of {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} has just reported to us a serious lack of hydrogen batteries in their supply depot, a situation that could result in a temporary shutdown of the entire station. We need to help them out, and I naturally thought of you to deliver the necessary goods to them — always give your friends a leg up, eh?

It's an easy job, and pays well. Just be sure you have enough space in your cargohold: This is a pretty big shipment.

136052.en: I'm uploading the coordinates as we speak, and the batteries will be in your station hangar by the time you're ready to leave. My thanks.

136053.en: My pleasure, {[character]player.name}, my pleasure. And my thanks.

136054.en: I'm interested, definitely. Just give me the coordinates and the batteries, and I'm off.

136055.en: Batteries delivered, crisis averted. Thanks for the job. Easy money.

136057.en: Bring me the neophite and we'll talk.

136058.en:
I'm in kind of a tight spot at the moment, but I can't reveal anything to you until I'm certain of your intentions. To prove yourself to me, bring me a piece of the extremely valuable mineral, neophite. You'll get it back when I'm done with you, but I really need to have something that will keep you from double-crossing me before I can give you any of the details of my situation.

I hear Akira Helkelen has a little neophite in stock; you might want to pay him a visit at the Rush Town Ruins if you don't have any neophite yourself.

136060.en: It's really nothing personal, but I just don't know you well enough to trust you without some kind of collateral. So now that I have this to hang onto, I may be able to give you some real information.

136061.en: Ah, this will do nicely.  You did well, {[character]player.name}. Now there's just one more obstacle to overcome before I can get out of here.

136062.en:
Now that you've neutralized the sheriff, it's time to prepare my getaway ship. I will need a cloaking device to keep myself from being detected, just in case CONCORD or Customs have been notified about me. Being cloaked doesn't make my plan foolproof, but it will increase my chance of escape significantly.

You should be able to find a Prototype Cloaking Device on the market; I'd buy it myself if I wasn't trying to lie low. If you don't think you'll be able to get ahold of one, don't screw me around.. just don't bother taking this job.

136064.en:
I'm almost ready to set off for the outer regions, where I can hide until my lawyer clears my name, but there's one final obstacle. I was scanning the stargate to Ihakana from a great distance to avoid detection, when I noticed a few Caldari bandits led by Bai Tarziiki camping nearby. I remember seeing Bai's face in a news bulletin a while back; he's reputed to be a member of the Kazka Bandits, a notorious gang of outlaw mercenaries in these parts. They are also rumored to have close ties with the corrupt security forces in Otitoh, which Eteri is a part of.

I'm not sure what Bai is up to, but I have a sinking feeling that he was sent by Eteri to block my exit. He probably knows that Ihakana is the first place I would go to. Outlaws like Bai are experts at sniffing out people in hiding, so there's no doubt that he has an anti-cloaking device and multiple scanners on his ship. I can't afford to take this kind of chance: if they catch me I'll be tortured and killed.

Your last task is simple. Take out Bai, and bring me proof that he won't bother me anymore. His corpse will do.

136066.en: Finally, I'm ready to go.  It's been a pleasure working with you, {[character]player.name}. I hope you enjoy your reward.

136079.en:
Hmm... Yes, I do have some work for you.

Although Sansha's Nation usually has a firm grip over the criminal strata in our system, the Angel Cartel has been poking its ugly nose in here of late-- which is perfectly fine with us. In fact, watching the two outlawed organizations duke it out is one of my favorite pastimes. If we're lucky, it will give both sides a good bruising, which will only work in our favor.

Of course, there's also bad news. An InterBus ship traveling to {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} got caught in the middle of one of the pirate warzones. The ship was damaged beyond repair and can neither warp out nor navigate away from the crossfire. Your task is to rescue the ship's crew. Please retrieve them before any more harm is done; they're already scared out of their minds. The faster you get this done, the better.

Good luck.

136097.en:
Hmm... Yes, I do have some work for you. Although the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} have traditionally had a firm grip over this system, Sansha's Nation has been poking its ugly nose in here of late. We were about to assemble a strike force to take care of their latest infiltration when we noticed something interesting. The Sansha fleet that we had stumbled upon is fighting for their lives against a sizable Gallente armada!

We aren't sure where the Gallente came from or what they're doing here, but I suspect it's one of those blasted entrepreneurs, scouring space outside of Federation borders for possible business opportunities. Either way, we're always happy when our enemies fight each other. When they're done, it's that much easier for us to clean up the pieces.

Now, what I need you to do is fairly simple: retrieve some of our valuable drug stash that's lying in the middle of their little warzone. You'll have to navigate through the contested deadspace area to get to it, but I'm sure someone of your caliber can handle that. Just stay clear of their main fleet and you'll make it.

Good luck.

Hmm... Yes, I do have some work for you.

Although the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} have traditionally had a firm grip over the {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} system, the Angel Cartel has been poking its ugly nose in here of late. We were about to assemble a strike force to take care of their latest infiltration when we noticed something interesting. The Cartel fleet that we had stumbled upon is fighting for its live against an armada of combined Imperial and Ammatar forces!

We aren't sure where the Amarr came from or what they're doing here, but I suspect it's some of those blasted slavers, scouring space outside of their borders for more slave labor. Either way, we're always happy when our enemies fight each other. When they're done, it's that much easier for us to clean up the pieces.

What I need you for is a covert ops mission: destroy one of our armories in a deadspace area near here. It's caught right in the middle of the largest battle between the Amarr slavers and the Cartel. We can't allow our military secrets to fall into the wrong hands. The armory's crew is expendable; just get the job done and get back here in one piece.

136100.en:

136102.en: I thought you had a bit more fortitude. It's people like you that allow the Federation to get away with committing this kind of treachery.

136103.en: Here's the coordinates for where the deal is going down. Good hunting, kirjuun.

136104.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}. You've done a great job for the State and this corporation.

136105.en: Most disappointing, pilot. How can you sit idly by while the Federation poisons our bodies and our minds? Hopefully someone else will have the courage to stand up to them.

136106.en: You failed to stop the drug deal, and likely Federation penetration of our borders as well. There is little doubt that this will put us at an even greater disadvantage against our enemies than we were already dealing with. While I hope for your sake that I am wrong, I fear that you have cost us more than you can possibly imagine.

136107.en: Due to your lack of action, {[character]player.name}, I was forced to find another pilot to carry out this mission. Hopefully, in the future, you will be more punctual, pilot.

136110.en: I'll take care of the problem, {[character]agentID.name}. This intrusion must be stopped.

136111.en: The drug runners' ships have been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}, and I managed to bring back a few of them alive for interrogation.

136112.en: I don't think I feel like dealing with this mess right now.

136113.en: How can I be of service to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} and the State, kirjuun?

136114.en:
It looks as if one of our public confidence operatives has turned. What's a public confidence operative? A person whose job it is to spread good news and make sure the general public doesn't lose faith in the government. Yes, I guess you could call it "propaganda management"… but hell, what's a government without propaganda?

Anyway, it seems those fascists in the Caldari State have managed to turn the guy, and he's heading for enemy space with a computer full of our public confidence procedures. He's met up with some Caldari warships, and they're escorting him to the frontier.

Stop them, destroy their ships, and bring back the data chip containing the public confidence procedures.

136115.en:
Good work. I'm glad I found you.

Take this data chip. On it, you will find evidence that the Wiyrkomi corporation have been engaging in terrorism against themselves in order to shift the public's opinion regarding both them and FON. It's not absolutely 100 percent reliable, but what there is seems solid enough. Bring this chip to Preaux Gallot in the Natura Seminary in Audaerne. There is more to be done yet, and I have a feeling this is all just beginning.

Thank you for all your help. You've done us a great service.

136116.en:
A traditional Caldari privateer's song

Oh, poor old man, your bunny will die.
And we say so, and we know so.
Oh, poor old man, your bunny gonna die
Oh, poor old man!

We'll drag it down to the State line,
We'll drop it down inside the border,
We'll drop it off into the void, hey.

We'll drop it off into the void, now,
Sing it down with a long, long roll.
The peggies can have its body,
And the devil can have its soul.

136117.en:
This is a pre-recorded message: Why are you lookin' here? You forget somethin'? Are you stupid, 's that it? We're barely done talkin' and it all already slipped outta your head? GO KILL THE DAMN TRAITOR.

Damn rookies.

136119.en:
You heard me, {[character]player.name}. Animal problems. And stop lookin' at me like I'm crazy or I'll be tempted to do somthin' we'll both regret. Just shut up and listen.

This is what happens: You scour the land, lookin' hard and far and wide and all that. After much of that business, you find yourself a good bunny. Real proper, no poser crap – the real deal. Least that's what you think. You give this bunny everything of yourself. All your knowledge, all your expertise, all your damn money. Hell… all your love, even. I said stop lookin' at me like that!

What was I–? Oh… right.

So, for a while that works well – with a real big emphasis on the "for a while" bit. This little bunny looks after itself proper, looks after you real good in turn too. As it damn well should, little bugger. Then one day, outta the blue, it seems to think it's had enough. Thinks it will just hop on over to the Mordus Legion and work for them instead. After everything you've done for it. "Better money," it says. "Doing what's right," it says. Dumb bunny. Real damn stupid.

You know what you do next, right? Go on, tell me what you do and prove you're not as green as you look.

136120.en: Eh… useless after all. I knew it. I could smell the fear on you, ya damn rookie! Howsabout you forget about that next time, eh? You got a damn pod, what more could ya want?

136121.en: Huh. That's right. Guess you might be useful after all. Alright, then, my young protégé: Stage two – here's the coordinates. I'm not giving you a damn thing. Go show me you're more than just talk!

136122.en: Good work, Rookie! Now go and have yourself a party on me. Oh, and remember: this is what happens to bad bunnies. Don't get any funny ideas under those long, furry ears of yours.

136123.en: Wrong answer, Rookie. Howsabout you take that tub of yours and paddle back to State space before you figure out you can't swim with the big fish.

136124.en: You take it out back, have one last look at it, then put a bullet in its furry little head.

136125.en: Hop, hop, bang. "Crap, I'm dead." I think it's payday.

136126.en: Uhm… what I do is… or what someone needs to do, at least, is stop gobbling the ol' Blue Pill. I think you need to get some rest… and maybe some rehab. Sheesh.

136127.en: I forgot what I was supposed to do, so I figure I'll just do nothing instead. Seeya.

136128.en: Uh… wha-?! Like, vermin in your apartment or something? You know I'm a capsuleer, right?

136129.en: I'm not sure you're thinking this through: the Brothers of Freedom are more of a threat than you realize. Perhaps you'll learn before it's too late.

136131.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}. Perhaps Torvil will restrict himself to overpaid speaking engagements for bleeding-heart, over-privileged Gallente from now on, instead of trying to spit in our faces.

136132.en: Don't tell me you actually sympathize with these morons? For your sake, I hope you don't.

136133.en: I never heard back from you, {[character]player.name}, so I'm going to assume you don't have the stomach to take care of this Brothers of Freedom tyuui. That's unfortunate, but thankfully there are plenty of other loyal Caldari pilots out there looking for work.

136137.en: The transmitter has been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm just disappointed I didn't catch Torvil there himself.

136138.en: I don't think I want to mess with it if it's inside the Republic. I hear they eat their prisoners.

136139.en: I've decided it's not worth risking my hide just to shut up someone who's making fun of you. Do your own dirty work.

136140.en: Oh? What sort of mission is that?

136141.en:
Sometimes calling itself "The Scions of Athra," the Athran Brotherhood is a group of Khanid secessionists with headquarters located on the Khanid homeworld of Amarr Prime (called Athra in the Old Khanid tongue). This group tends to rise perhaps every other generation or so, seemingly from its own ashes, making trouble for local government and interstellar trade alike.

Given the many large pirate organizations and other independent "freebooters" of New Eden, not to mention the constant weight of intergalactic politics and the ongoing "Minmatar Problem," Amarr rulers cannot generally spare a large-scale military effort to deal with these relatively minor troublemakers. Perhaps this is the reason the Brotherhood seems never to die, but always reappears just when authorities start to think they've rid themselves of the nuisance.

136142.en:
You've heard of the "Athran Brotherhood"? No? Well, that's no surprise, really. They're little more than a nuisance, and few in number. But they can be a pain at times. That's what I want you to find out for me, actually.

There's a small station built into an old asteroid near here: It used to be a mining outpost till they hollowed the thing out. It's been abandoned for a few years now, but some rumors of activity in that area have been surfacing. And I suspect it may have become the hideout for a chapter of the Athran Brotherhood. I need you to go check those rumors out and let me know what you find.

All you need to do is fly close to the structure and see if you pick up any short-range radio transmissions or see any other signs of activity. Then get back here and let me know what you found.

136144.en:
You don't say! Well, yes, in fact, I do have something I could use you for.

You've heard of the "Athran Brotherhood"? No? Well, that's no surprise, really. They're little more than a nuisance, and few in number. But they can be a pain at times. And we're pretty sure there's a chapter of them hereabouts. But we don't know where they're hiding out. That's what I want you to find out for me, actually.

There's a small station built into an old asteroid near here. Used to be a mining outpost till they hollowed the thing out. It's been abandoned for a few years now, but some rumors of activity in that area have been surfacing. I need you to go check those rumors out and let me know what you find.

Seem like something you'd be interested in?

136145.en: It's possible, but not generally, no. If they do engage, don't feel obliged to mess with them, unless you feel you're in no danger.

136146.en: Yeah, I got your ship's logs once you docked. Stick around and talk to me again in a bit, would you? We need to get to the bottom of this.

136147.en: Seems straightforward enough. Are these Athrans hostile?

136148.en: Alright, I went out there, and I definitely picked up some Athran radio transmissions. I also picked up some carbon scoring when they opened fire on me...

136149.en: Sounds pretty dull, actually. I think I'll pass.

136150.en: I've given it some more thought, and actually I'm not sure I'm up to tracking down these Athrans for you. Sorry.

136151.en: Well, thanks. I'm just wondering if you might have some work for a recent graduate. I'm a decent combat pilot.

136153.en: The Athrans seem pretty dangerous. I think I'm throwing in the towel. Sorry.

136154.en: What if it's a trap? I mean, they seemed to know I was coming last time, right? Sorry, but I just can't risk my ship....

136155.en: You bet. I'll be back before you can say, "Hey, where'd you go?"

136156.en: Suit yourself. I was giving you a chance to be of service to your nation, but if you want to hide behind your degree, well… I can't stop you.

136157.en: That's what I like to hear. Be careful out there, eh? These Athrans seem more... volatile than most.

136158.en: I had doubts about you all along, to be honest. Just goes to show I'm still a good judge of character.

136159.en:
Yes. We put a covert ops ship out there around the same time you left for your last mission, and the pilot corroborated your story. He also reports that the remaining Athrans pulled out as soon as you left. Fortunately, he was able to trail them to another location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

{[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and find out what's going on. See what these Athrans are up to, and report any suspicious activity back to me. And if they open fire on you again, you're fully authorized to shoot back. Don't take any chances.

136161.en:
Always be ready to warp out if you start taking heavy damage, whether in a mission or in lawless space. Sometimes it's a good idea to have a jump route selected before going into a mission so you can simply click your autopilot to get out quickly; this is a valid approach only with relatively small ships, though. Eventually, once you get into something like a Battleship, aligning to warp can take so long — especially if you begin once you're already taking heavy damage — that your ship might be destroyed by the time you actually start your warp.

Remember too that if you take damage in battle, you can always return to a nearby station for repairs; also be sure to replenish your ammunition while you're there if you're running low. Combat in EVE can be deadly and costly, so do what you can to cut your losses.

"It's better to warp away and fight again another day."

136162.en: I certainly am. Have you been able to discover what the Athrans were after?

136163.en: Uh, I've decided this mission isn't for me. Sorry, but you'll have to find someone else.

136164.en: Hm, I don't know. Their munitions depot is bound to be heavily guarded. Maybe you should get someone more experienced to handle this one. Too risky.

136165.en: Woo! That was one big explosion. That's my kind of mission.

136166.en: Finally, we're taking the fight to them. I'll be there in moments.

136167.en: You can't always take the safe way out, you know. Sometimes a warrior has to bleed a little to serve his nation... or hers. Point is, danger is part of the job.

136168.en: Glad you enjoyed it. Listen, this all may not be over yet, so don't wander too far off, okay?

136169.en: Good show. But be careful out there: They may know you're coming.

136170.en: The Athran Brotherhood has an ammunitions depot located in this very system. If we can take it out, we'll seriously disrupt their plans, whatever they might be. In fact, they have a Bestower full of explosives docking there shortly: Get over there and take out that ship, then deal with the depot itself.
