They're sure to have some guards, but you've proven yourself capable of dealing with them.

136171.en: I found those Athrans, alright. And they're in league with the Minmatar, it would seem. They made pretty short work of a chapel structure out there.

136172.en: I wonder what was so important about that chapel… Hm. Give me a while to look into this, then come back and see me, will you? Thanks.

136173.en: Attacking Couriers or Haulers in Hi-sec

136174.en: I see that my competitors have just put up a new selection of construction tools on the market. I assume then that you did not intercept the shipment, else I would have a shiny new set of tools.

136175.en: I see that my competitors have just put up a new selection of construction tools on the market. You missed the window of opportunity. I need timely and punctual help, not indecisive help.

136178.en: A chance to take out one of those spineless couriers without risking CONCORD? Consider it done!

136179.en: I'm not going to take out a lowly courier, risk or no risk.

136180.en: I'm not going to take out a lowly courier, risk or no risk.

136181.en: Nothing like a little healthy competition, right?

136182.en: That's what I like to hear!

136183.en: It's done. Here are the construction tools.

136184.en: Hah! Let's see how they do without their exclusive stock! Don't go anywhere. There's more to be done.

136185.en: Come on, this is a professional hauler. He almost doesn't even count as a person.

136186.en:
There's a small family-run corporation operating in the neighboring system. They keep getting exclusive contracts because they keep their shipments secret and secure. But I've figured out where they go.

Intercept the ship, blow it up, and bring the supplies--construction tools, I think-- back to me.

136187.en:
There's a small family-run corporation operating in the neighboring system. A real pain, you know? They've got a corner on just about every small commodity in the region. I can't even get any of their suppliers to sell to me, and it's pissing me off.

I've got a plan, though. They keep getting exclusive contracts because they keep their shipments secret and secure. But I've figured out where they go. I know when and where one of their supply shipments are going to be. And even better, it's in a dead space pocket that CONCORD doesn't monitor.

Intercept the ship, blow it up, and bring the supplies--construction tools, I think-- back to me.

136188.en: You know, our security personnel just barely stopped an attempt on my life. We are still in danger, and you just walk away? This isn't over yet. I'll never understand you capsuleers, I swear.

136189.en: Of course, yes. One does not ask a favor of a capsuleer otherwise, you know...

136190.en:
You're not alone in being attacked. Our security personnel barely stopped an attempt on my life just a few minutes after you left for that last mission. My life flashed before my eyes, I swear!

Listen, we need to end this. Let me look into this a bit further; come back and talk to me soon, though, okay? I'm not going to be able to sleep until we finish this thing.

136191.en: I guess my ISK and my friendship aren't incentive enough, huh? I see where we stand. Hmph. Thanks. For nothing.

136192.en: Sure, I can take it over there for you. I mean, you're paying me, right?

136193.en: Not really interested in playing delivery-stooge, no. Thanks anyway.

136194.en: I've had enough of this. Sorry, but I can't finish this mission. Keep your reward.

136195.en: Of course, {[character]agentID.name}. What do you need?

136196.en: Not going to-but it's just a courier! They were made to be popped!

136197.en: Truth be told, nowhere in the universe is safe for the humble courier. Even though CONCORD patrols the so-called "hi-sec" areas of space (security rating 0.5-1.0), that doesn't ensure your protection one hundred percent. It is possible for a capsuleer of sufficient skill or equipment to take out another capsuleer before CONCORD fully retaliates. Usually the certainty of losing a ship to CONCORD is enough to dissuade hi-sec attacks, but if the payout or cargo is worth enough, an attacker might think it worth the trouble.

136198.en: Head out to the deadspace location they Athrans are using as a hideout. Deal with those creeps and take out their leader, Cosensin Thrand.

136199.en:
We know who their leader is, {[character]player.name}: some woman called Cosensin Thrand. And it seems she's hiding out in this very star system. Now we can take these nut-jobs out once and for all.

I'll upload the coordinates of the deadspace location they're using as a hideout. Get on out there and deal with these creeps, and you'll be well rewarded. Good luck!

136200.en:
I see. Well, I must assume you have good reason.

Until next time.

136201.en: I thought you might, {[character]player.name}. I thought you might.

136202.en: Excellent news! I knew you would conclude this matter admirably. I shall speak on your behalf to my associates. God speed. And thank you.

136203.en: There is no room for cowardice in a capsuleer. I mean, you're virtually immortal! It's shameful.

136204.en: My pleasure. I'm going to enjoy this mission.

136205.en: Cosensin Thrand and her henchmen are no longer… well, they're just no longer. If you take my meaning.

136206.en:
Hm. These guys are pretty dangerous. And you want me to take out their leader? I don't know…

Nah, sounds too risky.

136207.en: This might be a problem for you, but I can't finish this mission. Sorry. I just can't.

136208.en: How so? What did you find?

136209.en:
Well, it seems they're simply trying to disrupt the local infrastructure. What they seek to gain by doing so, I don't know... but that's the terrorist mentality for you.

But what's more interesting is that I've discovered they have an ammunitions depot not far from here. If we can take it out, we'll seriously disrupt their plans, whatever they might be. In fact, they have a Bestower full of explosives docking shortly: Get over there and take out that ship, then deal with the depot itself. They're sure to have some guards, but you've proven yourself capable of dealing with them. God speed.

136210.en: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions — which more than negates any profit to be made from reprocessing the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

136211.en: Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and mine 333 units of Augumene ore.

136213.en:
Well, I need someone who can handle a ship, but who also knows how to rip ore. If you can do that, then we might be able to come to an agreement.

You've heard of Augumene ore before? It's not too common because it's too costly to refine safely. Thing is, though, a team of scientists working for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} think they've figured out a way to do it cheaply. We need someone to procure some of the ore, though, so they can run some tests.

Interested?

136214.en: Excellent. We'll make it worth your while.

136215.en: Well, that's up to our scientists, not me. But you did good work. In fact, I may have another job for you shortly, so come back in a bit, will you?

136216.en: But you won't be building any cred with {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} while you mine that way. Ah, well — your choice, not mine.

136217.en: Yeah, I'm a decent 'roid miner. I'll have this Augumene back to you in a jiffy.

136218.en: I've got your Augumene here. Good luck making any use of it.

136219.en: Not really interested in mining for someone else's profit, no. I can hit the belts on my own if I want to mine, and that way I cut out the middle man.

136220.en: I've changed my mind. Sorry. I can't be bothered mining for someone else, though. Just doesn't make sense.

136221.en: Capsuleer, in fact. You need a starship pilot? I might be available….

136222.en:
The Athrans seem to have vanished, so either we dealt with the last of them, or the remaining few have gone deep into hiding. Either way, it looks like we've seen the end of their plotting.

All that remains is for you to give a report to the Assistant Chief Security Officer for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. He's currently at a meeting at our office in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. So how about it? Do you mind flying over there and letting him know what's been happening? You'll be generously reimbursed for your time, of course.

136223.en: Prepare an oral report regarding your actions in the Athran Uprising for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s Assistant Chief Security Officer. He's currently at a meeting at our office in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

136224.en: Well, looks like the Minmatar were trying pretty hard to cover their tracks. Sorry I couldn't deliver the report — and, er... it looks like {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has some cleanup to do over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Not much left of your offices there.

136225.en: While academies and universities can provide a good foundation, successful capsuleers know that education continues forever. Skill books are the quickest and most reliable way for a capsuleer to learn to use new equipment or systems.

136226.en:
I have this crazy idea about owning my own outpost. I just need to put my plans into action.

First thing I need is an instructional book on running a corporation. I've found the perfect book for me. I'll pay you to go and pick it up for me.

136228.en:
I have this crazy idea about owning my own outpost. I've heard it's just like printing ISK. I'm in strong enough favor with the local powers, and I've secured a number of interested investors. Now I just need to put my plans into action.

First thing I need is an instructional book on running a corporation. The books you capsuleers use are a bit over my head. Luckily, I've found the perfect book for me. I'll pay you to go and pick it up for me.

136229.en: Bootleg? Are you kidding? The skill book makers track that stuff more than CONCORD. Their lawyers are more vicious, too.

136230.en: Show no fear! Show no mercy! Get the book!

136231.en: Thanks! I'll start reading this immediately. While I'm studying this, I have something else you can do for me.

136232.en: You're going to have a tough time of this universe if you can't be bothered to get a book.

136233.en: I could have spacewalked to the damn station, picked up my book, read it, and spacewalked back by now. Get with the program, huh?

136234.en: Why are you so indecisive about books? Do they frighten you? Are you afraid you might catch "the literacy"?

136237.en: I ain't afraid of no book. I'll get it.

136240.en: I'm not going to finish this book delivery. Just bootleg it or something.

136241.en: Oh yeah? What do you want?

136242.en:
Oh, it's nothing complicated or difficult, frankly. But it's not something I'd trust to a common courier service or even an encrypted FTL transmission.

Can you go pick up the formula our scientists have been working on and bring it back to me here? They've stored a copy in some encrypted data crystals. I need to have my personal team review the process before I can let the experiment go ahead.

136243.en: Of course, of course. Payment on delivery, as usual.

136244.en: Good job. And thanks again. Talk to me whenever you have time and we'll see if I can't dig up some more work for you.

136245.en: Well, if that's how you see it, then fine. But you do realize I would have paid you…?

136246.en: Sure. As long as I'm paid according to my station, then I'm all for it.

136247.en: Formula delivered, safe and sound. Glad to do business with you.

136248.en: You know, I didn't graduate from the best university in the universe just so I could pick up packages for people. So, no. Thanks, but no.

136249.en: I changed my mind. Sorry. I've got better things to do than fetch your formula for you.

136251.en:
Pick up the encrypted data crystals -- I've uploaded the destination into your NeoCom -- and bring it back to your agent.

Once you collect it, remember to put the data crystals in your cargohold before you leave the station.

136252.en:
I've recently hired a number of highly trained... I can't say that with a straight face.

Bums. I hired bums.

Go pick up my bums.

136253.en: You capsuleers are lucky. A couple of you get together, any of you can start a corporation. There are a bunch of you out in 0.0 controlling territory that rivals the empires. But even you guys have to work together to do it.

136255.en:
I hate people, personally. But it's damn hard to get anything done in this universe by yourself. With that in mind, I've recently hired a number of highly trained...I can't say that with a straight face.

Bums. I hired bums.

Go pick up my bums.

136256.en: I pick hating the homeless. It upsets me less.

136257.en: I pick hating the homeless. It upsets me less.

136258.en: Desperate is the best kind of work force.

136259.en: Good job. I'll have them broken and dehumanized within a week. You're turning into quite the helper.

136260.en: Never mind about the bums. I just filled all my positions with some of the local children. If you got the bums already, you can just go ahead and space them or something.

136261.en: I just received word that the homeless have been moved to another station. Apparently some bureaucratic know-nothing decided to have another capsuleer ship them off to improve appearances.

136266.en: I don't want to support your exploitation of the homeless, I hate the homeless and wish them to remain in abject poverty, or I am simply lazy. Take your pick.

136267.en: I don't want to support your exploitation of the homeless, I hate the homeless and wish them to remain in abject poverty, or I am simply lazy. Take your pick.

136269.en: The Augumene ore reprocessed using the new formula, for some reason, produces a deadly allergic reaction in most people of the Matari racial type. There are only a handful of survivors at that reprocessing station. Evacuate the surviving scientists from the quarantine station next to their outpost/lab.

136270.en:
Listen, things were going fine. Just fine. My team had approved the procedure and tested the results. But here's the thing. None of the science team was of Matari heritage. They were all Caldari or mixed-blood. So what we didn't realize until way too late is that the Augumene ore reprocessed using this new formula, for god knows what reason, produces a severe and deadly allergic reaction in most people of the Matari racial type.

{[character]player.name}, almost the entire population of that reprocessing lab was Matari. There are only a handful of survivors. It's a disaster, a huge disaster. First thing, we need to evacuate the surviving scientists from the quarantine station next to their lab. That's your first job. Come back when that's done, and we'll have more to do, I imagine.

136271.en: Oh, thank you. This is horrible. Horrible.

136272.en: So many things to do. Listen, thanks for getting them. Just give me a minute to figure out the next step and then come back, will you?

136273.en: It's not a disease, it's an allergic reaction. And these are the survivors, and they're in quarantine. But, hey, suit yourself. I've got enough problems already; I don't need you adding to them.

136274.en: Alright, calm down. It's a tragedy, but we'll manage. I'll go get the survivors, okay?

136275.en: Alright, I've picked up the survivors and brought them back. What's next?

136276.en: Uh, I'm not sure I want any people who might be infected with some weird disease on my ship. Er, no thanks.

136277.en: We do? We? Really? What in the world is it?

136278.en: What do you mean? What's happened now?

136279.en: I've decided to back out of this mission, actually. I'm just not up to it. Sorry.

136280.en: Um, I'm really not a combat pilot, if you take my meaning. Maybe this is more of a job for the navy? Sorry.

136281.en:
The lab is no more, and neither are the Amarr agents they sent in. Any more, that is. Uh, neither are they any more. "Anymore"? Ehh… either way, that doesn't make much sense, does it? I mean, they're all dead. And so is the lab. Or, well, it's not so much dead as…

Mission complete. All done. Thanks — sorry! Thanks.

136282.en: You got it. I've been looking forward to testing my new ship's fittings against Amarr scum. Perfect timing.

136283.en: Alright, fair enough. But good god, I hope they can get there in time. Imagine the death toll…

136284.en: Good, good. Be careful out there. Who knows what kind of force they'll have waiting.

136285.en:
The damned Amarr, that's what! What else?! God, I need a break.

Alright, it seems the Amarrians somehow caught wind of our, er, difficulties here, and they're eager as all hell to get their hands on the Augumene reprocessing formula. I mean, what better than a biological weapon for use against the Minmatar that was developed by the Minmatar and their allies, right?

Anyway, they may already have a team in that lab. I need you to head right back out there and destroy that lab before they get their hands on the formula. If you manage to blow up some Amarrian marines while you're at it, so much the better. And if they offer up any resistance, don't hesitate to take them out. We can cover up the destruction of a few ships, but we simply cannot afford to let them get the formula. Understand?

136286.en: The Amarrians somehow caught wind of our difficulties here, and they're eager to get their hands on the Augumene reprocessing formula. They may already have a team in that lab. Get out there and destroy that lab before they get their hands on the formula. And if they offer up any resistance, don't hesitate to take them out.

136287.en: Oh, thank you. I think. This may not be over yet, so don't go too far. Oh, and hold onto that blueprint I just gave you; we're going to need to produce an antidote for this allergen.

136288.en: Sounds good. What do you need me to do?

136289.en: I just can't be bothered to finish making the antidote. Sorry. Maybe someone can do it.

136290.en: Sorry, I'm not flying out to that place again. Twice is more than enough, thanks.

136291.en: Here's your antidote, {[character]agentID.name}. I pray we won't need to use it.

136292.en: Sounds pretty simple. Get DNA, make antidote. Sure, I can do that.

136293.en: Very well. I see how it is. Well, I'm sure I can find someone willing to do this job for me.

136294.en: I share your sentiment, my friend. Let us hope this whole incident is now far behind us.

136295.en: Excellent. You're doing us a great service, {[character]player.name}.

136296.en: You come this far and then quit?! Acts speak far more loudly than words, you know. And your inaction here has spoken to your character more clearly than you know.

136297.en:
Well, I gave you the blueprint we'd been working on for the antidote after your last mission. In theory, we don't need to worry about the reprocessed Augumene being produced anymore, but just in case, we want to have the antidote on hand in case the Amarr somehow did get a copy, despite your efforts. Or, for that matter, if their scientists were to rediscover the process on their own.

However, to make the antidote, we need a DNA sample from a Matari subject who was affected by the reprocessed Augumene — which means I need you to head back out to the lab site and sift through the debris out there. Once you have the DNA sample, find a station where you can manufacture the antidote, then bring the finished product back to me.

136299.en:
To make the antidote, we need a DNA sample from a Matari subject who was affected by the reprocessed Augumene — which means I need you to head back out to the lab site and sift through the debris out there. Once you have the DNA sample, find a station where you can manufacture the antidote, then bring the finished product back to me.

Use the blueprint copy I gave you at the end of your last mission; if you're unsure what to do, review Aura's "Industry" tutorial, which you can access from your NeoCom.

136300.en: To finish this mission, you first need to acquire the Minmatar DNA from the laboratory site (where you destroyed the lab in your last mission). Once you have the DNA, use it and the blueprint you received at the end of your last mission to manufacture the Modified Augumene Antidote. With the antidote in your hangar, talk to your agent again to complete the mission.

136301.en: Capsuleers can have their own structures (POS). These can be used for tasks such as mining, storage, or research. One of the ways capsuleers in 0.0 wage war is by attacking POSes. Though such an attack can be difficult to mount, the loss of a structure is a huge one.

136302.en:
That blasted family corp sent mercenaries after my new outpost. Can you believe that? Who do they think they are?!

Get to my outpost. Kill every mercenary you can. Maybe it's not too late to save it.

136304.en:
It's that blasted family corp! They've sent mercenaries after my new outpost. Can you believe that? I mean, yeah, I may have messed with their supply route a bit, but-- Who do they think they are?!

Get to my outpost. Kill every mercenary you can. Maybe it's not too late to save it.

136305.en: Wah, wah, wah. I don't want to get shot. Wah, wah, wah.

136306.en: You handle that. I need to... I need to figure out my next move.

136307.en:
Blew up? How the-- Oh, I'm going to get them. They will suffer.

...And I just paid that thing off!

136308.en: Fine. You don't want to share the blame? I don't want to share my money.

136309.en:
So, apparently my outpost EXPLODED. In a FIREBALL. I lost everything. The research, the equipment, the bums, EVERYTHING.

I'm mildly UPSET.

136310.en:
So, apparently my outpost EXPLODED. In a FIREBALL. I lost everything. The research, the equipment, the bums, EVERYTHING.

I'm mildly UPSET.

136313.en: Those mercenaries are as good as dead.

136314.en: So here's the thing: I killed all the mercenaries that were left. But, well... your station kind of, well, blew up.

136315.en: Yeah, um, no. Not going to defend your outpost from mercenaries that were sent in response to your mistake.

136316.en: You know, I've decided I don't want to be shot to hell by mercenaries. Sorry.

136318.en: Actually, the question is, can I help you? {[character]player.name}, capsuleer, at your service.

136319.en: Hm… not really into playing courier, no. Sorry. I'll look for something else.

136320.en: Got your electronic parts here. Anything else I can do for you?

136321.en: Oh, sure. Nice, easy work, with good pay? I'm all for that.

136322.en: I see. Easy money's not good enough, eh? Huh.

136323.en: I expect so, yeah. And thanks. Just give me a few minutes to pull up my files, will you?

136324.en: Excellent. I've just uploaded the coordinates of the pickup station to your NeoCom. Do be quick, okay?

136325.en:
Ah, a capsuleer? Perfect. Then yes, you most certainly can help me. A local company called Suntendi, competing directly against Egonics, Inc., has produced a new virtual reality implant that stands to make literally billions of ISK. We have a large stake in the company, so we're doing what we can to help get things off the ground.

The first wave of these new Suntendi Virtu-Real Implants has already hit market, but there's been a bit of a snag in production. Has to do with expected sales figures from the previous generation of implants or something… I don't know, corporate jargon, you know. Not my thing.

Anyway, the upshot is, we desperately need a shipment of electronics parts here, and the courier we normally work with is too busy shipping the finished product to get them here in time. So, do you think you could go pick up these parts for us and bring them back here? You'll be well paid, of course.

136327.en: Pick up the electronics from the station I've noted in the mission details and bring them back to {[location]agentStationID.name}.

136328.en:
Egonics, Inc., is unique in the Gallente music industry. Extremely popular among young citizens of virtually every star nation, Egonics produces the only entertainment headset that transmits music directly into the user's brain. The company's contracted musical artists tailor the music to the individual tastes of every listener.

The technology's growing popularity has caused it spread across the galaxy, except in the higher-security regions of the Amarr Empire, where possession of Egonics tech is outlawed.

136329.en: This universe can be an unforgiving one. Sometimes you will have to do terrible things to remain on top. Your fellow capsuleers can be the worst offenders, scamming and ganking their way to victory. It pays to have friends to scam and gank others with first.

136330.en: I have it on good authority that the mother and son owners of that corp are taking a scenic cruise aboard a tour ship, the Dainty Rose. I need you to destroy it. I'll make sure the battle is recorded as a pirate raid. Don't worry about taking out any other ships that might show up. The Dainty Rose is your only concern.

136332.en:
I will stay here to maintain appearances. You will be the instrument of my justice.

I have it on good authority that the mother and son owners of that corp are taking a scenic cruise aboard the tour ship, the Dainty Rose. Off seeing the sights of the universe or something. They think they're safe out in public. It's too bad pirates don't care about their public image.

I need you to destroy the Dainty Rose. I'll make sure it is recorded as a pirate raid. Don't worry about taking out any other ships that might show up. The Dainty Rose is your only concern.

136333.en: I'll tell you right now "innocent people" is an oxymoron.

136334.en: I'll tell you right now "innocent people" is an oxymoron.

136336.en:
Nefarious pirates? What are you talking-- Oh, right. I mean great! Great! Now I don't have to worry about their competition.

You've done good work for me, {[character]player.name}. I won't forget this.

Probably.

136337.en: I just wanted you to blow up a defenseless ship full of wealthy tourists. How soft of a target do you need? You could have shot pillows at them and they would explode. I need a drink.

136338.en: I just wanted you to blow up a defenseless ship full of wealthy tourists. How soft of a target do you need? You could have shot pillows at them and they would explode. I need a drink.

136339.en: Dainty Rose Returns from a Lovely Trip

136340.en: Dainty Rose Returns from a Lovely Trip

136341.en: A single sunk ship of civvies? Sure.

136342.en: The Dainty Rose had a most unfortunate encounter with a gang of nefarious pirates.

136343.en: I will not destroy a cruise ship full of innocent people.

136344.en: I will not destroy a cruise ship full of innocent people.

136346.en: Great. More courier work, or something else?

136347.en: I give up. Now I remember why I hate mining so much.

136348.en: Sorry, if there's one thing I hate, it's mining. I'll pass.

136349.en: Okay, here's your ore. Glad to help out.

136351.en: Hm. I see. Well, it's a free world — if you're a capsuleer. Not all of us are so lucky.

136352.en: Happy to have you. Listen, I'm likely to have some more work for you if you want to come back in just a little while.

136353.en: But we had a deal…! Okay, okay, fine. I'll just have to find someone else. With a better work ethic.

136354.en: Something different this time. We need a moderate quantity of Pyerite for production: We've traced the location of a Augumene asteroid — a source of Pyerite — of just about the right size. Dig the whole 'roid up and bring it back for me here. I'll upload its coordinates to your NeoCom.

136356.en:
We need a moderate quantity of Pyerite: We've traced the location of a Augumene asteroid — a source of Pyerite — of just about the right size. Dig the whole 'roid up and bring it back to {[location]agentStationID.name}. I've uploaded its coordinates to your NeoCom.

Be sure to fit a mining laser to your ship before you set out.

136357.en:
Pirates and ore thieves abound in the world of EVE. Even in high-security space, scoundrels may pop in from time to time, so having at least one weapon on your ship (or an ally to guard you while you're mining) is a good idea. The lower the security level of the system, the higher the likelihood of your encountering pirates — whether NPC ships or other players, either of whom are most likely more than willing to blow you to smithereens.

Always, in EVE, being aware of the chatter in the local chat channel can mean the difference between life and death… or at least between surviving in your current clone and having to buy a new one.

136358.en: Yeah, sure. That's why I'm here. But what's the matter?

136359.en: I'm getting tired of shuttling things around, people or otherwise. Sorry, I'm done.

136360.en: Here's your scientist. And you guy's had better figure this out soon — even my ship took damage because of those stupid implants.

136361.en: Okay, sure, I can do that. Be right back.

136362.en:
Damn! Why—

Alright, alright, fine. I can find someone else, I expect.

136363.en:
Oh, this is getting out of hand. I don't know…

Okay, please don't go far. I expect I'll need your help again before this is over.

136364.en: Excellent. Again, speed is of the essence.

136365.en:
It's these new Suntendi implants. For some reason, they're causing all kinds of electronic devices to short-circuit, even explode. Initial tests say it's due to some kind of bio-EM pulse. Even CONCORD billboards are being destroyed when people wearing these implants fly too close.

We need to get Suntendi's senior researcher over here to figure out what the heck is happening before we lose our shirts. The public outcry is already immense, and growing fast.

Go to our research outpost and pick up the lead scientist; bring him back here. We don't have much time, so I need you to hurry.

136366.en:
The new Suntendi implants are causing all kinds of electronic devices to short-circuit, even explode. Initial tests say it's due to some kind of bio-EM pulse. We need to get Suntendi's senior researcher over here to figure out what the heck is happening.

Go to our research outpost and pick up the lead scientist; bring him back here. We don't have much time, so I need you to hurry.

136367.en: Yep. You said you might have more for me to do, so…

136368.en: Not a fan of CONCORD's policies, actually. Sorry, but this is where I draw the line.

136369.en: Got your faulty implants here. Hope they help you figure out the problem. And fast.

136370.en: Sure, I can do that. Easy enough.

136371.en: Hm. Okay, didn't realize where you stood on the CONCORD issue. That's alright, I guess. Sorry to see you go, though.

136372.en: You and me both, I assure you. I haven't slept for… well, for far too long. Listen, give us a bit to see what we come up with, then come on back in, will you?

136373.en: Good. Listen, you've been a great help in this matter. Keep up the good work. See you shortly.

136374.en: Yes, indeed. Listen, we've got the researchers working away here, but can you do me a favor? Go pick up a load of faulty Suntendi Virtu-Real Implants and bring them back here so that we can look them over. They're out at a CONCORD building and repair station where they produce their stargate billboards; they've had each employee who used one unhook their implant and are holding them there for us.

136375.en: Go pick up a load of faulty Suntendi Virtu-Real Implants and bring them back here so that we can look them over. They're out at a CONCORD building and repair station where they produce their stargate billboards; they've had each employee who used one unhook their implant and are holding them there for us.

136376.en: Just like who? What is it? What did you find?

136377.en: This is just too hard. Sorry, but you need to find someone else. I can't do it.

136378.en: Whoa, hold up! I'm no soldier. I'm a business-person. You've got the wrong capsuleer.

136379.en: Mission complete. Transmitter destroyed, and Caldari put to the torch. And a pleasure it was.

136380.en: Hot damn! I'm on it. About time you paid me to do something more than flying components and researchers around!

136381.en: Well, that's… disappointing. I thought you people could all fight! Ah well, I guess I needs to find someone else. Or take this to the military.

136382.en: That's fantastic! Thank you, my friend. We've taken a big financial hit, but the government will help, now that the problem is shown to have been the result of espionage. Anyway, listen — thanks again for all your help.

136383.en: Good. Now get going. No mercy, my friend. Not a shred.

136384.en:
The damned Caldari, that's who! Messing around with our technology, scrambling the implant signals so they emit harmful EM pulses.

This is all-out, goddamned war! I mean it! I want to tear those bastards a new—

Forgive me. I get a little worked up sometimes. But this is… it's just so wrong! So many innocent people have been hurt by this!

Listen, long and short: We found out that some covert operations from the Caldari State have been sabotaging this whole project. While we were building the implants, they had spies putting in receptors that would allow a transmission station — which they were building nearby at the same time — to mess with the implants. That's what caused all the shorts and explosions.

Well, now we know where the station is. And, since you're a capsuleer, we've got the right person for the job right here among us. Go out there and blow that scrambling beacon to bits. And take any bloody Caldari you see out with it. You have full authority. Make them pay.

136386.en:
We found out that the Caldari State has been sabotaging this whole project. While we were building the implants, they had spies putting in receptors that would allow a transmission station — which they were building nearby at the same time — to mess with the implants. That's what caused all the shorts and explosions.

Well, now we know where the station is. Go out there and blow that scrambling beacon to bits. And take any bloody Caldari you see out with it. You have full authority. Make them pay.

136387.en:
Destroying structures can be a difficult undertaking. Most structures have very high hit points, at least relative to small ships like frigates, and they take a lot of punishment before being destroyed. And like ships, the bigger they are, the more shields and structure they generally have.

In a mission such as this, where you're asked to destroy a structure, it's generally a good idea to fit as much firepower on your ship as you're able: Otherwise, you simply might never be able to overcome your target's shield recharge rate, let alone rip apart its structure.

136388.en: You are indeed. You have any work suitable for an egg jockey?

136389.en: Sounds pretty dull, actually. Don't you have some pirates for me to fight or something?

136390.en: There's definitely something weird going on. I saw a strange ship out there, and it destroyed two Gallente Navy frigates. Warped away before I could get any kind of lock, though.

136391.en: You're right: Seems pretty interesting. I'll get out there right away.

136392.en: Uh. Yeah, maybe. Well, actually, I don't know. I mean, I guess you can come back later and see if I have anything else…

136393.en: Alright, that's enough for me. We need to investigate further. I'm going to add your findings into my initial report, and then I'd like you to drop it off for me; come right back, will you?

136394.en: Excellent. Let me know if you find anything out of the ordinary. Anything.

136395.en:
In fact I do. And it's pretty interesting, I think.

We've been getting a number of reports from in and around this system regarding "unidentified alien spacecraft." Sightings of weird-looking people have even come in from planetary surfaces. Theories abound, and people are saying it's the Jovians, or even one of the Ancients: Takhmal, Yan Jung, any number of things. A few folks even think it's some new alien race making an appearance.

Anyway, we could use someone to go and check these rumors out. Supposedly there was a sighting very recently out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If you're ready, head on out there and see what you can find. And don't worry — you'll be well paid for your time.

136397.en:
We've been getting a number of reports from in and around this system regarding "unidentified alien spacecraft." Theories abound, and people are saying it's the Jovians, or even one of the Ancients: Takhmal, Yan Jung, any number of things.

Supposedly there was a sighting very recently out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} — I've uploaded the precise coordinates to your NeoCom. Head on out there and see what you can find.

136398.en:
There are a number of ancient races who have left traces of their civilizations scattered throughout the EVE universe: The Takmahl, masters of cybernetics and bioengineering; the Talocan, with their hyper-advanced spatial manipulation technology; and Yan Jung, who excelled in gravitronics and force field theories. Others include the mysterious Sleepers, who some say are the ancestors of the enigmatic Jovians.

Those who wish to learn more of these ancient peoples are well-advised to develop their Science and Archaeology skills.

136399.en: Sounds good. Where do you need me to take it?

136400.en: I've changed my mind, actually. I must have better things to do with my time than deliver reports for people.

136401.en: I'm more into doing reconnaissance or combat missions, frankly. Courier jobs just aren't my thing. Sorry.

136402.en: Okay, report delivered. Any more word about these supposed aliens?

136403.en: Sure thing. You'll upload me the coordinates?

136404.en: Oh, I see. I guess my ISK doesn't change your mind? Fair enough. Who knows, something along those lines might come up.

136405.en: Yes, in fact. Come on back to my office and speak to me there. I have another job for you.

136406.en: I need to get this to a colleague over in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Just contact me once you're there and I'll have one of his people pick it up from your hangar.

136408.en: Deliver your agent's report to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. <font color = #EE3B3B>Remember to put the report in your cargohold before you leave the station.</font>

136409.en:
Given the FTL (faster-than-light) communications capabilities of contemporary starships, it would seem that transporting data or communications physically, by means data crystals or datapad, would be a thing of the distant past. However, for every data transfer via subspace or interstellar transmission, there is a risk of interception. Idea theft and espionage are par for the course in the competitive universe of EVE.

When governments and powerful corporations need to transfer information without risk of interference, they often rely on capsuleers. Common courier ships may be used for less sensitive yet vital data, but only capsuleers offer the combination of piloting ability and inherent security desired by the rich and powerful; of course, one must always take the risk that a capsuleer is trustworthy, but such employers can generally afford to pay their "couriers" well enough to buy their loyalty.

136410.en: Yep, that's why I'm here. What've you got?

136411.en: I've changed my mind. I don't really feel up to finishing this mission. Sorry.

136412.en: This is starting to sound a little risky. Maybe you should call in the Navy, or better yet, a more experienced capsuleer. I don't think I'm up to it.

136413.en: Alright, I found one of them. But I haven't got much to report. You can read my ship logs for yourself, though, in case I missed something.

136414.en: Sure. No problem. I can handle this.

136415.en: You need to have more faith in yourself. I wouldn't send you out if I didn't think you could handle it. But suit yourself. I'll find someone else.

136416.en: Okay, will do. Downloading them now. Come back in a bit and we'll discuss it further.

136417.en: Excellent. Just don't get too cocky — we don't know what we're up against here.

136418.en:
Well, we need to get some actual evidence about these things, these supposed aliens. Now, I don't doubt that people are seeing something unusual, but whether we're really dealing with another race of people, or with some Jovians, or what… well, who knows? But that's what I need you to find out.

We've got another set of coordinates here for a deadspace complex where sightings have been fairly common. Head out there and see if you can't approach one of these ships, assuming you find one, and then come back and tell me whatever you can about it.

Now, we have no idea if these things are hostile, if they really exist. But if what you told me is true, that you saw one take out a couple of Gallente ships, then we need to be careful. You need to be careful, that is. If you're under attack, get the hell out of there. And if not, well, just find out what you can. Don't take any unnecessary risks.

136419.en:
We need to get some actual evidence about these supposed aliens. We've got another set of coordinates here for a complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, where sightings have been fairly common. Head out there and see if you can't approach one of these ships, assuming you find one, and then come back and tell me whatever you can about it.

Now, we have no idea if these things are hostile. But if what you told me is true, that you saw one take out a couple of Gallente ships, then we need to be careful. You need to be careful, that is. If you're under attack, get the hell out of there. And if not, well, just find out what you can. Don't take any unnecessary risks.

136421.en: Look, these ships, whatever they are, are clearly beyond my means to deal with. You need to get someone else for this job. You can see that, right?

136422.en: Well, there weren't any aliens out there, just some Serpentis. I dealt with them, but I'm afraid there's not much left of that transport out there. Sorry.

136423.en: I'll get out there right away. Don't worry: I'll take care of it.

136424.en: I'm sorry you feel that way — I had high hopes that you were the right podder for the job. I'll find someone else, then… but in the future, don't sell yourself so short, okay?

136425.en:
Thing is, though, the last communication we got from the industrial's captain said the aliens warped out just before the Serpentis arrived… so who knows what really happened. Anyway, Navy Intelligence has stepped in and told us to halt any further investigation, so I guess we'll just have to wonder. For now, at least. But we'll get some answers eventually, I'm sure.

Anyway, thanks for all your help. Glad to have had you onboard.

136426.en: I hope so. I really do. Just be careful.

136427.en:
Yes. We've just received a distress call from an industrial that got stranded out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They claim they dropped out of warp prematurely, and that there were several "alien ships" waiting for them when they dropped. They claim these aliens somehow actually forced them out of warp. I mean, can you imagine the ramifications…?!

Anyway, they're still sitting out there, apparently, and haven't attacked or responded to attempts to hail them. Can you get out there as fast as possible and see what's going on? You're the only one who's seen one of these ships up close — it may be that they'll let you approach again.

But again, I warn you – be careful. I'd go out there ready to defend myself if I were you.

136428.en:
We've just received a distress call from an industrial that got stranded out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They claim they dropped out of warp prematurely, and that there were several "alien ships" waiting for them when they dropped. They claim these aliens somehow actually forced them out of warp.

Anyway, they're still sitting out there, apparently, and haven't attacked or responded to attempts to hail them. Can you get out there as fast as possible and see what's going on? You're the only one who's seen one of these ships up close — it may be that they'll let you approach again.

But again, I warn you – be careful. I'd go out there ready to defend myself if I were you.

136430.en: Not really too interested in forwarding any Amarrian political agenda. Thanks anyway.

136431.en: I've got your emissary here. And you were right about the death threats. The Minmatar seem hot to get this guy.

136432.en: Sure. Seems like a pretty easy job.

136433.en:
I'm very sorry you see it that way.

A word of caution? Or advice, if you will: One in your position might do well to swallow one's political distaste in the future.

136434.en: No surprise, given his current efforts. You do know about the Amarrian slave negotiations going on? In any case, I have some other work for you; just give me a short while to put a few things in order here, if you don't mind.

136435.en: Yes. You should know, though, that there have been threats against his life — not unusual for an Amarrian diplomat in this day and age. But do keep an eye out for any kind of trouble.

136436.en:
The government has implemented a program designed to locate and shut down a number of Minmatar smuggling operations in this region. Our corporation has won a contract to supply a number of resources to the task. And as part of that contract, we have funding to hire capsuleers for a number of jobs. I'm honored to be the first to welcome you as part of this initiative.

First off, if you're willing, I'd like you to pick up an Amarr dignitary from a nearby diplomatic outpost. We can't trust his security to common transport, and I'm afraid a military escort is out of the question in these turbulent times. I'll load the coordinates to your NeoCom momentarily.

136437.en: Pick up the Amarr diplomat from the Amarr-Caldari Mediation Center. The coordinates have been uploaded to your NeoCom.

136438.en: No problem at all. So what else have you got for me?

136439.en: I'm looking for something a little more exciting than just running courier missions. Sorry, not interested.

136441.en:
Okay, sure, I can get them for you.

A cult, eh? Sounds like I might have some more interesting work coming up, I guess.

136442.en: I see. Well, one can't expect to go far with that kind of attitude.

136443.en: Good work. Alright, give me a little while to have my staff go over these and then we'll have a better idea how to proceed. Come back in a bit.

136444.en: That's very possible, yes. But for now, just worry about those reports.

136445.en:
Well, first of all, have you heard of this group that calls itself the "Secret Starway"? It's a cult of some kind, comprised of traitors and murderers who are working to bring about the downfall of all we hold dear. And my sources tell me there may be a sect of the group located near here. It's our job to see that they are dealt with.

To do that, I need a number of reports that have been collected at another station not far from here. So, your first job is to collect those reports and bring them back here so I and my staff can figure out the best next step.

136447.en: Fetch the reports your agent requested and bring them back to {[location]agentStationID.name}.

136448.en:
It is easy to think of the Amarr Empire as a cold, cruel, hegemonic state endorsing terrible repression and subjugation. Anyone making such an argument would have a strong case. But of course life is never so simple: For every Amarrian "true believer" in the Empire, there is another who doubts not only his or her faith, but also the government that reifies religious doctrine.

That isn't to say that half of the Amarrians in the Empire are traitors and rebels — far from it. But to assume that every free Amarrian citizen condones slavery and colonization is to make a grievous error. There are many sympathizers to the Minmatar cause in Amarr.

One such group is the coalition of the "Secret Starway" (called by some the "Secret Stairway"), a loose network of liberal idealists who work actively, but always covertly, to assist escaped slaves slip out of the Empire's sovereignty. One of the chief ironies of this group is that most of its members are fervent believers in the State religion; they simply have alternate, "heretical" views of those passages from the Scriptures that tend to be used in support of slavery.

136449.en: That's what I was hoping to hear, {[character]agentID.name}. What is it?

136450.en: I've tired of this mission. Sorry, but I quit.

136451.en: God, I'm tired of doing courier runs for you. No, I've had enough, thanks.

136452.en: As long as they're all well-caged, then yeah — sure. I have a cousin who was mauled by those things, so I won't take any chances.

136453.en: It's not as if you aren't being well paid for your efforts, {[character]player.name}. But have it your way.

136454.en: Damn it! These "Starway" murderers must be stopped. Let me do a bit of digging and see what our intelligence has rooted out. Come back in a bit.

136455.en: Of course. They're entirely secure. No worries. Feel free to inspect them before they're loaded to your ship, if that'll make you feel better.

136456.en: Why take the mission in the first place only to quit now?! Fine, fine, have it your way.

136457.en: One of the tactics we've come up with in terms of dealing with this "Secret Starway" group is to use slaver hounds to sniff them out. So I've arranged for a large shipment of the beasts. Could you go and pick them up for me? It's a private deadspace compound, but I'll upload the coordinates for you and arrange for you to be allowed in with no hassles.

136459.en:
The sinuous slaver hound, mammalian yet rather serpentine in form, is commonly referred to as a "slaver." A native of Syrikos V, it has been bred by the Amarrians from the time they first settled that planet more than a millennium ago. The favorable use of the slaver as guard animal and hunting beast alike has led to its being exported from Syrikos V to virtually every other Amarrian agricultural planet, and to many industrial and mining colonies as well.

Over the centuries, the slaver has become fashionable among wealthy Amarrians as a pet for those willing to risk its often murderous nature; these hounds can become extremely loyal and devoted to their owners if disciplined well and handled with great care. As well, breeders and handlers have produced several subspecies of "toy slavers," smaller breeds more suitable for keeping as pets.

136460.en: How do you mean? What kind of progress?

136461.en: I may not be a fan of your courier missions, but I'm not an assassin either. This woman is a citizen of the Empire. At worst, she deserves a fair trial.

136463.en: I'm on it. She will suffer the fate of all traitors — long live the Empire!

136464.en: I had no idea you were in a position to judge the decrees of the Heirs themselves. Forgive me: I was not informed that you had been coronated the next emperor….

136465.en: Well done. You have served the Empire admirably. I foresee a grand future for you, my young friend.

136466.en: Excellent. Do this quickly, and I'll arrange a bonus.

136467.en:
It seems these "Starway" people have been avoiding detection only because they've had help — from a pathetic traitor in our own midst. Now that we've found her out, she's fled the station and is currently piloting a ship on her way out of the system. Presumably, out of the Empire. We cannot allow her to escape.

Apparently, she's made the mistake of wanting to stop off to pick up some things at her family's private habitat here in the system. I'll give you the coordinates: Get over there and make sure she doesn't escape. In fact, make sure she never has the opportunity to escape again, if you take my meaning. You've just been given free license.

136468.en:
It seems these "Starway" people have been avoiding detection only because they've had help — from a pathetic traitor in our own midst. Now that we've found her out, she's fled the station and is currently piloting a ship on her way out of the system. Presumably, out of the Empire. We cannot allow her to escape.

Apparently, she's made the mistake of wanting to stop off to pick up some things at her family's private habitat here in this star system. Get over there and make sure she doesn't escape.

In fact, make sure she never has the opportunity to escape again, if you take my meaning. You've just been given free license.

136487.en: It always pays to keep an eye on the Local chat window. Not only is it a great place to send and receive warnings on incoming pirates and the like, but it is also a handy way to see just which capsuleers are in-system.

136488.en:
We're receiving a rather garbled transmission. We can't tell who it's from, but it is damnably close to a Navy distress call. It's not certain, but I'm not going to be the one sacked for not responding quickly to a call from our boys.

Fly out to these coordinates and see what's going on. Take out any hostiles.

136490.en:
We're receiving a rather garbled transmission. We can't tell who it's from, but it is damnably close to a Navy distress call. It's not certain, but I'm not going to be the one sacked for not responding quickly to a call from our boys.

Fly out to these coordinates and see what's going on. Take out any hostiles.

136492.en: You're going to win medals one day.

136493.en: A pirate? Damn. Sorry about that. At least you were able to handle yourself.

136494.en: Fine. See if I give you a good mission next time you ask.

136495.en: Don't worry. If there's anyone in trouble out there, I'll bring them back safely.

136496.en: It was a setup. There was a rather inept and annoying pirate that demanded ISK. I spaced him, but still.

136497.en: Close or not, I'm not heading into the unknown just to protect your ass.

136498.en: I'm afraid I'm not up to finishing this investigation.

136500.en: Ships are generally designed to counter ships near their own size. The larger a ship is, the more trouble it has targeting smaller prey. Often frigate pilots exploit this, ganging up in groups called "wolf packs" to take down larger ships. The long targeting time and slower tracking of the larger ships makes taking down these wolf packs difficult. Often the best counter to wolf packs are other frigates, resulting in battles-within-battles.

136501.en: Our fleet is doing well, but there are more frigates than we were anticipating. We want you to provide anti-frigate support. Most of the fighting will be far away. We just need you to eliminate a few of the pirate's frigates. The rest of the fleet will take care of itself.

136504.en:
It's time for you to get your knuckles bruised.

Our fleet is doing well, but there are more frigates than we were anticipating. I realize you probably haven't been in a larger ship yet, but it's actually hard for big ships to target frigates. The difference in size is too great. We want you to provide anti-frigate support.

It's safer than you think. Most of the fighting will be far off. We just need you to eliminate a few of the pirates' frigates. The rest of the fleet will take care of itself.

136511.en: More ships are just more opportunities to succeed.

136513.en: I knew I could count on you. With your help, the pirate fleet crumbled. Even if there were any capsuleers that could come back from that, I doubt any of them will be so cavalier with pirating again.

136518.en: In this universe, there is no such thing as too big.

136519.en: I've been waiting for a chance to really do some damage!

136521.en: I can't do it. It's just too big.

136522.en: There were just too many ships. I couldn't complete the mission.

136523.en: Whatever it is, I'm up for it.

136532.en:
We've stirred up the hive on this one. Reports are that the pirates are amassing a small fleet for action against us. Lucky for us an informant has told us exactly where they're heading. We're going to be waiting for the bastards.

They have a scout scoping the place ahead of them. Only he's not going to get to the final area. He's going to be jumped by some other pirate. You will be that pirate.

The scout will be jumping through an old, decommissioned jump gate. Take a position by the gate, and wait for him to come through. Once he does, take him out.

136534.en: The pirates are going to find the trap, and we lose the best shot at taking this group out.

136537.en: That's exactly what I want to hear. Any minute now the ambush will begin.

136539.en: Scout neutralized. The pirates won't know what's coming.

136540.en: Sorry, boss, but this sounds too dangerous for me.

136541.en: Scouts are surprisingly resilient. I can't do it.

136543.en: Jet-can mining has become a common practice among capsuleers. One ship mines, ejects the ore, and continues on its way. Another ship will then pick up the ore and deliver it to the nearest station. This can save time for larger mining ops, but it also carries a risk that the jettisoned ore might be swiped by a quick--if unscrupulous--thief.

136544.en: We found a mining op being run by the pirates. I want you to fly out to one of their mining ops and steal their ore. I know it sounds dangerous, but if you're quick about it you should be fine. Just fly in, find their jet-can, and take the ore from it.

136546.en:
Yeah, I do.

Turns out these pirates knew each other. They're both in some upstart pirate gang. The name isn't important or creative enough to remember. They do, however, have a surprisingly robust roster. The ones we've been seeing are the less skilled of the bunch.

But I've got a plan. It starts with you flying out to one of their mining ops and stealing their ore. There's a group of them out there mining Banidine. Just fly in, find their jet-can, and take the ore from it. I know it sounds dangerous, but if you're quick about it you should be fine.

136547.en: Bah. Can't even get you to steal ore.

136548.en: Let's see how they like this.

136549.en: Hah! I wish I could have seen their faces!

136550.en: Petty theft? This would have been at least larceny.

136551.en: Fly in, get the ore, fly out. Got it.

136552.en: Behold, Banidine burgled from boisterous brigands!

136553.en: Pirates or no, I will not stoop to petty theft.

136554.en: There were rocks and ships and bullets and beeping and...I quit.

136555.en: Sounds like fun. Have anything in mind?

136556.en: Pirating is a common, if illegal, career path for capsuleers. Some turn to piracy for money, some for glory. Other do it just to be jerks. Fellow capsuleers have the least tolerance for the latter group, though CONCORD is eager to swat any of them.

136557.en:
We routinely make mining operations (or ops) to make some easy ISK. In hi-sec areas it's fairly reliable, with the only real risk being rats from the bigger pirate factions. Most capsuleer pirates immediately get the boot by CONCORD. This one pirate seems to be affiliated with neither, and is being an enormous pain for one of our miners.

We can't let this kind of behavior continue. Take that pirate out.

136559.en:
Because he's complaining about pirates that match the description you provided me.

We routinely make mining operations (or ops) to make some easy ISK. In hi-sec areas it's fairly reliable, with the only real risk being rats from the bigger pirate factions. Most capsuleer pirates immediately get the boot by CONCORD. This one pirate seems to be affiliated with neither, and is being an enormous pain for one of our miners.

We can't let this kind of behavior continue. Take that pirate out.

136560.en: If you quit, the pirates win.

136562.en: Drat. Ah well. Miners are an ISK a dozen. At least you took the pirate out.

136563.en: There will always be more pirates.

136564.en: After that last one, I'm ready to kill every pirate in sight.

136565.en: Bad news is the miner didn't survive. Good news is neither did the pirate.

136566.en: No more pirates, thank you. I've had my fill.

136567.en: I'm sorry. These guys are just too annoying to continue.

136568.en: How do we know this one is legit?

136587.en: I hope so: {[character]player.name}, capsuleer, looking for work.

136588.en: Hm. Must admit, I was looking for something a little more interesting than yet another stupid courier run…

136590.en: Okay, sounds good. I'll be back shortly.

136591.en: Oh, I see. Obviously you're not looking that hard for work….

136592.en: Excellent. Listen, I've just received a somewhat addled report, so if you could give me just a few minutes to go over it? Thanks. I'll have something more for you soon.

136594.en:
Hm. Oh, right, {[character]player.name}! Yes, I remember now.

Well, sure I have some work for you. It's nothing fancy, but maybe I can find something else for you while you handle this simple task. I have a shipment of robotics waiting in a nearby station, but I don't have anyone to pick them up at the moment. Think you could go get them for me?

136595.en: Go pick up the shipment of robotics from the station listed in the mission's details and bring them back to {[location]agentStationID.name}.

136596.en: Oh? Sounds good. What is it?

136597.en: It sounds like you're expecting something dangerous out there. And I gotta say, danger isn't my thing. Sorry, wrong capsuleer.

136598.en: Well, I suspect your hunch was right. Looks like maybe some rogue drones somehow got their messed up wiring mixed into the production line over there.

136599.en: Uh, sure, I guess. "Anything hostile"? Just what is it you're thinking might be wrong?

136600.en: I see. Alright, well, fair enough. Good to know that now, rather than to find out the hard way.

136601.en: Well, I can't say for certain at this juncture: A bad guess might be worse than not knowing what to expect at all. But make sure you have some weapons fitted to your ship.

136602.en:
It seems that one of our production outposts has been out of contact for a couple of days now — and it happens to be the same outpost that sent me that garbled report I was reading last time you were here. Something about strange occurrences in the production line.

I'm not sure what the problem might be, exactly, but I do have a hunch. Would you please go check it out for us? And if you encounter anything out of the ordinary — anything hostile, that is — deal with it for us?

136603.en:
One of our production outposts has been out of contact for a couple of days now. All I know for certain is that they reported something about strange occurrences in the production line. Several injuries, a couple of deaths.

I'm not sure what the problem might be, exactly, but I do have a hunch. Would you please go over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and check it out for us? And if you encounter anything out of the ordinary — anything hostile, that is — deal with it for us?

136604.en:
Damn. Not often that you wish you'd been wrong, but this is one of those times. Alright, I have a quick vid-meeting I need to attend, but then I should have some more work for you.

Oh, and hold onto that robotics blueprint I just gave you: You'll need it shortly.

136605.en: Sure am. More rogue drones to deal with?

136606.en: I can't finish this job for you. Sorry, but I just can't.

136607.en: I'm not much of an industry guy, actually. Sorry, but I don't think I can do this job for you.

136608.en: One batch of new robotics, as requested. Hope they work out for you.

136609.en: Sure. This is right up my alley — mining, reprocessing, manufacturing. I'll have the new robots for you in no time.

136610.en: Oh. Okay. I guess I misunderstood: I thought industry was your schtick.

136611.en: Fantastic! Alright, I'll get them up and running right away. In the meantime, we're going to need more, so stick around – next job coming up momentarily.

136612.en: That's what I expected to hear. Good stuff.

136613.en:
Not directly, but I'll admit that I'm not too keen on powering up those robots you picked up for me earlier. In fact, I'd much rather have you build me some new ones. That's why I gave you that Basic Robotics blueprint.

So, how about it? I have the location of some Scordite 'roids; feel like doing a bit of mining? Go get the Scordite for the materials for the robotics, then construct some new, safe robots for me.

136615.en:
I'm not too keen on powering up those robots you picked up for me earlier. In fact, I'd much rather have you build me some new ones. That's why I gave you that Basic Robotics blueprint copy.

So, how about it? I have the location of some Scordite 'roids; feel like doing a bit of mining? Go get the Scordite for the materials for the robotics, then construct some new, safe robots for me.

Use the blueprint copy I gave you at the end of your last mission; if you're unsure what to do, review Aura's "Industry" tutorial, which you can access from your NeoCom.

136616.en:
To finish this mission, you first need to acquire the Scordite from the deadspace site (listed in the mission details). Once you have the Scordite, reprocess it at a station; use the Pyerite and Tritanium you get from reprocessing it, along with the blueprint copy you received at the end of your last mission, to manufacture the Basic Robotics.

Finally, with the newly built Basic Robotics in your hangar (at the agent's station), talk to your agent again to complete the mission.

136617.en: Glad to help. Anything else I can do?

136618.en: I am so tired of this mission. So... tired.... Must... quit... (pretend to fall asleep)

136619.en: No thanks. Mining is for suckers. I'd rather stick a white-hot spanner in my ear.

136620.en: Here's the ore you needed. Oh, and I thought you might be interested to know a Gallente ship showed up briefly, followed by a bunch of rogue drones…

136621.en: I can mine like a bloody fiend! Sure, I'm on it.

136622.en: Why don't you tell me how you really feel…?

136623.en:
Well, that makes sense. You may be interested to know we've discovered a Gallente saboteur among the surviving workers from that production outpost.

Come back soon; I may need your help again shortly.

136624.en: Excellent. See you when you return, then.

136625.en: Yes, in fact. Now that we know the 'bots you produced were safe, we need more Tritanium and Pyerite for extended production. How do you feel about going to mine a bunch more Augumene for me?

136626.en: Mine the Augumene from the location your agent has given you.  <font color = #EE3B3B>Remember to fit a miner to your ship before you go. Keep in mind that pirates and ore thieves tend to collect around mining sites, though — it'd be wise to fit a weapon as well.</font>

136627.en: Puzzled out the whole Gallente involvement question, you mean?

136628.en: Ehhh… sounds a bit dangerous, methinks. No, sorry, not my strong suit, combat.

136629.en: The transmitter array's destroyed, along with a few drones and a couple of ships. Everything should be back to normal, I guess.

136631.en: Fine, but… you're a capsuleer, for crying out loud! You have nothing to fear. You're immortal!

136632.en: Wonderful news, {[character]player.name}. Well done, and thanks. You've done {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} a great service.

136633.en: I imagine they have some kind of security measures in place, yes, whether stationary batteries or mercenaries or whatnot.

136634.en:
Yes, precisely. As I mentioned, we discovered evidence of a Gallente saboteur. And once we figured out who it was, it was only a matter of time till we caught up to him. And let me just say that our internal security people can be very… persuasive. He gave up the whole story before he died.

The short version is this: The Gallente have set up a drone control tower not far from here that, combined with the chip our saboteur was putting into the robots, made them behave erratically. In fact, they started self-modifying as a result, effectively making themselves into rogue drones with limited AI.

But now we know where the control transmitter array is, and I've already sent in ships to destroy the "contaminated" outpost. Now all we need is for you to gear up and go take out the transmitter, and we'll be back in business. So how about it?

136635.en:
The Gallente set up a drone control tower not far from here that, combined with the chip their saboteur was putting into our robots, made them behave erratically. In fact, they started self-modifying as a result, effectively making themselves into rogue drones with limited AI.

But now we know where the control transmitter array is; all we need is for you to gear up and go take out the transmitter, and we'll be back in business.

136636.en: {[character]player.name}, recent graduate and capsuleer. And looking for work.

136637.en: Sounds kinda dangerous, like a job for a Navy scout or something. Don't you think?

136638.en: I found a structure out there alright — some kind of Caldari research outpost. Check my ship logs for the full specs.

136639.en: Sure, I can do that. Be back in a flash.

136640.en: What I think is that you're perfect for the job, not some Navy pilot who can't be replaced if his ship gets blown away. Not everyone flying a ship has the luxury of a capsule clone, you know.

136641.en: I will do that. Good work, {[character]player.name}. Stick around, will you? There will likely be more work for you once I'm done reading this over.

136642.en: Good. Be careful out there, though. We have no idea what you might find.

136643.en:
Oh, {[character]player.name}, yes, I remember the name. Right. Quite competent, from what I recall.

Well, it just so happens that I do have something appropriate for an egg-sailor like yourself. A couple of our scouts have reported possible Caldari activity over in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. How do you feel about going to have a look for me, see what you can find?

136644.en:
A couple of our scouts have reported possible Caldari activity over in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Fly over there, to the coordinates I've provided, and have a look around. If you find any structures, fly in and have a close look so your scanners can do a readout, and then come back to me here.

If you encounter any resistance, I leave it to your judgement how to proceed... but for now, at least, information is more important to us than hulling a few Caldari.

136645.en: Sure. Or… well, that depends on the favor, I guess.

136646.en: Data delivered. Anything else you need?

136647.en: Well, that's easy enough. Sure, I can do that.

136648.en: Yes, there is. Come on back to my office and we'll discuss it there in private, though, okay?

136649.en: Thanks. I'll see you when you get back.

136650.en: Oh, it's nothing too difficult. Or illegal or immoral or anything. I just need some very sensitive data taken to my colleagues, and I can't entrust it to FTL uplink. It's not too far away. And we would pay you, of course.

136652.en: Take the data chip to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for your agent.

136653.en:
Given the FTL (faster-than-light) communications capabilities of contemporary starships, it would seem that transporting data or communications physically, by means data crystals or datapad, would be a thing of the distant past. However, for every data transfer via subspace or interstellar transmission, there is a risk of interception. Idea theft and espionage are par for the course in the competitive universe of EVE.

When governments and powerful corporations need to transfer information without risk of interference, they often rely on capsuleers. Common courier ships may be used for less sensitive yet vital data, but only capsuleers offer the combination of piloting ability and inherent security desired by the rich and powerful; of course, one must always take the risk that a capsuleer is trustworthy, but such employers can generally afford to pay their "couriers" well enough to buy their loyalty.

136654.en: That's what I like to hear. So what's the target?

136655.en: Uh, take out an entire outpost? All by myself? Nope, too risky.

136656.en: Well, I didn't quite blow it up myself, but the outpost is gone. I have a feeling the Caldari aren't done here, though.

136657.en: Perfect. That's my kind of job.

136658.en: You're a capsuleer, for goodness' sake. If you can't do it, who can?!

136659.en: Agreed. Listen, one of our recon pilots spotted a couple of ships leaving the outpost just before you warped in; they must have had warning of your arrival. But we're tracking them now, so come back in a minute and I may have another target for you.

136660.en: Keep your eyes open. This won't be a cakewalk.

136661.en: The Caldari research outpost. Go on out there and take it out. We have full license to destroy any Caldari we see in the vicinity, as well.

136662.en: Go on back out there and take out that Caldari research outpost. We have full license to destroy any Caldari we see in the vicinity, as well.

136663.en: Good. Hook me up with the coords and I'm all over them.

136664.en: No, thanks. I'm getting tired of dealing with these Caldari. I'm sure you can find someone else.

136665.en: Got 'em. Looks like we bagged us a scientist.

136666.en: I can do that. Easiest thing in the world.

136667.en:
That's terrific news! If anyone can tell us what the hell they were doing out there, surely one of their scientists can. What luck!

Listen, make yourself available for just a bit longer, will you? we may need you again once we've had a chance to, er, talk to this fellow.

136668.en: Perhaps for a capsuleer. That's why people like you are so important.

136669.en:
The escaped ships are a shuttle and an escort. Our covert ops pilot tracked them to a deadspace location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I guess they thought they could lay low there and escape once they figured they'd evaded pursuit.

Head on over there to the coordinates I provide and take them out. Pick up whoever makes it into the escape pod from the shuttle and bring them back here.

136670.en: A shuttle with an escort escaped from the Caldari outpost. We've tracked them to a deadspace location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Head on over there to the coordinates I've provided and take them out. Pick up whoever makes it into the escape pod from the shuttle and bring them back to {[location]agentStationID.name}.

136671.en: Really? Tell me all about it!

136672.en: This mission is just way too hard. I quit.

136673.en: This sounds like it's crazy dangerous. No, sorry, but I'm out.

136674.en: The Caldari shield system is offline… for good. Let's just hope they don't come up with a better version and slip it under our noses somehow, eh?

136675.en: Sounds like my idea of a good time. Count me in.

136676.en: You have a pod, for Zane's sake! You can't die! What's your worry?!

136677.en: Yes indeed. But at least for now we've managed to deal with them. And as long as we have competent capsuleers like yourself around, I believe our chances are good.

136678.en: Excellent. But this may well be one of the hardest missions you've ever attempted, so don't be too hasty.

136679.en: I can't believe you're quitting now, with victory so close. Ach, well, I guess I'll have to find someone else to go out there.

136680.en:
I can't give you her name-- though you probably know it. She's the heir to an obscene amount of money, and she has enough demands that I can certainly use all the extra help I can get.

Her new pet-- a miniature slaver-- has just arrived at a nearby station. Of course, she wants it here, and here now. The sooner you can get it back here, the sooner we can both get on with our lives.

136682.en: I can't say that I blame you.

136684.en: Oh, thank you. I'm just receiving a new message-- I should have another job for you when you come back.

136685.en: I can't say that I blame you.

136686.en: She threw another tantrum. Not that it really matters.

136687.en: She threw another tantrum. Not that it really matters.

136693.en: Let the princess know she'll have to wait on her new toy. I'm not running your errands anymore.

136695.en:
While you were gone, she managed to crash a vehicle she wasn't supposed to have been driving on some backwater planet in a nearby system. And then security found boosters on her. She's being held at the nearest space station.

I need you to post her bail, preferably before the media gets wind of this. Drop off the currency in your hangar at the station. She won't ride in your ship, so just check in with me when you're done. I'm sure I'll have something else for you by then.
