136697.en: I can't say that I blame you.

136698.en: I appreciate your help; certainly we both know she doesn't deserve it.

136699.en: Thanks. I'm trying to talk her out of her latest demand. Check in again in a sec; I'm sure it won't work.

136700.en: I can't say that I blame you.

136701.en: I'll do it to help you out.

136703.en: I think I'll pass. The detention might do her some good.

136706.en: Some ores have no value on the open market, usually as a result of their unstable properties, but they can still be useful in completing missions.

136707.en:
I need you to go mine some polygypsum, as the Heiress has decided she wants a complete bedroom set made out of it. Yes, I know it sometimes spontaneously combusts. She still wants it. Obviously, reason has nothing to do with it.

So, bring me 20 units of polygypsum, and we'll see what she wants next.

136709.en:
I need you to go mine some polygypsum, as the Heiress has decided she wants a complete bedroom set made out of it. Yes, I know it sometimes spontaneously combusts. She still wants it. Obviously, reason has nothing to do with it.

So, bring me 20 units of polygypsum, and we'll see what she wants next.

136710.en: I can't say I blame you.

136711.en: Your willingness to help is astounding.

136712.en:
Oh, good. Maybe she'll blow herself up.

Ahem. I mean, I'll let her know the polygypsum is available. Check back in soon.

136713.en: I can't say I blame you.

136714.en: This is getting ridiculous, but I'll help you out again.

136715.en: I've got your hideously unstable rocks here.

136716.en: Sorry, this is nuts. You'll have to find someone else.

136719.en: The bad news is that the Heiress's inheritance is nearly hers: her grandfather has just died. The good news... well, I can't tell you that until after you've delivered her to the funeral. We're not sure if she'd actually get there if we let her go alone.

136720.en: The bad news is that the Heiress's inheritance is nearly hers: her grandfather has just died. The good news… well, I can't tell you that until after you've delivered her to the funeral. We're not sure if she'd actually get there if we let her go alone.

136721.en: Tsk, tsk. Just when things were starting to look brighter.

136722.en: Excellent. Hurry back, there's wonderful news waiting in the will.

136723.en: Thanks for getting her there intact. I have to speak with her grandfather's executor, but it shouldn't take long, and then I can let you in on the secret.

136724.en: It's a shame. Things were starting to look up.

136725.en: I have to say, I'm curious. I'll do it.

136727.en: I've had enough of these games. I'll pass.

136728.en: I don't care what she runs herself into; I'm done with this mess.

136730.en:
In order to stop her unceasing exploitation of her unearned fame and fortune, the Heiress's grandfather requested that she be killed outright in his will. I'm relieved to discover that he died with his wits intact, after all.

She's off celebrating, of course-- went straight from the funeral. I'll give you the approximate coordinates; you shouldn't have any trouble finding her private transport. It may take you awhile to destroy it, though, so be patient. If we're lucky, she may have some explosive substances on board that could trigger a chain reaction and speed things up considerably.

So, do you think you can kill the Heiress?

136731.en:
It turns out that the former Heiress's grandfather felt that she wasn't doing his family name any favors. The will he left behind disinherits her, but there's more.

In order to stop her unceasing exploitation of her unearned fame and fortune, he wants her dead.

That's right. The request that she be killed outright is in the old man's will. I'm relieved to discover that he died with his wits intact, after all.

She's off celebrating, of course-- went straight from the funeral. I'll give you the approximate coordinates; you shouldn't have any trouble finding her private transport. It may take you awhile to destroy it, though, so be patient. If we're lucky, she may have some explosive substances on board that could trigger a chain reaction and speed things up considerably.

So, do you think you can kill the Heiress?

136732.en: Weird. I thought you'd be thrilled.

136733.en: I thought you'd like it. Go get ‘er!

136734.en: Thanks for all your help. I'm just glad this whole thing is over with.

136735.en: Huh. I thought you'd be pleased about this one.

136736.en: Are you kidding? Wait, don't answer that. I accept!

136737.en: I hope you heard about the explosion?

136738.en: I can't say I like her, but I don't want to get involved in this. It seems kinda risky.

136739.en: Now it's just creepy. I'm out.

136741.en:
The thing is, I don't know. Look... I lost a bet with this guy I know, and I was dumb enough to agree to do five forfeits-- “to be named later”-- when I thought I was going to win. Now I've got no idea what he's holding over me.

On top of that, part of the deal is that I've got to stay put, so I have to find someone who'll follow these freaking bizarre directions.

If you're willing to help me out, I'll upload the station info to the mission details in your Opportunities interface; all you have to do is go pick up the item that doesn't belong there and bring it back to me.

136742.en:

136744.en: Oh, don't worry, the one thing I do know is that it's legal.

136745.en:
Oh, I should have known he'd pull something like this. That bastard knows--

Never mind. There're directions on the damn doll. Give me a minute to figure them out, and then I'll need your help again.

136746.en: Be careful you never bet something you don't want to lose.

136747.en: I guess... it's not gonna blow up or anything, right?

136749.en: Sorry, but I'm not signing up to carry something unless I know what it is.

136750.en: I think you should really do your own dirty work.

136752.en: Well, you're not going to like it. He's set a location-- I'll upload it for you-- and you're supposed to fly out there and wait around for a drop. I don't know how long he's gonna make you wait, so be patient. <font="#FF0000"> And don't fire on anybody!</font>

136754.en: Be careful you never bet something you don't want to lose.

136755.en: Remember not to fire on anybody! I don't know what'll happen if I screw up any of these.

136756.en:
It's about something that happened when I was a kid, all right? I don't want to talk about it.

There's another set of directions. I'll see you in a few.

136757.en: Be careful you never bet something you don't want to lose.

136758.en: You're right; I don't like it. But I'll do it.

136759.en: It's another doll. I think there's something you're not telling me.

136760.en: I think I'll pass. It sounds kinda suspicious.

136763.en: The empires are itching for a war. All they need is a good excuse. It's coming. It's more a question of when than if.

136764.en: So get this: This one Gallente dignitary is completely hammered and calls our side, "a bunch of humorless egg-jockeys." The higher ups are protesting by pulling out of the embassy. They need you to provide security while they pull out. Rumor has it some jingoist factions of the Gallente will try to make a move on the ambassadors to spark more conflict. Patrol the area outside the embassy until the dignitaries have completed their withdraw.

136766.en: You better hope this doesn't get as big as it could.

136768.en: That is troubling. I'm glad you were there to handle it.

136769.en: You better hope this doesn't get as big as it could.

136770.en: No harm will come to the diplomats.

136771.en: It's a good thing I was there. A Gallente and his drones began attacking during the withdraw. I don't know if he was Gallente Navy, though.

136772.en: Screw the diplomats. Let them hash this out themselves.

136773.en: Screw the diplomats. Let them hash this out themselves.

136775.en: Some structures are notoriously difficult to destroy with small weapons fire. If you're in a bit of a hurry, keep an eye out for more vulnerable targets attached to the structure. A good shot at a fuel or weapons depot might be what you need to bring a speedy end to the assault.

136776.en:
The Gallente media is painting both the Caldari and Amarr as overly sensitive ninnies because of the pullout. So there's going to be a little accident with one of the Gallente communication arrays.

Go make sure that accident happens.

136778.en:
The nature of the business, friend.

The Gallente media is painting both the Caldari and Amarr as overly sensitive ninnies because of the pullout. So there's going to be a little accident with one of the Gallente communication arrays.

Go make sure that accident happens.

136781.en: Hah! Let's see how whiney they get when their precious "free press" can't broadcast their filth.

136782.en: So you want them to think us weak? They're only more likely to attack.

136783.en: They should really put defenseless media towers somewhere safer.

136785.en: No. This is pushing things too far.

136786.en: I decided I have better things to do than pop broadcast towers.

136787.en: I like that I can almost hear the quotes in that sentence.

136788.en: Seriously, don't fire at the battleship.

136789.en:
There's a Gallente battleship "practicing maneuvers" in the region. You're going to practice maneuvers too--right across their bow. Pass by their ship as close as you can. It will scare the hell out of them.

But please, whatever you do, do not fire on the battleship. It will win that fight.

136791.en:

136792.en: You would have been fine if you just didn't fire first.

136794.en: Chickening out? Come on, don't let the Gallente be right.

136795.en: Time to give the Gallente a little scare.

136796.en: That was excessively fun. I bet they're shaking.

136798.en: It was a battleship. I thought better of it.

136800.en: Starting to get mixed reports of Gallente buildup. Ships are moving out of stations. Reserves are being called up. We don't know what's going on, but it needs to be investigated. I'm giving you the most likely location for a convergence, if there is one. Report back when you know what is going on.

136802.en: Starting to get mixed reports of Gallente buildup. Ships are moving out of stations. Reserves are being called up. We don't know what's going on, but it needs to be investigated. I'm giving you the most likely location for a convergence, if there is one. Report back when you know what is going on.

136805.en: I was afraid of that. Similar reports are popping up all over.

136808.en: There were ships. Lots of ships.

136809.en: I'm not involving myself in this anymore.

136810.en: I'm not involving myself in this anymore.

136814.en: I don't know that my mind is even capable of forming a response to that.

136816.en: We'll know if everything is going well by if there is a tomorrow.

136817.en: I think a few hurt feelings and wounded egos are worth it if it avoids war.

136818.en: I'll make sure he gets there safely.

136819.en: The envoy's been delivered. I hope everything goes well.

136820.en: Envoy? Like hell. They want peace, they'll apologize.

136821.en: You know, I decided I like war. Screw peace.

136822.en: I thought this is what you wanted? The Gallente are taking us seriously.

136823.en: Okay, what I need you to do for me is find one of the famed E-8CSQ gas clouds. Now of course I'm referring specifically to those gas clouds containing the materials I need for booster manufacturing. You must tell me where the cloud is and get me a sample from it. If you do this for me, I'll give you a booster blueprint copy, plus a little extra cash if you're fast. And you'll learn something in the process. Sounds useful, huh?

136824.en:
I need a shipment of Synthetic Oil delivered to this station as soon as possible. It's currently stored in one of our warehouses in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; I'll give you the coordinates, of course. Just warp to our outpost, navigate to the warehouse, and pick up the shipment, and then return it to {[location]agentStationID.name}. Simple, ain't it?

Just make sure you keep a lookout for any suspicious activity. We've had some run-ins with Angel Cartel recently in these parts, so watch your back.

136825.en:
Boosters are made by processing chemicals extracted from special gas clouds that can be found in certain deadspace areas in many regions. Some constellations, such as E-8CSQ, 09-4XW, 9HXQ-G, OK-FEM, Pegasus, Assilot, I-3ODK, and 760-9C, however, are rumored to have massive clouds of a scale not seen anywhere else. Finding these clouds requires the ability to conduct long-range scanning, for example via scan probes. Finding them is not always an easy task, though; it sometimes requires quite a bit of exploration.

The downside of searching for these clouds is the fact that they are generally located in dangerous pirate-infested space. Few if any of these clouds exist in civilized space, having been depleted long ago by the mega-corporations. Hence, searching for them can be quite risky and is not recommended for any but the most experienced combat pilots.

To extract the chemicals from the gas clouds, you need a gas cloud harvester module. You also need to find the correct type of gas cloud. Not all clouds have chemicals that the gas cloud harvester can extract, and therefore you might have to go through some trial and error at first before you get the hang of gas cloud harvesting.

Today, most boosters are very much illegal in civilized space, due to the horrible side-effects experienced by users during the Great Booster Craze many decades ago. Manufacturing them must therefore be done in lawless space, outside the spheres of power of the major civilized factions. Similarly, anyone caught smuggling illegal boosters into civilized space can face very steep penalties.

Manufacturing boosters can broken into a few phases. Phase 1 involves extracting the material from the gas cloud. Phase 2 requires a refinery structure with the appropriate service module to process the chemicals and create reactions. Phase 3 also requires a structure or station with the equipment for booster manufacturing to process the reaction and create the booster. This simple 3-step process will result in the creation of a fairly common booster. With additional work, the right blueprint, and a combination of several low-quality boosters, one can create higher-quality versions.

136832.en: A gang of Serpentis cartel thugs is being used by Federation intelligence to slip assets into the State during drugs runs. You are to intercept one of these runs in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, destroy the Serpentis vessels there, and recover any prisoners you can find. Bring them back to your agent so that they can be remanded to Tribunal custody.

136833.en:
Some critics might argue that the State has a complicated relationship with organized crime. While the various criminal enterprises in the State (including the Guristas) do cut into the bottom line of the megacorporations, these enterprises are also used by said corporations as a means of arm's-length corporate espionage. Or so the pundits say.

Therefore, these cynical observers aver, while corporate security generally tries to keep a firm hand against the criminal syndicates, their upper management simultaneously ensures that the symbiotic relationship between the corporations and the syndicates is preserved, often to the frustration of the security forces and the Navy.

136834.en:
We've recently received intelligence that a deal is going down in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system between a Caldari buyer and a minor, local branch of the Serpentis drug cartel. While this is a bit of a concern in and of itself, the bigger problem is that we believe the cartel is being paid by elements within the Federation intelligence community; their goal, apparently, is to use this particular drug route as a way to insert intelligence assets into the State. That is of considerably greater concern to us.

We would like you to fly to the coordinates of this rendezvous, eliminate the Serpentis vessels there, and recover any prisoners that you can find. We'll turn them over to the Tribunal for further questioning.

136835.en: I... I've decided that I don't want to go after these Serpentis guys. You did hear what they did to the last guy who tried, right?

136836.en: Even when on the brink of war, sometimes the people need a reminder just what all of their taxes are paying for. Air shows have long been a reliable PR program that gets the people excited about military tech in a slightly friendlier venue than a state-funded parade. There are accidents every so often, and the introduction of the vacuum of space has certainly not made them any safer, but damn if they are not still popular.

136837.en:
Perfect. You've just been invited to the Gallente-Minmatar Joint Air Show. I'm sure you're very excited.

Oh, what am I thinking? You need your entrance badge! Pick up your badge, then I'll be able to provide you with your show shuttle.

136839.en:
Perfect. You've just been invited to the Gallente-Minmatar Joint Air Show. I'm sure you're very excited.

As a representative of state-sponsored capsuleer programs, you'll be expected to perform a variety of piloting tricks. All very basic for you, I'm sure.

Oh, what am I thinking? You need your entrance badge! Pick up your badge, then I'll be able to provide you with your show shuttle.

136841.en: Good. Meanwhile I'll make sure your name is added to the program.

136842.en: I'll take that. Here's your shuttle.

136844.en: Pick up the entrance badge, bring it back here. Got it.

136846.en: Whoa, hang on there. I have no interest in being in your air show.

136847.en: On second thought, I have no interest in being in your air show.

136849.en:
These beacons were specifically designed for use in air shows. There are similar devices already used in construction, but that wouldn't have been nearly as fun as another inflated government contract.

Note: You will have to add Large Collidable Objects to your Overview to see these mission specific beacons. The first one will be called Beacon 1.

136851.en: Air shows are not about fun.

136852.en: What are you still doing here? Get flying!

136853.en: Never say "wow" again. I hate that word.

136854.en: Air shows are not about fun.

136857.en: Gee, as fun as that sounds, I think I quit.

136858.en: Gee, as fun as that sounds, I think I quit.

136860.en: Proper capsuleer pods are completely reliable and do not break on their own. They are, however, slow as all hell and liable to pop if looked at wrong. Traveling in one for any period of time is not recommended.

136861.en:
I'm getting word that one of our stunt craft just burst into flames. The pilot ejected successfully, but his pod is damaged. He can't make his way back under his own power.

{[character]player.name}, get out there and bring that pilot back. I'm not losing a pilot.

136863.en:
Hang on to that thought. I'm getting word that one of our stunt craft just burst into flames. I told them we were overloading the systems too much! Now we're…

Wait…yes, the pilot ejected successfully, but his pod is damaged. He can't make his way back under his own power.

{[character]player.name}, get out there and bring that pilot back. I'm not losing a pilot.

136864.en: You are out of the show. Get out of here.

136865.en: Hurry, but not too much. The audience likes some excitement, after all.

136866.en: Is he still alive? Yes? Good. Just dump him over here somewhere. I'm sure someone will get to him eventually.

136867.en: You are out of the show. Get out of here.

136868.en: Don't worry. I'll get that pilot out.

136870.en: That pilot knew the risks. Let the audience see the reality we face.

136871.en: That pilot knew the risks. Let the audience see the reality we face.

136873.en: Contrary to Caldari propaganda, not all drones gain sentience and turn on their masters. The Gallente have made great strides in drone technology. Modern drones are highly reliable. The one you will fight today have been made to simulate rogue drones, but it is only simulation.

136874.en:
This is the big combat section. We've got some drones flying around that you're going to pop. This is live fire, but it shouldn't be too dangerous. Just take out any drone you see. The people will love it.

Oh, and do note that you must fly something with weapons this time. Your shuttle will not cut it.

136876.en:
This is the big combat section. We've got some drones flying around that you're going to pop. This is live fire, but it shouldn't be too dangerous. Just take out any drone you see. The people will love it.

Oh, and do note that you must fly something with weapons this time. Your shuttle will not cut it.

136877.en: Come on. What's more entertaining than explosions?

136878.en: Then go out there and give everyone a good show.

136880.en: Come on. What's more entertaining than explosions?

136881.en: I can pop a few drones, no problem.

136882.en: The drones have been dispatched in a series of satisfying explosions.

136885.en: Just tell me since you'll interrupt me any--

136886.en: Because soundless space is not cool.

136889.en: Easy, but they do so love loud noises.

136890.en: Great work! Everyone loved the whole show. Why, at this rate we may even have another air show before too long.

136897.en: Is that so? Well, as long as it makes me rich, color me interested. What is it?

136898.en: I really don't have time for this. Find someone else to fight your battles for you. Or better yet, learn to fight them yourself.

136899.en: Boo-hoo, someone stole something from you. Deal with it yourself: I've got places to be.

136900.en:
Your thief is dead, here's your cargo. I taught your friend a lesson, all right — don't mess with me. Too bad he's dead, because I'd like to teach him that one again.

Now pay up.

136901.en: Sure, I don't mind teaching scum like that a lesson or two. Count me in.

136904.en: {[character]player.name}, I really could have used you on this job. It's unfortunate things didn't work out… but I'm sure the fault is all yours.

136905.en: Because of your failure to deal with the small matter of bringing justice to the Gallente thief at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, my business is now facing bankruptcy. Sooner or later, {[character]player.name}, you're going to have realize we're all in this together, and start acting accordingly.

136906.en: Oh, that's all I needed to hear today. No one gives a toss for a poor, honest businessman these days, it seems.

136907.en: Superbly done, {[character]player.name} ! If only I could have been there, to see him mewl as his ship crumbled around him — oh, the hilarity! Enjoy your reward, friend. You've earned it.

136908.en: This pleases me more than you know, {[character]player.name}. We'll show this crooked wretch how we do things downstation.

136909.en: You disappoint me, {[character]player.name}. If I can't count on you, then who can I count on? This universe grows darker every day...

136910.en:
I wish everyone was as straightforward as you, {[character]player.name}. Then I wouldn't be in this situation.

I supplied this Gallente leech with certain items he requested, and then he warps away before paying me. Some people, I tell you. So, I need to teach him some manners. Well, okay… I need you to teach him some manners.

My sources tell me he can be found at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. {[character]player.name}, I'd like you to do that — teach him his manners — by flying out there, blasting his ship to so much dust, then returning my stolen cargo to me. If that doesn't teach him, nothing will.

136912.en:
It's simple, really: I supplied this ungrateful Gallente leech with items he requested, and then he warps away before paying me. I'd like you teach him some manners — by blasting his ship to stardust, then returning my stolen cargo to me.

My sources tell me he can be found at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

136913.en:
Remember to keep an eye on your shields and armor during battle. But if you do forget and you happen to lose a ship, well… hey, that's the life of a capsuleer. Just get a new one, even if you've got to beg, borrow, or steal, and just get right back to work.

Get used to the idea: Ships — not to mention your current clone — won't last forever.

136914.en: Sure, but... how about something with a little action?

136915.en: Sorry, but Geeral escaped. There was nothing I could do.

136916.en: I don't want any part of royal family machinations. I hate politics.

136917.en: The Tash-Murkon traitor is in the hold — a little the worse for wear, but he's alive.

136918.en: He won't know what hit him.

136923.en: I hope I can find someone else to handle this.

136924.en: You have done well; the Tash-Murkon family will certainly appreciate your efforts. I shudder to think of the horrors that await Geeral when he is returned to his family.

136925.en: Don't waste any time! And don't worry: House Tash-Murkon has formally disowned Geeral already, so you'll face no repercussions from them.

136926.en: I must question your loyalty to the Emperor, or else your bravery. You are not the ship captain I thought you were.

136927.en:
I have just the thing, never fear.

As you may know, members of the royal families can be... er, marginally eccentric. However, rarely do they prove disloyal to the Empire. The Tash-Murkon family is one of the richest in the galaxy. The kind of wealth they can bring to bear is mind-boggling. One of their scions, an otherwise respectable man named Geeral — he is, in fact, one-hundred and seventy-eighth in line for the throne — has turned traitor.

He has stolen the access codes for some of the family's secret bank accounts and fled toward Gallente space. If he reaches it, the Gallente would be only too willing to drain those funds dry in an effort to throw the entire Amarrian government into chaos. Naturally, we cannot allow this to happen.

We have tracked Geeral Tash-Murkon to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We suspect he is going to meet his Gallentean allies, who will escort him back to Gallente space. Go out there and capture Geeral. Bring him back to me; destroy his allies.

136929.en:
As you may know, the Tash-Murkon family is one of the richest in the galaxy. The kind of wealth they can bring to bear is mind-boggling. One of their scions, an otherwise respectable man named Geeral — he is, in fact, one-hundred and seventy-eighth in line for the throne — has turned traitor. He has stolen the access codes for some of the family's secret bank accounts and fled toward Gallente space.

We have tracked Geeral Tash-Murkon to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We suspect he is going to meet his Gallentean allies, who will escort him back to Gallente space. Go out there and capture Geeral. Bring him back to me; destroy his allies.

You will need some firepower for this mission. A stoutly armed cruiser is recommended.

136930.en: The Tash-Murkon family is one of the royal families of Amarr, but their blood is not truly Amarrian blood. They were originally Udorian, but their immense wealth allowed them to buy their way to power.

136931.en: Yes, dolls. All kids love dolls.

136933.en: Be careful you never bet something you don't want to lose.

136934.en: Do hurry. I'm not sure I can take these dolls much longer.

136935.en: Just...just put them over there. With the others.

136936.en: Be careful you never bet something you don't want to lose.

136937.en: Four rooms, four dolls. Got it.

136939.en: To hell with this. I quit.

136940.en: To hell with this. I quit.

136941.en: What is the story with the dolls, anyway?

136943.en: He's hidden another one of those blasted dolls at another location. But it's not just anywhere, oh no, he's hidden it this time. It's in the middle of an asteroid field. You'll have to mine through those rocks until you find it.

136944.en: Don't you hear them? The dolls?

136945.en:
He's hidden another one of those blasted dolls at another location. But it's not just anywhere, oh no, he's hidden it this time. It's in the middle of an asteroid field. You'll have to mine through those rocks until you find it.

Yes, I'm serious. So go! Fetch the dolls! The more the merrier!

136946.en: You can't quit! There are still more dolls. Always more dolls.

136947.en: Another doll, and that'll be all. Another doll....

136948.en: Another doll! Almost done here! Yes....

136949.en: Have you ever looked at their faces? They look back.

136950.en: Easy, there. I'll get the doll.

136951.en: That was thoroughly unpleasant, but I have retrieved the doll.

136952.en: You're starting to scare me a little. I think I better go.

136953.en: This isn't even funny anymore. Quitting.

136955.en:
It's five acts, don't you see? The purity of it! The establishment, the turn, all wonderful. But the end!

...At last there will be a resolution.

136956.en: Find Enlil Bel. End his role in this story. Bring me his meat costume. I want to wear it.

136958.en:
Yes, the show. It's the real reason for all of this, you see. At first I thought he was being vindictive by constantly reminding me of that terrible night, but now I see. He is the only one that understood the significance of that night. He was trying to show me.

It's all been an act, you see? And it wasn't the dolls. They're just an audience. We! We are the performers. And this story, like all good comedies, ends with a death.

Find Enlil Bel. He is the one who began this tale.

End his role. Bring me his meat costume. I want to wear it.

136960.en: As good as dead! I love it! I'll have the curtain ready for our guests.

136961.en:
Enlil Bel? What are you--

You didn't talk to me when I was... Oh god, what did you do?

Oh dear, oh dear. I have to think of what to do now. Uh, here. Here's your payment. You don't know anything about what happened here, right? Neither of us know anything.

It's happening all over again.

136962.en: Enlil is as good as dead.

136963.en: Enlil Bel is dead. His part in this is done.

136964.en: I will not kill for you. Get help.

136965.en: I will not kill for you. Get help.

136967.en: Holoreels would have you believe that spies occupy romantic positions, such as enticing femme fatales or ceiling-crawling ninjas. The reality is that often the most effective spies are the ones posing as simple functionaries. Nobody expects the dull guy.

136968.en: Command has been hearing strange things about a certain Major. Unsettling things. It is felt that investigating the Major must be handled with more tact than a traditional inquiry would provide. The first step is implanting a spy into his staff. Deliver this man to the location provided; he will do the rest.

136970.en: Command has been hearing strange things about a certain Major. Unsettling things. Given our situation with the other empires, it is felt that investigating the Major must be handled with more tact than a traditional inquiry would provide. The first step is implanting a spy into his staff. Deliver this man to the location provided; he will do the rest.

136971.en: Sooner or later, you will have to involve yourself in the affairs of the world around you.

136972.en: Good. After this, the real work begins.

136973.en: That's great. In fact, our spy is already providing us with interesting data.

136975.en: I'll make sure he arrives safely.

136977.en: No, this sounds like something I want to stay away from.

136978.en: I decided that I don't want to get involved in this.

136980.en: You have to hire someone better.

136981.en:
There was a theft in the Major's office just before our spy arrived. The thief made off with a number of the Major's personal effects. The timing of this could be coincidental, but it's unlikely.

I want you to go out there and take out the thieves. Bring back whatever they stole.

136982.en: If you want something done right...

136983.en:
Apparently there was a theft in the Major's office just before our spy arrived. The thief made off with a number of the Major's personal effects. The timing of this could be coincidental, but it's unlikely. What's even stranger is that the Major has expressed no interest in chasing down the thieves. He claims it would, "be a waste of resources." We've been tracking the thieves, and we know just where they are.

I want you to go out there and take them out. Bring back whatever they stole. If my suspicions are right, what we find will greatly aid the investigation.

136984.en: Do you have any idea how hard it will be to get another free agent to do this without attracting attention?

136985.en: I hope this will be as big as I feel it is.

136986.en:
Good work. Let's see what we have here....

I don't get it. There's nothing but actual personal items here. Some medals, family photos; nothing valuable nor incriminating. Weird.

136987.en: Do you have any idea how hard it will be to get another free agent to do this without attracting attention?

136989.en: Here are the Major's personal effects.

136990.en: I can't bring that thief down. Sorry.

136991.en: I can't bring that thief down. Sorry.

136993.en: As a capsuleer, you never have to take out your own trash.

136994.en: Our spy has not been able to check what the Major has thrown away. Luckily we do know that the recent garbage has not been properly disposed of yet. Get out there and bring me that garbage.

136996.en:
We know nothing else has left the Major's office yet. Everything's just been business as usual. Our spy has not been able to check what the Major has thrown away. Rummaging around the garbage would be a bit suspicious. Luckily we do know that the recent garbage has not been properly disposed of yet. You know what I'm thinking, of course.

Get out there and bring me that garbage. There has to be something in there.

136997.en: Too high and mighty for garbage duty? Blasted capsuleers.

136998.en: Real investigative work is never glamorous.

136999.en:
Let's have another look.

This is interesting. It's some sort of letter from a Serpentis! Give me a minute to read this.

137000.en: It's not as glamorous as I'd hoped, but okay.

137002.en: Nope. I'm not wasting my time picking up garbage.

137003.en: I just can't do it. I quit.

137005.en: The Serpentis Corporation was founded a few decades ago by V.Salvador Sarpati. At first it was engaged in hi-tech research, but with time its ties with the underworld grew and the Serpentis research stations, scattered around in remote areas, became infamous pirate havens. It is strongly believed that Serpentis is the main developer and manufacturer of illegal neural boosters, especially since Sarpati's father was a renown specialist in that field. The home of Serpentis is in the Phoenix constellation in the Fountain region.

137006.en:
The Major has some sort of clandestine meeting with a member of the Serpentis. The meeting is out in the middle of an asteroid field, no less.

Go out to the meeting place and bring this Serpentis contact in.

137008.en:
Not quite, but it's close. According to this the Major has some sort of clandestine meeting with a member of the Serpentis. The meeting is out in the middle of an asteroid field, no less. If something illegal isn't going on, I'll kiss a slaver hound.

Go out to the meeting place and bring this Serpentis contact in. Let's blow this thing wide open.

137009.en: It's been my experience that the Serpentis are always angry.

137010.en: This better be the lead we need, or so help me....

137011.en: Excellent. Now if you'll excuse us, our new friend and I need to have a little chat.

137012.en: It's been my experience that the Serpentis are always angry.

137014.en: Here's the contact. He's still breathing, too.

137015.en: No can do. I'm not angering the Serpentis

137016.en: I quit. I'm not angering the Serpentis.

137018.en: There are many forms of brainwashing. None of them are very pleasant, particularly in the time frame that the Major's son was brainwashed in. He can get better, but it will be a long and strenuous process.

137019.en:
That Serpentis is the Major's son. He joined the Serpentis as part of some grey op about a year ago. A few months in he stopped reporting in. The Serpentis figured out who he was and put the boy through extreme conditioning. The Major has been trying to recover his son while keeping the operation that started this a secret. With the son now recovered, the Serpentis have nothing.

The boy needs to be sent for proper psychiatric care. It's going to take a while to scrub what the Serpentis did to him. The Major is waiting for him at the delivery point.

137021.en: There's nothing to be gained by being bitter. It's over.

137023.en:
You did good work, {[character]player.name}.

You know, it wasn't quite the big bust I was hoping, but I feel like we really did something good, you know? You don't get to feel like that every day in this universe. Savor it while you can.

137024.en: There's nothing to be gained by being bitter. It's over.

137025.en: I would be honored to bring this to do this.

137026.en: The Major has been reunited with his son, if briefly.

137027.en: After all this I am not just going to hand the boy over and pretend nothing happened.

137028.en: After all this I am not just going to hand the boy over and pretend nothing happened.

137029.en: What happened? What'd that Serpentis scum say?

137031.en:
Your first event is just to fly around the audience. You have to fly out to a beacon. Once you reach the beacon, that one will go quiet and the next one will appear. Make the whole circuit, and your first act is done. Simple, yeah?

Oh, and make sure you're flying a shuttle. You received one for signing up, but really any shuttle will do.

137032.en:
Your first event is just to fly around the audience. Don't get too excited, everything is carefully choreographed. You have to fly out to a beacon. Once you reach the beacon, that one will go quiet and the next one will appear. Make the whole circuit, and your first act is done. Simple, yeah?

Oh, and make sure you're flying a shuttle. You received one for signing up, but really any shuttle will do.

137039.en: We've received reports that the enemy has completed repairs on Lupus Nivius. They've moved out and begun raiding. Your mission is a failure, and now the Republic will suffer for it. Let us hope the Navy can send reinforcements here in a hurry — but it's not as if they don't have their hands full already.

137040.en: That's a fine way to defend our Republic. I'm disappointed.

137041.en: The sector is safe from the Amarrians for now, but I fear for the future, {[character]player.name}.

137042.en: We're counting on you, {[character]player.name}. Good luck.

137043.en: The Amarrians will be loose in our systems in a matter of hours, then, thanks to you.

137044.en:
Our naval units managed to ambush an Amarrian strike force and forced them to jump into Republic space. Now, just between you and me, our action was a ploy to pin the incident on the Empire and gain support for our war efforts... but I never told you that, right?

Well, I was against the plan from the beginning, since those blasted religious fanatics always have some kind of trick up their sleeves. In this case, it turns out that their force was simply stronger than our intelligence led us to believe, and we took some serious damage. And now they're loose inside Republic territory.

Personally, I think they were expecting it all along and just used our attack as an excuse to get a raiding force inside our borders. Now we've got a wolf by the ears — a number of enemy ships escorting the carrier Lupus Nivius. They took some losses in the initial battle, but our ships are even worse off and we simply don't have the resources in this sector to stop them.

We're looking for resourceful pilots to fly to the Lupus's last known location and hit it hard before the crew can effect repairs and start raiding. There's a squadron guarding her, so you'll have to take them down too. I'll upload the enemy's location to your Neocom.

I suggest you find some help for this one — they're going to be pretty tough to take down on your own. Can you do it?

137046.en:
We've got a wolf by the ears — a number of enemy ships escorting the Amarrian carrier Lupus Nivius. We simply don't have the resources in this sector to stop them. We're looking for resourceful pilots to fly to the Lupus's last known location and hit it hard before the crew can effect repairs and start raiding. There's a squadron guarding her, so you'll have to take them down too. The enemy's location has been programmed into your Neocom, and time is of the essence.

I suggest you find some help for this mission — these Amarrians are going to be pretty tough to take down on your own.

137047.en:
One of the most infamous of Amarrian vessels, the Lupus Nivius is nearly 80 years old, and has participated in many different engagements during its long and varied career. The Lupus has been extensively refitted with advanced technology and high-end weaponry. It has served as a raider par exellence, often leading flotillas of battleships and cruisers on missions deep inside Minmatar and Gallente territory.

The Lupus participated in the bombardment of several planets during the Empire's attempts to reconquer the Khanid Kingdom, and its name is spoken of with hatred and fear in Minmatar space — it is widely believed that the Lupus was responsible for the massacre of several refugee convoys as they attempted to escape from Ammatar space three decades ago.

137049.en:
Those short-sighted fools at the Center for Scientific Advancement have no idea what they've done! To dismiss my contributions to the furtherance of human knowledge with a mere honorable mention is an insult! An insult!

Well, we'll show them, won't we? Go blow up the old farts' convention! You'll find a large container of explosives right next to the facility. I'd intended to make a gift of them-- my own new design, very strong-- when I accepted my rightful prize. It seems fitting to use them as the agent of destruction for those too blind to see the brilliance right before their eyes.

137051.en:
Congratulations? Congratulations? Those short-sighted fools at the Center for Scientific Advancement have no idea what they've done! To dismiss my contributions to the furtherance of human knowledge with a mere honorable mention is an insult! An insult!

Well, we'll show them, won't we? Go blow up the old farts' convention! You'll find a large container of explosives right next to the facility. I'd intended to make a gift of them-- my own new design, very strong-- when I accepted my rightful prize. It seems fitting to use them as the agent of destruction for those too blind to see the brilliance right before their eyes.

137052.en: I should have known better than to trust someone of such obviously sub-par intelligence with any aspect of my work.

137053.en: Yes, they'll pay for their temerity. Off you go!

137055.en: Hmph. I should have known that someone like you couldn't comprehend the magnitude of this offense any more than you could grasp the true significance of my work.

137056.en: Um, okay. I'm gonna back away slowly and go blow up the nasty old prize committee.

137057.en: I blew up the Center for Scientific Advancement. The prize committee is now in very small pieces.

137058.en: What? No! I'm not blowing up a civic center just because they didn't give you first prize!

137059.en: On second thought, this is ridiculous. Do your own dirty work for a change.

137061.en: The data you brought me proved very interesting. Now I need you to go collect the physical samples. Again, they're in the same location. I've left them in a container with very little shielding to observe the effects of exposure to the peculiar conditions of the area over time. Pick them up and bring them back to me; the faster, the better.

137062.en: Ah, yes, well. The data you brought me proved very interesting. Now I need you to go collect the physical samples. Again, they're in the same location. I've left them in a container with very little shielding to observe the effects of exposure to the peculiar conditions of the area over time. Pick them up and bring them back to me; the faster, the better.

137063.en: I should have known better than to trust someone of such obviously sub-par intelligence with any aspect of my work.

137064.en: Speed is of the essence, so hurry up.

137065.en: Give me a few minutes for analysis, then come back. Go away now.

137066.en: I should have known better than to trust someone of such obviously sub-par intelligence with any aspect of my work.

137070.en: I'm bored with all this science crap. I quit.

137071.en: That's not getting old at all. You told me to come back, you jerk.

137072.en:
Well, I've reset the password, but the fact remains: I don't trust whatshisname anymore. I'd like you to go collect my data from the area where you found my former assistant. You're on the system's allowed list, so you should be fine.

There are a series of cloaked beacons in the area, which contain devices for collecting and recording data. They are also capable of transmitting the data, but only over a very short range. You'll need to get in close to each beacon. Once you've gotten close enough, my device will collect the transmission and the next beacon will decloak.

137073.en:

137074.en: I should have known better than to trust someone of such obviously sub-par intelligence with any aspect of my work.

137075.en: Go on then, enough time's been wasted already.

137076.en: I need silence to assess these data. Come back when I'm done.

137077.en: I should have known better than to trust someone of such obviously sub-par intelligence with any aspect of my work.

137078.en: Get close to the beacons, bring back the data. Got it.

137081.en: Get your own damn data. I quit.

137082.en:
You still have that device I gave you, right? Make sure it's in your cargohold before you head out after my lab assistant. I've loaded a program that will initiate my security's stand-down sequence as soon as you get close enough. All you have to do is approach the trapped ship-- my device will take care of the rest.

Don't go shooting anything! I've got sensitive equipment in there.

137083.en:
You still have that device I gave you, right? Make sure it's in your cargohold before you head out after my lab assistant. 137084.en: I've been meaning to get a new lab assistant anyway.

137086.en: Typical. Take this device and come back in a few minutes. I'll need you to do some work for me.

137087.en: I've been meaning to get a new lab assistant anyway.

137088.en: Sure, I can help you out.

137090.en: Nah, you can find someone else.

137092.en: Uh... you have another job for me, right?

137093.en:
My stupid lab assistant has managed to trigger the security protocols in one of my research areas, and now he's stuck in there. He's just lucky he managed to get off a brief call for help, because as it happens, the lockdown procedure includes jamming all long-distance communications.

I need you to go pick up one of my data chips. I'm storing them at another station; I'll let them know to leave one in your hangar. I can explain more after you bring it to me.
