137095.en: I've been meaning to get a new lab assistant anyway.

137096.en: That remains to be seen. Get on with it!

137097.en: I'll have this ready in a few moments if you stop bothering me.

137098.en: I've been meaning to get a new lab assistant anyway.

137099.en: I've been meaning to get a new lab assistant anyway.

137100.en: I've been meaning to get a new lab assistant anyway.

137104.en: Here's your data chip. That was hardly a challenge.

137105.en: Since you're such a charmer... get your own damn chip.

137106.en: I quit. You can run your own errands.

137108.en: So you have need of my particular brand of, er, justice?

137109.en: I can't handle this. I give up.

137110.en: Miners?! I don't have time to help a bunch of miserable rock-zappers.

137111.en: Mission accomplished. The surviving miners are safe, and the Gallente privateers are space dust.

137112.en: I can handle it. "Danger" is my middle name.

137117.en: Excellent. Ducia Foundry is most pleased that you were able to save their miners. And taking down those Gallente privateers was an added bonus.

137119.en: I guess those Gallente privateers were too much for you. Don't worry, I doubt I'll overestimate you again.

137120.en:
Yes. Well, not me personally — but Ducia Foundry needs your help. As you probably know, Ducia often sends mining ops into dangerous areas. Most of the time, they are able to handle whatever belt-rats come along, but it sounds like something terrible has happened this time. They lost contact with their mining colony in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

The only information we have is a garbled message. Listen...

...*SQUAWK crackle crackle* ... unknown intruders ... picking apart ... communications ... *hisssss* ... help us! ... escorts are ..."

We fear its already too late, but we have to do something. We‘ve made several attempts to contact them, but their com network appears to be down.

We want you to enter the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and look for survivors. If you find any, pick them up and bring them to me. And be careful. We don't know what might be out there.

137122.en:
Go to the Ducia Foundry mining colony in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take out any hostiles you encounter. Then look for survivors; if you find any, pick them up and bring them back to {[location]agentStationID.name}.

We're not expecting you to have to go to war, but whoever took down that mining station was able to defeat a heavily armed escort. Just be prepared for a tough fight.

137123.en: Ducia Foundry is one of the most ambitious mining corporations in the Amarr Empire. They routinely send heavily armed mining expeditions into low-sec space to mine the most profitable ore deposits.

137124.en: Oh? What's happened? And does it mean work for me?

137125.en: Sorry, but I don't like the political ramifications. You'll have to find someone else.

137126.en: I have the central data core on board.

137127.en: I'll see what I can do.

137128.en: I hope I can find someone else to handle this.

137129.en: Nicely done. This information core might just be priceless.

137131.en: You just helped us miss a golden opportunity. This doesn't bode well for your future.

137133.en: How can I serve {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}? Eager to help, as always.

137134.en: I am afraid I will not be able to carry out your orders, {[character]agentID.name}.

137135.en: I'm not going to kill this man just to solve a few headaches.

137137.en: I will deal with him, kirjuun.

137139.en: I'm afraid I couldn't wait any longer for a response from you on this mission, pilot. Thankfully, I was able to contact another pilot to take care of the matter while the window of opportunity was still open, and she managed to deal with the problem. Next time, please be a bit more punctual in your response.

137140.en: If you do not have the fortitude to do what must be done, I suppose I can find someone else with the courage to see it through. I cannot hide my disappointment in you, however.

137141.en: I'm glad to hear that, {[character]player.name}. Perhaps with him out of the way, that division will begin to show the profit we have been expecting for the last year.

137142.en: Excellent. Here are the coordinates of the transfer station; you should proceed there post-haste. I'll be waiting to hear from you upon your return.

137143.en: That is unfortunate. We may not have another chance to dispose of this fool quietly for some time. Your failure here has cost us a considerable amount of money, pilot.

137144.en:
Well, we have a bit of a problem we need to deal with, {[character]player.name}. A low-level executive here has consistently failed to live up to our standards, but because of his position in a sensitive area of the corporation, simply terminating his contract would have an unfortunate effect on our stock prices. As a result, it has become necessary to— shall we say, "eliminate his salary line"? Yes, that works. Eliminate his salary line, through alternate means.

This executive and his entourage, consisting of a number of security vessels, will be stopping by a transfer station in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system shortly. We would like you to fly to the transfer station and eliminate his vessel; you can do as you like with the security detail, but their elimination is not strictly necessary.

Once you've completed the job, return to me and I'll make sure you are amply rewarded.

137146.en: An incompetent executive will be passing through a transfer station in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. In order to eliminate this problem for the company and keep it from hurting our stock price, you will need to intercept the executive and his security detail at the transfer station and eliminate the executive's ship. You may engage the security detail if you wish, but it is not strictly necessary.

137147.en: How can I serve the State and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, kirjuun?

137148.en: The Gurista force there is too strong for me; I can't even get close to the ship! Find someone else for this suicide run.

137149.en: I don't think I am really the person for this job.

137150.en: I have recovered the VIPs, {[character]agentID.name}. Unfortunately, the ship was a total loss.

137151.en: Don't worry, {[character]agentID.name}. I'll handle this right away.

137154.en: Due to your indecisiveness, I was forced to contact another pilot about handling this mission. He was able to assist the stranded vessel in time. Perhaps next time you will be more prompt.

137155.en: The shareholders have been captured by the Guristas, along with the valuable information they carried. This is a dark day for the State, {[character]player.name}; this failure rests upon your shoulders.

137156.en: Most unfortunate. Well, I'm sure someone else will accept the honor of such an important mission for the State.

137157.en: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. Well done. We could use more pilots like you.

137158.en: Good luck, {[character]player.name}. We're all counting on you.

137159.en: You've failed not only me, but the State itself. I have no doubt you will come to regret this.

137160.en:
We have a bit of a problem, {[character]player.name}. A number of important shareholders were aboard a transport vessel in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system when their ship was attacked and incapacitated by Gurista raiders. We need you to fly out there, secure the area, recover the VIPs, and bring them safely back here.

Can you handle that, {[character]player.name}?

137161.en: A number of important shareholders were aboard a transport vessel in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system when their ship was attacked and incapacitated by Gurista raiders. Fly out there, secure the area, recover the VIPs, and bring them safely back to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name}.

137162.en: While Caldari society is not what most people would call democratic, the shareholder meeting is one of the few places in the State where a certain type of democracy still exists. Anyone who is a corporate shareholder is welcome to attend a shareholder meeting either in person or virtually and voice their concerns to the corporation's board of directors, whether they own one share or millions. While most small shareholders do not bother to attend and simply proxy their shares to one of the large voting blocs within the corporation (the largest of which is usually the board of directors itself), this has been used on occasion to embarrass corporate officers; those who do so, however, do not generally have long to revel in their triumph.

137164.en:
So what you're going to be doing is an old fashioned tower-buzz. It's rather simple. I'll give you a series of nine start and end points. Fly between these points. This will take you past the onlookers, giving them a good buzz.

If you have the skills and equipment, you can use a Micro-Warp Drive (MWD) for this. It's not required, but you'll go crazy fast.

Note: You will have to add Large Collidable Objects to your Overview to see these mission specific beacons. The first one will be called Beacon 1.

137165.en:
So what you're going to be doing is an old fashioned tower-buzz. It's rather simple. I'll give you a series of nine start and end points. Fly between these points. This will take you past the onlookers, giving them a good buzz.

Of course there is no air in space, so the buzz will be simulated with massive subwoofers we've hidden around their seating, but they'll love it.

If you have the skills and equipment, you can use a Micro-Warp Drive (MWD) for this. It's not required, but you'll go crazy fast.

Note: You will have to add Large Collidable Objects to your Overview to see these mission specific beacons. The first one will be called Beacon 1.

137166.en: The CCA is a division of the Caldari Business Tribunal, which is the only nationwide law enforcement agency in the Caldari State. The CCA is in charge of policing trade at the borders of Caldari space and enforcing any customs duties or tariffs, though the State generally has few of those with both the Liberal and Practical factions both being free trade advocates. However, the CCA tends to be short-staffed, despite being adequately funded, and as a result they often outsource customs duties to the Navy or corporate security forces, who will in turn sometimes subcontract to individual pod-pilots. In general, customs duties are a low priority (and sometimes an obstruction) for many of the Caldari megacorporations' operations, so they tend to be pushed upon pilots and officers towards the low end of the totem pole.

137167.en: We need you to intercept a possible group of smugglers trying to get out of the State with some military-grade sensor components in secure storage containers. You'll need to fly to the intercept point and wait for our signal. If it's the right ship, we want you to disable the vessel and take possession of the cargo and crew. Bring them back to your agent, and he'll turn them over to the proper authorities.

137169.en: I've been asked to help the Customs Authority apprehend a group of smugglers trying to get some military-grade sensor components out of the State where they can sell them to the highest bidder. They've sent us a list of possible targets and we've been tracking them; one of the suspect vessels has just entered our jurisdiction. I'd like you to intercept this ship; once you're there, we'll let you know if that's the one we're looking for. If it is, you'll need to disable the vessel, apprehend the crew, and confiscate the sensor components, which are being carried in small secure containers. Can you handle that for me?

137170.en: Unfortunate. Those smugglers will be selling those sensor components on the black market soon enough, I'm sure. We'll have to find some other way to deal with this.

137171.en: Excellent. Good hunting out there, {[character]player.name}. Keep an eye out for anyone that might come to their aid; you don't want to be caught in an ambush.

137172.en: Good work, {[character]player.name}. You handled that admirably; I've got another mission for you, if you're interested. Just let me know when you're ready.

137173.en: Well, sorry it's not your cup of tea, but someone's got to do it, after all. I'll see if I can't find something more your speed for next time.

137174.en: I couldn't hold this mission for you any longer, {[character]player.name}; those smugglers were going to get away if we didn't do something and fast. Next time, please let me know if you're going to be able to help or not; we managed to catch them this time, but it won't always work out that way.

137176.en: Just leave it to me, {[character]agentID.name}. I'll catch those smugglers.

137177.en: I managed to catch the smugglers and capture their cargo. Had to deal with a few miscreants along the way, though.

137178.en: I don't really feel like playing the State's meter maid today.

137179.en: I'm not going to have time to take care of this penny-ante business, {[character]agentID.name}.

137180.en: I might be. What's the job?

137181.en: The Cult of the Lash is a splinter sect of the Blood Raiders. The center of their belief is that the amount of pain and suffering in the universe is a constant, and that therefore they must inflict as much pain on others to reduce the amount of suffering visited upon the rest of humanity, especially themselves. Their most frequent victims are captured crews and slaves from their raids upon Amarr colonies, due to their special contempt for the Amarr faith, but they have been expanding their raids into other areas of the cluster. Like the main Blood Raider cult, the Cult of Lash actually has small groups of adherents secreted away in almost every region of the cluster, practicing in secret on kidnapped members of dispossessed classes.

137182.en: We've been asked by the Customs Authority to intercept a transport ship that has been tracked coming from the Amarr Empire that they believe is carrying a cargo of slaves, which is of course illegal here in the State. They have intelligence that this ship may be linked to a splinter sect of the Blood Raider cults, so you'll need to keep a lookout for trouble when you're trying to apprehend them.

137184.en: We've been asked by the Customs Authority to intercept a transport ship that has been tracked coming from the Amarr Empire that they believe is carrying a cargo of slaves, which is of course illegal here in the State. They have intelligence that this ship may be linked to a splinter sect of the Blood Raider cults, so you'll need to keep a lookout for trouble when you're trying to apprehend them. Think you can handle this for me?

137185.en: Great things come from many small deeds. Hopefully someday you'll realize that.

137186.en: Glad to hear it. I'll see you when you return.

137187.en: Excellent work. You've helped us smash a dangerous cult of Blood Raiders; against such a dangerous menace, every small victory helps.

137188.en: Someone has to do it, and not every mission is an easy one. In the future, I hope you'll realize the obligation that we all have to do our small part for the State.

137189.en: If you aren't going to get back to me, pilot, you give me no choice but to turn to other pilots to take care of my jobs. Thankfully, the pilot I selected for this mission managed to take care of the job with aplomb-- she broke up the Blood Raider cult behind this smuggling operation. Next time, please let me know if you won't be able to take care of the job promptly, instead of letting me hang.

137191.en: I'll take care of it, no problem.

137192.en: I've recovered the slave cargo, {[character]agentID.name}, and it looks like the ship did belong to the Blood Raiders. They've been dealt with.

137193.en: Blood Raiders? I don't think this is really my line of work. I'll pass.

137194.en: On second thought, I've decided I'm not interested in being the Customs Authority's errand boy.

137196.en: Despite the death of Dr. Ullia Hnolku at the hands of Caldari paramilitary forces and the capture of all remaining insorum samples by enemies of the State, Zainou Biotech continues to research the process for creating the material at various locations in the Caldari State. Speculation continues as to what their intentions are if they ever manage to replicate the process; some within the Amarr Empire fear the Caldari will use it as a weapon should they have reason to fight the Empire, while the Federation's halls echo with concerns that the Caldari will use it as a counterweight to break the Republic from the grasp of the Gallente. The only sure bet is that the Republic would pay almost any price, in money or blood, to have the secret of insorum creation in its hands.

137197.en:
A convoy belonging to the Zainou Biotech corporation has broadcast a distress call to all nearby stations, saying they are under attack by unknown hostiles and going down fast. Because the convoy's cargo, chemical components of an insorum prototype, is such a valuable and dangerous one, the CEP itself has given orders for all nearby agents to find ships capable of rescuing the cargo, even if the ships in the convoy are otherwise unsalvageable.

You will need to fly to the last reported location of the convoy, eliminate the attacking vessels, and either escort the convoy to safety or recover the insorum components from the wreckage if it is already too late. It is imperative that this be taken care of as soon as possible; we cannot allow this cargo to fall into the wrong hands.

You will need a Salvager to complete this task.

137199.en:
We've just received a distress call from a Zainou Biotech transport ship nearby, saying that she was under attack by unknown hostiles and her escort force was failing fast. Unfortunately, most of the nearby vessels are unable to assist and as a result the CEP has ordered everyone in the general vicinity to try and find pod pilots willing to assist the transport before it is too late.

It is critical that they receive that assistance, because that convoy is carrying a large quantity of chemical components for a new synthesis of insorum. No doubt you're aware of how valuable such a thing would be, and how dangerous it would be if it were to fall into the wrong hands. Zainou, and the State, cannot allow such a compound to fall into the hands of terrorists or foreign powers. We need you to fly to the last reported location of this convoy and destroy any attackers; if the convoy is still in serviceable shape, escort it to the nearest safe station, otherwise, recover whatever you can of the insorum synthesis components and bring them back to me immediately. Are you up to it?

You will need a Salvager to complete this task.

137200.en: Do you understand what you're doing? You're handing over a doomsday weapon to people who have no compunctions against its use! I sincerely hope that you never have cause to look back at this day and realize what a mistake you made, but I fear that time will come all too soon.

137201.en: Good hunting, pilot. For the sake of the State and its citizens, I hope you do not fail.

137202.en: Minmatar terrorists, eh? We should have known. You have performed a great service for the Caldari State. You've earned your reward ten times over today. Enjoy it while you can.

137203.en: Perhaps it's for the best. After all, it would be better to place something of such import in the hands of someone more responsible.

137204.en: You've failed both me and the Caldari State. Your failure to recover the insorum prototype components has as good as handed them over to Minmatar extremists, and who knows what those primitives will do? I hope you can sleep at night with that resting on your conscience, pilot.

137205.en: I'm afraid this mission was far too important to let sit any longer. Thankfully, you're not the only pod pilot in the service of the State, and one of them was able to take care of the problem, keeping this valuable cargo from falling into the hands of Minmatar extremists. Next time, I hope you will heed the call and come to the aid of the State promptly, instead of neglecting your obligations.

137207.en: Insorum convoy rescued by loyalist pilot

137208.en: I won't let something so dangerous fall into enemy hands, I swear.

137209.en: The convoy was destroyed by Minmatar terrorists, {[character]agentID.name}, but I was able to recover the insorum components.

137210.en: I don't have time to take on this sort of responsibility right now, {[character]agentID.name}.

137211.en: I can't take care of this right now; you'll have to find someone else. Or not; I don't really care.

137212.en: I'll certainly try, kirjuun. What can I do to serve the State today?

137213.en:
There are a number of treaties that regulate the way in which the various nations of the cluster are supposed to relate to each other and what behaviors are and are not acceptable for them to take against one another. In reality, every nation subverts these same treaties by engaging in a number of questionable practices, perpetuating a state of cold war where men and women on both sides fight and die while the two sides pretend to make nice with one another.

Perhaps nowhere is this more apparent than between the Caldari State and the Gallente Federation. While Caldari megacorporations have made a science of public relations and marketing, and the Federation has carefully cultivated a sympathetic image since the end of the Yulai Convention, beneath the polite veneer of both nations, knives flash in the dark. For the State, this shadow war is not about dominance or revenge, but fear. For all their seeming arrogance, the Caldari are deathly afraid that the Federation is only waiting for a moment of vulnerability before they can begin the process of re-assimilating the State into their nation, something which many Caldari already see them doing to the Republic. Often, this war gets the most bloody when the Gallente make what look like altruistic gestures, as the Caldari tend to interpret this as an attempt to get them to drop their guard in preparation for some sort of attack.

137214.en: In order to prevent a number of Gallente corporations from appropriately countering a move by Sukuuvesta, we need to eliminate a Gallente listening post which is providing intelligence to those corporations. You and any pilots accompanying you are to fly to the listening post in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and destroy it. There will very likely be a strong Federation defense fleet stationed there, but the destruction of that fleet is not required. The listening post is your top priority.

137216.en:
Recently, the Sukuuvesta corporation has been planning a major operation in a number of systems along the Gallente border, an operation which would be, shall we say, detrimental to the market share of a number of Gallente corporations. Unfortunately, these corporations are also politically well-connected, and we know that they have extensive connections within the Federation intelligence community. They've used these connections to get a Federation listening post to focus its attention on the very systems Sukuuvesta is planning their operation in, and as a result if Sukuuvesta makes a move, they will have enough forewarning to counter it, costing the megacorporation and the State billions.

The listening post attached to this particular region of space is in a rather precarious position; technically, according to the Gallente government, it is actually a civilian data archive and not at all related to the Federation intelligence apparatus. Furthermore, acting on behalf of the Gallente corporations, unlike in the State, is actually a violation of Gallente law. This means that were it to suffer an “accident” at the hands of someone not specifically affiliated with the State, there would be little the Federation could do in response. Hopefully, you can be that someone for us.

137217.en: I hope you know what you're doing. It isn't wise to anger one of the megacorps, and you've just endangered billions of Sukuuvesta investment dollars. I'd watch my back if I were you.

137218.en: Excellent. I'll send word that you're on the case; let me know as soon as you've finished taking care of the listening post.

137219.en: Perfect; I'll inform Sukuuvesta at once. They'll be indebted to us – and you – for a long time to come.

137220.en: Very well, I suppose this sort of job isn't for everyone. I'll have to find something more suited to your talents.

137221.en: You waited far too long to get this done, and Sukuuvesta was forced to go ahead with their plans. Unfortunately, exactly what we expected happened, and their acquisition was blocked-- thanks to some rather “prescient” financial maneuvering. You've cost them a great deal. I'd watch my back if I were you.

137222.en: I never heard back from you, so I was forced to find someone else to take care of this problem. Time, tide, and megacorps wait for no man. Next time, do us both a favor and give me an answer so that we don't waste this time again.

137223.en: Sukuuvesta acquistion blocked by Gallente coalition

137225.en: A chance to collect interest on a debt they've owed us for a century? I'll gladly help any way I can, kirjuun.

137226.en: The Gallente listening post has been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}.

137227.en: I don't particularly feel like wading into the middle of an international incident right now.

137228.en: This is crazy-- what were you thinking? I can't possibly fight all those ships!

137229.en: I am ready to do my duty, kirjuun. How can I serve the State today?

137230.en:
An enemy cruiser squadron has been causing some serious trouble for our forces in this area. Unfortunately, we're also trying to deal with an Amarr offensive in this sector, and that means that regular naval forces are stretched thin. In order to take some pressure off, we need you to take out the tactical relay that they are using to coordinate their activities. Hopefully, that will buy our fleet some time to deal with the offensive.

Fly to the given coordinates, find and eliminate the tactical relay, and return to your agent.

137231.en: Bla Bla Ambush the enemy convoy

137232.en:
Those damn Amarr have managed to discover an asteroid belt in one of the contested systems nearby! Head over there and destroy them as soon as possible. Once you do, we can exploit the resources ourselves.

Just make sure you're ready to fight. Capsuleers loyal to the Empire might be out in force.

137233.en: We've been watching Imperial Navy units piling into a contested sector nearby. We were moments away from moving on them until we noticed one of their more highly-ranked Field Commanders arriving on the scene. This woman has killed countless Matari; most of them non-combatants I no longer give a damn about anything except that Commander and her guards. Kill them and you'll get your pay, maybe even some respect.

137234.en: I hear you might have some work for me...

137235.en:
I don't know how to tell you this. Here goes: I quit your mission.

Heh, I guess I do know how to tell you.

137236.en: I don't know if I'll be able to take this mission. Find someone else.

137237.en: I've brought in your snitch. The Serpentis shouldn't suspect a thing.

137238.en: Don't worry. I can handle this.

137241.en: Waiting is not an option. Because of this, I've had to assign the job to another pilot. Come back when you're ready to actually work.

137242.en: The informant grew nervous waiting around for you to come extract him. Because of that, it looks like we've lost an opportunity to gain valuable information about our enemies. I am disappointed in your failure.

137243.en: You should not refuse missions so lightly.

137244.en: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}! Without your help, we may never have been able to extract the informant from the Serpentis. They do not like traitors and, if they found out, he'd have met an ugly death.

137245.en: I knew I could count on you. Just be sure you make the fight look real. If not, Serpentis will suspect something. And his associates will be trying to kill you for real anyway.

137246.en: You can't even beat someone who wants to lose? Hmph, what are we going to do with you?

137247.en:
As you well know, the Serpentis are notorious pirates across the galaxy. They are particularly troublesome here, pushing their drugs and committing all sorts of crimes against the Federation. Every so often, though, one of them finds a conscience and decides to change his criminal ways.

It just so happens that a Serpentis captain is ready to turn himself in. Of course, he can't just dock in one of our stations and surrender: He'd be dead before he exited warp. Now, that wouldn't be a big deal, normally, but this one has information that can help bring down several higher ranking Serpentis members.

We've agreed to send someone over there for a show for this captain's friends, someone to fight with him and destroy his ship. He'll have already ejected of course and made his way to your cargo hold. Are you up to it?

137248.en: A Serpentis captain wants to surrender to us and help right his wrongs. He's currently hiding out in a small deadspace pocket with some other Serpentis watching him. Get over there, make a show of wiping him and his followers out, and then bring him back to us unharmed.

137250.en: I've decided I had enough of this. I quit.

137251.en: Come back to me when you've got something interesting.

137252.en: I've picked up the parts, as you asked.

137253.en: That sounds simple enough. Sure, I can do it.

137256.en: Yes or no, that's all we needed. Instead, you made us wait. I can't stand indecision.

137257.en: The Mannar are nothing if not patient! But they can't wait for those parts to be repaired any longer. I've had to send someone else in with new equipment.

137258.en: Your lack of willingness is disheartening.

137259.en: I hope those rogue drones weren't too much trouble? I doubted they'd be much of a match for you.

137260.en: I knew you'd be up for it. Careful out there.

137261.en: I was hoping I wouldn't have to waste our resources to deliver new parts, but I guess I will now.

137262.en:
This one should be pretty simple. Near here is a mining colony owned and run by some Mannar workers. Usually, they keep things pretty solid. We even have a deal with them where we protect them and supply them with parts in exchange for a cheap supply of minerals. It all works out fine.

Recently, though, they've had some problems with rogue drones, and some of their equipment was damaged. Trouble is, we're in the middle of arming to protect against the Caldari threat, so we can't wait for them to fix their machines. Instead, I've been authorized to have their tools repaired.

You'll have to fly out to their base and pick up the tools. It shouldn't be much of a problem, though you might encounter some rogue drones or a few pirates, maybe. So you'd better go in armed.

137263.en:
A Mannar mining colony has recently been attacked by rogue drones. Unfortunately, this mining colony supplies us with a good deal of cheap minerals we use for our defense initiatives. We can't wait for them to repair the damage done by the drones, so we've decided to fix their equipment for them, free of charge. The sooner we can get them back to work, the better.

All you need to do is pick up the parts from their mining colony and bring them back here. Good luck!

137264.en: Oh, sorry 'bout that. Listen – I'm just here for some work. I hear you might have something?

137265.en: Sorry to disappoint, {[character]player.name}, but I don't see this job working out for me the way I'd prefer — you know, like me surviving it. Find yourself another hero. One with less foresight.

137266.en: So you've already lost two teams of your employees to some mysterious fate… and you want me to join them?! Do I have "IDIOT" written on my forehead? No thanks, {[character]agentID.name}.

137267.en: Your mining crew ran into a slave-raiding party. Those scum won't be slave raiding anymore, though — or breathing, for that matter. Here's your crew; now hand over the ISK!

137268.en: I do love the ominous, dangerous-sounding jobs. I'll do it, {[character]agentID.name}.

137271.en: {[character]player.name} — since replying to potential employers is so low on your priority list, I've gone and hired someone else for the job we discussed. I hope you find the time in your busy schedule to read this message.

137272.en: Not that you probably care, {[character]player.name}, but thanks to your inability to do the job, those miners are probably dead now. Or worse. Have a nice night!

137273.en: Well, I'm sorry the job sounds too dangerous for you, {[character]player.name}. If I get any jobs that involve ice cream and lollipops, should I give you a call?

137274.en: Oh, wonderfully done, {[character]player.name}! Those miner implants are safe and sound! You've done {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} a great service, one we probably won't forget.

137275.en: Oh, thank you. You know, if you can bring back those miners in a hurry, I could maybe slap a bonus on your fee. So get moving!

137276.en: I'm not disappointed, {[character]player.name}. I actually had a bet going that you would quit. Thanks for letting me win!

137277.en:
Yes, that's true. You're {[character]player.name}, right? So many new capsuleers these days – hard to keep them all straight. My apologies.

Anyway, listen: We recently lost contact with a small group of miners at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Outside of the miners' distress beacon being activated, we've heard nothing from them for two days. Just... silence.

Normally, we'd just hire new crews. But we spent a fortune on implants for those miners, and we're not ready to write those off. So would you please go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and see what's what?

Whatever the case, you'll need to bring those miners back here for examination and questioning.

137279.en: Investigate the distress beacon at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and rescue the lost miners.

137280.en:
It never fails to amuse the more cynical in New Eden that the Amarr — with all their holier than thou piety — see nothing wrong with their use of slaves. Still, this darker side of the Amarrian faith, while upsetting to many, never fails to generate the gleam of potential profits for those willing to provide such slaves.

The Angel Cartel — arguably the strongest criminal organization plaguing the star lanes today — has not let this business opportunity go amiss. Yet it is a matter even the Cartel handles delicately, since it has no wish to openly provoke the Minmatar Empire or its Gallente allies. Still, if a few Minmatar ships go missing, who would notice? The blackness of space promises many dangers to the unwary, and much ISK to those who happen to be in the right place at the right time (with the right weapons...).

137281.en: Mission accomplished. The communications platform is so much space dust.

137282.en: I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.

137283.en: Excellent. The Emperor will be pleased. Fear not, only the Amarrian government will know of your involvement in this enterprise.

137285.en: I guess I'll have to find someone with a little stronger loyalty to the Empire.

137289.en: We've learned that an Amarrian agent has infiltrated our ranks and has been actively working against us ever since. Maybe we spooked him, or perhaps the timing is just a coincidence, but he's been spotted in a nearby contested sector organizing a small squadron of troops to undoubtedly strike at our weakest points. Whether he knows we're on to him or not is irrelevant now; dead spies pose no threat, understood?

137290.en:
The Amarr are resupplying one of their relay stations in a nearby contested system-- it's due to run out soon and the convoy dispatched to resupply it hasn't arrived yet. Your job is to intercept the convoy and destroy the industrials before they have a chance to complete their mission.

The mission shouldn't be too difficult, as long as you don't encounter any pod pilots fighting for the Amarr. You should fit your ship to defend itself from other pod pilots just in case.

137291.en:
I'm glad you're here, pilot. It's come to my attention that the Amarr have a relay station in a nearby contested system. The station is being used to send monitor classified Republic transmissions and then transmit them back to Amarr space, where their code-breakers can get to work figuring out what we mean. So far, we haven't had an opportunity to strike at it, and it's unlikely we'll get one soon.

However, we've received intelligence that the Amarr have dispatched a convoy to refuel the station. If we can destroy that convoy, we'll hamper their spying operations for at least a little while.

137292.en: That relay station is causing serious problems for us. I'll have to get someone else to stop them.

137293.en: I knew you would be up for it, pilot. The convoy is lightly guarded and the only important targets are their industrials. Once you destroy them, you can get out of there or mop up as needed. Just remember, because the system is contested, pod pilots working for the Amarr may try to stop you. Be sure that your ship is set up to counter them as well.

137294.en: Good work. I knew I could count on you. With that relay station out of commission, our local transmissions will be harder for the Amarr to intercept, at least until they manage to sneak another convoy in there.

137295.en: Is destroying a few industrials really that difficult? I suppose I'll have to find someone else to complete this mission for me.

137296.en: Blowing up some supply industrials? Sounds easy enough.

137297.en: That station won't be seeing new supplies any time soon.

137299.en: I have to abandon your mission.

137301.en:
The Minmatar are resupplying one of their relay stations in a nearby contested system-- it's due to run out soon and the convoy dispatched to resupply it hasn't arrived yet. Your job is to intercept the convoy and destroy the industrials before they have a chance to complete their mission.

The mission shouldn't be too difficult, as long as you don't encounter any pod pilots fighting for the Minmatar. You should fit your ship to defend itself from other pod pilots just in case.

137309.en: I can't do that for you.

137310.en: I'm afraid I have to abandon your mission.

The Caldari are resupplying one of their relay stations in a nearby contested system-- it's due to run out soon and the convoy dispatched to resupply it hasn't arrived yet. Your job is to get to the convoy and destroy the industrials before they have a chance to complete their mission.

137328.en: Blowing up some supply industrials? Sounds easy enough.

137329.en: That station won't be seeing new supplies any time soon.

137330.en: I can't do that for you.

137331.en: I'm afraid I have to abandon your mission.

137332.en: What can I do to help?

137333.en:
Amarr forces in this sector have been taking heavy losses from enemy hit and run attacks on our fleets, damaging morale and stalling our offensives. Naval Intelligence believes that these attacks are being masterminded by the local Minmatar sector commander, and has determined that our best option for ending these attacks is to eliminate him.

We have located a staging point that the sector commander is using for his attacks. You need to fly to these coordinates and wait for the commander and his escort to arrive, then eliminate him. Be aware that you may need to engage multiple groups of enemy forces while waiting, so be prepared for a protracted battle. Return to your agent when the sector commander has been destroyed.

137334.en:
We've been taking some heavy losses in the last few weeks along this area of the front. An enemy frigate squadron has been hitting our ships hard, taking out stragglers and scouts and then fading into space before we can counterattack, and it's starting to take its toll not only on our physical resources but an even heavier one on our morale. Our captains are getting too cautious, too unwilling to push for gains, and our general staff is getting concerned that the front will be stalled because of this. This is unacceptable.

Naval Intelligence believes that the person behind these attacks is the local Minmatar sector commander. Eliminating him will hopefully end these attacks, give our forces a morale boost, and shift the momentum in this sector back to our side. Because of our problems with morale, we aren't sure that regular naval forces can handle this job; we'd like you to deal with this problem for us.

We've located a rendezvous point that this commander is going to be using for staging his next series of raids. You will need to fly there, eliminate his ship, and then report in. There will likely be a significant enemy presence there aside from the sector commander and his direct escort, so be prepared for a protracted battle.

137335.en: Excellent. I'll be looking forward to hearing from you. Remember, this commander is an expert at surprise attacks, so don't let him sneak up on you.

137336.en: Great work, pilot. We'll make sure that word of your victory is spread to the rest of our forces; that will help morale more than you can realize.

137339.en:
Caldari forces in this sector have been taking heavy losses from enemy hit and run attacks on our fleets, damaging morale and stalling our offensives. Naval Intelligence believes that these attacks are being masterminded by the local Gallente sector commander, and has determined that our best option for ending these attacks is to eliminate him.

We have located a staging point that the sector commander is using for these attacks. You need to fly to these coordinates and wait for the commander and his escort to arrive, then eliminate him. Be aware that you may need to engage multiple groups of enemy forces while waiting, so be prepared for a protracted battle. Return to your agent when the sector commander has been destroyed.

We've been taking some heavy losses in the last few weeks along this area of the front. An enemy frigate squadron has been hitting our ships hard, taking out stragglers and scouts and then fading into space before we can counterattack, and it's starting to take its toll not only on our physical resources but an even heavier one on our morale. Our captains are getting too cautious, too unwilling to push for gains, and our general staff is getting concerned that the front will be stalled because of this. This is unacceptable.

Naval Intelligence believes that the person behind these attacks is the local Gallente sector commander. Eliminating him will hopefully end these attacks, give our forces a morale boost, and shift the momentum in this sector back to our side. Because of our problems with morale, we aren't sure that regular naval forces can handle this job; we'd like you to deal with this problem for us.

We've located a rendezvous point that this commander is going to be using for staging his next series of raids. You will need to fly there, eliminate his ship, and then report in. There will likely be a significant enemy presence there aside from the sector commander and his direct escort, so be prepared for a protracted battle.

137398.en:

A capsuleer working for us managed to take the guards out some time ago, after which we then sent in forces to deactivate it. For a while, it seemed like the Republic would simply abandon the gate.

Unfortunately, that's not the case. We've detected a squad of ships heading to the gate to initiate repairs on the gate and reactivate it, probably so they can more easily move forces into the area. Luckily, it will take them quite some time to get it operational. We want you to head out there and stop them before they can. Can you handle this?

Just remember, this gate is in a contested system. That means pod pilots flying for the Republic might try to stop you. Be careful.

137505.en: The life of a reconnaissance pilot is fraught with real and present danger at all times. Since even the slightest mistake can cost an entire squadron their lives, operations behind enemy lines are a task carried out by some of the most disciplined and battle-hardened pilots each empire has.

137506.en:
We just received a priority transmission from one of our Recon task forces currently operating inside hostile space. As per their orders, they were scouting the area for enemy forces and this is precisely what they've found. They sent out the call for reinforcements as they were unable to tackle them alone.

I relayed to them that we'd send some capsuleer assistance as soon as we could find someone, but I've not heard any further replies since. Get your ass out there. I want them supported in any way possible.

137508.en:
Alright then, I suppose I've got something for you.

We just received a priority transmission from one of our Recon task forces currently operating inside hostile space. As per their orders, they were scouting the area for enemy forces and this is precisely what they've found. They sent out the call for reinforcements as they were unable to tackle them alone.

I relayed to them that we'd send some capsuleer assistance as soon as we could find someone, but I've not heard any further replies since. They've either had to maintain comms silence to avoid being detected or they've been forced to engage prematurely.

In any case, get your ass out there. Those are good men and women putting their lives on the line. I want them supported in any way possible.

137509.en: In a time of war, there are very few people who will not find themselves caught in the crossfire. Civilians and non-combatants who directly assist armed forces are invariably seen as valid targets – no empire will risk letting their efforts go unhindered. In such dark times, necessity always takes precedent over morality.

137510.en: Sorry for the let down? Is that all you have to say? They're probably dead or cornered and that's all you offer me? Keep that callous attitude up and you'll find yourself barred from any further work inside our borders.

137512.en: Good. Keep your comms line open, I'll be relaying further information when you give me a clear picture of the situation.

137513.en:
The task I have for you today is an important one. It is significant not only in strategic terms, but also a test of your loyalty.

We have identified a civilian facility inside a nearby contested sector that houses a great number of engineers and mechanics, all of whom assist with the repair of Minmatar vessels far from their home stations. Though they may technically be non-combatants, these people are directly and unarguably assisting Republic forces. They must be dealt with.

Fortunately for us, there is a small window of opportunity where we can strike at them. Repaired ships that are awaiting further deployment usually stand on guard at the facility. However, the large majority of them have been recalled to another higher priority assignment. We have a chance to strike here, rookie. Will you help the Empire?

137514.en: Yes, they succeeded in clearing the area of hostiles just moments ago. Good work out there rookie, keep it up.

137515.en: Useless. Don't offer your services unless you intend to provide them wherever and whenever you are asked to!

137517.en: I just made it back, is everything ok now?

137518.en: Oh…sorry, I won't be able to leave immediately. You better find someone else.

137609.en:
The Gallente Federation is trying to set up a starbase inside one of the contested systems. If they manage to get it up and running, they'll have a staging point from which to launch further attacks against us. Luckily, it is not yet fully operational and has a highly explosive reactor that is just waiting to be destroyed.

I've uploaded the location of the starbase to your NeoCom. Head over there and destroy the reactor. Just watch out for the pod pilots working for the Federation. They will try to stop you if they can.

137610.en:
Those damn Gallente. Always up to something sneaky. Thankfully we've enough spies in their midst to keep them from pulling off anything too big. One of those spies just reported that the Federation is trying to construct a starbase inside a nearby contested system.

A fully functioning starbase can cause us a huge headache. They're tough and require a lot of manpower to destroy. Because of our spies we have a first strike advantage. The starbase hasn't been completed yet, and the idiot Gallente have filled their main reactor full of fuel.

If you head over there and destroy the reactor, the entire starbase will blow. Do you think you can do this for me?

137611.en: I suppose I can send someone else to finish the job.

137612.en: Good deal. I've uploaded the location to your NeoCom. There will be some defenses there, but they shouldn't be too difficult for you. However, pod pilots working for the Federation may be flying in the area. Prepare yourself to face them.

137613.en: Excellent work. I wish I could have been there to see that thing go. I bet it was quite a display! Hopefully, this will set the Gallente back and make them hesitate before trying to set up a starbase here again!

137614.en: Don't you think you can handle this?

137615.en: Blowing up a reactor is what I've been dreaming of! Count me in.

137616.en: I've destroyed the reactor and the starbase went up like a State Independence celebration!

137618.en: That starbase reactor was tougher than I expected.

137687.en: An old smuggler's gate connects a system deep inside Republic territory with one of the contested systems nearby. It's been offline for years, but the Republic is trying to get it running again. Destroy the repair ships trying to repair the gate.

137688.en:
Our contested territory is riddled with old, inoperable gates. Some of them were put up by our enemies, others by common smugglers hoping to get past customs. Well, it turns out that the Republic has discovered one of these derelict gates. Normally, this wouldn't be an issue, but the gate connects to a system deep in Republic space.

I don't need to tell you what could happen if those Minmatar slave dogs get that gate online. We can't spare the manpower to destroy the gate itself, but the ships working to repair it aren't nearly so sturdy.

I want you to fly over there and take them out. Are you up for it?

137707.en: An old smuggler's gate connects a system deep inside Federation territory with one of the contested systems nearby. It's been offline for years, but the Federation is trying to get it running again. Destroy the repair ships trying to repair the gate.

137708.en:
Our contested territory is riddled with old, inoperable gates. Some of them were put up by our enemies, others by common smugglers hoping to get past customs. Well, it turns out that the Federation has discovered one of these derelict gates. Normally, this wouldn't be an issue, but the gate connects to a system deep in Federation space.

I don't need to tell you what could happen if those Caldari fascists get that gate online. We can't spare the manpower to destroy the gate itself, but the ships working to repair it aren't nearly so sturdy.

I want you to fly over there and take them out. Are you up for it?

137729.en: A reconnaissance patrol has located the base of a group of Minmatar raiders operating near this system. In order to secure our supply lines, you will need to fly to the base and destroy its main reactor, knocking it out of action. Any additional damage you can do to static defenses or the enemy raiding fleets would certainly be appreciated.

137730.en:
Our supply lines have been taking heavy damage from Minmatar raids near this system. Until recently, we were baffled as to where the enemy force was resupplying. Luckily, a reconnaissance patrol just returned with sensor data that seems to correspond with the reactor emissions of a Minmatar base, and it's in exactly the right place to be supporting these raids.

We want you to fly to the location of these reactor emissions, locate the base, and destroy its main reactor; that should be enough to put it out of action for a while. The thing to remember is that the base is likely to be well-protected, with static defenses if nothing else. I'd advise being careful on your approach. Keep an eye out for any raiding groups returning to resupply. Are you ready?

137731.en: I'm extremely disappointed. Hopefully, I can find someone else to take this mission before they hit us again; if I can't, I hope you realize that those losses will be on your head, pilot.

137732.en: Excellent.  Remember, take out the reactor; anything else is just a bonus. Good hunting, pilot.

137733.en: Great work, pilot. We're already putting together a counterstrike in case they come to repair it. You've helped us bait the trap perfectly, and saved a load of war materiel and lives in the process.

137734.en: I don't know what you're talking about, but if that's the way you're going to be, then I'll find someone else to do it.

137762.en:
The Navy is planning a new offensive against Republic positions, but Naval Intelligence has been unable to make headway getting the information necessary to plan a coordinated strike. In order to get the intelligence we need, we're going to need you to make a raid on a secure enemy datastore.

You'll need to jump into the deadspace area, eliminate the defenders, and recover the Tactical Information Sheet from the datastore. Once you've got it, bring it back to your agent so that Naval Intelligence can analyze it in preparation for the offensive.

137763.en:
The Navy's general staff is planning an offensive against Minmatar positions in this sector, but Naval Intelligence is having difficulty piercing the veil of enemy counterintelligence. Optimally, we'd like to get a better idea of Minmatar positions, communications codes, fleet readiness and their own intelligence estimates of our disposition, but they've been working hard to keep us from getting our hands on anything more than a vague picture.

We've decided to try a bit of an end-run around their counterintelligence screen. We know where they have a secure datastore in an area of deadspace. We're going to send you in to recover the information from the datastore, but we'll only have a short window for this, so you'll need to move quickly. Can you handle that?

137764.en: Good. Return here as soon as you get the data.

137765.en: Nice work, pilot. I'll pass this up the chain to Naval Intelligence. Drinks are on us tonight.

137766.en: This war isn't going to get any easier, pilot.  You'd better start thinking whether or not you're really cut out for this line of work.

137768.en: I think I've found what you were looking for. Is this it?

137769.en: Sounds pretty dicey. I'm going to sit this one out.

137803.en: The breakdown in relations between the empires has seen huge losses in civilian life as they all target “weak points” and set missions specifically to “maximize morale loss.” In a war, there are few who will not see the atrocities of conflict and defenseless non-combatants are no exception. Those who lead such missions however, sit at the very top of their enemy's target lists.

137804.en: We've been watching Republic Fleet units piling into a contested sector nearby. We were moments away from moving on them until we noticed one of their more highly-ranked Field Commanders arriving on the scene. This woman has killed countless Amarrians; most of them non-combatants I no longer give a damn about anything except that Commander and her guards. Kill them and you'll get your pay, maybe even some respect.

We've been watching Republic Fleet units piling into a contested sector nearby. We were moments away from moving on them until we noticed one of their more highly-ranked Field Commanders arriving on the scene. This woman has killed countless Amarrians; most of them non-combatants. She has a penchant for hitting weakened and unsupported civilian structures. She is scum, and I want her dead.

This is surgical stuff, pilot. She'll slip away if we go in there with full force. I no longer give a damn about anything except that Commander and her guards. Kill them and you'll get your pay, maybe even some respect.

Simple as that, now get going.

137850.en: Changes in technology and in particular, the advent of the jump drive, has made the battlefields of space a dynamic and unpredictable arena. Where previously reinforcements could take many hours or even days to arrive on-field, now they can be dropped immediately into the fray with a single cynosaural field. When the technology first appeared, all four empires had to drastically revise their outdated battle tactics and this is a process still happening even today. Mistakes are still made, and the cost of hubris and underestimation is usually high.

137851.en: Moments ago we launched an offensive against a Minmatar compound inside a hostile sector where they have strong numbers and superior logistics support. We're not going to risk getting slaughtered however, and this is where you come in. I want you to fly over there and ensure the success of this operation. I'll personally relay further information to you once you've made it onto the field.

137853.en:
Moments ago we launched an offensive against a Minmatar compound inside a hostile sector where they have strong numbers and superior logistics support.

Initial reconnaissance has suggested they may have the capability to field more vessels than we had originally anticipated. Naturally, we're not turning around in the face of this news, we've come too far and a retreat will only encourage them. We're not going to risk getting slaughtered however, and this is where you come in.

I want you to fly over there and ensure the success of this operation. I'll personally relay further information to you once you've made it onto the field. Don't worry about any orders or cohesion with our own forces there, you'll be answering directly to me and following only my orders.

Briefing over. Get going.

137854.en: What?! I already told my superiors the matter was being handled. I'm really glad you hope I can find someone else, rookie. That means so much to me whilst our own people are out there risking their lives. Don't let me catch you repeating this performance.

137855.en: You'll hear from me shortly. Pay close attention to my orders and obey them exactly.

137856.en: Orders are only as good as the people who carry them out. That was some good work out there, pilot; calm, precise and efficient. You fly like a real Amarrian. Keep it up.

137857.en: Why should I care? You asked how you could help so I'm telling you. Clearly I'm wasting my damn time in the process. A piece of advice rookie, don't ask if you can help when you have no concept of the expectations likely to be put upon you.

137859.en: Good call on the Commander, it seems to have worked.

137860.en: I won't be able to help with something like this I'm afraid, that sector is too far out of my way.

137861.en: I can't commit myself to this after all. Hopefully you can find someone else in time.

137862.en: That's why I'm here, how can I help?

Unfortunately, our regular naval forces have their hands full dealing with an enemy offensive several systems away and protecting our supply lines holding the line in that area. As a result, I've been tasked with finding a loyal capsuleer who can take care of the problem for us. We'd like for you to give it a shot.

The general staff has decided to put an end to this campaign by striking a crippling blow to their morale. We want you to eliminate the enemy sector commander at these coordinates; all other targets are secondary.

138199.en:

Lately, the Gallente have enjoyed a string of small but dramatic victories over our forces in this sector. Though the damage inflicted to our forces has been negligible, the enemy forces responsible for these actions, especially their commander, have been emboldened and now they are pushing their luck more and more.

The general staff has determined that striking a crippling blow to their morale will likely put an end to this nonsense once and for all. We want you to eliminate their commander. With any luck, this will scatter them to the winds and put an end to these raids.

In order to get that intelligence, we need you to raid the base of an enemy force in this sector. We need you to get the tactical information sheet from the outpost and bring it back here in preparation for the prisoner raid.

According to the latest intelligence reports, enemy forces in this sector have been building up for a major offensive. Over the last 48 hours, we've detected a number of enemy support squadrons moving into positions that will let them hit a variety of targets with little notice. It's likely that they're planning a carefully coordinated strike against us, hoping for a breakthrough. Reinforcements are en route to this sector, but we need to buy some time.

We've located an enemy communications relay that is most likely serving as the coordination center for a large part of the enemy support fleet. While they're keeping a sharp eye on our forces, a capsuleer like yourself could sneak past their lines and hit them where they aren't looking. With the relay down, they won't be able to coordinate their attacks, and we should be able to hold them off long enough for reinforcements to arrive.

The two of them are very close, and the elder is well known to be a bit protective of the commander.

While the sector commander is not a particularly important or successful one, we believe that if he goes missing, the elder will demand that his Navy drop everything to look for his adopted son. This will force them to scour space for the missing commander, which should buy us a few days.

We want you to intercept and eliminate the sector commander before he knows what hit him.

138517.en:
The added responsibility and higher profile that comes with promotion is never without a great amount of personal risk. This is true across all the navies of the empires. Enemy Field Commanders are one of the most common targets of assassinations, and though the high honor of attaining such a rank is something countless people work towards, many do not hold the position for very long.

This is particularly true of the most brilliant commanders, who are often the first to be targeted for removal. With loyal capsuleers at their disposal, the empires are only too happy to pay large sums to have the most promising enemy commanders ruthlessly culled.

138518.en:
A few weeks ago we dispatched a small squadron of Federation vessels that had made it inside our borders to a contested sector. We thought the job was finished and the area secure but it seems we've been duped. The entire regiment we cleared was just a decoy, and they've been massing hostiles in a nearby location.

Various sources of ours have pointed towards one of their Field Commanders being the key strategist behind these latest maneuvers. We need her assassinated.

138520.en:
We have a serious situation on our hands, pilot.

A few weeks ago we dispatched a small squadron of Federation vessels that had made it inside our borders to a contested sector. We thought the job was finished and the area secure but it seems we've been duped. The entire regiment we cleared was just a decoy, and they've been massing hostiles in a nearby location with the use of covert technology.

The situation is not only embarrassing; it's undoubtedly boosted their own morale to have deceived us so effectively. We relocated all of our forces from there only days ago and re-establishing a presence will be admitting to our own people that those Federation scum outsmarted us…or one of them in particular, actually.

Various sources of ours have pointed towards one of their Field Commanders being the key strategist behind these latest maneuvers. We need her assassinated, pilot. Not only will her death impede their progress, but it should send a message to other commanders inside the Federation. Fly out there and make it clear to them: we have capsuleers ready and able to strike down their best and brightest. Let that be the first thought in their mind before they step up to lead fleets against our people.

138521.en: I trusted you and only you with this, what am I supposed to do now? Now they know we sent some of our best and failed, you've only emboldened them further! It seems I'll have to seriously reassess your worth to us.

138522.en: I knew I could rely on you. I'll be eagerly awaiting news of your success.

138523.en: Excellent work, pilot. That should leave it clear to aspiring commanders just what exactly their promotion brings.

138524.en: A disappointing remark, especially coming from one such as you. A million brave deeds in good times cannot compare to a single act made when everything has begun to fall apart. This is Admiral Tovil-Toba's lesson, pilot. Remember it well.

138525.en: Understood. I'll make sure she's made an example of.

Despite the frequent death of civilians in a war, it is nonetheless exceptionally rare for large-scale casualties to happen without even a shred of reason. Engineers, mechanics, scientists, these and other professions – when used directly to aid combatant forces – can be said to have justifiably draw the wrath of their enemies. There just enough shades of grey to allow it.

No empire, however, is foolish enough to outright murder citizens without any involvement in a conflict. Or as some might argue, they are not so foolish as to get caught in the act. The rise of the capsuleer has spawned a dark new age where culpability is little more than an elusive dream.

138534.en: Very recently, we spotted a huge transport fleet carrying thousands upon thousands of Gallente towards our borders. We let them enter, pretending as always that we had not noticed. This time however, we reinforced all of the likely exit points with additional patrols. As a result they have not yet been able to leave. They are sitting largely defenseless as they wait for an opportunity to pass back out into Federation borders. Do what must be done.

Good, listen carefully.

The Federation has been moving their own citizens through our space, shuttling them back home from distant and lawless frontiers. We've been watching this for some time now and for the most part, simply ignoring it. Predictable as they are, we knew the appearance of lax border security would embolden them and this is precisely what has happened.

Very recently, we spotted a huge transport fleet carrying thousands upon thousands of their people towards our borders. We let them enter, pretending as always that we had not noticed. This time however, we reinforced all of the likely exit points with additional patrols. As a result they have not yet been able to leave.

They are currently holed up in a nearby contested sector, where Federation forces will offer them some protection, but only a little. They are sitting largely defenseless as they wait for an opportunity to pass back out into Gallente borders. I will give you those coordinates if you can promise me you will do something useful with them.

Am I being understood here, pilot?

138560.en:
Despite the frequent death of civilians in a war, it is nonetheless exceptionally rare for large-scale casualties to happen without even a shred of reason. Engineers, mechanics, scientists, these and other professions – when used directly to aid combatant forces – can be said to have justifiably draw the wrath of their enemies. There just enough shades of grey to allow it.

No empire, however, is foolish enough to outright murder citizens without any involvement in a conflict. Or as some might argue, they are not so foolish as to get caught in the act. The rise of the capsuleer has spawned a dark new age where culpability is little more than an elusive dream.

This time however, we reinforced all of the likely exit points with additional patrols. As a result they have not yet been able to leave. They are sitting largely defenseless as they wait for an opportunity to pass back out into State borders. Do what must be done.

Intelligence has been using an agent on an Amarr tactical relay to eavesdrop on their communications in this sector. A few days ago we lost contact with him and all reports ceased, leaving us with a giant blind spot. We assumed that our agent had been discovered and eliminated.

It seems that the problem is even worse than we feared. Intelligence intercepted a communiqué indicating that our agent was not just caught, but turned-- he's ready to tell the enemy everything he knows about our operations in this area. This must not happen.

Fortunately, at the moment he's still being held on the tactical relay, putting him within our striking distance. We need you to slip past enemy lines and destroy that relay before it's too late.

138564.en: Even the smallest of battlefields can become a focal point of a larger war when both sides refuse to back down. The localized strategic objectives of the battle can slowly fall out of view, as the fight in a particular area comes to represent the conflict at large; with both sides stubbornly fighting for a victory they believe will set the precedent for further ones.

Caldari forces have begun to deploy a cynosural field network in this sector.

In order to find the beacons comprising this network and destroy them, we need to get the records on where those beacons have been deployed. To find that, we need to get the tactical information sheet from the Caldari outpost not far from here. You'll need to fight your way to the outpost and grab the sheet. Bring it back to me as quickly as possible.

138589.en: I could have stayed around to help further, you know. Was that really all you needed done?

138590.en:
One of the key advantages we've had so far in this sector is our extensive cynosural field network, which allows us to drop our capital ships in on the enemy almost at will. The enemy, meanwhile, is forced to leave their ships vulnerable during cynosural field generation.

Unfortunately, our advantage may be crumbling. Yesterday, a task force engaging a Caldari blockade suffered serious losses when three enemy carriers dropped on them. The disturbing part is that the cynosural field was activated by a beacon, not by a Caldari ship. That means the Caldari have put up a limited cynosural field network to compete with ours. No doubt they're expanding it as fast as they can.

The network needs to be destroyed, but we need to know where those beacons have been deployed so that we can get all of them when we do a sweep. In order to do this, we want you to penetrate the security at the Caldari outpost nearby and get the tactical information sheet there. Bring it back here, and we'll have Naval Intelligence find those beacons. Understood?

The added responsibility and higher profile that comes with promotion is never without a great amount of personal risk. This is true across all the navies of the empires. Enemy Field Commanders are one of the most common targets of assassinations, and though the high honor of attaining such a rank is something countless people work towards, many do not hold the position for very long.

This is particularly true of the most brilliant commanders, who are often the first to be targeted for removal. With loyal capsuleers at their disposal, the empires are only too happy to pay large sums to have the most promising enemy commanders ruthlessly culled.

138622.en:
A few weeks ago we dispatched a small squadron of Caldari vessels that had made it inside our borders to a contested sector. We thought the job was finished and the area secure but it seems we've been duped. The entire regiment we cleared was just a decoy, and they've been massing hostiles in a nearby location.

Various sources of ours have pointed towards one of their Field Commanders being the key strategist behind these latest maneuvers. We need her assassinated.

The situation is not only embarrassing; it's undoubtedly boosted their own morale to have deceived us so effectively. We relocated all of our forces from there only days ago and re-establishing a presence will be admitting to our own people that those Federation scum outsmarted us…or one of them in particular, actually.

Various sources of ours have pointed towards one of their Field Commanders being the key strategist behind these latest maneuvers. We need her assassinated, pilot. Not only will her death impede their progress, but it should send a message to other commanders inside the State. Fly out there and make it clear to them: we have capsuleers ready and able to strike down their best and brightest. Let that be the first thought in their mind before they step up to lead fleets against our people.

In a nearby contested system, the Amarr Empire has long held illusions of claiming it entirely for themselves. Now, we've always been able to stop them, but lately they've started moving ground troops into their command outpost there.

We cannot attack the command outpost directly. It's too well guarded and our forces are kept occupied in other areas. However, if they manage to get enough ground troops there, they can launch an attack on our planetary holdings.

Our scanners have picked up a lightly guarded convoy filled with troops heading toward the command outpost. You can take them out, no sweat, right?

138673.en: If our ground forces are forced into a confrontation, thousands of lives will be lost.

138674.en: No offense, but I'd rather serve the Federation in other, more important ways. I'm not some trophy you wave around.

138675.en:
I knew you would be up for it. The convoy guards should not pose a significant challenge to you. And besides, the only real targets are the industrials carrying the ground troops. Destroy them and you can avoid fighting the other ships, unless you want to.

The main threat to your mission will be capsuleers supporting the Empire.

Capsuleers loyal to the Federation are out and about and may try to stop you.

Luckily, the gate is set to only accept ships broadcasting a specific Cartel transponder code. The Gallente have to reset both ends before they can utilize the gate.

Their repair team is at the gate now, doing the maintenance required to switch the codes. We need you to get over there and stop them immediately!
