I've been asked to find a pod pilot capable of taking out the sector commander who ordered this massacre. His battleship group is currently resupplying, and is temporarily vulnerable. It won't be easy; despite his cowardly choice of targets, he's quite capable and has a significant force at his disposal.

138708.en: I'm glad to hear it, pilot, and I'm sure the families of those lost will be, too. I'll be awaiting news of your victory.

138709.en: Excellent work, pilot. The families of the dead owe you a great debt.

138710.en: I see. I'm disappointed, pilot, but I'm glad you told me now rather than later. I'll have to see if I can find someone more capable for a mission of this import.

138711.en: You really couldn't handle it? I guess you aren't as capable as they say.

138712.en: It will be an honor to eliminate him.

138713.en: Perfect. The miners should be coming in and out of the belt. We doubt they'll be heavily defended, so you shouldn't have any problem destroying them. Capsuleers who foolishly cast their lot in with the Empire may be patrolling the area.

138714.en: That murderer won't be committing any more acts of butchery.

138715.en: I can just imagine those miners cursing the commander who sent them into hostile territory for some ore. Well, before you sent them to a fiery demise, of course.

138716.en: I don't know if I can handle this, sir. You better find someone else.

138718.en: The advent of the Starbase has seen vast changes in the nature of entrenched, long-term warfare. The tactics of battlefield logistics had to be almost entirely reinvented when forces suddenly had the capability to restock and reship inside hostile space. This process is ongoing even today, as empires discover new ways to utilize the potent abilities afforded by these structures.

138719.en: Are you worried it will be too difficult?

138720.en: Miners in a combat zone? They should see what I'm going to do to them coming!

138721.en: Those mining vessels made a very pleasing explosion.

138722.en: We've recently had to deal with some rather resilient Federation forces in a nearby contested sector. It seemed like every hard-earned victory counted for nothing; they would simply retreat, regroup and repair. We knew they had to have a Starbase somewhere to do this as effectively as they were. That Starbase has now been found. You simply need to destroy the Main Reactor powering the shields. From there we can send in a team to clear the rest out.

138723.en: Don't you have anything different for me to do?

138725.en: The Caldari State is trying to open up an old smuggler's gate belonging to Sansha's Nation. If they can get it open, they will be able to bring in overwhelming forces before we can respond. Head out there and destroy the repair ships. Just make sure you're ready for a real fight. Capsuleers loyal to the State are out and about and may try to stop you.

138727.en:
I've just received some very disturbing intelligence from my operatives inside the Caldari State. It seems that the Amarr Empire has turned over an old Sansha gate that leads into a nearby contested system. We never tore it down since Sansha's Nation doesn't bother us too often.

It looks like that has come back to bite us. The Caldari are planning on using the gate to launch an attack into our space. Luckily, the gate is set to only accept ships broadcasting a specific Sansha's transponder code. The Caldari have to reset both ends before they can utilize the gate.

Their repair team is at the gate now, doing the maintenance required to switch the codes. We need you to get over there and stop them immediately!

138728.en:
Excellent. I'll give you our top priority assignment since I know how reliable you are.

We've recently had to deal with some rather resilient Federation forces in a nearby contested sector. It seemed like every hard-earned victory counted for nothing; they would simply retreat, regroup and repair. We knew they had to have a Starbase somewhere to do this as effectively as they were. That Starbase has now been found.

I can see the look in your eyes, don't worry, we have a plan to take it down that won't involve fielding Capital vessels. You simply need to destroy the Main Reactor powering the shields. From there we can send in a team to clear the rest out.

This mission isn't without risk; you are assaulting a Starbase after all. Expect some resistance and prepare yourself accordingly. Are you up to the task?

138729.en: I'm expecting good things of you. The repair ships are only lightly guarded, with most of the enemy forces waiting to invade. However, capsuleers aligned with the State may be waiting to attack.

138730.en: You have a reputation for reliability, pilot. Don't let me see you undo all the hard work that earned it. I will find someone else, but I'm not impressed. This better be the last time you fail me.

138731.en: Excellent, I will be awaiting news of your success.

138732.en: I knew I could rely on you. Excellent work, I'll give the order to mobilize immediately. Here is your pay, take it with my gratitude.

138733.en: Unusual for you to behave like such a coward, I hope you're not starting to lose your nerve? Very well, I'll find someone else but…sort yourself out, please.

138734.en: Sounds like my kind of work. Send me the location and I'll head out there.

138735.en: Don't you realize how important this mission is? Now what will we do?

138736.en: I've destroyed the reactor; you can send our people in now.

138737.en: I'm not going up against a Starbase, even with a plan like this. You best find someone else more willing to lose their ship and crew.

138738.en: I apologize, but I won't be able to complete this mission after all. Hopefully you can find someone else in time.

138739.en: That's what I'm here for, throw me one.

138740.en: Your hesitation is disheartening. I shall find someone made of sterner stuff.

138741.en: I'll get out there right away!

138742.en: The Amarr Empire is trying to open up an old Guristas gate. Just make sure you're ready for a real fight. Capsuleers loyal to the Empire are out and about and may try to stop you.

138743.en: I've wiped the repair crew out to a man. The invasion has been stopped, for now.

138746.en: You're putting a lot on my shoulders here...

138753.en: You're putting a lot on my shoulders here...

138756.en:
The added responsibility and higher profile that comes with promotion is never without a great amount of personal risk. This is true across all the navies of the empires. Enemy Field Commanders are one of the most common targets of assassinations, and though the high honor of attaining such a rank is something countless people work towards, many do not hold the position for very long.

This is particularly true of the most brilliant commanders, who are often the first to be targeted for removal. With loyal capsuleers at their disposal, the empires are only too happy to pay large sums to have the most promising enemy commanders ruthlessly culled.

138757.en:
A few weeks ago we dispatched a small squadron of Amarrian vessels that had made it inside our borders to a contested sector. We thought the job was finished and the area secure but it seems we've been duped. The entire regiment we cleared was just a decoy, and they've been massing hostiles in a nearby location.

Various sources of ours have pointed towards one of their Field Commanders being the key strategist behind these latest maneuvers. We need her assassinated.

138759.en: I trusted you and only you with this, what am I supposed to do now? Now they know we sent some of our best and failed, you've only emboldened them further! It seems I'll have to seriously reassess your worth to us.

138760.en: I knew I could rely on you. I'll be eagerly awaiting news of your success.

138761.en: Excellent work, pilot. That should leave it clear to aspiring commanders just what exactly their promotion brings.

138762.en: A disappointing remark, especially coming from one such as you. A million brave deeds in good times cannot compare to a single act made when everything has begun to fall apart.

138763.en: Understood. I'll make sure she's made an example of.

138764.en: The Field Commander and her guards are dead.

138765.en: I'm not here to clean up the mistakes of others, find someone else.

138766.en: She's too well defended I'm afraid. I can't get to her.

138767.en: Of course. How can I serve?

138768.en: I could have stayed around to help further, you know. Was that really all you needed done?

138769.en: Yes, it helped more than I think you realize, we couldn't get to their Commander as quickly and effectively as you. Your actions freed us up to identify and remove the rest of their chain of command. We'll come away with the victory we needed, despite some heavy losses. Let our mistake be a lesson for you, pilot. Good work today though, here's your pay.

138770.en: Even the smallest of battlefields can become a focal point of a larger war when both sides refuse to back down. The localized strategic objectives of the battle can slowly fall out of view, as the fight in a particular area comes to represent the conflict at large; with both sides stubbornly fighting for a victory they believe will set the precedent for further ones.

138771.en: We're about to launch an operation in a heavily contested sector where we've seen mixed success recently. We'll be targeting one of the Amarrian Empire's largest ship logistics depots in an effort to halt their progress. You'll fly over there, hang at the back of the fighting and show them we even brought capsuleers to deal with their puny forces. I may have orders for you but I doubt it, though I still want you on standby just in case.

138773.en:
I did, I need you to support some forces of ours in the way only a capsuleer can.

We're about to launch an operation in a heavily contested sector where we've seen mixed success recently. We'll be targeting one of the Amarrian Empire's largest ship logistics depots in an effort to halt their progress. If we can remove their ability to repair and re-supply then we can push the advantage and hopefully clear them out of there altogether.

Admittedly, they've been a tough opponent so far and we've suffered some heavy losses. We're not taking any chances this time however, we need to come away with a victory today. That's why we've called in additional numbers…lots of them. Victory is all but assured this time but I want more than just success today, I want those slaver scum utterly crushed and left without hope. I want them reeling from this defeat. That's where you come in.

You'll fly over there, hang at the back of the fighting and show them we even brought capsuleers to deal with their puny forces. I may have orders for you but I doubt it, though I still want you on standby just in case. You're there simply to crush their morale, to show them that no matter what they brought, their defeat was inevitable. It's an easy assignment, pilot; you should have no problem with it.

138774.en: Your lack of commitment does a great disservice to your reputation, pilot. I suggest you not repeat this mistake.  You are known for your loyalty and reliability, do not unravel all that hard work.

138775.en: Good, I'm relaying the coordinates now. Be on standby once you get there, I may still have some targets of opportunity for you.

138776.en: Yes, it helped more than I think you realize, we couldn't get to their Commander as quickly and effectively as you. 138778.en: Then you do not understand your own importance, pilot. The mere presence of a capsuleer on the field can fill an entire fleet with terror. I'm disappointed that you cannot see the value in a mission such as this. Oh well, I'll make other arrangements.

138779.en: Sure, sounds easy enough. I'll head out immediately.

138780.en: No offense, but I'd rather serve the Republic in other, more important ways. I'm not some trophy you wave around.

138781.en: I won't be able to help with this after all, something more important than a chest-beating mission came up and I'm giving it priority.

138782.en: That's why I'm talking to you. Did you have some work for me?

138783.en:
Despite the frequent death of civilians in a war, it is nonetheless exceptionally rare for large-scale casualties to happen without even a shred of reason. Engineers, mechanics, scientists, these and other professions – when used directly to aid combatant forces – can be said to have justifiably draw the wrath of their enemies. There just enough shades of grey to allow it.

No empire, however, is foolish enough to outright murder citizens without any involvement in a conflict. Or as some might argue, they are not so foolish as to get caught in the act. The rise of the capsuleer has spawned a dark new age where culpability is little more than an elusive dream.

138784.en: Very recently, we spotted a huge transport fleet carrying thousands upon thousands of Amarrians towards our borders. We let them enter, pretending as always that we had not noticed. This time however, we reinforced all of the likely exit points with additional patrols. As a result they have not yet been able to leave. They are sitting largely defenseless as they wait for an opportunity to pass back out into Empire borders. Do what must be done.

138786.en:
Good, listen carefully. The Amarrians have been moving their own citizens through our space, shuttling them back home from distant and lawless frontiers. We've been watching this for some time now and for the most part, simply ignoring it. Predictable as they are, we knew the appearance of lax border security would embolden them and this is precisely what has happened.

Very recently, we spotted a huge transport fleet carrying thousands upon thousands of their people towards our borders. We let them enter, pretending as always that we had not noticed. This time however, we reinforced all of the likely exit points with additional patrols. As a result they have not yet been able to leave.

They are currently holed up in a nearby contested sector, where Amarrian forces will offer them some protection, but only a little. They are sitting largely defenseless as they wait for an opportunity to pass back out into Empire borders. I will give you those coordinates if you can promise me you will do something useful with them.

Am I being understood here, pilot?

138787.en: Your loyalty has been tested and found lacking, along with your resolve. I can only hope that your discretion does not follow the same path, it would be a shame to lose such a capable pilot.

138788.en: Uploading them now. Do what must be done.

138789.en: I knew you could be trusted. Here is your payment, take it with my thanks.

138790.en: Very well. See that you do a good job of pretending. I would hate to see someone like yourself in the sort of trouble that leaking this information would land you in.

138793.en: I'm just going to pretend I never had this conversation.

138794.en: I've had a change of heart. I cannot do what I think it is you want me to.

138795.en: I'm ready for anything, you can count on my discretion.

138796.en: Your mission will be to slip past enemy lines and destroy the Minmatar tactical relay and the spy on board. With him out of the way, our intelligence network in this sector should remain secure and the war effort will not be seriously threatened by his capture. Haste is of utmost importance, so don't waste any time.

138797.en:
Intelligence has been using an agent on a Minmatar tactical relay to eavesdrop on their communications in this sector. A few days ago we lost contact with him and all reports ceased, leaving us with a giant blind spot. We assumed that our agent had been discovered and eliminated.

It seems that the problem is even worse than we feared. Intelligence intercepted a communiqué indicating that our agent was not just caught, but turned-- he's ready to tell the enemy everything he knows about our operations in this area. This must not happen.

Fortunately, at the moment he's still being held on the tactical relay, putting him within our striking distance. We need you to slip past enemy lines and destroy that relay before it's too late.

138798.en: You have hurt us deeply here, pilot; I hope you realize that.

138799.en: Good. Don't take any chances; that relay is our top priority. Everything else is a secondary target.

138800.en: Superb work, pilot. I'll make sure your name gets mentioned up the chain.

138801.en: We're all in this war together, pilot, or we're all in deep trouble. You need to realize that sooner rather than later.

138802.en: Executing that traitor will be my honor. Don't worry, I'll make sure he's taken care of.

138803.en: The tactical relay has been eliminated.

138804.en: Look, I don't feel like cleaning up someone else's mess here. Find someone else to do your dirty work.

138806.en:
A Minmatar task force destroyed a civilian convoy fleeing the front lines. Included in the missing and presumed dead are the daughter of a prominent Holder and her family, and the general staff is outraged by the attack. We must have revenge for this brutal massacre.

The sector commander responsible for ordering the attack is currently resupplying, leaving him temporarily vulnerable. We don't intend to let him get away. Fly to the base at the coordinates you've been given and make sure the sector commander does not survive. Any other targets are secondary, but don't hold back. Show these bastards the wrath of the righteous.

138807.en:
I've just received word that a fleeing civilian convoy was destroyed by the Minmatar, pilot. There were over two thousand fatalities before a Navy search-and-rescue force was able to reach the scene and recover the survivors.

In addition to the utter disregard for human life that this act displayed, evidently the daughter of a prominent Holder and her family were on board one of the industrial ships with the convoy. They are still missing, but the Navy isn't hopeful that they will be found. We are outraged, and they want to show those terrorists that they can't get away with this kind of butchery.

I've been asked to find a pod pilot capable of taking out the sector commander who ordered this massacre. His battleship group is currently resupplying, and is temporarily vulnerable. It won't be easy; despite his cowardly choice of targets, he's quite capable and has a significant force at his disposal.

138808.en: I'm glad to hear it, pilot, and I'm sure the families of those lost will be, too. I'll be awaiting news of your victory.

138809.en: Excellent work, pilot. The families of the dead owe you a great debt.

138810.en: I see. I'm disappointed, pilot, but I'm glad you told me now rather than later. I'll have to see if I can find someone more capable for a mission of this import.

138811.en: It will be an honor to eliminate him.

138812.en: That murderer won't be committing any more acts of butchery.

138813.en: I don't know if I can handle this, sir. You better find someone else.

138815.en:
Minmatar forces have begun to deploy a cynosural field network in this sector.

In order to find the beacons comprising this network and destroy them, we need to get the records on where those beacons have been deployed. To find that, we need to get the tactical information sheet from the Minmatar outpost not far from here. You'll need to fight your way to the outpost and grab the sheet. Bring it back to me as quickly as possible.

138816.en:
One of the key advantages we've had so far in this sector is our extensive cynosural field network, which allows us to drop our capital ships in on the enemy almost at will. The enemy, meanwhile, is forced to leave their ships vulnerable during cynosural field generation.

Unfortunately, our advantage may be crumbling. Yesterday, a task force engaging a Minmatar blockade suffered serious losses when three enemy carriers dropped on them. The disturbing part is that the cynosural field was activated by a beacon, not by a Minmatar ship. That means the Minmatar have put up a limited cynosural field network to compete with ours. No doubt they're expanding it as fast as they can.

The network needs to be destroyed, but we need to know where those beacons have been deployed so that we can get all of them when we do a sweep. In order to do this, we want you to penetrate the security at the Minmatar outpost nearby and get the tactical information sheet there. Bring it back here, and we'll have Naval Intelligence find those beacons. Understood?

138817.en: You're setting our entire war effort back weeks, pilot. If you can't carry out missions, then you're no use to us. You'd better work a little harder in the future.

138818.en: : I'll be looking forward to hearing from you. Don't let me down.

138819.en: Good work, pilot. I'll get that to Naval Intelligence right away.

138820.en: If you won't do it, I'll have to find someone else who will.

138821.en: I'll get that intelligence. You can count on me.

138822.en: I've managed to get the tactical information sheet you needed. I hope it helps.

138823.en: I'm going to sit this one out.

138824.en: I can't do this; it's way over my head. You're going to have to find someone else.

138825.en: Of course. I'm always ready to do my part for the war effort.

138826.en:
The Minmatar Republic is building up its ground troops in a nearby contested system with plans to launch an attack on our fortified positions.

We've discovered a troop transport moving toward their command outpost. You need merely destroy the industrials and don't need to bother with the convoy guards.

138827.en:
In a nearby contested system, the Minmatar Republic has long held illusions of claiming it entirely for themselves. Now, we've always been able to stop them, but lately they've started moving ground troops into their command outpost there.

We cannot attack the command outpost directly. It's too well guarded and our forces are kept occupied in other areas. However, if they manage to get enough ground troops there, they can launch an attack on our planetary holdings.

Our scanners have picked up a lightly guarded convoy filled with troops heading toward the command outpost. You can take them out, no sweat, right?

138828.en: If our ground forces are forced into a confrontation, thousands of lives will be lost.

138829.en:
I knew you would be up for it. The convoy guards should not pose a significant challenge to you. And besides, the only real targets are the industrials carrying the ground troops. Destroy them and you can avoid fighting the other ships, unless you want to.

The main threat to your mission will be capsuleers supporting the Republic.

138830.en: With their troops eliminated, we'll be able to reinforce our own positions. And maybe soon, we'll be able to push forward and overwhelm the Minmatar positions as well! Just another step towards victory! Excellent work.

138831.en: You would really turn down my offer? I'm not sure you know the severity of this mission.

138832.en: I'll make sure those troops never reach their destinations!

138833.en: The troop transports have been destroyed. The Empire need not fear any longer!

138834.en: Anyone can take out a few transports! Why can't you give me something more substantial?

138835.en: Yipes! That didn't turn out as easy as I hoped. I'm going to have to quit.

138836.en: Serving the Empire is serving the side of right!

138837.en:
Good news, follower! We've just discovered the Republic doing something incredibly foolish! It turns out they've been sending in miners to a nearby contested system. The impudence! Did they think they could do this right under our noses and we wouldn't notice? I hope they're ready to pay for their folly.

I want you to be the one to make them pay. Our normal forces are occupied with other objectives. I'd like you to head over there and take out those miners. It will deny the Minmatar a large amount of precious mineral resources. What do you say?

138838.en: You really couldn't handle it? I guess you aren't as capable as they say.

138839.en: Perfect. The miners should be coming in and out of the belt. We doubt they'll be heavily defended, so you shouldn't have any problem destroying them. Capsuleers who foolishly cast their lot in with the Republic may be patrolling the area.

138840.en: I can just imagine those miners cursing the commander who sent them into hostile territory for some ore. Well, before you sent them to a fiery demise, of course.

138841.en: Are you worried it will be too difficult?

138842.en: Miners in a combat zone? They should see what I'm going to do to them coming!

138843.en: Those mining vessels made a very pleasing explosion.

138844.en: Don't you have anything different for me to do?

138847.en: The Minmatar Republic is trying to open up an old smuggler's gate belonging to the Serpentis. If they can get it open, they will be able to bring in overwhelming forces before we can respond. Head out there and destroy the repair ships. Just make sure you're ready for a real fight. Capsuleers loyal to the Republic are out and about and may try to stop you.

138851.en: Your hesitation is disheartening. I shall find someone made of sterner stuff.

138852.en: I'll get out there right away!

138853.en: I've wiped the repair crew out to a man. The invasion has been stopped, for now.

138854.en: You're putting a lot on my shoulders here...

138855.en: I don't know how to say this, but I've been beaten. You'll need to find someone else to complete things.

138859.en:
We have a serious situation on our hands, pilot.

A few weeks ago we dispatched a small squadron of Minmatar vessels that had made it inside our borders to a contested sector. We thought the job was finished and the area secure but it seems we've been duped. The entire regiment we cleared was just a decoy, and they've been massing hostiles in a nearby location with the use of covert technology.

The situation is not only embarrassing; it's undoubtedly boosted their own morale to have deceived us so effectively. We relocated all of our forces from there only days ago and re-establishing a presence will be admitting to our own people that those Federation scum outsmarted us…or one of them in particular, actually.

Various sources of ours have pointed towards one of their Field Commanders being the key strategist behind these latest maneuvers. We need her assassinated, pilot. Not only will her death impede their progress, but it should send a message to other commanders inside the Republic. Fly out there and make it clear to them: we have capsuleers ready and able to strike down their best and brightest. Let that be the first thought in their mind before they step up to lead fleets against our people.

138860.en: I trusted you and only you with this, what am I supposed to do now? Now they know we sent some of our best and failed, you've only emboldened them further! It seems I'll have to seriously reassess your worth to us.

138870.en: We're about to launch an operation in a heavily contested sector where we've seen mixed success recently. We'll be targeting one of the Minmatar Republic's largest ship logistics depots in an effort to halt their progress. You'll fly over there, hang at the back of the fighting and show them we even brought capsuleers to deal with their puny forces. I may have orders for you but I doubt it, though I still want you on standby just in case.

138872.en:
I did, I need you to support some forces of ours in the way only a capsuleer can.

We're about to launch an operation in a heavily contested sector where we've seen mixed success recently. We'll be targeting one of the Minmatar Republic's largest ship logistics depots in an effort to halt their progress. If we can remove their ability to repair and re-supply then we can push the advantage and hopefully clear them out of there altogether.

Admittedly, they've been a tough opponent so far and we've suffered some heavy losses. We're not taking any chances this time however, we need to come away with a victory today. That's why we've called in additional numbers…lots of them. Victory is all but assured this time but I want more than just success today, I want those savages utterly crushed and left without hope. I want them reeling from this defeat. That's where you come in.

You'll fly over there, hang at the back of the fighting and show them we even brought capsuleers to deal with their puny forces. I may have orders for you but I doubt it, though I still want you on standby just in case. You're there simply to crush their morale, to show them that no matter what they brought, their defeat was inevitable. It's an easy assignment, pilot; you should have no problem with it.

138873.en: Your lack of commitment does a great disservice to your reputation, pilot. I suggest you not repeat this mistake.  You are known for your loyalty and reliability, do not unravel all that hard work.

138874.en: Good, I'm relaying the coordinates now. Be on standby once you get there, I may still have some targets of opportunity for you.

138875.en: I could have stayed around to help further, you know. Was that really all you needed done?

138876.en: Then you do not understand your own importance, pilot. The mere presence of a capsuleer on the field can fill an entire fleet with terror. I'm disappointed that you cannot see the value in a mission such as this. Oh well, I'll make other arrangements.

138877.en: Sure, sounds easy enough. I'll head out immediately.

138878.en: Yes, it helped more than I think you realize, we couldn't get to their Commander as quickly and effectively as you. Your actions freed us up to identify and remove the rest of their chain of command. We'll come away with the victory we needed, despite some heavy losses. Let our mistake be a lesson for you, pilot. Good work today though, here's your pay.

138879.en: No offense, but I'd rather serve the Empire in other, more important ways. I'm not some trophy you wave around.

138880.en: I won't be able to help with this after all, something more important than a chest-beating mission came up and I'm giving it priority.

138881.en: That's why I'm talking to you. Did you have some work for me?

138882.en:
Despite the frequent death of civilians in a war, it is nonetheless exceptionally rare for large-scale casualties to happen without even a shred of reason. Engineers, mechanics, scientists, these and other professions – when used directly to aid combatant forces – can be said to have justifiably draw the wrath of their enemies. There just enough shades of grey to allow it.

No empire, however, is foolish enough to outright murder citizens without any involvement in a conflict. Or as some might argue, they are not so foolish as to get caught in the act. The rise of the capsuleer has spawned a dark new age where culpability is little more than an elusive dream.

138883.en: Very recently, we spotted a huge transport fleet carrying thousands upon thousands of Minmatar towards our borders. We let them enter, pretending as always that we had not noticed. This time however, we reinforced all of the likely exit points with additional patrols. As a result they have not yet been able to leave. They are sitting largely defenseless as they wait for an opportunity to pass back out into Republic borders. Do what must be done.

138885.en:
Good, listen carefully.

The Minmatar have been moving their own citizens through our space, shuttling them back home from distant and lawless frontiers. We've been watching this for some time now and for the most part, simply ignoring it. Predictable as they are, we knew the appearance of lax border security would embolden them and this is precisely what has happened.

Very recently, we spotted a huge transport fleet carrying thousands upon thousands of their people towards our borders. We let them enter, pretending as always that we had not noticed. This time however, we reinforced all of the likely exit points with additional patrols. As a result they have not yet been able to leave.

They are currently holed up in a nearby contested sector, where Minmatar forces will offer them some protection, but only a little. They are sitting largely defenseless as they wait for an opportunity to pass back out into Republic borders. I will give you those coordinates if you can promise me you will do something useful with them.

Am I being understood here, pilot?

138886.en: Your loyalty and faith has been tested and found lacking, along with your resolve. I can only hope that your discretion does not follow the same path, it would be a shame to lose such a capable pilot.

138887.en: Uploading them now. Do what must be done. Go with God's blessing, pilot.

138888.en: I knew you could be trusted. Here is your payment, take it with my thanks.

138889.en: Very well. See that you do a good job of pretending. I would hate to see someone like yourself in the sort of trouble that leaking this information would land you in.

138892.en: I'm just going to pretend I never had this conversation.

138893.en: I've had a change of heart. I cannot do what I think it is you want me to.

138894.en: I'm ready for anything, you can count on my discretion.

138895.en:
We've spotted an unauthorized Blood Raider personnel transport flying through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Cargo scanners revealed a load of militants on board, no doubt a part of a ground force intended to strike a target near here. We don't know where they are headed or what they're up to, but we definitely want to find out. I request that you intercept the transport and capture the men on board. Bring them back to us for questioning.

We believe the escort team is split up into a few groups. If you strike fast and hard, you'll probably avoid getting swarmed by them all at once. Just keep a look out for any stray ships; we don't want them escaping back to their home base to report the incident.

138896.en:
Because of the importance placed on "saving face" in Caldari culture, mid- and high-level executives often remain employed despite failures in leadership or performance, simply because firing them publicly would damage the corporation's reputation. In extreme cases, it is not altogether unknown for superiors within the corporation to arrange "accidents" for executives who fail to meet objectives and threaten their employer's bottom line. This eliminates the drain on corporate resources and allows them to save face.

While such methods of dealing with "problem employees" are simply not discussed openly (doing so would be in horribly poor taste, after all), it is something that lurks in the back of every corporate executive's mind.

138897.en:
Boosters are made by processing chemicals extracted from special gas clouds that can be found in certain deadspace areas in many regions. Some constellations, such as E-8CSQ, 09-4XW, 9HXQ-G, OK-FEM, Pegasus, Assilot, I-3ODK, and 760-9C, however, are rumored to have massive clouds of a scale not seen anywhere else. Finding these clouds requires the ability to conduct long-range scanning, for example via scan probes. Finding them is not always an easy task, though; it sometimes requires quite a bit of exploration.

The downside of searching for these clouds is the fact that they are generally located in dangerous pirate-infested space. Few if any of these clouds exist in civilized space, having been depleted long ago by the mega-corporations. Hence, searching for them can be quite risky and is not recommended for any but the most experienced combat pilots.

To extract the chemicals from the gas clouds, you need a gas cloud harvester module. You also need to find the correct type of gas cloud. Not all clouds have chemicals that the gas cloud harvester can extract, and therefore you might have to go through some trial and error at first before you get the hang of gas cloud harvesting.

Today, most boosters are very much illegal in civilized space, due to the horrible side-effects experienced by users during the Great Booster Craze many decades ago. Manufacturing them must therefore be done in lawless space, outside the spheres of power of the major civilized factions. Similarly, anyone caught smuggling illegal boosters into civilized space can face very steep penalties.

Manufacturing boosters can broken into a few phases. Phase 1 involves extracting the material from the gas cloud. Phase 2 requires a refinery structure with the appropriate service module to process the chemicals and create reactions. Phase 3 also requires a structure or station with the equipment for booster manufacturing to process the reaction and create the booster. This simple 3-step process will result in the creation of a fairly common booster. With additional work, the right blueprint, and a combination of several low-quality boosters, one can create higher-quality versions.

138898.en: The advent of the Starbase has seen vast changes in the nature of entrenched, long-term warfare. The tactics of battlefield logistics had to be almost entirely reinvented when forces suddenly had the capability to restock and reship inside hostile space. This process is ongoing even today, as empires discover new ways to utilize the potent abilities afforded by these structures.

138899.en: We've recently had to deal with some rather resilient Caldari forces in a nearby contested sector. It seemed like every hard-earned victory counted for nothing; they would simply retreat, regroup and repair. We knew they had to have a Starbase somewhere to do this as effectively as they were. That Starbase has now been found. You simply need to destroy the Main Reactor powering the shields. From there we can send in a team to clear the rest out.

138901.en:
Excellent. I'll give you our top priority assignment since I know how reliable you are.

We've recently had to deal with some rather resilient Caldari forces in a nearby contested sector. It seemed like every hard-earned victory counted for nothing; they would simply retreat, regroup and repair. We knew they had to have a Starbase somewhere to do this as effectively as they were. That Starbase has now been found.

I can see the look in your eyes, don't worry, we have a plan to take it down that won't involve fielding Capital vessels. You simply need to destroy the Main Reactor powering the shields. From there we can send in a team to clear the rest out.

This mission isn't without risk; you are assaulting a Starbase after all. Expect some resistance and prepare yourself accordingly. Are you up to the task?

138907.en: Excellent, I will be awaiting news of your success.

138908.en: I knew I could rely on you. Excellent work, I'll give the order to mobilize immediately. Here is your pay, take it with my gratitude.

138909.en: Unusual for you to behave like such a coward, I hope you're not starting to lose your nerve? Very well, I'll find someone else but…sort yourself out, please.

138910.en: Sounds like my kind of work. Send me the location and I'll head out there.

138911.en: I've destroyed the reactor; you can send our people in now.

138912.en: I'm not going up against a Starbase, even with a plan like this. You best find someone else more willing to lose their ship and crew.

138913.en: I apologize, but I won't be able to complete this mission after all. Hopefully you can find someone else in time.

138914.en: That's what I'm here for, throw me one.

138937.en: We've been watching Federation Navy units piling into a contested sector nearby. We were moments away from moving on them until we noticed one of their more highly-ranked Field Commanders arriving on the scene. This woman has killed countless Caldari; most of them non-combatants I no longer give a damn about anything except that Commander and her guards. Kill them and you'll get your pay, maybe even some respect.

138938.en:
I knew you would be up for it. The convoy guards should not pose a significant challenge to you. And besides, the only real targets are the industrials carrying the ground troops. Destroy them and you can avoid fighting the other ships, unless you want to.

The main threat to your mission will be capsuleers supporting the Federation.

138939.en: Excellent. Without supplies, the Caldari forces in the area will lose morale and fight at less than 100 percent! It'll allow us to make inroads into the system.

138940.en:
The Minmatar Republic has located numerous hidden asteroid belts that our miners use to provide resources for the war effort. Usually, they don't get touched by anyone except us and the people we send out there... even if they're not technically in Republic space. However, it seems the Amarr Empire has sent some miners into one of our fields in an area of space they consider theirs; while we've been busy with other things, they've been sneaking in and mining our ore!

This is unacceptable. I've uploaded the location of the belt to your NeoCom. I want you to go out there and destroy those miners and show them that we're always watching. Just prepare yourself for any pod pilots working for the Amarr. They're sure to be in the area.

138941.en:
Amarr has located numerous hidden asteroid belts that we mine for the betterment of the Empire. Usually, these locations are known only to us... even if they're not technically in our sovereign space. However, it seems the Minmatar have sent some miners into one of our fields in an area of space they consider "theirs"; while we've been busy with other things, they've been sneaking in and mining our ore!

This situation is unacceptable. I've uploaded the location of the belt to your NeoCom. I want you to go out there and destroy those miners and show them that the Empire is always watching. Just prepare yourself for any pod pilots working for the Matari scum: They're sure to be in the area.

138942.en:
The State has numerous asteroid belts secreted away, from which our miners provide resources for the war effort. Usually, these sites don't get touched by anyone except us and the companies we contract out to mine them. However, it seems the Gallente have recently sent some miners in to steal our asteroids. This is unacceptable.

I've uploaded the location of the belt to your NeoCom. I want you to go out there and destroy those miners; show them that we're always vigilant. Just be ready for any Federation-sponsored pod pilots: They've been reported in the area.

138943.en:
The Federation has located numerous asteroid belts hidden away all over charted space. Usually, these sites are so out of the way that they're rarely found, let alone touched by anyone except us. But it seems the Caldari State has found one of them and sent some miners in to steal those asteroids: Those capitalist pigs have been sneaking in and mining our ore!

As you can see, this situation is entirely unacceptable. I've uploaded the location of the belt to your NeoCom -- I want you to go out there and destroy those miners. Show them that the Federation will not tolerate such acts. Just be wary of any pod pilots working for the State. They'll almost certainly attack you on sight.

138944.en:
Uncountable numbers of hidden asteroid belts dot all of known space; some of them are quite valuable -- so much that both we and our enemies would risk going into contested space to find and exploit them. The Minmatar have recently sent miners into a rich field we discovered some time ago -- in a region of "contested space" -- and we certainly can't have them taking our ore.

If you can drive them out of there, we'll have those precious mineral resources all to ourselves. Can you do it?

138945.en:
Our scanners haven't revealed any combat ships escorting the miners. That could be simple hubris on the part of the Gallente, or it could mean they've reinforcements a short way away. The miners are the only important targets, so focus on them.

Just be careful, as I said earlier -- capsuleers loyal to the Federation are in the area.

138946.en:
It's no secret that many hidden asteroid belts dot all of known space. Some of them are so valuable that our people would risk going into contested space to find and exploit them. Well, we've recently done just that -- we discovered a fairly sizable asteroid belt. In Gallente-contested space...

Trouble is, the Gallente seem to have noticed. But we simply can't let them take it: If you can drive them out of there, we'll send in a special ops mining force and have those precious mineral resources all to ourselves. Can you do it?

138947.en:
Our scanners haven't revealed any combat ships escorting the miners. That could be simple hubris on the part of the Caldari, or it could mean they've reinforcements a short way away. The miners are the only important targets, so focus on them.

Again, be careful -- capsuleers loyal to the State are in the area.

138948.en:
Those damn Caldari have managed to discover an asteroid belt we had claimed in one of the contested systems nearby! Head over there and destroy them as soon as possible. Once you do, we can exploit the resources ourselves.

Just make sure you're ready to fight. Capsuleers loyal to the State might be out in force.

138949.en:
As you know, there are a large number of hidden asteroid belts all throughout space. Some of them are quite valuable, so much that both we and our enemies would risk going into contested space to find them. Well, we've recently done just that... but the Caldari have apparently spotted our ships in the vicinity.

We discovered a fairly sizable asteroid belt that had managed to elude our scanners for some time. Now that the Caldari have also pinpointed it, though, we need to get in there fast. We simply can't let them strip it of all value. We want to be the ones to do that. If you can drive them out of there, we'll have those precious mineral resources all to ourselves -- and keep their war-mongering fingers away from it. Can you do it?

138950.en:
Our scanners haven't revealed any combat ships escorting the miners. That could be simple hubris on the part of the Amarr, or it could mean they've reinforcements a short way away. The miners are the only important targets, so focus on them.

Just be careful out there, like I said.

138951.en:
It's no secret that a large number of hidden asteroid belts dot all parts of space, including the Republic -- and Amarr. Some of them are quite valuable, so much that we would most certainly risk going into Amarr space to procure them. Well, our scouts recently found just such a field in Amarr-contested space.

They've discovered a fairly sizable asteroid belt. Now that we've pinpointed it, though, the Amarr seem to have noticed our activities there... and we simply can't let them strip the site of all those resources. If you can drive them out of there, we'll have those precious minerals all to ourselves. Can you do it?

138953.en: Miners in a combat zone? Don't they know what could happen to them? They should see it coming!

138954.en: It looks like the State likes to send its citizens into dangerous territory to mine. Well, their stupidity is to our benefit. All you have to do is head over there and blow up the mining vessels, then report back to us. The miners and any escort they have should pose no problem to you. However, capsuleers loyal to the State are in the area; they might prove difficult.

138955.en: I can just imagine those miners cursing the commander who sent them into hostile territory for some ore. Just before you sent them to a fiery demise, of course.

138956.en:
Good news, follower! We've just discovered the State doing something incredibly foolish! It turns out they've been sending miners into a contested system for ore. The impudence! Did they think they could do this with impunity!? I hope they're ready to pay for their folly.

I want you to be the one to make them pay. Our normal forces are occupied with other objectives. I'd like you to head over there and take out those miners. It will deny the Caldari a large amount of precious mineral resources. What do you say?

138957.en: Miners in a combat zone? How can they be so stupid?!

138958.en: It seems the Federation likes to send its citizens into hostile territory to mine. Ah, well. Their mistake. And to our benefit. All you have to do is head over there and blow up the mining vessels, then report back to us. The miners and any escort they have should pose no problem to you. However, capsuleers loyal to the Federation are likely to be in the area, and they might prove more difficult.

138959.en: The Empire has made a mistake. A really dumb one: They've sent miners out into hostile territory for ore. What's their stupidity is to our benefit. Just head over there and blow up the mining vessels, then report back to us. The miners and any escort they have should pose no problem to you. However, some Amarrian capsuleers have been spotted in the area, so be ready for a firefight.

138960.en:
Good news, follower! We've just discovered the Empire doing something incredibly foolish! It turns out they've been sending in miners to a contested system near their sovereign space. I hope they're ready to pay for their folly.

I want you to be the one to make them pay. Our normal forces are occupied with other objectives: I'd like you to head over there and take out those miners. Not only will it deny Amarr a large amount of precious mineral resources, it will also sting their sickening pride. What do you say?

138961.en: The Republic has sent workers into hostile territory to mine asteroids. Well, their foolish overconfidence is to our benefit. All you have to do is head over there and blow up the mining vessels, then report back to us. The miners and any escort they have should pose no problem to you; however, the Republic capsuleers in the area might prove difficult. Be ready.

138963.en: I hope it wasn't too much trouble for you. With that repair crew out of the way, we can take our time and send a demolition crew to destroy it when we get the chance. You have done the State proud.

138964.en:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} surveillance spotted a small team of Thukker mercenaries in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, probably up to no good. They're wanted men, and need to be taken care of. I would ask you to bring them in for trial but that really isn't necessary, the exception being their captain. I want him taken alive and brought to me. We'd like to figure out exactly what they've been up to.

Your objectives in this mission are not as simple as they sound, however. We haven't been able to locate their captain's hideout yet. but we expect him to show up if you warp to some of his minions who are holed up in a small asteroid belt in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. So I suggest you destroy the first group of mercenaries you encounter as fast as you can, before more reinforcements arrive, or you'll have a heck of a battle on your hands.

138968.en:
Moments ago we launched an offensive against a Caldari compound inside a hostile sector where they have strong numbers and superior logistics support.

Initial reconnaissance has suggested they may have the capability to field more vessels than we had originally anticipated. Naturally, we're not turning around in the face of this news, we've come too far and a retreat will only encourage them. We're not going to risk getting slaughtered however, and this is where you come in.

I want you to fly over there and ensure the success of this operation. I'll personally relay further information to you once you've made it onto the field. Don't worry about any orders or cohesion with our own forces there, you'll be answering directly to me and following only my orders.

Briefing over. Get going.

138969.en:
We've learned that the remaining Athrans pulled out as soon as you left your last mission. Fortunately, one of our recon pilots was able to trail them to another location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

{[character]player.name}, head out there and find out what's going on. See what these Athrans are up to, and report any suspicious activity back to me. And if they open fire on you again, you're fully authorized to shoot back. Don't take any chances.

138970.en:
Today is a day of mourning, {[character]player.name}. One of our most esteemed officers was brutally murdered by Sansha scum. He had been in the forefront of our campaign to rid {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} space of those filthy pirate dogs, and now he is dead. We will miss his services to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} greatly, and I hope to see you at his funeral, {[character]player.name}.

Now to the point. This great injustice demands retribution, and you will be the deliverer of our wrath. We know of a Sansha Outpost lurking in the fringes of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and you are to find it and destroy it. I'll supply you with a bookmark that should take you to an acceleration gate leading to it. Once there, your task is to completely obliterate their base. However be warned, their outpost is heavily guarded, I suggest you clear the guards before attempting to destroy the Outpost structure itself. Good luck.

138980.en:
The easiest way to travel to a destination station quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group. Once you have selected "stargate" in the Overview settings, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in the mission details in your Opportunities interface and choose "set destination." You will notice that the applicable stargate in your Overview is now yellow, as well as the one in space that leads to the next system along your route.

Next, simply right-click on the yellow stargate in the Overview (or in space) and hit "warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot and simply sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

Once you have arrived in the correct star system, simply right-click anywhere in space. In the drop-down window that appears, your current mission information appears at the bottom. From there, select the "dock" option and your Autopilot will bring you into the station momentarily.

Once the weapons are delivered, return to your agent's home station (also available via the drop-down simply by right-clicking anywhere in space) to collect your reward.

138981.en:
Quafe has been secretly developing a new soft drink called Quafe Unleashed that they say will revolutionize the entire soft drink industry. But only hours ago, the formula was stolen. Security records show that a Quafe employee, a guy called Quince Nemirda, has just left the station with the top-secret formula in his possession. Quafe representatives believe that he might be on his way to try to sell or deliver the formula to one of Quafe's competitors, and have offered a reward for the recovery of the formula.

We were able to track him for a while, and we've just heard that he's now in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. I‘ll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom. Stop him before he meets his contact, and bring back the formula.

We're not expecting you to go to war for this, but you should be prepared to meet some rough customers.

138982.en:
I just received an emergency communication from an insider in the Quafe Corporation. Perhaps you've heard of them, the single biggest soft drink manufacturer in the galaxy? Yes, they're a filthy Gallente corporation, but the political clout they garnered after their peace-brokering in the Girani-Fa incident gave them some pull, even in our space.

Anyway, Quafe has been secretly developing a new soft drink called Quafe Unleashed that they say will revolutionize the entire soft drink industry. They've been developing it here because, since this isn't their corporate headquarters, news of their efforts would be less likely to leak out.

But only hours ago, the formula was stolen. Security records show that a Quafe employee, a guy called Quince Nemirda, has just left the station with the top-secret formula in his possession. Quafe representatives believe that he might be on his way to try to sell or deliver the formula to one of Quafe's competitors, and have offered a reward for the recovery of the formula.

We could make big points if we could find Nemirda. We were able to track him for a while, and we've just heard that he's now in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. I‘ll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom. Stop him before he meets his contact, and bring back the formula.

Oh, and make sure you keep this to yourself. Quafe doesn't want it to get out that this formula even exists.

138987.en: The Darkonnen is an organization that sprung up from rogue elements within the Khanid Kingdom, starting off as a small band of smugglers operating between lawless space and Khanid-controlled territory. They were renowned for their ruthlessness in dealing with their competitors, eliminating a good deal of small-time criminals within the Kingdom, as well as cleverly eluding the local authorities most of the time. A few years ago, their founder and leader, Michelin Adonnis, was captured by Khanid secret police and sentenced to life in prison for various offenses. His arrest caused a slight setback for the outlawed organization, but in the end it turned out to be not enough to halt their inevitable expansion. Today they are a well known pirate/smuggler network who base their operations in numerous systems in Amarr and Khanid space.

138988.en:
The freighter Bright Prospect struck an asteroid when emerging from warp in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The jump drive was badly damaged and they thought it might blow, but they managed to make it back in one piece. However, among the cargo, which was mostly expendable, was a set of important Ishukone corporate records; they were forced to jettison the records lest they be lost if the ship's warp core blew. We don't have backups, so the records are irreplaceable.

We need someone to get out there and recover those records. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed, as well as my gratitude.

I've uploaded the location of the Bright Prospect's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and bring them back to me here.

138989.en:
You look pretty green to me, youngster. Still, we've got a situation here and maybe you can help us out.

Our freighter Bright Prospect struck an asteroid when emerging from warp in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The jump drive was badly damaged and they thought it might blow, but they managed to make it back in one piece. However, among the cargo, which was mostly expendable, was a set of important Ishukone corporate records; they were forced to jettison the records lest they be lost if the ship's warp core blew. At present we don't have backups due to a database malfunction, so those records might be irreplaceable.

We need someone to get out there and recover those records. I've uploaded the location of the Bright Prospect's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and bring them back to me here. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed, of course, as well as my gratitude.

138990.en: I believe in you {[character]player.name}, but I'd like some results before I celebrate thank you.  Destroy the viral agent ASAP.

138991.en:
Our spies discovered that a few convoys of Amarrian ships carrying a viral agent are heading to one of the planets in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, with the intention of carrying out a biological attack on the populace! They must not be allowed to release the toxin into the planet's atmosphere! I desperately need you to find and intercept the convoys before they finish their mission. I can supply you with bookmarks to their last sighting, I just hope you can find them in time.

Be careful though, we suspect that they have an interceptor or two guarding the convoys as well as other nasties. But I'm sure that's no problem for a seasoned pilot like yourself.

138996.en:
The Caldari State is building up its ground troops in a nearby contested system with plans to launch an attack on our fortified positions.

We've discovered a troop transport moving toward their command outpost. You need merely destroy the industrials and don't need to bother with the convoy guards.

138997.en:
In a nearby contested system, the Caldari State has long held illusions of claiming it entirely for themselves. Now, we've always been able to stop them, but lately they've started moving ground troops into their command outpost there.

We cannot attack the command outpost directly. It's too well guarded and our forces are kept occupied in other areas. However, if they manage to get enough ground troops there, they can launch an attack on our planetary holdings.

Our scanners have picked up a lightly guarded convoy filled with troops heading toward the command outpost. You can take them out, no sweat, right?

138998.en:
What I am about to ask you is strictly confidential, understood?

We've come across a civilian facility inside a nearby sector where the State's presence is strong. This compound has become a home away from home for thousands of their citizens, the majority of whom are families of the soldiers and commanders serving abroad – that is, who are killing our own Gallente people.

Their arrogance is astounding, no? They seem to think we will allow them to exist in peace simply because they bear no weapons. Their weak security presence suggests as much. Understand pilot; these people are as significant a threat as any other. What they provide may not be firepower or logistics but it is crucial to their war effort nonetheless. These people are here to boost the morale of their forces; this is something that cannot be allowed to continue.

We've found they have one major weakness: their supply line. The colony is completely dependent on regular shipments from Industrials. If you can intercept and destroy these Industrials, we can starve the enemy out.
