139010.en:
I have terrible news, {[character]player.name}. A major personnel convoy carrying countless {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} members was completely obliterated by Guristas ships, led by that damned commander of theirs, Rachen Mysuna. His reputation as a brutal Guristas military leader has traveled far and wide these past few years, and it's time to put an end to his miserable existence.

I want you to be the bringer of our vengeance, {[character]player.name}. Strike him down like the dog he is. When his battleship has been turned to dust, then you shall receive your reward.

139011.en: Some of our explorers have just located a hidden asteroid belt that is apparently full of rare ore — here in local space. That's more than a little suspicious. The signature the belt is giving off is obvious enough that it seems nearly impossible it hasn't been found and mined out before now. We're afraid it might be a trap of some sort. We want you to warp over there and check it out, then report back.

139012.en:
Yes, I certainly do have something for you. Recently, some explorers employed by {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} discovered an extremely strong gravimetric signature. Their scanners indicated the hidden belt was full of rare ore. Now, while this news would normally be cause for joy, I'm suspicious.

I'd like you to fly over to the belt and check it out. If it really is full of ore-- wonderful. If not, get back to me with the news as quickly as possible.

139013.en: I should have known better than to trust you.

139014.en: Excellent. Remember, we have no idea who might be there waiting for you. So be ready for anything.

139015.en: I've never heard of them setting ambushes before. That is disturbing news.

139016.en: I can understand your nervousness, I suppose. I'll have to find someone else.

139017.en: Is the prospect of springing a trap really that unnerving? I'm afraid I can't wait for your courage to show up.

139018.en: You still haven't answered me about the mission. I'm assuming that means "no", so I'll find someone else.

139022.en: Looks like rogue drones staged this ambush.

139023.en: You want me to walk into a trap on purpose? No, thanks-- find some other patsy.

139024.en: The prospect of walking into a trap doesn't appeal to me. I'm quitting your mission.

139025.en: I know, I'm awesome. Anyway, you got anything to do?

139026.en:
Formerly an extremist labor movement in the State, the Brothers of Freedom led a widespread revolt against corporate security forces on a number of Caldari planets a number of years ago -- some time before Tibus Heth's vastly more successful revolt of a similar nature -- after 65,000 protesters were killed by Caldari paramilitary forces while trying to force their way onto a CEP station in the New Caldari system. After months of dogged pursuit by Caldari authorities, the riots were put down and most of the leaders were killed or arrested.

Some of the leadership, including the ringleader Melarius Torvil, did manage to escape the final Caldari Navy operation that crushed the Brothers' movement. Torvil and a small group of associates fled to the Minmatar Republic and applied for asylum from Caldari persecution, which was granted by then-President Midular's Gallente-friendly government.

Today, though they have been largely eliminated as a major force in the State, the Brothers of Freedom continue to spread anti-corporate propaganda and speak out against the CEP's government in the Gallente Federation and the Minmatar Nation, as well as outlying State settlements and facilities.

139027.en: Good. Here are the coordinates for the transmitter; remember, you must destroy it and any vessels that would defend it, but it isn't necessary to engage the Republic Navy ships. Get out if you have to.

139028.en: Because you couldn't take out the Brothers of Freedom transmitter, some soft-headed fools at one of our border mining colonies seem to have taken their “sermons” to heart and, in the wake of Heth's recent successes, have begun a wildcat strike, setting back production and causing a number of injuries and even a few deaths. I hope you realize what your failure here cost us, {[character]player.name}.

139029.en: You said I should come back, remember?

139030.en: Well, I must say — you are not the fearless captain I had thought you were.

139031.en: Nice work.  I'll keep you in mind when something else comes up.

139032.en: I hope I can find someone else to handle this.

139033.en: I'll raze the outpost until nothing is left but fiery debris.

139034.en: I destroyed it all. Those Gallente won't be getting any more of that Arkonor anytime soon.

139035.en: Listen, I've got enough to worry about without getting the Gallente pissed at me. And there's already plenty of Caldari to mess with out there.

139036.en: There's a lot of Gallente out there: You might need to call in some big guns on this one. Sorry, I'm done.

139037.en: Good stuff. That's why I'm here.

139038.en: A high-ranking Gallente officer has experienced a religious conversion and wants to defect to Amarr. This man, Admiral Meledier, has apparently arranged to lead a reconnaissance foray into our space and is holed up in an old outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Get out there and extract him from the rendezvous point.

139039.en:
A Gallente admiral has seen the light of true faith and experienced a religious conversion. A hand-written, hand-delivered letter — on actual paper! — arrived in the office this morning, expressing Admiral Meledier's desire to defect. Having a high-ranking Gallente officer suddenly join our side could cause tremendous damage to the ability of their capsuleers to wage war against us: His knowledge of their systems and tactics would be staggering.

We want you to go collect him from the rendezvous point in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. You game?

139040.en: Fantastic. Alright, you might as well move out: A chance like this won't come again anytime soon.

139041.en: Excellent work. You have done well. Glory to Amarr!

139042.en: How very disappointing, {[character]player.name}. The Empire will not look with pleasure upon your lack of courage.

139043.en: Yes, of course. What is it, {[character]agentID.name}?

139044.en: Are you kidding? I'm not going up against an entire squadron of the Gallente Navy!

139045.en: Mission accomplished. Admiral Meledier is on board.

139046.en: I'll bring him in safe and sound.

139051.en: Several of our brethren were slain by a group of infidel miners encroaching on our territory in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. These outsiders are stealing our precious resources. Go out there and kill them all; bring their cargo back to me.

139052.en:
Very good, young capsuleer. Accept the purity of Blood and all will be well with you.

Recently, several of our brethren were slain by a group of infidel miners encroaching on our territory in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. These outsiders are stealing our precious resources. Go out there and kill them all, and then bring their cargo back to me. The Collectors will move in once you've finished the job.

139053.en: Excellent. Now go and do your work. Never merciful.

139054.en: You have done well — you've sent a message to those who would encroach on what is ours.

139055.en: Have you no courage, {[character]player.name}? Do you not follow the sacred creed? Never merciful.

139057.en: The miners have been destroyed, O Sanguine One. Their cargo is in my hold.

139058.en: I will not slay some helpless miners. Can we not just drive them away?

139059.en: Of course, Sanguine One. Let me prove my loyalty. Who needs bleeding?

139060.en: I'm well, thanks. Do you have any work available?

139061.en: I'm not the right pilot for this job. I resign.

139062.en: Doesn't sound like my kind of job. I'm sure you can find someone else.

139063.en: You can get your recon module back now. I ran into a few Amarrian gnats, but I swatted them away.

139064.en: It sounds like a good deal to me. Sure, I'll help you.

139066.en: Fine work, my friend. Here's your reward.

139067.en: I'm sorry to hear that, sorry indeed. You've wasted a valuable opportunity.

139068.en: I'm well, thanks. Do you have any work available?

139069.en: I'm not the right pilot for this job. I resign.

139070.en: Doesn't sound like my kind of job. I'm sure you can find someone else.

139071.en: You can get your recon module back now. I ran into a few Amarrian gnats, but I swatted them away.

139072.en: It sounds like a good deal to me. Sure, I'll help you.

139074.en: Fine work, my friend. Here's your reward.

139075.en: I'm sorry to hear that, sorry indeed. You've wasted a valuable opportunity.

139076.en:
Many bars have their fair share of tall tales, but one recurring favorite is that of the fabled “lost Jovian gate.” This tale always follows a similar narrative: the friend-of-a-friend was traveling in one of the outer regions, when, suddenly, his ship dropped out of warp. The crew found themselves in the middle of nowhere, with an inactive jump gate of strange design just in front of them.

As they approached the gate, it suddenly activated, propelling the crew into Jovian space, which was either some sort of utopia or a place of blackest horror. Before the crew could gather any evidence, some sort of danger-- usually a Jovian warship of marvelous design-- immediately appeared to force the pilot back through the gate, undertaking an emergency warp as back on the other side. Invariably, the ship's log was somehow erased. The gate, of course, cannot be rediscovered, and is once more lost to time.

139077.en:
Our spies have intercepted a leaked transmission from a mining survey crew who reported the discovery of an abandoned jump gate. Now, that may not sound exciting, but based on what the mining crew's description of the gate's position and general design, we think it could be a lost Jovian jump gate, able to access their space.

I want you to travel to the gate coordinates and secure that location until the elite forces arrive. Sounds easy, but it's going to be anything but.

139078.en: Tales of the Lost Jovian Gate

139079.en:
Our spies have intercepted a leaked transmission from a mining survey crew who reported the discovery of an abandoned jump gate. Now, that may not sound exciting, but based on what the mining crew's description of the gate's position and general design, we think it could be a lost Jovian jump gate, able to access their space.

I want you to travel to the gate coordinates and secure that location until the elite forces arrive. Sounds easy, but it's going to be anything but.

139081.en: Make sure you take plenty of ammo-- this gate is the sort of thing our competition will sacrifice almost anything to secure.

139082.en: You've given us the opportunity to study the gate, which could lead to some considerable technological advances. Good work.

139083.en: You must've come to the wrong office. Missions for those lacking guts are down the hall, to the right.

139084.en: Do you understand how important this mission was to the Cartel? We're now forced into a major military action to take the gate from the forces established there. Don't think we'll forget your incompetence any time soon.

139085.en: What are you doing? Securing the asset before any of the other factions arrived was a matter of timing as well as firepower! I'll find someone else, as you're obviously not up to the task.

139088.en: I'll secure the gate for you, piece of cake.

139089.en: That space is a graveyard now. But it's a secure, Cartel-owned graveyard.

139090.en: Is this a “take it or leave it” option?  If so, I'll leave it.

139091.en: It's hell out there! I'm not losing my stuff over some antique jump gate – I quit!

139092.en: It usually is. Please, go on.

139093.en:
Certain unofficial militia groups in several Caldari systems are very interested in acquiring themselves some serious firepower. They must also have some well-connected financial backers, as they want to pay top ISK to get their hands on these weapons, and in large quantities, ASAP.

You've got a solid reputation with us, so I want you to broker the deal on my behalf. Meet my man at the rendezvous point provided. He'll have the weapons cache. Everything goes well; the Caldari will show up, you'll trade the stuff, the end. But if the deal goes south, I want you to take out every last one of them and bring the weapons back here.

139094.en:
Have you been following the news? All that unrest over in Caldari space? Certain unofficial militia groups in several Caldari systems are very interested in acquiring themselves some serious firepower. They must also have some well-connected financial backers, as they want to pay top ISK to get their hands on these weapons, and in large quantities, ASAP.

You've got a solid reputation with us, so I want you to broker the deal on my behalf. Meet my man at the rendezvous point provided. He'll have the weapons cache. Everything goes well; the Caldari will show up, you'll trade the stuff, the end. But if the deal goes south, I want you to take out every last one of them and bring the weapons back here.

139095.en: Let's forgo the exit interview-- just remember that you can't keep messing us around like this and retain all of your body parts.

139096.en: Get going, champ; they'll be waiting.

139097.en: Really? I never thought such shady, anonymous characters would even consider betrayal. How about that?

139098.en: Easy there, I'm not gonna make you do it. I'll just find another pilot to represent me at the deal.

139099.en: Because of you, the deal has fallen through. If you weren't one of those “elite” pilots, you'd be out of an airlock by now. Sleep lightly, friend.

139100.en: If you didn't want the gig, you should've said so to begin with. I'll go find someone who's actually interested and reliable.

139103.en: I have no problem handling weapons-- have you seen my ship lately? I'll happily broker the deal.

139104.en: Well, the "deal" proved to be a straight setup, but I showed them what it means to mess with the Cartel.

139105.en: So, the odds of something going wrong are high enough that you want me to go instead of you? I'll pass, thanks.

139106.en: I had a bad feeling about this when I took the mission, and now things are just bad all around. I quit.

139107.en: When you say "negotiation", I'm assuming you mean "shooting." What's happening?

139108.en: Good work. I knew I could count on you. With that relay station out of commission, our local transmissions will be harder for the Caldari to intercept, at least until they manage to sneak another convoy in there.

139109.en:
In the last few weeks, we've become aware of an FTL transmitter in the area which has been broadcasting anti-corporate propaganda into the State. Usually, the Federation isn't quite this bold in its slander of our state, so a number of corporate intelligence offices looked into the matter and found to our surprise that this transmitter is actually being run by someone we are all too familiar with: Melarius Torvil and his so-called “Brothers of Freedom.”

Obviously, we cannot allow this situation to continue. Torvil's persistent ability to elude capture by Caldari authorities is frustrating enough, but we cannot simply stand by while he rubs it in our faces. Frankly, the fact that the Republic is allowing this kind of dangerous nonsense makes me thankful our militia capsuleers are giving them a hard time.

Anyway, we would like you to fly to the transmitter in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}: Destroy it and any Minmatar vessels in the area. If the Republic Navy sends any ships to assist, feel free to eliminate them as well, but it isn't necessary; I don't think they'll be willing to stick their necks out over what is a rather diplomatically shady activity anyway.

What do you say? Can you handle this for me?

139110.en: The "Brothers of Freedom" have set up an FTL transmitter in the area of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and are broadcasting anti-corporate propaganda into the State, with the help of some Minmatar sympathizers. This situation is completely unacceptable; the transmitter must be destroyed, and we want you take care of it. Eliminate the transmitter and any hostile ships nearby. If the Minmatar Navy interferes, you can take out their vessels as well, but it's not strictly necessary.

139111.en: Engage the hostile fleet.  Watch out for reinforcements.  Kill as many as you can and then get out.

139113.en: We have reports of a strange Angel fleet massing in a nearby system.  The reports say they're all small ships, but I'm not sure if I'd trust that.  I need a pilot to round up some mates and go take them out.  You game?

139114.en: Funny, I thought you were a combat pilot.

139117.en: Oh, so I suppose you want to do something a little less dangerous?

139118.en: Or were you just too busy watching vids?

139119.en: Had to send someone else. Sorry, chump.

139123.en: Man, that was a lot of little ships.  What the heck was that all about?

139124.en: Sounds risky. I think I'll pass.

139125.en: This is too much work. Find some other chump.

139126.en: That depends. You got something interesting for me?

139127.en: I just might be, yes. What have you got?

139128.en: I'm taking more damage than I expected. I need to bail out of this mission, {[character]agentID.name}. Sorry.

139130.en: Base and enemy vessels destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. It looks as if the Angel Cartel took some interest in things as well.

139131.en: I'll take care of the Amarrians for you, happily.

139132.en: Too bad. Soon we're all going to have to help out whether we want to or not.

139133.en: Good work. I guess the Angels really are interested in this sector.

139135.en: This isn't going to look good to my superiors, {[character]player.name}, but I accept your decision.

139136.en:
Oh, we have a number of possibilities, but only a few really choice assignments for especially trustworthy capsuleers like yourself.

These are definitely dangerous times, {[character]player.name}. The corsairs are getting bolder, crime is rampant, and the empires are pretty much at war, which will plunge us all into chaos and cost millions of lives. Unfortunately for people like me, there's not much we can do to change the inevitable; all we can do is try to make sure that what comes costs us as little as possible — in lives, worlds, and materials. To that end, I'm overseeing a lot of war prep in this region, and I'm in need of good pilots who know their stuff and aren't afraid to take some risks now and again.

This has been a hot sector lately. The Angel Cartel is especially active, but fortunately for us they're equal opportunity raiders, and have been as hard on the Caldari and the Amarr as they have on us. Amarr, for their part, have been sending in reconnaissance craft, which suggests either that they have designs on this region or they think we'll be using it as a staging area.

In fact, we think Imperial forces are rebuilding an abandoned CONCORD station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and will be using it to service their vessels, so they may be planning a more long-term presence in the region. These are just the opening moves in the great game, I assure you, but we can't let ourselves be outmaneuvered.

We're short-handed right now, so we're not above hiring independents; we'd like you to take out this station. There may be some Amarrian ships in the area, but we don't anticipate anything like a full-scale defense. Get in, destroy the base, and get out, and you'll have earned yourself a nice reward... and helped to keep the Empire out of this sector.

139137.en:
We think Imperial forces are rebuilding an abandoned CONCORD station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and will be using it to service their vessels, so they may be planning a more long-term presence in the region. These are just the opening moves in the great war, I assure you, but we can't let ourselves be outmaneuvered.

We're short-handed right now, so we're not above hiring independents; we'd like you to take out this station. There may be some Amarrian ships in the area, but we don't anticipate anything like a full-scale defense. Get in, destroy the base, and get out.

139138.en: If you're paying well, then you're right — I am perfect for it.

139139.en: Shouldn't this really be something the police could take care of?

139140.en: You were right: the customs official was letting slaves into the Federation. But he won't be doing so any longer.

139141.en: I will do anything necessary to ensure that the Federation remains a bastion of freedom!

139146.en: I am surprised. I wouldn't have taken you for someone who'd allow such an injustice to continue.

139147.en: Good work. The Federation does its utmost to make sure our enemies cannot undermine our way of life, and you've struck a great blow today in that pursuit.

139148.en: Excellent. Now, get out there and catch this scumbag. And vaporize the smugglers as well. They're not our main targets, but eliminating a few of them should help you let off some steam.

139149.en: Great. Unless something is done, this problem will just continue to grow. I never thought you would be so selfish.

139150.en:
A customs officer has long been suspected of taking bribes from the Amarr. There is an old smuggler's gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that is supposed to have been deactivated, but lately ships have been registered coming through it. We believe it is the customs officer, allowing illegal slavers to bypass our normal checkpoints and bring slaves through the Federation.

We want you to fly out to the stargate and catch him in the act. Once you do, you're free to eliminate him with extreme prejudice.

139151.en:
It is a sad day when you cannot trust your own citizens, don't you agree? Well, today is a sad day. You see, one of our customs agents may be accepting bribes. What's worse, he may actually be helping those Amarr slaver scum smuggle slaves through the Federation.

We have long suspected the officer, but never had any concrete proof. He has been incredibly careful in covering his tracks. But finally, we think we've got him. There's an old smuggler's stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that's supposed to be inactive. It seems the transmission logger isn't inactive, though, and it recently sent us a traffic report… and several industrial ships belonging to "Imperial Human Resources," a well-known Amarrian slave company, were recorded passing through the gate.

We believe the customs official is the one opening the gate for the smugglers, and he just left the station a short time ago. We planted a bug on his ship, so we have his current location. I want you to fly out there, catch the customs official in the act of opening the gate, and destroy him.

139152.en: I thought you were a warrior of the Republic. I must've been thinking of somebody else.

139154.en: Unbelievable. You destroyed the shipyard and their fleet. And you came back, which is a bonus.

139155.en: Oh, so I suppose you want to do something a little less dangerous?

139157.en: I'll just get someone who has some balls, then.

139160.en: I'll need to round up my wingmen, but consider that shipyard dust.

139163.en: Okay, this is a bit much. I'm gonna have to quit.

139165.en:
You know what they say about assumptions, right? …something about, uh, sums and options… I think.

Why am I here again?

139166.en: Hey, I didn't sign up for this when I accepted your mission!

139167.en: Wow, you know, I have something more important to do. Like... uh... yeah — no thanks.

139168.en: I've destroyed the satellite, but I think there's something more going on here than meets the eye.

139169.en: You really must not like people who grew up planetside. Anyway, I'll take care of it.

139174.en: You're really turning me down? If I have to deal directly with those dust-snufflers, I'll scream.

139175.en: What? Caldari forces protecting that satellite? Great. Just great. Now we'll have to launch a whole investigation into the matter. I might even get sent planetside. I do hate this job sometimes.

139176.en: The sooner you deal with this, the better. I hate having to interact with those petty land-lice.

139177.en: Great. You can't get the job done, so now I'll have to deal with it even more.

139178.en:
Ehh, politics, I believe. Oh, I never get tired of them. Dear, sweet politics. Oh, wait. No. I hate politics.

But without politics, our great democratic and free society would collapse. It's the nature of the beast, I'm afraid. And, well, the Federation has numerous laws to prevent politicians from being abusive with their politicking. Now, some dirtside political office is up for grabs after the incumbent died of a heart attack after a night at a pleasure hub. "Vice Commissioner of Waste Management for the Civic Council" or something unimportant like that.

Normally, we wouldn't even bother with something this trivial. Those silly dirtside hillhuggers and their governments aren't much to look at. But one of them had to go and break some laws, and now it's our job to clean it up. You see, someone has hijacked some broadcast waves and is sending out a constant message denouncing one of the candidates. And because it's a space-based satellite doing the broadcasting, we're the ones that have to deal with it.

Now, we don't know who it is that's making the broadcasts, and frankly, I don't care. As long as they're stopped, I'm happy with it. We've pinned down the offending satellite, so I want you to fly over there and blow it up. There might be some automated defenses, but it's just some mudsucker's place, so they can't be that great.

139180.en:
Someone has illegally hijacked a broadcast satellite and is using it to play a message denigrating a local politician running for office. I could care less, but those sand-sifters won't stop nagging me about it. We've found the offending satellite, we just need it destroyed — the sooner, the better. That way I'll stop having to hear complaints about it.

Oh, there might be some automated defenses, but they probably won't be that hard to handle.

139181.en:
The Gallente Federation is a massive democracy. It is divided up into several regions, which are subdivided into districts, which are further divided into sub-districts… which make up several individual systems, each of which has one or more planetary governments, each of which further has additional subdivisions. Though every planet follows some basic rules, such as having regular elections with universal suffrage, the systems on each planet are as varied as the Gallente people.

For most observers, planetary politics in the Federation are incredibly tedious. Some, however, count the politics of the planets as the most fascinating and vital part of the democracy. There is a huge amount of bureaucracy involved, which makes it too dense for most to penetrate. But the amount of energy put forth by many individuals (who are unlikely to be remembered once their terms are finished) exemplifies the true spirit of the Federation.

139182.en:
Technically, I had nothing to do with getting you into this in the first place. I was just...

Ah, never mind. What do you need?

139183.en: I'm too lazy to finish your mission. Sorry.

139184.en: Zzzz... What? Huh? Oh, you should find someone else, I guess, since your proposal's making me fall asleep.

139185.en: I brought the politician back, as asked.

139186.en: I've carried worse around. One politician shouldn't be too bad.

139191.en: I suppose I'll have to send someone else to do it for me.

139192.en: Alright, now I've got to go have a little chat with our politician. Come back to me later to see what I've discovered.

139193.en: Hurry over there and get him. The sooner he's back, the sooner I can get rid of him.

139194.en: I don't want to deal with this any more than you do. You're really quitting on me?

139195.en:
There's a badly damaged Gallente convoy nearby. One or two of the vessels may be capable of defending themselves, but we don't think they're up to much of a fight. We want you to head out there; finish them off and get as much of that salvage as you can. Somewhere in all that cargo and salvage there's a sealed container of great value to the Cartel, so we'll provide you with a generous bonus if you get it back to us intact.

Oh, yes, one more thing... The Gallente convoy got off a distress signal, so you might have to contend with a Gallente rescue mission. And we've heard some chatter from the Serpentis saying that they might be sending ships soon, so best be on your guard. Our intelligence says that neither of those factions has very much in the way of resources in the area, so you shouldn't have too much to do.

Things might get dicey, but I'm sure it's nothing you can't handle.

139196.en:
Well, it turns out that the Caldari Navy is behind those transmissions. The question is why… Why do the Caldari care who wins some meaningless election on some planetary hovel? That's what we have to find out now. The first step in taking care of this will be to question the candidate they were broadcasting about.

Now, I've received word that the man is vacationing with his family a few systems away. We've already sent word over to have him recalled as a matter of official Federation business. By the time you get there, he should be ready for pick up.

What, I didn't mention that? Yes, you get the great pleasure of taxiing that earthbounder back to us. I know you'll accept, won't you?

139197.en:
So, it turns out that the Caldari Navy is the one behind those transmissions. The question is, why? Why do the Caldari care who wins some meaningless election on some planetary hovel? That's what we have to find out now. The first step in taking care of this will be to question the candidate they were broadcasting about.

Now, I've received word that the man is vacationing with his family a few systems away. We've already sent word over to have him recalled as a matter of official Federation business. By the time you get there, he should be ready for pick up.

139198.en:
There's a badly damaged Gallente convoy nearby. One or two of the vessels may be capable of defending themselves, but we don't think they're up to much of a fight. We want you to head out there; finish them off and get as much of that salvage as you can. Somewhere in all that cargo and salvage, there's a sealed container of great value to the Cartel, so we'll provide you with a generous bonus if you get it back to us intact.

Oh, yes, one more thing... The Gallente convoy got off a distress signal, so you might have to contend with a Gallente rescue mission. And we've heard some chatter from the Serpentis saying that they might be sending ships soon, so best be on your guard. Our intelligence says that neither of those factions has very much in the way of resources in the area, so you shouldn't have too much to do.

Things might get dicey, but I'm sure it's nothing you can't handle.

139199.en: I never said you wouldn't get your hair a little mussed. I'm sorry that the mean ol' bad guys scratched up your precious paint job.

139200.en: ASAP, {[character]player.name}. See you when you get back.

139201.en: I can't imagine why you're complaining. You got the job done, after all.

139203.en: Sure, I'll give it a shot, {[character]agentID.name}. When do I leave?

139204.en: You were definitely low-balling the risk, {[character]agentID.name}. Here's your precious container.

139205.en: I think you're low-balling the risk here. I'll look for opportunities elsewhere.

139206.en: Holy crap, where are all those ships coming from? I'm taking too much damage. I quit!

139207.en: I've been busy. What've you got cooking?

139208.en: Really? You can't? I would never have guessed.

139209.en: It turns out those Caldari Navy guys are pretty tough. I quit.

139210.en: I'm sorry, but I'm not going to handle someone else's bully.

139211.en: The Caldari have learned not to mess with our local district elections.

139212.en: At last, something interesting! I'll do it!

139217.en: Nnnggg.... You're just trying to give me an aneurysm, aren't you?

139218.en: Good. Of course, now everyone thinks our politician's some great hero, important enough for the Caldari Navy to try and get rid of him. The fool will probably become President some day. Makes my skin crawl just thinking about it.

139219.en: I've uploaded the location to your NeoCom.

139220.en: You couldn't even take care of one lone Caldari officer? What kind of pod pilot are you?

139221.en:
Our politician friend managed to annoy a Caldari Navy officer back in the day and now that officer is out for revenge. He's the one behind all these broadcasts. I guess he figured since it was such a meaningless, tiny local election, the Federation wouldn't stop his revenge.

I guess he doesn't know that we'll take any opportunity there is to blow up a few Caldari Navy vessels.

We've tracked his base down and want you to go over there and take him out. The sooner this headache is over, the better.

139222.en:
No, it's true. I know I always speak glowingly of them, but really, they get under my skin.

Anyway, my questioning finally got some answers out of that damn fool politician. It turns out that there is no vast conspiracy after all. Not really. It turns out the idiot is just a little too loud-mouthed for his own good. He used to be in the Navy… before he was discharged because he kept fainting every time he went onto the battlefield. But before he demonstrated that bit of heroism, he managed to piss off a Caldari Navy officer by throwing up on him during a diplomatic summit.

Apparently, the officer in question never lived it down and still gets heckled about the event to this day. And now he's out for revenge by trying to disrupt our man, the stupid politician. It's… it's so tedious and… stupid.

Anyway, I guess this officer figured that, since it was such a meaningless little election, the Federation wouldn't bother to interfere with his revenge. Heh. I guess he doesn't know that we'll take any opportunity there is to blow up a few Caldari Navy vessels. We've tracked his base down and want you to go over there and take him out.

The sooner this headache is over, the better.

139223.en:
The workers in a corporate mining facility are striking, taking control of the facility's defense grid and arming their mining vessels. They have shut the mining operation down completely and locked corporate personnel out of the area until their demands are met.

This situation is not acceptable. You are to enter the facility and neutralize any armed resistance: bring the strike to an end before there is any more damage to corporate property or loss of production. Do what you can to minimize collateral damage, but ending this as soon as possible is your top priority.

139224.en: I certainly hope you're not a sympathizer, pilot.  You won't go far if you keep up this attitude.

139225.en: Good.  Here are the coordinates for the entrance to the mining facility.  Return to me as soon as the job is done.

139226.en: Excellent.  Hopefully the new manager of that facility will be able to get production up and running in short order.

139227.en: I certainly hope you're not turning this down because you sympathize with them.  I suppose I'll have to find someone else with a more realistic idea of the situation to handle this.

139228.en: You've taken too long: the strike has gotten far too out of control and corporate assets are in serious danger.  We've called in the military to deal with the situation. Your services are no longer needed, pilot.

139229.en: I couldn't wait any longer for you to decide if you could handle this for me. I was forced to call in another pilot to take care of the matter.  While I am not exactly a fan of her methods, she has been able to bring the strike to a quick end.  Perhaps next time you will make sure you get back to me in a timely manner.

139231.en: Wildcat strike brought to bloody end

139232.en: I'll deal with the strike.  You can count on me.

139233.en: The strike has been brought to an end.

139234.en: I'm not sure this is really a job for me.

139235.en: I've decided I don't have time to clean up this particular mess.

139237.en: Scientific progress grinds to a halt, thanks to you.

139238.en:
Well, Dr. Calus is not ready to reveal the nature of her project, but rest assured that it will be huge. However, the good doctors require some critical datacores to help them put their ideas into physical form. Sometimes scientific ideas race ahead of one's ability to fabricate the results effectively.

We need you to go pick up a unique Mechanical Engineering datacore put together for the project by one of Dr. Calus's colleagues not far from here and bring it back as soon as possible. You will be rewarded, of course, as usual.

139240.en: Go pick up a shipment of slaver hounds from a private deadspace compound in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They're inside the base, stored in secured containers in case those Starway freaks try anything.

139241.en: I got your slavers. But I don't think you'll be getting any more from that supplier-— someone bombed the place but good, just as I got there. And I'm thinking it was no coincidence.

139242.en:
Well, it just so happens that we're in the middle of some operations that might require a capsuleer's assistance.

The Amarrians have been busy lately, building bases and moving fleet resources back and forth along the frontier. We've done recon in several of the systems where the Amarrians have been active, but we recently observed unusual comings and goings in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. We think they might be building a base in one of the system's asteroid fields, but we can't be sure as all of our ships are tied down in other locations.

I'd like to install a reconnaissance module in your ship, then have you fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} posing as a freelance miner. Go to the asteroid field that we've entered into your NeoCom and mine 2000 units of Scordite. We'll take the ore off your hands when you get back to make sure everything looks aboveboard.

While you're mining, the recon module will be scanning the region and monitoring Amarrian activity around the system. You'll never even notice it's there. Once you've finished, head back here and we'll recover the recon unit, take the ore, and reward you for your efforts.

Note, I'd advise caution. Will you do it, {[character]player.name}?

139243.en: We've entered the coordinates into your NeoCom, and the recon unit has been installed in your ship. Remember, you won't even know it's there.

139244.en:
I'd like you to fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} posing as a freelance miner; while you're out there, we'll have a reconnaissance module installed in your ship. Go to the asteroid field that we've entered into your NeoCom and mine 2,000 units of Scordite. Of course we'll reimburse you generously for your time and for the ore – the mining mission is just a cover for the recon mission.

While you're mining, the recon module will be scanning the region and monitoring Amarrian activity around the system. You'll never even notice it's there. Once you've finished, head back here and we'll recover the recon unit, take the ore, and reward you for your efforts. I'd advise caution in the area as well: There are lots of miners around, but the Amarr will be suspicious of any vessel that originates from Republic space.

139245.en:
Well, it just so happens that we're in the middle of some operations that might require a capsuleer's assistance.

The Caldari have been busy lately, building bases and moving fleet resources back and forth along the frontier. We've done recon in several of the systems where the Caldari have been active, but we recently observed unusual comings and goings in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. We think they might be building a base in one of the system's asteroid fields, but we can't be sure as all of our ships are tied down in other locations.

I'd like to install a reconnaissance module in your ship, then have you fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} posing as a freelance miner. Go to the asteroid field that we've entered into your NeoCom and mine 2000 units of Scordite. We'll take the ore off your hands when you get back to make sure everything looks aboveboard.

While you're mining, the recon module will be scanning the region and monitoring Caldari activity around the system. You'll never even notice it's there. Once you've finished, head back here and we'll recover the recon unit, take the ore, and reward you for your efforts.



Note, I'd advise caution. Will you do it, {[character]player.name}?

139246.en: We've entered the coordinates into your NeoCom, and the recon unit has been installed in your ship. Remember, you won't even know it's there.

139247.en:
I'd like you to fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} posing as a freelance miner; while you're out there, we'll have a reconnaissance module installed in your ship. Go to the asteroid field that we've entered into your NeoCom and mine 2,000 units of Scordite. Of course we'll reimburse you generously for your time and for the ore – the mining mission is just a cover for the recon mission.

While you're mining, the recon module will be scanning the region and monitoring Caldari activity around the system. You'll never even notice it's there. Once you've finished, head back here and we'll recover the recon unit, take the ore, and reward you for your efforts.I'd advise caution in the area as well: There are lots of miners around, but the Caldari will be suspicious of any vessel that originates from Federation space.

139248.en: You should hear the reports. The Gallente are now paranoid that we're going to roll right over them! Of course our line is just that you were taking photographs for your family or something, but they're scared senseless.

139249.en:
Reports are that the pirates are amassing a small fleet for action against us. They have a scout scoping the place ahead of them. Only he's not going to get to the final area.

The scout will be jumping through an old, decommissioned jump gate. Take a position by the gate, and wait for him to come through. Once he does, take him out.

139250.en: But you stole ore! Danger is your middle name!

139251.en: Gate camps are groups of ships who wait outside jump gates for other ships to pass through. Once a ship comes through the gate camp bombards it, putting their target at a great disadvantage. The use of warp bubbles and scramblers can further ruin an unsuspecting target's day, preventing it from warping away from the fight. For this reason, warp stabilizers are common fitting for any ships passing through low- or null- security space.

139252.en: The Gallente are great lovers of wealth and luxury, and especially of beauty. They produce countless holos, from the cheapest porn flicks to high-priced stage shows and beyond. The stars of these productions are greatly esteemed for the entertainment they provide, and therefore hold influence and power in some circles.

139253.en: The daughter of a prominent Holder has eloped with a famous Gallente holo star, despite having a proper marriage with an Amarr man awaiting her at home. Retrieve her from this seducer and kill him.

139255.en:
Yes, I have work for you. The daughter of a prominent Holder has been seduced by a famous Gallente holo star. She's run away with him, likely planning to get married as soon as she is out of her family's reach.

She was already betrothed to a perfectly suitable Amarrian man, a match approved by her family and her faith. Obviously, she must be brought back into the fold.

You will be well rewarded if you can deliver her back to her family before she can shame herself any further. If you destroy this seducer in the process-- well, that's all the better.

139256.en: And I thought you were a true Amarr. You cannot expect to keep a good reputation if you fail to do these jobs.

139257.en: I knew you were the right person for the job. Take care, as this holo star does have bodyguards.

139258.en: I knew I could count on you. You are indeed a faithful Amarr; your reputation will only benefit from the work you have done.

139259.en: And I thought you were a good Amarr. You cannot expect to keep a good reputation if you won't put in any effort.

139260.en: Thanks to you, {[character]player.name}, the Holder's daughter has married the Gallente holo star and brought shame to her family and to the Amarr. Do not think that you can let things like this happen without suffering any consequences.

139261.en: Thanks to you, {[character]player.name}, the Holder's daughter has married the Gallente holo star and brought shame to her family and to the Amarr. Do not think that you can let things like this happen and without suffering any consequences.

139265.en: I, uh, found the girl. You take her.

139266.en: I don't have time to chase down some runaway. I have more important things to do.

139267.en: I don't have time to chase down some runaway. I have more important things to do.

139268.en: I heard you had a job for me.

139269.en:
The Amarr Empire is ruled by the Emperor and the five Heirs. When the Emperor dies, these Heirs go through a set of ritual competitions to become the next Emperor.

In 22762 AD, Khanid was the Heir of one of the other five families, but he refused to acknowledge the election of the new Emperor. He also refused to commit ritual suicide, which is done by the remaining Heirs in order to keep resentments and past problems from interfering with the new ruler's regime.

Instead of being obedient and faithful, Khanid fled Amarr and set out to create his own empire. He formed the Khanid Kingdom, which is also known as the “Dark Amarr.”

139270.en: The Minmatar are attempting to form an alliance with the Khanid Kingdom in order to gain an ally against the Amarr Empire. This could be dangerous to the Empire, as the Khanid may know much that could help Amarr's enemies. Find, intercept and destroy the Minmatar ambassador's vessel and its escorts and bring the ambassador back for interrogation.

139272.en:
That is correct.

The Minmatar, deceitful devils that they are, are attempting to form an alliance with the Khanid Kingdom. Khanid is a traitor to our beliefs, and he knows much about us that the Minmatar could exploit if they manage to forge an alliance.

We cannot risk the chance that the Minmatar might succeed. Go find the Minmatar vessel and destroy it before it reaches Khanid. Take care to bring the ambassador back for questioning. Be cautious, however – the Minmatar have the distasteful habit of thinking they can fight back against us.

139273.en: I thought you were a better pod pilot than that. A true Amarr would understand how much this refusal could damage a reputation.

139274.en: Wonderful! Remember to take care – Minmatar are always hard to break.

139275.en: Excellent. Thank you for your efforts.  Here is your reward.

139276.en: I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}. I thought you would see the importance of this mission.

139277.en: I cannot believe that you could not find and destroy the Minmatar vessels. You are not the pod pilot I thought you were. As a result of this failure, the Khanid Kingdom may have leaked dangerous secrets to the Minmatar.

139278.en: You should make decisions more quickly, capsuleer. As a result of your failure to destroy the ship, the Minmatar ambassador met with someone within the Khanid Kingdom; whether or not an alliance will be forged is still unknown.

139281.en: Nothing would please me more than to put a stop to this plot.

139282.en: I found and destroyed the Minmatar ambassador's ship. I've brought you the "envoy" for questioning.

139283.en: I don't see this as a threat to us. Khanid might not conform as he should, but he is still Amarr.

139284.en: I don't have time to hunt down these Minmatar vessels. You'll have to find someone else.

139285.en: I heard that you needed someone willing to do a combat mission.

139286.en: I see.  Well, perhaps you will be of some use next time.

139287.en: I see.  Well, perhaps you will be of some use next time.

139288.en: I see.  Well, perhaps you will be of some use next time.

139289.en: I see.  Well, perhaps you will be of some use next time.

139290.en:
When the Amarr Empire first came across the Minmatar, they began raiding this new people for slaves as they had with every other race they'd come across, a practice that is sanctified and even encouraged by the Amarr religion.

Though the Minmatar have since rebelled and managed to expel the Amarr and their allies from Minmatar space, approximately a third of all Minmatar are still enslaved under the Amarr.

139291.en: Some Minmatar slaves have rebelled, killing several Amarr and stealing a ship. Track them down so that they can be returned to their owner.

139293.en:
So the news is out.

It's true, some slaves have rebelled, and their actions have caused the deaths of several people. They have stolen a ship, and thus far they've managed to evade capture as well. This is insult on top of injury and cannot be tolerated.

I want you to track them down so that they can be returned to their owner.

139294.en: Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.

139295.en: God's will be with you. You will be greatly rewarded when you bring them back.

139296.en: I knew I could count on you to retrieve those upstarts. Stay close: I suspect I'll have another mission for you shortly.

139297.en: Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.

139298.en: Inaction speaks, pilot. Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.

139299.en: Inaction speaks, pilot. Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.

139302.en: I'll find them and bring them back.

139305.en: These slaves aren't worth the trouble I've gone to; get someone else to hunt them down.

139306.en: I've heard rumors about a slave uprising.

139307.en:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places and go to the Bookmarks tab. Then right-click on the objective item (the roster) and choose "Set Destination." On your ship's control panel, click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate star system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click on the roster and select "Warp to within 0." Once you've arrived at the location, look at your Overview and find the cargo container; right-click on it and select "Approach." Once you've approached to within 1500 meters, right-click the cargo container and open it. A window will now pop up, displaying the container's contents. Click and drag the item(s) into your cargo hold: Once you've done that, you will have obtained the Brutor Tribe roster. All that will remain is to return with it to your agent for your reward.

139308.en: What's up, {[character]agentID.name}? I take it you have some work for me.

139309.en: I'm encountering more difficulty than I'd anticipated. I have to to withdraw from the mission, {[character]agentID.name}.

139310.en: That sounds awfully fishy to me. I prefer to let other people get dirty with the propaganda machine.

139311.en: The Mordu's Legion fleet is defeated. And the Caldari have egg all over their faces.

139312.en: I'm up for anything that will embarrass the Caldari. I'll do it.

139313.en: That isn't what we're doing at all! But it's obvious to me you don't want the job, so forget it anyway.

139314.en: Excellent. Your reward has been entered into your interstellar account. Many thanks, {[character]player.name}.

139315.en: Well done. The system coordinates have been sent to your NeoCom.

139317.en:
If you're willing. Given the current state of interstellar affairs, Mordu's Legion is in the thick of things. They've been engaging in raids and reconnaissance, harassing merchant traffic, and generally making trouble for us. In this sector, at least, they're doing just what the Caldari want them to — keeping our fleet tied down so those greedy bastards can martial their own forces in relative peace.

We might have an ace in the hole, however. We have good intelligence that many Intaki inside the Caldari State are growing impatient and restless, suffering discrimination and unemployment. Many blame the Caldari for their woes, and with the right incentive they might even be persuaded to secede back to the Federation. An incident involving the State-sanctioned Mordu's Legion may be just enough to tip the scales.

We've been monitoring subspace chatter, and we think that the Legion may be planning on hitting one of our bases in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We're planning on making it known that the base is full of Intaki refugees, but just to clinch the deal, it would be best if some heroic pilot caught the Mordus in the act and drove them off before the base was completely destroyed.

What we'd like you to do is get over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take up position near the station. When the Legion ships arrive, destroy them or drive them off. We'll be monitoring things by video drone, so we'll have clear evidence of the attack.

Oh, and the Legion may be coming in strength, so you might want to bring some friends along. So, what do you say?

139319.en:
We think that Mordu's Legion may be planning on hitting one of our bases in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. What we'd like you to do is get over there and take up position near the station. When the Legion ships arrive, destroy them or drive them off. We'll be monitoring things by video drone, so we'll have clear evidence of the attack.

Oh, and the Legion may be coming in strength, so you might want to bring some friends along.

139320.en:
Mordu's Legion is descended from a group of Intaki military personnel who sided with the Caldari State when it chose to secede from the Gallente Federation. It was led by a brilliant Caldari officer named Muryia Mordu, who fought the Gallente with great distinction.

After the war, the Intaki were given land around Waschi City on the planet Kamokor IV, but soon racial tensions flared between them and Caldari nationalists, who called for the expulsion of all foreigners. The Intaki called upon their hero Mordu for assistance, and the aging commander emerged from retirement to lead an independent mercenary group dedicated to preserving Intaki rights and property. Mordu's Legion helped defeat the nationalists and made peace with the Caldari authorities.

Today, the Legion remains a well-known mercenary band that often works closely with the Caldari State. Many Intaki continue to suffer discrimination at the hands of the xenophobic Caldari and have grown disillusioned with life in the corporate state. Nevertheless, Mordu remains a revered character among the Intaki, many of whom see him as a savior who will one day return to deliver his adopted people from the repression and poverty that they suffer from today.

139321.en: Might be, {[character]agentID.name}. What have you got?

139322.en: I'm taking too much damage, and this is taking too long. I quit.

139323.en: That doesn't sound very interesting. Have you got anything else?

139324.en: The enemy gate is destroyed, along with some of their hardware, {[character]agentID.name}. Thanks for the mission.

139325.en: Sounds like a decent job. I'll do it.

139326.en: That's too bad, {[character]player.name}. Nothing else available right now, I'm afraid.

139328.en: Thanks for your help. The coordinates are in your NeoCom, along with my instructions.

139329.en: I expected better from you, to be honest. You are a capsuleer, right? You're not just impersonating one?

139330.en:
Well, we've had some suspicious activity in this system lately. We suspect that someone — Angel Cartel, or possibly Serpentis, maybe even the Amarrians — might be sneaking in and prepping the system for attack with hidden bases, supplies, and the like. There may even be a hidden jumpgate somewhere in the vicinity; we've certainly detected some suspicious warp signatures and have been able to triangulate them down to several potential locations, all quite close to each other.

If we make a move with a large fleet, though, we might spook the enemy, so we're looking for a freelancer who's willing to take a risk on behalf of the Federation. We need someone to fly to the possible locations of the acceleration gate and see what's there. I'll enter the location of the first acceleration gate into your NeoCom; you should be able to reach the others using whatever internal gate array they've put in place. Fly through each one in turn and check the area for any gates that look suspicious. If you find one, you need to blast it before the enemy can jump any more ships around in this system.

Mind you, if there are enemy ships, you might have to fight them too, and no one can say for sure what might come through the gate. There might even be static defense turrets or drones as well. Who knows?

Once the gate is destroyed, return here and report; do it quickly and you'll earn yourself a nice bonus. Are you in?

139331.en:
We need someone to fly to the possible locations of the secret gate and see what's there. I'll enter the location of the first acceleration gate into your NeoCom; you should be able to reach the others using whatever internal gate array they've put in place. Fly through each one in turn and check the area for any gates that look suspicious. If you find one, you need to blast it before the enemy can jump any more ships around in this system.

Mind you, if there are enemy ships, you might have to fight them too, and no one can say for sure what might come through the gate. There might even be static defense turrets or drones as well.

139332.en: Destroy the three enemy shipyards and the control tower at the specified location.  Defend yourself and destroy any resistance.  You may need backup for this one.

139333.en:
The Republic needs your help with this one. We've discovered one of the facilities of a corporation that's a major supplier for the Amarrian Navy. By destroying it, we'll deliver a serious blow to their military buildup, which can only help the Republic.

Expect major resistance on this-- you'll need some backup of your own. Think you can handle this?

139334.en: A significant percentage of the Minmatar population resides within the Gallente Federation, forming a rather powerful political bloc. This bloc is one reason that the relations between Amarr and Gallente remain constantly tense.

139335.en: The slaves provided us with a location. There was supposed to be a data chip in a dead drop at this rendezvous. In the interest of preventing further mayhem, I need you to bring me that chip.

139337.en:
Yes. We interrogated several of the Minmatar slaves you brought back after they escaped.

It seems that the errant Minmatar were headed to a group of their own kind within the Gallente Federation. In fact, they might not have managed to escape at all without the help of a Gallente contact.

When we applied more pressure, the slaves could only provide us with a location. There was supposed to be a data chip in a dead drop at this rendezvous. In the interest of preventing further mayhem, I need you to bring me that chip.

139338.en: I'll have to find someone else.

139339.en: I look forward to seeing what you find.

139340.en: Good work. Let me see what this says; I may have another mission for you shortly.

139341.en: And here I thought you were a brave one.

139342.en: You've waited too long to do what I asked. You've taught me not to mistake you for dependable.

139343.en: I've waited too long for your reply. You've taught me not to mistake you for dependable.

139346.en: Sounds important. I'll take care of it.

139348.en: I don't want to risk angering the Gallente. I'll pass.

139349.en: Something else has come up. I quit.

139350.en: You said you might have more work for me?

139351.en: A significant percentage of the Minmatar population resides within the Gallente Federation, forming a rather powerful political bloc. This bloc is one reason that the relations between Amarr and Gallente remain constantly tense.

139352.en: The data cube yielded the name of a single member of the powerful Minmatar political bloc in the Federation. This man was the contact that helped the slaves escape. Kill him and any who protect him.

139354.en: And here I thought you were brave, {[character]player.name}.

139355.en: I knew I could count on you. Remember that we're setting an example here.

139358.en: I hope I can find someone capable who'll be able to kill the Gallente contact before he finds out that he's a target. I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

139359.en: I hope I can find someone capable who'll be able to kill the Gallente contact before he finds out that he's a target. I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

139362.en: I'll make certain that he doesn't cause any more trouble.

139363.en: You won't have any more problems with that Minmatar collaborator.

139364.en: It isn't wise to go after someone with such high connections. I won't do it.

139365.en: I don't want to go after someone with such high connections. I'm done with this.

139366.en: Did that data chip have anything interesting on it?

139368.en:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} wants a massive shipment of Augumene right away, so we need you to get out there and bring some back. I've been looking for a miner who's experienced enough, with the right kind of ship, and maybe you fit the bill. Time is critical on this one. There's a big bonus for you if you can bring it in fast enough.

Pirates and claimjumpers abound in these parts, so you should also be prepared to defend your ship from such scavengers.

Finally, this amount of raw Augumene ore may require multiple trips unless you have a Hulk or a similarly large hauler for the job.

139370.en:
Some Amarr officer has gone crazy - he ignored orders, broke communications with his commanding officers, commandeered an Imperial Navy vessel, and then disappeared. Our intel says he's headed our way: apparently he's not willing to let freelance capsuleers handle the fight, and instead wants to be a part of it himself.

Fix this little problem for us and you will be well rewarded.

139371.en:
Due in large part to the values and teachings of the Amarr faith, the Amarr have the most extensive libraries, archives, and collections of artifacts pertaining to post-Eden life and, possibly, the EVE gate.

One of the heirs of the Ardishapur family, hailed as a paragon of the faith, has amassed what may be the largest array of religious artifacts in a private collection. Some of his pieces are even suspected to pre-date the closure of the EVE gate.

139374.en: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}.

139375.en: Here is your reward. You have truly earned it.

139377.en: Due to your sloth, the miners who discovered the artifact found another buyer, one from outside the faith. Thanks to your neglect, we may never discover the true religious significance of this piece of living history.

139378.en: Due to your sloth, the miners who discovered the artifact found another buyer, one from outside the faith. Thanks to your neglect, we may never discover the true religious significance of this piece of living history.

139381.en: I would be honored to undertake such a mission.

139382.en: I hope you find this as valuable as you thought it would be. The miners have already paid with their lives.

139383.en: I'm not going to go haring off over some unidentified piece of ancient junk. My time's worth more than that.

139384.en: I'm done haring off over some unidentified piece of ancient junk. My time's worth more than this.

139385.en: I thought you might have some work for me today.

139386.en:
Ship racing has become very popular in the past few years. Pilots race their ships to see who can complete a circuit the fastest and thus show off proper ship handling, attention to quick course corrections, and how much power can be coaxed out of a ship.

The Amarr have some of the best racers in the sector and to commemorate their successes, they are building a new racing area in one of our poorer systems to help stimulate the economy, while at the same time showcasing Amarr skill in flying the best ships in pod pilot hands today.

139387.en: Then I take it you've got a high-paying job for me, right?

139388.en: I'm getting a really bad feeling about this job, and I've learned to trust my gut. I'm out. And go easy on batting those eyelashes, {[character]agentID.name} — you'll pull a muscle.

139389.en: A new race track is being built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. During the final stages of building, we received reports of some ships bearing Gallente markings, and several suspicious "accidents" have occurred. Sabotage is suspected. Go find these ships and destroy them so that no harm will come to participants or viewers during the big race.

139390.en: If you want a clean-up job, hire a janitor.  Not interested.

139392.en: The Caldari cruiser is now dust. Would have been nice of you to let me know about the Guristas, though.

139393.en:
I have a task that must be done quickly, and it requires punitive force.

A new race track is being designed and built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and it is supposed to be the grandest and most beautiful and complicated tracks yet ever to exist in all of the known sectors! A substantial quantity of money and work have gone into this track, and there are plans to hold one of the largest races ever as soon as the track is finished.

However, some suspicious ships have been seen in the vicinity. They evade patrols, but we've received reports that they bear Gallente markings. A couple of "accidents" have already occurred while testing the track, and investigations have led to suspicion of sabotage.

We think that these Gallente ships have been sabotaging this new track, probably in hopes of killing many Holders and their families when the time comes for the great inaugural race.

I want you to put a stop to this nonsense before it has any further impact. Destroy those ships; it's time we sent a message.

139395.en: You are not the pilot I thought you were. I'll be sure to spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.

139397.en: Excellent. Do take care. Our intelligence on these ships is sketchy at best, so they may be more powerful than we know.

139398.en: I knew you were the right pilot for the job.

You may rest assured that I will spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.

139411.en: Your intelligence must be wrong because I can't find these mysterious ships. Find someone else who has nothing better to do than playing hide-and-seek with phantom troublemakers.

139412.en: You have work for me, then?

139413.en: I'm so happy to hear the ship is no longer an issue for us — and especially that you're okay, {[character]player.name}. And so sorry about those Guristas. You're right, I should have said something...

139414.en: {[character]player.name} — you are the absolute best! I knew today was my lucky day!

139415.en: That's so funny, {[character]player.name}, because I just got this funny sensation behind my eyes when I saw you walk in — sort of like an ulcer, but in my brain.

139416.en:
I do, in fact, have a little matter that needs your attention. It's rather... delicate.

My corporation recently had a small misunderstanding with a Caldari business rival. Fortunately, after some of our folks met with the Caldari to have a… discussion, our people managed to limp back here; unfortunately, they left the wreckage of the Caldari ship intact, including the ship's log.

Now, it would impact any future dealings we might have with the Caldari if this dispute became known to their authorities. I'm sure they'd insist on petty things like vengeance. So we'd rather that didn't happen. We'd like you to go destroy all evidence of the Caldari cruiser. It can be found at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

So, will you be a pal and do this for me?

139418.en: Destroy the Caldari cruiser at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} along with any other hostile ships you may encounter. No witnesses!

139419.en:
The worst enemy is the one who was once an ally. This is a lesson not lost on the Caldari Navy, for it was from within their own ranks that the seeds of the Guristas pirates were born.

The Guristas were founded by two ex-Caldari Navy members now known only as "Fatal" and "The Rabbit." Utilizing their knowledge of the Navy's procedures — and thus its weaknesses — these two renegades have confounded their previous employers for many years with their persistence and ingenuity.

The Guristas cannot totally disown their militaristic origins: among pirates, they remain arguably the most honorable among a dishonorable bunch. Yet spacefarers shouldn't take too much comfort from that fact, or from their amusing bunny-skull logo. The Guristas will still slit your throat if there's profit involved.

Honor, as many have learned, goes only so far when ISK is concerned.

139420.en: Funny you should mention the Guristas, because I kind of wanted an explanation about that. You knew they'd be there?

139421.en: I've just done the math, {[character]agentID.name}. Bunch of Guristas + me not trusting you = I quit.

139422.en: Sorry, {[character]agentID.name}, but no thanks. You seem about as trustworthy as a Thukker ship salesman. Go play some other sucker, 'cause I'm gone.

139423.en: I destroyed those Guristas, {[character]agentID.name}, and I got the ship log. But, uh, I checked it to make sure it's the right log, and it… well, it has some interesting information. Is there something you want to tell me?

139424.en: This job just keeps getting better and better. And yes, that's sarcasm. But yes, I'll do it — for the ISK. I can't spend your gratitude.

139427.en:
Hey {[character]player.name},

Just a quick note to let you know your laxity in retrieving that ship log has led to several Caldari vigilante attacks on my corporation. At last count, 200 people are dead. Have a nice day!

139429.en: I did say I was sorry about forgetting to mention the pirates… but it seems obvious you're just afraid to fight. Run along then, little egger, run along.

139430.en:
Oh, yeah, {[character]player.name}, about that....

Listen, give me a minute to wrap this up, and then come back and I'll explain everything, okay?

139431.en: It speaks very well of you that you aren't running away when things get hot, {[character]player.name}. I like that in a capsuleer.

139432.en:
You surprise me, to be honest. I would have thought that kind of complex addition quite beyond you.

Bye now.

139433.en:
I'm so sorry about those Guristas! You're right. I should have said something... but I knew you'd be able to handle it.

Anyway, it seems they boarded that Caldari cruiser before you arrived and took the ship's log. Now they're threatening to turn it over to the Caldari Navy if we don't pay up. We've got enough on our plate at the moment without fomenting open war with Caldari. Amarr'd just love that, huh?

So, we've tracked them to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If you could go and take care of them, I'd be really, really grateful.

139434.en: Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  and destroy the Guristas pirates there. Don't forget to recover the ship log that they stole from the Caldari cruiser. They won't be there long, so please hurry!

139435.en: Well, maybe. Kinda depends on what it is you tell me now and what you want next, really.

139436.en: I've just had a sudden attack of common sense, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm out of here before I end up in either a casket or a rubber room.

139437.en: Newsflash, {[character]agentID.name}! You're obviously out of your mind. I'm putting as much distance between you and me as humanly possible. See ya, crackpot!

139438.en: Well, it's done. Maybe not the way you wanted, but it's done. The buyer is dead, the pirates are dead, you've got your secret package back, and I need a drink. Now pay up!

139439.en: You've lied to me, you've manipulated me, and you've almost gotten me killed. I've got to admit, {[character]agentID.name} — I'm starting to like your style. I'm in!

139442.en:
{[character]player.name},

It seems unfortunate that you would go so far in this operation only to wander off right at the end. And since you had the prototype, we couldn't get paid, either. Not a good idea to upset Covert Ops that way, you know? Really Bad Idea.

139443.en:
{[character]player.name},

How difficult was it to just deliver the prototype? What, the thought of a few Guristas out for revenge stopped you? Maybe you just didn't want it enough. Ever think of that? Very, very disappointed, me.

139444.en: But I'm really in deep with Covert Ops! I have an honorary badge and everything! And a set of spy glasses, too. I'm the real deal!

139445.en: Congratulations, {[character]player.name}! Not only have you done the impossible, but you've made me 100,000 ISK in a side bet! My partners thought you'd die long before this! Thanks a bunch! Here's your reward, and a little extra besides! Don't spend it all in one place, champ.

139447.en: Wow. What a build-up to the letdown you turned out to be, {[character]player.name}. Oh, well — there must remain some expendable suckers out there I can use, I'm sure.

We have a bit of a problem, {[character]player.name}. A corporate executive seems to have used some rather unorthodox methods to try to speed up production in his mining fields, and the strain this placed on the labor force there has led to a wildcat strike which has shut down production in that field entirely, causing materials shortages all the way up our supply chain. Of course, this is entirely unacceptable; it is imperative that this strike be brought to a close immediately and production resume as soon as possible.

Corporate security is stretched rather thin in this sector, so we would like you to go to the mining facility in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and eliminate any threats to corporate assets. You should be aware that the striking miners have taken control of the facility's defense grid and armed many of their mining vessels with makeshift weapons, so you should expect heavy resistance.

Avoid any collateral damage to corporate assets if possible; we don't want this strike to cost us any more than it already has.

139481.en:
I always have work for a good pod pilot.

It has recently come to my attention that a small group of nearby pirates stumbled across something rather unusual. While mining for ore, they made a lucky discovery-- they uncovered what appears to be a religious artifact.

As you know, such an object is of great importance to all Amarr. There are many Holders who would pay large sums to get their hands on such a find; even better, there are collectors among the royal family who would give large rewards to add such a thing to their private collections.

I want you to find these rogue miners and retrieve this artifact from them. Bring it here, and you will be well rewarded.

The attack on the meeting between the Gallente and Minmatar emissaries went perfectly. Now we need to finish the job. After escaping the scene of the attack, the Minmatar ambassador was whisked away to a nearby staging area.

A raid on the Minmatar delegation now will look like a reprisal raid from the Gallente delegation, and since the Minmatar know they weren't responsible for the initial attack, they'll be even angrier. We have reason to believe that the enemy diplomats have been transferred aboard the Minmatar flagship to ensure their safety. It's the only battleship in the delegation, and it must be destroyed.
