140113.en: Wonderful! You will be greatly rewarded for this service.

140114.en:
The Sisters of EVE are a religious humanitarian aid organization. They believe that heaven resides on the other side of the EVE gate, and if they can get back through the gate, they will be able to talk to God. Allying their religion with science, they frequently experiment on the EVE gate, with the goal of one day unlocking its secrets.

The Sisters are politically neutral, with members from every faction. They have been providing aid to those in need since the Gallente-Caldari War. They have a number of stations set up outside of empire borders.

140115.en: A Caldari pilot who has been helpful to the Empire in the past was ambushed by Gallente ships and managed to limp away to the safe haven of a station run by the Sisters of EVE. Go make sure that the lingering Gallente ship that is waiting for her to leave will not be a problem.

140117.en:
The Gallente have ambushed a Caldari pilot who has been very helpful to us in the past. Her vessel suffered serious damage, and she barely escaped.

She managed to reach a station operated by the Sisters of EVE, who provided her with help. However, her ship is still damaged, and there is a Gallente ship that is waiting to finish her off as soon as she leaves the station's shelter.

I would like you to assist her by making certain that the Gallente ship will no longer be a problem.

140118.en: Remember: in helping our allies, we help ourselves. It's yourself you're leaving in the lurch here, friend.

140119.en: Take care not to underestimate the Gallente.

140120.en: Well done. Aid given to our allies is aid that will be returned to us twofold in the times to come.

140121.en: Remember: in helping our allies, we help ourselves. It's yourself you're leaving in the lurch here, friend.

140122.en: Due to your laziness and disregard, the Gallente ship managed to destroy our Caldari friend. You have cost us a valuable and proven ally; your reputation will suffer for this.

140123.en: Due to your laziness and disregard, the Gallente ship managed to destroy our Caldari friend. You have cost us a valuable and proven ally; your reputation will suffer for this.

140127.en: That vulturous Gallente ship is no longer a threat to anyone.

140128.en: The Caldari can take care of their own. I'm sure she'll be fine.

140129.en: I don't have time for this anymore. The Caldari can take care of their own. I'm sure she'll be fine.

140130.en: I heard you had a job for me?

140131.en: The Caldari-Gallente war began based upon differences of thought and opinion of the Federation they were both a part of. It ripped the Federation completely down the middle and became particularly vicious.

140132.en: A Caldari envoy is soliciting our assistance for his particular area of space. However, his transport ship is poorly guarded. Meet him at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and escort him the rest of the way here.

140134.en: A Caldari envoy is soliciting our assistance for his particular area of space. However, his transport ship is poorly guarded. Meet him at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and escort him the rest of the way here.

140135.en: Your reputation will suffer for this.

140136.en: Keep him safe and you will be well rewarded.

140137.en: Excellent job. Here is your reward.

140138.en: Your reputation will suffer for this.

140139.en:
Thanks to you, the Caldari envoy had to wait for another transport, and in that time, a Gallente ship managed to sneak into the area and attack the vessel he was on. Unfortunately for all involved, the assassination succeeded.

The loss of our ally is your fault.

140140.en:
Thanks to you, the Caldari envoy had to wait for another transport, and in that time, a Gallente ship managed to sneak into the area and attack the vessel he was on. Unfortunately for all involved, the assassination succeeded.

The loss of our ally is your fault.

140144.en: Here he is, safe and sound.

140145.en: I don't have time to ferry around pampered envoys. Find someone else for your babysitting job.

140146.en: I don't have time to ferry around pampered envoys. Find someone else for your babysitting job.

140148.en:
Supply and munitions interdiction raids are a critical part of ongoing operations against the Gallente Federation. Depriving the enemy of the materiel necessary to sustain the fight can only make it easier for our own forces to prevail.

After recent fighting in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, the enemy is no doubt attempting to undertake just such re-supply operations. There are State interdiction patrols active in the area and I'd like you to lend them a hand. If you see any enemy transports, destroy them immediately.

140149.en:
Of course.

Supply and munitions interdiction raids are a critical part of ongoing operations against the Gallente Federation. Depriving the enemy of the materiel necessary to sustain the fight can only make it easier for our own forces to prevail.

After recent fighting in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, the enemy is no doubt attempting to undertake just such re-supply operations. There are State interdiction patrols active in the area and I'd like you to lend them a hand. If you see any enemy transports, destroy them immediately.

Will you do this? There's a sizable bounty in it for you if you're successful.

140151.en: I knew I could count on you.

140152.en: I have deposited the funds in your account. Check back with me as soon as you're able – I have another task for you.

140153.en: Very well. I'll find a real patriot to do it instead. You are dismissed, pilot.

140154.en: Was I unclear in my explanation of the work I expected of you? You have accomplished nothing since taking on the task we discussed. This is unacceptable. I have made note of this dereliction of duty in your permanent record. Perhaps in the future you'll see fit to follow through on your obligations.

140155.en: Even as we speak another Gallente task force is re-supplying in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It appears that our attempts to stop them from rearming have been unsuccessful. No matter, we will try again when the opportunity presents itself. At that time, be ready {[character]player.name}. I don't want to let another chance to hit a soft target pass us by.

140158.en: Bounty's the magic word. Count me in.

140159.en: I destroyed an enemy convoy. Now where's that bounty you mentioned?

140160.en: No thanks; I'm not interested in patrolling.

140161.en: Sorry, I'm not going to be able to complete this task.

140162.en: I'm looking for work. Do you have anything for me?

140163.en:
Chemical warfare may not be as flashy as space lasers or doomsday weapons, but it just might decide the outcome of this war we're in. After all, what's the value of taking over territory if all your planets are uninhabitable? Of course, our foes have found counters to most of the known chemical agents. So the key to victory will be new compounds.

That's why I want you to acquire a big bunch of Augumene for us. The stuff is insanely toxic, hence its absence on the market. But in this case, its very toxicity is what we want to harness.

140164.en: Hey, suit yerself, pal. Heh. I'm sure there's a "common pilot" around here somewheres without that stuck-up capsuleer vibe you got in spades.

140165.en: Hey, suit yourself, pal. I'm sure there's a "common pilot" around here who's not quite so stuck up.

140166.en:
{[character]player.name}, a local boss who basically runs the {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} station nearby has been a thorn in my side for years, but my boss has finally given me the thumbs up for a, um, hostile takeover.

I need you to transport a unit of my hired marines over there so the station can be brought under ... er, new management. Do not get involved personally. Just get the soldiers into the docking area and then look the other way.

140167.en:
{[character]player.name}, a local boss who basically runs the {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} station nearby has been a thorn in my side for years, but my boss has finally given me the thumbs up for a hostile takeover.

I need you to transport a unit of my hired marines over there so the station can be brought under ... er, new management. Do not get involved personally. Just get the soldiers into the docking area and then look the other way.

140168.en: Not bad, rookie. Not bad at all. You've a long way left to go to prove your worth, however.

140169.en:
Nothing major, which is why you're getting the job. Prove to us you can handle this and we'll have plenty more to throw you later on. Screw up, however, and it's going on your record.

We've got an Imperial Navy Field Commander who recently arrived inside our own borders. Communications taps have revealed plans to consolidate their position and move more ships in. If we allow them room to breathe, they'll have Navy Battleships and perhaps even more entrenched in the system within a week. You're going to see to it that this doesn't happen.

Fly over there and kill that commander and any of his guards present. Without him calling the shots, his people will fall back to regroup, and that buys us enough time to reinforce the area properly with skilled pilots.

Briefing's over, rookie: move your ass.

140170.en: We've got an Imperial Navy Field Commander who recently arrived inside our own borders. Communications taps have revealed plans to consolidate their position and move more ships in. You're going to see to it that this doesn't happen. Fly over there; kill that commander and any of his guards present. This should scatter their forces long enough for our own reinforcements to arrive.

140171.en: We've got Minmatar Republic Field Commander who recently arrived inside our own borders. Communications taps have revealed plans to consolidate their position and move more ships in. You're going to see to it that this doesn't happen. Fly over there; kill that commander and any of his guards present. This should scatter their forces long enough for our own reinforcements to arrive.

140172.en:
Nothing major, which is why you're getting the job. Prove to us you can handle this and we'll have plenty more to throw you later on. Screw up, however, and it's going on your record.

We've got a Republic Fleet Field Commander who recently arrived inside our own borders. Communications taps have revealed plans to consolidate their position and move more ships in. If we allow them room to breathe, they'll have Fleet battleships and perhaps even more entrenched in the system within a week.

You're going to see to it that this doesn't happen. Fly over there and kill that commander and any of his guards present. Without him calling the shots, his people will fall back to regroup, and that buys us enough time to reinforce the area properly.

Briefing's over, rookie: move your ass.

140173.en: Minmatar combat units have become increasingly bold with their incursions into Amarr Empire sovereign space, even after the Elder Fleet's recent defeat at Jamyl Sarum's hands. At times, Amarr field commanders in charge of small units are not even on authorized missions; tribal vendettas and raids to recover Matari slaves are usually at the root of these sorties.

140175.en: We've got a Federation Navy Field Commander who recently arrived inside our own borders. Communications taps have revealed plans to consolidate their position and move more ships in. You're going to see to it that this doesn't happen. Fly over there; kill that commander and any of his guards present. This should scatter their forces long enough for our own reinforcements to arrive.

140176.en: Not bad, rookie. Not bad at all. You've a long way left to go to prove your worth, however.

140177.en: Gallente Federation combat units have become increasingly bold flying into Caldari sovereign space. At times, the commanders in charge of their small units are not even on authorized missions: Glory and revenge are strong motivators. Though the problem is by no means significant or crippling, the individualism for which Gallenteans are known has found its way even into the Federation Navy.

140178.en:
Nothing major, which is why you're getting the job. Prove to us you can handle this and we'll have plenty more to throw you later on. Screw up, however, and it's going on your record.

We've got a Federation Navy Field Commander who recently arrived inside our own borders. Communications taps have revealed plans to consolidate their position and move more ships in. If we allow them room to breathe, they'll have Navy battleships, and perhaps even more, entrenched in the system within a week.

You're going to see to it that this doesn't happen. Fly over there and kill that commander and any of his guards present. Without him calling the shots, his people will fall back to regroup, and that buys us enough time to reinforce the area.

140179.en: I can't finish this mission; there're too many hostiles getting in my way.

140180.en: We've got a Caldari Navy Field Commander who recently arrived inside our own borders. Communications taps have revealed plans to consolidate their position and move more ships in. You're going to see to it that this doesn't happen. Fly over there; kill that commander and any of his guards present. This should scatter their forces long enough for our own reinforcements to arrive.

140181.en: Don't worry - I won't let you down.

140182.en: Mission complete: The Field Commander and his guards have been dealt with.

140183.en: Not bad, rookie. Not bad at all. You've a long way to go to prove your worth, however.

140184.en: I had a suspicion you would balk at the thought of live combat. You'd best sort your act out, rookie.

140185.en: Caldari State combat units have little compunction about raiding into Gallente sovereign space; the State navy is perhaps the most disciplined in the universe, but anti-Gallentean sentiment currently runs very high, and even disciplined soldier occasionally let emotion overrule duty.

140187.en:
Nothing major, which is why you're getting the job. Prove to us you can handle this and we'll have plenty more to throw you later on. Screw up, however, and it's going on your record.

We've got a Caldari Navy Field Commander who recently arrived inside our own borders. Communications taps have revealed plans to consolidate their position and move more ships in. If we allow them room to breathe, they might have Navy battleships and even worse entrenched in our system within a week. You're going to see to it that this doesn't happen.

Fly over there and kill that commander and his guards. Without him calling the shots, his people will most likely fall back to regroup, and that buys us enough time to reinforce the area.

So, briefing's over rookie - move your ass!

140188.en: I can't finish this mission - too many hostiles in my way.

140189.en: I am relieved to see you have such good judgement. I'm sending you the location now; move quickly, before their compound is reinforced once again.

140190.en: During a routine recon operation in a contested sector, we discovered a large facility housing thousands of Minmatar citizens. In all likelihood they are assisting Republic forces in some way, either directly or indirectly. We have an opportunity for to remove that threat, whatever it may be. Kill them. Kill them all.

140191.en: I have done as you asked - the facility is destroyed.

140192.en: You have done well, pilot: That seems to be the only way we can rest reassured those Minmatar scum pose no further threat. Good work.

140193.en: No, I won't do this. We should investigate before we start shooting. Get back to me when you've done so, and then I might be interested.

140194.en: "Those who would seek peace in times of war must stay unmistakably clear of it. Withdraw yourselves from the view of your enemy and remain unseen, for even the most innocent action is a threat in the eyes of your enemy. This you must understand, for to tempt fate too often is invariably to meet it."

140195.en: The Pacifist Manifesto: Chapter I, Verso xxiv.

140196.en:
There is, and I hope you will understand the importance of what I am about to ask you.

During a routine recon operation in a contested sector, we discovered a large facility housing thousands of Minmatar citizens. We are unsure why they are there. In all likelihood they are assisting Republic forces in some way, either directly or indirectly. It matters little - they are savage scum who are obviously up to something.

That defensive force they had installed just recently moved elsewhere, and scouts tell us that the compound is now sitting largely defenseless. This represents an opportunity for us to remove the threat, whatever it may be. Kill them. Kill them all.

140197.en: I will not do this. I cannot kill people who may well be innocent bystanders, savages though they are.

140198.en: Save me your confused morality, pilot. They are clearly more than innocent bystanders: Look at where they are and how heavily they were guarded! You've fallen into precisely the trap they wished to set. What a dismal display of clouded judgment. You have failed this test of faith!

140199.en: I am relieved to see you have such good judgement. I'm sending you the location now; move quickly before their compound is reinforced once again.

140200.en:
During a routine recon operation inside a nearby contested sector, we discovered a large facility housing thousands of Gallente; in all likelihood they are mercenaries assisting Federation Navy forces in some way. We have an opportunity to remove the threat, though, whatever it may be.

Though it is a grim task I ask of you, it is one that must be done. Destroy the facility, for the security of our great State.

140201.en: I have done as you asked: the facility is destroyed.

140202.en: You have done well, pilot. Those Federation guerrillas can pose no further threat.

140203.en: "Those who would seek peace in times of war must stay unmistakably clear of it. Withdraw yourselves from the view of your enemy and remain unseen, for even the most innocent action is a threat in the eyes of your enemy. This you must understand, for to tempt fate too often is invariably to meet it."

140204.en: The Pacifist Manifesto: Chapter I, Verso xxiv

140205.en:
There is, and I hope you will understand the importance of what I am about to ask you.

During a recon operation in a nearby contested sector, we discovered a large facility housing thousands of Gallente. We've had no luck infiltrating the compound, so we are unsure why they are here. In all likelihood they are assisting Federation forces in some way, though: When we first discovered the facility, it was heavily guarded. They are obviously up to something.

That defensive force they had installed just recently moved elsewhere, however, and the compound is now sitting largely defenseless. This represents an opportunity for us to remove the potential threat. Though it is a grim task I ask of you, it is one that must be done. Can I rely on you to carry it out?

140206.en: I cannot kill thousands of people unless I am assured of their guilt, {[character]agentID.name}, Gallente or otherwise.

140207.en: Spare me your philosophizing - we are at war! They are clearly more than innocent bystanders; just look at where they are and how heavily they were guarded. Obviously you are not the right person for this job. I will find another.

140219.en: "Those who would seek peace in times of war must stay unmistakably clear of it. Withdraw yourselves from the view of your enemy and remain unseen, for even the most innocent action is a threat in the eyes of your enemy. This you must understand, for to tempt fate too often is invariably to meet it."

140220.en: The Pacifist Manifesto: Chapter I, Verso xxiv.

140222.en: Good. I like your spirit. I'm sending you the location now: Move quickly, before their compound is reinforced once again.

140223.en: That's why I've come. You have work you can give me?

140224.en: What if these people are nothing but innocent bystanders? Even if they are Amarrian, do we not become what we hate if we simply kill them outright?!

140225.en: This is war, pilot! Do you think the Heirs and their high-minded Paladins would offer our people the same courtesy?! You fool. They are clearly more than innocent bystanders: Why else were they so heavily guarded? You've disappointed me once. Do not let it happen again.

140226.en: For years, the booming Gallente economy has lured millions of Minmatar immigrants from their homes in the Republic, where poverty and unemployment are chronic. Often freed slaves come to the Federation, where they take menial jobs for little pay. These immigrant workers have further fueled Gallente business ventures by allowing them to reduce labor-related production costs.

140227.en: The Federation is relying on the cheap labor provided by Minmatar immigrants to provide munitions. Even now, the Federation is building new factories to take advantage of these “human assets.” These assets must be captured or destroyed, just like any other enemy war materiel. One of our spies has managed to obtain information about a group of these workers being transported through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Capture them and bring them here.

140229.en:
As you may have noticed on your last interdiction raid, the transports you destroyed were of Minmatar origin. It seems that the Federation is relying on the cheap labor provided by Minmatar immigrants to provide munitions.

Even now the Federation is building new factories and taking advantage of these “human assets.” One of our spies has managed to obtain information about a group of these workers being transported through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They must be captured, just like any other enemy war materiel.

Still interested?

140230.en: Dammit, you could have told me earlier.

140231.en: Remember, those “workers” are of no value to us dead.

140232.en: Stop by again when you're available. We're going to interrogate some of these Minmatar vagrants before shipping them off. Maybe we'll be able to find out where they were headed.

140233.en: Good to know that you don't have the stomach to do what's necessary.

140236.en: No problem. I'll get right on it.

140238.en: That sounds an awful lot like a slave raid to me. Count me out.

140239.en: On second thought, I'm not going to take this job after all.

140241.en: Suit yourself, but just be aware that every hour that factory is operating, it's cranking out ammunition that might be used to speed up your next clone activation.

140242.en: I knew I could count on you.

140243.en: Good job, {[character]player.name}. You've struck a major blow to the Gallente war effort.

140246.en: That arms factory is no longer a current event.

140248.en: Sorry, I'm not going to be able to destroy that munitions plant after all.

140250.en:
There are few who can deny the majestic beauty of an ice field: the slowly rotating towers of glistening blue-green ice set against the colder backdrop of the stars can give even the most jaded pilot pause. Yet such beauty hides a darker truth: if you are not prepared, an ice field can quickly become your very own sparkling graveyard.

While some ice fields can be found in Empire space, the rarer– and more profitable– ice ores are found in 0.0 space. As always, low sec can promise more ISK– or it can promise the dubious thrill of seeing your ship pounded into dust by eager pirates. Far too many inexperienced pilots have seen their mining barges blown apart-- with the hours and ISK needed to outfit them-- now so much vapor floating around their blinking pod.

Yet for most, the lure of the ice fields is too much to resist. With the sure promise of such treasures as Strontium Clathrates and Liquid Ozone, to name a few, the dangers of low sec will be dared. And even if it all ends in a fiery explosion, pilots can still enjoy the way their ship's destruction makes the ice sparkle all that more beautifully, if only for a few, rare seconds.

140251.en: {[character]player.name}, I need you to go and procure 10 units of a very particular ice-- Azure Ice, I believe, is what you're looking for on your scanner. I also need it within the next 24 hours, so get to that ice field!

140252.en: Cold Beauty: The Irresistible Danger of Ice Mining

140253.en:
I've been having a spot of bother filling an order, {[character]player.name}. It's starting to affect my usually sunny disposition. I'm hoping you can clear this off my docket, and bring the smile back to my face.

My client requires hydrogen isotopes to run her control tower, and she's getting a little snippy about the time it's taking me to provide it. She's even sent along a few assassins to vent her displeasure. No patience, that woman.

{[character]player.name}, I need you to procure 10 units of a very particular ice-- Azure Ice, I believe, is what you're looking for on your scanner; I can extract the hydrogen myself. I've lost a few good ships and a few incompetent pilots in the ice fields trying to fill this order, and I really need you to live up to your reputation, {[character]player.name}-- within the next 24 hours. Can I count on you, {[character]player.name}?

140254.en: Or it could be that you need a Courage Implant along with an upgrade of Job Dedication? Just tossing it out there, {[character]player.name}.

140255.en: You're good with the bravado, {[character]player.name}, I'll give you that– now just get me my ice!

140256.en: Finally, someone with a degree of competence! Thanks for your work, {[character]player.name}. Just mind that airlock door on your way out...

140257.en: Well, you do live up to your reputation-- as a selfish churl. Good riddance, {[character]player.name}!

140258.en: {[character]player.name}– just a quick note to let you know your incompetence has had some rather spectacular consequences. Since you failed to provide the hydrogen isotopes I requested, I've had to deal with assassination attempts courtesy of both my client and my CEO. If you wish to make amends, please take a stroll through the nearest airlock. Thanks, {[character]player.name}!

140259.en: Perhaps my instructions were too complex for you, {[character]player.name}, but I needed that ice mining job done in 24 hours– not you making up your mind in 24 hours. Since the chronometer's ticking, I've gone and found someone who understands the concepts of ‘time pressure' and ‘manners'. If you want to apologize, please go fly into a black hole.

140262.en: Ice mining in low sec– I can't think of a better way to spend the day, {[character]agentID.name}. I'd even do it for free, but not today!

140263.en: What did I tell you, {[character]agentID.name}? Here's the ice you need, with time to spare.

140264.en: Sorry, {[character]agentID.name}-- I like to stay frosty with my weapons turrets, not some boring mining laser. I'm off to find work a little more glorious than this– goodbye!

140265.en: I'm not really feeling this job, {[character]agentID.name}. It could be the constant pirate attacks, or the sheer boredom of mining frozen water rocks.  Hard to say, but either way, I'm gone.

140266.en: If I don't live up to my reputation, I'll open the airlock for you, {[character]agentID.name}.  So what do you have for me?

140267.en: Might be.... What have you got for me?

140268.en: Sorry, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm not going to be able to finish this assignment.

140269.en: I don't really care too much for the Khanid Kingdom, or for any Amarrians, actually. No way I'm going to help them.

140270.en: Well, I did my part. Have we got the Minmatar on the run?

140271.en: Sure, I'll do it. Minmatar, Amarr - who cares, as long as I get to shoot them in the face, right?

140272.en: Sorry to hear that, {[character]player.name}. Your loss.

140273.en: Yes, we do - tails between their legs. Good work, {[character]player.name}.

140275.en:
Well, as you know, the Cartel has a pretty good thing going here in Curse – we're able to strike into the heart of all the other empires and remain relatively safe from retaliation. Now that the conflict between the Amarr Empire and the Minmatar Republic has heated up, though, we're getting pressure from both sides. The Minmatar have been pushing hard in some places, and now we've decided that it's time to push back.

We've been working with representatives of the Khanid Kingdom to give the Minmatar a surprise. The Republic has been building up forces in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. In exchange for some generous financial compensation, we've agreed to help the Khanids push the Minmatar out. But we need a good capsuleer to keep the light Minmatar escorts busy while we help the Khanids destroy the larger vessels.

Will you do it?

140276.en: No, I'm sorry, {[character]player.name}. Sorry you don't have what it takes.

140278.en:
The Minmatar Republic has been building up forces in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. In exchange for some generous financial compensation, we've agreed to help the Khanids push the Minmatar out. But we need a capsuleer to fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to keep the light Minmatar escorts busy while we help the Khanids destroy the larger vessels.

We've loaded the location into your NeoCom. Destroy any Republic vessels you encounter there.

140279.en:
The Khanid Kingdom is a small empire of a dozen or so systems that was founded by the renegade Amarr Heir Khanid II. Rather than commit ritual suicide when he failed to attain the imperial throne, Khanid declared independence from the Empire. The next few years were spent fighting a rebellion by Khanid's brother and fellow heir Dakos, and turning back an invasion by the Empire.

Since then, Khanid's rule has continued, his small empire has prospered, and trade relations with his former imperial enemies have expanded considerably. The Kingdom acts as a small point of contact between the secretive people of Amarr and the rest of civilized space. Today, the kingdom's primary enemies are the Minmatar, who, despite Khanid II's secession, still see it as an ally of the hated Amarr Empire.

140280.en: Heh. I wondered why your security officers were being so nice, {[character]agentID.name}. Continue the trend and give me a decent job, why don't you?

140281.en: This mission isn't really for me. I like blowing things up, not sneaking around like a... well, like a sneaky person. I'm going to do something a little more… uh, epic.

140282.en: Sorry — I'm not flying into an Amarr base with anything short of a Ragnarok. Dying for a holo-reel isn't how I plan to go out.

140283.en: Get out the firewater, boys, 'cause we got reason to celebrate. Mission complete: Minmatar victory.

140284.en: Any chance to wipe some Amarr off the roster is one I'll take. Count me in.

140287.en: I waited for as long as I could, {[character]player.name}, but I had to go with someone else on this job. It's unfortunate you found this task beneath your notice — it could have led to bigger and better things. But, uh, I guess not for you!

140288.en: I'm at a loss, {[character]player.name} — I thought my directions were fairly straightforward. Perhaps I should maybe hold your hand next time?

140289.en: Oh, I perfectly understand, {[character]player.name} — a mission like this requires courage, skill, and heroism… qualities you are clearly lacking. Have you forgotten you're one of the bloody immortals!?

140290.en: That is good news… but let's not get too far ahead of ourselves. I've just got some disturbing news about that broadcast plot — come back in a minute, will you, and then maybe I'll have the details sorted out.

140291.en: Perfect: I thought this was your sort of job, my friend. It needs courage, skill, and heroism — and you've got 'em all.

140292.en: Well, you gave it your best, {[character]player.name}. Keep telling yourself that. It'll ease the sting of cowardice you should be feeling.

140293.en:
A job, eh? Hm. Yeah, I've got something for you. Pretty urgent, too.

Seems the Amarr have been broadcasting holo-reels of their military "victory" over the Elder Fleet when that Sarum bitch returned to power. Thing is, we've found that someone has set up a broadcast hub to send the damned holos out here — into Minmatar space! I guess they're trying to intimidate us, or to play some kind of psychological war. Well, you know how happy that makes me. Which is to say, not at all.

Anyway, {[character]player.name}, I'd like you to head out there and blow that broadcast array of theirs to bits. Take your favorite ship, along with a couple friends, maybe, and head to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

Time to disrupt a lot of bedtime stories...

140295.en: Infiltrate the secret Amarr deadspace complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and destroy the communications hub found there.

140296.en:
A key element in sustaining an Empire is maintaining control, however illusory. This lesson of Imperial longevity has been much on the Amarr Empire's mind of late.

The Jovian War. The Minmatar Rebellion. Gallente interference. The Caldari threat. All of these and more have seemed to herald the twilight of the Empire, and even with the miraculous return of Heir Apparent Jamyl Sarum, many Amarr are skeptical. Faith can hold one for only so long, it seems.

The last thing the Amarr Empire needs now is civil unrest, and what better way to occupy the minds of its citizenry than a good, righteous war? To that end, Amarr Intelligence frequently provides footage of Amarr's victories over the rebellious Minmatar for an eager and appreciative public. The fact that certain critics claim much of the footage is (re)constructed by skilled holo-efx techs is irrelevant: All that matters is that the people are happy and not asking questions.

Because the last thing any Empire wants is people asking too many questions. The wrong questions can be hard to control.

140297.en: Well, you've got my interest: What's happened?

140298.en: This is getting way too hot for me, {[character]agentID.name}. To hell with the politics — break out the Fleet if you want that code bad enough.

140299.en:
You want me to take on the Angel Cartel? Here's an even better idea: you pay me for the holoreel job, and I walk away from this one.

Yeah… yeah, I like that idea better.

140300.en: I got a little singed, but the job's done. Here's the data chip — just wipe the Angel blood off and you're good to go.

140301.en: Now this is more like it! Consider that code acquired.

140302.en: Data Chip? Encryption Codes? Not in My Hand?

140305.en: Fine, {[character]player.name}. Some champion you turned out to be. You know, you could do with a new wardrobe. Something in yellow would be appropriate, I think.

140306.en: You are amazing, no lie — and it looks like we need to you keep it up: More trouble, it seems.

140307.en: I'm happy you're happy, {[character]player.name} — but the timer's ticking. Now go!

140308.en: Fine, just fine.  But a question before you go: How do you fit your tail between your legs inside that egg of yours? Is it kind of cramped? Or just kind of embarrassing?

140309.en:
Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and retrieve the data chip with the encryption codes from the Angel Cartel ship there, and then return to your agent with the chip. 
<font color = #EE3B3B>Be sure you check the timer for this mission; you won't have too long before the Angels are sure to clear out.</font>

140310.en:
Whatever their other gifts, the Amarr are very good at two things: piety and self-justification. Both of these qualities, but most assuredly the second, come in handy when one considers the issue of slavery.

Since slavery is a consistently inherent theme in their religious doctrine (and how can something be wrong if faith allows it?), the Amarr must contend at all times with the disgust other races feel toward slavery. Chief among their opponents are the Gallente, whose displeasure is undoubtedly fueled by the many transplanted Minmatar flooding their homeworlds and stations. In the halcyon days of the Empire, the Amarr would easily have dismissed such concerns — but recent history has brought to some Amarr, at least, both humility and prudence.

Yet the need for slaves has not diminished — and in fact, since the recent Elder Fleet "recovery" effort in Amarr space, that need has grown terribly. However, the Amarr tradition of collecting slaves has necessarily become problematic for those Heirs and Holders, who may face trade embargoes and similar punitive actions from other nations. So many Amarr look surreptitiously to more "independent" sources of slaves — sources who don't care for any optics outside of their own bank balances.

140312.en:
My techs here have come across some disturbing information. We were monitoring that holo-reel hub and its vicinity, and just before you neutralized the array, we intercepted a garbled message from a nearby Angel Cartel ship… sent to the Amarr homeworld. It was pretty broken up, but we did make out the words "Minmatar" and "payment." We must know more.

We've managed to track the Angel ship that made that broadcast to an outpost that's, surprisingly, not too far from here. We need the code to decrypt that message, and that ship seems our best bet.

Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and get that ship's log, no matter what it takes.

And you'll have to make it snappy, 'cause I'm pretty sure the Angels won't hang around there too long — you won't have much time once you accept this mission!

140313.en: Yeah, I'm up for it. What do we need done?

140314.en: I think I've done enough for the Minmatar people, don't you? It's someone else's turn to step up. I'm done with this job.

140315.en: If rescuing our own people from slavers isn't a job for the Republic Fleet, then what is? I'm not risking my ship because the navy refuses to do its job.

140316.en: I've returned with the rescued slaves. And I've wiped out every single Cartel ship involved in their abduction. You have to admit, {[character]agentID.name} — I am pretty awesome.

140317.en: There are no worse scum than slave raiders. It'll be my pleasure to wipe them from the stars.

140320.en:
You leave me speechless, {[character]player.name}. I would have thought rescuing your own people from slavery would be a priority. Obviously not….

I just don't know what more to say.

140321.en: I rather hope you're dead, {[character]player.name}, because there's no other excuse for allowing our people to be enslaved. I'd hate to think you just decided you couldn't be bothered.

140322.en: If blaming others helps you rationalize your cowardice, {[character]player.name}, then so be it. Take your "worthy self" and get out of my sight.

140323.en: I'd have to agree with your rather modest assessment, yes. You have served both the Republic Fleet and our people with honor. Such exemplary work deserves an appropriate reward. Enjoy, hero!

140324.en: Spoken like a true warrior, {[character]player.name}.  Now make those pirate dogs beg for mercy. And offer none.

140325.en: Fine. Know this, though: Your blatant selfishness may have condemned those poor souls to indentured servitude, or worse. Let that comfort you at night.

140326.en:
My techs decrypted the rest of that message, thanks to the code you recovered. It seems those Cartel ships you destroyed were part of a gang that've been moonlighting as freelance slave raiders. They're supplying the Amarr with slaves from outlying worlds! They've been abducting entire families living in isolated areas so the alarm won't be raised for weeks to come.

That ends now.

We've managed to track the Angel slaver ships to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, with — according to the message — a hundred of our people on board. We could send in the Fleet, but frankly they're still reeling, and they just might not get there in time. I need you to rescue those people, {[character]player.name}. Bring in whoever you need to help you on this one: Just get it done.

140328.en:
Eradicate all pirate ships at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and then rescue the slaves from the Cartel ships.

You might want to go in with some backup — intel says there's a bunch of the buggers out there.

140329.en:
In the heinous world of spaceship piracy, only the worst — or best, depending on your outlook — rise to the top and stay there. The Angel Cartel is among the very few pirate organizations that can claim this dubious honor.

The Cartel is the most widespread criminal organization blackening the space lanes. There are many reasons for this, chief among them being that the Angels fully embrace the sound business policy of diversity. Outside of common piracy, the Angels have their fingers in most illegal pies, be they protection rackets, industrial blackmail, or murder for hire. There are also rumors the Cartel is involved in even more despicable operations — yet attempts to investigate these claims have only produced numerous law enforcement corpses.

Most spacers know that to cross the Cartel is tantamount to suicide. Without mercy, without compassion, and allegedly armed with long-lost Jovian technology, the Cartel is best avoided by those with a fondness for breathing.

But sometimes even pirates can go too far....

140330.en: We've had a chance to interrogate some of the prisoners you brought back. Fortune smiles upon us – we've learned the location of the munitions plant in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to which they were headed. That factory must be destroyed as soon as possible.

140331.en: I thought so. We've had a chance to interrogate some of the prisoners you brought back. Fortune smiles upon us – we've learned the location of the munitions plant in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to which they were headed. That factory must be destroyed as soon as possible.

140332.en:
When I did not hear back from you after assigning you the task of destroying that munitions plant, I feared the worst. I took the liberty of assigning another pilot to the task, and I am happy to report that the factory has been destroyed.

If you find yourself in need of work in the future, please do not hesitate to look me up. I'm sure I can find something for you to do.

Something less important.

140334.en:
When I did not hear back from you after assigning you the task of destroying that munitions plant, I feared the worst. I took the liberty of assigning another pilot to the task, and I am happy to report that the factory has been destroyed.

If you find yourself in need of work in the future, please do not hesitate to look me up. I'm sure I can find something for you to do.

Something less important.

140336.en: Well, looks like your waiting has paid off. Now get out there and do this!

140337.en:
Have you seen my daughter, Isone Flosin, by any chance? She went missing some time ago while inside the Roden Shipyard Outpost in Fluekele. If you find her, tell her I'm very displeased and she should come see me immediately.

I heard Nilla Elermare was asking about Isone, too. You may want to start by talking to her.

140338.en:
Have you seen my daughter, Isone Flosin, by any chance? She went missing some time ago while inside the Roden Shipyard Outpost in Fluekele. If you find her, tell her I'm very displeased and she should come see me immediately.

I heard Nilla Elermare was asking about Isone, too. You may want to start by talking to her.

140340.en: Mission complete. The Field Commander and his guards have been dealt with.

140341.en: I had a suspicion you would balk at the thought of live combat. You'd best sort your act out, rookie.

140342.en: Imperial Navy combat units have become increasingly bold with their incursions into Minmatar Republic sovereign space. At times, the Field Commanders in charge of their small units are not even on authorized missions, dangerous as such a thing is inside the Empire. Grabs for glory and personal vendettas make for a very disturbing trend when inside one of the largest navies in existence.

140343.en: Suit yourself. Maybe I'll find a pilot with a shred of patriotism to do it instead. Good day, {[character]player.name}.

140344.en: Suit yourself. Maybe I'll find a pilot with a shred of patriotism to do it instead. Good day, {[character]player.name}.

140345.en: Good. Come back when you can tell me that the Gallente is done for.

140346.en: Good. Come back when you can tell me that the Gallente is done for.

140347.en:
I've been contacted by one of the mining harvesters working in the vicinity. It's a private matter, and the poor man is desperate for assistance. His niece, a good-looking but rather quiet woman, lives with him and takes care of their living quarters, but when he got home a few days back, she was gone. After much searching, he discovered that she had been kidnapped by the Angel Cartel, in an operation led by the pirate captain Rubin Sozar.

We need you to go find the girl. Her uncle is beside himself with worry and is willing to give up all his savings for her safe retrieval, along with the destruction of the man who put him through all this grief. It is imperative that you get his niece back to us before going after Rubin Sozar, because if anything goes wrong with the rescue we will need him alive to barter for her return. Needless to say, her uncle's savings will not go to you unless the young woman is back where she belongs, safe and sound.

140348.en:
The filthy terrorist organization TFF just struck our slave compound. They sent one of their best men, and he managed to capture a heap of our precious slaves and is making his getaway now. I need you to intercept him before he manages to escape from this system.

This guy has a very long history of criminal and terrorist activity, belonging to the international network of thugs calling themselves the Freedom Fighters. I want his head on a platter, and the slaves back here alive.

140349.en:
Yes. Yes, I do. The filthy terrorist organization TFF just struck another one of our slave compounds. They sent one of their best men, and he managed to capture a heap of our precious slaves and is no doubt trying to make his getaway. I need you to intercept him before he manages to escape from this system.

Beware: This guy has a very long history of criminal and terrorist activity, belonging to the international network of thugs calling themselves the Freedom Fighters. I want his head on a platter, and the slaves brought back here alive. Do this and you will receive a healthy reward along with the bounty on his head.

140350.en: Good. Just don't go in alone and unprepared — he's already killed dozens of capsuleers.

140351.en: Wow, I thought you were a goner, but you made it back in one piece! You've done {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} an invaluable favor by ridding us of that pest.

140352.en: A capsuleer, immortal and wealthy beyond measure, and you're afraid of this guy?! Very disappointing. Very, very disappointing.

140353.en: Sounds good. I like a tough fight now and then.

140354.en: Alright, it's done. The slaves are here in the station.

140355.en: No thanks. I think I've heard about this guy. His ship is supposed to be pretty tough. And I just got my hull refitted, so I'm not about to get it all smashed up again.

140356.en: This guy is ridiculous! I mean, he's a total badass! I quit.

140357.en: My pleasure. I hear you might have a job for me?

140388.en:
Yes, we found some very useful information on it.

It seems that the Minmatar faction within the Federation has garnered the secret support of some influential members of the Gallente government.

Those officials were not named, but the slaves' contact within the Minmatar faction was. I want you to go to the location that the data chip indicated, and kill that contact and any who defend him.

140391.en: Oh, and also be on the lookout for the mercenary gang that owns the repair station. I doubt they'll look too kindly upon your attacking their precious structure.

140401.en: Though Scope (the corporation taking its name from its famed primetime holocast, The Scope), was originally based inside the Gallente Federation, it has expanded to the point where it is now considered the leading news agency throughout the empires.

140402.en: Not every mission you get requires you to kill every enemy in sight. It's often easier to warp out once your objective is done, enemy ships be damned.

140403.en: Excellent. Don't waste any time. <font color=#FF0000>And remember, you won't make it in in a battleship, so take something smaller.</font>

140404.en:
I thought as much. Okay. Good.

We recently received word that the Gallente have discovered a massive hidden deposit of Prime Arkonor in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and are setting up an industrial mining operation there. Prime Arkonor, as you probably know, is one of the most valuable minerals in the galaxy. And while we can't seem to pin down the location of the field itself, we do know where their processing base is.

Enter the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and wipe out the mining infrastructure they have constructed there. Your objective is the ore processor station itself, but you may want to take out their communications relay first so they can't call for backup. And don't go barging in there in a battleship, either. Try to be a little more subtle.

140405.en:
We recently received word that the Gallente have discovered a massive hidden deposit of Prime Arkonor in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and are setting up an industrial mining operation there. Prime Arkonor, as you probably know, is one of the most valuable minerals in the galaxy. And while we can't seem to pin down the location of the field itself, we do know where their processing base is.

Enter the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and wipe out the mining infrastructure they have constructed there. Your objective is the ore processor station itself, but you may want to take out their communications relay first so they can't call for backup. And don't go barging in there in a battleship, either. Try to be a little more subtle.

140406.en: Go to Caldari station 464, hack the relay center so that the data in its computers can be collected, and return to {[character]agentID.name}.

140407.en: We received a report just a couple hours ago from our secret agents that revealed plans by our enemies to make a sneak attack against us in this very system! I personally received a message from our esteemed CEO to send my most trusted contacts against these scoundrels, and so I ask you {[character]player.name}, are you up to it?  All I need you to do is infiltrate an area swarming with the pirates and destroy all of the hostile ships you encounter, my other clients will take care of the rest.  This will hopefully deter them from any further mobilization within {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}.

140521.en:
I received a response from Zunbar Alefon, the person that was supposed to identify the prisoners that you captured in a previous mission. Apparently, one of them is a very famous Gallente archaeologist, Karzath Pinazi, distantly related to Senator Tarek Pinazi! This is an incredible stroke of fortune for us, capturing a relative of a Gallente senator and famous icon is almost unheard of. I've no doubt that he will get us a mighty fine ransom. The only bad news is that this will probably bring a lot of bounty hunters into our backyard ... but hey, we have you to deal with that problem.

Now, on to your assignment. I need you to go to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} with a data chip that I'll have dropped off into your hangar. This chip contains all of our demands towards the Gallente Federation in exchange for the release of the prisoners. In it, we also threaten them with the slaying of their dear archaeologist team if they dare to launch a full scale assault on our station. I'm pretty sure that will keep them at bay for the time being.

140523.en:
With the population explosion in recent centuries within empire space many people have found themselves without homes or jobs, and have been pushed into leaving their homeworld for greener pastures. Many of these settlers have wound up in neutral space, and some even in space historically controlled by the outlawed "pirate" organizations. These settlers often have to fight a very difficult battle to survive, against both the forces of nature and those of man.

Although the empires generally consider the areas outside of their own realm being lawless and do not recognize them as sovereign states, there actually are rules to be followed even in the most bloodthirsty and barbaric nations. Each of the pirate organizations has their own culture and history, but one thing most of them do have in common is their willingness to milk the settlements in "their" solar systems for tribute. Sometimes these settlements consist entirely of slaves which have been captured elsewhere, or free people who decided to take their chances and settle on a promising planet despite its hazardous location. Either way, these settlements are a great way for the pirate factions to recruit new members, find new slaves and extract tribute in the form of credits, foodstuffs or manufactured goods.

Normally, the pirate organizations ban all settlements in their territory from having any form of high-tech weaponry in their possession, diligently enforcing this rule. This prevents the suppressed peoples from fighting back most of the time ... but with all rules, there are exceptions.

These settlers often have to fight a very difficult battle to survive, against both the forces of nature and those of man.

Although the empires generally consider the areas outside of their own realm being lawless and do not recognize them as sovereign states, there actually are rules to be followed even in the most bloodthirsty and barbaric nations. Each of the pirate organizations has their own culture and history, but one thing most of them do have in common is their willingness to milk the settlements in "their" solar systems for tribute. Sometimes these settlements consist entirely of slaves which have been captured elsewhere, or free people who decided to take their chances and settle on a promising planet despite its hazardous location. Either way, these settlements are a great way for the pirate factions to recruit new members, find new slaves and extract tribute in the form of credits, foodstuffs or manufactured goods.

Normally, the pirate organizations ban all settlements in their territory from having any form of high-tech weaponry in their possession, diligently enforcing this rule. This prevents the suppressed peoples from fighting back most of the time ... but with all rules, there are exceptions.

I don't want to talk about it. Whenever I close my eyes I can still hear the screams...

So, yes, more dolls. There are four dolls hidden in a series of deadspace pockets. How he found an unused chain of acceleration gates, I have no idea. But they're out there. Go to each canister, take a doll, and then use the acceleration gate to get to the next room. There should be four rooms and four dolls.

140529.en:
Now is the time to finally quash this pathetic rebellion. The last of the rebel ships and their Mordu lackeys have been gathering at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, to make a final stand against us. We have confirmed reports of a new militia leader being among this last group of traitors. We require him to be brought to us alive for his due punishment.

Once this group of ships has been destroyed, we will have total control over the skies on {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, allowing us to bombard them at will. They will suffer dearly for their outrageous impudence.

140533.en:
The data you retrieved earlier has some very important information. I don't know if the Amarr forces have guessed that the data chip you recovered had survived the explosion of the control tower, but either way we need to move fast while we still have the advantage.

This data directs us to two areas in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. One is the deadspace area that you must be familiar with by now, the other area is not in deadspace. I would like you to investigate area two. I will include a bookmark in the mission details uploaded to your Opportunity interface of course.
