The Federation is grateful for your service, {[character]player.name}. Thanks to your combat expertise we've got one less scumbag pirate boss to worry about.
If you would like to further your career in enforcement, there are Agents hiring across the cluster. I've heard the Sisters of EVE are looking for capable pilots, check out The Blood-Stained Stars for more information. If you'd rather broaden your skill set instead, you could start a conversation with any of the other Career Agents in this station.
Thanks again for everything, and good luck out there!

141226.en:
I ask for help, and they send me a capsuleer.

You are a capsuleer, aren't you? An immortal pilot who subverts the rules of life and death, who shapes the fate of empires? You'll have to excuse my skepticism.

I work with a humanitarian organization, the Sisters of EVE. I've seen your kind hasten the deaths of millions every day. You expect me to believe that you're different? To prove yourself, your actions will have to do the talking.

We've just received a distress call from a ship called the Damsel, and you're the closest aid available right now. Get out there and save some lives. Prove to me you're not just another murderous liar with a god complex. With all the power at your disposal, you certainly could be a force for good. And one thing is certain: Good is in dire need of allies these days.

141227.en: It seems CONCORD was faster to respond, but your backup was definitely appreciated. There were a handful of survivors picked up. They've been taken to various care facilities in the area – wherever vacancies could be found.

141228.en: You allied with Adani Yusev of the Caldari State.

141229.en:
We've gone a long way, but we've found the key survivor. Her name is Tahaki Karin. She was the engineer on the main ship from the ruined fleet, and she's signed on to the crew of the Heartbreak. She may be the only one who knows what really happened.

You know the drill by now: Get out there and get her before someone else does. I'm fairly certain there'll be someone there to shoot at you.

141230.en: Wonderful! The R&D team has been waiting for your return. Are you available for another mission?

141231.en: The first drones in the Gallente-Caldari war were little more than mines with proximity detonators and limited movement, but soon they advanced to a level where a single drone rivaled a solo-fighter's capabilities. The drones reversed the tide of the war and helped create a stalemate between the two empires.

141232.en:
Alitura said you needed more information about some kind of drone problem.

The Sisters have referred a few promising capsuleers in the past, so I'm willing to give you a chance, but I can't do anything else until this mess I'm dealing with has been taken care of. If you could retrieve some drones from {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, that would speed things up considerably.

You see, every drone in that system has ceased responding to signals. That just doesn't happen with Federation technology… unless the drones have been destroyed. Our research and development team needs whatever components still exist in order to analyze the remains.

Fly out there and bring back one of the drones – or any parts that might remain. You'll need to be careful. There were no signs of other ships in the system, so I have no idea what could have destroyed our drones.

141233.en:
So the soulless drones returned. I confess their behavior is strange. I had heard that the automatons have a free will of their own, but I never gave it much weight until now. There's something much larger going on than we realize.

But that is a mystery for another day. You have been an ally to the Empress and the Amarr people. Whether you continue your efforts defending the Empires or forge your own empires with your fellow capsuleers in the depths of lawless space, know that you have proven your worth as a capsuleer.

141234.en:
Greetings {[character]player.name} and welcome to the Minmatar nation. My name is Keita Eslin, Advisor to the Krusual Tribe. I'm glad to see you arrived, and with an abundance of useful information as well.

You needn't worry, I have good information and if you follow through on it, then we will certainly be helping one another.

141235.en:
Dagan was the pilot leading the fleet that the drones first destroyed, and a known terrorist. He was supposed to be dead. It's very important that he is made dead. The Sisters consider this a top priority.

Dagan is heading for a system in Minmatar space. He can't have gone far. I'll connect you with Keita Eslin, Advisor to the Krusual Tribe. She can help you track down Dagan.

I've been to Minmatar space quite a few times myself, {[character]player.name}. It's not so bad there, but just be careful where you wander and what you say. Their way of doing things can be a little rough around the edges at times, but I've also never known a Minmatar to not get a job done. In case you don't know, the Krusual can be a little sly. Just make sure this one looks after your interests, too. Still, I'm sure you can handle yourself.

141236.en: You contacted Keita Eslin and continued your investigation.

141238.en:
More drones appeared, but did not attack? That is a strange thing. I heard that they were truly sentient, but I never quite believed it. There's something much larger going on than we realize.

Regardless, you have proven yourself a friend of the Minmatar Republic. Whether you continue your efforts defending the Empires or forge your own empires with your fellow capsuleers in the depths of lawless space, know that you have proven your worth as a demigod.

141239.en:
The rogue drones did what? That's the damndest thing. I've heard that they can think for themselves, but I've never heard of them just watching like that. There's something much larger going on than we realize.

Regardless, you've been a tremendous help to the Caldari State. Whether you continue your efforts defending the Empires or forge your own empires with your fellow capsuleers in the depths of lawless space, know that you have proven your worth as a demigod.

141240.en: As payment for their aid, the Sisters of EVE have demanded we give them Dagan. I would rather see him stand trial for his crimes, but my superiors have agreed to the Sisters' terms. A ship awaits his delivery. Sister Alitura will accept nobody other than you to approach. Deliver Dagan to their hands, and let us be done with this.

141241.en: You delivered Dagan into the Sisters' custody, from which he is unlikely to return. While delivering Dagan, a large rogue drone hive appeared but did not attack. Sister Alitura was suspiciously unalarmed.

141247.en: Sometimes objects and entities found in space are not displayed in the default overview settings. Adding "Large Collidable Objects" in Celestials  and "Large Collidable Structures" in Entities to the overview can reveal details such as object names.

141248.en:
That Serpentis scum is the Major's son. I've just confirmed it with intelligence.

What happened is that the Major's son joined the Serpentis as part of some grey op about a year ago. A few months in the kid stopped reporting in. He was presumed dead. We now know that the Serpentis figured out who he was, and put the boy through extreme conditioning.

The Major has been trying to recover his son while keeping the operation that started this a secret. The Serpentis meanwhile have been trying to blackmail the Major. We're lucky they thought small by threatening the Major's career with exposing his son as a traitor. With the son now recovered, the Serpentis have nothing.

The boy needs to be sent for proper psychiatric care. It's going to take a while to scrub what the Serpentis did to him. The Major is waiting for him at the delivery point. I can't think of a better person than you to give closure to all this.

141249.en: Kitar Ang, a veteran of the Minmatar Republic Fleet, awaits you in Avyuh. She is a brilliant tactician, if impatient.

141250.en: Kitar Ang, a veteran of the Minmatar Republic Fleet, awaits you in Avyuh. She is a brilliant tactician, if impatient.

141251.en:
Damn Vitamala! He wasn't coordinating with the Navy's emergency logistics division. There's a colony nearby that missed a shipment of farming supplies thanks to the chaos caused by these drones. If we don't make the delivery ourselves, then we risk their entire agricultural economy. Once you take these goods over to our fleet, they will deal with the rest; we can finally turn our focus towards the underlying cause of all these problems.  

<font color = #EE3B3B>You will need at least 150m3 of cargo space to make the delivery. Keep that in mind.</font>

141253.en: Adani Yusev, a contractor with Ishukone, is eager to speak with you in Sosh. I've heard he is the very model of an efficient Caldari soldier.

141254.en: Adani Yusev, a contractor with Ishukone, is eager to speak with you in Sosh. I've heard he is the very model of an efficient Caldari soldier.

141255.en:
To get straight to business, I deal in body parts. Now don't get all pale and shocked on me, eh? I'm not one of those crazy Blood Raider flesh-eaters, ya know. All I do is acquire body parts of the deceased and sell them to the highest bidder, usually to the medical divisions within some of the major corporations of the Republic. You know, for research or cheap transplants to needy patients.

Anyway, I need some frozen livers I recently purchased to be transferred to the Eifyr and Co. research center in Eram. I'll provide you with a bookmark and everything; all you need to do is drop off the goods at your hangar there and my associates will pick it up.

141256.en:
If that's the case, I got something I think you're suited for. People here avoid me like the plague, and I can't fathom why. I just make my living like the next guy ... I got a family to feed, ya know.

141257.en: Great, I'll unload the goods into your hangar right away then.

141261.en: There is a monument where a battle in the Gallente-Caldari war occurred within Gallente space. We once tolerated Caldari pilgrims, but with this war we cannot allow the Caldari any excuse to proceed this deep within our space. Such leniency would only invite terrorism. I need you to destroy the monument, and any witnesses to the event. This may include some of our own people, but you needn't worry about any kind of standings complications, I will handle the political fallout.

141262.en:
There is a monument where a battle in the Gallente-Caldari war occurred within Gallente space. We once tolerated Caldari pilgrims, but with this war we cannot allow the Caldari any excuse to proceed this deep within our space. Such leniency would only invite terrorism.

I need you to destroy the monument, and any witnesses to the event. This may include some of our own people, but you needn't worry about any kind of standings complications, I will handle the political fallout. We will then release a statement that the site was attacked by pirates and, although the Caldari won't believe this, it will provide us with enough plausible deniability.

Undoubtedly there will be an uproar about this. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} will disavow any involvement. You will be best served by remaining silent yourself.

141263.en:
We have received word from an informant that an Amarrian terrorist, some religious zealot, is planning to plant a nuclear bomb somewhere on the Crystal Boulevard. Even though the structures of the crystal buildings are hardened against attack, a blast like that would kill thousands, not to mention shutting down the Boulevard — which, I needn't stress, would cause untold losses in profits.

Fortunately, we've just gotten intelligence regarding the lunatic's current whereabouts. Head out to these coordinates in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and stop this madman from executing his scheme.

Keep in mind though, {[character]player.name}, you must exercise a little stealth in approach. You will need to fly something smaller than a Battleship. Beyond that one restriction, I don't really care what you use. I just don't want you broadcasting your intentions before you even arrive on scene.

141264.en:
We have received word from an informant that an Amarrian terrorist, some religious zealot, is planning to plant a nuclear bomb somewhere on the Crystal Boulevard. Even though the structures of the crystal buildings are hardened against attack, a blast like that would kill thousands, not to mention shutting down the Boulevard — which, I needn't stress, would cause untold losses in profits.

Fortunately, we've just gotten intelligence regarding the lunatic's current whereabouts. Head out there, will you? Stop this madman from executing his fanatic scheme.

Keep in mind though, {[character]player.name}, you must exercise a little stealth in approach. You will need to fly something smaller than a Battleship. Beyond that one restriction, I don't really care what you use. I just don't want you broadcasting your intentions before you even arrive on scene.

141265.en:
Those blasted migrants are causing trouble again. Because of the abundance of gas clouds in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, our space is just crawling with them. As a matter of fact, a large group of Khanid harvesters built an outpost right next to my hideout in M0O-JG! I spent years building that place, and now they want to keep me out of my own home. I can't even go back without being shot at. It's just not right I tell you.

What I need you to do is find their outpost and blow it to bits. That should nudge them away, but it's not going to be easy. They locked and booby-trapped the acceleration gate leading into the deadspace pocket containing their base, so we have to find the key somehow. I know where they normally work, which is near a collection of massive gas clouds which they tend to harvest. I want you to ambush them there, and bring back captives for interrogation.

141267.en:
The interrogation is going well. They coughed up the access codes to the acceleration gate immediately. They look like frightened animals in fact, so entertaining. We'll have such fun together...

But now to more important matters. I will upload the access codes into your ship's mainframe, that should allow you to use the acceleration gate without problems. Once you have the bookmark, I expect you to warp out there and obliterate that base. And bring any stragglers to me, I so enjoy those sacrificial rituals.

141269.en:
I have a very dire situation on my hands at the moment. I have been the caretaker of a few dozen slaves for 5 years now, and recently the unthinkable happened. They managed to convert a few of our pod clones to their side, and together they have made an audacious get-away from the slave pens. Fortunately, we still have them on our radar, but we fear they might try to use one of the smuggler gates in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} to escape.

Obviously, it will set a very bad precedent should they manage to successfully get away. We can't have that. There's enough rebelliousness and infighting as it is within our ranks.

Although it pains me to say this, I require that you destroy all of the vessels carrying these rebels. They will be flying our ships, but will not hesitate to fire upon you - so feel free to extend the same courtesy. I will give you the precise coordinates of their whereabouts, of course.

141273.en:
Unfortunately, we discovered a few stragglers who avoided the fate of those rebels you took care of in that last assignment. Worse, we think they're about to make an attempt to reach an old abandoned stargate in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. Their getting away would be a huge embarrassment, so I want you to get to that stargate first in order to foil their plans.

There's something that will work in your favor though: This particular stargate is a very old model, and it needs to be powered up for a while before it will work. Therefore you'll have a few minutes to destroy the escapees before the stargate is completely powered up. Don't bother to attack the stargate itself ? if you destroy it they'll just warp away, and then who knows when we'll have another chance to catch them.

Oh, and bring me the head of their leader. I will present that to our people as a reminder of what happens to those who double-cross the Blood Raiders.

141274.en:
I need someone to help me retrieve one of my clones. He's stuck near the Pagera Manton, his ship pretty much destroyed by Kalorr's gang when it accidentally ventured too close to the Pagera. We must act quickly, before Kalorr decides to make a meal out of the guy.

I will give you a bookmark to the Pagera. But whatever you do, don't venture too close to the holy site. Kalorr will not look too kindly upon that, and I have a feeling he's not in the best of moods ... not ever.

141277.en: You won't have to look hard for Nekmar.  We know of his base of operations; I'll supply you with a bookmark to it.

141278.en:
I have a problem. It's about my son, Torin. He recently graduated from the academy, and I was giving him a tour of {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} in his brand-new Kestrel. We were going to have such a wonderful time celebrating his achievement when we were set upon by rogue drones. A battle ensued, which eventually I won, but when I looked for Torin his ship was a smoking hulk. He has very little practical experience with combat, despite graduating in the top 5 percentile of his class. However, his capsule was nowhere to be found: I think some of the drones must have captured his pod and fled before I noticed them. If he had died, my sensors would have registered the destruction of his pod, but they found nothing.

I want my son back, or at least vengeance on whoever is responsible for his death. I'll be out searching myself, but for each moment that passes...

I just want to find him and destroy those drones before they attack anyone else.

141279.en: I am...truly grateful for your assistance. I've detected a number of anomalies in this system that may indicate the presence of rogue drones. I've passed by a number of them and destroyed numerous drones, but have found no hive yet; perhaps you will have better luck. I will upload the coordinates of one of the reconnaissance points to the mission details in your Opportunity interface. Please take a look and see if you can find a drone hive. If you do, destroy it; we must ensure the safety of the people in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} above all else.

141280.en: Impressive work, {[character]player.name}! I'll pass the analyses on to my superiors immediately. Thank you once again.

141281.en: Impressive work, {[character]player.name}! I'll pass the analyses on to my superiors immediately. Thank you once again.

141284.en: There are rumors of Angels attempting to outmaneuver their enemies with squads of small ships, sacrificing firepower for mobility. While these are just rumors, there may be some merit to their tactics. Be wary.

141285.en: Some associates of mine have come across a fragile package which must be handled delicately, if you get what I mean. You needn't take it far and I've had your path cleared of any obstacles. Transport is simply a matter of discretion on your behalf. Once you have made the delivery, contact me again.

141286.en:
Welcome to Poinen, {[character]player.name}. I've been expecting you. In fact, I was quite pleased to have someone offer their services so soon after I put the word out.

As I'm sure you know by now, my name is Katsen Isha. I work part-time as a lawyer and consultant for Nugoeihuvi Corporation here in the Onirvura Constellation, where much of our company's most important business is handled.

That brings me to the first task I have for someone, perhaps you. Some associates of mine have come across a fragile package that must be handled delicately. You needn't take it far, and I've had your path cleared of any obstacles. Transport is simply a matter of discretion on your behalf. Could you deliver the cargo to our headquarters in Josameto?

141287.en: As his first task for me, Katsen Isha wants some kind of “delicate” cargo moved from his own station in Poinen to the Nugoeihuvi headquarters in Josameto.

141289.en:
I'm glad to see you're enthusiastic, but let me make this clear; you're not the first egger I've worked with. I say this so you know that I am well aware of just how capable – and yet completely unreliable – your type can be.

If you work with me, I expect results and I demand integrity. I'll keep plenty of ISK flowing in your direction, but you're going to have to earn it. I don't pay for half-assed jobs. Forgive the bluntness, {[character]player.name}, but I would rather be proven wrong, than told that I am.

141290.en: Goodbye then, {[character]player.name}, I don't have time to waste.

141292.en: I have not yet received any word of a delivery to Josameto HQ. Until that point, I have nothing further to say to you, {[character]player.name}.

141293.en: Nicknamed the “Shadow HQ” after its curious location, the Nugoeihuvi station in Poinen sits just one jump out from their Headquarters and shares the system with Internal Security HQ, the security arm of NOH. For certain individuals, the station is ideally situated, offering fast and easy personal access to many of NOH's highest-ranking officials – whilst remaining on the periphery of things, unnoticed in the shadow of the 13th moon. To those who are charged with the defense of Nugoeihuvi interests, it is not Josameto but Poinen that is considered the nexus, the bustling heart of a corporation that is their whole world.

141295.en: You have your instructions, {[character]player.name}. I've nothing further to say until you carry them out.

141296.en:
Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. I have to say…it's somewhat pleasing to watch Hyasyoda executives seethe quietly about a theft they cannot report. Hopefully they've learned the same lesson we in NOH did many years ago. Well…no…actually, I hope they screw up this badly every day.

Get back to me when you're ready to discuss how we're going to sell this.

141297.en: I could see that weakness in your eyes even as you accepted the assignment, how disappointing that my instincts proved right. Your replacement is already en route so kindly make yourself disappear, {[character]player.name}.

141298.en:
Rivalry among the corporations of the Caldari State is a daily reality, even today. The breakdown of relations with the Federation, opportunistic Guristas invasions and countless other problems facing the Caldari people have done little to ease inter-corporate tensions, some of which predate the existence of the State itself.

In other situations, rather than unifying the Caldari people, external threats only cause further divisiveness, and it is not uncommon for such issues to be leapt upon and twisted towards serving the agenda of one corporation or another. Survival within the harsh political arenas of the State requires a mastery of political cunning. To succeed requires even more – not only the ability to deeply understand events, but the capacity to shape them as well.

141299.en: It will not be hard for me to find another capsuleer to do this for me, {[character]player.name}. Suit yourself.

141300.en: I just received reports of criminal activity in our sector. A certain pilot attacked and destroyed a ship belonging to an ally of ours which was flying through CONCORD-protected space. He managed to flee before CONCORD got a hold of him. I want you to fly to the coordinates where he was last spotted, find him, and put him out of business. He's an extremely elusive fellow, who has managed to evade CONCORD for quite some time, so be wary.

But their ships recently pulled out, no doubt on the way to a dirtside raid or something - and the compound is now sitting largely defenseless. This is our chance to remove their threat.

141305.en: The arrogance of you eggers! I do not report to you, but to true servants of the divine Empire. I will find someone else to carry out this task - your refusal has achieved nothing but my disdain.

141306.en:
I have terrible news, {[character]player.name}. A major personnel convoy carrying countless {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} members was completely obliterated by Blood Raider ships, led by that damned commander of theirs, Faramon Mundan. His reputation as a brutal Covenant military leader has traveled far and wide these past few years, and it's time to put an end to his miserable existence.

I want you to be the bringer of our vengeance, {[character]player.name}. Strike him down like the dog he is. When his battleship has been turned to dust, then you shall receive your reward.

141307.en:
I have terrible news, {[character]player.name}. A major personnel convoy carrying countless {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} members was completely obliterated by Serpentis ships, led by that damned commander of theirs, Xevni Jipon. His reputation as a brutal Serpentis military leader has traveled far and wide these past few years, and it's time to put an end to his miserable existence.

I want you to be the bringer of our vengeance, {[character]player.name}. Strike him down like the dog he is. When his battleship has been turned to dust, then you shall receive your reward.

141308.en:
I have terrible news, {[character]player.name}. A major personnel convoy carrying countless {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} members was completely obliterated by Cartel ships, led by that damned commander of theirs, Hoborak Moon. His reputation as a brutal Cartel military leader has traveled far and wide these past few years, and it's time to put an end to his miserable existence.

141309.en:
I have terrible news, {[character]player.name}. A major personnel convoy carrying countless {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} members was completely obliterated by Sansha's fighters, led by that damned commander of theirs, Draben Kuvakei. His reputation as a brutal Sansha military leader has traveled far and wide these past few years, and it's time to put an end to his miserable existence.

I want you to be the bringer of our vengeance, {[character]player.name}. Strike him down like the dog he is. When his battleship has been turned to dust, then you shall receive your reward.

141314.en:
I do, and I hope you'll understand the importance of what I am about to ask you.

During a recon operation in a contested sector, we discovered a large facility housing thousands of Amarrians. In all likelihood they are assisting Empire Navy forces in some way. When we first discovered the facility it was heavily guarded, so they are obviously up to something.

But that defensive force recently pulled out, no doubt on the way to a dirtside raid or something - and the compound is now sitting largely defenseless. This is our chance to remove their threat. Can I rely on you?

141315.en: KFR-ZE, {[character]player.name}. That is your current destination. Our people are waiting for you.

141316.en:
I admit I am impressed. You have shown a surprising level of patience and commitment here, {[character]player.name}. Here is your pay; you have earned every last Kredit.

Take some time to relax, place a few bets, buy a few drinks…whatever it is you eggers do in your spare time. When you are ready to continue our work, I have someone I want you to meet.

141317.en:
There is not much else I can offer, {[character]player.name}. If you cannot commit to this task, then there is no hope that you will be able to see the entirety of our business to its conclusion.

Take some time, train up, gain some confidence. If you find the courage to take this on, I may still have the job open for you. No guarantees, though — there are plenty of capable eggers out there who'd leap on a job like this.

141318.en:

141319.en:
We have to bring Katsen Isha down, and we have to be exceptionally careful about how we do it. Dealing with Nugoeihuvi requires cunning and guile. You've shown sound judgment by coming to us early, {[character]player.name}. The problem is that it will only get worse if you leave things as they are now. We need answers to the questions you've brought to light.

We will count on you to earn Isha's trust, so you can uncover whatever you need to help us. We need you on the inside if we're ever going to see this resolved; Nugoeihuvi are too well trained at covering up their tracks.

We will be there every step of the way to assist you. I've granted you provisional support from one of our best counter-intelligence teams. They will observe your actions from a distance and monitor any relevant data from your fluid router cache. Anything Isha says to you over FTL, we will have. Anything your camera drones see, we will see.

You will have to keep your assignment strictly confidential, even from other Hyasyoda members. Nobody can know. Not your lover, not your mother, not even the Maker. If you need to get in touch, I will be here. Otherwise, act as if this conversation never happened.

141320.en: Angel pirate vessels have been terrorizing passersby in a nearby system. Find and destroy their leader.  We'll upload the last known location of the enemy ships to your NeoCom.

141321.en: A few of those dratted Guristas pirate vessels are terrorizing passersby in a nearby system.  Find and destroy their leader.  We've uploaded the last known location of the enemy ships to your NeoCom.

141322.en: Guristas pirate vessels have been terrorizing passersby in a nearby system. Find and destroy their leader. We're uploading the last known location of the enemy ships to your NeoCom.  We need you to put these pirates out of business ASAP.

141323.en: A few of those dratted Guristas pirate vessels have been terrorizing passersby in a nearby system.  Find and destroy them.  We'll upload the last known location of the enemy ships to your NeoCom.  We need to put them out of business ASAP.

141331.en:
We have a rather comical situation on our hands, {[character]player.name}. A foolhardy Amarrian noble named Kazar Numon has claimed ownership of a sizable portion of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, claiming one of his ancestors was given this part of space as a reward for his duties to the emperor. Turns out that, many centuries ago, {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} had just recently been discovered by an Amarrian exploration team, which apparently included a long-distant relative of his. The area includes a couple of planets, their satellites, and an asteroid field. Anyway, this guy has now sent us an official warning that any aggression against "his" assets will be met with an iron fist.

I want you to put this goofball out of his misery, {[character]player.name}. He completely underestimates our strength in the region, believing that his small mercenary force will scare us off. Fly to their position where they have set up a small outpost and destroy its Control Tower, along with the mercenary forces defending it.

141332.en:
A minor Amarrian noble has claimed ownership of a sizable portion of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, claiming one of his ancestors was given this part of space as a reward for his ancestor's duties to the emperor. The area includes a couple of planets, their satellites, and an asteroid field. Anyway, this guy has now sent us an official warning that any aggression against "his" assets will be met with an iron fist.

He completely underestimates our strength in the region, believing his small mercenary force sufficient to scare us off. Fly to the fool's position and destroy the Control Tower he's holding out there, along with the mercenary forces defending him. Let's put this idiot out of his misery.

141333.en:
Nice work. He may have a clone somewhere, being a noble, but with his mercenary force eliminated, I'm sure Kazar will think twice before attempting anything like this again within our territory.

And don't you leave just yet: I have another assignment waiting for you!

141334.en:
What did I tell you?

Goodbye, {[character]player.name}.

141335.en:
There is not much else I can offer, {[character]player.name}. If you cannot commit to this task, then there is no hope that you will be able to see the entirety of our business to its conclusion.

Take some time, train up, gain some confidence. If you find the courage to take this on, I may still have the job open for you. No guarantees. though. There are plenty of capable eggers out there who'd leap at a job like this.

141336.en:
I admit I am impressed. You have shown commendable patience and commitment here, {[character]player.name}. Honestly, I think you could have made it all the way to KFR-ZE, but oh well. Here is your pay: you have earned every last Kredit.  
Take some time to relax, place a few bets, buy a few drinks… whatever it is you eggers do in your spare time. When you are ready to continue our work, I have someone I want you to meet.

141337.en: Faurulle, {[character]player.name}. That is your current destination. Our people are waiting for you.

141338.en:
There has been an unfortunate turn of events. Your successful attack on the Numon mercenary outpost seems to be sitting badly with certain factions within the Amarr Empire. A few high-ranking members of the Sarum family have taken up Kazar's cause directly to the Empress, and they've already started mobilizing their personal fleets to make a trip here to get involved in our little territorial dispute.

We've already sent out scan probes to collect data on any Imperial activity in the {[location]agentRegionID.name} region. This data will be stored in a computer disc which I expect you to fetch for me at {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}. Once we retrieve this data we will have a better picture of what we might be up against. But we still have our fingers crossed that this fiasco will die down before Empress Catiz herself gets involved.

141340.en: Cross the river before you laugh at the current.

141341.en:
I have some good and some bad news, {[character]player.name}. The good news is that the Amarr Empress has publicly declined to intervene officially in the territorial dispute between us and Kazar Numon. The bad news is that she also expressly has not forbidden other Amarr Holders from acting privately in this matter. It's a political game she's playing, and she plays it well.

As a result, the Sarum lords who originally campaigned for intervention have ordered an outlying fleet of Imperial Navy ships to aid Numon anyway. They are led by an Imperial Fleet Commander who's part of House Sarum, one Ishtai Sarum. We need to prevent him from moving his fleet into defensive positions around the area claimed by Numon. To do this, we must execute a number of hit-and-run attacks while they move through our territory.

We've located what seems to be a reconnaissance team of theirs, en route to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They are currently flying through {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}, and we'd like you to intercept them immediately.

Leave no survivors - we don't want them reporting anything back to their commander.

141342.en:
The Amarr Empress has publicly declined to intervene officially in the territorial dispute between us and Kazar Numon. Sadly, she also expressly has not forbidden other Amarr Holders from acting privately in this matter.

As a result, the Sarum lords who originally campaigned for intervention have ordered an outlying fleet of Imperial Navy ships to aid Numon anyway. They are led by an Imperial Fleet Commander who's part of House Sarum, one Ishtai Sarum. We need to prevent him from moving his fleet into defensive positions around the area claimed by Numon. To do this, we must execute a number of hit-and-run attacks while they move through our territory.

We've located what seems to be a reconnaissance team of theirs, en route to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They are currently flying through {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}, and we'd like you to intercept them immediately.

Leave no survivors - we don't want them reporting anything back to their commander.

141343.en:
Our surveillance teams have reported another large force of Imperial Navy ships moving through {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, probably heading toward {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If we let them all arrive safely at their destination, we will have a very difficult fight on our hands: We need to weaken their forces before they have a chance to settle in and fortify themselves at their destination.

A part of their fleet is currently amassed in a deadspace pocket in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. Their plan seems to be to move slowly between deadspace areas to prevent our heavy artillery from locking on to them. I want you to conduct an attack on the couple of squadrons that have already arrived at that deadspace pocket; I will provide you with bookmarks to the exact location.

Speed is crucial for your success here. You need to strike them hard and fast and get out of there before they know what hit them. Tarry too long, and you'll have the entire fleet on your ass.

Good luck.

141344.en:

If we let them all arrive safely at their destination, we will have a very difficult fight on our hands: We need to weaken them before they have a chance to settle in and fortify themselves at their destination.

Part of their fleet is currently in a deadspace pocket in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. Their plan seems to be to move slowly between deadspace areas to prevent our heavy artillery from locking on to them. I want you to conduct an attack on the couple of squadrons that have already arrived at that deadspace pocket; I will provide you with bookmarks to the exact location.

Speed is crucial for your success here. You need to strike them hard and fast and get out of there before they know what hit them. Tarry too long, and you'll have the entire fleet on you.

141345.en:
Our guerrilla tactics have worked wonderfully, {[character]player.name}. The remainder of the Amarr fleet has reached its destination, but they are substantially weakened. Some were destroyed in your attacks, some were destroyed by other pirate marauders, and, subsequently, some deserted. Now it's time to launch our final attack.

The remaining forces have started to rebuild the defensive perimeter around the territory the Numon family claimed for themselves. The remnants of Numon's mercenary force guards the area now, along with the partial Navy fleet. Kazar, head of House Numon, has apparently decided to risk his own hide to defend his precious section of space. Killing him again will be the icing on the cake for us.

Your task is simple, {[character]player.name}. Attack the Numon and Amarr forces head on, and obliterate them completely. Leave no survivors - but do bring me Numon's head. It will make a nice souvenir.

141346.en:
Our guerrilla tactics have worked well. The remainder of the Amarr fleet has reached its destination, but they are substantially weakened. Now it's time to launch our final attack.

The remaining forces have started to rebuild the defensive perimeter around the Numon claim. The remnants of Numon's mercenary force guards the area now, along with the partial Navy fleet.

Best, though, is the fact that Kazar, head of House Numon, has apparently decided to risk his own hide to defend his precious section of space. Killing him will be the icing on the cake for us. Your task is simple, {[character]player.name}. Attack the Numon and Amarr forces head on, and obliterate them completely. Leave no survivors.

But do bring me Numon's head. It will make a nice souvenir.

141347.en: Good, then. Remember, {[character]player.name} — the Logistics Center is your only target. You can limit the loss of life here by taking it down quickly and then getting the hell out. If you linger, they will most likely swarm you with reinforcements and pin you down. Don't get complacent just because they're mercs; Hyasyoda is funding them and will make damn sure they get their money's worth.

141348.en: Time is our greatest enemy, {[character]player.name}. You should get going. The CPF could replace their stand-in mercs at any moment.

141349.en: Well, ok then. Good luck in your journeys, I've a replacement to find.

141350.en: Yes, I can understand your hesitance, but there is no other way to resolve this, {[character]player.name}. Good luck in your journeys, I've a replacement to find.

141351.en: Isha has somehow learned of the Hyasyoda investigation team and, worse yet, knows the location of their headquarters. He has asked me to level the place and destroy the mercenary ships guarding it. Hyasyoda assured me that any orders Isha gave over FTL comms would find their way back to the team, so I can only assume they're aware of the matter. I should head back to Arikio Kuretsu at the Hyasyoda HQ to see how she wants to proceed.

141352.en: Hyasyoda is one of the oldest of the Caldari megacorporations, having been formed shortly after first contact with Gallente when the Caldari were still in their Industrial Age. Throughout State history, Hyasyoda executives have always been conservative and cautious. As a result the corporation has informally claimed as theirs the age old Caldari saying, “only the paranoid survive.”

141354.en:
We need to reposition our people out of Nugoeihuvi's way and not let Isha realize we're aware of his intentions in the process. You must convince Isha that you have destroyed the facility and everyone in it.

We have found a series of bugs implanted by NOH agents throughout our compound. We have not interfered with them in any way so far. Our plan is to have you disable them only moments before you move everyone out. Immediately after that point, we will trigger the detonation of explosive charges already set in each compromised facility. When Nugoeihuvi notice their surveillance has gone down, they'll suspect one of two things; that you have carried out your task, or that their bugs have been compromised. We want it to be the former.

141355.en: I met again with Hyasyoda Agent Arikio Kuretsu after learning that Isha had discovered the location of the investigation team's Headquarters. She told me that the CPF has a plan to deal with him personally, but for now I have been tasked with salvaging the situation. It seems that NOH have bugged the CPF compound, but we can use that against them. The strategy is to hack into their surveillance software, disable it, quickly evacuate everyone, and then clear the area before Hyasyoda agents detonate explosives laid inside. The explosions should register on the other bugging devices, and once each of them are destroyed, nobody will know that they were disabled a few moments beforehand, nor what happened in that small window of time after they were. At least, that's the plan.

141356.en: Good. I will give you further instructions out there. Pay careful attention to them, everything rests on your shoulders.

141357.en: You have come with us this far, {[character]player.name}, can you not see us through to the end? We cannot trust any other egger. If there was something else you needed to do then go do it. I will be eagerly awaiting your return.

141358.en: Then leave. If you cannot be trusted to help us in this time of need, then you cannot be trusted, period.

141359.en:
You know, {[character]player.name}, all I've ever seen from your kind is death and destruction, until today, at least. We are – and I am – humbled to have you working for us.

I will leave it at that, for now. You have done enough today that I would feel overbearing trying to dump yet more work on your shoulders. Whenever you are ready though, we would like to brief you on one last assignment before you return to Katsen Isha. Until then, rest well. You've certainly earned it.

141360.en: Head out to the investigation team's HQ, {[character]player.name}. I will provide further instructions once you're on-site.

141361.en:
The facility you were instructed to raid has not been under Hyasyoda control for almost a year now. I was told that if you do your research you should find that we also legally rented the area from Sukuuvestaa too, before Serpentis overran it and forced us out. Of course, SuVee could pay the House of Records and the Caldari Business Tribunal a few administrative fees to make that information disappear, if someone were to ever poke around.

What I think you may also find interesting to know, though, is that around the time our lease was coming up for renewal, Serpentis began to show up in larger numbers and with better equipment. We always suspected someone local was funding them, a rogue Guristas outfit or even Gallente extremists, but the idea that it might be one of our own corporations, at a time like this, it just never crossed our mind.

Something definitely isn't right here. I suspect Nugoeihuvi learned of the facility through Sukuuvestaa, who I can only guess, never wanted us to extend our lease for some reason. NOH, doing what it does best, brought in some thugs to clear the matter up. That's until you arrived and, I hope, saw that something wasn't adding up.

Now, the question is whether or not we can trust you. Obviously we are happy to share this information, but there is more to the story than we will share with an egger who has stolen from us. If you are serious about seeing this affair brought to a just end, then you will return what you took and prove your intentions.

141362.en:
We noticed something when you left towards Syndicate to make the blueprint delivery. Isha was on the move himself. Our surveillance team monitored a visit he made to an unknown Caldari Navy compound. The unmarked shuttle he flew there has now been sighted back inside Nugoeihuvi's docking bay at Poinen. Interestingly, it has been given priority docking position, meaning another launch is likely to happen soon.

We don't want to arrive at any conclusions just yet, but our first impression is that Isha is involved in some kind of black market activity, perhaps weapons or information smuggling. We noticed that he mentioned introducing you to someone – we think they may be the buyer. His visit to this Caldari Navy facility raises a lot of questions in that regard.

See what you can do about meeting this friend of Isha's, then discover what you can about them. We'll be watching closely {[character]player.name}, good luck.

141363.en:
There was someone I wanted you to meet. I'm afraid I can't do it myself; he and I must be careful not to be associated with one another. This is not for any good reason, {[character]player.name}, it is simply the way our judgmental world works. A Caldari Navy officer of his kind cannot afford the rumors that a friendship with me brings.

My friend's name is Sinas Egassuo. You will find him somewhere around {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, just look for the Caldari Navy compound in the system, and be careful. He may not be known and loved by the Caldari people, but the leadership of the Gallente Navy is well acquainted with him and his work, and has long wanted him dead. His outfit deals with assassins and bounty hunters on a daily basis. Expect nothing less when you find the compound.

141364.en:
The Corporate Police Force investigation must be brought to an end before it can uncover anything that could lead back to us. The forces inside the facility right now are not Hyasyoda or CPF personnel, just some hired mercs. This gives us an opportunity to strike preemptively at the compound without causing an incident and further complicating matters.

If you can destroy the Logistics Center quickly, it will set them back weeks. The paths that lead back to us to will have faded into the background by the time they can resume their investigation. You can limit the loss of life here by taking it down quickly and then getting the hell out. If you linger, they will most likely swarm you with reinforcements.

141365.en:
The Corporate Police Force investigation must be brought to an end before it can uncover anything that could lead back to us. The forces inside the facility right now are not Hyasyoda or CPF personnel, just some hired mercs. This gives us an opportunity to strike preemptively at the compound without causing an incident and further complicating matters.

If you can destroy the Logistics Center quickly, it will set them back weeks. The paths that lead back to us to will have faded into the background by the time they can resume their investigation. You can limit the loss of life by taking the target down quickly and then getting the hell out. If you linger, they will most likely swarm you with reinforcements.

141366.en:
The CPF investigation team is in Onirvura because of some intel – intel I believe we can manipulate. I have learned that they partially decrypted a communication between my people here and our blueprint buyers in KFR-ZE. Fortunately for us, they couldn't fully decipher the location we were transmitting to, so all they know is that this area is where the transmission originated and that the destination system started with KF and has a Z and E in its name.

Your assignment is to secure a nearby Blood Raider facility and safely deliver our own signal operators to the Communications Tower inside. They will use it to transmit fake intelligence to the CPF team, and hopefully, lead them to KFIE-Z.

141367.en:
There was someone I wanted you to meet. I'm afraid I can't do it myself; he and I must be careful not to be associated with one another. This is not for any good reason, {[character]player.name}, it is simply the way our judgmental world works. A Caldari Navy officer of his kind cannot afford the rumors that a friendship with me brings.

My friend's name is Sinas Egassuo. You will find him somewhere around {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, just look for the Caldari Navy compound in the system, and be careful. He may not be known and loved by the Caldari people, but the leadership of the Gallente Navy is well acquainted with him and his work, and has long wanted him dead. His outfit deals with assassins and bounty hunters on a daily basis. Expect nothing less when you find the compound.

141369.en: That is unfortunate. I was expecting you to finish this for me.

141370.en: I suppose I can't blame you. Tracking down a truant employee is not the most exciting work.

141371.en: These reports suggest that a group of Sansha's Nation ships were seen heading for a listening outpost owned by one Lord Touraj Miyan, a local Holder. The Sansha must have killed my agent to prevent this information from getting out. Head over to the outpost and give the Sansha a surprise.

141372.en: A listening outpost owned by Lord Miyan is under attack.

141373.en: Remember, destroy any and all Sansha. We don't want any escaping this fight.

141374.en: Are you giving up so easily?

141375.en: What are risks to a capsuleer like you?

141376.en: The Sansha attempted to destroy an outpost owned by Lord Touraj Miyan.

141379.en: How could you let them get away?

141380.en: How could you refuse me? After all this?

141381.en: Okay, we have his location. Follow the bookmark and take him down.

141382.en: The Sansha commander is on the run.

141383.en: You handle the commander, I'll figure out how the Sansha are getting past our defenses.

141384.en: We're so close to getting this guy and you quit now?

141385.en: Do you have the commander yet?

141386.en: The commander escaped, aided by a third party flying Amarr ships.

141387.en: I can't believe the commander got away again! Who was flying those Amarr ships? And where did that gate come from?

141389.en: We need to get to the bottom of this. You can break this thing wide open. You need to talk to someone with both a knowledge of the Sansha and has local connections. Luckily, I have just such a contact: Aralin Jick.

141390.en: The Sansha attacks are obviously targeted at Touraj Miyan. Riff Hebian, Miyan's chief of security, is smart but skeptical. Head to Miyan's manor in Nebian and convince Hebian of the threat.

141391.en:
Remember those Amarr ships you ran into? It seems that one Lord Manik has been shopping around for mercenaries.

I'm giving you the meeting location I found while innocently perusing Manik's records. There should be a mercenary contact. You're going to find out who they are, and then we're going to wipe them out. I'll have more instructions when you reach the site.

141392.en: I've got the coordinates to the mercenary camp. Tear down everything you find. Time to ruin someone's day.

141393.en: For a few weeks now, we've known of a small Amarrian reconnaissance outpost in the system. So far we've left them alone because we wanted to know what they were up to. Now we know. This morning they were joined by a highly respected Amarr general; we are certain he is planning a strike on one of our stations in the system. I will update the coordinates to the mission details in your Opportunity interface: if you can go and bring their plans to a halt - I think you know what I mean - you will be handsomely rewarded.

141394.en:
Ah, a capsuleer, are you? Fortunate.
I am Kandus Sandar, the Ministry of Internal Order officer in charge of Pirate Affairs in this area. Under normal circumstances, I would send you to one of our many agents for proper work, but I have a special task for you.
I am waiting for one of my investigators. He is now several hours overdue in delivering his reports. Fly out to his last known location. Despite whatever you may find there, I need those reports.

141395.en: I am waiting for one of my investigators. He is now several hours overdue in delivering his reports. I need someone to fly out to his last known location. Despite whatever you may find there, I need those reports.

141396.en:
I would fly out there, but a capsuleer like yourself will have less trouble should you encounter any complications. Plus, if you do encounter danger, you at least have a pod to save you. I do not have that luxury.

I have uploaded the location of the last communique to your NeoCom. Head over there immediately. I cannot have more delays.

141397.en: Your story matches these reports. Sansha activity is on the rise. The Sansha that frequent this region are usually nothing more than opportunists, salvaging for parts and human life wherever they can find it.

141398.en: Cross the river before you laugh at the current.

141400.en: Find Logut and bring him to your agent, alive. Your agent told you to find the objective near a moon orbiting Eram IV.

141401.en: The Sansha ambushed and destroyed an MIO investigator.

141402.en: I've taken the liberty of examining your ship's logs. That outpost was unmanned, in disrepair, and not particularly valuable. There's no reason a group of marauders would attack it. There must be something more.

141403.en: A group of Sansha's Nation ships are attacking a listening outpost owned by Lord Touraj Miyan. Head to the outpost and stop them from destroying that outpost. I will retrieve logs from the fight from your ship's computer once you return.

141404.en:
This needs to be taken care of quickly, {[character]player.name}. Another group of Sansha's Nation ships has launched an attack. This time, they targeted a slave convoy belonging to - take a guess - Lord Touraj Miyan.

However, we've got word that an unusual ship joined the Sansha in the attack. The transmission cut off before we could get concrete details on who or what it was, but I'm willing to bet it's the commander of the bunch. The fleet is large, but should be a non-issue for a capsuleer.

Stop the Sansha and their commander.

141405.en: Good job, but it's not over yet. I've got a lock on the commander that ran away.

141406.en: A Sansha's Nation fleet attacked a slave convoy belonging to Touraj Miyan. Their commander may be present at the conflict. Your primary objective is to discover the identity of their commander and destroy him.

141407.en: Sansha are attacking a slave convoy. Their commander is present.

141408.en: The Sansha were driven away from one of Miyan's slave convoys, but the commander escaped.

141409.en: No! We were so close to catching him!

141410.en:
We need to get to the bottom of this. Those Amarr ships came from somewhere and someone.

I can't do the legwork myself. My MIO clearance can open a lot of doors, but there's too much red tape for me to jump through. You, however, can do what I can't. You can break this thing wide open.

You need to talk to someone with both a knowledge of the Sansha and local connections. Luckily, I have just such a contact: Aralin Jick.

141411.en:
He has a rather intimate knowledge of Sansha's Nation. I'll let him decide if he wants to share the details with you.

Since he works directly for the Kor-Azor Family, he is in a position to do more digging in the area than I can, and he'll step on toes if necessary.

Just remember: Whoever is leading these Sansha is targeting a Holder. There aren't many people we can trust, so be diligent.

141412.en: You're giving up the chase now?

141413.en: You're giving up the chase now?

141414.en: Sandar sent you, eh? He probably sent you to me to keep an eye on me as much as anything else.  Did he tell you my history? No, of course not. I'm going to help you anyway, because despite whatever Sandar thinks, I want the Sansha gone.

141415.en:
As I mentioned before, there was someone I wanted you to meet. I'm afraid I can't do it myself; he and I must be careful not to be associated with one another. This is not for any good reason, {[character]player.name}, it is simply the way our judgmental world works. A Caldari Navy officer of his kind cannot afford the rumors that a friendship with me brings. You will learn though, in time, how little truth there is to them. You've already shown a great capacity to see through the surface of things, to the heart. You wouldn't be here still if that wasn't the case.

My friend's name is Sinas Egassuo. He is a man in a similar position to me, working quietly in the engine room, seeking results, not glory. He too, works as an Advisor, and almost every important operation undertaken by our Navy in the last decade bears his imprint. You will hear talk of Caldari patriots in your time in the State, and doubtless already have. This man is a living definition of one.

You will find him somewhere around {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, just look for the Caldari Navy compound in the system, and be careful. He may not be known and loved by the Caldari people, but the leadership of the Gallente Navy is well acquainted with him and his work, and has long wanted him dead. His outfit deals with assassins and bounty hunters on a daily basis. Expect nothing less when you find the compound.

Oh, and if his surname seems familiar that's because you've probably met his sister. She works as a capsuleer liaison for the Navy's Command Division in Motsu. I wouldn't mention anything about her though; sisters are a sore spot for him.

141416.en: Good then. Trust what I said {[character]player.name}, the State is lucky to have people like Sinas.

141417.en: We were just about to begin the real work, {[character]player.name}! Well, fine. If you have other things to deal with, get to them. You would not be the first egger to walk out on a job barely started. I had expected more from you though, I am sad to say.

141418.en: I…already set things in motion. Your failure here has cost me much, much more than you realize. Go then, {[character]player.name}. If you cannot be relied upon, I have no desire to give you any further work.

141419.en: You have reached the Nugoeihuvi Corporation Advisory Office, Poinen. No-one is available to take your call at this moment. Please try again later.

141420.en: You have reached the Nugoeihuvi Corporation Advisory Office, Poinen. No-one is available to take your call at this moment. Please try again later.

141421.en: The patriot faction has become increasingly influential since the breakdown in relations with the Federation. The patriots are led by the mighty Kaalakiota Corporation although Lai Dai and Wiyrkomi are often just as vocal in their beliefs. The patriots cultivate the Caldari heritage, reminisce about the great Raata Empire of old and joyously celebrate the reclamation of their homeworld, Caldari Prime.

141423.en: Your first task is to investigate a possible filming location. We're not expecting any major problems, but after an accident last week scouting a similar location, I'd rather have these matters handled by someone who really knows what they're doing. I'll leave my comms link open; once you've scouted the area and it's safe to proceed, get back in touch with me.

141424.en: You met Aralin Jick, your local contact.

141426.en: Refusal is unacceptable, I will find someone else. Goodbye {[character]player.name}.

141427.en: Failure is not an option, {[character]player.name}. I will find someone else.

141429.en:
I heard you tore them apart, {[character]player.name}. I can't say I'm surprised, either by their presence or by their swift disappearance at your hands. You are a constant reminder of why I should bother with the hassle of enlisting capsuleers.

I've received word from the operators that the comms tower is onlining now. They'll begin transmitting shortly. It looks like we're in the clear. Excellent news, I'm sure you'll agree.

When you feel up to it, I still had someone I wanted you to meet, now that our first order of business is finally settled.

141431.en: It is not unheard of for Blood Raider vessels to stray into State space. Having something of a relationship with the Guristas in the north, the Covenant has erected various safe havens for members who make the long journey up to Venal through Caldari space.

141432.en: Upon speaking with Isha again, I have learned that the CPF investigation team is chasing up their only lead; a fragment of an intercepted transmission that suggests the culprits are in a nullsec system starting with “KF” and with a Z and E in the name. Isha wants me to fool them into thinking the system is KFIE-Z, the Blood Raiders HQ. From what he describes, the task will not be an easy one. I am told to expect the “very worst” of the Covenant given their silence, which Isha tells me is not a good sign.

141435.en: Riff Hebian isn't going to believe me. A capsuleer, however....

141436.en: Very well. Go find someone else to bother then.

141437.en: The Sansha attacked? The Empress' grace is upon us, friend. If we weren't going to kill every one of them, I'd give whoever ordered that Sansha attack a medal.

141439.en:
Even though many Holder titles extend back thousands of years, the position is a precarious one. Families waxed and waned over the centuries. Most families realize the rule of fools is inevitable; all they can do is hope too much damage isn't done before a proper ruler can ascend again.

House Miyan has ruled much of the Jatari constellation for centuries. Miyan grew to be one of the top Holder houses, rivaling Kor-Azor in local influence. In 109, Lord Miyan died and passed his title to his only son, Touraj Miyan.

Touraj is considered a dolt, accused of being more likely to make a pass at subordinate Holders' wives than realize his chief advisor is dipping into senility. Lord Iraj Darabi, a minor but well-respected neighboring Holder, used Touraj's unpopularity and foolishness to his own advantage. In 110, he annexed two of the systems under House Miyan control for himself, sparking a minor conflict between the two Houses.

In the end, Darabi's superior commanders and advisors forced Miyan to surrender. So far, Miyan has managed to hold on to his remaining lands.

141440.en:
This Corporate Police Force investigation must be brought to an end before it can uncover anything that could lead back to us, unlikely as that may be. The forces inside the facility right now are not Hyasyoda or CPF personnel, just some hired mercs. This gives us an opportunity to strike preemptively at the compound without causing an incident and further complicating matters.

I cannot guarantee how long they will be on duty, however, nor what kind of reaction your arrival on scene will provoke. What I do know is that if you can destroy the Logistics Center quickly, it will set them back weeks. The paths that lead back to us to will no doubt have faded into the background by the time they can resume their investigation.

141441.en: Good, then. Remember, {[character]player.name}, the Logistics Center is your only target. You can limit the loss of life by taking it down quickly and then getting the hell out. If you linger, they will most likely swarm you with reinforcements and pin you down. Don't get complacent just because they're mercs, Hyasyoda is funding them and will make damn sure they get their money's worth.

141442.en: Yes, I understand your hesitance. Perhaps it is better to focus on misdirection instead. I will prepare your briefing for that task and you can judge for yourself. Speak with me again when you'd like to hear it.

141443.en: I won't deny the assignment was a challenging one, but can I suggest that you look into safer work in the future? Speaking of which, I need to find your replacement. Thank you for the time you gave.

141444.en: Time is our greatest enemy here, {[character]player.name}. You should get going. The CPF could replace their stand-in mercs at any moment.

141445.en:
Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. Truly. Our ISK is secure and nobody alive suspects us. You have done well, and the money we have secured will help us pursue important things.

Take some time to relax and recuperate. When you are ready, our real work can finally begin.

141446.en: Hyasyoda is one of the oldest of the Caldari megacorporations, having been formed shortly after first contact with Gallente when the Caldari were still in their Industrial Age. Throughout State history, Hyasyoda executives have always been conservative and cautious. As a result, the corporation has informally claimed as theirs the age-old Caldari saying that “only the paranoid survive.”

141448.en: I have committed myself to thwarting the Corporate Police Force investigation. Isha tells me that there is a particular structure inside their compound that is crucial to their progress. If I can destroy it, then I will hamper their investigation for weeks — long enough for the trail back to us to dry up.

141449.en: Lady Jariza may be a minor noble, but she can still afford a small army. Don't mess with her guards directly unless you want a needless fight on your hands.

141450.en: Stopping Sansha's Nation is the utmost priority. If you have a weak stomach, I think you should look elsewhere.

141451.en: You couldn't do it? I thought you were made of sterner stuff.

141452.en: Have you retrieved those logs from the communications array yet?

141453.en:
Let me look over these logs.

Strange. There's a lot of chatter between Lady Jariza and Lord Darabi, another local Holder. Been a lot of money transactions from him, too. Although Lord Darabi is a rival of Miyan, there's nothing here that appears sinister. Most likely Lady Jariza has merely given up on courting Miyan and is trying for the next titled family.

141454.en: Lady Jariza, a minor Holder who was rejected by Lord Miyan for political marriage, has been courting Lord Darabi in recent months.

141455.en: Lady Jariza was once rejected by Lord Miyan. Her communications array may hide signs of a revenge plot.

141456.en:
I have a few contacts in Lord Darabi's territory. Maybe something will turn up with this Jariza connection, but I doubt it.

I've learned of a more pressing lead for you. Remember those Amarr ships you ran into? It seems that one Lord Manik has been shopping around for mercenaries.

I'm giving you the meeting location I found while innocently perusing Manik's records. There should be a mercenary contact. You're going to find out who they are, and then we're going to wipe them out. I'll have more instructions when you reach the site.

141457.en: Good luck. I'll contact you remotely when you're done.

141458.en: You're backing out now? I can't believe you'd do that.

141459.en: We didn't even get to the blowing-stuff-up part.

141460.en: Has the deal happened? What's going on?

141461.en: I've got a lock on the contact. I know where he's going.

141463.en: You are to stake out a meeting between Lord Manik's people and mercenaries.

141464.en: Aralin Jick suspects the Amarr ships you encountered were mercenaries hired by Lord Manik. You successfully tracked the mercenaries back to their camp.

141465.en: I'm sending you the mercenary's coordinates. This should be the base they've been operating out of. Wipe them out. Leave no opportunity to rebuild.

141466.en: They're not Sansha, but popping mercs will do in a pinch.

141467.en: Killing mercs isn't even morally objectionable!

141468.en: Killing mercs isn't even morally objectionable!

141470.en: I wish I was there. Looking at the damage estimates, I bet that gang will never be able to rebuild.

141471.en: You know the location of the mercenary camp.

141472.en: You severely ruined the mercenaries' day.

141473.en:
There is not much else I can offer, {[character]player.name}. If you cannot commit to this task, then there is no hope that you will be able to see the entirety of our business to its conclusion.

Take some time, train up, gain some confidence. If you find the courage to take this on, I may still have the job open for you. No guarantees, though — there are plenty of capable eggers out there who'd leap on a job like this.

141474.en:
What did I tell you?

Goodbye, {[character]player.name}.

141475.en: Faurulle, {[character]player.name}. That is your current destination. Our people are waiting for you.

141476.en:
I admit I am impressed. You have shown a surprising level of patience and commitment here, {[character]player.name}. Honestly, I think you could have made it all the way to KFR-ZE, but oh well. Here is your pay: you have earned every last Kredit.

Take some time to relax, place a few bets, buy a few drinks… whatever it is you eggers do in your spare time. When you are ready to continue our work, I have someone I want you to meet.

141477.en: Cross the river before you laugh at the current.

141479.en:
{[character]player.name}, good. I hope the visit to Faurulle didn't take too much out of you. Once again, good work out there. Sadly, it turns out we have one more loose end to tie up.

My people tell me that Hyasyoda has already launched an investigation into the blueprint theft. I suppose this is a play to lend an air of legitimacy to the racket they've been running. The situation is an amusing one, yet also dangerous for us. Our tracks are well covered, but – as they often say in Hyasyoda itself – only the paranoid survive.

They've deployed their security wing, the Corporate Police Force, into “various locations of interest.” I have learned that Onirvura was listed as an area to investigate. They're right here in the constellation, setting up a temporary base for interrogation and imprisonment. Fortunately for us, the CPF has hired a mercenary crew to handle facility defense while they set up. This gives us an opportunity to strike at them without it constituting a direct attack on Hyasyoda personnel. That would muddy the waters a bit, as I'm sure you can appreciate.

I cannot guarantee how long these mercenaries will be on duty, however, nor what kind of reaction your arrival on scene will provoke. What I do know is that if you can destroy the Logistics Center quickly, it will set them back weeks. The paths that lead back to us to will easily have faded into the background by the time they can resume their investigation.

141480.en: Good, then. Remember, {[character]player.name}: The Logistics Center is your only target. You can limit the loss of life here by taking it down quickly and then getting the hell out. If you linger, they will most likely swarm you with reinforcements and pin you down. Don't get complacent just because they're mercs — Hyasyoda is funding them and will make damn sure they get their money's worth.

141481.en: Yes, I can understand your hesitance. Perhaps it is better to focus on misdirection instead. I will prepare your briefing for that task and you can judge for yourself. Speak with me again when you'd like to hear it.

141482.en: Don't worry, {[character]player.name}. I won't deny the assignment was a challenging one. Perhaps you should look into this misdirection plan I have in mind, instead. All is not yet lost.

141483.en: Time is our greatest enemy here, {[character]player.name}. You should get going. The CPF could replace their stand-in mercs at any moment.

141484.en:
Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. Truly. Our ISK is secure and nobody alive suspects us. You have done well, and the money we have secured will help us pursue important things.

Take some time to relax and recuperate. When you are ready, our real work can finally begin.

141485.en: Hyasyoda is one of the oldest of the Caldari mega corporations, having been formed shortly after first contact with Gallente when the Caldari were still in the Industrial Age. Throughout State history, Hyasyoda executives have always been conservative and cautious. As a result, the corporation has informally claimed as theirs the age old Caldari saying that “only the paranoid survive.”

141487.en: After making the sale in Faurulle, I contacted Katsen Isha once more. He tells me that Hyasyoda has launched an investigation into our raid on the facility. I must stop the Corporate Police Force investigation before it can uncover anything. Isha stated that there is a particular structure inside their compound that is crucial to their progress. If I can destroy it, then I will hamper their investigation for weeks — long enough for the trail back to us to dry up.

141489.en:
You want more time? Very well, {[character]player.name}.

I'll hold the job for you a little longer, but if I get the impression that you won't be returning, then I'll just hand it off to someone less busy. Business is business, my friend.

141490.en: What? I think I might just hire someone else. Thanks anyhow, {[character]player.name}.

141491.en: What? I think I might just hire someone else. Thanks anyhow, {[character]player.name}.

141492.en: Have you cleared your schedule yet?

141493.en: I lied to Isha, telling him that I need time to think about our options for selling the formulas. I plan to take this matter to Hyasyoda, even though it was their own facility I just broke into. I have my doubts about Nugoeihuvi, just as I'm unsure that Hyasyoda will even hear me out, but I won't be sure of the full story until I've tried to hear both sides.

141494.en: Very well. We look forward to continued cooperation with you, {[character]player.name}.

141495.en: Then why did you come here? What am I to make of this refusal? I think our business with one another is concluded.

141496.en: I expected as much, I have to say.

141498.en:
Hmm, that is indeed the formula. Good then, I suppose we are going to be working together after all.

Speak with me again when you're ready to talk about where we go from here.

141499.en:
Ah, the famous {[character]player.name}. Welcome! I don't get to mingle with an egger every day, so it's an honor to finally meet you face to face -- or close enough to it anyways.

I assume you've come to help with my next holoreel project here at Impetus? Yes, well, quite a few setbacks already, I'm afraid. As someone like you might appreciate, I didn't fully understand what I was getting into when I decided to film everything in space. Things have become a little more difficult than I expected. We could really use an experienced capsuleer like you to keep everything on track. Frankly, I don't know why we didn't consider the option sooner.

If you're able to help out, then your first task would be to investigate a possible filming location. We're not expecting any major problems, but after an accident last week scouting a similar location, I'd rather have these matters handled by someone who really knows what they're doing. I don't suppose you'd be free and willing to scout the area?

141500.en: I appreciate you stepping in to help us out. I'll talk with accounting about sorting out some pay for your troubles; that shouldn't be a problem. I'll leave my comms link open; once you've scouted the area and it's safe to proceed, get back in touch with me.

141501.en: I understand, {[character]player.name}. Thanks for taking the time to listen, at least, and if you see anyone else in your travels who might be able to help, let me know.

141502.en: No problem, {[character]player.name}. I understand how precious an egger's time can be. Thank you for trying, in any case.

141503.en: Any new information on the site?

141504.en:
Rogue drones and Minmatar, eh? Hmm. Yes, well, I've heard rumors, but I thought that was all just a scary tale to keep people out of there. The place has a history, you see. That's partly why we wanted to film there in the first place, and probably what made those Minnie vagrants think it was a safe place to squat. I suppose we can shoot the area from certain angles to exclude the damn drone hive, but I'll have to check it out myself. At least we can proceed with that, thanks to your good work.

There's a few other favors I'd ask of you, {[character]player.name}, if you're still free. Get back to me if you're interested.

141506.en: Impetus is the main producer of holoreels in New Eden, creating anything from epic historical movies to cheap porn flicks. Their cadre of established directors alone number in the tens of thousands; the actors they employ are literally countless. On one hand, the near infinite nature of their resources allows for the production of many risky, experimental holoreel projects, and yet at the same time, it is all too easy for an aspiring holoreel actress to get lost among a thousand other beautiful faces.

141507.en: I met with Gian Parele, an Impetus holoreel director. His next project involves filming scenes in space, and so he needs the help of a pilot like me. I've been offered a job scouting out one of their shooting locations and making sure it will be safe for them to move in.

141508.en: I met with Gian Parele, an Impetus holoreel director. His next project involves filming scenes in space, and so he asked for my assistance. I accepted a job scouting out one of his team's shooting locations. The place was swarming with rogue drones, and I also noticed a gang of Minmatar pilots in combat cruisers loitering a good distance away. Gian figures them for vagrants and doesn't seem worried. It looks like his crew is going to head in and start filming there soon.

141509.en: The shining star in this holoreel project of mine is a fairly high profile individual, as you might expect. His name is Ralie Ardanne, and he's the son of a low-profile Senator. He's looking to expand his already vast popularity into holoreels, which is where Impetus comes in. Of course, a boy his age and with his connections shouldn't be travelling the spacelanes unguarded. I was hoping you would be interested in meeting him at his father's senatorial residence. I'll let Ralie's guardians know that you are on the way to pick him up. Let me know when you've arrived.

141510.en:
The shining star in this holoreel project of mine is a fairly high profile individual, as you might expect. His name is Ralie Ardanne; the son of a low-profile Senator.
