143215.en:
We need someone to get in there, find their assembly station, and take their ship designs. Since you didn't want to go through the minefield, you'll be taking a more direct approach. If you can't go around it, then you might as well go through it, right?

We've scrambled your comms signal to a Navy frequency. You should, theoretically, read as one of them. This is, of course, according to our guests from Minedrill. You should definitely fit your ship like you're expecting a fight. Hopefully you'll get past the initial security. If not, then you'll have to do some fighting. But that's what you're good for, isn't it? And if the Minedrill guys were lying to us, then we'll take care of them for good.

You can take a more direct approach. You can approach the shipyard proper and try to either sneak past the sentry guns, or blast your way though. Sort of a run-and-gun operation. Same deal, though: once inside, you'll grab the designs and get out of there. Guristas Production will examine them when you return, and we'll probably send some folks over there to level the place depending on what we find. It might even be you.

143216.en:
Alright. Irichi. There is a small chance you may have worked with him before. He was a Lai Dai ordinance engineer who failed one of his annual psychological evaluations. From there, he stowed away aboard a capsuleer's ship heading into lowsec space. His mistake. The capsuleer's crew found him, and he became the capsuleer's toy for two years before he escaped, absolutely insane and missing half of his body parts. We've been taking care of him ever since, and when he's lucid, Irichi is actually quite brilliant. He has made some small recoveries, but we're not out to make him normal. If we did, he might not want to be a pirate any longer. See the problem in that?

The notes you found make a lot more sense under that context, don't they? The fact that he's sending you missives on his “transformation,” or whatever the hell he's calling it, means you're either his favorite culprit at the moment, as is any capsuleer that he comes across, or he suspects someone you're working with. That worries me.

Any time he becomes particularly active in this sort of way, somebody gets killed. Don't believe anything he says about me unless you think it's gonna somehow give you an advantage, okay? He's dangerous, and even if he sees you as some kind of instrument, it's not beyond him to kill you for amusement. Be careful.

143217.en:
Kori is one of the reasons I came over to the Guristas. But he's become soft, and he meddles. I've been monitoring his transmissions to you in the field, and I'm sure he's working with the Navy.

He won't be willing to work with you directly right now. I've arranged for you to meet with one of his operatives, Eroma Eralen. You'll meet him in a deadspace pocket at these coordinates. Be careful, though: Eroma is renowned for his technological ability. He's not good at anything else, but he sure does know his way around illegal pirate tech, especially wavelength and frequency modulation. Meet with him and see what he knows. He owes me a favor, anyway.

143218.en: Obviously, the Sansha need to be cleared from our wormhole site. If you can prove yourself on this, chances are I'll be able to request more assignments to give you. We have early reports of more problems abroad, so I'm sure we can keep you moving from target to target out there.

143219.en:
Alright, you want to pursue the Sansha? That works for me.

Once you've dealt with them report back to me. I'll keep my comms link open.

143220.en:
Listen, {[character]player.name}, the Federation is in dire straits. I'm sure you know that the Caldari megacorporations have “bought” some Gallente systems in Tibus Heth's illegal blind auction. Those bastards have some nerve. But it's time the Federation took it all back!

Nugoeihuvi is attempting to form a foothold in Iges. They've got the early stages of a mining base established and plan to begin production very soon. From the looks of it, Nugoeihuvi plans to be there for a long time. We need you to spoil their plans. Take out all the industrial vessels you can find at this base. Be wary of any escorts, though: they do not look willing to leave.

< font color = #EE3B3B >Be careful: This mission will take you into lowsec. I would recommend switching to a ship designed for inter-capsuleer conflicts, just in case your piratical brethren want a piece of you en route. Once you get to the site itself, though, you shouldn't receive very much resistance. The megacorporations aren't exactly known for the might of their security forces.

143221.en:
We've spotted a few Angel Cartel ships roaming near here. We believe that they are part of a reconnaissance force sent to scout for a weakness in security. We sent men out to intercept them, but none have returned. Another surveillance team caught sight of the pirates again recently, though.

The Angels are led by an infamous captain, Jenmai Hirokan. Do not underestimate him! Many have done so in the past and have paid the ultimate price.

I won't keep you here any longer. I'm sure you'll want to get going before we lose sight of Hirokan and his allies again.

143224.en:
The Caldari Providence Directorate has today announced the winning bids for their recent auction of Gallente space. Big winners include Kaalakiota and Sukuuvestaa, while Ishukone makes do with just a single system. The winning corporations are now authorized to exploit these systems to the fullest for as long as they remain in Caldari hands.

As expected, the "blind auction" format seems to have made it difficult for even comparatively wealthy sub-megas, such as perennially successful Ytiri, to gain any kind of foothold. All eight megacorps had at least one successful bid, with Suvee leading the charge and claiming fourteen systems. Meanwhile, in a move many are describing as "baffling," Ishukone has laid claim to a single system: Intaki, generally considered the least promising prospect in the auction due to its comparative lack of mineral wealth and vast native population. Sources believe that this was the only bid Ishukone made, and several political commentators have questioned where the financially struggling megacorp managed to find the money.

You best get going. I'd thank you for the assistance you provided, but an invitation to a meeting with a Domination agent says more than any words of mine will.

143235.en:
Perhaps it's not worth the trouble to take down the Sansha encampment. They might have already gone in and destabilized the wormhole. We play by risk and reward, and the reward here looks like it'll be too low.

There's a high-priority shipment that has been sitting around waiting for someone capable enough to move it. It's headed to the Serpentis research facilities in Fountain, but Sarpati's crew is going to handle moving it from Curse over to their Headquarters. They were supposed to take it directly from this station but we've lost contact with the research team in charge of that operation. The job is yours if you want it. All you need to do is get it to nearby Serpentis Corp. transport hub, from there they'll handle the rest.

The cargo is small so you could easily fit it inside an interceptor or covert ops and I would suggest you do just that, {[character]player.name}. I will not accept any excuses for the cargo's disappearance.

143236.en:
At the moment I have more work than I have people, so you need to choose how you want to proceed.

We also have a shipment of important research material that needs to make it to Serpentis hands. The Inquest scientists in charge of the operation have been delayed, and moving the goods is a high-priority task we need someone to take over. We may also require an investigation into the reasons for the delay at Serpentis' end.

Both tasks need to be followed up. I don't care what you choose; we'll give one to you, and one to the next egger brave or stupid enough to show up down here.

Lai Dai Corporation is attempting to form a foothold in Esesier. They've got the early stages of a mining base established and plan to begin production very soon. From the looks of it, Lai Dai Corporation plans to be there for a long time. We need you to spoil their plans. Take out all the industrial vessels you can find at this base. Be wary of any escorts, though: They do not look willing to leave.

< font color = #EE3B3B >Be careful: This mission will take you into lowsec. I would recommend switching to a ship designed for inter-capsuleer conflicts, just in case your piratical brethren want a piece of you en route. Once you get to the site itself, though, you shouldn't receive very much resistance. The megacorporations aren't exactly known for the might of their security forces.

143248.en:
The Caldari Providence Directorate has today announced the winning bids for their recent auction of Gallente space. Big winners include Kaalakiota and Sukuuvestaa, while Ishukone makes do with just a single system. The winning corporations are now authorized to exploit these systems to the fullest for as long as they remain in Caldari hands.

As expected, the "blind auction" format seems to have made it difficult for even comparatively wealthy sub-megas, such as perennially successful Ytiri, to gain any kind of foothold. All eight megacorps had at least one successful bid, with Suvee leading the charge and claiming fourteen systems. Meanwhile, in a move many are describing as "baffling," Ishukone has laid claim to a single system: Intaki, generally considered the least promising prospect in the auction due to its comparative lack of mineral wealth and vast native population. Sources believe that this was the only bid Ishukone made, and several political commentators have questioned where the financially struggling megacorp managed to find the money.

143250.en:
Damn Heth and his illegal auctions! He “sold” entire Gallente systems to Caldari megacorporations as if he actually owned Gallente space. The Federation will not stand for it anymore, and you will help us in fighting back!

Kaalakiota is sending its own security forces to Alamel in an effort to bolster its influence. Seems like they were expecting a fight all along – they know the true tenacity of the Gallente people. We've tracked a caravan of troop transport ships in Alamel; we think they're getting ready for a planetside invasion. Luckily, you can stop them in their tracks. Take out the transport ships while there's still time.

143251.en: The Caldari fleet is docked at a fueling station, preparing for their attack. They're sitting ducks, or fish in a barrel, or whatever cliché you want to use. What makes this a great opportunity for us is their fueling depots. Those silos have enough energy stored in them to take out three fleets, if they happen to catch on fire. And that's what you'll be doing. Destroy at least one of the fuel depots, which will cascade and destroy the surrounding ships. Ignore the big ships and go straight for the fuel depots. There may be some guards there, but your main targets are the fuel depots. This is way more bang for your buck than you were expecting, huh?

143252.en: Using the information from the hacked Venal Regional Comms tower, Cilis discovered the location of burgeoning Caldari Navy fleet. Stationed at a fueling depot, gearing up for an inclement strike on the Guristas, the fleet was prone, an easy target to pick off. Cilis's plan was to have me attack the fuel silos, so the explosion would cascade and destroy the ships as they wait to refuel. The damage done in this strike took out a significant portion of the Navy fleet.

143253.en: Using the information from the hacked Venal Regional Comms tower, Cilis discovered the location of burgeoning Caldari Navy fleet. Stationed at a fueling depot, gearing up for an imminent strike on the Guristas, the fleet is prone, an easy target to pick off. Cilis's plan is to have me attack the fuel silos, which will cascade and destroy the ships as they wait to refuel. Any damage done in this strike will take out a significant portion of the Navy fleet.

143254.en: We'll make arrangements, but you'd be mistaken to think that we'll just forget this.

143255.en:
Thanks to your work back at the comms tower, we've discovered the locations of a budding Navy fleet. This Navy group is much larger than ones we've seen in recent times. It looks like they're trying to weaken our hold on the fringe systems and consolidate power in Venal.

Not quite a bad plan on paper, to be completely honest. But they're becoming cocky, expecting to sneak up on us and take out our forces with ease. We'll do them one better, though, and surprise them. If we strike first, they won't be able to muster their forces enough to overwhelm us. And that's where you come in.

The fleet is docked at a fueling station, preparing for their attack. They're sitting ducks, or fish in a barrel, or whatever cliché you want to use. What makes this a great opportunity for us is their fueling depots. Those silos have enough energy stored in them to take out three fleets, if they happen to catch on fire. And that's what you'll be doing. Destroy at least one of the fuel depots, which will cascade and destroy the surrounding ships. Ignore the big ships and go straight for the fuel depots. There may be some guards there, but your main targets are the fuel depots. This is way more bang for your buck than you were expecting, huh?

143256.en: The Navy has a habit of locking their gates before a big strike so that only smaller ships can get through. This is a stealth operation: run and gun. You may be flying something small, but you'll take out so much more than your ship should be capable of. Wanton destruction is a rather satisfying feeling, to be sure.

143257.en: The miners are happy, but now the station owners are not. An Angel Cartel pirate has stolen some sensitive documents from them, and I'm tasked with quietly resolving the matter. I'm entrusting you with this. Get those documents back for me.

143258.en: The miners are happy, but now the station owners are not. A Guristas pirate has stolen some sensitive documents from them, and I'm tasked with quietly resolving the matter. I'm entrusting you with this. Get those documents back for me.

143259.en: The miners are happy, but now the station owners are not. A Blood Raider pirate has stolen some sensitive documents from them, and I'm tasked with quietly resolving the matter. I'm entrusting you with this. Get those documents back for me.

143260.en: The miners are happy, but now the station owners are not. A Serpentis pirate has stolen some sensitive documents from them, and I'm tasked with quietly resolving the matter. I'm entrusting you with this. Get those documents back for me.

143263.en:
Thanks to your efforts we've got our man back, and more importantly the information he had inside that skull of his.

It seems our enemies have been busy. They have secretly been building up a Bio-Weapon Facility in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Such facilities are in direct violation of the Yulai convention between the empires. However, we're not going to inform CONCORD of this. No doubt they would just claim it to be a chemical storage facility or some such.

No, what we're going to do is remove the facility by force. I want the facility razed, the main processing center destroyed and, if you get the chance, acquire a sample of the bioweapon.

143271.en:
You have no idea how much you frightened the Navy with that last strike. They're completely demoralized and retreating to a rally point in a nearby deadspace pocket. Turns out, they had a carrier waiting in their midst to bring extra destruction to our members. Well, we'll take care of that.

The fleet is pinned down, but we're having trouble getting to them. They've locked themselves in the pocket, only allowing shuttles to get through their gates. We thought we'd have a large siege on our hands, but a rather brilliant idea came to me. I am, of course, a capsuleer like yourself; we think differently than the mortals we have to deal with.

Time for a suicide run. Doesn't that sound like fun? We'll give you a shuttle to take specifically for this mission. (We have quite a stockpile of useless Caldari shuttles, for some reason.) You can join our talented Guristas Capsuleer Fleet, which specializes in suicide missions. Meet with the fleet at the deadspace pocket, pick up some of our “dirty” explosives from a fellow fleet member, and fly at the carrier. You'll lose the shuttle, but you'll take out that carrier. I wish I could go on this mission, but I've got my own orders to follow.

You will lose this shuttle that we have provided you, but you won't get podded. However, you will be a very easy target for wayward pirates in the area. Not to worry, though: You can minimize the risk for this mission. Besides, I'll make sure that you're handsomely rewarded for this effort. Hell, the thrill of the kill should be enough, right?

143272.en: You're quitting this mission because you're scared, aren't you? Coward.

143274.en: Travel to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system where miners are in conflict over an asteroid field. Find out what's happened to a small, independent mining operation fallen silent. Also, keep an eye on any messages in your Local channel. I don't want you bringing the crew back here, but they might need to be moved to someplace safe.

143275.en: Hey, {[character]player.name}, ever been screwed over by the big corporations? Well, here's a chance for some payback. There's controversy out in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, where ORE lays dubious mining claim to a massive asteroid field. Problem is, independent groups working the field are at risk of being consumed – literally. There's something strange going on out there. Interested in finding out what's happening, and striking a blow for the little guy?

143276.en: Good, because there's no time to lose. We received a distress signal from a small operation. They were trying to get what they could from the field before the ORE hulks blew through. Something seems to have gone wrong. Find out what happened and save the crew, materiel and product that you can.

143277.en: What's your progress on offering aid to those miners? Without their independent streak, the big corps might take over that entire system. And don't be bringing any of the miners to my front door, either.

143278.en: Yes, I suppose the blood money offered elsewhere might be more lucrative.

143279.en: Yes, I suppose the blood money offered elsewhere might be more lucrative.

143280.en: A convoy of civilian ships traveling through a region known to be rife with pirate activity has become vulnerable due to its contingent of escort combat vessels not showing up for some reason.  Their distress signal has been picked up in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system.

143281.en: Travel to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system where miners are in conflict over an asteroid field. Find out what's happened to a small, independent mining operation fallen silent. Also, keep an eye on any messages in your Local channel. I don't want you bringing the crew back here, but they might need to be moved to someplace safe.

143282.en:
While I enjoy the tremendous service capsuleers provide agents like me, I can't begin to count how many times I've been let down over the years by those lacking the proper skills, judgment, diligence, or a rudimentary attention span. It seems that the last few I hired to provide an armed escort for a convoy of civilian transports has gone missing, probably lured away by a more lucrative job.

I need you to head to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and meet up with the convoy at once. If they‘re in any kind of trouble when you arrive, please take care of it.

143283.en: There's really no more time to waste with conversation.  Head out at once.

143284.en: What a surprise.  Yet another unreliable capsuleer.

143286.en: You shouldn't be chatting with me when you have work to do.

143287.en: Well done fending off those pirates. Some of them escaped, you say?

143288.en: Hey, {[character]player.name}, ever been screwed over by the big corporations? Well, here's a chance for some payback. 143291.en: Yes, I suppose the blood money offered elsewhere might be more lucrative.

Something seems to have gone wrong. Find out what happened and save the crew, materiel and product that you can.

143293.en: After only being able to make off with a fraction of the civilians from their raid, The Seven were tracked back to their hideout.  Attacking them there should eliminate their local base of operations and allow for the remaining hostages to be rescued.

143294.en: There's hope yet for the small entrepreneur! ORE's dismissive attitude toward miner claims in that system has brought a lot of bad publicity on the corporation. Your efforts have gone a long way toward causing that.

143295.en:
The Seven? I was hoping it wasn't that particular gang again.

While we're very grateful that you managed to prevent most of the civilians from being kidnapped, there is still the issue of the ones that were taken. When they warped away from the last encounter, we were able to track them down and obtain the coordinates of that hideout. I'm prepared to grant you the authority, on behalf of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, to hunt down these criminals. What do you say? Are you still willing to help?

143296.en: Great!  You should depart at once if you're going to catch the Seven before the hostages are moved to another facility.

143297.en: Whatever.  I'll find someone else to clean up your mess.

143298.en: Hey, I understand.  We all have priorities in life.  Mine just happen to be productivity, compassion, and loyalty, while yours appear to be somewhere between lethargy and unscrupulousness.

143299.en: It might be a good idea to maintain radio silence during this particular mission, don't you think?

143300.en: I'd flatter you with congratulations, but there's still work to be done.

143301.en: Phenod, the resident idiot of The Seven's organization, has stranded himself on his way to pick up some hostages.  With his DNA, a suitable transponder disguise can be forged allowing some undercover work against the gang.

143302.en:
One of those hostages you rescued turned out to be quite resourceful. While aboard the pirate's vessel, she hacked into its communication logs and discovered something interesting. One of The Seven's core members, a man named Phenod, has managed to strand himself in space on his way to pick up some victims that were kidnapped some time ago.

We have a golden opportunity here to not only strike a blow to The Seven, but recover some of our earlier losses as well. Head out to these coordinates at once and blast Phenod to pieces, but be sure to scrape some of his DNA off the front of your ship before returning. We'll use it to forge an identification transponder for your next mission.

143304.en: Am I going to have to take care of this myself?

143305.en: Seriously?  Phenod is too much for you to handle?  I've heard he's The Seven's resident idiot.

143306.en: Do you have a sample of Phenod's DNA yet?

143307.en: Stick around, there's more to do.

143308.en: Using Phenod's DNA to concoct a disguised transponder beacon, the shuttle provided by the agent should be large enough to retrieve the additional hostages and bring them to safety.  The only problem is that, if whoever shows up to drop off the hostages isn't fooled, the shuttle will be unable to respond.

143309.en:
I hope you didn't have too much trouble with Phenod.

Our engineers have completed the fake transponder and installed it in a shuttle, which is ready for you to take it to the rendezvous point. The story is that Phenod's ship was disabled and he's been forced to limp to the rendezvous point in an ordinary shuttle. I don't know who's going to meet you there, but it'll probably be another officer from The Seven, so try not to pick a fight. Remember, this shuttle is unarmed and doesn't have any real defenses, so if your disguise fails, you'll have to make a run for it.

Oh, and there's one last thing: That shuttle doesn't have the oxygen capacity to hold that many people for very long, so you won't be able to make it back here. We're sending a rescue vessel to linger nearby, but for obvious reasons it can't be anywhere inside sensor range of this meeting. Use the acceleration gate in the area to meet up with it and drop off the hostages.

143310.en: Not many capsuleers volunteer for this kind of duty outside the comforts of their preferred ship.  I admire your courage.

143311.en: So you've gotten this far only to give up now?

143312.en: Oh well, let's just hope CONCORD doesn't see you in that shuttle broadcasting a pirate faction signature.  Good luck!

143314.en: Now that was some really impressive flying, I have to admit!  The hostages are quite grateful to have been returned safely.  In fact, I have a message for you from one of them, if you can stick around for a minute or two.

143315.en: One of the hostages rescued during the previous mission has offered a reward for destroying Locced's ship and provided coordinates to his current location.

143316.en:
Here's the rescued hostage's message:

“Brave Capsuleer,

Allow me to offer my sincere thanks for your efforts to rescue me and my fellow hostages from the clutches of The Seven. If you would be interested, I've offered {[character]agentID.name} a sum of ISK to pay you in exchange for doing me a little favor.

During my time with The Seven, one of their officers was so cruel that I‘m inclined to seek revenge on a personal level. Seeing as you have become quite familiar with their organization and tactics, I can think of no one better suited for carrying out this task. Please destroy his ship for me.

If you‘re interested, the target‘s name is Locced and I happen to know where he‘ll be in the near future, as one of his lieutenants let the information slip during casual conversation when I was nearby.

Once again, thank you for freeing me from The Seven‘s clutches. I hope you find my offer appealing.“

Well, {[character]player.name}, what do you say?

143317.en: The former hostage will be very excited to hear you accepted the offer.  Here are Locced's coordinates.

143318.en: That former hostage is going to be heartbroken.

143319.en: I'm going to assume Locced beat you down like a helpless child, at least that's what I'm going to tell every other capsuleer I deal with from this point forward.

143320.en: The former hostage is eagerly awaiting news of your victory.

143321.en:
What am I, your receptionist? Here's another message from that hostage you rescued:

“Trustworthy Capsuleer,

It's going to take Locced quite a while to replace that ship. Well done, and thank you again for all of your efforts against The Seven.”

143322.en: Travel to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} here a disabled ship is in jeopardy. Save the crew by addressing whatever problem afflicts the vessel.

143323.en: {[character]player.name}, a mission of mercy needs your immediate attention. One of our ships has suffered an almost complete power loss near a spatial rift, and is adrift toward the anomaly. There's no time to lose. Get to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, find the ship, and help get it operational again.

143324.en: {[character]player.name}, what are you doing? Our people are going to die out there. “Can't do it?” You mean “Won't do it”! Bloody pirate!

143325.en: Good. You have no time to lose.

143326.en: What are you doing? Our people are dying in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. There's no time for this!

143327.en: Good work. Your efforts have not gone unnoticed. We'll try to get that model upgraded to avoid this kind of problem again.

143328.en: What? Maybe I didn't make myself clear. There are lives at stake!

143329.en: I should have known. Your kind disgusts me.

143330.en: What? You're telling me profit is more important than innocent lives?

143331.en: You're doing the right thing. Countless lives depend on you.

143332.en:
We have an unfortunate situation on our hands. One of our officers has apparently been targeted by a Mordu's assassination squad. We aren't sure who hired them, but we suspect that it's an internal dispute, i.e. they were hired by someone inside the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name}. We need the bounty hunters eliminated ASAP, before they are able to do any permanent damage. We would rather that the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name}'s good relationship with the Mordus Legion will not be tainted by this incident, so keep it clean and leave no evidence of the battle behind if possible. The Mordus Legion are a powerful mercenary organization that we sometimes rely on, but obviously that does not deter all of their members from targeting our people if the price is right...

Just a word of warning though, these Mordus goons are no laughing matter. Don't underestimate them.

143333.en:
One of our patrols spotted a Mordu's Legion strike force not far from here. We're not certain about their intentions, but we'd like you to take them out just in case. Those damned Mordu's assassination squads have been known to murder our members in the past, so we keep a good eye on them. We know their exact location this time, and I'd like you to take them out before they know what hit them. I'm counting on you {[character]player.name}.

Just a word of warning though, these Mordus goons are no laughing matter. Don't underestimate them.

We would rather that the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name}'s good relationship with the Mordus Legion will not be tainted by this incident, so keep it clean and leave no evidence of the battle behind if possible.  The Mordus Legion are a powerful mercenary organization that we sometimes rely on, but obviously that does not deter all of their members from targeting our people if the price is right...

143337.en:
One of our patrols spotted a Mordu's Legion strike force not far from here. We're not certain about their intentions, but we'd like you to take them out just incase. Those damned Mordu's assassination squads have been known to murder our members in the past, so we keep a good eye on them. We know their exact location this time, and I'd like you to take them out before they know what hit them. I'm counting on you {[character]player.name}.

Just a word of warning though, these Mordus goons are no laughing matter. Don't underestimate them.

143339.en: Bring Arizam a Graduation Certificate which you can acquire by speaking to one of his agents. The agents are located at Data Centers near one of the stargates in Kudi, Polfaly and Ferira.

143340.en: Bring Pinala a Graduation Certificate which you can acquire by speaking to one of her agents. The agents are located in Data Centers in Arlulf, Emolgranlan and Engosi.

143341.en: Unless you've been sent here by one of my subordinates, I have nothing for you.  If you're interested, you can find them in the Data Centers in Arlulf, Emolgranlan and Engosi.

143342.en: Unless you've been sent here by one of my subordinates, I have nothing for you.  If you're interested, you can find them in the Data Centers in Kudi, Polfaly and Ferira.

143345.en: Unless you've been sent here by one of my subordinates, I have nothing for you.  If you're interested, you can find them in Data Centers in Muer, Abenync and Ekuenbiron.

143347.en:
There's a difference between being taken seriously and letting the inmates run the asylum. Diplomacy must resume, even if to only keep things just below war being declared.

It's a strange game, friend. I don't think even the diplomats fully understand it. Still, this is one of those times diplomats are useful again.

Take our envoy over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. From there he will meet with the Gallente envoy to begin non-public negotiations. If all goes well, the situation will simply vanish from the public's consciousness and life will continue as normal.

143348.en: This situation snowballed. Diplomacy must resume, even if to only keep things just below war being declared. Take our envoy over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. From there he will meet with the Gallente envoy to begin non-public negotiations. If all goes well, the situation will simply vanish from the public's consciousness and life will continue as normal.

143349.en:
We need to move fast. The situation is evolving in unexpected ways. No no, don't sit down. I'll explain this as fast as I can.

While you were out on your last assignment, Ekire himself was mortally wounded in an assassination attempt by unknown assailants. We suspect Wiyrkomi, of course - they have the most to gain from his death, both politically and pragmatically speaking. Likewise, if he dies we stand to take a massive political blow.

Ekire is currently at the Egonics Inc. Development Studio at Parchanier V, bleeding severely and fading fast. Due to a rare blood condition he contracted in an Umokkan jungle while serving as a Legion marine a decade back, transfusion via normal means would kill him. For the procedure to be at all possible he needs an aortal purifier, a seldom-used piece of medical equipment which they don't have at that particular station's med bay.

I need you to head out to Auderne immediately, to the Poteque Pharmaceuticals Biotech Production plant there, and pick up what may be the only aortal purifier available in this whole damn constellation, then bring it out to the doctors in Parchanier. His life - and our success in our campaign here - may very well depend on your speed in this matter.

Go! Fly swiftly.

143350.en: Green Arisite is relatively worthless because of the high costs of reprocessing; one is far better off mining Gneiss instead. As a result, you won't find the former ore on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Arisite at the mission location, loading the "Mining" default overview will show all ores. If you're familiar with creating custom overview settings, Green Arisite is shown by enabling "Gneiss".

143351.en: You met MIO investigator Kandus Sandar.

143352.en: Kandus Sandar, an MIO agent in Nahyeen, requires aid.

143353.en: Excellent. There are at least three survivors who escaped in life pods. Find them, and we'll be able to figure out what went wrong. And be careful out there - it's an experimental ship, and we don't know what kind of threat it might pose.

143354.en: Have you rescued the crew of The Paryi yet? I've got some very important people breathing down my neck about this.

143355.en: That's your call. Honestly, I don't blame you for backing out now - I'm not superstitious, but this situation spooks me out.

143356.en: That's your call. Honestly, I don't blame you for backing out now - I'm not superstitious, but this situation spooks me out.

143357.en:
Dr. Ateshi has provided proof that The Anomaly is active and dangerous. The experimental warp drive successfully opened a wormhole, but it was unstable and the resulting radiation fried the crew's equipment, and their brains. They've been trapped in the darkest parts of space for two decades, slowly succumbing to the sickness - there's nothing human left about them. Now that they're back in our space, the radiation is a risk not just to us but everything for hundreds of kilometers around.

My superiors have determined that it's not worth the risk of retrieving the warp drive; you need to destroy the ship entirely before the damage spreads. Fortunately, we know where they went: They jumped into the middle of a rogue drone hive. Dr. Ateshi thinks they're trying to feed off the rogue drones' power to recharge. If you can get her to one of the surrounding ships, she can jam their equipment and make them vulnerable.

143358.en: I'm so relieved to hear that. Keep your wits about you and you should do just fine. Remember, don't bother shooting until Dr. Ateshi has deactivated their shield rechargers.

143359.en: Have you destroyed The Anomaly yet? It's essential that you do it before it has the chance to jump away again!

143360.en: Shame about Dr. Ateshi, but she knew the risks. Good job - you've earned everything coming to you.

143361.en: After coming so far? Do you know what they're going to do to me when they find out you quit?

143362.en: After coming so far? Do you know what they're going to do to me when they find out you quit?

143363.en: Great. You get out there, and you've got some rescue money coming your way. I don't really care who you rescue, just so long as you rescue someone. Fair warning, though – the ones you don't rescue are likely to remember it.

143364.en: Can't say I blame you, though I'm going to have to let you go for now. Getting these kinds of jobs filled can bring an agent like me to the notice of important people, you know? Talk to you later.

143365.en: Really? That's it? You're quitting? Why'd you agree to do it in the first place, then?

143367.en: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your reward, and the limelight for being a hero to those folks – you've earned it. You should know, however, that the folks you didn't save have already made it very clear that they're not happy with you.

143369.en: The Prophet of the Seventh Sphere

143373.en: Since the scouting party is dead and gone, we've got the primary fleet hanging around in space and practically begging for someone to blow them to pieces. Seeing as how you did such a thorough job with their scouts, you were naturally our first choice for taking on their big guns. Once you're finished with them, Okelle won't have anyone to help him except his brother. And once our interrogators are done with Okelle, he'll have given us all the information we need to hunt down Martogar. It's only a matter of time - that is, unless the primary fleet manages to deploy more scouts and continue their murderous rampage, so you better get on your way to stop them.

143374.en:
I'm glad I can rely on you for something like this, {[character]player.name}. It seems so many capsuleers are becoming more risk-averse these days. It's a mindset I simply can't understand.

Remember that our cargo is precious and there is zero room for error here. If that formula goes missing, so will my desire to work with you. That is our ISK, and the entirety of our business together. Prepare yourself accordingly.

143375.en:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places and go to "Bookmarks." Then right-click on the objective item (the relic) and choose "Set Destination." Then go to your ship's control panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate star system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click on the relic and select "Warp to within 0." Once you've arrived at the location, look at your Overview and find the cargo container; right-click on it and select "Approach." Once you've approached to within 2500 meters, right-click the cargo container and select "Open." A window will now open, displaying the container's contents. Click and drag the relic into your cargo hold. Now return with it to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name} for your reward.

143376.en:
Hmm... Yes, I do have some work for you.

Although the Cartel usually has a firm grip over the criminal strata in our system, Sansha's Nation has been poking its ugly nose in here of late-- which is perfectly fine with us. In fact, watching the two outlawed organizations duke it out is one of my favorite pastimes. If we're lucky, it will give both sides a good bruising, which will only work in our favor.

Of course, there's also bad news. An InterBus ship traveling to {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} got caught in the middle of one of the pirate warzones. The ship was damaged beyond repair and can neither warp out nor navigate away from the crossfire. Your task is to rescue the ship's crew. Please retrieve them before any more harm is done; they're already scared out of their minds. The faster you get this done, the better.

Oh, and before you leave I'd like to give you a word of advice. When you venture into this particular deadspace area, the warpgates are not locked, which gives you the chance to avoid most of the conflict, if you're not up to the fight. However, I'm told only frigate and destroyer-class ships can activate the first gate.

Good luck.

143386.en:
Quitting a mission invariably results in a loss of faction standing; it is almost always in a character's best interest to complete all missions he or she accepts.

However, a character may freely decline a mission when it is first offered, as long as it isn't one of those rare "storyline" missions; after that, declining another mission within four hours of the first does result in a loss of standing. Still, in general, a capsuleer's career is usually long and eventful enough that a few such minor hits to standing may not be too large a price.

143387.en:
Your last assignment is to scan down a Gas cloud. We've created an artificial cloud pocket for you, and while you'd usually reap it with a Gas Cloud Harvester, our only concern is that you make it through to the second area and bring back the Proof of Discovery document.

The materials found inside these clouds are used to make biochemical enhancers known as boosters. It is a dangerous industry, populated by dangerous people. You're safe this time, but Gas clouds will occasionally be inhabited by pirates. Stay alert if you're on the prowl for them.

As soon as you accept the mission, we'll provide you with the passkey into the second area.

143407.en:
Banidine is normally all but worthless, so real miners don't usually bother with the stuff. Still, I've found a buyer who's willing to take whatever we can mine. So, get me 20,000 units of Banidine and I'll make it worth your while.

There's an asteroid field near here that's lousy with the stuff – I've bookmarked it for you. Get back as soon as you can and I'll arrange a little bonus.

Remember to fit a decent miner to your ship before you go. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, loading the "Mining" default overview will show all ores. If you're familiar with creating custom overview settings, Banidine is shown by enabling "Veldspar".

143408.en: You've destroyed a pirate ring that would have taken us months to work through. High marks all around.

143409.en:
Harkan?! Terrus Harkan is the traitor? Harkan, former head of Lord Miyan's security and hero of the countless military campaigns, is the traitor?

This is very bad.

143410.en: Yes, don't worry.  I've no more tricks up my sleeve, you'll definitely get what you want when you're done with this simple courier job.

143411.en: I need you to help out. There is fierce fighting going on in a nearby system and we have marines here that need to be moved out there as soon as humanly possible. Are you willing to help our cause?

143412.en: The local news recently aired a story on poor immigrants in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  Apparently some of the families have fallen on hard times and lack the funds to even buy the most basic necessities.  A few concerned citizens in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} asked me to have these clothes delivered to the needy in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, which they can make use of.  I'd like you to make the first leg of the trip, which is to drop off the goods at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Officials at the station will take care of the rest.

143413.en: Take these people to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and don't tell anyone they were here.

143414.en: Deliver the secure coded package for your agent.

143415.en:
Well, it's my sister. I mean, I remembered her birthday this time, I swear. I planned out the gift, got it ordered in advance — and it was not cheap, let me tell you. I found a specialty perfume maker, and it turns out my sister likes the smells of really damn expensive things. And of course the fancy-pants perfumer has a ridiculous waiting list. But I got everything done in time!

I just need you to deliver it. I'll pay you, okay?

143416.en:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is in the middle of constructing an outpost in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Our engineers there claim to lack a few loads of construction blocks to finish the work, and I was asked to deliver some blocks to that station.

Could you please take the material straight to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}? Our people in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} will take care of retrieving them from your hangar there for the construction project.

143417.en: They'll offload the chemicals immediately. You should be fine on your ship. They'll be gassing every corner of the structure, though.

143418.en:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is in the middle of constructing an outpost in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Our engineers there claim to lack a few loads of construction blocks to finish the work, and I was asked to deliver some blocks to that station.

Could you please take the material straight to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}? Our people in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} will take care of retrieving them from your hangar there for the construction project.

143419.en:
Now what I need you to do is deliver a batch of veldspar ore to a location not far from here. I was supposed to drop off the batch there for one of my clients, but Gatti's attack 'complicated' matters. I dare not leave my current location, if an agent of the Zhara family or Kazka Bandits spots me, I'm done for.

I managed to smuggle the ore out of the asteroid belt during my escape, so as long as you can bring an industrial over here then you're all set to go.

143424.en: I need you to help out. There is fierce fighting going on in a nearby system and we have marines here that need to be moved out there as soon as humanly possible. Are you willing to help our cause?

143425.en: Take these people to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and don't tell anyone they were here.

143426.en:
I have not been very impressed by your performance, and as a result this will be your last task for me. I have another student arriving soon, somebody who I'm hoping will not fail me like you have. Everything must be in order when he arrives, and for that to happen I'm going to need you to bring me some electronic parts. Replacing and rebuilding the things that were stolen from me will take some time.

Even though you are not competent enough to become my disciple, I do appreciate your interest. If you complete this quickly, maybe I'll reward you with a little bit extra.

143428.en:
You've mined, processed, built and fought. Now let's see if you can transport my goods safely.

Take these electronic parts out to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} as fast as possible.

143430.en:
