143432.en:
You've mined, processed, built and fought. Now let's see if you can transport my goods safely.

Take these electronic parts out to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} as fast as possible.

143434.en:
You've mined, processed, built and fought. Now let's see if you can transport my goods safely.

Take these electronic parts out to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} as fast as possible.

143436.en:
We've got a shipment of vaccines that need to be delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} in a hurry. I'm willing to provide a substantial bonus if they're delivered right away. Regardless, the meds need to be delivered soon, though.

Be sure to move the medicine into your cargo hold before you set out. And note the hasty delivery required — you don't have much time!

143437.en:
Well, you're pretty green, by the look of you, but I've got no choice. You may have heard all the rumors. The entire frontier is buzzing with reports that we're pretty much at war with the Amarrians. I can't say either way, for sure, but I do know that all this war talk has led to some big headaches when it comes to commercial traffic and trade-route management. Passenger liners are all booked, haulers have been pre-empted by the military or by wealthy clients... god, it's just a mess out there.

Anyway, as you may have seen, the docks here at {[location]agentStationID.name} are filled to overflowing with tons of goods, and we can't seem to find enough transport to get them to their destinations. I need to get some of this stuff out of here.

Ah, here: we've got a shipment of vaccines that need to be delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} in a hurry. I'm willing to provide a substantial bonus if they're delivered right away. Regardless, the meds need to be delivered soon, though.

Say the word and you can move the stuff into your cargo hold. Can you do it?

143438.en: The {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} station manager has reported a lack of mono-cell batteries in their supply depot, a situation that could result in a temporary shutdown of the entire station. Deliver the batteries to them as quickly as possible.

143439.en:
"The deal," as you so quaintly put it, my young friend, is this: The station manager of {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} recently reported to us a serious lack of mono-cell batteries in their supply depot, a situation that could result in a temporary shutdown of the entire station. We need to help them out, and I'd like you to deliver the necessary goods to them.

Simple enough, eh? Well, are you interested or not? I know of several others who would happily take this offer in your stead.

143440.en: It's tough to quit smoking when you've got a warehouse full of cigarettes within arm's reach. Take every crate of that crap you can find in that warehouse over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and leave it there. Quickly, before I change my mind!

143441.en:
A convoy of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} ships stumbled upon a stash of viral agents in {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name} while passing through the system. They dropped it off here so that a specialist can take a look at it and perhaps trace it to a particular individual or corporation. Now that they're done, I need you to take it to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for further research.

Don't worry about getting busted by customs for transporting the viral agents: We've cleared the matter with them and they'll be expecting you.

143442.en: One commodity we all have a hard time living without is oxygen. One of our buyers is on a station that's close to running out of air, so I want you to fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and give them  a bit more.

143443.en: A friend of mine, Professor Tsulmeki, has asked me to safely transport his most recent graduating class to a seminar. Could you go over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off for me? Bring them there on time; I don't want them to be late.

143444.en: A friend of mine, Professor Tsulmeki, has asked me to safely transport his entire research team to an important seminar. Could you go over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off for me? Bring them there on time; I don't want them to be late.

143445.en: Deliver these crates of long-limb roes to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}  station.

143446.en: We've been having some trouble with deliveries ending up at incorrect destinations. I guess these shipping companies can't be trusted to do their job properly, so I need you to fill in for them. Take these holoreels to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I will reward you for the effort.

143447.en: Have you seen the price of oil around here lately? It's absurd! Our clients are demanding more, but all we've got is the synthetic stuff, so take a load of it over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

143448.en: We've been having some trouble with deliveries ending up at incorrect destinations. I guess these shipping companies can't be trusted to do their job properly, so I need you to fill in for them. Take these holoreels to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I will reward you for the effort.

143449.en: Somebody broke into my brother's home yesterday and stole his entire gun collection. He'll get into heaps of trouble with his superiors if they find out, so I want you to help him make the problem go away. Fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop off a new set of weapons. I'll modify the ID codes on the guns, and nobody will suspect a thing.

143450.en: My friend is getting married. We need entertainment for his bachelor party tomorrow, but I can't just show up with the dancers myself. Take these "performers" to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. Be sure to get them there on time so we can start the fun!

143451.en:
A convoy of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} ships stumbled upon a stash of viral agents in {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name} while passing through the system. They dropped it off here so that a specialist can take a look at it and perhaps trace it to a particular individual or corporation. Now that they're done, I need you to take it to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for further research.

Don't worry about getting busted by customs for transporting the viral agents: We've cleared the matter with them and they'll be expecting you.

143452.en: A short while ago, we had a huge problem with rodents that required us to hire an army of janitors. Now that the job's done, however, we need to reallocate these people to a place where they could be more effective. Take them to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off for me.

143453.en: Have you seen the price of oil around here lately? It's absurd! Our clients are demanding more, but all we've got is the synthetic stuff, so take a load of it over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

143454.en: My friend is getting married. We need entertainment for his bachelor party tomorrow, but I can't just show up with the dancers myself. Take these "performers" to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. Be sure to get them there on time so we can start the fun!

143455.en: A short while ago, we had a huge problem with rodents that required us to hire an army of janitors. Now that the job's done, however, we need to reallocate these people to a place where they could be more effective. Take them to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off for me.

143456.en:
Well, our little gambit worked. The bigwig's been driven out of Wiyrkomi and a blow's been struck for the little guy. Thanks so much for your help.

One last favor, if you will. Some of our guys are founding an environmentalist education facility on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and they need some construction materials brought over. You think you could do this for me? I'll pay you well.

143457.en:
I need a shipment of Silicate Glass delivered to this station as soon as possible. It's currently stored in one of our warehouses in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; I'll give you the coordinates, of course. Just warp to our outpost, navigate to the warehouse, and pick up the shipment, and then return it to {[location]agentStationID.name}. Simple, ain't it?

Just make sure you keep a lookout for any suspicious activity. You can't be too careful these days.

143458.en:
I need a shipment of Silicate Glass delivered to this station as soon as possible. It's currently stored in one of our warehouses in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; I'll give you the coordinates, of course. Just warp to our outpost, navigate to the warehouse, and pick up the shipment, and then return it to {[location]agentStationID.name}. Simple, ain't it?

Just make sure you keep a lookout for any suspicious activity. You can't be too careful these days.

143459.en: Looks like food supplies are dwindling fast at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I think people are consuming a lot more than they were before. Take them a shipment of frozen food so we can feed the hungry.

143460.en: One commodity we all have a hard time living without is oxygen. One of our buyers is on a station that's close to running out of air, so I want you to fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and give them  a bit more.

143461.en: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  and retrieve the missing war dead. Destroy all Caldari standing in your way.

143462.en: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and clear the area for the humanitarian convoy.

143463.en:
Just when you think scars from the first Gallente-Caldari War begin to heal, something comes along and the old wounds reopen. We recently intercepted chatter about a missing contingent of Federation soldiers from that conflict who were recently recovered. They were stranded out in a 'roid field after engaging the enemy. Supplies ran out. Neither side came to the rescue.

It's a depressing story, sure, but there's a happy ending if you want to be a part of it. The Federation is willing to pay for secure, respectful transport for our war dead so they can finally be laid to rest in their respective homeworlds. This may sound easy, but it's not. The Caldari have also become aware of the battle site, and already have forces onsite. They refuse to allow us a proper retrieval.

You must go to the battle site and clear out the Caldari forces. Remember, they are invaders still, and recovering our soldiers is of paramount importance.

143465.en: Well, they've waited this long. They can wait a little longer yet, I guess.

143466.en: Glad to have you onboard. I appreciate that you're willing to do this for the Gallente people. Symbols are important in these politically volatile times.

143467.en: Good flying, egger. Thanks to you, we'll be able to put these soldiers to rest. It's long overdue.

143468.en: Well, they've waited this long. They can wait a little longer yet, I guess.

143469.en:
We need someone to escort a convoy running humanitarian aid into {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Well, mostly humanitarian aid. We're moving medicine and food, as well as aid workers from the Sisters of EVE. But, there're also military personnel and equipment hidden among those ships. There's a big operation planned in that system, and our forces will need all the help that they can get.

Essentially, there's sensitive cargo onboard, and not everybody needs to know about it. We're posing this convoy as a peaceful operation to keep the State off our backs, but that doesn't mean other groups would be interested in the convoy as a potential target. We don't want to lose it, and we certainly don't want to lose it to someone like the Syndicate or the Serpentis. Unfortunately, we don't have a lot of time before these things are needed, so please forgive me for omitting classified details. This is one of their “blanket operations,” whatever that means. We need you to make sure the coast is clear and that the convoy makes it to their destination safely.

143471.en: That's all right. We can find other pilots if you don't like this job. Thanks for your time.

143472.en: That's all right. We can find other pilots if you don't like this job. Thanks for your time.

143473.en: “When you made a mistake as a child and you were in a rush to hide it, what did you do? You covered it with a blanket and hoped that nobody noticed. Sometimes, we never grow out of this line of thinking.” –Sister Evetelle Boun, organizer of Operation Hope.

143474.en: You'll be joining them in the most dangerous leg of their journey, right in the middle of a remote outpost. I can't give you many details about this place, though. Push through this deadspace pocket and make sure the convoy gets to their destination. More instructions will follow when you get there.

143475.en: You actually lost a few ships, but things could have been much worse if you hadn't been there. We'll consider this matter closed, though it looks like the navy will disavow any knowledge of this event ever taking place.

143477.en: Destroy the Blood Raider installation and any ships trying to defend it. Bring back any tourists that are somehow still alive and in one piece. Remember, the Blood Raiders treat their victims like cattle to be drained and consumed. Therefore, search any cargo containers you discover. Each ship may have its own supply.

143478.en:
In the past several months, several cruise ships carrying close to 100,000 Amarr citizens have vanished without a trace. Of course, we first believed these disappearances to be accidents. We enlisted the help of several ISK-strapped capsuleers to poke around neighboring systems and scan the planets and moons for something.

One of these pilots discovered a Blood Raider installation in a system three jumps from the last known transport ship disappearance. Over the local comms channels, this brave pilot overheard the Raiders refer to it as a "Blood Farm."

We know now that the ships were hijacked and our citizens taken to this installation. There, they were systematically butchered.

I need you to go to this Blood Farm and eliminate anything that even smells like a Blood Raider operation. Don't stop until every last heretic has been utterly and completely destroyed. If there are any tourists still alive, bring them home.

143479.en: Make sure that the Blood Farm can never be used to massacre our people ever again.

143480.en: We can't let them massacre any more of our citizens. Get to that station and wipe it from existence.

143481.en: Too much Amarr blood for you, eh?

143482.en: I understand. Defending the blood of our ancestors is a serious task. Most capsuleers simply cannot find the strength for that type of commitment.

143483.en: So few left alive. I can't imagine the horrors they faced. Thank you for your service. Now I must inform the families of those who didn't make it.

143485.en: Stop the dissidents' fleet by destroying every last one of them.

143486.en:
Apparently, a rival corporation is afraid of our rapid growth in the field of starship design. An “associate” of ours has informed us that a shipment of datacores heading to one of our research stations is to be intercepted by a fleet of Guristas mercenaries. What's disturbing is that an Amarr corporation has allegedly hired the pirates to do this dirty work.

We want you to intercept and eliminate the Guristas threat. What we need is proof that our rivals are pulling their strings or that they have nothing to do with this whatsoever.

143487.en:
Perhaps you know the history of Further Foodstuffs? It provides food and supplies to both the Sarum Family and the Ardishapur Family, as well as to the Imperial Navy. Some dissidents, however, believe that this organization denies the military essential supplies that are necessary in the continuing struggles against our enemies.

Some of these low-life dissidents are attempting to disrupt the food supply to the royal families who run this corporation as a way of emphasizing their belief systems. How the scum were able to procure a fleet of ships is beyond my understanding. Perhaps they had help from members of the military who actually believe their propaganda? Regardless, they have amassed a great deal of firepower. If they hurt Further Foodstuffs, they hurt themselves. Does that make any sense to you?

Eliminate this rag-tag fleet.

143488.en: Time is of the essence. Get going, {[character]player.name}.

143489.en: Better now than later. At least I still have time to find someone dependable.

143490.en: Are you kidding me? I spent a great deal of time searching for a good pilot.

143492.en: Good job. Now the two most prominent families in the Empire (and our hard-working military, of course) won't feel the loss of their favorite delicacies.

143494.en: Further Foodstuffs is a small agricultural company jointly owned by the Ardishapur and Sarum families. The products of Further Foodstuffs are mostly used by the subjects of these two families, while what little surplus is left is sold on the open market. This has curbed the expansion opportunities of the company, though it means the fleets of Ardishapur and Sarum will never lack for food.

143495.en:
Apparently, a rival corporation is afraid of our rapid growth in the field of starship design. An “associate” of ours has informed us that a shipment of datacores heading to one of our research stations is to be intercepted by a fleet of Guristas mercenaries. What's disturbing is that an Amarr corporation has allegedly hired the pirates to do this dirty work. If that's true, there is a major shift in philosophy among our adversaries, both in the boardroom and in space. We need more information before we can act upon this.

We want you to intercept and eliminate the Guristas threat. Find out, if you can, who is behind this. What we need is proof that our rivals are pulling their strings or that they have nothing to do with this whatsoever.

143496.en: A job well done, friend! Here is that reward I promised.

143497.en:
It appears the Gallente have been making hostile moves again in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. They've been continuously launching attacks from a command vessel somewhere in a deadspace pocket. Our scouts have located the Federation admiral responsible for these raids and now we just need her taken care of.

We've dealt with this thing before, so we're confident that removing her from the picture will disrupt the rest of the Gallente operations in our area. The only issue is that the Navy won't be able to mobilize against her in time – they're the Navy after all, not a hit squad. I've been asked to recruit a capsuleer if possible, so we can bypass internal military procedures altogether.

That's where you come in {[character]player.name}. We need you to travel over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enter the deadspace pocket our scouts have found, then kill the commander and her fleet.

She'll undoubtedly be back at some point even if your mission is successful. The Gallente are a persistent enemy, so after you've killed her, leave the body in the communication array she's been coordinating the forces out of. That should send a message. It might even spook her into seeking reassignment elsewhere, away from our corporation's space.

143498.en: Coward! I knew I shouldn't have trusted you.

143499.en:
Good to see you again, {[character]player.name}. We've got something you'd be perfect for.

It appears the Gallente have been making hostile moves again in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. They've been continuously launching attacks from a command vessel somewhere in a deadspace pocket. Our scouts have located the Federation admiral responsible for these raids and now we just need her taken care of.

We've dealt with this thing before, so we're confident that removing her from the picture will disrupt the rest of the Gallente operations in our area. The only issue is that the Navy won't be able to mobilize against her in time – they're the Navy after all, not a hit squad. I've been asked to recruit a capsuleer if possible, so we can bypass internal military procedures altogether.

That's where you come in {[character]player.name}. We need you to travel over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enter the deadspace pocket our scouts have found, then kill the commander and her fleet.

She'll undoubtedly be back at some point even if your mission is successful. The Gallente are a persistent enemy, so after you've killed her, leave the body in the communication array she's been coordinating the forces out of. That should send a message. It might even spook her into seeking reassignment elsewhere, away from our corporation's space.

143500.en: Excellent. I have uploaded the coordinates to the mission details in your Opportunity interface.

143501.en: I thought a patriot like you would be up for this. I'll leave your name out of my report to the Navy, but I am a little disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

143502.en: I'm afraid your name was already put forward to deal with this. This won't reflect well on you, {[character]player.name}.

143503.en: The admiral isn't going to stay in that location for very long. Take her out as quickly as you can.

143504.en: Great work, {[character]player.name}. Intel places her at a cloning station deep inside Federation space. I imagine it will be a while before she tries that move again, and if she does, you've left a reminder on how it will end.

143505.en: A hefty award awaits you upon successful completion of this mission.

143506.en: Great to hear. I've uploaded the coordinates.

143507.en: I'm surprised that someone like you would be afraid to take on a few rogue miners.

143508.en: I will have to find someone else more capable, then. I'm surprised you couldn't handle this, {[character]player.name}.

143509.en:
Within the next week the Gallente Federation will officially claim sovereignty over the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} , citing a recent worker's riot as proof of “a desire for democracy”. The Federation has moved a division of their Navy into the system, and if we don't forcibly push them out soon the riots could escalate further.

Slip past the Navy forces from their rear flank and destroy the Gallente command ship and its escorts.. This will throw the rest of the division into disarray momentarily, and at that point, the Caldari Navy will move in.

143510.en: Great work; hopefully those thieves won't come back any time soon.

143511.en:
Sometimes it's easy to forget we're at war with the Gallente. Maybe not for you, of course, since it's you capsuleers who are doing most of the fighting, but for the rest of us things can seem awfully “business as usual” at times.

I'm saying this because we've had a development recently; something that's reminded a lot of senior people there's a war still going on. They've asked me to scout for capsuleers willing to deal with this situation, and that request has brought you to me, {[character]player.name}.

We have credible intel that sometime within the next week the Gallente Federation will officially claim sovereignty over the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and relocate an entire Navy division to support this claim. They will justify these actions by citing a recent worker's riot as proof of “a desire for democracy”. In reality, they just want to inflame the few unhappy people further and cost our entire corporation massive amounts of ISK in the process. They have no desire to genuinely help anyone but themselves.

The Federation has moved a division of their Navy into the system, and if we don't forcibly push them out soon the riots could escalate further. We must do everything we can to avoid a repeat of the Brothers of Freedom. The State has seen enough high-profile dissenters in recent years; yet another would not help our people. We obviously cannot allow this claim to ever happen, or for this Federation task force to gain any momentum whatsoever.

We need you to slip past the Navy forces and destroy the Gallente command ship leading them. This will throw the rest of the division into disarray momentarily, and at that point, the Caldari Navy will move in. We've discovered a deadspace route that will allow you to strike the command ship and its escorts from a rear flank. They shouldn't even see you coming.

143512.en:
I knew I was right to choose you for this. I've added the command vessel's location to the mission details in your Opportunity interface.

I'd expect a difficult battle, {[character]player.name}. You're about the draw the attention of an entire Federation Navy division. You will likely have to fight your way through to the commander once they realize you've breached.

143513.en: I set this task aside just for you, and you repay me by throwing it back in my face? We're done here.

143514.en: You've made us both look bad, {[character]player.name}, and if we don't stop that force, the entire State will look even worse. We do not have the luxury of failing. Someone more reliable will have to be found to replace you.

143515.en: The Navy is waiting on you to take out that command vessel. As soon as you do, they'll make their move.

143516.en: Great job {[character]player.name}. We've already taken care of most of the forces in one decisive sweep. The Federation will surely be on the retreat soon.

143518.en:
Formerly an extremist labor movement in the State, the Brothers of Freedom led a widespread revolt against corporate security forces on a number of Caldari planets in YC 109 – some time before Tibus Heth's vastly more successful revolt of a similar nature -- after 65,000 protesters were killed by Caldari paramilitary forces while trying to force their way onto a CEP station in the New Caldari system. After months of dogged pursuit by Caldari authorities, the riots were put down and most of the leaders were killed or arrested.

Some of the leadership, including the ringleader Melarius Torvil, did manage to escape the final Caldari Navy operation that crushed the Brothers' movement. Torvil and a small group of associates fled to the Minmatar Republic and applied for asylum from Caldari persecution, which was granted by the late President Midular's Gallente-friendly government.

Today, though they have been largely eliminated as a major force in the State, the Brothers of Freedom continue to spread anti-corporate propaganda and speak out against the CEP's government in the Gallente Federation and the Minmatar Nation, as well as outlying State settlements and facilities.

143519.en: A Minmatar merc plans to kidnap an Amarr young noble, so we need you to take him out before he can even make the attempt.  We know where he is preparing his plan.  You need to get in and dispose of him before he can even make his attempt. . He's a crafty SOB, so expect not just a fight, but some unorthodox challenges when he realizes you're on to him. He's especially fond of drawing pursuers into hazardous clouds.

143520.en:
A confidential informant has warned us of an impending kidnapping attempt on a young noble by a notorious Minmatar mercenary. One of my associates, who owes me a lifetime worth of favors, discovered the plot during a card game. The merc's mouth and ego are both the size of New Eden itself. He talked openly about his plan without a second thought. We need your help in stopping him before he can carry out his plans.

His staging ground is at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Find and kill him with any and all means at your disposal. He's a crafty SOB, so expect not just a fight, but some unorthodox challenges when he realizes you're on to him. He's especially fond of drawing pursuers into hazardous clouds. Odds are good he'll have some ex-Navy Minnies flying back-up. He might be a braggart, but he's still a paranoid merc. Be careful.

143521.en: Too tough for you, eh?  This merc has defeated greater men than you, so don't let it hurt your ego too much.

143522.en: The merc's sneaky.  He will use every trick he knows to escape.  Keep your eyes open for clues he may leave behind!

143523.en: I have to find a braver pilot than you, apparently.

143525.en: A significant number of Minmatar make their living on the darker side of the law, acting as pirates, smugglers and peddlers in all kinds of illegal goods. Many of the larger criminal groups in the world of EVE are run by Minmatar.

143526.en: The Amarr Empire thanks you for your assistance in this matter. Please use all speed and discretion in apprehending this degenerate.

143527.en: Great job, {[character]player.name}.  The Amarr Empire is in your debt.

143528.en: Still nothing from the maintenance team.  Advise me on your status.

143529.en: It had to be done.  We'll get another gate built out there and a military presence to protect it.  In the meantime, the citizens at the listening post will have to make due with the supplies they have.  Rest assured that we will do everything we can to get back to them as quickly as possible.

143530.en: Damn, just what I need.  Another political firestorm.  I had better find a way to fix this quickly.

143531.en: Very well.  I will find someone else.

143532.en:
A maintenance team assigned to a top secret acceleration gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has stopped transmitting progress reports. As this gate leads to one of our new listening outposts, alarm rang out in military circles.

Travel to the acceleration gate. Destroy any hostiles. Use the acceleration gate and check on the outpost. If the outpost's location has been compromised, you are ordered to eliminate the hostiles and then destroy the gate. You must ensure that the enemy cannot return to the exact location of our outpost.

You have your orders. Will you execute them to the best of your ability?

143533.en: As to those citizens stationed at the outpost, yes, they will be cut off from all outside contact until a new acceleration gate can be built.  The good news is that the outpost is equipped with a Stealth Emitter Array that will keep it hidden until we can return.  The not-so-good news is that those citizens could experience some long term side effects from the energies emitted by the array, but they knew the risks when they signed on.  Secrecy is paramount, both from a political and a military perspective.

143534.en: Excellent.  Remember, this operation is classified as top secret.  You are not to discuss it with anyone.

143536.en: A portion of the fleet is preparing a set of protracted war games  in the next few days. There was some mix up with a circuitry order that I only just found out about. Collect the custom circuitry from the production line in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The level of piracy in the area is unknown.

143537.en: I don't have anything else for you {[character]player.name}. What are you waiting for?

143538.en: You're kidding. This is one disaster after another.

143539.en: You were attacked? What would they want with training drone AI ? Wonderful, now we'll have to hold up the war games   for a security check of the entire shipment. I didn't realize Angel Cartel could be subtle. Given how this went for them, maybe they should stick to the direct approach.

143540.en: Well so much for all that wasted time.

143541.en: Production for all types of goods can be found in all corners of New Eden. Every so often, though, something of a specific design is required that must be produced from a specific area. Sometimes this is due to patents, sometimes it's more to do with a sudden requirement for obsolete or cutting edge equipment.  Desperation on the part of the buyer can lead to major holes in market security.

143543.en: I'll thank you later. Please get going.

143544.en: The Blood Raider Covenant is a particularly gruesome sect of the generally reviled Sani Sabik cult. While some modern Sani Sabik rituals use blood in some manner or another, the Covenant places particular value on the blood of cloned humans, and they are utterly ruthless in obtaining it, regularly boarding other spacecraft and abducting all aboard. From their base in Delve they launch lightning-fast raiding parties and surprisingly well-coordinated incursions deep into Empire space in pursuit of their goals.

143545.en: Move quickly, {[character]player.name}. Every hour that passes means more profit lost.

143546.en:
I'm glad to see you made it over, {[character]player.name}. I have a problem with some Gallente miners that I think you'd be perfect for.

The Gallente have set up another mining operation near one of our asteroid belts. They bring in semi-mobile reprocessing stations and then mine the location dry. You have to recognize this as just another act of war, {[character]player.name}. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has lost millions of ISK to these Federation parasites. It's almost as damaging as a direct attack, but it doesn't draw the sort of military response an overt assault would, which is why we need capsuleer assistance to deal with this quickly.

We know they've set up mining outpost at one of the smaller deadspace asteroid pockets {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} frequents. They do this in the hope that nobody will come after them. I need you to send the Federation a message that they're wrong – that the State will pursue them every time. You must show them that there's no profit to be made from illegally mining belts we have claimed.

Go to the outpost and destroy absolutely everything; all the miners and any reprocessing stations you see. Level the place entirely. The loss of personnel and equipment will set them back and send a clear message to stick to their own space.

143547.en:
The Gallente have set up another mining operation near one of our asteroid belts. They bring in semi-mobile reprocessing stations and then mine the location dry. You have to recognize this as just another act of war, {[character]player.name}. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has lost millions of ISK to these Federation parasites. It's almost as damaging as a direct attack, but it doesn't draw the sort of military response an overt assault would, which is why we need capsuleer assistance to deal with this quickly.

We know they've set up mining outpost at one of the smaller deadspace asteroid pockets {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} frequents. They do this in the hope that nobody will come after them. I need you to send the Federation a message that they're wrong – that the State will pursue them every time. You must show them that there's no profit to be made from illegally mining belts we have claimed.

Go to the outpost and destroy absolutely everything; all the miners and any reprocessing stations you see. Level the place entirely. The loss of personnel and equipment will set them back and send a clear message to stick to their own space.

143548.en: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, drop the band off at their manager's station, and take care of the pirates.

143549.en:
Have you ever heard of the band Quantum Entanglement? They're a heavy metal rock opera group with a theatric, costumed stage presence. Seriously, they're all the rage among the Federation's youth. The front man is none other than Halo Axegrinder, who was one of the founding members of Starved Fedo. Remember them?

Okay, personally I can't stand that garbage, but billions of fans can't be wrong, right? Anyway, their manager is one of my old school chums and he's asked me for a personal favor. He says they thrive on adrenalin, and since most of their songs are about war, he thinks they might be inspired by experiencing a little combat action.

Coincidentally, I've got a little pirate attack that needs to be dealt with in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system; it's a task I would usually allocate to some rookie capsuleer far below your standing with the corporation. If you're packing the kind of firepower I think you are, you should be able to take this installation down without breaking a sweat. Let a few hits bounce off of your defenses to give these guys the ride of their lives and that should give them enough inspiration for a lifetime of edgy, hard-hitting chart-toppers. I think that's the right terminology.

143550.en: Thank you for doing this. Entertainment is becoming more and more important to the citizens of the Federation, and it's widely believed that whatever troubles may befall us, we'll overcome them based on our willingness to defend our culture.

143551.en: Well, thanks for your time. I'll just have to tell their manager to hold on while I find another reputable pilot. Lucky me.  You cap-pilots are common these days, but not ones I'd be willing to work with.

143552.en: What went wrong? You've put me in a spot here. I can't say I appreciate this but it's not like I can do anything about it.

143553.en: Are they getting on your nerves yet?

143554.en:
Outstanding work, egger. The label was still willing to pay your fee, and the producer was recovered and brought up on charges.

On a side note, the entire band was psyched about what you did. I think you inspired a real creative explosion in them, and I hope we can look forward to better music.

143556.en: This heavy metal rock opera band was made famous by their first album's cover, which depicted two naked individuals engaging in sexual intercourse while floating in space without spacesuits. Gallente politicians tried to have the album, called Unprotected, banned. Not because of the adult content, they claimed, but because it promoted unsafe extravehicular activities.

143557.en: Find the lost fleet in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and recover the data cores; destroy anything that stands in your way.

143558.en:
We just lost a fleet out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's a waste of hardware and personnel, but at the very least, we'd like to recover the data cores of each ship. If the vultures haven't started in on the carcass yet, they will soon. We can't afford a whole recovery effort, but we'd rather hire a capsuleer like you than let those blood-suckers run off with our data.

Keep anything else you like from the site, and if a few raiders and pirates end up dead, I doubt anyone would complain, if you know what I mean.

143559.en: It's all yours. We'll upload the identification beacons to your ship now.

143560.en: Damn. We were hoping to attract someone of your reputation and firepower. We'll see if we can't settle for someone else.

143561.en: Damn. We were hoping to attract someone of your reputation and firepower. We'll see if we can't settle for someone else.

143562.en: Time is running out. By the time you get there, it might already be picked clean.

143564.en: Go pick up the Caldari operative from the penal station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring him back.

143565.en:
I've got a delicate yet dangerous task that just wouldn't suit anyone other than a capsuleer. Here's the situation:

We caught a Caldari operative trying to walk out of the University of Callie with, and I say this literally, an armful of data cores stolen from the university's research hospital. We've had him locked down at a penal instillation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} since then, but our more convincing interrogators have changed his mind about giving up some information.

The catch is that he's demanded to be transferred to a more "dignified" location before he offers his full cooperation. That's where you come in.

Pick up the Caldari operative and bring him back here immediately.

143566.en:
Good. Head out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I've sent word, so they should know to hand him over to you when you get there. They haven't responded yet, but it's an old installation, and a busy one, too. I'm sure it's nothing.

When you get him, bring him back here.

143567.en: Sorry to hear that. You sure? Simple, lucrative work doesn't come around every day.

143568.en: You're leaving me in a spot here. I'll have to get another trusted courier and contact the jail again.

143570.en: Good work. You really thought on your feet for that one. We'll be debriefing the operative shortly. Your payment is well deserved, unfortunately the Caldari did get away with a lot of prisoners.

143571.en: A drone network virus seems has taken over a mining colony and is infecting any ship that approaches. Eradicate all infected ships and destroy the virus before it infects yours.

143572.en:
A rogue drone virus has gone live at a mining colony. The machinery is malfunctioning and the problem spreading throughout the entire network. We sent a small rescue crew and it took over their systems. The crews are still alive but they're held hostage by their own ships. Unfortunately, we can't let that cloud our judgment. The infection must be destroyed… completely.

We have reason to believe your capsuleer vessel will be able to withstand infection long enough to eradicate the problem.

143574.en: Can't say I blame you, but it still doesn't help me out any. You'll have to excuse me.

143575.en: That doesn't leave me many options. You couldn't have told me earlier? No matter.

143576.en: Please try to maintain radio silence during this mission; I don't want that virus ending up in our computers here on the station!

143577.en: That was close. A shame for those that lost their lives, but you did incredible work out there. We'll send a scuttle crew out to sweep up and find out what happened.

143579.en: Rogue drones and wild drones are the terms used over advanced drones that mutated out of control. A few years ago some ingenious Gallente inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own - in essence acting in every sense like a regular space ship except being unmanned and computer controlled. First prototypes were encouraging, but then disaster struck. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Some of these were huge - the largest drones ever constructed, these drones were even equipped with warp drives and equipped with the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. These mother drones, as they were called, along with several lesser drones soon managed to spread out, not only within the same system as the research facility that birthed them, but also to other systems. Only later men discovered exactly how - the drones attacked and took over space ships, then used them to jump to other systems, the drones themselves safely hidden within the ship. Needless to say the super-drone research was soon abandoned by the Gallente.

143580.en: A pirate faction in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system has taken hostages and plan on executing them shortly. The innocent people need to be rescued and returned to the agent as soon as possible.

143581.en:
I can tell you're a bit more experienced than the average capsuleer, which means you might be interested in something a little more challenging than the usual chores.

A small gang of pirates has carved a niche for itself in the evidence disposal business. They've setup a base near an uncharted acidic cloud, which allows them to charge huge sums of money to other pirate factions that need to get rid of salvage, bodies, data cores, or whatever in a discrete location.

Unfortunately, they're currently holding some hostages that we need to have recovered. I think you can figure out the rest on your own.

143582.en: I don't think I need to remind you that, if you fail, a bunch of innocent people are going to get jettisoned into a cloud of acid, where they will be simultaneously decompressed, frozen, and dissolved.

143585.en: I'm no starship pilot, but it seems like it would be a good idea to avoid the acid cloud.

143586.en: Clever capsuleer, you've done it! On behalf of my corporation and the hostages you rescued, thank you very much!

143587.en: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and look for signs of the missing passenger ships. Evacuate any survivors you find and bring them back here.

143588.en:
We've gotten reports of missing passenger ships in and around {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We've lost track of three of them just this week. We'd like you to go out and see what's happening to the ships. If possible, recover the crew as well. Thousands of people are missing because of these lost ships – the worst incident so far. I'm afraid that this situation could gain a lot of unwanted attention very quickly.

I want you to look into it. I'd like to be optimistic and say that they've simply had technical difficulties, but we're past the breaking point here. Bring back any survivors you can find.

143589.en: Thank you.  I have no idea who would be disrupting our space lanes like this. Whoever it is, they're bold to take on the Federation. We'll have medical specialists on standby to take of the survivors.

143590.en: The Federation will not look kindly on your inaction.

143591.en: Sorry to hear that. You'll be happy to know that CONCORD has taken notice of this case and they'll be dispatching a squadron to look into the disappearances.

143593.en: This mission was a bigger story than I imagined. Looks like the State was using these mercenaries as a source of domestic warfare within the Federation. That's low, especially for the State. But you know what they say about war, right? Anyway, I'll report this incident to the higher-ups in the FIO. They'll be very interested in the State's recent activities.

143594.en: A Quote from Admiral Edan Gore, Federation Navy

143595.en: "Honor does not exist in this day and age, not out in space and especially not among the capsuleer communities. The only honor left is down here, planet side, where we do not resort to domestic terrorism, and where respect for the basic rights of the private citizen still exists. The stars shine on fear."

143596.en: Hunt down the rogue Minmatar in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  Destroy his pirated prototype ship and deliver his corpse to Minmatar caretakers.

143597.en:
You've shown a great deal of loyalty to the Republic, {[character]player.name}. I wonder if that speaks as much to your feelings towards the Amarr, or if it's a matter of convenience. It's been my experience that the older a capsuleer is, the more uncertain his or her motives become.

Mortals are slightly less difficult. Fervent extremists particularly. A particularly troubled Minmatar has apparently taken it upon himself to conduct a personal war against the Empire. Ordinarily, my superiors and I would quietly applaud his effort and wait for word of his death. This particular person, however, managed to commandeer a prototype stealth ship to carry out his war.

We can't let the ship fall into Amarrian hands, but we can't send the fleet in either. With him already in Amarr territory, they could easily construe it as a sanctioned act of war. As much as I want to cut out my tongue for saying it, we need you to help the Amarr kill one of our own. We'll have to smooth out the political mess through our liaison with CONCORD.

Reports place him somewhere in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If you can manage it, bring back his remains. I don't want to think how those pious... how the Amarr would treat him.

143598.en: I hope you won't mind if I don't thank you outright. Oh, and don't expect the Amarr to welcome your assistance either.

143599.en: You're leaving us with dangerously few options, {[character]player.name}.

143600.en: I understand how distasteful the whole deal is, but this doesn't help.

143601.en: I have nothing else to tell you, {[character]player.name}. Please just contact me when this is finished.

143602.en: Our rampaging kinsman is gone? His ship, too? If you'll take a bit of advice from a lowly mortal, {[character]player.name}; when unethical decisions are made, eventually you're left with nothing but unethical options.

143604.en: Reflecting on the personal toll invariably endured, a wise figure once offered this advice to anyone considering a career in politics: “Don't.” In New Eden, with so many different factions all delicately counterbalanced, such sage advice may have never been more humanitarian.

143605.en:
A maintenance team assigned to a top secret acceleration gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has stopped transmitting progress reports. As this gate leads to one of our new listening outposts, alarm rang out in military circles.

Travel to the acceleration gate. Destroy any hostiles. Use the acceleration gate and check on the outpost. If the outpost's location has been compromised, you are ordered to eliminate the hostiles and then destroy the gate. You must ensure that the enemy cannot return to the exact location of our outpost.

143606.en: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  to monitor and disperse the slave trading operation that has set up shop there.

143607.en:
We have a lead on a potential slave trade in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and I need someone to patrol that area and find out what's happening. We think they're trading Gallente citizens, which is an open act of hostility against the Federation, so we need to shut this ring down as soon as possible. But first, we have to know who's behind it.

Understand that you won't be trying to actually stop the slavers; all we need is information on who's behind it. If you encounter any hostiles, however, please take care of them.

143608.en: That's what I like to hear. A capsuleer will really be able to send these slavers a message. Thank you for agreeing to be the voice of our culture.

143609.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Some other time.

143610.en: You're aware of what you're doing? These people need immediate help.  We'll scramble some pilots now, but you're leaving us high and dry.

143611.en: Interesting that you should contact me. Is it done?

143612.en: I've dispatched ships to pick up the slaves. They'll receive counseling and be sent back to their respective home worlds, courtesy of Interbus. It's safe to say I'm not satisfied with this outcome. I've never heard of the Serpentis dealing in human traffic, but I hope that this isn't indicative of a larger trend in that organization. But we've got the information we need, and the Federation can move forward based on your intel. Good work.

143613.en: Wipe out the Sansha hijackers in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The more humiliating, the better.

143614.en:
There is an old saying: “Money makes the world go round.” Actually, it's gravity and thermodynamics, among other things, but money and physics all come together in a big way when you're talking about wormholes.

However, wormholes rarely occur in civilized space; take a wild guess what that means. I hope you have some experience in dealing with pirates, {[character]player.name}. Specifically, the Sansha. They seem particularly fixated on wormhole research, so much so that they've been a major pain for scientific ventures regardless of ownership.

There's no word of sanctions against the “Nation,” so we'll have to take care of it ourselves. More work for you, anyway.

We'd send a fleet detachment to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to reclaim a wormhole we've been studying recently, but we'd rather outsource to a capsuleer like you and humiliate them.

143615.en: Good hunting. Personally, I suggested we just spray the area with used motor oil.

143616.en: I expected someone with your reputation to jump at the chance for a little rough play. I'm sure some up and coming fleet captain will be eager for the assignment.

143617.en: You were supposed to embarrass those androids, not your employers. I'll call in the fleet.

143618.en: Our scientists can't safely get back to work until you've sent the cyborgs running, {[character]player.name}.

143619.en: What do you mean they came through from the other end? You're suggesting they were able to predict of the most random, unpredictable pathway in existence?

143621.en: The inner workings of a wormhole were apparently well understood at one time. Since the Dark Ages, however, the best New Eden has managed is basic reverse engineering of ancient jump gates, significantly less powerful than the natural phenomena. This makes the appearance of a natural wormhole a dangerously valuable occurrence, over which factions will openly oppose each other in order to study and utilize the anomalies exclusively.

143622.en:
Glad my invitation reached you, {[character]player.name}. A portion of the fleet  is preparing a set of protracted war games in the next few days. I've been put in charge of constructing decoy ships and structures, but there was some mix up with a circuitry order that I only just found out about.
I found a replacement vendo. All my subordinates are too occupied to retrieve it.
You'll be picking up the goods direct from a production line, not through their public market. I haven't had time to check reports on local piracy though. There may be hostiles. Be ready for a fight. I don't care if you have to blow the storage facility apart, we need those chips.

143623.en: A rogue drone infestation in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system is causing problems and needs to be taken care of.

143624.en:
Hang on, I need to finish this call.

Really, another one? That same station, huh? Well, I don't know what the capsuleer was flying. What do you want me to do, hold their hands? No, don't even joke about that. One more? Do you really think it's going to be any different? Okay, but don't blame me if this one fails, too.

Okay now, where were we? Oh, yes, the exciting opportunity I have for you today! It's a bit run-of-the-mill, but I think you've earned an easy one, friend. It's just a tiny little rogue drone problem. There couldn't be more than half a dozen of the little bastards. I'll bet if you just zip in there and rattle off a few shots at the infested station, they'll scatter like frightened children. What do you say?

143625.en: Perfect! Run over to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and clean up those pesky drones.

143626.en: You flew all the way out here just to decline a simple task like this?

143627.en: You flew all the way out here just to decline a simple task like this?

143628.en: How is that cleanup coming along?

143629.en: You actually did it? You destroyed that infested station? Do you have any idea how many capsuleers lost their- Uhm, I mean, great work! I'll keep you in mind when I come across important missions like this in the future.

143630.en: Find the tainted tattoo chemical being developed in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  The exact location of the chemical is unknown.  Be prepared to destroy any number of large structures.

143631.en:
Tattoos are more than art to the Minmatar, {[character]player.name}. We have entire ceremonies built up around the markings we come to wear in our lives. Not to bore you with details, but ours aren't the simple ink-and-needle hatchet jobs most people think of. Exactly how the chemical process works is a closely guarded secret even within our own culture.

Word has reached my office that some Amarr splinter faction is working on their own chemical in order to contaminate Minmatar ceremonial supplies. It could mean anything from the appearance of Amarr propagandist symbols to some unexplored form of chemical dependence on the Empire.

The logistics of such a plan actually working are laughably impossible, and of course we'll never be able to tie anything back to mainline Imperial channels. Still, any threat to our freedom must be treated seriously. Well, that and the whole concept is just insulting.

We want you to bring us a sample of this chemical. I can't pinpoint exactly where the chemicals are being made. Our best information points to a deadspace complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

I mentioned the insult of the program. Tear through the place. I don't care how many structures you have to obliterate, just bring us this new ink.

143632.en: Discretion can be the better part of valor. I'm sure there's a less scrupulous capsuleer out there somewhere.

143633.en: I didn't expect a capsuleer to have a weak stomach.

143634.en: If you felt the least bit heartless blasting through them, remember which side consciously chose to use innocent victims as living shields, {[character]player.name}. We've already sent teams in behind you to rescue who we can. Or capture, as the case may be. I'll be interested to learn exactly what this substance is supposed to do.

143636.en: The Minmatar coming-of-age ceremony, known as the Voluval, involves an injection of a hallucinatory chemical which puts the youth in a trance. As the visions wear off, the individual finds him or herself marked with a tattoo of an unpredictable pattern on an unpredictable portion of body. The chemical used to induce trance and create the mark is so well guarded, even some Minmatar wonder if there is not more to the process than their elders admit.

143637.en: According to your agent, a convoy was sent out with a group of pirates pretending to be security. Intercept the convoy and take out its escort.

143638.en:
Please, you have to help me! I hired a group of mercenaries to escort a friend's cargo shipment; however, I just learned that the people I sent are pirate agents!

I know it would be helpful if you knew who you were going up against, but all I have is a few fragments of information here; there are no specifics so be ready for anything!

I need you to intercept that convoy and eliminate the pirates!

143639.en: Thank you for doing this. The convoy should be passing through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} very soon. There's still time to head them off!

143640.en: Damn it. I need to find someone to help and quick. Time is running out.

143641.en: Damn it. I need to find someone to help and quick. Time is running out.

143642.en: What are you doing? Time is running out!

143643.en: I cannot properly express how helpful you've been, so hopefully this reward will do.

143645.en: It's a common misconception that it is CONCORD that engages pirates with below -5.0 security status in high security space, while it is in fact the local navy that does so. CONCORD will only engage if the outlaw has incurred a GCC (Global Criminal Countdown) caused by committing a crime in Empire Space. The local navies are not as powerful as CONCORD and it is possible to survive their onslaught and limp back to the gate, or even escape before they warp scramble the ship.

143646.en:
Only a few moments ago the CEO from one of our subsidiaries was attacked and ransomed by Guristas, right in front of our trade delegation. Local security forces were overwhelmed and the pirates managed to escape. Our scouts pursued the Guristas vessels back to a Federation detention facility, which suggests the Guristas are only acting as mercenaries and the Gallente are really the ones to blame.

We have scouts holding above the detention facility, and they're tapping communications to look for evidence of a connection, but in the meantime we want to make an attempt to get our people out using capsuleer assistance. We're concerned that more reinforcements could be on the way, and that if they arrive, we'll lose our people for good. You need to act quickly.

Your assignment is to assault the facility and return our people to us before things escalate any further.

143647.en:
I'm glad you're here {[character]player.name}, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is in desperate need of your help.

Only a few moments ago the CEO from one of our subsidiaries was attacked and ransomed by Guristas, right in front of our trade delegation, too. Local security forces were overwhelmed and the pirates managed to escape. Our scouts pursued the Guristas vessels back to a Federation detention facility, which suggests the Guristas are only acting as mercenaries and the Gallente are really the ones to blame.

We have scouts hidden near the detention facility, and they're monitoring communications to look for evidence of a connection, but in the meantime we want to make an attempt to get our people out using capsuleer assistance. We're concerned that more reinforcements could be on the way, and that if they arrive, we'll lose our people for good. You need to act quickly.

Your assignment is to assault the facility and return our people to us before things escalate any further. Can we count on you for this?

143648.en: If that CEO dies, it'll be on your head! I don't know how you sleep at night.

143650.en: Time is of the essence. Get moving {[character]player.name}!

143651.en: What? I pray to the Maker that I can find someone else in time.

143652.en: Understood. Be careful how you approach this, {[character]player.name}; the Guristas must be getting paid a fortune for such a brazen attack, and they will fight to the death for that money.

143653.en: The best possible result, and proof once again that hiring capsuleers is the way to get that. Thank you, {[character]player.name}, you've made us both look good. I'll be sure to pass my recommendations along, right after I take a few calls about some pay adjustments of my own.

143654.en: The Guristas are famous for their raids into civilized territory, something that very few pirate clans are willing or able to do. The mission of these raids is most often simply to steal cargo or passengers (for ransom) from freighters, but on numerous occasions their main intention seems to be to sabotage empire installations (mining facilities, sentry guns, and the like). This has led to speculations that some unscrupulous empire companies or even governments are hiring the Guristas to take out property of the competition.

143655.en:
Ah, {[character]player.name}, I'm glad to see you received my mail. I have something that requires complete discretion. It's entirely legal of course, but this will need to be kept quiet all the same. You've proven yourself trustworthy so if you want the assignment I'll hand it over to you.

During a routine system scan, some of my people stumbled upon something that may be a significant archaeological find. I can't just call in anyone to confirm it, though, that would risk a leak. I don't want anyone else claiming this discovery as their own, especially if it turns out to be a lucrative one.

What we could do is rig your vessel's camera drones to relay a live feed of the site back to me and my people. From there, we would be able to direct you around the area to observe places of interest. What you relay back could help us confirm or disprove our earlier findings. The site is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so you wouldn't be travelling very far to investigate, either. The only problem my scouts reported was a light pirate presence. I'm sure you can deal with a few Guristas.

Not the usual assignment I know, but one of potentially great importance…and profit. It would be ideal if we could rely on capsuleer assistance for this.

143656.en:
Ah, {[character]player.name}, I'm glad to see you received my mail. I have something that requires complete discretion. It's entirely legal of course, but this will need to be kept quiet all the same. You've proven yourself trustworthy so if you want the assignment I'll hand it over to you.

During a routine system scan, some of my people stumbled upon something that may be a significant archaeological find. I can't just call in anyone to confirm it, though, that would risk a leak. I don't want anyone else claiming this discovery as their own, especially if it turns out to be a lucrative one.

What we could do is rig your vessel's camera drones to relay a live feed of the site back to me and a friend of mine at the House of Records. From there, my friend would be able to direct you around the area to observe places of interest. What you relay back could help us confirm or disprove our earlier findings. The site is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so you wouldn't be travelling very far to investigate, either. Our scouts reported there was a light pirate presence, and interference was making the use of microwarpdrives impossible in there, but I'm sure you can deal with a few Guristas and using afterburner.

Not the usual assignment I know, but one of potentially great importance…and profit. It would be ideal if we could rely on capsuleer assistance for this. What do you say?

143657.en: Fine. I will find someone else.

143658.en: Then it would be in your best interests to forget we ever had this discussion.

143659.en: An arms dealer passing through the system just sold us a cache of weapons. I need you to take it to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. Don't worry, we've already acquired a permit for them, so you won't have any trouble at customs.

143660.en: An arms dealer passing through the system just sold us a cache of weapons. I need you to take it to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. Don't worry, we've already acquired a permit for them, so you won't have any trouble at customs.

143661.en:
I knew I chose the right person. I'm uploading the coordinates to you now.

Once you arrive at the archaeological site, I will issue further instructions.

143662.en:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. Exceptionally well. It will take a little longer to fully confirm, but we believe we've discovered an ancient Caldari outpost – one of the first established after we broke away from the Federation. If true, this would be a welcome injection to the system's local tourism industry, and we'll get a commission on the money earned there. Here's your cut of the deal.

Even if it turns out to be a false discovery we're insured against the ISK, so I see no reason not to give it to you now. Thanks once again.

143663.en: We stand to make a lot of ISK if that site is what we think it is.

143664.en: Shortly after jump gate technology was jointly discovered by the Gallente and the Caldari a little over five hundred years before the Federation formed, the Caldari corporations had started their own interstellar surveying and colonization, separate from that conducted by the Gallente. It was these colonies, kept as a secret from the Gallenteans, that became the source of friction between the Gallenteans and the Caldari, culminating in the latter's defection from the Federation and an ensuing war between the two races.

143666.en:
Your agent's corporation suspects a rival corporation may have caused a transport crash. Go to the location in the mission details and investigate the wreckage you find. Bring any evidence back to your agent.

You will require a salvager.

143667.en:
Glad to have you here, {[character]player.name}. I have some work for you.

A few days ago, a passenger vessel was passing through an asteroid belt, when it had a critical failure of its navigational computer. The vessel slammed into the asteroids and suffered critical damage. Before the vessel's reactor went critical, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} personnel evacuated the passengers and got them to safety.

While this story has a happy ending, there seems to be something suspicious about the crash. A small corporation with alleged ties to the Guristas is having money troubles, and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} suspects the incident may have not been an accident. Things just seem a little too perfect and well-timed.

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} needs you to go to the crash site and investigate the wreckage. Look for any evidence that might hint at the real cause of the accident. Bring any evidence back to me and I will submit it to the proper authorities.

I don't want to tell you how to do your job, but a salvager might help you get to the bottom of this a little faster than just looking around with your on-board sensors.

143668.en: I was relying on you to figure out what went wrong. I just hope the evidence is still there by the time I find someone else.

143669.en: Great to hear, {[character]player.name}. I have uploaded the coordinates to your NeoCom.

143670.en: There are millions of ISK resting on this investigation. Who I am supposed to find to do this?

143671.en: I have a feeling there might be a cover up in the works, so get moving.

143672.en: This is some interesting evidence. Now we can bring some people to justice.

143673.en: I heard you were having problems dealing with this. Well, thanks for letting me know of your failure first-hand, I suppose.

143674.en: Excellent. Here are the coordinates. Don't hesitate out there, {[character]player.name};  be ready for a fight.

143675.en: Great Work, {[character]player.name}. It should be a long time, or a lot of ISK in bribes, before they can re-establish themselves around here again.

143676.en: Very well, if you're not interested I can find others. An unexpected refusal though, I must say.

143677.en: There's a number of ships holding outside the station. They won't be able to dock until you inspect them for contraband. Try not to keep the innocent ones waiting.

143678.en: Fly to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and obtain the salvaged electronics, then return them to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name}. Destroy any Angel Cartel ships that get in the way.

143679.en:
You're just the kind of capsuleer I've been waiting for, {[character]player.name}. If you're interested, I've got something important that needs to get done, something I can't trust just anyone with. Your loyalty to the Republic is becoming legendary.

We're working on something big, {[character]player.name}, something very big. I can't go into specifics, but I can tell you that {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has been tasked with gathering materials from anywhere we can find them. Luckily, two of our objectives coincide.

It just happens that our old friends, the Angel Cartel, are sitting on a veritable treasure trove of spare parts and salvage out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. What do you say we kill two birds with one stone? Swing out there, vaporize all the Angel clowns you like, and bring us back some salvaged electronics. Sound good?

143680.en: I see your reputation was well-deserved! I look forward to adding my name to your list of recommendations, {[character]player.name}.

143681.en: I can't imagine what you have to do that's more important than this, but I understand.

143682.en: Oh, so you're too good to help out the Republic when it needs you? You capsuleers are all the same.

143683.en: Sometimes I regret taking this desk job. Hey, while you're out there, blast a few Angel goons for me, would you?

143684.en: Yes, this is perfect. You've done the Republic a great service, {[character]player.name}. When the time comes and you witness our greatest accomplishment, you'll be able to say that you had a small part in paving the way for the future of all Minmatar!

143685.en: Don't expect them to roll over and hand you the formula. Leave no stone unturned, and what I mean by that is don't be afraid to destroy every structure you see in search of your objective.

143686.en: Why haven't you brought me the chemical yet? Did you turn every structure inside out, because they probably won't be hiding it in some ship's cargo bay.

143687.en:
Though I doubt she'll run from a fight, you might want to bring a warp scrambler or disruptor to stop her from running deeper into cover.

Oh, and if you see some merchant vessels loitering around, hold your fire. That's my surveillance team. They may have some further intel once you arrive.

143688.en:
Have you ever heard of Anire Scarlet? Well, she's practically an urban legend among the local pirates. It seems any outlaw with a clone bay and rhetorical skills can amass a following these days. The sorts of degenerates that hang around this area are easily impressed too, so apparently has built quite a posse, but then, that could just be another one of the myths about her.

As for where you come in: all this attention has earned her a CONCORD bounty. I'd very much like to claim that ISK, {[character]player.name}, with your help. I've hired an undercover surveillance team to locate her, and they've had some luck turning up a lead. If you're able to follow it up and take her out then we can split the bounty money equally. The surveillance team found her flagship vessel, The Crimson Dawn. She is sure to be either inside it, or very close by. If you think yourself capable of eliminating her, then I'll trade you the coordinates.

143689.en: Nicely handled, {[character]player.name}. I'll keep you in mind for another bounty contract if she ever shows her head again.

143690.en: Well, I can't say I blame you. I hear Anire Scarlet's pirates are pretty rough. They're all hell-bent on impressing their “Queen.”

143691.en:
{[character]player.name}, it's good to see you. I have something a little outside of the ordinary that needs taking care of. A personal business opportunity for the both of us, I guess you could say.

What do you say? Do we have a deal?

143692.en: Too much for you to handle, huh?

143699.en: You have a bounty to collect, {[character]player.name}.

143700.en: You have a bounty to collect, {[character]player.name}.

143701.en: Break Zazzmatazz out of Consolidated Holdings Inc.

143702.en:
Hello {[character]player.name}, up for some action? I have just received an offer from followers of the notorious pirate Zazzmatazz. The mission is to break him out of a private prison, Consolidated Holdings Inc. , which has a contract with Concord. Zazz is being held there, somewhat unexpectedly, for a very short time.

The client warns that once you have broken into the prison complex you will need to FINISH IT IN ONE run. Retreating is failure! The upside is that the client has promised some significant rewards if you prove capable and as a bonus, Consolidated Holdings Inc. is rumored to hold many secrets.

Are you up for it?

143703.en: Good! There are several deadspace acceleration gates that and need to be unlocked one at a time in isolated deadspace pockets while a strike force moves in through the complex and finds Zazzmatazz.

143704.en: Alright! It is a little disappointing, but it's your call. This kind of mission doesn't float by every day.

143705.en: I guess I overestimated your abilities and the strength of your network of friends.

143706.en: Bring Zazzmatazz back as soon as you spring him out. There is a lot of heat on us because of this and I'm trying to stay out of the limelight.

143707.en: Zazzmatazz may have eluded you but our client might settle for his DNA instead. It is better than nothing at least. Contact me soon for his response, it shouldn't take long.

143708.en: Deliver Zazzmatazz – or his DNA, to be more exact – to either Consolidated Holdings, Inc., or to the pirate Ragnar Bloodthorn. Consolidated Holdings has set up a meeting with your agent, and Ragnar Bloodthorn said he will be in touch. Both clients are very angry over the turn of events: Bloodthorn was expecting Zazzmatazz himself from your initial services, not his DNA, and Consolidated Holdings has lost a lot of assets and taken a blow to its reputation. Both have a score to settle with you, but they desperately need your cooperation as well, at least until they have secured Zazzmatazz's DNA.

143709.en:
Hello {[character]player.name}. Our client was furious about Zazzmatazz not being retrieved, but is willing to negotiate for his DNA. However, Consolidated Holdings, Inc., also contacted me about making a deal to get his DNA back. I'll leave it up to you who to deal with. I have arranged a meeting with Consolidated Holdings, but the pirate contact said he will be in touch with you. His real name is Ragnar Bloodthorn. When you've met them, make a decision quick, please — this is one problem I'd like out of my hands!

So, do you want to go to the meeting?

143710.en: Alright, the locations for both targets are in the mission briefing. I'll see you around.

143711.en: Alright! Keep Zazzmatazz's DNA for yourself, then. I don't want anything more to do with it.

143712.en: I thought you were taking care of that DNA business! Now I have both Bloodthorn and Consolidated Holdings breathing down my neck because of you.

143713.en: Get back to me when you have delivered Zazzmatazz's DNA to either party.

143714.en: Good job, {[character]player.name}; this played out nicely. Consolidated Holdings, Inc., and this Ragnar Bloodthorn now have something to yell into the emptiness of space – they both got what they deserved!

143715.en:
Have you heard those crazy prophecies which have been picking up publicity? No, not Macaper's, I mean the ones delivered by this “prophet” who calls himself Tolmak?

In any case, all you need to know is that this fool is trying to create his own religion, and he's had some successes recently in building up his numbers. It seems each new day he lures more discontented people into his cult, and recently we've been affected by this new trend.

One of his acolytes set up shop in our little corner of the universe and began preaching to the locals. This “priest” is not exactly causing trouble, but he's making certain powerful people uncomfortable. Not only that, but we've heard reports of violence against this cult in other sectors. We'd like to quietly remove this preacher from the picture to avoid any possibility for backlash in our own areas. At the same time, we don't want to make a martyr out of him and build further support for this cult. The situation needs to be handled discretely.

He's currently preaching on Yunshin Z, a refining complex. This is a low population industrial center with little contact to the outside world. We can afford to make bold moves here. Your task is to find this preacher and return him to us. We'll handle the rest.

143716.en:
Have you heard those crazy sermons that people are talking about? The ones delivered by this self-proclaimed “prophet” who calls himself Tolmak? Yeah, that freak who's trying to create a religion. He's got a lot of converts among the discontents of our little corner of the universe. But he's also got a lot of enemies, people who don't like what he's been spewing. People who might try to kill him. Thing is, certain powerful people find him useful. A nice distraction from more political pursuits. They'd like him alive.

One of his acolytes set up shop in our little corner of the universe and began preaching to the locals. This “priest” is not exactly causing trouble, but he's making certain powerful people uncomfortable. Not only that, but we've heard reports of violence against this cult in other sectors.
