143717.en: Excellent. Be careful out there, {[character]player.name}. We've also had reports of unusual fleet movements around the refinery. You may not be the only one looking for this preacher.

143718.en: Very well, I'll find someone else.

143720.en: I hope the capture of this preacher is worth the cost of hiring you.

143721.en:
Ah, you have him? Good work, {[character]player.name}. I hadn't heard any reports of conflict at the refinery, so I can only assume the mission went smoothly.

In fact, I'd rather continue to keep on assuming that, if you get me. My paperwork is going to indicate that Tolmak's friend came willingly, without a struggle, and that the entire operation was conducted peacefully and with the utmost respect to all involved parties.

143722.en: Great job, risking your neck like that! I mean, I'm sure there was no risk at all - in any case, we've already spoken with Dr. Ateshi about how to proceed.

143723.en: Finally, we have all the information necessary to make an informed decision. I'll see what Dr. Ateshi has to say.

143724.en: Destroy The Anomaly before it can do further damage. Bring Dr. Ateshi to the rogue drone hive where the ship is hiding so that she can deactivate its shields.

143725.en: Good. Dr. Ateshi will accompany you to the ship and give you details on delivering the scanner. Get in, drop the scanner, get out.

143726.en: I don't think you understand what you're turning down here. The fate of The Anomaly is important to a great many very powerful people, and they won't be happy.

143727.en: Travel to The Anomaly and deliver the Neurowave Pattern Scanner.

143728.en: Have you delivered the Neurowave Pattern Scanner yet? There's a lot of pressure on me to get this done.

143729.en:
We've spoken with Fajah Ateshi about The Anomaly, and I'm afraid things look dire. Her readings were damaged from the explosion aboard The Paryi, and she needs to return to The Anomaly to get further information. Since the two of you are the only ones who've come near the ship and retained both your lives and sanity, we have to send you out again.

We're still not entirely sure if anyone is alive aboard there, though Dr. Ateshi insists that she heard garbled transmissions from survivors disoriented from radiation sickness. I tell you, all this mystery doesn't make me comfortable, and it makes the people at the top very, very unhappy. If you find survivors, excellent, but your survival and Dr. Ateshi's readings are more important. You need to attach her Neurowave Pattern Scanner to The Anomaly.

143730.en: I don't think you understand what you're turning down here. The fate of The Anomaly is important to a great many very powerful people, and they won't be happy.

143731.en: You need to rescue The Paryi's survivors and learn what they know. The Anomaly was a very expensive project and some very powerful people are invested in figuring out how it vanished.

143732.en:
{[character]player.name}? Good. I have a job that's probably outside your normal scope. This one is humanitarian.

A pandemic has broken out on a planet in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Fortunately, a cure was already developed and mass-produced. The contagion originated on another planet nearby, you see, so the people of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} already have experience in dealing with this particular disease.

The Sisters of Eve sent a medical drone with the vaccine onboard down to the planet, but some degenerate pirates have intercepted the craft, disabled it, and are now trying to demand a ransom for its release. The Sisters say that if the drone is destroyed it could be days before we can mass-produce more vaccine – something about being unable to accelerate the bacterial cultivation. A few more days with this disease uncontrolled could mean everything. We must recapture the drone.

We're depending on you here, {[character]player.name}. Once you've secured the drone, they can deploy repair teams and send it back on its way.

143734.en: You've done a great thing! Countless people owe you their lives. We should have just enough time to get the medicine to the planet. The Sisters are coordinating with Mordu's Legion this time. They'll escort it safely to the people of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

143735.en: We don't have any time to waste. Get moving.

143740.en: What? You're telling me profit is more important than innocent lives?

143741.en: I should have known. Your kind disgusts me.

143742.en:
Hey there, {[character]player.name}. I've got a routine run for you...just a second. I've got emergency messages coming in. Hm. You up for a rescue mission?

I just received an alert across multiple communication channels asking for evacuation help. A diplomatic station, not far from here, is undergoing a traumatic systems shut-down cascade. It's all going, and people need off that station. The rescue requires a smaller ship than what they have available to get in past the field of debris now ringing the station.

That's what happens when none of the empires will trust the others enough to allow them to send in their best station engineers and construction teams, and so they all agree on a third-party freelance company to build their stations. Happens all the time, I hear. Ridiculous.
Anyway – are you interested?

143743.en: A diplomatic station not far from here is undergoing a traumatic systems shut-down cascade. It's all going, and people need off that station.

143744.en:
I just received an alert across multiple communication channels asking for evacuation help. A diplomatic station not far from here is undergoing a traumatic systems shut-down cascade. 143745.en: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your reward, and the limelight for being a hero to those folks – you've earned it. You should know, however, that the folks you didn't save have already made it very clear that they're not happy with you.

143746.en: Great. You get out there, and you've got some rescue money coming your way. I don't really care who you rescue, just so long as you rescue someone. Fair warning, though – the ones you don't rescue are likely to remember it.

143748.en: Really? That's it? You're quitting? Why'd you agree to do it in the first place, then?

143750.en: You will lose standing with those factions you choose not to rescue. Fair warning.

143753.en:
Ever heard of The Anomaly? Lots of superstition around that name - it's one of our ships that vanished completely while testing an experimental jump drive. A trading vessel heard The Anomaly's signal last week and so we sent out a salvage crew, The Paryi, to investigate the site where it reappeared, but something went wrong. We received The Paryi's distress call yesterday and can't make sense of it. It seems some of them were killed in an explosion near The Anomaly, and the survivors escaped in life pods but are trapped there by gravity waves exuding from the ship. But the other things they said… well, some of them must have cracked under the stress. If there were any survivors from The Anomaly, they would've contacted us, after all.

You need to rescue The Paryi's survivors, especially Dr. Fajah Ateshi. Once we learn what they uncovered, we'll have a better sense of how to proceed. The Anomaly was a very expensive project, and some very powerful people are invested in figuring out how it vanished.

143754.en:
There's been an influx of neural boosters to our area recently, and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is trying to stem the flow. We normally turn a blind eye to light drug trafficking but that only seems to have encouraged the local smugglers, who are now flooding the area with cheap, more dangerous drugs.

We know where they base out of, however, and have already taken the liberty of blockading their station in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. What we need is a capsuleer who can go in there and check out some of the larger vessels currently in holding. You are of course cleared to engage anyone caught with illegal boosters in their cargo, although if you catch anyone be prepared for them to start shooting.

143755.en: Who doesn't love a nice fat slice of beef? Well, vegetarians and vegans aside, I suppose, but they're a dying breed in this era, eh? Anyway, one of my clients loves his beef, and that's why I want you to fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and deliver a shipment of cattle to him.

143756.en: Who doesn't love a nice fat slice of beef? Well, vegetarians and vegans aside, I suppose, but they're a dying breed in this era, eh? Anyway, one of my clients loves his beef, and that's why I want you to fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and deliver a shipment of cattle to him.

143757.en: Our security and military ground forces have been experiencing a slow but steady increase in the numbers and severity of injuries suffered during a wide range of armed conflicts. A recent study by Amarr military scientists has determined that the primary cause of this has been a failure to adequately improve the lightweight body armor worn by millions of our soldiers, Marines, police, and other fighting forces. As fate would have it, one of our intelligence units has obtained what they claim to be a revolutionary new fabric that could provide fifty percent better protection across the board in all types of engagements. We need you to deliver this very sensitive cargo to a station we designate.

143758.en:
Thank you for coming, pilot. As you know, the Amarr Empire is in a constant state of conflict. Our enemies have included organized criminal gangs, drug traffickers, terrorists of every conceivable motivation, pirates, unpacified slave populations, and even the occasional low level skirmish against our fair-weather friends, the Caldari, Gallente, and, lest we forget, the Minmatar. This requires the Empire to always remain vigilant to any situations that may call for the use of force on levels ranging from simple urban pacification to outright military combat. What you do not know is that a high-level internal Empire report has revealed that our casualty levels have been steadily increasing over the last several years, often requiring evacuation to more robust – and already overburdened – medical facilities.

In the “recommendations” section of this report, the researchers concluded that the single most identifiable cause of these excessive casualties is a systemic problem with our lightweight body armor. This armor is standard issue for millions of police and security personnel, as well as our military reconnaissance units. Unless a drastic improvement in the quality and durability of this body armor can be found, we will continue to suffer the consequences.

This morning I received a priority communication from an Amarr Intelligence Officer claiming that his team had just “obtained” a revolutionary new fabric that, if properly processed, could literally double the strength of our existing armor. I know this officer only by reputation, and it is best not to pry any further into how his team came across this “miracle cloth.” Nonetheless, we have been advised that they will arrive at this station within moments to transfer the fabric here for transshipment to a more secure facility.

So, pilot, will you transport this prototype body armor fabric to the station facility we designate?

143760.en: Quitting mid-mission is not something I expected from you. Now I am going to have to answer to the intelligence team. Oh, and don't expect any further jobs from me until your failure here has been long forgotten. Damn… I need a stress pill….

143761.en: I must say I am disappointed in your decision to turn down this mission. I vouched for you personally, given what I have seen in your files about your excellent mission completion record. I will not soon forget your refusal.

143762.en: Lightweight body armor is a common and often required element of any police or security forces' operational gear. Modern armor of this type can stop most projectile, laser, and other light weapon fire. However, as small arms weaponry continued to evolve with regard to the amount of damage it can inflict, so to must the defensive technologies designed to maintain parity with these weapons. On rare occasions, a corporation, military laboratory, or other entity will produce a light body armor system that represents nothing short of a generational leap in design and protection. The multilayered fabrics used in these latter applications are usually amongst the most highly guarded secrets of any civilization, for many reasons. The most advanced of these contain nanotechnology which also can change color and density depending on ambient conditions and/or input from the wearer.

143763.en: Outstanding, pilot. You were even a bit ahead of schedule. Our offloading team is en route to your ship, and the Intel guards will stay with the shipment until that has been completed. I will keep your name in my “go to” list should any more missions come up in the future.

143764.en: Thank you for the update pilot, but no need to contact me until you arrive. The Intel security team on your ship is keeping me quite well informed.

143765.en: A small, platoon-sized Caldari special operation team is in hiding on a Gallente planet and in danger of being captured or killed. They are low on water, food, weapons, and other equipment and will not last long unless they are extracted. We have a rescue standing by; however, we need you to deliver the required materials to their station so that they can then proceed with this critical rescue mission.

143766.en:
One of our Caldari Navy Special Forces units conducting clandestine reconnaissance of a contested ocean planet – a Gallente-claimed planet, by the way, with extremely rare seabed minerals – sent an emergency burst communication to the covert ops ship in orbit above the planet, requesting immediate extraction. This signal was, in turn, transmitted to the classified comms center here on this station. When we attempted to contact both the team and the ship, however, we received no response. Our immediate reaction was to divert one of our long range Crow-class interceptors, which was in the region on an unrelated mission, to investigate. Soon after its arrival, its sensors confirmed that the covert ops ship had been destroyed.

There is nothing we can do for our lost covops ship; however, this series of events has left the Special Forces team alone and without a means to evacuate the planet. Even worse was a fragment from the original communication indicating that the team was on the run and low on food, water, weapons, and ammunition. They have taken refuge in a disused ocean mining facility, though it is doubtful that they will stay hidden for long. There simply aren't many places to hide on that planet, given the fact that it is mostly covered by massive oceans, with very little land mass. It will not take long for the Gallente to track down our team and either kill them or, worse, capture them for interrogation.

The good news in all this is that we have an extraction team in place, along with a shuttle-equipped vessel to deliver them to the planet. However, given the immediacy of this mission, they had to leave their original base without much of their usual equipment and weaponry. This is where you come in. We need you to transport several containers of highly specialized small arms and related equipment to the station at which the extraction team is currently located. Once you drop off this cargo, the team will gear-up and shuttle down to the planet to rescue the stranded team.

So, pilot, what is it gonna be? Will you help us?

143767.en: Do not contact us until you have completed this shipment. There is simply no time for idle chatter, not to mention the likelihood that the enemy is almost certainly listening in.

143768.en: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our military personnel at great risk. It is doubtful that we will be able to find anyone else to get this critical shipment to the station in time.

143769.en: Your refusal to accept this mission will almost certainly result in the loss of this Special Forces team, not to mention placing the now-dangerously unequipped extraction team at great risk.

143770.en: Thank you for accepting this important, time-sensitive mission. You have been given priority clearance for station undock, so please leave as soon as possible.

143771.en:
Due to a recent series of inspections by the regional mine monitoring commission, we have found it necessary to purchase a large quantity of the latest generation of environmentally-friendly drills and related equipment.

In order to avoid financial penalties and the possible loss of our mining rights, that company must get these quite expensive new drills into the hands of the miners as soon as possible. If you can deliver this cargo to the station that serves as our logistical hub for this system, they can then have their own pilots transship them to the required planetary mining locations.

143772.en:
Let me start at the beginning. As you have probably seen on the news channels, a prominent Caldari mining company is in the middle of a very nasty battle for economic survival with a new, up-and-coming mining company from within the same large conglomerate. Both of these companies specialize in the extraction of ores from some of the more inhospitable and dangerous locations in this and several adjoining systems. While this can be hazardous with regard to men and equipment, the profit potential from these largely untapped ore reserves can be quite significant, which brings me to our current predicament.

As you may know, the specialized manual labor required for some of these mines can be significant in terms of numbers. Well, the Mining Health and Safety Commission, or MHSC, for this region recently conducted a survey of the first company's operations, and found that their mining practices at certain locations may have resulted in excessive pollution, then further alleged a corresponding link to long-term miner health problems. The company has loudly complained that this is a ridiculous witch hunt brought about by their new competitor, which happens to have several “friends” on the commission. While they work to ensure they are equally “represented” on that commission, the recent finding has mandated that they immediately improve worker conditions and reduce pollution or risk losing their mining rights. To remedy this problem, they recently purchased a large number of the latest environmentally-friendly – and obscenely expensive – manportable drills, which seems to have assuaged the MHSC for the moment. They do, however, have a deadline for actually putting these new drills into the hands of the miners, which brings us to the reason I contacted you.

We need you to deliver a rather large shipment of drills and other related equipment to a station that serves as a central service hub. From there, logistics pilots will deliver this and other items to the various mines in the system. Will you take on this important job?

143773.en: We are shocked to hear that you have chosen to quit this job in the middle of the contract. We will now have to pay another pilot double to pick up where you left off. You should have let us know from the outset that you could not take on this important job. Hopefully, we will never have to rely on you again.

143774.en: Well, I must say we are quite disappointed that you would turn down this very easy contract. We shall find another pilot and move your name to the bottom of our list. Don't call us, we'll call you.

143775.en: I certainly do appreciate your help, pilot. Hopefully, if we can get these drills into the hands of the miners in short order, the company should be able to retain its mining rights and return to profitability.

143776.en: You seem to be on schedule and we look forward to the prompt delivery of the equipment to the designated station. Contact us through the usual channels after you have offloaded this gear.

143777.en: Job well done. Our logistics teams are loading your shipment into their transport vessels as we speak, and we should have the drills and equipment in place shortly. We will definitely contact you again, should we require your services.

143778.en: There has been an uprising at one of our slave Labor Reeducation Centers, or LRCs, near a rather large ore mine. The slaves are almost wholly Minmatar, so we cannot afford to have this incident continue for even one more day. The longer it goes on, the greater the chances that some reporter or news agency will get wind of this and splash the story all over the region. Given that the Minmatar Republic may feel compelled to take action to aid their brethren, this can only lead to dire consequences. That, of course, is unacceptable. We do have a plan in place, however, that should end this uprising before it has a chance to truly take root. We need you to transport a large contingent of Riot Interdiction Team (RIT) personnel to a designated station. From there the assembled security teams will join up and embark a small fleet of frigates and cruisers to race to the prison, where they will use all necessary force to terminate this uprising before it gets completely out of control.

143779.en: Bah – I should have known you wouldn't help us. I could tell when I first met you that you were beyond salvation.

143780.en: Good job, pilot. Please make all possible haste to the station as the other teams are waiting on you. The assault phase will begin after you deliver the RIT personnel and their equipment.

143781.en:
The Amarr Empire, realizing many centuries ago that it could not simply work slaves to the point of death, instituted a number of improvements to worker conditions in an effort to prolong the usable lifespan of its slaves. These changes were not universal across the Empire, due in large part to the Empress's unwillingness to create what might have amounted to significant friction between slave -based companies. Therefore, these decisions were largely left to the Five Heirs and their subordinate regional offices. Thus, we can state here that history has shown a lack of consistent application of these worker improvement programs across the Empire. Those Amarr systems that have chosen to incorporate these adaptations have, however, consistently derived greater revenues due to these enhanced and ongoing pacification efforts.

These shortcomings led directly to the establishment of Labor Reeducation Centers (LRC). An LRC is designed much like a multilevel prison, with facilities for low, medium, and high risk inmates. The inmates are those slaves who consistently exhibit defiance or even outright hostility towards the managerial staff at the mine, construction site, or other location to which they are assigned as slave labor. Once we have identified these persons they are immediately removed from their job site and taken to the nearest LRC for corrective behavioral conditioning. This conditioning can include a wide variety of attitude modification methodologies, from intensive drug assisted counseling, to religious indoctrination, and from advanced torture techniques and a concurrent system of rewards - the so-called “carrot and stick approach” - and any number of programs in between. In this way, we break the individual slave's will so that he may be returned to the workforce as a docile and useful component in the labor pool.

143782.en: Bless the Empress – I am very glad to hear you've decided to help. The RIT personnel will meet you in the hangar bay shortly.  Please feel free to take any of our religious literature with you for your enlightenment during the flight.

143783.en: You soulless coward! Without the men you agreed to deliver our assault on the prison will undoubtedly lead to unnecessary casualties on all sides.

143785.en: Following a string of suicide terrorist attacks yesterday, we managed to capture a high ranking member of their organization. Interrogations have revealed, however, that a devastating viral weapon, based on nanotechnology, is already in place and primed for release. We need you to deliver the only known countermeasure to this agent, manportable electromagnetic weapons. If we are successful, these weapons could eradicate the virus before it has a chance to spread and infect the entire station.

143786.en: Pilot, there is simply no time to discuss this any further. Deliver the cargo to the station immediately, before that horrible weapon kills thousands of innocent men, women, and children.

143787.en:
Last night, a strike team of suicide terrorists from the Anti-Corporatist Revolutionary Front, or ACRF, struck at more than twenty Caldari offices and stations throughout the region. During one of these attacks a terrorist was captured with a well-shielded, improvised nuclear device hidden in his rucksack. Obviously this event represents an entirely new level of threat from the ACRF, now that they have proven themselves willing to carry out such a horrendous and indiscriminate mass casualty attack.

The only upside to this is that the terrorist has turned out to be the most notorious operative of the ACRF, a woman known as Commander Rachendia. Having her in custody has offered us an opportunity to gain information related to her group's future plans to strike at the Caldari State. During one of the more aggressive interrogations, she disclosed information about a pending attack against one of our nearby stations. The nature of the attack is not entirely clear; however, we know with certainty that it involves the surreptitious introduction of a viral agent into the life support and air circulation systems.

Our initial searches for these hidden canisters at that station have, so far, been fruitless – with the exception of one small aerosol-type canister. A preliminary test revealed that these viral weapons appear to be based on a self-replicating nanotechnology. Once released from stasis in their container, they seek out and consume human tissue, and leaving behind little more than dust. Our medical scientists have calculated that just one container, released into the central air processing vents, could result in the deaths of all human life aboard a medium-sized station within no more than four hours. The only good news is that these nanos are programmed to self-terminate within 12 hours. Of course, this would be far more time than would be necessary to kill everyone aboard all but the largest of stations.

Your role in this desperate situation is to deliver a cargo of electromagnetic weapons, modified to emit a short-range pulse that will literally "fry" any nanos within its range. So, we are asking: will you deliver these containers to the station immediately? Thousands of lives may depend on your answer.

143788.en: We had placed all our hope in you completing this mission. It's too late now to find another pilot and another ship. I fear many thousands of lives may be lost due to what can only be your cowardice. Obviously, you are not a man of your word, and we won't forget that.

143789.en: Your bravery and skillful piloting without question, saved the lives of untold numbers of innocent people. We will definitely move your name to the top of our list for any future time-sensitive missions!

143790.en: We're very glad to hear you are willing to take on this important mission. If we can get these EM devices to the station in time, I know we can save many innocent lives.

143791.en: We are all terribly disappointed in your refusal to transport these electromagnetic weapons to the station. We shall now have to find another pilot and another ship, and I fear even then we will be too late. I doubt you will be sleeping very well after you see what may become of that station.

143792.en: Terrorists, working with criminal scientists, have developed a strain of viral weaponry that is based on nanotechnology. When combined, the "hive mind" of the viral strain works to seek out human tissue at which point the microscopic nanos begin to quickly disassemble the tissue, leading to a slow and painful death. Research into electromagnetic pulses has provided some promising leads with regard to countermeasures, but these have not yet been field tested.

143794.en: The Imperial Navy recently made a final attempt to scour the battlefield graveyard of The Battle of Vak-Atioth. This battle pitted our brave Navy against the Jovian enemy; however, due to a number of unforeseeable factors, we did not emerge victorious. The graveyard itself has been picked over for decades by scavengers and others seeking some quick isk. The Amarr ships sent to perform this duty were attacked by pirates, and only one ship eventually returned. But when it did, it brought with it a valuable icon of Amarr military history: a selection of data chips holding recordings of a small part of that legendary battle. We need these chips delivered to a distant station for proper cleaning and processing.

143795.en:
As you almost certainly know, many decades ago our Grand Fleet met the hated Jovians on the field of battle in a system known as Vak-Atioth. Most unfortunately, our fleet was destroyed by the technologically superior Jovian ships and their advanced weaponry, marking one of the darkest moments in our history. Still, we learned much from this encounter, and the lessons learned there continue to benefit our military to this day, which brings us to why I called you here.

Several days ago, Imperial naval intelligence mounted a highly classified effort to revisit the Vak-Atioth system, now known simply as Atioth, to conduct a final intensive search for any remaining debris that might provide some insight into the tactics and weapons used by the Jovians. Needless to say, this once-massive floating graveyard has long since been picked over by not only our own salvage fleets, but by scavengers and opportunists alike. All has not been lost, however.

Much to our surprise, the Anathema covert ops ships sent to scan this system returned with a damaged but still readable supply of TIL-1A Nexus Chips. A preliminary review of the information they contain reveals only a portion of the great battle. We are hoping, however, that a more thorough analysis of these chips will reveal some insight into Jovian tactics and technology. If nothing else, they provide a very rare first-hand accounting of the battle which will add greatly to our historical archives and, when displayed at one of our leading military academies, will provide a stirring motivational icon for future generations of brave Imperial naval warriors.

Now that you understand the importance of these chips to the Empire, I must ask: will you transport this invaluable cargo to the designated station?

143796.en: Many decades ago, a large portion of the Imperial Grand Navy met the Jovians in combat at what today is referred to as The Battle of Vak-Atioth. It was our intention in opening that battle with the as-yet untested Jovians to destroy their fleet utterly, thus forcing their subjugation, as we had done with so many enemies in the past. Without going into great detail, the fearless Amarr fleet was utterly surprised by an enemy that possessed incredible destructive power and remarkably advanced battle tactics. This, coupled with the unforgivable impetuousness of our fleet's leadership, resulted in the near-total annihilation of our warships, at an estimated cost of only one-third of the Jovian armada. We were never again to take to the field of battle against that most dangerous and mysterious opponent. However, while some ships escaped, in less than six hours of battle we left behind a vast field of our dead and dying ships. Today, this system – known now only as Atioth – holds almost none of these battlefield remains, having long since been swept clean by Amarr salvagers and various scavengers. Nonetheless, this system remains an eternal reminder of the vigilance and bravery of our Grand Fleet and the sacrifices they are often called on to make in service of the Empire.

143797.en: Well, pilot, I could have at least understood refusing this mission in the first place. At least that would have been somewhat understandable given the value nature of the threat. But to quit in mid-shipment is something we did not expect from you. We shall retrieve the chips and deliver them ourselves.

143798.en: Thank you, pilot. You will be doing the Empire a great service in even such a brief undertaking as this.

143799.en: You have made a significant contribution to the Empire, pilot. We cannot thank you enough. Of course, no record will be kept of your part in this episode, as we cannot be seen to have been even slightly concerned over the risk of attack and the potential loss of these chips. We will, however, fulfill our financial obligation, as outlined in the mission contract.

143800.en: I can understand your reluctance to undertake this mission, as we do not know who or what might be out there waiting to attack you in order to obtain these chips. This is a rare moment in that we bear you no malice for your fear.

143801.en: Please remain off this comms channel, pilot. While your voice is encrypted, the communication itself can be hacked. Contact us only after docking, or, of course in the event you are attacked.

143803.en: Some decades ago, Amarr veterinary scientists achieved a milestone in genetic manipulation with the creation of hybrid slaver hounds. These new breeds are specifically designed to live and work in extreme climate conditions, which is a boon for all those slave labor facilities on ice planets and other harsh environments. Demand for these animals has been overwhelming and we are struggling to maintain our delivery schedule. I need a large shipment of these hybrid slaver hounds delivered to a nearby station. From there they will be transshipped to a desert planet and put to work as guard animals.

143804.en: I really am surprised that you're declining this one. It was a good chance to make some quick ISK with very little risk. Well, no bother. There is no shortage of pilots looking for an easy trip.

143805.en:
Amarr slavers on Syrikos V first learned to breed and train slaver hounds to provide an extra layer of low-cost security for their slave labor operations. These animals soon proved their worth, particularly as a last line of defense for any slave that managed to bypass a facility's security controls and escape into the whatever wilderness lay beyond the facility's walls. So keen are the senses of these animals, and so lethal their attacks, that most slaves will give up any hope of escape before even making the attempt. One problem that arose, however, was that many slave labor operations were located in some of the harshest imaginable environments, often so harsh that they were unsuitable for your average slaver hound.

So, it was with tremendous satisfaction that Amarr veterinary scientists reported recently that they had managed to create stable, obedient hybrids of the breed, each type adapted for a different geographic or atmospheric condition. Thus, if you are a slave owner on an ice planet, for example, you can now purchase slaver hounds with thicker pelts, greater body fat, and higher overall tolerance to cold and freezing wind. These new hybrids have proven remarkably adaptable, and have long since spread to slave labor facilities throughout the Empire.

143806.en: Good to know the hounds haven't caused you any trouble. Please contact me when you reach the station. Offloading has already been arranged.

143807.en: You're quitting this mission? You should know that quitting a mission as simple as this one does not look good on a pilot's record.

143808.en: The Origins of Hybrid Slaver Hounds

143809.en: See? I told you this one was a no-brainer.  I would suggest, though, remaining in your ship until the hounds have been safely offloaded. I wouldn't want to be hanging around your cargo bay if one of them got loose, as the sedatives will have worn off by now.

143810.en: I had a feeling an easy job like this one might interest you. Good chance to flip on the autopilot and take a nap.  Just make sure the cages are secure and locked and your cargo bay doors are sealed.

143811.en:
I'm not sure how much you know about Amarr slave labor installations, such as mines, agricultural harvesting fields, moon mineral extraction zones, and the like. Well, I can tell you that these facilities are often of such size and complexity that they cannot always be wholly secured against slave escape attempts. Certainly, all but the most primitive and poorly administrated of these locations feature any and all manner of perimeter alarms, security cameras, remote sentry drones, microwave motion detectors, infrared barrier fences, you name it. As you can imagine, though, this can get quite expensive given not only the capital outlay for the equipment, but for the manpower needed to operate and maintain them year-round, 24 hours a day.

It was during this search for lower cost alternatives to these technologies that the animals we call slaver hounds were introduced to the overall security plans of select slave labor facilities, used to detect, track, and interdict runaway slaves. Their acutely tuned senses coupled with their remarkable natural endurance and speed made them an ideal choice for many Amarr slave operations. However, it was not long before it was realized that the standard, purebred slaver hound was not suitable for all environments. This resulted in the creation of genetically modified breeds more at home in harsher environments such as swamps, frozen wastelands, jungles, and the like. Today, these more adaptable variants can be found on many such installations throughout the Empire, despite their comparatively high cost when compared to your usual slaver hounds.

This brings us to the reason I contacted you. I need a large shipment of these hybrid slaver hounds delivered to a nearby station for transshipment to an Amarr desert planet. As long as the hounds remain sedated and don't find their way out of their cages, this should be a simple, trouble-free courier job.

143812.en:
Yes, I think I have some work for you.

One of our research outposts in Molden Heath came under attack by rogue drones last week. This is highly unusual, since drones are rarely seen beyond Etherium Reach. The outpost's defense systems managed to keep our scientists safe, and the downed drones were retrieved for examination. They found unusual mineral deposits replacing the drones' original microboard networks, which appear to work far more efficiently.

Of course we don't want anyone else getting ahold of the samples before we can replicate them. The samples have been in transit via a series of drops in order to keep them safe. Take them on to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

143813.en: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I can't wait to see what we've got.

143814.en: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.

143815.en: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.

143816.en: {[character]player.name}, have you done what I asked?

143817.en: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. We're one step closer to the forefront of technological advancement!

143818.en: One of my clients asked me to send over drones to replace the ones his company's been losing in the line of work. That's all he said. He never said anything about needing mining drones; of course I sent him a set of scout drones, and he was very upset at me for not being able to read his mind. People should be more specific about things. Take these mining drones over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for him, and if he asks why the paint looks new, tell him they're fresh off the production line.

143819.en: Just make sure to tell him how sorry I am, okay?

143820.en: Fine. I can always find someone else.

143821.en: I am very disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

143822.en: Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?

143823.en: Excellent. I've been trying to get those old things off my hands for months.

143824.en: I accidentally sent a client the wrong set of drones because they never specified what type he needed. Take the right cargo to him. Hopefully he won't ask too many questions.

143826.en:
After the successes of the first drones in the first Caldari-Gallente war, every empire set out to design a combat drone that suited their particular combat needs, though the small, pilotless tools clearly suited some empires' needs more than others. The Gallente company, CreoDron, has flourished, while the Carthum Conglomerate in Amarr maintains drone production more as a counter to their rival, Khanid Innovation, which stresses a reliance on rocket technology. Minmatar-based Boundless Creation has profited easily from drone production, but not enough to justify a specialized branch of operations; similarly, Ishukone in the Caldari State produces drones simply because demand exists rather than a desire to encourage a reliance upon them.

Like any other drone, a mining drone is simply an extension of a pilot's control. Unlike combat drones, mining drones have no offensive or defensive capabilities. Wastage factors for individual drones can be quite high, but the speed and convenience of having several extra mining lasers at the pilot's disposal outweighs the mineral loss.

143827.en: While examining wrecked rogue drones following a failed attack, strange minerals were found which replaced some of the drones' usual systems. The compounds seem to run more efficiently than the parts they replaced, and your agent has hired you to take the find to researchers for examination.

143829.en: Once part of a Gallente scientist's experiments in self-controlled drone technology, rogue drones can now be found throughout the cluster, having escaped and begun to replicate themselves. In certain undeveloped parts of null-security space they thrive and expand their numbers from hives hidden deep within deadspace pockets and asteroid fields. These regions are called ‘drone regions', and the only people brave enough and confident enough to attempt to build out there are the capsuleers.

143830.en: Our spies have succeeded in smuggling pieces of the latest experimental Amarrian starship technology back to the Republic. I need you to take the samples on to the lab where they can be properly analyzed.

143831.en:
You need to keep this quiet, {[character]player.name}. I know you capsuleers aren't accustomed to being told how to do your job, but this is bigger than anything else and if word gets out, all this effort will be for nothing.

We've acquired samples of the Amarr's latest experimental starship tech. Don't ask me how, I don't want to know, and neither do you. We're not sure what these pieces do; our source is suggesting it's a system that reduces the effectiveness of our electronic warfare systems. This could be bad news for us. Get the stuff over to the lab at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. And keep your trap shut. We don't want it getting back to the Amarr that we have this.

143832.en: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I knew we could count on you.

143833.en: I guess your loyalty isn't worth as much as I thought.

143834.en: I guess your loyalty isn't worth as much as I thought.

143835.en: Have you delivered that stuff to the lab, {[character]player.name}?

143836.en: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Our research team is saying the tech deflects target painter beams away towards an area of space just behind the ship it's fitted on. Our torpedoes will start missing targets if they manage to make this widely available. We need to find a way to counter this, and fast.

143838.en: The Minmatar Republic's reliance on speed for the majority of its fleet comes at a cost: up close, high transversal speed reduces the chance to hit the target, while fighting at distance brings fleet ships to the edge of their falloff range. The more mass a target has, the less difficult it is to react and hit. Target painters were eventually developed for the Republic's electronic warfare division, low-yield lasers which increase the mass profile of a target and reduce the negative effects of fighters moving at high velocity.

143839.en: Planetary officials have asked me to bring in a team of mercenaries they've hired to deal with a terrorist threat. Your job is to keep them in line en route.

143840.en: We have a planetary situation we need your help with. A group of pro-Amarr terrorists is wreaking havoc in outlying provinces, and the local government's hired a group of mercenaries to deal with them. You know mercs, I'm sure; they never really listen to anyone they think is softer than they are. We're having trouble finding an ordinary captain who's willing to ferry the guys over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for transit planetside. I think they'll be more likely to behave if the captain is someone who can and will follow through on a threat to vent the ship to vacuum. Someone like you, in other words. Can we count on you to keep the unruly lot in line?

143841.en: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! Don't actually vent the ship, though. We need these guys.

143842.en: Sad. Now I'll have to find someone else. You were the best option, too.

143843.en: Sad. Now I'll have to find someone else. You were the best option, too.

143844.en: Those mercs aren't giving you too much trouble, I hope.

143845.en: Excellent, {[character]player.name}! I'll let the local government know their solution is on its way.

143847.en: Mercenaries often get a bad reputation from the few who go nuts while on assignment, cause unacceptable collateral damage and demand higher pay for the effort involved in discretion. The majority are reasonable businessmen, primarily ex-military, who take their work seriously and simply demand respect for the risks they take.

143848.en: Our salvagers have built up a load of industrial-quality scrap metal to be used in ship building. I need you to take it to the reclamation facility so we can recover the useable parts.

143849.en:
Okay, here's one for you. Don't look at me like that. Yes, it's a load of metal scraps we need taken to a reclamation facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Contrary to popular belief, our ships are not made solely of scrap-metal, utility adhesive and chewing gum, but we do recycle extensively.

The reason I'm asking you to do this rather than hiring a much cheaper regular captain is that these bits are industrial quality, or they will be once they've been processed. They're worth a lot of cred on the black market – peanuts to you capsuleers, but a year's wages to anyone else.

143850.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. It's not a glamorous job but someone's gotta do it.

143852.en: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I had hoped you were the reliable sort.

143853.en: Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?

143854.en: Good! You've been a big help, {[character]player.name}.

143856.en: In the early days of space travel, after so long under the yoke of Amarr, the Minmatar were required to make do with what little they could find, with limited facilities and funding. The ability to create space-worthy ships from the most unlikely of materials became legendary. In the present-day Republic, scarcity is no longer a problem, but materials are still stretched as far as engineers can make them go for the sake of pride in their efficiency.

143857.en: A Nefantar House is relocating to a planet within the Republic, and we've had a tip-off that they're working against us for someone in the Empire. We've planted surveillance nanobots in a shipment of materials for their planetside home; take it over to the depot. The logs will show nothing amiss.

143858.en:
I hope I can trust you to be discreet, {[character]player.name}.

As part of a goodwill gesture to the Nefantar tribe, the Republic has offered allotments of planetary territory within our space on which to build embassies or summer homes or whatever else they need land for. I don't care what it is, I don't trust ‘em, but the government is determined to make sure we all get along.

Yesterday I got an alert from one of my colleagues; it seems one Nefantar house is in collusion with elements from the Empire. Obviously we can't just point fingers without evidence, but I'm in a perfect position to obtain that. The contractor they hired to design and build a house on their new property is a friend of mine. He's given us one shipment of interior facing materials to seed with nanite spyware. Take the load to the depot at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I know I can trust you to keep quiet about the additions to the cargo.

143859.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. If anyone asks where those came from, the manifest will show their usual station.

143861.en: I'm beginning to question your loyalty, {[character]player.name}.

143862.en: Have you delivered your cargo for me, {[character]player.name}?

143863.en: Thanks to your assistance, {[character]player.name}, we've been able to record some rather incriminating communications from these people already. They wasted no time in contacting their associates in the Empire to let them know they were settled in.

143865.en:
The day Drupar Maak struck down Arkon Ardishapur on Starkman Prime with the Heir's own sceptre began the darkest night for his people. In retribution for the death of his father and their attempted rebellion, Idonis Ardishapur ordered the annihilation of the Starkmanir tribe.

At the same time, the Nefantar tribe approached the Empire with an offer, making a bargain for mercy in exchange for assisting in the subjugation of the Minmatar. The tribe took on many aspects of the Empire, including open practise of their faith and owning Minmatar slaves, themselves. Despite the recent revelation that their conversion helped to protect the last Starkmanir to survive the purge, many within the Republic are hesitant to forgive the Nefantar for their actions.

143866.en: One of our planetside subsidiaries has recently lost a lot of farming equipment to a storm. I need you to take these parts to the assembly plant so we can recoup our losses.

143867.en: One of our subsidiaries has recently suffered a major setback, {[character]player.name}. A hurricane wiped out half their planetside crops and wrecked the equipment. Most of it was already falling apart, the storm just finished it off. Obviously, this is a big problem for them, and us, but it's still the early part of the first growing season. Deliver these parts to the assembly plant at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can replace the equipment before they lose too much from this harvest.

143871.en: Have you delivered those parts yet, {[character]player.name}?

143872.en: Thank you for your help, {[character]player.name}. Our subsidiary has managed to save more than they first thought of the initial crops and they're good to go for the second growing season.

143874.en:
Recent decades have seen a resurgence in attempts to control planetary weather patterns on a full global scale, particularly on technologically advanced agricultural worlds. Ensuring a regular cycle of rain and sun enables farmers to plant crops throughout the year with a smaller margin for error.

Despite the advances, the most that can be claimed is weather ‘guidance'. The one successfully controlled year on Aforat in the Mishi system was followed by two years of raging, uncontrollable storms which flattened fields with hail and flooded river valleys. The blame was laid on aggressive methods exercised by the corporation in charge of the project; reactors placed within existing ocean currents prevented seawater from cooling regularly in the colder months, disrupting the planetary climate entirely.

143875.en: Against my better judgment, I've been asked to order several sets of educational packages of the Amarr Scriptures for the children of families who have been released by the Empire. It leaves a sour taste in the mouth, but maybe we can use the teaching materials to our own ends.

143876.en:
I'm in a bit of an awkward position here, {[character]player.name}. With all the people being released from slavery in the Empire, we're getting more and more families who practice the Amarr religion. No thanks to Jamyl, she knew this would happen. The edict from our government is that we need to respect the poor deluded people and gently introduce them to a new way of thinking. It won't be easy, and it's putting a strain on all of us.

My problem right now is that a bunch of the refugee families have requested that some Amarr Scriptures be included in the course structure at the schools we've set up for their children. It's our own people doing the teaching, so we can slowly steer the education in the right direction, but we all still feel dirty for having to use it.

Do you think you'd be willing to take a shipment of books over to one of the schools?

143877.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. I knew I could count on you.

143881.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. I know it's an unsavory business, but our instructions from on high are to try to get along and help these people adjust.

143883.en: With the release of several generations of slaves from the Empire, Jamyl struck a blow at the heart of Minmatar culture, forcing the Republic to accept those who have known only the ways of Amarr and what little Minmatar tradition they had been able to maintain through the years. Inducting such people into modern Republic society has proven troublesome and at times outright frustrating; allowing released slaves to practice the religion they grew up with has been a bitter necessity as counselors struggle to help the people adapt to their new lives.

143887.en: I haven't received confirmation of your delivery yet, {[character]player.name}. Is there a problem?

143888.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. The testers have already submitted a preliminary report; looks like the formula needs some work. They say it's not enough of an improvement on the current industry standard to be worth producing on a large scale. One member of the team has suggested an application involving crystalline fullerides and dropping C86 entirely; it'll have to go up for review.

143890.en: Smaller ships rely upon their speed and smaller signature radius to make it difficult for larger ships to track and target them. The heat output from propulsion systems increases signature radius, making a small target much easier to track; the greater the speed, the greater the heat production. Specialized coatings help to reduce the effect and prevent expansion of the parts within propulsion systems, helping them to operate much more efficiently.

143891.en: I have to request a difficult task of you: play nice with a swarm of Angel Cartel representatives and their entourage on your ship. Hopefully they won't try to cause you trouble.

143892.en:
This is a list of people I want you to escort to a meeting. They have quite a large security entourage, and as you can see from some of the names, they have a reason for it. These people are members of the Angel Cartel. While the Cartel are thugs and pirate scum, and are not particularly welcome in Minmatar space, it does not mean that some corporations don't have certain dealings with them which require us to overlook certain... failings.

Escort them safely to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. It's nothing you'll be in trouble with the Republic for, but for the sake of our business relations, try to treat them politely.

143894.en: I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}, but I can understand why you might decline.

143896.en: Hello, {[character]player.name}. Have you finished your work for me?

143899.en: The Angel Cartel's reputation for engaging in any activity regardless of its legality has earned it the DED's description of the most dangerous criminal organization in the cluster. With a corporate command structure and open recruitment policy, the Cartel are less thugs than sharks in pinstripe suits, capable of operating on all levels of society. With a major operational base in Etherium Reach on the edge of Minmatar space, the Cartel is held with deep suspicion within the Republic. Their annexation of the Skarkon system in YC 110 and sudden withdrawal left many unanswered questions regarding both the Cartel's intentions towards the Republic and what deals were forged under the table to make them leave... and what those deals might have cost.

143900.en: A pair of civilians too wealthy for their own good are holding a decadent reception for their wedding, and ordered a tremendously expensive champagne to keep their guests entertained. A regular pilot can't be trusted to ship the drinks in, but what's a thousand-ISK bottle of wine to a capsuleer?

143901.en:
You must have heard of Chaylie Vann. No? What rock have you been living under? She's a big-name actress, does a lot of calculated lobbying for various charities in Placid, and she's getting married to some seriously old-money geezer from Intaki – yeah, we all know how that relationship is going to end. Never mind that. They're paying big bucks for an extravagant reception at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and put in a massive order for Feille d'Marnne in order to keep their guests happy.

Feille d'Marnne is some seriously posh champagne, {[character]player.name}. Each case of this stuff costs as much as an Incursus, and they're buying more than one. Obviously, we can't trust anyone less than a capsuleer to deliver the lot – an ordinary pilot would be more likely to run the stuff onto the black market.

143902.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}, I knew we could count on you.

143903.en: Fine, I'll find someone else, hopefully before it's too late.

143904.en: I'm not laughing, {[character]player.name}. I have a reputation to maintain, you know.

143905.en: I haven't received a receipt for that champagne yet. What's the hold up?

143906.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. I was able to secure an invitation to the reception thanks to your work. You should have seen the old man staggering around after hoarding several bottles of the champagne. He and Vann got into an argument towards the end of the night; turns out neither of them was as well-off as they appeared to be, even to each other, and they couldn't afford to pay the event bill. It's the latest scandal, the news services are all over it.

143908.en: Nobody loves a good party more than the Gallente. The hedonistic stereotype is one that the Federation revels in and flaunts shamelessly. Public figures actively compete to host the wildest and most fashionable affairs, vying for the attention of news services and gossip magazines. Among the celebrity elite, a wedding, birth or even a funeral is simply another excuse to splash out and stand in the limelight.

143909.en: A friend and I are running a small holoreel bootlegging operation on the side. The shipments are bound for Syndicate, but I only need you to take them on to where my business partner is operating from.

143910.en:
I like nice things, {[character]player.name}. Who doesn't? Handing missions out to you people all day doesn't offer nearly enough to cover my expenses, so a friend and I run a shipping business out to Syndicate space. Nothing big enough to interfere with the Syndicate itself, mind you. We provide a humanitarian service importing the latest holos from the heart of civilization. It's the only way they can get the things for a reasonable cost – buying them direct from the companies in the Federation incurs immense shipping charges.

Our usual courier is out of commission today, with her ship in for repairs after a pirate attack. If you want to make yourself useful, take the latest shipment over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and ask for Amelyn. They'll know who you mean, just say that “Imba” sent you.

143912.en: Fine. It's not like anyone would believe you if you told them, anyway.

143913.en: Fine. It's not like anyone would believe you if you told them, anyway.

143914.en: Amelyn hasn't contacted me yet, {[character]player.name}. What's the hold up?

143915.en: Thanks for your help, {[character]player.name}. Turns out our normal courier sold us out; the hangar we normally use was raided just after you left for your cargo run and officials from the Federal Performance Rights Union came around asking nosy questions. Good thing we were using your hangar, huh?

143917.en:
The Syndicate is the underbelly of Federation society, filled with its outcasts and criminals; it's a place where they can move freely and openly, and even prosper outside the reach of the law. As a result, supplies of luxury items at affordable rates are hard to come by, leading to a thriving black market in everything from sweets and the latest fashions from the Crystal Boulevard to ship parts and broadcasting equipment.

For those who reside under the independent governorship of the station managers, life can be more expensive when acquired legally. Official companies within the Federation add a high tariff for the risk of shipping through low-security and lawless space; the more frequent the attacks, the higher the cost. Residents who aspire to a higher-quality life must live with a daily balancing act of legality and affordability. Even such minor offenses as purchasing necessities via the black markets can potentially bar an otherwise law-abiding citizen from finding an honest living within Empire space.

143918.en: I accidentally sent the wrong shipment over to another laboratory. I need to you take these frogs over; it's the right shipment, this time, I'm positive!

143919.en:
Yes, yes, perhaps you could help me out.

A few days ago, I was at one of those parties - you know the type, where they shoot you full of stims if you start to drag, and you just keep going until reality starts to fold in on itself and turn into confetti, and there's the scent of rosewater and….

To make a long story short, I accidentally sent the wrong cargo over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. They were less than amused to receive a crate of live Intaki peepers rather than the cryo-stored Luminaire skippers they needed. One frog is much like another, but the pet-shop variety make very poor laboratory testing groups. Take these over, and they may forgive me enough to require my services in the future.

143920.en: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I doubt they'll give the peepers back, since they all escaped into the labs when the box was opened, but it's worth asking.

143921.en: You needn't get snooty about it. As if you've never made errors under the influence before.

143923.en: Have you delivered those frogs yet, {[character]player.name}?

143926.en: In laboratory work, animals are still used occasionally for testing in appropriate situations. The most popular subjects are Luminaire skippers, a common amphibian from Gallente Prime, and Harst's Greater Earless Rat, which is actually a kind of marsupial of indeterminate origin due to its habit of hitching rides in ship cargo holds.

143927.en: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has a number of outposts in w-space systems, exploring what lies beyond known space. They've turned up some unusual pieces which I need you to take to a more extensive laboratory for identification.

143928.en:
Yes, I have some work for you.

We have several research outposts in various w-space systems. It's one of those things that nobody discusses but everybody knows about anyway. They've recovered bits of ancient technology which seem to have unusual properties... well, compared to what we're used to seeing, at least. We're hoping these might be a clue to the Sleepers' technology... but it could easily be remnants of a scrapyard, for all we know. Take these samples over to the lab at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, so we can figure out what we've got.

143929.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Hurry up! This could be our biggest breakthrough yet!

143930.en: If it's not worth your time, you could have just said so.

143932.en: I've not received a receipt for the cargo yet, {[character]player.name}.

143935.en: Capsuleers aren't the only people to explore the systems accessible via wormholes. Every corporation wants to be the first to make the Next Big Discovery, and then market the developments from researching it. Most corporations will categorically deny that this is what they're doing, creating an atmosphere of both paranoia and plausible deniability if their explorations turn up nothing of value.

143936.en: A nearby station has suffered a life-support failure. They got the atmospheric regulators working again, but the interior temperature is starting to drop. Get the heating units over there quickly, before the place gets too cold.

143937.en:
A severe accident has occurred on another station, {[character]player.name}; they suffered a freak blowout in primary life-support and the station's environmental control shut down entirely. No, don't panic, they stabilized the atmosphere as soon as they could, so the people on the station won't asphyxiate. But the internal heating units have yet to be replaced. People are bundling up as their heat bleeds out – the external insulation is some protection, but it's not enough.

To help out, we've put together as many portable emergency heating units as we could find on such short notice. Take them over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and quickly!

143939.en: Well, I'm certain we can find someone who values their job more.

143940.en: You're heartless, {[character]player.name}. What about all those people?

143941.en: Have you delivered the heating units yet?

143944.en: The most vital systems on a space station or starship, life-support covers everything from atmosphere generation and recycling to environmental control to the recycling of drinking and pumping water. Originally a series of tanks containing specialized filters, as residence in space extended from long-term to lifetimes, advances in bioengineering developed hydroponics systems for stations which both produce and recycle air and water efficiently. Environmental control, which cycles water and air through the station and maintains an even internal temperature despite the cold of space outside nibbling at the edges, runs off the same generator as the internal electrical circuits. External electrical devices, such as guide-lights, shielding and containment fields, security systems and communications, run from separate generators with extensive backup arrays.

143945.en: One of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s archaeological teams has uncovered a load of pre-Federation relics. I need you to transport the pieces to a laboratory for analysis.

143946.en: One of our archaeological teams has unearthed a load of pre-Federation tech from a moon in this system. We're really excited about this; I don't think I need to explain to you how the results of this find could give us a leg up on the competition. Get this lot over to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and don't tell anyone!

143948.en: Sad. I thought you'd have more interest than that.

143950.en: {[character]player.name}, have you delivered those artifacts yet?

143951.en: Excellent! We'll get started on the analysis immediately. This is so exciting!

143953.en: Corporations often sponsor archaeological and research projects, paying for work permits and equipment when the people involved need them. In exchange, the corporations obtain exclusive rights to any discoveries which are made. This includes the right to display and charge viewing fees, or to make new developments based upon information obtained from the artifacts.

143954.en: This shipment of Cerrocentite needs to be taken to the manufacturer on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The cargo is radioactive, and while the containment units are good enough for a short period, the mineral really requires an industrial containment in a stable and controlled environment.

143955.en: Okay, take a look at this. You know what this is? Yes, yes, it's a rock. It's a rare mineral, actually, called Cerrocentite. It has industrial applications, but it's mostly used in security systems. The reason it's in a special containment field is that it's also fairly radioactive. Take this shipment over to the manufacturers at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and don't bloody open it!

143956.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. Do try to hurry, you don't want this stuff sitting around too long in your cargo hold.

143959.en: Have you delivered that Cerrocentite, {[character]player.name}? You don't want to expose your ship to it for much longer.

143962.en: Security systems on stations are all-in-one, monitoring room occupancy, ambient temperature and humidity, and the gas mix from environmental control. It can be set to go on alert for various stimuli, and contains several redundant systems to ensure that an interrupt on one line does not prevent a problem being reported. Small pieces of radioactive material which are sensitive to various stimuli are an integral part of such systems.

143963.en: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is hosting a fashion show for publicity, and your agent needs you to pick up the models. For some reason, they think you won't get fed up and drop them all off in orbit around the nearest moon.

143964.en:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is playing host to a fashion show. It's just another publicity stunt, but we need something to gain the public eye again.

We need someone to pick up the models and fashionistas from {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. You can kind of guess what they're like – a normal pilot just isn't good enough for them, so I have to find a capsuleer I think is level-headed enough to not vent cargo into space if they get too annoying. I know you can handle it, it's not like you have to speak with them face to face, anyway.

143965.en: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I'll make it worth your while.

143966.en: Regrettable, but I can't say I blame you, {[character]player.name}.

143967.en: I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. We have a reputation to maintain.

143968.en: Have you picked up the models yet? The show's only a few hours away!

143969.en: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! Tonight's show should be spectacular.

143971.en:
Like most small corporate entities relying on creativity and artistry, Gallente fashion houses frequently accept patronage from larger corporations, which then sponsor shows and displays. The artists benefit from the visibility and the patron corporations gain another reason to be in the news. Occasionally, the artists incorporate symbols relating to their sponsors in their work, such as logos, corporate colors and mantras, or materials produced by the company.

As always, some art houses denounce the practice, stating that corporate ties bias the work produced by the artists, and accuse the other artists of “selling out,” sacrificing their autonomy for a little planetary cred.

143972.en: The Natural Way is a group which promotes a lower-tech way of life. They're throwing around a lot of cred to start a fitness initiative encouraging kids to stay away from body modding, and I see nothing wrong with encouraging them in exchange for a little ISK.

143973.en: Just don't watch those, okay? They gave me nightmares.

143974.en: What? Who doesn't want to take advantage of anti-tech crazies?

143975.en: Well, fine. But burn the holos. We don't want normal people watching that stuff.

143976.en: You haven't WATCHED those, have you?

143977.en: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. My mother's been giving those to my kids for their birthdays every year, and I was afraid I'd never get rid of them.

143979.en:
There was a time when our children roamed free beneath the sun. They grew strong and healthy under the clear breezes and warm rains. But then technology arose, and with it pollution, sedentary lifestyles, and then the means to compensate for it artificially. But is this truly healthy? Instead of living naturally long lifespans, we turn to medicine and modifications to improve ourselves. Today's teenager spends their days in front of a holoscreen; many of them don't even leave the house of their parents to attend school, preferring to interface remotely.

My friends, is this how we want our children to live?” -- Excerpt from The Natural Way's introductory leaflet

143980.en:
I'm sure you're all too aware of our war with the Caldari State. It's been dragging on for years with no end in sight... until now, that is. We've been making some good headway on the active front and our research and development has been busy behind the scenes. Military scientists have developed a hybrid round that works like single-target burst ECM, and it's time to introduce it to the military for an active field-test.

Take these over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

143981.en: Do not fail us, {[character]player.name}. The Federation is depending on you.

143982.en: I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}. I thought your loyalty might mean more to you.

143983.en: I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. If we find that you've shared this with the Caldari, it will not go well for you.

143985.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. You are a true child of the Federation.

143987.en: Despite their origins in the same solar system, the history between the Gallente Federation and the Caldari State has been laced with conflict since the early days. Initially unified in reaching to the stars through the development of stargate technology, relations rapidly degenerated after the Caldari struck out on their own. Now, separated by a closely-watched border zone, the focus of the two empires lies in staying a few steps ahead of each other.

143988.en: A small fleet of unidentified frigates has attacked one of our remote communications outposts, killing and injuring dozens of our personnel. Those who survived the attack managed to pilot a high-speed shuttle to the nearest station. However, we have strong reason to believe that a team of assassins is en route to their location to eliminate them before they can pass along the information about the organization responsible for this attack. We need you to make all possible haste to their location and rescue the survivors before this hit team arrives.

143989.en: We are disappointed that you have chosen not to complete this critical mission; you've left our contractors at great risk. We will have to find another pilot elsewhere, though I doubt this will be possible at this late stage.

143990.en: Your refusal to accept this mission will undoubtedly result in numerous civilian casualties. We must now try to find someone else to undertake this rescue operation.

143991.en: Your skillful handing of your ship in this vital rescue mission has saved the lives of many civilians who would have otherwise surely perished in the damaged outpost. We knew we could count on you and we will now move you to the top of our list for future missions.

143992.en:
Earlier today, a small, unknown group of frigates attacked one of our remote signals intelligence (SIGINT) communications outposts, causing catastrophic damage and killing dozens of our personnel. This station belongs – or should I say belonged - to a small Caldari corporation with a poorly hidden contractual link to our military intelligence services. Fortunately, the survivors managed to escape, via their high-speed emergency shuttle and are expected to arrive at a nearby station within the hour.

As you might expect, we are working hard to determine the identities of the aggressors, but as yet we have no solid leads. Of course, this is not your concern. What is your concern, should you choose to help us, is a report we just received indicating that the surviving team of SIGINT contractors have been targeted for immediate assassination by the same mysterious organization behind the outpost attack. Apparently, someone does not want these individuals to provide us with whatever information they must have obtained during the course of their recent duties.

Within the last few hours, we intercepted a poorly encrypted communication indicating that a covert hit squad is en route to the station aboard an unspecified vessel – or may actually be at the station already! This station's security force, while well armed and highly trained, is insufficient to detect and defeat the kind of lethal operatives that we believe intend to kill our contractors. Therefore, we need you to rescue this team immediately and bring them back to us for an emergency debriefing and to ensure their safety.

After running a check of qualified pilots in our office database, your name was near the top of the list. We estimate there will only be sufficient time for this one rescue attempt before the assassins strike.

143994.en: The Caldari Navy, much like the military services of other races, operates a covert network of signals intelligence outposts along the borders of the Caldari State. The specific, primary mission of these stations is to provide advance early warning of any hostile incursion by the Gallente military. Beyond this vital mission, however, the outposts are also tasked with gathering intelligence on a wide variety of other targets, both military and civilian. Of particular interest is the regular provision of information on the movement of the commercial and industrial fleets of other races, given the competition between the Caldari corporate system and foreign companies. In this way, the outposts not only provide an essential early warning system for any hostile forces, but also provide data of immense economic value, thus better enabling the Caldari private business sector to better compete in the merciless realm of interstellar business.

143995.en: There is no time to discuss this mission further given the haste with which you will need to accomplish this. Please contact me only when you have delivered the contractors safely to the final destination.

143996.en: Thank you for agreeing to attempt the rescue of our civilian contractors. You must leave very soon if we are to have any hope of reaching them before the hit team arrives.

143997.en: Amarr scientists, working at a clandestine engineering laboratory in a nearby system may have developed the hardest metal yet known to science, known as Ditanium. The potential applications for warfare, specifically, in hardening our warships, is simply too tempting to pass up. Therefore, the full weight of the Amarr military science machine is waiting eagerly for the results of the pending tests, in which the Ditanium plates will be affixed to a specially modified frigate for flight testing. Therefore, we need you to deliver a large quantity of these plates to a nearby station where it will be transshipped to a military shipyard for fitting to the Punisher testbed ship.

143998.en:
As you know, Amarr warships rely heavily on the various armors that we use in the construction and upgrading of our ships. For the most part, we rely on the same metals and alloys found in markets and hangars found in virtually every corner of the populated regions.
