Thus, it is a rare thing when a wholly new metal appears – and rarer still when only one race discovers it, unbeknownst to the others.

Such an occurrence, I can tell you now only in the strictest confidence, has indeed taken place at a remote clandestine Amarr metallurgical research facility. Masquerading as a routine ore processing laboratory near an otherwise uninteresting Veldspar-laden asteroid field, this facility has been conducting advanced research exclusively into an extremely rare and highly classified metal, found only in the ore of a small fraction of the asteroids present in that specific field: a new metal we call Ditanium. To date, this is the strongest naturally occurring metal yet encountered by our scientists. While we are confident that this metal exists elsewhere in space, to our knowledge, we are the first to actually find it.

Given the rarity of this metal and the significant complexities of its mining and processing, it has taken two full months to produce just enough finished metal plates to fit a single Punisher-class frigate. We intend to use this ship for Phase I field testing, which includes flight handling characteristics, radar cross-section analysis, temperature extremes testing, and other critical operational parameters. If successful, we are confident that we may be able to begin full scale production and ship fitting within two years.

However, before this test can take place, we need someone to courier these Ditanium plates to a station we designate. From there, it will be transshipped to a military shipyard for fitting to the Punisher testbed ship. We do not anticipate this shipment will present any problems, particularly given the high level of secrecy relating to the project, but with potentially many hundreds of billions of ISK riding on the successful integration of Ditanium into our armor plates and other protective ship components, we are taking no chances.

We need to know immediately if you will deliver this Ditanium to the designated station.

143999.en: I was just informed that you have chosen to quit this important mission prior to the agreed on completion conditions. Please return the Ditanium plates to the nearest Amarr station and we will consider this arrangement terminated.

144000.en: Well, it is unfortunate that you've chosen not to help us. We trust that you will not discuss this meeting with any other parties, though we are confident that if you did, they would likely laugh you out of whatever station bar you frequent. And if we do hear of you babbling your mouth about this, be assured that we will find you and liquidate any chance of a future partnership, if you catch my meaning.

144001.en: Outstanding news, {[character]player.name}. Our scientists have verified receipt of the Ditanium plates and are right now moving those pallets to other ships for transshipment to the final destination. Well done and please contact us again in the future should you seek further employment. And remember: you were never here.

144002.en: Yes, well, we were quite confident that this would be a fairly routine mission, so we were glad to hear that is indeed the case. Fly safe, pilot.

144003.en: We have reason to believe that a small team of Gallente saboteurs has managed to destroy one of our new – and not yet fully operational – Command Centers on a nearby ice planet. These facilities are critical elements in our overall plan to dominate the planet such that we can then exploit the vast and lucrative materials that we have identified there in abundance. We need you to deliver a large complement of Arctic Warfare Marines to a forward station so that they can then be transferred down to provide the security we so desperately need. Their massive amounts of equipment will be brought in on other ships, so we need you to deliver these men safely and securely – everything depends on their safe arrival.

144005.en: Are the Marines behaving themselves? Good. Please continue to make all possible haste in delivering them to the station. They tend to get a bit rowdy when they are cooped up too long.

144006.en: How you can quit this mission mid-stream is absolutely beyond me. Do you have any idea the mountains of isk that this is going to cause my department and the Planetary Exploitation Division as a whole? Don't ever come back here for a while.

144007.en: I'm glad to you hear that you've agreed to help us out on this one. If you'll just confirm this manifest, we'll rally the Marines and have them report to your ship immediately. You'd better get moving – don't want to keep the troops waiting.

144008.en: We have so far managed to keep this event a closely held secret, as we do not want to discourage the senior management of the company from further exploiting the extremely valuable materials that are in largely untapped abundance on the sea floor. If word of this was to get out at this critical stage, it might give them reason pack up and move to a safer location - perhaps even to another planet. Well, this would simply be unacceptable, as our new planetary industry efforts have so far generated record revenues - the one thing keeping our shareholders and investors happy. And we want to keep them happy, if you understand my meaning. We must allow nothing to interrupt that flow of ISK into our corporate coffers.

144009.en: I just got word that you delivered all the Marines safely to the station, great job! However, I must now coordinate the follow-on shipment of their equipment and weapons, which is going to mean another all-nighter here at the office. Oh well, business first, yes?  We will be in touch for future missions, so thanks again.

144010.en: That you have chosen to decline this mission has put this company in a very difficult position, to say the least. Well, get out of here then; let us hope the Marines don't hear about this and decide to give you a rather rough send-off.

144011.en:
Two days ago, a covert Gallente strike team infiltrated and destroyed a brand new Command Center on a nearby ice planet. We think they managed to infiltrate as local civilian workers due the fact that the facility's Personnel Security Identification Systems had not yet been fully brought online. This unforgivable lapse in security enabled the four-man team to gain access to a highly secure area that contains the controls for the counter-harmonic stabilizers which, in short, keep the entire facility level and secure in the very harsh climates encountered on that planet. A series of well-placed explosives damaged these stabilizers, however, taking them offline and causing the entire command center to collapse and sink through the ice to the ocean floor some two kilometers below. Fortunately, the bulk of the work force was not scheduled to arrive for two more weeks, so casualties were very light. The financial and economic costs were, however, staggering.

Now that you understand the gravity of the situation, we can proceed to the reason that we contacted you to help us in this critical moment in the company's ongoing rapid expansion phase. We need you to very quietly transport a company of our best Arctic Warfare Marines from this station to the destination station with all possible haste. From there they will flown to the ice planet to provide a very high level of security for this and other nearby command centers and facilities. It is just a matter of time before this disastrous event becomes public knowledge, and we need to prove to the senior management, shareholders, and investors that we have the security situation resolutely in hand.

So, {[character]player.name}, are you willing to help us out by delivering a large number of Arctic Marines to the designated station?

144012.en: The daughter of a Caldari executive was kidnapped this morning by a group of slavers while she was on holiday. They are demanding we provide them a large quantity of our rarest and most expensive metal, quantrium, in exchange for her life. There is no time to mount a rescue operation, so our only choice is to provide this shipment immediately. We will deal with those criminals once the girl has been released to us. However, time is of the essence, and our primary mission now is to deliver this shipment to a transshipment station for further transportation to the slavers' designated rendezvous point.

144013.en:
Time is a factor here, so I will get to the point. The daughter of a prominent Caldari industrialist, CEO of a large scrap metal corporation, was kidnapped while she was on holiday with her school classmates. At the time of her abduction, she was in a lowsec system she should not have been in, one well known for its hedonistic night life. Apparently, the girls each told a bit of a fib to their parents, indicating they were traveling to a much safer, highsec destination resort. Well, early this morning we received an urgent call from the executive's chief of security telling us that the daughter had been grabbed and thrown into a vehicle by some dangerous-looking men outside a bar after a night of drinking.

While we had hoped it was part of some prank or a misunderstanding as to what the girls really saw, our worst fears have been realized. We have been contacted, through a circuitous channel, by a notorious band of slavers. As proof of life, they have transmitted the daughter's DNA sequence to us. Analysis of this information has verified her identity.

The kidnappers have given us a very short window in which we can secure the girl's safe release, after which they will sell her into slavery – and I don't want to even imagine what horrors that might entail. As expected, they are demanding a very large payoff in exchange for her life. Specifically, they want our entire stockpile of our rarest and most expensive metal, quantrium – one found only in the wiring of electronic countermeasures (ECM) equipment of the Caldari Navy's Rook-class combat reconnaissance ships.

What I need you to do is to quickly move this quantrium to the designated station for transshipment to the slavers' rendezvous point. We will take it from there.

144014.en: Please, pilot, do make haste. The quantrium must be delivered as soon as possible. If we are even one minute late to the rendezvous, the slavers will assume we have involved the authorities, and we will never see the young girl again.

144015.en: The kidnappers have been listening to our comms, and have heard that you have chosen to quit. They have let us know that we will not see the executive's daughter again. I hope your reasons for quitting are worth the life of an innocent young girl.

144016.en: We were counting on you. You were our only hope for the safe return of the CEO's daughter. I hope your cowardice here today will haunt you for the rest of your miserable life!

144017.en: We just got word from the hotel security staff – the executive's daughter was returned to them safe and sound, as the kidnappers promised!  We owe you a debt I hope we can repay one day! We will not forget you!

144018.en: Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. During a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's sensor cross-section, making it much easier to detect and attack. Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Therefore, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet.

144019.en:
Greetings, {[character]player.name}. Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. He swallowed a hidden poison tablet as we moved in to arrest him, so he is no longer a threat.

However, during a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's signature radius, making it much easier for our enemies to detect and attack.

Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Essentially, the Widow's commander would not know that his ship had lost its critical operational advantage until he was detected and targeted by hostile combatants. Given the very specialized role of this ship, not only would the Widow be compromised, but it is possible than any ships he might be bridging in via its covert jump portal generator could be unknowingly hot dropped near a waiting enemy fleet, instead of empty space.

In order to remedy this critical situation, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet. This shipment represents our best and only hope to quickly repair the damage done by the Gallente spy and ensure the safety of our brave Widow pilots and crew.

144020.en: Do not contact me on an open channel until this mission is complete. Remember, this is a clandestine operation!

144021.en: Your successful delivery of the prototype nanites will undoubtedly save the lives of many Black Ops pilots and crew. You have the makings of a good counter operative!

144022.en: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our Black Ops teams at great risk. We will have to find another operative elsewhere.

144023.en: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to accept this critical mission. We will have to find another pilot elsewhere.

144024.en: Produced by the Kaalakiota megacorporation, the Widow-class Black Ops battleship represents the current edge technology for Caldari military vessels used in covert operations. The primary function of the Widow is to conduct infiltration and espionage behind enemy lines. Specifically, when equipped with covert cynosural field generators and covert jump portal generators, the ship can create a “bridge” through which conventional ships are instantly transported, much like a jump gate. The effect of this is to surprise an enemy by instantly “hot dropping” a combat fleet into what was, moments prior, only empty space. In addition, it can also be fitted with ECM modules and cruise missiles such that it can provide jamming capabilities and supporting firepower if necessary. Using this technology, the Widow represents a significant force multiplier in the ongoing conflicts faced by the Caldari State.

144025.en: We are relieved to hear that you've accepted this important mission. It is imperative that you deliver this cargo with all possible haste.

144027.en: A team of mercenaries led by a man calling himself “Black Dog” has killed one of our senior managers as he toured an asteroid field not far from here. Intelligence has indicated that he intends to continue these operations into the foreseeable future. To remedy this unacceptable situation, we need you to transport a trained assassin and his entourage to a station closer to the scene of the crime. Once this is done, you will have completed the terms of this contract. We appreciate your discretion in this endeavor.

144029.en: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our executives and even our miners at significant risk from these mercenaries.

144030.en: Your unwillingness to assist us in this matter is going to cost this corporation a great deal of isk until we can find some other way to resolve it. Mr. Smith may soon take a personal interest in you, as you've now disrupted his lucrative contract. I certainly don't want to be in your shoes once he gets the word.

144031.en: We all know the saying, “business is war.” Nowhere is this adage practiced more seriously than in the Caldari corporate world. The soldiers in this fight are typically thought of as the salesmen, managers, executives, and other boardroom warriors. However, from time to time a very special skill set is required to deal with an equally specific threat. For these situations, corporate assassins are sometimes required to resolve issues that cannot be otherwise remedied through conventional channels. In the most extreme cases, these highly-trained operatives, most of whom served particularly arduous and dangerous careers in the Caldari Special Forces and intelligence groups, are hired to carry out very selective missions with very limited goals. The missions they are paid, - highly paid at that - to undertake would rival any holovid espionage movie, though the consequences are, of course, much more serious. You don't want to mess with these guys, and gals, as it is usually the last thing you'll ever do.

144032.en: We just received word from Mr. Smith that you did indeed deliver him on time and without attracting any unusual inquiries. We hope the compensation for this mission was worth your time. The Caldari State can use more competent and discretionary pilots like you.

144034.en:
Before we begin, I must make one thing perfectly clear: You were never here, and this meeting never took place. You do understand what I mean, yes?

We are in need of a pilot who can deliver a very sensitive cargo from this station to a nearby station, without attracting any undue attention. You may have heard in the news or the local gossip channels that a Caldari regional director for mining operations was murdered yesterday by unknown assailants while touring an asteroid field in his personal shuttle. That much is indeed true. However, what has not been reported is that we have, in the last few hours, learned the identity of the assassin, a mercenary who goes by the name “Black Dog”, and that he and his team have already begun to plan for an ongoing hit-and-run campaign designed to try and scare off Caldari corporations from any future mining activities in the region.

Of course, we cannot allow this kind of disruption to what has proven a highly lucrative endeavor – the Board and our shareholders simply will not tolerate any further dips in revenues. To remedy this interruption, one of our sister companies that specializes in, shall we say, discrete solutions, has loaned us one of their most highly trained specialists to resolve this issue. His name, as you might expect, is Mr. Smith. His mission, in brief, is to liquidate Black Dog, along with any associates that may be operating with him at the time.

What we need from you, and need soon, is for you to transport Mr. Smith and his entourage to a station closer to the action – one with a hangar walkway the leads directly to an unmarked office. Once you have dropped him off, your role in this action will be complete.

So, what is it going to be, pilot? We need a yes or no right now if this operation is to stay on schedule.

144035.en: We know the mission is proceeding well, as we've got a cloaked Covert Ops ship following you at a discrete distance. Please contact me only in the event of an emergency.

144036.en: I'm glad to hear you're going to help us out here. We aren't expecting any trouble with this one, but with corporate espionage, you never know – keep your eyes open.

144037.en: By quitting mid-mission you've singlehandedly compromised the whole operation! I doubt we'll be able to flush out the spy now, given the fact that you've interrupted the shipment – no doubt he will sense something is up and simply remain unknown to us.

144038.en: Well, we are disappointed that you've turned this one down. We'll have to use one of our own transportation pilots to get this done.

144039.en: Outstanding job, {[character]player.name}! As you may have heard by now, the spy was caught trying to remove the device from the offload cargo bay on the station. Needless to say, he has a very uncomfortable future ahead of him in one of our interrogation facilities. Thanks to your piloting skills and discretion, our work on the new cloak remains a well guarded secret.

144040.en: In order to get around the laws pertaining to the transportation of illegal drugs through Amarr Empire space, we have been forced to create new and unknown substances for use on, or by, rather, our various slave labor enclaves. This new drug, Blue Paradise, does away with many of the harmful chemicals previously used while actually increasing the pleasurable effects. We are certain that, properly controlled and distributed, introduction of this drug into the slave labor workforce will increase productivity by a substantial margin. We are counting on you to deliver it to the designation transshipment station as soon as possible.

144041.en: Biochemical Agents for Improved Slave Workloads

144042.en: Well, you have certainly wasted my very valuable time. I thought we could count on you, but obviously I was misinformed. Don't count on working for me any time soon.

144043.en: Excellent. We are transferring your cargo to a dozen smaller ships equipped for high speed runs to the more remote work sites in the region. I see a lot of profit in your future, {[character]player.name}, if you stick with us.

144044.en: There are few things I despise more than a quitter. If you come back to my station I am sure we can find you a position on the station slave labor gang, scrubbing the personal hygiene tanks with a toothbrush for the next six months.

144045.en:
History has shown us that a properly motivated slave work force can work harder and longer - especially in harsh conditions - if they are provided the means to enhance their everyday lives. Well, for many decades, the provision of various stimulant drugs to slave laborers was considered a standard method of doing business. However, the downside to this was that, while the use of stims typically increased productivity, more often than not it resulted in significant long term health problems for the slaves leading to shortened lifespans and, more importantly, to decreased profits. So, while the use of stimulants has largely been discontinued, the idea that drugs could increase slave output never entirely went away, though it did require a new approach.

To this end, my company recently developed an inexpensive new drug that works on the pleasure centers of the brain, providing what we might call a “reward” for hard work. Importantly, this drug, known as Blue Paradise, or "Beep" as the techs call it, has been proven in real-world testing to increase slave labor output by as much as twenty percent across the board, without any known long term health problems. As you can guess, the increased profit potential here is, well, staggering. Equally important is the fact that we have not reported this new drug to the various control boards; nor do we intend to at this juncture.

We need you to deliver a very large shipment of this drug to a forward logistics hub station from which it will be transshipped to ore mines, agricultural farms, and other slave-intensive operations. I can give you my guarantee that this cargo will not be flagged by customs or the police, as it is not yet deemed an illegal substance.

So, can we count on you to deliver this?

144046.en: Good, glad to hear it. I will immediately order the refrigerated secure containers moved into your cargo hold for your prompt departure.

144047.en:
We all know that there have been a long series of proclamations, laws, and rules banning the transportation of illegal drugs (and some legal drugs) in Amarr space for use in slave labor. These prohibitions have typically had no real teeth, unless of course the Empress herself sets forth an official decree specifically banning a given substance. The logical, time-tested way around this has been to create entirely new generations of performance enhancing biochemical drugs.

As slaves are typically wary of any pills or other obvious means of altering their behavior (recalling, as we must, the various slave uprisings that have occurred when we tried to openly force drugs on them), we've had to resort to less obvious methods. For example, we have surreptitiously and gradually delivered the drugs into laborer's systems through aerosols in their habitat ventilation systems, impregnated substances into their foodstuffs and water supplies, and other rather clever means, I won't go into here. What is important is that the result has almost always been a positive one, with significant increases in worker productivity.

The downside to this, however, has been a decline in overall slave lifespans due to the long term effects of these drugs. Normally, this would be considered simple attrition; a cost of doing businesses. However, as it continues to become more and more difficult to obtain new slaves (particularly given the intolerable and unjust interference of the other empires), this solution is less and less viable. We need them to live as long as possible. This reality, of course, leads us to the only other benign option – drugs as a part of a rewards system for those slaves who meet a certain work quota each day.

To this end, we shall continue to develop new substances to both avoid interference by Customs and police forces and to ensure the maximum possible output by our slave laborers.

144048.en:
I'm sure you're all too aware of our war with the Caldari State. It's been dragging on for years with no end in sight... until now, that is. We've been making some good headway on the active front and our research and development has been busy behind the scenes. Military scientists have developed a hybrid round that works like single-target burst ECM, and it's time to introduce it to the military for an active field-test.

Take these over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

144049.en: Do not fail us, {[character]player.name}. The Federation is depending on you.

144050.en: I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}. I thought your loyalty might mean more to you.

144051.en: I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. If we find that you've shared this with the Caldari, it will not go well for you.

144053.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. You are a true child of the Federation.

144055.en: There has always been contention over the effectiveness of the Federation's sensor-dampening ewar tactics against the State's ECM. Some military scientists feel that, in adding ECM to the hybrid arsenal, the Federation would be admitting to a weakness and confirming the State's superiority; others argue that turning the enemy's tactics against them is an essential facet of wartime, and that rejecting the opportunity is effectively signing off on the Federation's defeat. The debate rages in both the staterooms and the laboratories even as research and development continues.

144056.en: Excellent news, pilot, thank you for updating us as to your position and condition. Please make all possible speed to the destination so that we can then dispatch the combined rescue team package.

144057.en: We've received confirmation that you did indeed fulfill your promise and deliver the Marines to the station. As we speak, the combined rescue team is loading into other ship for immediate transport to the Harbinger. Hopefully, we will reach them in time.

144058.en: Quitting? Now?  You have placed our marines and hundreds of other personnel in grave danger by abandoning them mid-mission. We will have to find some way to get them to our damaged strategic cruiser, though I feel it is now too late.

144059.en: We will not forget this – the moment you chose to abandon our people in a time of great need. Your assistance could have turned the tide of this whole disaster. Do not contact me again.

144060.en: I have to request a difficult task of you: play nice with a swarm of Angel Cartel representatives and their entourage on your ship. Hopefully they won't try to cause you trouble.

144061.en:
This is a list of people I want you to escort to a meeting. They have quite a large security entourage, and as you can see from some of the names, they have a reason for it. These people are members of the Angel Cartel. While the Cartel are thugs and pirate scum, and are not particularly welcome in Minmatar space, it does not mean that some corporations don't have certain dealings with them.

This isn't your usual business meeting this time, however. Evidently, the Cartel overstepped their bounds, and the corporation took it to the Republic. Escort these Angel representatives to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; we'll take care of the rest. For the sake of appearances, try to treat them politely. We don't want them to know it's a set-up until they get to the boardroom.

144063.en: I'm disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}, but I can understand why you might decline.

144065.en: Hello, {[character]player.name}. Have you finished your work for me?

144066.en: Excellent, thank you, {[character]player.name}. I think we got our point across to them; there are some things you do not try to push in the Republic.

144068.en: The Angel Cartel's reputation for engaging in any activity regardless of its legality has earned it the DED's description of the most dangerous criminal organization in the cluster. With a corporate command structure and open recruitment policy, the Cartel are less thugs than sharks in pinstripe suits, capable of operating on all levels of society. With a major operational base in Etherium Reach on the edge of Minmatar space, the Cartel is held with deep suspicion within the Republic. Their annexation of the Skarkon system in YC 110 and sudden withdrawal left many unanswered questions regarding both the Cartel's intentions towards the Republic and what deals were forged under the table to make them leave... and what those deals might have cost.

144069.en:
A short time ago, Minmatar terrorists in a combined fleet of frigates and cruisers attacked one of our Harbinger-class strategic cruisers as it was transporting slaves from a recently closed mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in a nearby system. While all but one of the attackers was annihilated, our convoy's escorts were destroyed and our cruiser is burning. Making a bad situation worse, we are anticipating that the terrorists will return in force within the next several hours to attempt the theft of our slaves, as they almost certainly know the cruiser is alone and all but helpless.

Our concern is that if the terrorists feel that they have a window of opportunity to recover these slaves, it is likely that they will throw everything they have into the effort. Our intelligence assessments of the terrorists' fleet assets are even less reassuring: we believe that they could send as many as four battlecruisers into this fight – more than enough to wipe out the arriving frigates and forcefully board our heavily damaged strategic cruiser. However, we have calculated that if we can delay any terrorist boarding parties long enough, this should give us enough time for the much larger main rescue fleet to arrive.

The only bright side to this situation, in what is unquestionably an act of divine providence, is that a large contingent of marines are aboard this station as we speak, having just completed specialized refresher training in counter-boarding operations. We need you to deliver them to the station closest to the last reported position of our cruiser. From there, we will transport a combined team of marines, engineers, medics, and other essential personnel to hopefully stop the fire and save the ship - along with its cargo of highly valuable slaves. However, this mission must be undertaken immediately. Any delay will surely doom the Harbinger and her brave crew.

144070.en: Our deepest thanks for taking on this mission. I can tell you that our best analysts feel that you should be fairly safe in this mission, as the terrorist will have to focus all their efforts on targeting the stricken cruiser. They simply won't have the ships or the time to even attempt to interdict your ship as you make your way to the destination station.

144071.en: What? Who doesn't want to take advantage of anti-tech crazies?

144072.en: Well, fine. But burn the holos. We don't want normal people watching that stuff.

144074.en: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is hosting a fashion show for publicity, and your agent needs you to pick up the models. For some reason, they think you won't get fed up and drop them all off in orbit around the nearest moon.

144075.en: The Federal Talent Showcase is upon us, that time of year where all the artists and “artists” come out of hiding and shove the products of the past year in our faces. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is playing host to a fashion show and we need someone to pick up the models and fashionistas from {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. You can kind of guess what they're like – a normal pilot just isn't good enough for them, so I have to find a capsuleer I think is level-headed enough to not vent cargo into space if they get too annoying. I know you can handle it, it's not like you have to speak with them face to face, anyway.

144076.en: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I'll make it worth your while.

144077.en: Regrettable, but I can't say I blame you, {[character]player.name}.

144078.en: I'm disappointed, {[character]player.name}. We have a reputation to maintain.

144079.en: Have you picked up the models yet? The show's only a few hours away!

144080.en: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I imagine you're happy to have that lot off your hands.

144082.en: In a culture as materialistic and appearance-conscious as the Gallente, the ability to stay on the bleeding edge is a valuable asset. “Clothes,” fashion critic Marko Envaumier said in a well-known interview with the Scope, “are an outward expression of man's inner nature and outlook toward life. Professional secretaries study fashion alongside the other office skills ... to learn to gauge the worth of both potential clients and employees for the companies that hire them. Next time you walk into an office, remember that the boy or girl behind the desk is checking your tailoring.”

144083.en: We have recently been experiencing an increase in terrorist attacks by groups seeking to free Amarr slaves in this region. Their raids have become more complex and lethal, resulting in the loss of untold millions of ISK worth of valuable property. More importantly, one of the regional governors is having his annual gala event at his estate on a nearby planet. We need you to deliver a cargo of elite conditioned slaves to a station we will designate. From there they will be transported to the governor's estate by heavily armed ships.

144084.en:
You are aware, no doubt, of the rumors of extremist antislavery terrorist groups within the Amarr Empire itself. Well, you know then that their loyalty to the Empire is indeed secondary to their overarching desire to see all slaves freed and made equal members of society. This is a condition that we, as the greatest state in all of New Eden, simply cannot tolerate. However, our efforts at arresting and reeducating those insurgents have largely failed to permanently change the mindsets of these rather fanatical individuals.

This system has been particularly hard hit by this and other like-minded groups. Most recently, an Anathema-class covert ops ship, specially configured to transport elite slaves to the estates of senior Amarr leaders in the region, was somehow decloaked, its weapons and sensors jammed, and ruthlessly attacked to the point of near-total structure failure. The terrorists then demanded the pilot transfer the slaves to this mystery ship, on threat of the total destruction of the covert ops vessel. The pilot complied, though he has since been punished for his cowardice.

It is for this reason that I called you here today. I need you to transport a new shipment of elite slaves to a nearby station for further transshipment to the residence of one of the regional governors. This shipment is of particular urgency as the governor is hosting his annual gala event at his estate, and the usual staff of slaves simply will not do. We need these specific slaves, as they have been trained in protocol, proper food and drink service, entertainment, and numerous other talents that I need not mention here.

Will you take on this courier mission on behalf of the Empire and deliver these highly trained and extremely expensive slaves to the designated station?

144086.en: While it might seem impossible at first glance, there are indeed small bands of terrorists who seek to upset the very core foundation of our society by working to eliminate slavery throughout the Empire. We have had significant success in disrupting these groups, with many members killed or taken prisoner. Nonetheless, like a hydra they continue to grow and adapt to our tactics and operations, making them a quite annoying thorn in our side. The Amarr Empire is devoting increasing resources to the eradication of these groups; however, even the most optimistic analysts concede that it may be quite some time before this nascent insurgency can be eradicated.

144087.en: Our spies have succeeded in smuggling pieces of the latest experimental Amarrian starship technology back to the Republic. I need you to take the samples on to the lab where they can be properly analyzed.

144088.en:
You need to keep this quiet, {[character]player.name}. I know you capsuleers aren't accustomed to being told how to do your job, but this is bigger than anything else and if word gets out, all this effort will be for nothing.

We've acquired samples of the Amarr's latest experimental starship tech. Don't ask me how, I don't want to know, and neither do you. We're not sure what these pieces do; our source is suggesting it's a system that reduces the effectiveness of our electronic warfare systems. This could be bad news for us. Get the stuff over to the lab at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. And keep your trap shut. We don't want it getting back to the Amarr that we have this.

144089.en: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. I knew we could count on you.

144090.en: I guess your loyalty isn't worth as much as I thought.

144091.en: I guess your loyalty isn't worth as much as I thought.

144092.en: Have you delivered that stuff to the lab, {[character]player.name}?

144093.en: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Our research team is saying the tech deflects target painter beams away towards an area of space just behind the ship it's fitted on. Our torpedoes will start missing targets if they manage to make this widely available. We need to find a way to counter this, and fast.

144095.en: The current war between the Republic and the Empire is not solely left to warfare in space. Spies and sympathizers work behind the scenes to sabotage war efforts and uncover the Empire's secrets, helping the Republic to meet the Empire's forces equally. The Empire has its own spies, however, and the underlying conflict can sap morale and lead to high levels of paranoia.

144096.en: Thank you for the update pilot, it is rather reassuring that you are flying without any interference from our unwanted friends. Please contact me again when you are being towed in to the dock, as only then will I feel assured that this courier mission was a success.

144097.en: You must be kidding?!? I have already guaranteed the governor's office that you are en route and will arrive at the scheduled time. This act on your part is probably going to get me reassigned to some asteroid in an uncharted system a million light years from here. Well, I will make sure I'm not the only one who will feel the heat for this failure.

144098.en: While I must say I am rather shocked at your refusal to undertake this mission, we are fortunate in that we do have contingency plans in place. So, while we will have to risk the crew and slaves in another run, I feel confident that only you will bear the negative feedback for failing us here today.

144099.en: Great job, {[character]player.name}. The slaves are being offloaded now and will be en route to the governor's estate shortly. I can't thank you enough for your reliability and promptness.

144100.en: That is very good news, pilot. I will contact the governor's aide myself to let her know that you have accepted and will be departing shortly.

144101.en: Thank you a million times over, pilot, for taking on this mission. The hearts and minds of the Amarr faithful in that station and elsewhere will benefit immeasurably from your prompt delivery of these hallowed holoreels.

144102.en: Well, I was not expecting this. All we needed was for you to make a simple run from this station to the designated station and drop off our cargo. Well, suffice to say, you will not be receiving any prayers of blessing from me tonight!

144103.en: Our hearts are glad to know that you are en route to the station and will be docking there shortly. Please contact me on arrival.

144104.en: During a high-level security assessment, a decoy maglev train designed to mimic the regional governor's chartered train was destroyed by unknown saboteurs while traveling at very high speed. Our investigation has yet to uncover the traitors; however, we are confident that a prompt scientific examination of the wreckage will provide the clues we need to resolve this internal security matter. We are sending a team of senior investigators to the wreck site so that they might help determine the identities of the attackers. We are counting on you to fly them to the designated station.

144105.en:
I know the security screening process at this station has been time-consuming and a bit, well, intrusive. Now that you have passed our various tests, however, I feel confident that I can now let you in on the reason you are here.

One of our regional governors had recently been planning an unannounced visit to one of the new planetary command centers in a nearby system. For security reasons, this information was restricted to only those in the governor's inner circle, to include the commander of his personal security detail. Well, this commander decided to test his internal security prior to this event, to best ensure the governor's safe travel. So, for this exercise, he created a painstakingly detailed agenda, identical in every detail to an actual state visit. In this scenario, the governor was to travel by chartered high-speed maglev train to a number of the new planetary command centers.

As the Governor's decoy train traveled through a large canyon, however, a series of explosive charges detonated on the rail line, sending the train off its track and into the canyon wall. As it turned out, the security commander's ruse had worked perfectly; someone in the governor's inner circle had tipped his or her hand and provided information to unknown assassins.

So far, however, we have not been able to determine the traitor's identity, and each member of the inner circle is vehemently denying any involvement, despite our best chemical interrogations. So, what this investigation will likely boil down to is to what clues can be solved from the train wreckage, the destroyed maglev track sections, and the soil around the site of the blasts.

We need you to transport several investigative teams, along with a considerable amount of equipment, to a nearby station where they will then be transported via shuttle to the planet. Will you take on this mission?

144106.en: Thank you for agreeing to aid the Empire in this matter. My assistant will provide you all the details you will need to deliver these personnel to the designated station.

144107.en: We are extremely disappointed in your decision to leave this mission. I am quite sure the Regional Governor's office will not soon forget this offense to the Empire.

144108.en: We are disappointed in your decision not to assist the Empire in its hour of need. However, we do have another pilot waiting in the next room, so you may leave. And I need not remind you of the consequences should you discuss any of what you have been told here today.

144109.en: Excellent work, pilot. The personnel you transported for us have already developed some interesting leads, and it seems – at least at this early juncture – that the assassins may be of Minmatar descent. Further testing, we expect, will confirm this. We will retain your contact information, should this incident require more of your courier skills.

144113.en: I haven't received confirmation of your delivery yet, {[character]player.name}. Is there a problem?

144115.en: Smaller ships rely upon their speed and smaller signature radius to make it difficult for larger ships to track and target them. The heat output from propulsion systems increases signature radius, making a small target much easier to track; the greater the speed, the greater the heat production. Specialized coatings help to reduce the effect and prevent expansion of the parts within propulsion systems, helping them to operate much more efficiently.

144116.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. The testers have already submitted a preliminary report. The results seem favorable towards our new design, and we've received permission to begin a small first-run production.

144117.en: This shipment of Mesarchonite needs to be taken to the manufacturer on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The cargo is radioactive, and while the containment units are good enough for a short period, the mineral really requires an industrial containment in a stable and controlled environment.

144118.en: Okay, take a look at this. You know what this is? Yes, yes, it's a rock. It's a rare mineral, actually, called Mesarchonite. It has industrial applications, but it's mostly used in security systems. The reason it's in a special containment field is that it's also fairly radioactive. Take this shipment over to the manufacturers at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and don't bloody open it!

144119.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. Do try to hurry, you don't want this stuff sitting around too long in your cargo hold.

144122.en: Have you delivered that Mesarchonite, {[character]player.name}? You don't want to expose your ship to it for much longer.

144125.en: Security systems on stations are all-in-one, monitoring room occupancy, ambient temperature and humidity, and the gas mix from environmental control. It can be set to go on alert for various stimuli, and contains several redundant systems to ensure that an interrupt on one line does not prevent a problem being reported. Small pieces of radioactive material which are sensitive to various stimuli are an integral part of such systems.

144126.en: One of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s archaeological teams has uncovered a load of pre-Federation relics. I need you to transport the pieces to a laboratory for analysis.

144127.en: One of our archaeological teams has unearthed a load of pre-Federation tech from a moon in this system. We're really excited about this; I don't think I need to explain to you how the results of this find could give us a leg up on the competition. Get this lot over to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and don't tell anyone!

144129.en: Sad. I thought you'd have more interest than that.

144131.en: {[character]player.name}, have you delivered those artifacts yet?

144132.en: Thank you for your help, {[character]player.name}. The minerals that society was focusing on are pretty worthless to us -- it's just crystalline octenase, borealt and the like -- but it looks like they were used in the basic construction of the ship they used for the outpost. Who would have thought of coating low-density tritanium panels with a lassenium compound? With a little work, we can find out where their culture came from, and why they're not here anymore.

144134.en: Corporations often sponsor archaeological and research projects, paying for work permits and equipment when the people involved need them. In exchange, the corporations obtain exclusive rights to any discoveries which are made. This includes the right to display and charge viewing fees, or to make new developments based upon information obtained from the artifacts.

144135.en:
Oh! {[character]player.name}, perfect timing!

One of our research outposts in Molden Heath came under attack by rogue drones last week. This is highly unusual, since drones are rarely seen beyond Etherium Reach. The outpost's defense systems managed to keep our scientists safe, and the downed drones were retrieved for examination. They found unusual mineral deposits replacing the drones' original microboard networks, which appear to work far more efficiently.

Of course we don't want anyone else getting ahold of the samples before we can replicate them. The samples have been in transit via a series of drops in order to keep them safe. Take them on to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

144136.en: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I can't wait to see what we've got.

144137.en: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.

144138.en: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.

144139.en: {[character]player.name}, have you done what I asked?

144140.en: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. We're one step closer to the forefront of technological advancement!

144141.en: While examining wrecked rogue drones following a failed attack, strange minerals were found which replaced some of the drones' usual systems. The compounds seem to run more efficiently than the parts they replaced, and your agent has hired you to take the find to researchers for examination.

144143.en:
Rogue drones began innocently enough, as part of a Gallente scientist's research into drones that could learn and operate independently. The artificial intelligence he created was in itself fairly primitive and non-threatening, but in its self-perpetuation it developed beyond the scope of the scientist's work, and the drones began to truly think for themselves.
Using the justification that the results had produced extreme and life-threatening risk to human life, CONCORD declared all research into artificial intelligence illegal unless performed in a controlled and isolated environment under the watchful eye of DED experts. Proposals for engaging in such research are vetted carefully and the scientists presenting the proposals are subject to extreme background scrutiny.

144144.en: Against my better judgment, I've been asked to order several sets of educational packages of the Amarr Scriptures for the children of families who have been released by the Empire. It leaves a sour taste in the mouth, but maybe we can use the teaching materials to our own ends.

144145.en:
I'm in a bit of an awkward position here, {[character]player.name}. With all the people being released from slavery in the Empire, we're getting more and more families who practice the Amarr religion. No thanks to Jamyl, she knew this would happen. The edict from our government is that we need to respect the poor deluded people and gently introduce them to a new way of thinking. It won't be easy, and it's putting a strain on all of us.

My problem right now is that a bunch of the refugee families have requested that some Amarr Scriptures be included in the course structure at the schools we've set up for their children. It's our own people doing the teaching, so we can slowly steer the education in the right direction, but we all still feel dirty for having to use it.

Do you think you'd be willing to take a shipment of books over to one of the schools?

144146.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. I knew I could count on you.

144150.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. I know it's an unsavory business, but our instructions from on high are to try to get along and help these people adjust.

144152.en: With the release of several generations of slaves from the Empire, Jamyl struck a blow at the heart of Minmatar culture, forcing the Republic to accept those who have known only the ways of Amarr and what little Minmatar tradition they had been able to maintain through the years. Inducting such people into modern Republic society has proven troublesome and at times outright frustrating; allowing released slaves to practice the religion they grew up with has been a bitter necessity as counselors struggle to help the people adapt to their new lives.

144153.en: A nearby station has suffered a life-support failure. They got the atmospheric regulators working again, but the interior temperature is starting to drop. Get the heating units over there quickly, before the place gets too cold.

144154.en:
A severe accident has occurred on another station, {[character]player.name}; they suffered a freak blowout in primary life-support, and the station's environmental control shut down entirely. No, don't panic, they stabilized the atmosphere as soon as they could, so the people on the station won't asphyxiate. But the internal heating units have yet to be replaced. People are bundling up as their heat bleeds out – the external insulation is some protection, but it's not enough.

Fortunately for them, we've been developing some hyper-efficient portable heaters here. Donating a bunch will be good publicity for us. It'll also be a good field test for the heaters, and we may get a few preorders from it if people like them. Take these over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and make sure you let them know who donated them.

144156.en: Well, I'm certain we can find someone who values their job more.

144157.en: You're heartless, {[character]player.name}. What about all those people?

144158.en: Have you delivered the heating units yet?

144159.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}! The field-test was invaluable. Turns out the units couldn't handle consistent use for more than 16 hours, something we never tested for in the labs. The next version of the heaters will be much better!

144161.en: The most vital systems on a space station or starship, life-support covers everything from atmosphere generation and recycling to environmental control to the recycling of drinking and pumping water. Originally a series of tanks containing specialized filters, as residence in space extended from long-term to lifetimes, advances in bioengineering developed hydroponics systems for stations which both produce and recycle air and water efficiently. Environmental control, which cycles water and air through the station and maintains an even internal temperature despite the cold of space outside nibbling at the edges, runs off the same generator as the internal electrical circuits. External electrical devices, such as guide-lights, shielding and containment fields, security systems and communications, run from separate generators with extensive backup arrays.

144162.en: One of our planetside subsidiaries has recently lost a lot of farming equipment to a storm. I need you to take these parts to the assembly plant so we can recoup our losses.

144163.en: One of our subsidiaries has recently suffered a major setback, {[character]player.name}. A hurricane wiped out half their planetside crops and wrecked the equipment. Most of it was already falling apart, the storm just finished it off. Obviously, this is a big problem for them, and us, but it's still the early part of the first growing season. Deliver these parts to the assembly plant at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can replace the equipment before they lose too much from this harvest.

144167.en: Have you delivered those parts yet, {[character]player.name}?

144168.en: Thank you for your help, {[character]player.name}. Our subsidiary has managed to save more than they first thought of the initial crops and they're good to go for the second growing season.

144170.en: Despite the increasing popularity of fully-automated hydroponics farms, many planetary economies continue to rely on large-scale land-farming to provide jobs and food for local populations. On particularly fertile worlds even small start-up farms can be instantly successful, but in order to compete with larger farms in the market, these smaller farms frequently approach large corporations, offering to supply certain vital organic produce in exchange for controlling market shares.

144171.en: A Nefantar House is relocating to a planet within the Republic, and we've had a tip-off that they're working against us for someone in the Empire. We've planted surveillance nanobots in a shipment of materials for their planetside home; take it over to the depot. The logs will show nothing amiss.

144172.en:
I hope I can trust you to be discreet, {[character]player.name}.

As part of a goodwill gesture to the Nefantar tribe, the Republic has offered allotments of planetary territory within our space on which to build embassies or summer homes or whatever else they need land for. I don't care what it is, I don't trust ‘em, but the government is determined to make sure we all get along.

Yesterday I got an alert from one of my colleagues; it seems one Nefantar house is in collusion with elements from the Empire. Obviously we can't just point fingers without evidence, but I'm in a perfect position to obtain that. The contractor they hired to design and build a house on their new property is a friend of mine. He's given us one shipment of interior facing materials to seed with nanite spyware. Take the load to the depot at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I know I can trust you to keep quiet about the additions to the cargo.

144173.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. If anyone asks where those came from, the manifest will show their usual station.

144175.en: I'm beginning to question your loyalty, {[character]player.name}.

144176.en: Have you delivered your cargo for me, {[character]player.name}?

144177.en: Thanks to your assistance, {[character]player.name}, we've been able to record some rather incriminating communications from these people already. They wasted no time in contacting their associates in the Empire to let them know they were settled in.

144179.en:
The day Drupar Maak struck down Arkon Ardishapur on Starkman Prime with the Heir's own sceptre began the darkest night for his people. In retribution for the death of his father and their attempted rebellion, Idonis Ardishapur ordered the annihilation of the Starkmanir tribe.

At the same time, the Nefantar tribe approached the Empire with an offer, making a bargain for mercy in exchange for assisting in the subjugation of the Minmatar. The tribe took on many aspects of the Empire, including open practise of their faith and owning Minmatar slaves, themselves. Despite the recent revelation that their conversion helped to protect the last Starkmanir to survive the purge, many within the Republic are hesitant to forgive the Nefantar for their actions.

144180.en: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has a number of outposts in w-space systems, exploring what lies beyond known space. They've turned up some unusual pieces which I need you to take to a more extensive laboratory for identification.

144181.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Hurry up! This could be our biggest breakthrough yet!

144182.en: If it's not worth your time, you could have just said so.

144184.en: I've not received a receipt for the cargo yet, {[character]player.name}.

144185.en: The strangest thing happened when they got all the pieces slotted together: the light inside them stopped flickering and turned blue. We're not certain what that means, since nothing else happened, but it appears to be a sign we're on the right track!

144187.en: Capsuleers aren't the only people to explore the systems accessible via wormholes. Every corporation wants to be the first to make the Next Big Discovery, and then market the developments from researching it. Most corporations will categorically deny that this is what they're doing, creating an atmosphere of both paranoia and plausible deniability if their explorations turn up nothing of value.

144188.en: A small startup that {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has recently invested in has been hired to build a water garden for a Gallente politician, but the frogs he wanted are too dangerous to the fish. Fortunately, there's a variety that are just as ornamental without the side effects. I need you to take them over before we lose our investment.

144189.en:
Yes, yes, perhaps you could help me out.

A well-known politician is having a vacation suite commissioned in another station, and decided that he just could not live without an ornamental water-garden. One of our daughter-companies was hired for the work, and it could be just the break they need to make a name for themselves in the interior design industry.

Thing is, on stations, such gardens need to be self-supporting ecosystems in their own right. He had a load of very pretty frogs shipped in to add color and control the inevitable insect populations, but those lovely little Leina's Darters are also beautifully toxic, and the fish that eat them are dying. We've finally discovered a variety that won't prevent the fish from reproducing. Take this load over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and quickly, before His Honor decides he wants a rock garden instead and we lose our investment.

144191.en: I'm sorry to hear that, {[character]player.name}. I'll just have to find someone else.

144193.en: Have you delivered those frogs yet, {[character]player.name}?

144194.en: Thanks to your work, it looks like Holistic Habitat, LLC is on its way up. The politician can't praise the quality of his water-garden enough.

144196.en: Nothing boasts of a flexible wallet than a private garden within the walls of one's apartment. Society's elite will spend a great deal of money to obtain a perfect replica of the Intaki rainforests or Mannar seaside in which to entertain guests and impress prospective clients. Extra emphasis is placed on making such gardens self-supporting, including specially-engineered fauna to keep the flora happy.

144197.en: Our salvagers have built up a load of industrial-quality scrap metal to be used in ship building. I need you to take it to the reclamation facility so we can recover the useable parts.

144198.en:
Okay, here's one for you. Don't look at me like that. Yes, it's a load of metal scraps we need taken to a reclamation facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Contrary to popular belief, our ships are not made solely of scrap-metal, utility adhesive and chewing gum, but we do recycle extensively.

The reason I'm asking you to do this rather than hiring a much cheaper regular captain is that these bits are industrial quality, or they will be once they've been processed. They're worth a lot of cred on the black market – peanuts to you capsuleers, but a year's wages to anyone else.

144199.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. It's not a glamorous job but someone's gotta do it.

144201.en: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I had hoped you were the reliable sort.

144202.en: Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?

144203.en: Good! You've been a big help, {[character]player.name}.

144205.en:
Since its dawning days, New Eden's landscape has been riddled with conflict, both political and physical. Battles waged and lost have left scars upon planets and littered constellations with floating wrecks. Close to where the Eve Gate lies in Genesis, abandoned stations pose navigational threats to pilots, and many stars are developing orbital rings of human-made space junk.

Despite the risks inherent in a single scrap of metal the size of a man, hurtling through space at just below light-speed – never mind something as vast as a wrecked starship – governments either cannot afford or cannot be bothered to send teams to clean them up. The most dangerous pieces are towed out of the primary space-lanes, then left adrift in deadspace, marked with tracking-beacons. Scavenging is publicly discouraged, though authorities tend to turn a blind eye when various pieces end up on the market. Most of the finds end up in the hands of artists, inventors and archaeologists. One large piece of hull-plating found on the market, still bearing the much-corroded legend MAF Commandant Aurora, was identified as belonging to one of the earliest Gallente interplanetary shuttles, and now forms part of a wall in a museum on Gallente Prime.

144206.en: A friend and I are running a small holoreel bootlegging operation on the side. The shipments are bound for Syndicate, but I only need you to take them on to where my business partner is operating from. The cargo has been disguised as standard holoreels, an effective disguise provided nobody looks too closely at the contents.

144207.en:
I like nice things, {[character]player.name}. Who doesn't? Handing missions out to you people all day doesn't offer nearly enough to cover my expenses, so a friend and I run a shipping business out to Syndicate space. Nothing big enough to interfere with the Syndicate itself, mind you. We provide a humanitarian service importing the latest holos from the heart of civilization. It's the only way they can get the things for a reasonable cost – buying them direct from the companies in the Federation incurs immense shipping charges.

Our usual courier is out of commission today, with her ship in for repairs after a pirate attack. If you want to make yourself useful, take the latest shipment over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and ask for Amelyn. They'll know who you mean, just say that “Imba” sent you.

144208.en: Good, good. Get going, would you?

144209.en: Fine. It's not like anyone would believe you if you told them, anyway.

144210.en: What? Why now? Couldn't you just have refused at the start? Now we'll have to move our operation elsewhere.

144211.en: Amelyn hasn't contacted me yet, {[character]player.name}. What's the hold up?

144214.en: Founded by Intaki exiles after the first Caldari-Gallente war, Syndicate rapidly became a safe haven for criminals and the more unsavoury sorts of businesses which can't operate as freely in Empire space. Anything and everything can be found on the market, including things people would rather not be shared openly. Secrets – both personal and professional – fetch a good price, and the sellers rarely care who the money comes from.

144215.en: A pair of civilians too wealthy for their own good are holding a decadent reception for their wedding, and ordered a tremendously expensive champagne to keep their guests entertained. A regular pilot can't be trusted to ship the drinks in, but what's a thousand-ISK bottle of wine to a capsuleer?

144216.en:
Do you read the gossip rags? I wouldn't expect you to; you capsuleers obviously have greater concerns than who's mocking whom this week. The big news right now is this wedding being planned by Ahvir en Foilien, the former co-star of Under Wraps. He's not been heard from since he got canned as the host of the Sugar Sweep game show, but now he's caused a ruckus by arranging a marriage to the daughter of Material Acquisition bigwig Hemy Selvah. A lot of money obviously changed hands to manage this, since Selvah's daughter isn't quite ten years old, and en Foilien already has a wife, a husband and a few playmates on the side.

If you believe what the tabloids say, that is. Who knows what the truth might be?

En Foilien has arranged a lavish party on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} which is undoubtedly meant to encourage the public and the reporters to overlook the dodgy circumstances and remind them that he used to be important. It doesn't really matter. He's ordered several crates of Feille d'Marnne champagne to loosen them up and assist with the memory loss.

144217.en: Thanks, {[character]player.name}, I knew we could count on you.

144218.en: Fine, I'll find someone else, hopefully before it's too late.

144219.en: I'm not laughing, {[character]player.name}. I have a reputation to maintain, you know.

144220.en: I haven't received a receipt for that champagne yet. What's the hold up?

144221.en: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. That party isn't one the glitterati will soon forget; Selvah's daughter threw her entire glass of champagne in en Foilien's face and called him some very unflattering schoolyard names. Of course it was all caught on camera, and the media is having a field day.

144223.en: Nobody loves a good party more than the Gallente. The hedonistic stereotype is one that the Federation revels in and flaunts shamelessly. Public figures actively compete to host the wildest and most fashionable affairs, vying for the attention of news services and gossip magazines. Among the celebrity elite, a wedding, birth or even a funeral is simply another excuse to splash out and stand in the limelight. Occasionally, an event will be engineered so a falling star can make a desperate final grasp at publicity and salvage a faded career.

144224.en: One of my clients asked me to send over drones to replace the ones his company's been losing in the line of work. That's all he said. He never said anything about needing mining drones; of course I sent him a set of scout drones, and he was very upset at me for not being able to read his mind. People should be more specific about things. Take these mining drones over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for him, and if he asks why the paint looks new, tell him they're fresh off the production line.

144225.en: Just make sure to tell him how sorry I am, okay?

144226.en: Fine. I can always find someone else.

144227.en: I am very disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.

144228.en: Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?

144229.en: Excellent. I've been trying to get those old things off my hands for months.

144230.en: I accidentally sent a client the wrong set of drones because they never specified what type he needed. Take the right cargo to him. Hopefully he won't ask too many questions.

144232.en: The most common mining drone, the Spider Drone, is manufactured by Ishukone. The brainchild of Chief Foreman Jaartu Mediuri in the early days following the first Caldari-Gallente war, the first mining drones were little more than immense strip-mining factories which were deposited on the surface of an asteroid to chew through the surface and process useful minerals until their belly holds were full, then sending an alert to the foreman for uplift and unloading. It wasn't until advances simplified the operation of the mining laser that Mediuri proposed automating a laser and attaching directional thrusters. The project was shelved indefinitely after the initial models failed repeatedly, but after Ishukone headhunted the prodigy roboticist Vayan Hemitaru from Sukuuvestaa, the programme restarted with renewed energy and interest. Eventually a self-powered, mobile mining laser was produced. Some contention was held over its need for basic guidance from an operator, but Ishukone argued that full autonomy was unnecessary, particularly since use of capsule-controlled ships had become common and a capsuleer controller could, through experience and training, more than accommodate for the lack.

144233.en: Planetary officials have asked me to bring in a team of mercenaries they've hired to deal with a terrorist threat. Your job is to keep them in line en route.

144234.en: We have a planetary situation we need your help with. A group of pro-Amarr terrorists is wreaking havoc in outlying provinces, and the local government's hired a group of mercenaries to deal with them. You know mercs, I'm sure; they never really listen to anyone they think is softer than they are. We're having trouble finding an ordinary captain who's willing to ferry the guys over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for transit planetside. I think they'll be more likely to behave if the captain is someone who can and will follow through on a threat to vent the ship to vacuum. Someone like you, in other words. Can we count on you to keep the unruly lot in line?

144235.en: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! Don't actually vent the ship, though. We need these guys.

144236.en: Sad. Now I'll have to find someone else. You were the best option, too.

144237.en: Sad. Now I'll have to find someone else. You were the best option, too.

144238.en: Those mercs aren't giving you too much trouble, I hope.

144239.en: Excellent, {[character]player.name}! I'll let the local government know their solution is on its way.

144241.en:
Despite centuries of enslavement and the systematic erasure of half their culture, some Minmatar advocate a return to “the old ways,” total service the Amarr. Many of these are adherents to the Amarr religion, others are simply willing to do anything for the right pay.

Activism can be as tame as preaching on street-corners or door-to-door, or as extreme as acts of violence and sabotage. The general population of the Republic resents being proselytized and threatened, and in some parts of the Republic clashes have occurred between demonstrators and bystanders. One notable clash on Huggar left 39 dead and hundreds hospitalized for shrapnel wounds and burns.

144242.en: There has been an uprising at one of our slave Labor Reeducation Centers, or LRCs, near a rather large ore mine. The slaves are almost wholly Minmatar, so we cannot afford to have this incident continue for even one more day. The longer it goes on, the greater the chances that some reporter or news agency will get wind of this and splash the story all over the region. Given that the Minmatar Republic may feel compelled to take action to aid their brethren, this can only lead to dire consequences. That, of course, is unacceptable. We do have a plan in place, however, that should end this uprising before it has a chance to truly take root. We need you to transport a large contingent of Riot Interdiction Team (RIT) personnel to a designated station. From there the assembled security teams will join up and embark a small fleet of frigates and cruisers to race to the prison, where they will use all necessary force to terminate this uprising before it gets completely out of control.

144243.en: Bah – I should have known you wouldn't help us. I could tell when I first met you that you were beyond salvation.

144244.en: Good job, pilot. Please make all possible haste to the station as the other teams are waiting on you. The assault phase will begin after you deliver the RIT personnel and their equipment.

144245.en:
The Amarr Empire, realizing many centuries ago that it could not simply work slaves to the point of death, instituted a number of improvements to worker conditions in an effort to prolong the usable lifespan of its slaves. These changes were not universal across the Empire, due in large part to the Empress's unwillingness to create what might have amounted to significant friction between slave -based companies. Therefore, these decisions were largely left to the Five Heirs and their subordinate regional offices. Thus, we can state here that history has shown a lack of consistent application of these worker improvement programs across the Empire. Those Amarr systems that have chosen to incorporate these adaptations have, however, consistently derived greater revenues due to these enhanced and ongoing pacification efforts.

These shortcomings led directly to the establishment of Labor Reeducation Centers (LRC). An LRC is designed much like a multilevel prison, with facilities for low, medium, and high risk inmates. The inmates are those slaves who consistently exhibit defiance or even outright hostility towards the managerial staff at the mine, construction site, or other location to which they are assigned as slave labor. Once we have identified these persons they are immediately removed from their job site and taken to the nearest LRC for corrective behavioral conditioning. This conditioning can include a wide variety of attitude modification methodologies, from intensive drug assisted counseling, to religious indoctrination, and from advanced torture techniques and a concurrent system of rewards - the so-called “carrot and stick approach” - and any number of programs in between. In this way, we break the individual slave's will so that he may be returned to the workforce as a docile and useful component in the labor pool.

144246.en: Bless the Empress – I am very glad to hear you've decided to help. The RIT personnel will meet you in the hangar bay shortly.  Please feel free to take any of our religious literature with you for your enlightenment during the flight.

144247.en: You soulless coward! Without the men you agreed to deliver our assault on the prison will undoubtedly lead to unnecessary casualties on all sides.

144249.en: Our security and military ground forces have been experiencing a slow but steady increase in the numbers and severity of injuries suffered during a wide range of armed conflicts. A recent study by Amarr military scientists has determined that the primary cause of this has been a failure to adequately improve the lightweight body armor worn by millions of our soldiers, Marines, police, and other fighting forces. As fate would have it, one of our intelligence units has obtained what they claim to be a revolutionary new fabric that could provide fifty percent better protection across the board in all types of engagements. We need you to deliver this very sensitive cargo to a station we designate.

144250.en:
Thank you for coming, pilot. As you know, the Amarr Empire is in a constant state of conflict. Our enemies have included organized criminal gangs, drug traffickers, terrorists of every conceivable motivation, pirates, unpacified slave populations, and even the occasional low level skirmish against our fair-weather friends, the Caldari, Gallente, and, lest we forget, the Minmatar. This requires the Empire to always remain vigilant to any situations that may call for the use of force on levels ranging from simple urban pacification to outright military combat. What you do not know is that a high-level internal Empire report has revealed that our casualty levels have been steadily increasing over the last several years, often requiring evacuation to more robust – and already overburdened – medical facilities.

In the “recommendations” section of this report, the researchers concluded that the single most identifiable cause of these excessive casualties is a systemic problem with our lightweight body armor. This armor is standard issue for millions of police and security personnel, as well as our military reconnaissance units.
