Apparently the Navy has been on the lookout for some pilots to hire for various jobs, and they want some background info. That's why I couldn't just send this information via a transmission: Caldari law prohibits doing that with personal information since such transmissions can be hacked.

If you do the job for me, I'll give you a nice reward. And even a bonus if you get it done quickly.

144415.en:
I'm supposed to transport these reports to the Caldari Navy station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, but I really have a tight schedule at the moment. The contents of the reports are confidential, something about the new recruits we've been getting. Apparently the Navy has been on the lookout for some pilots to hire for various jobs, and they want some background info. That's why I couldn't just send this information via a transmission: Caldari law prohibits doing that with personal information since such transmissions can be hacked.

If you do the job for me, I'll give you a nice reward. And even a bonus if you get it done quickly!

144416.en: Looks like there was some kind of explosion on a colony in this system, and thousands of people are without a home. I want you to take some of them over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can do our part in providing shelter for less fortunate people.

144417.en: Looks like there was some kind of explosion on a colony in this system, and thousands of people are without a home. I want you to take some of them over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can do our part in providing shelter for less fortunate people.

144418.en: We have received word that the extraction team has taken delivery of your cargo and is now en route to the planet. Given the speed with which you delivered this essential shipment, we assess a high likelihood that the stranded team will be safely extracted. Well done!

144419.en: We have received word that the extraction team has taken delivery of your cargo and is now en route to the planet. Given the speed with which you delivered this essential shipment, we assess a high likelihood that the stranded team will be safely extracted. Well done!

144420.en:
The bank manager at the local State and Region vault has heard some worrying rumors that some thugs are planning a run on his bank. He is in no position to investigate the matter himself, so he sent for the cavalry. The Caldari Navy, that is. I was sent here by the Navy to check out the validity of these rumors. I haven't dug up anything of interest yet, but just to be on the safe side I'd like to put some heat on the bandits roaming in the area. I've asked my buddy Jali Tanaka to help me out too, but he's busy setting up a surveillance system, so I don't want to take too much of his time.

The Kazka bandits over in Sakkikainen seem like likely candidates for this sort of an operation. I don't know for sure, but it doesn't hurt to stir things up a little. You seem like a hardy pilot more than capable of roughing them up a bit. How about you get in there all guns blazing and bring me back, say, 30 drifter spurs? That should shake them up, hopefully enough for one of them to spill his beans into the wrong ear.

Finally, be very careful. The Kazka bandits are rough. Make sure you only target their grunts, the others are too tough to be worth the hassle.

144421.en: You found him!  I'll notify his family immediately.  I'll also report our success here directly to my contact in The Scope. Thank you for your assistance.

144422.en:
As you know, there are many hundreds of thousands of Minmatar slaves working to provide essential services to the Empire, just as they have for centuries. Given their considerable natural physical abilities, they have always made up one of the most important and valuable ethnic groups within the vast Amarr slave workforce. One unavoidable consequence of this, however, is that we have had to invest a considerable amount of money, not only in the health and welfare of these slaves, but also to ensure their obedience.

One important aspect of this latter effort has been the establishment of Labor Reeducation Centers, or LRC's, which are designed to house some of the more problematic slaves in order to facilitate their eventual return to the workforce. In recent months, however, there has been a significant increase in violent disobedience at certain LRC's, with some of the more severe instances leading to near-riots.

Our immediate problem is that one of these facilities, LRC-12A, has been taken over during just such an uprising. The slaves have reportedly killed and injured dozens of our personnel and taken the remainder hostage. They are demanding the immediate release of their fellow slaves at a nearby Amarr mining operation, along with transportation to a destination of their choosing. We have, so far, managed to keep this incident quiet; if the Minmatar Republic leadership were to learn of this, it could very easily lead to much more severe consequences for both races. The only way to ensure this does not happen is through the immediate application of overwhelming force.

Therefore, we need you to deliver a large contingent of specially trained Riot Interdiction Teams to a nearby station, from which they will join up with other security elements for final transportation to LRC-12A. Will you assist us?

144423.en: The teams have begun to embark on a small fleet of frigates and cruisers for LRC-12A. With this amount of men and lethal weaponry, there is no doubt that we shall prevail!

144424.en: The teams have begun to embark on a small fleet of frigates and cruisers for LRC-12A. With this amount of men and lethal weaponry, there is no doubt that we shall prevail!

144426.en: Good. We appreciate your assistance in this matter. Please ensure this operation continues to enjoy the level of security that we've been able to sustain so far. Make no stops, scheduled or unscheduled, between this station and the final destination.

144427.en: Good. We appreciate your assistance in this matter. Please ensure this operation continues to enjoy the level of security that we've been able to sustain so far. Make no stops, scheduled or unscheduled, between this station and the final destination.

144429.en:
Our engineering scientists, working at our highly secure, clandestine R&D facility on a nearby planet have produced a new type of cloaking device that, when fitted to Covert Ops ships, could theoretically enable them to jump through stargates without uncloaking! And yes, I can see by the look on your face that you must think I've had far too many Extra Strength Quafe sodas today. However, I can assure you that, while it may be many years before this technology is perfected and suitable for even experimental use, the science behind it is quite real, and this is where this story takes a very important twist.

Our internal security teams have managed to uncover a plan formulated by one of our competitors to steal the prototype cloaking system at some point between the time it leaves the lab up until it arrives at the field testing facility over in the next system. Problem is, we don't yet know who the spy is, so we devised a plan to get that spy to expose himself so that we can then move in and make the arrest.

To this end, you will be delivering is a very detailed mock-up series of the actual prototype, one that will withstand an initial visual and electronic scrutiny on the part of the thief. In all practical terms, however, these devices could no more cloak a ship than it could cook your morning breakfast. We are naming this event Operation Doorstop, which is our planning team's attempt at humor, given the uselessness of this particular lump of metal and wires. What we do need, though, is your absolute confidentiality on this shipment. If the spy gets any whiff that this is a set-up, we will likely never know who he or she is, and we will remain at ongoing risk of one of our most important R&D projects potentially falling into the wrong hands.

So, what do you say, {[character]player.name}? Willing to take on this rather interesting assignment?

144432.en: One of our R&D facilities has been working hard to produce a new type of cloaking device for Covert Ops vessels that will allow those ships to remain cloaked while jumping stargates. However, it has recently been brought to our attention that a corporate espionage agent sent by a rival company is targeting this new technology, for obvious reasons. In order to flush him out and arrest him, however, we need to catch him in the act. So, we are asking you to transport a decoy prototype cloaking device from this station to one we designate. With such a juicy target, we feel the spy will not be able to resist making an attempt to steal is somewhere between here and there. We need you to fly this device to that station utilizing absolute secrecy.

144433.en: That is very good news, thank you. With your permission, we will begin loading pallets of the Ditanium plates into your hangar.

144434.en: That is very good news, thank you. With your permission, we will begin loading pallets of the Ditanium plates into your hangar.

144448.en: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s R&D branch has been working on more efficient version of the inertial compensator units used in starship propulsion systems. I need you to take the latest batch to the testing facility.

144449.en: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s R&D branch has been working on a more efficient version of Carbon-86 epoxy resin. I need you to take the latest batch to the testing facility.

144450.en: Federation R&D specialists have been working to find counters for Caldari military tactics; the latest development is a special type of ammunition that works similarly to a lock breaker bomb, but on a single target. I want you to take it over to a navy base for testing, and you need to keep word of this development from going very far.

144451.en: Federation R&D specialists have been working to find counters for Caldari military tactics; the latest development is a special type of ammunition that works similarly to a lock breaker bomb, but on a single target. I want you to take it over to a navy base for testing, and you need to keep word of this development from going very far.

144452.en:
Yes, I have some work for you.

We have several research outposts in various w-space systems. It's common, one of those things that nobody discusses but everybody knows about anyway. A while ago, they recovered bits of ancient technology which seemed to have unusual properties.. We thought for a while it might be some sort of Sleeper computer core, but now it appears to be Talocan in origin. Another of our laboratories has more pieces, and they're suggesting it's actually the core of a station's life-support system, with multiple redundant modules that can back each other up and be easily replaced if they fail. They're setting up to test their theory right now at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I need you to take our samples over so they can complete the network they've pieced together.

144453.en: That is very good to hear, thank you. We will transfer the cargo to your hangar immediately, along with a small element of the intelligence team, who have stated that they will provide security through to the final destination station. You'd best head to your ship quickly, as I wouldn't want those guys on board my ship without an escort, especially as the rather unique weapons they usually carry are easily capable of punching a nice little hole in your hull.

144454.en: That is very good to hear, thank you. We will transfer the cargo to your hangar immediately, along with a small element of the intelligence team, who have stated that they will provide security through to the final destination station. You'd best head to your ship quickly, as I wouldn't want those guys on board my ship without an escort, especially as the rather unique weapons they usually carry are easily capable of punching a nice little hole in your hull.

144455.en:
As you probably know all too well, speed is the lifeblood of the Republic's defense fleets, particularly for the smaller frigates and cruisers. There's a lot that goes into it: low-density reactor cores, kinesthetic maneuvering thrusters, hyper-responsive gyroscopic stabilizers. All the housings are built using nano-alloy rather than the more heavyweight materials the other empires use; it was simply more convenient back when the ships were first designed, but it gives them that little bit of extra boost that's become our signature.

Our R&D specialists have been working on a new formula for the C-86 thermal epoxy resin used on engine housings and other parts of the propulsion systems; I want you to take this batch over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for application and field testing.

144456.en:
As you probably know all too well, speed is the lifeblood of the Republic's defense fleets, particularly for the smaller frigates and cruisers. There's a lot that goes into it: low-density reactor engines, kinesthetic maneuvering thrusters, hyper-responsive gyroscopic stabilizers. All the housings are built using nanofiber rather than the more heavyweight materials the other empires use; it was simply more conveniently available back when the ships were first designed, but it gives them that little bit of extra boost that's become our signature.

The lighter construction does have the drawback of making the systems more fragile. Our R&D specialists have been working on a more efficient design for the inertial compensators which keep the drive components from shaking themselves to bits; I want you to take this batch over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for application and field testing.

144457.en: See, I told you this would be a smooth run. Customs and the police have been advised that you will be transiting their space and that you are not to be disturbed. Have a safe flight. Hell, you can practically autopilot this one!

144458.en: See, I told you this would be a smooth run. Customs and the police have been advised that you will be transiting their space and that you are not to be disturbed. Have a safe flight. Hell, you can practically autopilot this one!

144459.en: We are escalating our production so we can increase our military strength in light of recent political upheavals in the world. Increased production requires more minerals. I want you to get {[item]objectiveTypeID.quantityName, quantity=objectiveQuantity} to one of our main production facilities. Your help will undoubtedly get a positive response from other corporate members.

144460.en: Great! Your achievements for us have not gone unnoticed.

144461.en: We are escalating our production so we can increase our military strength in light of recent political upheavals in the world. Increased production requires more minerals. I want you to get {[item]objectiveTypeID.quantityName, quantity=objectiveQuantity} to one of our main production facilities. Your help will undoubtedly get a positive response from other corporate members.

144462.en: Thank you for agreeing to help us. We will have the quantrium moved into your item hangar as soon as possible. You have already been cleared for emergency departure.

144463.en: Thank you for agreeing to help us. We will have the quantrium moved into your item hangar as soon as possible. You have already been cleared for emergency departure.

144464.en:
Ah, {[character]player.name}! It is good to see there are freelancers who still maintain some loyalty to the Federation. It pleases me greatly that capsuleers like yourself still prove willing to help us out at need. Anyway, if you are looking for something to do, I know a little job that might just mix profit with pleasure.

The Serpentis are setting up a little shop in this area where they are training their fighters, intending to bring them into the tournament. Now, we aren't afraid of a little competition, but these fighters aren't all-natural, if you know what I mean. We're going to need them kidnapped and brought back here. Chances are you're going to find the substance the Serps have been feeding their fighters as well, and I know some people who are very interested to see it recovered. Purely for research, of course. I wouldn't dream of touching the stuff myself....

OK, OK, so maybe years ago when I was younger I might have tried some, but everyone experiments a little. No harm in that. Right? Just don't let me find out that you've kept a little for yourself. I need ... I mean, I want it all. To give to our researchers, of course. Ahem. Yes.

So, well, before you go ... listen, I would appreciate it if you could keep this matter to yourself. I'm sure you'll agree that not everybody needs to know about this, hm?

144465.en:
Thanks for meeting me in person, {[character]player.name}. We have a problem: My superiors have transcripts of our earlier communication and know about the drugs you brought back. It's okay, though, they've given me a chance to get rid of the stuff.

I need you to head out to Q-UA3C. The Serps have had a small shipping checkpoint there for a while, one which our investigative reporters have been monitoring for a big exposé on the way Serpentis supply chains work. Since my bosses want this little "mistake" of mine rectified quietly in order to prevent a scandal, they want the drugs taken there and the outpost destroyed. And that's what will happen.

Between you and me, though, I can't stand the idea of letting such a valuable commodity go to waste. So what I want you to do is head out there and kill everything you see, but leave the drug disposal to me. I'll convince my superiors and anyone else who asks that the drugs were destroyed at the outpost, and everyone will be happy ? at least, assuming that you can keep this a secret. And that is what you will do, I trust.

144469.en:
We have data sheets miles long on the Gallenteans. While a lot of it is complete crap, it does give us good information on their typical ship load outs, including the ships flown by pirate groups working in Gallente space, such as the Serpentis.

Serpentis ships favor Kinetic and Thermal weapons, so be prepared for that. Their armor is tough, but cannot turn a point: Using an ammo type that does Kinetic damage should do the trick. Scourge light missiles or rockets work well.

144470.en:
The Amarrians were busy out here. It seems they were up to a lot more than just scouting. One of their missions was apparently to place mines along some of our major shipping routes. {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, in particular, is full of the blasted things, and we've got a convoy coming through within four standard hours. We need to get someone to both systems and clear out those mines!

These "mines" are quite something, though. They are highly explosive proximity charges built into structures, but when they blow, they also launch a bunch of drones into space to finish off anything not torn entirely apart by the explosion. It's a tough job, but if they're not cleared by the time the convoy gets there, our people are in serious trouble.

144471.en: The Amarrians now know that we're manufacturing high-tech EMP smart bombs in this vicinity. They can't attack this station -- it's too well defended -- but they also know we need Mexallon to produce the bombs, and they are trying to cut off our supply. We need you to deliver some Mexallon to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.

144472.en:
We recently found a number of new mining fields in adjacent systems, and the usual assortment of pirate trash has come out of the woodwork to exploit it. We'll need them mined soon because even those thieving bastards have friends in places high enough to put the legal status of these sites in doubt. For some reason they've taken an interest even in Banidine, too, and we'll need to find out why; all my workers are busy with the more profitable fields, but I'm not taking any chances.

I'm uploading a bookmark to your People & Places databank; it shows the location of a Banidine mining operation. I need you to head out there and mine all the Banidine. Should be 18,000 units, my foreman tells me. Once we've made an undisputed claim, we're free to mine there again without interference, and I'll provide you with a little something for your trouble.

144473.en:
My boss wants Banidine; something to do with manufacturing cheaper parts for refrigeration units or something. I don't know. Point is, he's made it my job to get the ore. And now I'm makin' it your job.

There's a few Banidine rocks out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enough for 20,000 units, the scouts tell me. Go out there, mine it, bring it back. Should be easy enough, right?

144474.en:
We've gotten word of the location of a bunch of Mercium ore here in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but we believe that our information has also been leaked to other factions, including the Gallenteans. It's vital that you collect all the Mercium: It cannot be allowed to fall into enemy hands.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

144475.en: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

144476.en: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

144477.en: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

144478.en:
We've found an old mining post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. But, the thing is, we can't find who used to own it: There are no records of its being built or even existing. It's simply empty. No sign of anyone left there, dead or otherwise. Our initial investigation found extensive fire damage, gas leaks; you name it, it went wrong. Lots of explosive damage, though we can't tell if that was accidental or intentional. And some marks... well, we just don't know what could do that to metal. It's damn creepy, that's for sure.

Anyway, near as we can tell, the miners were working on a large Lyavite deposit. They didn't finish, because there's still about 5,000 units of it at the site. Now, I know Lyavite isn't the most popular rock, but nobody just leaves that much ore lying around. And besides, the brains at the lab figure they can use the stuff for some of their research, so this opportunity is too good to pass up.

That's where you come in. Warp in, mine the Lyavite, and warp out. It's that easy.

144479.en: You've heard of Parriaval Mastes, the infamous troublemaker? Well, he's escaped from the prison camp where he was held. We need someone to locate him and bring him back here discreetly. If word of his escape gets out, political dissidents from all across the Empire will start causing trouble. Fortunately, we've tracked the ship he stole and located its signal at a suspected terrorists' outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Are you willing to fly out there and retrieve him? There's a significant reward.

144480.en:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places, go to Bookmarks, right-click on this mission objective, and choose "Set destination." Then go to your Ship Control Panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click again on this mission, and select "Warp to location." Once you've arrived at the fugitive's location, you'll see him as a red target icon on your Overview. Engage and destroy his ship. Once the fugitive's vessel has been destroyed, a cargo container will eject from it. This is Parriaval's escape capsule. Once you're within 2,500 meters, right-click on the cargo container and select "Open" (or use the "Open" icon above your Overview). A window will now open displaying the contents: Click and hold the prisoner and drag him into your cargo hold.

Congratulations, you've recaptured Parriaval Mastes! Now return to {[character]agentID.name} for your reward.

144485.en:
Since we've drawn so much attention to the plight of the Matari, there's been a news leak: one of the slave colonies has staged a rebellion. Now, the Amarr always respond to rebellion with brute force, so those people are pretty much doomed. But we can save them, and still make it look like they all perished once again at the hands of the Amarrians.

Destroy the mining colony before the Amarrians do, and bring the survivors back here for safekeeping.

144486.en: Trade is a booming industry. Humanity is spread out over such a vast area of space that everything is rare somewhere, and there's always someone willing to make that journey for a profit, however small.

144487.en:
Unbeknownst to us, a botanist here named Horei Falcosis took one of the seeds for examination before you shipped the package; a short time ago, as he worked with it, it shot out a tendril and sank it into his flesh. It was several minutes before he was discovered, and by that time, the seed's tendrils had penetrated his body in several locations. Falcosis was unconscious by this time, and the seed had pulled itself close to his body and started to secrete a protective resin.

Sadly, this station does not have the proper facilities to care for him. And since this tree has now been designated noxious and dangerous--the other seeds were all incinerated safely, I understand--Falcosis has been placed in cryogenic stasis for transport.

Deliver him to the station I've included in the mission details, would you?

144488.en: We couldn't wait for you any longer. We sent someone else after the book. Because of your delay, it will now be months before we can reclaim that part of the station, if not the whole thing. Who knows?

144489.en: We couldn't wait for you any longer. We sent someone else after the book. Because of your delay, it will now be months before we can reclaim that part of the station, if not the whole thing. Who knows?

144490.en:
No doubt you've see that little furrier that's been bouncing around the station for the last few days, {[character]player.name}? You haven't? Well, I certainly have. Nasty little creature. It bites, you know.

In any event, it was part of a shipment of exotic pets intended for delivery to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, but it got left behind because I spilled a drink all over the cargo manifest. We need someone to take this furrier, special delivery, over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and get it the hell out of our hair. We need a special pilot, a pilot with skill and daring, a pilot who doesn't know the meaning of the word "fear"… and who isn't allergic to furriers. You interested?

144491.en:
One of the functions of my job is to ensure things operate smoothly in this region. I have a number of informants that keep me in the loop of the less visible happenings. They tend to be skittish by nature, but recently one of my informants was noticeably shaken. He won't send the information, and he won't meet me in person. He's insisted that I send a third party to pick up the data.

Normally I'd just find another informant, but this one was on the trail of a particularly virulent heretic. The man can't be anything but mad--he calls himself The Crackpot, for one thing--but it's damned hard to track a madman. He's been attracting attention, even followers from among the weak-minded, and it's long past time to put a stop to his nonsense.

If you'll go and pick up that data, it could help us track this menace down.

144492.en: {[character]player.name}, because of your inaction, the drone swarm found the Banidine. This rare mineral is now even rarer because you let those automatons get to it first, and that can't be good for any of us.

144493.en:
It's not a well-kept secret that as rogue drones get more advanced, they're becoming more unpredictable. Talk to any seasoned pod pilot and they'll tell you about the dozens of rogue drones they've had to fight off just in the course of their regular business. Even more disturbing are reports of drone hives, massive constructs of debris that no one can quite figure out, but which are always full of haywire drones.

So what's their interest in Banidine? Who knows?! Most humans don't go looking for the stuff: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother giving it its own entry in their mining packages when they produce ship scanners. (If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in the mission details in your Opportunity interface entry and select "Add to Overview.")

So, again, why the interest from the drones? Well, none but the drones can say, and they're not talking. Suffice to say that their interest can't mean anything good for the humans that share their space.

144494.en:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} wants a massive shipment of Augumene right away, so we need you to get out there and bring some back. They seem to think they might be able to find some use for the stuff for chemical warfare, I guess? But that's just between you and me, right?

Anyway, I've been looking for a miner who's experienced enough, with the right kind of ship, and maybe you fit the bill. Time is critical on this one. There's a big bonus for you if you can bring it in fast enough.

Seriously, we need a mountain of this stuff, so get on it. I've uploaded the location to your People & Places databank.

144495.en: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions that more than negate any profit to be made from refining the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

144496.en: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions — which more than negates any profit to be made from reprocessing the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

144497.en:
Turns out someone got the bright idea that if mining drones mine more ore, bigger drones would mine even more ore. This guy's team slapped some mining drone's AI into non-regulation heavy combat units and threw some mining lasers on. He even hacked the firmware so that the mining brains could control the weaponry, making some sort of self-sufficient mining machines.

Now there's a bunch of haywire drones zipping about this rare mineral that we want. Our guys in the lab need it for research, I guess. The drones aren't even mining the rock, last I heard, but they have tried to bore through any ship we send out there....

It's getting ridiculous. If you can, get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, neutralize the drones, and bring back all the Mercium; we'll pay you well for your efforts.

144498.en: Someone else got to the Mercium before we did; most likely those drones, which have also disappeared. You better start getting on the ball.

144499.en:
Mine 20 units of Crystalline Icicles. Oh, and watch out for pirates or rogue drones. Lots of them around these parts.

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Crystalline Icicles ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

144500.en:
Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, a respected Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, and hence unmanned.

Unfortunately, the drones became unruly, then unmanageable, and soon developed the ability to "infect" other drones, and eventually even ships, with their capricious artificial intelligence. Needless to say, Gallente soon abandoned this line of research.

144501.en:
Drones scare the daylights out of some people. To be completely honest, the big hives even scare me a little. The smaller drone groups are annoying, but more manageable. Usually.

Anyway, there's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting these wild drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. So the best solution is to just remove the cloud: no cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.

144502.en: Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.

144503.en:
Well, we've located some asteroids that contain substantial amounts of Polygypsum. It's a comparatively rare mineral, and almost completely unknown in this system. Our guys want to have a look at the stuff and see if they can figure out some way to make use of it; however, we don't have anyone who wants to deal with the stuff. So guess who I thought of first?

You'll need to grab all 2,800 units of the stuff and get it back here. So what do you think? Are you in?

144504.en:
Polygypsum is widely considered worthless because of the dangers associated with storing and reprocessing it. As a result, you won't find this ore on the market. In fact, for this reason, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother putting it as a unique entry in the computers when they install standard ship scanners.

If you're having trouble finding the correct ore at the mission location, you can right-click the "Polygypsum" icon in the mission details in your Opportunities interface and select "Add to Overview."

144505.en:
No, no. There are no Gallente. It's those cursed rogue drones. If the Gallente hadn't made those things way back during the Caldari-Gallente War, I wouldn't have this headache to deal with.

Here's the odd thing: There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. The best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.

144506.en: Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.

144507.en: I'm afraid that my datapad went missing on your watch, {[character]player.name}. It is an unfortunate thing, very unfortunate indeed. I'm afraid, also, that I'll have to hold you responsible for its contents and any action--or in this case, inaction--they might have inspired.

144514.en:
Following the widespread release of cloning technology, as it became both financially viable and CONCORD-sanctioned, Zainou Biotech enjoyed a period of unprecedented profits. Securing almost one third of the market share in clone sales, the corporation was set to become one of the most important Caldari corporations in the cluster, which would only have added further influence to its parent company, Ishukone.

In those days, Zainou handled all cloning, though, then as today, only the fabulously wealthy could afford the technology. However, since the event known as the "Insorum Imbroglio," when Zainou lost the trust of the other State corporations, the CEP has mandated that the highest levels of office and those of great value to the State would have their clones stored in other facilities.

Little is known about these cloning centers. Details such as their number, location, staff, administrative structure, and resources all remain closely guarded secrets.

144516.en: I'm afraid that my datapad went missing on your watch, {[character]player.name}. It is an unfortunate thing, very unfortunate indeed. I'm afraid, also, that I'll have to hold you responsible for its contents and any action--or in this case, inaction--they might have inspired.

144517.en: I'm afraid that my datapad went missing on your watch, {[character]player.name}. It is an unfortunate thing, very unfortunate indeed. I'm afraid, also, that I'll have to hold you responsible for its contents and any action--or in this case, inaction--they might have inspired.

144518.en:
There's been an increase in Caldari activity in surrounding systems. We think those self-righteous bastards might be up to something. Of course, that's nothing new.

We've placed passive reconnaissance units in several nearby locations, but we don't want any direct transmissions from them for fear of attracting Caldari attention. So we've decided to dispatch "unofficial" vessels like yours to pick up the data chips from their base and bring them back here. The Caldari are less likely to suspect--or at least less likely to interfere with--a capsuleer, so they should leave you alone.

If you do get jumped, however, remember that the recon unit is the top priority. Get it out of there if you can. Do it fast and there'll be a substantial bonus.

144519.en:
A number of the mega-corporations have joined together to produce SPLET: the State Personnel Life Enrichment Tour.

The first thing we need is food, and there are crates of frozen food waiting not too far from here. Bring the food here so our chefs can start to figure out how to stretch it into an appropriately festive-- but still economical-- dish.

144520.en:
One of our intelligence technicians has gone rogue. He isn't a very high-level operator, but he has access to some sensitive passwords, code keys, and patrol routes. We think he was bought off by the Caldari and is headed out of system.

We've located him in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and we need someone to stop him and grab his ship's log if possible. It may contain information about his destination and, more importantly, about who recruited him. It's an important mission.

144521.en:
One of our intelligence technicians has gone rogue. He isn't a very high-level operator, but he has access to some sensitive passwords, code keys, and patrol routes. We think he was bought off by the Caldari and is headed out of system.

We've located him in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and we need someone to stop him and grab his ship's log if possible. It may contain information about his destination and, more importantly, about who recruited him. It's an important mission. Are you game?

144522.en:
There has been an outbreak of commerce raiding in this sector. We strongly suspect the Caldari are behind it, either directly or through proxies such as Mordu's Legion. They've hit a convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but there was too much cargo for them to loot immediately. We suspect that they'll be returning in a few hours with a transport and some escorts.

We want to strike back, but also to learn something about who these raiders are and whether the Caldari are really behind the attacks. Take out the transport and escorts when they arrive in-system, and return to us with any logs or transponders you're able to recover. The lost cargo is yours if you want it. Insurance has already covered those losses, so consider that a little extra bonus for yourself.

144523.en:
There's been an outbreak of commerce raiding in this sector. We strongly suspect the Caldari are behind it, either directly or through something like Mordu's Legion. Whoever it is, they've hit a convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but it seems there was too much cargo for them to loot immediately. We suspect that they'll be returning in a few hours with a transport and some escorts.

We want to strike back, of course, but also to learn something about who these raiders are and whether the Caldari are really behind the attacks. Take out the transport and escorts when they arrive in-system, and return to us with any logs or transponders you're able to recover.

Take these guys down and we'll make it worth your time. You might even get a piece of the action if we find out who's behind the raids. The lost cargo is also yours if you want it. Insurance has already covered those losses, so consider that a little extra bonus for yourself.

144524.en:
There's a Caldari supply depot located at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that we want destroyed. We can't offer you much support, but we know you don't really need it. That's why we're sending you in, and not some Navy rookie. We want the Caldari to know that we can cause them grief with only a single ship. It doesn't take us a whole fleet.

I won't lie, it's risky.The depot is likely to be guarded, and they may send reinforcements once the action begins.

144525.en:
An Amarrian slaver has found a way to hack the Egonics signal, at least at short range. Security cameras in a nearby station show hundreds of people--all of them wearing Egonics devices--simply walking into the cargohold of an Amarrian Bestower. It wasn't until after the ship had departed the station and the missing persons reports starting coming in that we realized anything was amiss. Security found that this Amarrian "citizen" had inserted subliminal commands into the Egonics signals at the station.

If you can get all of those citizens back, there's a big reward for you.

There are over 1,000 people missing. You will need a large cargo capacity to carry them all at once, unless you intend to make multiple runs to the deadspace location where the Amarrain ship is located.

144526.en:
There's a flotilla of Amarrian ships operating illegally out of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We need you to go take them out. Leave as much wreckage as you can so the Empire can't deny its actions in our space.

Now, we're not sure how many fleet resources they have in the region, so it might be a tough fight. A real tough fight.

144527.en:
A short time ago, Minmatar terrorists in a combined fleet of frigates and cruisers attacked one of our Harbinger-class battlecruisers as it was transporting slaves from a recently closed mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in a nearby system. While all but one of the attackers was annihilated, our convoy's escorts were destroyed and our cruiser is burning. Making a bad situation worse, we are anticipating that the terrorists will return in force within the next several hours to attempt the theft of our slaves, as they almost certainly know the cruiser is alone and all but helpless.

Our concern is that if the terrorists feel that they have a window of opportunity to recover these slaves, it is likely that they will throw everything they have into the effort. Our intelligence assessments of the terrorists' fleet assets are even less reassuring: we believe that they could send as many as four battlecruisers into this fight – more than enough to wipe out the arriving frigates and forcefully board our heavily damaged strategic cruiser. However, we have calculated that if we can delay any terrorist boarding parties long enough, this should give us enough time for the much larger main rescue fleet to arrive.

The only bright side to this situation, in what is unquestionably an act of divine providence, is that a large contingent of marines are aboard this station as we speak, having just completed specialized refresher training in counter-boarding operations. We need you to deliver them to the station closest to the last reported position of our cruiser. From there, we will transport a combined team of marines, engineers, medics, and other essential personnel to hopefully stop the fire and save the ship - along with its cargo of highly valuable slaves. However, this mission must be undertaken immediately. Any delay will surely doom the Harbinger and her brave crew.

144528.en: While transporting Minmatar slaves from a recently close ore mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in nearby system, the convoy was attacked by terrorists, destroying the escort frigates and heavily damaging the Harbinger-class battlecruiser carrying the slaves. We believe it is likely that the terrorists will return, and in larger ships, to attempt a rescue of the slaves before we can respond with reinforcements. The window of opportunity for the terrorists is short, so it is imperative that we immediately render as much help as possible. What we need you to do is deliver a contingent of heavily armed marines recently trained in counter-boarding operations to a station closer to the site of the battle. From there, they will join other Amarr military and rescue teams for immediate transportation to the damaged cruiser.

144529.en:
{[character]player.name}! Glad you could make it on such short notice. Let me get right to the point: Yesterday, as you almost certainly know, a regional governor delivered her State of the Region address. Needless to say, we were quite excited and thus put forth a maximum effort to ensure that her speech was broadcast on every possible channel and to the maximum ranges of our civilian and military communications networks.

However, for various reasons at many remote locations, this signal did not reach many who would have otherwise benefitted from this opportunity. For all our efforts, there are some locations that can only be reached the hard way -- ferrying holoreels directly to each and every one of them. We have already dispatched messengers, primarily in interceptors and other fast ships, to these more dangerous destinations.

We need you to transport a quantity of holoreels containing the State of the Region speech to one station in particular and hand them over to an agent who will be waiting for them there. He will then handle all further distribution of the 'reels.

So, can you help us with what should be a straightforward courier job?

144530.en: The regional governor herself delivered an important State of the Region speech yesterday to all her billions of faithful followers. Due to technical problems, however, this message did not reach as many citizens as it should have. Fortunately, we have managed to correct this rather quickly through dispatching a small fleet of interceptors to the problem locations. We need you, however, to take a shipment of holoreels to the station we designate, as our usual contact there is indisposed at the moment and may not be available for some time. When you deliver these to that station, our contact's second-in-command will take charge of the cargo and facilitate further broadcasting.

144531.en: Thank you so very much, {[character]player.name}. The Amarr representative has already informed us that he is offloading the holoreels as we speak. We will not forget this service to the Empire.

144532.en: I must say we are quite disappointed. As you know, all of our pilots are gone, taking these 'reels to the faithful. Your refusal leaves a gap in this coverage that will leave many faithful Amarr without this important message from the governor.

144537.en:
Impetus is considering putting out a new holoreel about the enslaved Matari. Now that people think the Amarr would rather blow up CONCORD ships than allow the public to see how slaves are treated, there's talk of a major project, not just a documentary. This is exactly what we need!

News and documentaries are useful, but this would really reach the public. The average person needs things black and white, and that's what holos are for.

This is the last thing I'm going to ask of you, and it won't be easy. Since we've drawn so much attention to the plight of the Matari, there's been a news leak: one of the slave colonies has staged a rebellion. Now, the Amarr always respond to rebellion with brute force, so those people are pretty much doomed.

But we can save them--at least a good number of them--and still make it look like they all perished, once again at the hands of the Amarrians. And it's unlikely Amarr will even bother to deny responsibility since everyone knows they'd destroy the whole colony anyway. Remember, if you leave it to the Amarr to destroy the colony themselves, those Matari will only suffer further torture and degradation, and then be killed anyway.

Can you do this final task for the cause?

144538.en:
The corporations of the State have many friends, as you know... many friends in many interesting and useful places. Why is this relevant, you ask? Well, it's not at all… it was merely an idle thought I had today that I wanted to impart upon you.

But actually, now I come to think about the topic of friends… I am reminded of a particular friend of mine in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them. But it would be very, er, helpful... for me--for us--if this friend of ours were to get what he wants.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, with all the random third party violence these days, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Right. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I better go and lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

144539.en:
It's those damn Gallente, what else!? They're not even trying to maintain the appearance of peace between us anymore! I'm deadly serious, {[character]player.name}. If this isn't a direct act to provoke all-out war, then I don't know what is. We are dealing with a blatant assault on one of our most important facilities, right within our own borders!

Alright, here's the deal: They've somehow discovered one of our secret cloning facilities, and I'm told their orders to attack it have come from the most senior of Federation military officials.

I can't stress enough the importance of this mission. If those clone bays go down, we'll have a huge problem on our hands. Hell, for all we know this could be only the first step before key individuals are targeted, without clones to save them. I don't have the clearance to know exactly whose clones are being stored where, nor if they are the only copies. All I know is that they are holding important people, very important.

You need to fly over there immediately, and destroy any and all hostiles you see. Once the facility is secure, we can send in the relocation fleet and move it all safely away. You must move quickly, though! This initial force is undoubtedly just the scouting party since they're not attacking the facility yet. We need them cleared out before we have a fleet of Navy Moros besieging the facility.

If we can't trust you with this, {[character]player.name}, then I don't know who we can trust anymore.

144540.en:
We've got some more information from the data you brought back. It seems that these enemies are indeed Mordu's Legion, with their squadron insignia obscured. That means the Caldari are likely behind the raids and we need to send them a message that we know about it.

There's a Caldari supply depot located at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that we want destroyed. We can't offer you much support, but we know you don't really need it. That's why we're sending you in, and not some Navy rookie. We want the Caldari to know that we can cause them grief with only a single ship. It doesn't take us a whole fleet.

So, you want to go in? I won't lie, it's risky--the depot is likely to be guarded, and they may send reinforcements once the action begins.

144541.en:
There's been a lot of Amarrian activity along the frontier lately. We think they're preparing for war with the Minmatar, but there's no love lost between them and us, as you know. Or perhaps they want to start a conflict that will involve all four major powers. We can't say.

What we do know is that there is a flotilla of Amarrian ships operating out of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. To avoid the political confrontation, we'd been leaving them alone until now, but they've been snooping where they aren't welcome, and we think they may even be raiding some of our supply convoys. We need you to go take them out--leave as much wreckage as you can so the Empire can't deny it had an illegal military outpost in our space.

Now, we're not sure how many fleet resources they have in the region, so it might be a tough fight. A real tough fight. Are you up for it?

144542.en:
I found this woman in a bar in the Lai Dai station in Otitoh, and she seduced me. The next morning, I woke up with a terrible hangover in her bed--a bed which also happened to belong to Officer Eteri Tazaki of the Lai Dai Protection Services.

I've been running ever since. The fact is, every law enforcement officer in this system seems to be corrupt, and by the virtue of his position alone, Tazaki has managed to convince the authorities that I raped his wife. I'm now a wanted man, hunted by those I once trusted with my life. I'm still trying to come to terms with what has happened, but it's hard. I just hope my family doesn't hear about this until I have time to explain everything in person.

Your first task will be a difficult one. The sheriff of Otitoh, Togany, has been snooping around the area looking for me. I think he must have been tipped off by one of the locals, because he's currently scouring the asteroid belts near here, where I usually run at the first sight of law enforcement officers. You must take him out. Destroy his ship or whatever; just prevent him from finding me. I fear that if he's not taken care of soon, I will be caught. If he catches me, he'll call in back-up, and there'll be no stopping them. He's currently located near one of the moons of Otitoh VII. Bring me proof of his demise and you will be rewarded.

144544.en:
Welcome back. Now we're going for speed.

You can use two types of active propulsion modules: Afterburners and their bigger brother Microwarpdrives (or MWDs). We're about to teach you how to use Afterburners.

Afterburners don't increase your speed as drastically as MWDs, but they suffer less penalties: They use only a moderate amount of capacitor to run and cannot be disabled by Warp Scramblers. Afterburners are also much easier to fit to your ship - they use less power grid and less CPU, and have no fitting penalties.

We've got an area riddled with dangerous electromagnetic interference that will damage your ship periodically. Your task is to fly through the clouds of EM disturbance using an Afterburner, and make it to the other side in one piece.

144560.en:
Zira Cobalus, the slave leader you dispatched for us, might have been a Minmatar agent sent into our slave population to foment rebellion among the masses. This is intolerable. However, we must verify that she was indeed a spy, and our databanks here are inadequate to this task.

Take this data chip for examination at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Intelligence personnel there will compare our data with theirs, and hopefully we will get a match.

144562.en:
Your agent wants you to meet with the buyer at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

And you might want to keep an eye out for the Guristas. They might be a little peeved with you.

144563.en:
We have a serious situation on our hands, pilot.

A few weeks ago we dispatched a small squadron of Amarrian vessels that had made it inside our borders to a contested sector. We thought the job was finished and the area secure but it seems we've been duped. The entire regiment we cleared was just a decoy, and they've been massing hostiles in a nearby location with the use of covert technology.

The situation is not only embarrassing; it's undoubtedly boosted their own morale to have deceived us so effectively. We relocated all of our forces from there only days ago and re-establishing a presence will be admitting to our own people that those Imperial scum outsmarted us…or one of them in particular, actually.

Various sources of ours have pointed towards one of their Field Commanders being the key strategist behind these latest maneuvers. We need her assassinated, pilot. Not only will her death impede their progress, but it should send a message to other commanders inside the Empire. Fly out there and make it clear to them: we have capsuleers ready and able to strike down their best and brightest. Let that be the first thought in their mind before they step up to lead fleets against our people.

144564.en:
One of the key advantages we've had so far in this sector is our extensive cynosural field network, which allows us to drop our capital ships in on the enemy almost at will. The enemy, meanwhile, is forced to leave their ships vulnerable during cynosural field generation.

Unfortunately, our advantage may be crumbling. Yesterday, a task force engaging an Amarr blockade suffered serious losses when three enemy carriers dropped on them. The disturbing part is that the cynosural field was activated by a beacon, not by an Amarr ship. That means the Amarr have put up a limited cynosural field network to compete with ours. No doubt they're expanding it as fast as they can.

The network needs to be destroyed, but we need to know where those beacons have been deployed so that we can get all of them when we do a sweep. In order to do this, we want you to penetrate the security at the Amarr outpost nearby and get the tactical information sheet there. Bring it back here, and we'll have Republic Intelligence find those beacons. Understood?

144565.en:
Amarr forces have begun to deploy a cynosural field network in this sector.

In order to find the beacons comprising this network and destroy them, we need to get the records on where those beacons have been deployed. To find that, we need to get the tactical information sheet from the Amarr outpost not far from here. You'll need to fight your way to the outpost and grab the sheet. Bring it back to me as quickly as possible.

144566.en:
It's time to act fast, {[character]player.name}. We've just received reports that the Caldari Navy has established a forward outpost in the Otitoh system, in preparation for a strike at our complex in the area. According to our information they have a sizable force there already, and are preparing to move in more people. We're happy to tell you, however, that the EMP charge you placed at the Lai Dai station had its desired effect, severely damaging a substantial number of support vessels and equipment the Navy had meant for use in Otitoh. Now is therefore the time to strike, while they are weakened and working to compensate for the loss of backup assets.

We need you to go in there and take out the Navy's Command and Control center in the area. Any losses you can inflict on them while doing so will be most appreciated, but the primary target is the Command and Control center. If that is taken down, the Navy will have to retreat from the area, and our plans for this constellation will be that much closer to fruition. Once the building is destroyed, report back to me and I will see to it that you are rewarded handsomely for your efforts. The Guristas will not forget this one, {[character]player.name}. Good luck.

144567.en:
I've just received word that a fleeing civilian convoy was destroyed by the Amarr, pilot. There were over two thousand fatalities before a Fleet search-and-rescue force was able to reach the scene and recover the survivors.

In addition to the utter disregard for human life that this act displayed, evidently the daughter of a prominent Elder and her family were on board one of the industrial ships with the convoy. They are still missing, but the Fleet isn't hopeful that they will be found. We are outraged, and they want to show those terrorists that they can't get away with this kind of butchery.

I've been asked to find a pod pilot capable of taking out the sector commander who ordered this massacre. His battleship group is currently resupplying, and is temporarily vulnerable. It won't be easy; despite his cowardly choice of targets, he's quite capable and has a significant force at his disposal.

144568.en:
An Amarr task force destroyed a civilian convoy fleeing the front lines. Included in the missing and presumed dead are the daughter of a prominent Elder and her family, and the general staff is outraged by the attack. We must have revenge for this brutal massacre.

The sector commander responsible for ordering the attack is currently resupplying, leaving him temporarily vulnerable. We don't intend to let him get away. Fly to the base at the coordinates you've been given and make sure the sector commander does not survive. Any other targets are secondary, but don't hold back. Blow those slaving bastards out of the sky.

144570.en:
We've decided to do our agents in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} a favor. They've been complaining for quite some time of being overworked and underpaid, so we've decided to send them the perfect gift to soothe their nerves. A few packs of tobacco should do the trick, heh heh. It's at least something, until we come up with a better solution.

Deliver the batch to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and a local supplier will pick it up from there and deliver it to where they're staying.

144572.en: Zainou has requested a batch of silicon for their production facility in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  Deliver the goods there on time and you'll be eligible for a bonus reward.

144573.en:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. You can continue working for various corporations in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} as long as you like. I suggest finding an agent that has a greater variety of tasks available. Simply search the stations that are owned by a corporation within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} and you are bound to find an agent to your liking. You can also search for agents who will speak to you by checking the database information for the corporation of your choice. To do that simply open the People and Places menu through your NeoCom and search for the corporation name. Right click on it and choose 'show info'. There you should find a list of all of its agents that are available. Their division should give you a hint as to what type of mission they are associated with.

Take care!

144574.en:
It's those damned rogue drones again! They never seem to get enough!
This time it's big. Two of our main mining facilities in the system have been completely overrun by rogue drones. If you can go clear them out we can save some of the miners and perhaps even the facilities themselves. Please don't fail me on this one. Those facilities provide a large portion of both our incomes and it would be a big loss to both of us if they were lost

144575.en: It's tough to quit smoking when you've got a warehouse full of cigarettes within arm's reach. Take every crate of that crap you can find in that warehouse over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and leave it there. Quickly, before I change my mind!

144576.en:
I'm so glad to see you {[character]player.name}. I had almost given up hope on finding a skilled mercenary to do some dangerous work for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. I've looked everywhere in this run-down system but you're the first ray of hope that I've encountered so far.

We have a serious problem on our hands at the State And Region Bank in Ihakana. A gang of hooligans has been terrorizing passersby in the area, allegedly causing damage to our property and pestering our customers. We haven't been able to pin anything major on them yet, but our patience has worn out. I will pay you a large sum of ISK if you take care of these pests yourself, before they do any serious harm.

The deadpsace pocket is hidden from passive sensors. You will need to use probes to scan down the Kazka blockade.

144578.en:
I just received a transmission from my family on Otomainen XI, apparently the Kazka Bandits have erected a blockade at key areas around the planet to prevent anyone associated with me to leave or enter in one piece. Of course the local authorities haven't lifted a finger yet to stop these pirates from going along with their business, since XI is so sparsely populated and the Kazka Bandits have close ties to some of the corrupt officials here.

Since the planet is not technically habitable, my family has to live inside an enclosed bio dome, and we are totally dependant on supply convoys to survive. We have a little agriculture going on down there inside the dome, but not enough to feed the entire population. I'm afraid that if the Kazka become desperate, they might cut off our food supply and force the mayor to order my family to leave. That would surely be their death sentence.

The blockade is comprised of Kazka thugs, lead by one of their leaders, Pata Wakori. Kill their leader, and I'm sure you'll kill the blockade.

The deadpsace pocket is hidden from passive sensors. You will need to use probes to scan down the Kazka blockade. Take care of them quickly will you, time is of the essence here.

144580.en:
The most important task is behind us, but there are a couple more assignments that I'd like you to accomplish before you leave. The first of these assignments is to destroy a small armory near G5ED-Y II. It's being used to re-supply Guristas fighters in the system, and therefore must be destroyed. You may keep any of the supplies found inside, but do bring back some evidence of its demise.

The armory is in a deadspace pocket hidden from passive sensors. You will need to use probes to scan it down.

144584.en: Gallentean society is currently enjoying the fruits of unprecedented economic prosperity and growth, undergoing a cultural and spiritual revitalization. President Foiritan, still popular despite being ousted by President Roden, takes credit for ushering in this age, expanding trade with other nations and pouring money into massive projects. In all of New Eden, no other nation has as many concurrent terraforming initiatives underway as the Federation; the demand for labor has grown so great that it now draws immigrants from many other nations, especially from the Minmatar Republic.

144586.en:
We have a big problem, and very little time to deal with it, {[character]player.name}. Four days ago, two of our squadrons conducted a strike on a small outpost not far from here, not realizing the place was a key tactical and scientific asset belonging to the Federation. In retaliation, Fed Navy HICOM has issued three platoons of combat ships to attack the Fountain region. According to our intel, they will be striking several vital targets of ours in the next twenty-four-hour period. Rumor has it the order came from President Roden himself, so we can expect them to bring big guns and larger numbers.

Losing these outposts is something we cannot afford, so we have to move swiftly and meet them head-on before they do their damage. Two teams have already been sent to intercept the first two squads. I want you to handle the third. We believe that they are currently residing at 4-EP12. Get over there and send them back to Yulai.

I need you to head to a nearby system, pick up construction blocks and bring them over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Do this for me and I will give you your next assignment.

144601.en: Pirates are a blight on New Eden. Make sure you kill every last one, or they will scatter and regather somewhere else.

144604.en: You're a little twisted. And I'm okay with that. Yeah, I'll get you your Augumene.

144605.en: Excellent. Go get me some of that magnificent ore.

144606.en: You seem happy. What is it?

144607.en:
I was talking to some blowhard in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} when his station was destroyed. So, I'm thinking raiders, right? But no, it's even better. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh!

It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me! I want you to go out there, and bring me back all of that Augumene.

144608.en: Here's the Augumene. Where's my ISK?

144609.en: Ah, it even feels like providence. And cold, hard kredits. Speaking of which, here's yours.

144610.en: You seem entirely too happy with all this. And that troubles me. I'm going to decline, I'm afraid.

144611.en: What? You don't like free ISK?

144612.en: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes very expensive safety precautions. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.

144614.en:
I'm on the comm, talking to this blowhard I knew back from my days at the academy, right...? So he's going on and on about how his corporation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is going to make ISK hand over fist mining some rare ore, blah blah blah. Then all these alarms start going off on his end. And I'm thinking his stupid corp is getting raided or something. Then, all of a sudden, the wall behind him disappears and he's ripped away from the screen! The blowhard got spaced right in front of my eyes!

Now, here's the best part. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh! It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me!

So, anyway, I want you to go out there and bring me back all of that Augumene. Do that, and I'll have a nice reward here for you when your come back, alright?

144615.en: I don't have time to wait for you to decide whether you like ISK or not. I'll get someone else to mine my lucky rock. So you can just get lost, okay?

144617.en: This is more than a little weird. I'm not mining this Augumene anymore.

144618.en: Don't tell me you're scared of a little rock?

144619.en: Great. You took just long enough for some other vultures to get all the Augumene. That rock was meant for me, but no, you had to prance around until it was too late. Thanks for nothing.

144621.en: Sounds like a good deal. I'm in.

144622.en: Remember, move fast. Time's of the essence, huh?

144624.en:
Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

Be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.

144625.en: Here's your Mercium. So, where's my cut?

144626.en:
Here you go. Oh, this is gonna be just like hacking into that SCC station computer and making ISK for myself!

Uh, I mean, not that I've ever done that....

144627.en: I'm not interested in getting caught in a four-way crossfire just to mine some rocks that might be worth something to someone at some point.

144628.en: Not everybody's got what it takes. I knew that when I first looked at you.

144630.en:
This thing: Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Alright? You gotta get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

144631.en: I don't have this kinda time, {[character]player.name}. I gotta move on this Mercium before it's gone.

144633.en: Selling to all four of the big empires? Uh... even I don't want to piss off that many people. Nah, I quit.

144634.en: Don't worry, I'll find someone who's willing to make some decent ISK.

144635.en: Somebody else already beat you to that Mercium, bonehead. Way to go.

144637.en: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

144639.en: Get it quick. I don't like waiting.

144641.en: Mine 18,000 units of Banidine at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring it to {[character]agentID.name}.

144642.en: I've got your Banidine right here, pal.

144644.en: I don't work for crazy people.

144645.en: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in the mission details in your Opportunities interface  and select "Add to Overview."

144647.en:
Look, I need some… ah, building materials, but I've got a client who's a bit particular. He wants it special, from some asteroids that already destroyed a shuttle of his, I guess. He gave me a location; you just go there, mine all 18,000 units of the Banidine that's there, and bring it back. Now, you won't find this stuff anywhere else, so don't go looking to bring me back something similar and easier to come across — you try and rip me off on this, and I'll know. Got it? Alright.

So, you game?

144648.en: I got no time for games. I'll find somebody who can get it done.

144650.en: I'm done with this weird stuff. Banidine? It's worthless! So I get to wondering… who the hell wants this stuff, and for what? And I decide, maybe I ought not to do this, huh?

144651.en: Thanks a bundle. I didn't pay ya to think. That's my job. Remember that next time.

144652.en: I need this done yesterday. I found someone else who can do the job faster.

144655.en: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good gas harvester around here.

144656.en: You know me, ready for anything.

144657.en:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. And you also gotta deal with any drones there. Fair enough?

144658.en: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.

144659.en: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.

144660.en: I'm afraid I can't do this. So... "no thanks."

144661.en: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Hey, thanks for being honest, though.

144663.en:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. I don't know why. It's like insects to a flame or somethin'. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. It's annoying as hell.

I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. If you don't or ya can't, just say "no thanks." You can decline one mission about every 4 hours without pissing me off, so no worries.

144664.en: Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.

144665.en: The career advisor agents will be able to help you choose what skills to train, and how to specialize as a capsule pilot.
