144669.en:
We're returning to interdiction tactics by having you test out a Stasis Webifier module. When activated on a target ship, the Stasis Webifier will encase it in a containment field and slow it down dramatically.

Time for you to see for yourself. We've chased a pirate down to a nearby hideout and we want you to pin him down. We'll provide you with a Civilian Stasis Webifier, and you may want to fit an afterburner, too.

144957.en: Colonists eking out a living on godforsaken rocks in space are finding it hard to maintain food production, so we're giving them a boost. The moment you've brought those crates of frozen plant seeds over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, our caravans will pick them up and haul them to those thankful pioneers.

144958.en:
You capsuleers spend so much time in the midst of mayhem and destruction, and you leave countless wreckages in your wake. Now, though, you and I have an opportunity to help sustain new life. I want you to transport some large crates of frozen plant seeds for me.

It will not surprise you that we are always trying to establish new colonies in even the most desolate parts of space. Colonization is always an exciting opportunity, not only for the settlers who dare venture out into space and stake their fortunes on some desolate rock, but for local entrepreneurs, businesses and politicians to support them. You won't hear of these, because your kind is so far up above piddly little local events, but it's a big deal for those involved.

Unfortunately, local support can't last forever. After the initial interest has waned, the citizens on those colonies have to fend for themselves. Sometimes they manage to create self-sustaining habitats where no outside intervention is needed. Occasionally they get lucky, and the outcome of their scientific experiments, ore search, or whatever else they were up to, makes them enough money that they can buy whatever they need off local orbitals.

All too often, though, we have to step in. Your cargo, once delivered to their colony, will hopefully enable them to bootstrap themselves to a self-sustaining life cycle. Colony life is hard enough as it is.

144959.en: Really? Ah well, back to destruction it is.

144960.en: I am greatly disappointed. Their food stores were already running low.

144961.en: Take care to keep those seeds frozen at all times.

144962.en: Excellent. Caravans will take the seeds to the colony. You have earned back some of your karma, capsuleer.

144963.en: Some entertainment-hungry collectors out there are waiting for a lot of specially ordered holoreels that were manufactured, stamped, signed and compiled in special editions elsewhere in the cluster. I need you to bring these large holoreel crates to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} before they risk starting something silly like reading books.

144964.en:
Most often we leave the shipment of entertainment material to the more slow-moving vessels in our employ. Every so often, though, we receive sufficient premium orders from other stations and the planets in their vicinity that we dispatch a special courier with the payload.

That courier is you, and the payload is huge stacks of holoreels, most of them ordered on some manner of timed interstellar delivery offer.

This isn't the primary business of our own corporation as such, but we have enough ties to the producers of all this material - as would any corporation large enough to have gone interstellar - that it's incumbent on us to find ways of delivering it to the customers.

Believe me, I wish we could just transfer all of this digitally, but for most of this cargo that is simply not an option. Some of these holoreels are under trade restrictions that prevent them from being beamed over and saved or stamped on the spot; others are special collectors' editions that may include anything from specially signed copies to boxed sets weighed down with any number of collectable objects.

Please ensure your crew doesn't open any of the crates, either. These people are collectors and paid a galactic premium for their items. If they so much as smell another human being's presence on the merchandise, they will resort either to lawsuits or assassinations.

144965.en: Very well. They'll just have to watch empty screens for a little longer.

144966.en: The customers will not be happy with this.

144967.en: Don't open any of those sealed special editions, you hear?

144968.en: Excellent. Your crew left the holoreels untouched, I trust.

144969.en: We have come into possession of large amounts of garbage, and since we can't legally rid ourselves of it here, I need you to transport it over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. They have some good people there who don't have ethical qualms about destroying any kind of trash, even if a limb or two is dangling out of the crate.

144970.en:
In all honesty, I find it just unbelievable that in this day and age we are expending actual capsuleer man-hours, not to mention the time and effort of your crew, and asking actual spaceships to travel interstellar distances only to shift around a cargohold of something as pitiable as actual garbage. Garbage. Especially the type we've got here, which takes up a bunch of room, has to be stored in nonporous containers, and, frankly, is starting to smell.

Nonetheless, here we are. We could have this cargo sent down planetside and destroyed, except that while those people are perfectly happy to toss up any number of shipments with whatever trinkets the station clientele is demanding that week, they have frothing conniptions if we so much as suggest that we might want to send anything like this back down in return. The merest whisper of it is enough for them to drag out the lawyers. It's not as if they don't have the space.

You aren't too big to help out, I trust. All we need you to do is haul this smelly, half-liquidized garbage to another station, where they'll have ways to get rid of it without endless complaints or moral qualms. I swear, if the PR department would just let us stop accepting all these colony refugees, we wouldn't have this problem.

Actually, forget I said that last part.

144971.en: Look, it was just normal, everyday garbage. There was no reason for you not to take this on.

144972.en: I am disappointed. I hope you didn't root around in the cargo.

144973.en: If your crew tells you that anything was moving in the garbage, don't believe them.

144974.en: Thanks. Now we have them off our hands. The garbage, I mean.  Off our hands.

144975.en: We have a small outburst of violent behavior to deal with on a nearby station. Refugees from interstellar violence have begun gathering forces and are demanding compensation, hearings and whatnot. Now, this is just a damn stupid situation, and we have people who can put it right, but they need a bit of a boost. That's where you come in. Transport these large crates of small arms to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll take it from there.

144976.en:
Our people at a nearby station are in need of more firepower. They are going to have to subdue unruly refugees from destroyed colonies and crews from recently destroyed ships.

I know it sounds ludicrous. The thing is, when you have near-death experiences of that kind, you may come to the realization that life is fickle, short and dangerous, and that everything you took for granted may be taken from you in the blink of an eye. It tends to upset people, make them aggressive and reckless.

That is, if they're mortal. You being a capsuleer, you'll just have to take my word for it. I'm sure death has a great impact on your sense of the world, but thus far in my experience, it doesn't make you half as crazy as near-death, and at least your type has the sense to take it outside when you feel the need to blow something up.

Incidentally, there are always claims - by silly local news outlets nobody listens to - that representatives of our corporation may not always react immediately when they hear that people are floating out there in escape pods, waiting in to be rescued. Do not let those claims bother you. Those same people are sitting in the midst of a deadly capsuleer battlefield and are in dire need of learning the blessed virtue of patience.

144977.en: Alright. We'll have to find other ways of subduing them, then.

144978.en: I'm disappointed. I hope you're not siding with these rebellious people.

144979.en: I know you have plenty of firepower, too, but let's leave this one to station personnel.

144980.en: Thanks! And don't feel bad for those people - I'm sure there'll be some survivors.

144981.en: You have a juicy and slightly sticky mission on your hands. Quafe is conducting one of their local marketing campaigns and are in need of exotic drinks - which in this case means another shipment of Quafe manufactured in another solar system. Bring these large crates of quafe over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and you'll make a lot of thirsty people very happy.

144982.en:
Quafe is preparing for one of their routine planetside campaigns, and as a premium they want to offer special bottles of the ubiquitous drink.

To be honest, there is nothing special about the drink. It's the same cola, with the same water, color, sugar, additives and perfectly legal trace elements, that you'd find on any civilized planet in the cluster. What's important isn't so much the brand as the bottles themselves . They were manufactured on another planet, so their design is subtly different from what's available where you're taking them, and the labeling indicates their origins.

People go crazy for this stuff. I'm serious. This will be hard for a capsuleer to understand, but most people don't even travel that much between the continents on their own planets. To hold in your hand an item that was manufactured in another solar system is an experience that's truly special to a huge number of people.

This only works for things like Quafe, mind you. Taking anything this thoroughly familiar and changing it just slightly has a higher excitement freakout value than even if you'd brought in some unknown artifact made by actual aliens.

144983.en: You sure? But everybody loves Quafe!

144984.en: That's a disappointment. If you and your crew drank it all, it's okay to say so. You're not the only ones with a habit.

144985.en: Keep moving. I don't trust the sealants on those crates, and I'd hate for the Quafe to go flat.

144986.en: Perfect. Help yourself to a nice, cool, fizzy drink as a reward.

144987.en: Our pod fluid vats in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are in dire need of refilling, lest you find yourself floating in something that's more like a swamp lake after a hot summer. Collect from your hangar those large crates of ectoplasm we dredged up and haul them over there as soon as you can!

144988.en:
You capsuleers are amazing. Not only have you got the interstellar corporations doing crazy business in ore, minerals, modules and ammunition, but you also routinely exhaust our storages for the equipment that's required to even keep you people in the air. I need you to transport something that's vital for your own continued success.

I'm not referring to the capsules themselves or the unimaginably complex electronics that help you interface with your ship. No, this is something much more mundane. We need to replenish our vats of pod fluid, and for that, we need ectoplasm. This way, whenever you visit our fair station, we can drain and replace your capsule if our tests show that its contents have become a little too stale.

Also, should you have a clone contract with any of our stations and later on find yourself inconvenienced to the point of ... well, to the point of death, we want to ensure that we can put you into a new capsule filled to the brim with pod fluid that's proper, fresh and new. Nothing's quite as disgusting as waking up in a brand new body only to realize that it's been plunged into someone else's used pod fluid.

144989.en: Fair enough. Keep floating in your own goo, then.

144990.en: Really? Alright, but don't be surprised if your pod starts to thicken up a little in time.

144991.en: You'll ... not want to taste the cargo. Trust me.

144992.en: Wonderful. We'll happily let you try out the first batch.

Excellent work, {[character]player.name}! You've proven you know how to handle yourself in deadly situations.

We can always use good pilots like yourself, you should consider enlisting in Factional Warfare, where you can fight alongside other pilots pledged to the Republic. If instead, you would rather broaden your skills, you can start a conversation with any of my fellow Career Agents right here in this station.

Whatever you choose to do next, I thank you for the help you've given us. Fly safe, Captain.

145013.en: You've really saved our butts today. If the State got that gate working, we'd be faced with a large invasion force behind our front lines. I suppose we'll have to be more diligent in the future with those sort of things.

145014.en: You've really saved our butts today. If the Federation got that gate working, we'd be faced with a large invasion force behind our front lines. That could have been catastrophic. I suppose we'll have to be more diligent in the future with those sort of things.

145015.en: You've really saved our butts today. If the Empire got that gate working, we'd be faced with a large invasion force behind our front lines. I suppose we'll have to be more diligent in the future with those sort of things.

145016.en: You've really saved our butts today. If the Republic got that gate working, we'd be faced with a large invasion force behind our front lines. That could have been catastrophic. I suppose we'll have to be more diligent in the future with those sort of things.

145017.en:
Few have the skills to enter the world of Covert Ops, and fewer still survive long once they enter it. And of those who do survive, rare are those who can claim to be totally sane afterwards.

One of the first lessons in Covert Ops is "plausible deniability"; this, along with the selective use of misinformation, allows a government and or a military entity to distance itself from its spies and operatives should their activities become known. Paradoxically, though, while every government and military organization requires Covert Ops to survive, it can be extremely harmful to admit such groups' existence, at least without a feasible back-up story — a story usually provided by the covert agents themselves.

At times, the distance between a Covert Ops agency and its parent organization can become so byzantine that funding can present a dangerous optic. When that occurs, operatives may have to raise funds themselves, in ways only they can...

145018.en:
Okay, I haven't been totally honest with you. I'm currently working on behalf of a Covert Ops agent for the Republic Navy.

That Caldari ship? Belonged to a disgruntled military scientist who was going to sell us a bio-weapon prototype. Unfortunately, we had a small misunderstanding over price, and now he's dead. Things happen, you know? I hired you to retrieve the ship logs so we could have a little thing called "plausible deniability" if things went badly. Like they kinda did.

{[character]player.name}, here's the new plan. First of all, the weapon is useless — the scientist was as terrible a researcher as he was a negotiator. But rumors we whispered into the right ears have got people believing otherwise. This whole operation was about raising funds for Navy Covert Ops, after all. Spy stuff isn't cheap!

Anyway, we need you to meet with the buyer at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Will you do this for me?

Sorry about all the fibs. Please? Pretty please?

145019.en:
Ok, you're now all set to speak with Arizam Gimit. You'll probably find her at her desk in the Amarr station in Lossa. And don't forget to bring your graduation certificate when you pay her a visit!

If you forget the location of this agent, you can always look it up by opening the 'show info' window for the graduation certificate.

145020.en:
{[character]player.name}, the Caldari have built an observation base in Gallente space. It has been designated “Station 464.” One of the structures is a relay station, and it is being used to store all the information the Caldari have collected in the system. I need you to hack the relay station so we can see what kind of information they have collected and thus the purpose of the base.

The data center is heavily protected so be ready for a real fight. I will upload the location to your Neocom.

145021.en:
Hello, {[character]player.name}. At the moment, all you have to fly is a capsule. Our first priority is to get you into a starship.

Your assignment: Follow the tutorial steps, I will guide you to a hidden location in space.

If you ever get lost, remember to use the back and next buttons and read the tutorial slides or you can quit the mission and start over again from the beginning.

There are a number of career training agents not far from here who can teach you about all the various activities and careers available to you. They'll let you get hands-on training and experience with everything from asteroid mining to deep space exploration.

When you're ready, I will refer you to them. You should take everything else with you as well, since you probably won't be coming back here afterward.

145108.en:
Hello, {[character]player.name}. At the moment, all you have to fly is a capsule. Our first priority is to get you into a starship.

Your assignment: Follow the tutorial steps, I will guide you to a hidden location in space.

If you ever get lost, remember to use the back and next buttons and read the tutorial slides or you can quit the mission and start over again from the beginning.

145152.en:
Next up is a kind of interdiction called warp disruption. When activated on another targeted ship, these kinds of modules "tackle" it, disabling its warp drive.

Tackling only works if you keep the target within your module's range and can overpower its Warp Strength. A Warp Disruptor lowers a ship's Warp Strength by 1, while the more powerful Warp Scrambler modules reduce it by 2.

I'll give you a Civilian Warp Disruptor to test out on a pirate that escaped from the headquarters you just blew up. Pin him down, but don't blow him up.

145158.en:
I'm not going to beat around the bush with you on this one, as there isn't any time. We have a developing emergency in {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name}. Several of our commercial convoys have been ripped to shreds in the last few months by an extremely dangerous band of terrorists. As you can see from these camera drone recordings, they have even been willing to fly their ships directly into our freighters and other unarmed haulers. And yes, before you ask, we have been escorting these convoys with heavily armed security vessels, though to little effect.

As these terrorists are obviously willing to die for their cause, they aren't bothering to attack our warships. They simply seem to appear out of nowhere, accelerate to high speeds and slam into the cargo ships. Depending on the cargo, this action can, at best, tear open the cargo bays and release the contents into the vacuum of space, or, at worst, strike a shipment of fuels or ammunition, and destroy the freighter in one huge explosion. One such explosion destroyed an entire convoy.

However, an ultra-secure communications intercept satellite recently picked up a communication that we believe indicates the terrorists are now considering turning their deadly tactic against some unidentified stations in the region. Given our huge civilian population on these stations, the decision has been made to conduct a partial evacuation of all potential target stations.

What we need from you is your help in getting these civilians – mostly the spouses and children of station personnel – to a station that is further away from the terrorists' known area of operation. Normally, I would not ask this of a capsuleer, but I am begging you: will you help us evacuate these people until this threat has passed? We need to know right now, as we have already begun to organize the evacuation fleet; can we count you in?

145160.en:
An infestation of nasty, biting roaches has taken hold on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and it is growing out of control. In fact, it's gotten so bad that they've considered venting the emergency airlocks briefly and allowing the station atmosphere to empty into space, but scientists tell us the little bastards can survive even in space for hours.

The only answer is to gas the entire station. The substance they want to use is a special concoction designed specifically to grant this particular species of roach a quick death. I have a shipment of the stuff; I just need you to get it there. This stuff is more dangerous than the cockroaches.

Note the hasty delivery required — you don't have much time to complete this mission.

145162.en: Goddamnit, what is Irichi doing? That bastard is losing his mind. He hasn't been the same since he lost his legs, and he blames me for that. Well, I guess he should. I was the one who tortured him when I was working for the Federation. But we're Guristas now, and we pirates have to stick together, right? It's the pirate's code. That, and “every pirate for herself."

145163.en:
Religious freaks like to spread all sorts of apocalyptic messages, and in recent times there are few who have captured the imagination of conspiracy theorists in the way that Tolmak has. The so-called “Prophet of the Seventh Sphere,” Tolmak is an enigmatic and elusive character. He has never shown himself publicly for fear of reprisal, and relies instead of proxies to spread his word. Others say his real strength comes from the media outlets that cover these preachers. Outlets that, for their own part, are mostly concerned with the profit to be made from the inevitable controversy his message brings.

Among other things, Tolmak's elaborate revelations paint a universe governed by demonic forces that secretly control the heads of all the empires. He reserves special bile for the capsuleer class, teaching that their clones are not actually the same person reborn, but are instead, demonic simulacra.

145165.en:
So good to see you, {[character]player.name}. I've been on a pretty tight schedule for the past two weeks, ever since we discovered the strange, and increasing, Serpentis activity in the system. Our CEO demands an explanation, yet we still don't know enough about the situation to determine what's really going on. And that's where you come in.

Serpentis activity on this scale in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is unheard of, and quite frankly we aren't well enough prepared at the moment to deal with any major conflict with them. Not only that, but those greedy pirates are insatiable, and news of their appearance around here has sent the trade lanes into a state of panic. People are leaving this station already, making my superiors ... less than content if you know what I mean. We're losing good people because of this unacceptable situation and we need to put an end to it.

The first thing I want you to do is undertake a reconnaisance mission for us into an area where we have witnessed most of the Serpentis activity. We've already lost a few patrols that ventured into this area, so be careful. If you do find any Serpentis ships out there, eliminate them. We don't want any prisoners, interrogating these deviants won't do us any good. Report your findings to me a.s.a.p.

145167.en: Watch your back out there, {[character]player.name}.  And whatever you do, don't let them take you prisoner, I've heard they have some insidious ways of making you spill your secrets...

145168.en: You showed some class out there, {[character]player.name}.  Take your pay and report for your next assignment.

145169.en: Because of your successful reconnaissance mission, we've managed to narrow down the location of the main Serpentis activity a bit.  The data that we extracted from your system scanner also revealed to us a few Serpentis ships that were not mentioned in your preliminary report.  It appears to be some sort of convoy, at least one of their ships was clearly an industrial.  Because of this we guess that it may be a routine shipment, meaning that they might get a convoy at regular intervals.  We'd like you to fly out there, preferably with a cloaking device, and lay in wait for any possible sign of another Serpentis convoy.  If you do see one, destroy it and bring back the contents of the industrials to me for inspection.

145171.en: Construction blocks?  I was afraid of that.  This doesn't seem to be a mere smuggling operation, but something much more sinister.  But we still don't know what they are building ... And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!

145172.en:
Now that we've established the general location of the Serpentis activity within {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, it's actually time to find out exactly what they are building. In your last mission you destroyed one of their construction block transports, but this brings us no closer to finding their base of operations. We've had no luck interrogating these pirates before, and the surveillance teams we have sent to investigate the area have either found nothing or disappeared. This leaves us with very few options. But after brainstorming possible solutions to our problem, I came up with a devious plan.

We have in our possession so called 'spy drones', straight from our science labs, which attach themselves to a nearby ships hull and emits a low frequency signal which is picked up by one of our beacons which are strewn around {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, which in turn sends a high frequency signal to our control tower in {[location]agentStationID.name}.

Now we know that an agent of the Serpentis Corporation regularly picks up shipments of Ectoplasm at a certain station near here. If we can place the spy drone into his next shipment, this might allow us to track his ship to its destination.

Our men have placed beacons throughout our constellation, so everything is in place. All you need to do is take these crates filled with ectoplasm, and our spy drones, to the station specified in the mission details, our agents there will take care of the rest. With luck we'll soon know the location of the Serpentis base.

145174.en: Good job {[character]player.name}.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!

145175.en:
After reviewing the intel we received from the spy drones which you transferred for us in your last mission, we managed to pinpoint the location of a military outpost they are building in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It appears to be a part of a defensive perimeter that they are setting up around their territory, which has elevated our fears that they have actually managed to erect a large colony inside our solarsystem.

But for now let's keep our sights on the current task, to breach a hole in their defensive wall. We believe that the outpost in question hasn't been fully built, and therefore will be a fairly easy target for you if it's defensive installations aren't complete. Contact with the spy drones was cut off before we could fully analyze the Serpentis forces in the area. But one thing's for sure, there will most certainly be guards nearby, and they will have to be dealt with. You will receive a bookmark to the location of the outpost, and your instructions are simple, destroy the habitat of their construction workers. That should slow them down a bit. Good luck.

145177.en: Magnificent job, {[character]player.name}.  Those Serpentis really put up a fight didn't they?  However I believe you've done as much for us as we can possibly expect of you, the Serpentis data sheets you brought back with you have confirmed our worst fears, the Serpentis Corporation has a fully functional colony inside {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}!  It will take a massive force to take it out, and we can't expect you to handle a mission like that yet.  Good luck on your future endeavors.

145178.en: Somebody broke into my brother's home yesterday and stole his entire gun collection. He'll get into heaps of trouble with his superiors if they find out, so I want you to help him make the problem go away. Fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop off a new set of weapons. I'll modify the ID codes on the guns, and nobody will suspect a thing.

145180.en: Small, independent trade hubs throughout New Eden are sometimes referred to by a most peculiar and archaic term: “Roadhouses.” Though no one quite remembers why they're called that, it's common knowledge that roadhouses are ideal locations for moving stolen goods, making underworld contacts, or getting hurt. Needless to say, these establishments are frequented by unscrupulous roughnecks for whom pain doesn't hurt.

145206.en:
This incident comes at a very bad time. Political relations between our governments are extremely volatile at the moment, and there are rumors of war floating around everywhere. So I have explicit orders to tell you to keep this quiet. With your record I know I can trust you, don't speak of this to anyone. Just find the missing reporters, destroy their captors, return them to me and keep your mouth shut.

The first group of Gallente civilians went missing in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} reporting on a story involving a group of Caldari Smugglers, who were said to have been smuggling armed terrorists to our stations in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, to cause mayhem no doubt. I'll give you the coordinates to their last known position. Find them and bring them back, dead or alive. Their families must be informed of their fate, or they will never be at peace. If you find any hostiles at the scene, feel free to use deadly force.

The first Amarrian civilian went missing in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} reporting on a story involving a group of Minmatar terrorists, who were said to have been smuggling arms and other illegal goods to some of the more notorious criminal organizations in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, to what purpose we can only guess. I'll give you the coordinates to his last known position. Find him and bring him back, whether dead or alive. His family must know what happened to him. If you find any Minmatar ships at the scene, offer them no dialogue, just destroy them.

234396.en: Sculpting is performed by left-clicking directly on the character and holding down the button, then moving the mouse to alter the area selected. To alter the camera's position, hold the right mouse button and move the mouse in the direction you want the camera to move. To zoom, either scroll with the mouse wheel or hold both left and right mouse buttons and move the mouse back and forth. Some sculpting areas will be differently affected depending on camera position.

234397.en: The Portrait step allows you to pose your character, select backgrounds and set up lighting for the portrait that will be used to represent you in-game. Facial expression and head position are changed by left-clicking directly on the character and holding down the button, then moving the mouse to alter the area selected. To alter the camera's position, hold the right mouse button and move the mouse in the direction you want the camera to move. To zoom, either scroll with the mouse wheel or hold both left and right mouse buttons and move the mouse back and forth. You can capture up to 4 portraits, but only one will be used to represent your character in the game. Select the one you wish to use before proceeding to the next step.

234398.en: The identity step allows you to review everything you have done while creating your character. In addition you can select an ancestry, a starting school and a name for your character. When naming your character, you can create two names within the name field and one within the family name field.

234399.en: Re-customization for the altering of cosmetic options, but no sculpting of the characters can be done. To alter the camera's position, hold the right mouse button and move the mouse in the direction you want the camera to move. To zoom, either scroll with the mouse wheel or hold both left and right mouse buttons and move the mouse back and forth.

234400.en: The Portrait step allows you to pose your character, select backgrounds and set up lighting for the portrait that will be used to represent you in-game. To alter the camera's position, hold the right mouse button and move the mouse in the direction you want the camera to move. To zoom, either scroll with the mouse wheel or hold both left and right mouse buttons and move the mouse back and forth. You can capture up to 4 portraits, but only one will be used to represent your character in the game. Select the one you wish to use before proceeding to the next step.

234559.en: "The State had lost its way. The corporations forgot the principles upon which they were founded. The people suffered. The State suffered. We were an embarrassment. Our forefathers turned in their graves at the depths to which our leaders had allowed our State to fall. No more. We are strong once again. We are Caldari once again. We are the State once again, and our homeland is ours at last. We are at war. The State calls out to you, the capsuleer, for we need your strength and your leadership to fend off the encroaching Gallente menace. They seek to bring us to heel. The State! The State bends for no one and no thing. The State stands strong, The State will not fall. Join us. Fight. Win."

234560.en: "Millions of souls cry out for emancipation, begging to be freed from a life where they are treated no better than captive animals. The Minmatar heart sings for freedom and the Minmatar soul strives for open skies, but the Minmatar heart withers away in captivity. It is now up to you, the capsuleer. You hold the power to free our people. You are the heroes of your generation. It is finally time to make the Amarr pay for their atrocities. We will find those who called themselves "masters", and we will bring them to their knees! Look to your heart, look to our people. Join us! Death to Amarr!"

234561.en: "The Amarr Empire used to shine as a beacon to humanity of what it meant to be civilized: To be strong, and to lead by example. Through God's words we spread civilization throughout the stars and it is by our leadership that New Eden achieved its wings. It is up to you to carry this example, the lessons of God's chosen, and reinstate the Empire of Amarr to its former and rightful glory. We need you to reclaim the Minmatar from the drudge, chaos and inhumanity in which they currently dwell, and into God's light. We are their angels. We must be their saviors. By your power they shall be rescued from the dark. God wills it, and so it shall be."

234562.en: "The Federation is the standard, indeed the only example, of equality, justice, freedom and sanity in today's universe. While the rest of the Empires seek to expand in willful acts of destruction, the Federation seeks to protect its people and its borders from the deprivations of the Caldari who have shown unprovoked aggression against us. We attempted to be civilized, to talk, to travel the road of peace, but they refused. The Federation has awoken to the threat, and now its strength shall be tried. We wanted peace, and now we are faced with war. We are the Federation. We shall not stumble, we shall not falter. We shall stand victorious on the field of battle, a testament to the values of liberty and justice. The people of the Federation need you. With your strength and your conviction we shall endure."

235578.en:
Subject: Domination Excavator (ID: Modified Cyclone)
Military Specifications: Cruiser-class vessel. Houses both advanced scientific and military technologies.
Additional Intelligence: Cartel forays beyond Angel territories have escalated each year since the discovery of wormhole space in YC 111. The Domination Excavator was first seen in one of these operations in 113. The ship itself contains a wide array of hi-tech defensive and offensive capabilities, including redundant power systems and a range of Domination modules. Large sections of crew quarters are converted to specialized lab space, able to perform on-site analysis of found materials. Plasma igniters ensure the labs are burned at temperatures exceeding 45000 Kelvin, should the vessel be captured. Agent Trereval, Republic Security Services.
Authorized for capsuleer dissemination.

Subject: True Sansha Foreman (ID: Modified Phantasm)
Military Specifications: Cruiser-class vessel. Modified for increased mining efficiency of local Slaves.
Additional Intelligence: Pre-YC 113, the True Sansha Foreman variant was once a rare sight outside of the Sansha home region of Stain. As an alternative to capsuleer-dependent strip mining, the Foreman is specially designed to coordinate large crews of Slaves in a local deadspace pocket. Exact figures are difficult to determine, but mining Slaves under the Foreman seem to operate at around 125% efficiency. This link is both fragile and experimental. If the link is violently severed (i.e. the Foreman is destroyed), the affected Slaves in the mining equipment are damaged and unable to continue their work.
Analyst Fawlon, Ministry of Assessment.
Authorized for capsuleer dissemination.

236048.en: CONCORD invalidates war declared by {declaredByName} against {againstName}

236049.en:
For your convenience we have included the appropriate CONCORD War Rules:

The weekly cost is {[numeric]cost.isk} and the attacking organization will receive a bill which needs to be paid promptly to maintain the war. If the bill is not paid before it is due then the war will be cancelled.

Both sides in a war must control at least one structure in space in order to be war eligible. If either side loses their last structure, they lose their war eligibility and the war is cancelled.
The attacking side of a war must designate one highsec Upwell structure that they control as the War HQ for the conflict. If the War HQ is destroyed or removed from space the war will be cancelled.

When an active war has been cancelled, there is a 24 hour cooldown period during which fighting can legally continue.

If you are at war with a corporation that joins an alliance then the war will change from being against the corporation to being against the alliance.

If you are at war with an alliance and a corporation leaves that alliance then you will still be at war with the alliance and a new war will be created with the corporation that left. This new war is subject to its own bills and all the normal war eligibility requirements.

The distinctive design of Vallou's officer coats is inspired by historical images of high-ranking military members from the heyday of the Garoun Empire, ancestors of the Gallente Federation. 236476.en:
The Excavator has been eliminated. Whatever the Cartel was looking for, they aren't getting it now.
Don't forget to rob the wreckage of delicious prizes.

236478.en:
Despite numerous laws across the empires bolstering security regulations after the outbreak of Sansha incursions in YC 113, mining colonies still provide a weak, target-rich environment for pirate factions....
Sansha raiding fleets are wiping out the colonists and using their own Slaves to crew the mining equipment until it fails, leaving the colony as an empty husk. Eliminating the True Sansha Foreman is the most reliable way of shutting down the entire operation.
DED Threat Assessment: 4 of 10

236479.en: True Sansha Foreman detected in the next pocket. Eliminating this ship will cause the Sansha miners to lose their efficiency and eventually abandon the base.

236480.en:
Despite numerous laws across the empires bolstering security regulations after the outbreak of Sansha incursions in YC 113, mining colonies still provide a weak, target-rich environment for pirate factions....
The Angel Cartel takes an unorthodox approach to these colonies, imprisoning the miners and replacing them with their own excavation teams, led by a Domination Excavator. The CDIA has yet to determine what the Cartel is after, though no significant amount of traditionally valuable ore has been taken.
DED Threat Assessment: 4 of 10

236481.en: I'm reading the presence of a Domination Excavator. Prepare yourself for a fight. Scientists or not, the Cartel only fields warships.

236484.en:
The Foreman has been eliminated. All attached Slaves in the colony are now useless to the Sansha.
Time to scoop up the loot.

236486.en:
Subject: Domination Grigori (ID: Modified Daredevil)
Military Specifications: Frigate-class vessel. Veteran-level crew.
Additional Intelligence: Designed specifically for lightning raids in enemy space, the Grigori variant of the daunted Daredevil can catch the inexperience ship captain unaware. What is most impressive is that, beyond a handful of experimental Angel technologies, the Grigori's advantage comes almost exclusively from employing an all-veteran crew. The efficiency and skill a Grigori crew brings to battle can rival those of a capsuleer. Luckily, the loss of a Grigori crew can be extremely demoralizing for local Cartel forces, leading them to eventually abandon complexes where a Grigori was destroyed.
Analyst Kental, DED.
Authorized for capsuleer dissemination.

236490.en:
The Domination Grigori and all its crew have been eliminated. I wonder how many people that actually is? Or was?
Oh well. Let's see if it dropped any neat stuff.

236492.en:
To the frustration of the Minmatar Republic, the Angel Cartel still enjoys a great deal of success with piracy throughout Republic space. A contributing factor to the Angel's ubiquity is their ability to repurpose small gang outposts as camps.
A Domination Grigori is sent with a small frigate wing to clear out a minor smuggler outpost. Once temporary fortifications are made, the location is further masked with a series of interference broadcasts designed to confound Republic sensors.
DED Threat Assessment: 3 of 10

236493.en: This next pocket is generating multiple interference signals. Once we are further into the complex I can gather more intel.

236494.en: That's better. My analysis shows there are three more pockets in this complex. The last pocket should contain a Domination Grigori. Eliminating this ship severely ruin the Cartel's day.

236710.en: Your generosity astounds me, but I could never forgive myself for taking more of your money so soon.

236712.en: Great! Please drop by, so we can formalize the mission contract.

236713.en: Sorry, I have no jobs for the general public.

236715.en: You don't have the items I required at {[location]agentStationID.name}.  The item(s) must be located in your cargo hold or in your personal hangar.  If you have multiple objectives of the same item type in the same location, please use either the hangar or your cargo hold, but not both.  If a specific item was requested as opposed to any item of the specified type, please be sure that the correct specific item is indeed being provided.  Otherwise, please make sure that the item is not assembled, packaged or damaged.  Check the mission details in your Opportunity interface for more details.

236716.en: You don't have the items I required in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}.  The item(s) must be located in your cargo hold.  If a specific item was requested as opposed to any item of the specified type, please be sure that the correct specific item is indeed being provided.  Otherwise, please make sure that the item is not assembled, packaged or damaged.  Check the mission details in your Opportunities interface for more details.

236717.en: I am currently off in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}.  If you want to talk, please meet me in person.

236718.en: Hello {[character]player.name}. Good to see you again. I would like to remind you that you have previously completed this epic arc and for you to embark on it once again I would have to erase all memory of the arc from your mind. Are you sure you would like to start this journey once again and lose all history of this arc?

236719.en: My offices are located at {[location]agentStationID.name}.  If you want to talk, please meet me in person.

236720.en: So you think you're tough? If that's the case, I might have some use for you.

236721.en: You have a long and prosperous future within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name}, {[character]player.name}.

236723.en: I am exhilarated at seeing you, {[character]player.name}. I hope I can be of assistance.

236725.en: Why hello there. What do you want?

236726.en: {[character]player.name}! You're back! Please have a seat and make yourself feel comfortable. If there is anything you need, just ask.

236727.en: I hope you're not here to ask me for a favor. I hate beggars.

236728.en: What do you want? Spit it out, stooge.

236730.en: Nice to see you, {[character]player.name}, but you know you still have an unfinished mission from me, right?

236731.en: Always a pleasure, of course. But the last mission I gave you isn't going to complete itself.

236732.en: Hey, {[character]player.name}. I really like your style... come talk to me when you have completed your objectives.

236733.en: {[character]player.name}! You're back! If there is anything you need, just ask. But you are going to finish your current mission, right?

236734.en: Great to see you, {[character]player.name}, as always. I have to assume there's a good reason that you've come back before finishing your current mission??

236735.en: You do know you haven't finished your current mission for me, right?

236736.en: {[character]player.name}, come talk to me when you finish your current mission.

236737.en: You need to finish your current mission. Don't talk to me until then.

236740.en: Good good, now get out there and give me some results.

236744.en: Now be careful out there, you hear me?

236746.en: I knew I could count on you.

236747.en: Great.  I know I can trust you with this, mate.

236749.en: Wonderful.  I expect a quick result with you on the job.

236750.en: Fabulous.  I couldn't have asked for a better man for the job.

236751.en: Not bad.  Get back to me later for another assignment will you?

236752.en: Nice work.  I'm starting to like your style.

236753.en: Thanks, your services to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} are duly appreciated.

236754.en: Thank you.  Your accomplishment has been noted and saved into our database.

236756.en: Thanks, I really appreciate your help.

236760.en: Thank you very much, I really appreciate it.

236761.en: Well done!  Take this reward and my gratitude as well.

236762.en: It's a pleasure doing business with you.

236763.en: Excellent work!  Care for another assignment?

236764.en: I look forward to your next visit.

236765.en: Again you finish the job right on time.  Keep this up and I'll probably get a promotion.

236766.en: I thank you from the bottom of my heart.

236767.en: If only I had more excellent pilots like you, {[character]player.name} ...

236768.en: Your talents as a pilot never cease to amaze me.  Keep up the good work!

236769.en: I am in your debt {[character]player.name}.  If you ever need anything, just look me up.

236770.en: Sorry, I have no jobs for the general public.

236774.en: {agentFactionName} does not provide work to the general public.

236775.en:
Hello, {[character]player.name}. I was given the assignment of handing out a valuable item to loyal supporters of {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name}. If you know of someone who has proven him or herself time and time again for {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} then point that person to me and perhaps we can come to an 'arrangement' ...

You on the other hand do not meet my requirements or have already received my offer.

236776.en:
You haven't heard? Gigantic harvestable gas clouds have been discovered here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}! All you need is a Gas Cloud Harvester module and the persistence to find one of these clouds and you'll make a fortune! And if you have a Starbase or Outpost nearby, you might even be able to create valuable boosters out of the chemicals. Well, as long as you have a blueprint.

I've managed to bribe the local pirate captains so that they'll leave me alone, but I'm worried about going deeper into {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. It's pretty dangerous out there.

236777.en: I take it you are back for some more research?  If so then I'll see if I can assist you.

236778.en: Why hello there.  What do you want?

236779.en: If you're here to find an excuse to show off those big, shiny weapons of yours, then I suggest you go find some nincompoop working for the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} military and leave me alone.  If not, then I might lend you an ear, depending on your worth to me.

236780.en: You just interrupted me from my studies.  This better be good ...

236781.en: I take it you are interested in scientific studies.  Perhaps I can be of assistance.

236782.en: Ah, how lucky I am to see you again!  Then again, luck is an expression for the simple minded, as all occurances can easily be explained with mathematical calculations. Oh what am I rambling about, please have a seat and tell me what is on your mind.

236783.en: Welcome, fellow colleague.  I guess you came to discuss my new theory on quantum mechanics, or are you here on other business?

236784.en: It's always a pleasure meeting you, {[character]player.name}.  I suppose you are here for some research, or some work perhaps?

236785.en: What planet were you born on?  Check your standings next time or I'll drill a hole in you.

236787.en: Have you even bothered to check your standings?

236788.en: You've got a lot of nerve, showing your face around here.

236790.en: I don't know you well enough to accept your money. Try seeking out an agent further down the corporate ladder until your standings have improved.

236791.en: Your money isn't good enough. Try seeking out an agent further down the corporate ladder until your standings have improved.

236792.en: Nobody sent you? I only work with people I trust. Talk to one of my subordinates until your standings have improved.

236793.en: Too bad, I'll try to find someone else then for that job.

236794.en: Bah, that mission wasn't that bad. Oh well, wait a bit and I'll come up with something else.

236796.en: Well, don't expect me to come up with something as good later on.

236798.en: Sorry, kid, nothing at the moment. Could you come back later?

236799.en: I'm sorry, but what I've got is promised to another pilot already. Could you come back later?

236800.en: I had a hunch you wouldn't pull through.

236802.en: Your wayward ways displease me, young one.

236804.en:
Yes, I have something for you.

{missionBriefingText}

236806.en:
I have just the thing you want.

{missionBriefingText}

236807.en:
Something just came up that's right up your alley.

{missionBriefingText}

236808.en:
For you, my friend, there's always something.

{missionBriefingText}

236809.en:
Here is a mission suited for someone of your caliber.

{missionBriefingText}

236810.en: Come to do a little research eh?  I'm a busy {[character]agentID.gender -> "man", "girl"}, but I guess I can spare a few moments of my time.

236811.en: Good job!  I don't know how we'd be able to complete this research project without you!

236812.en: Nice work.  Our research will definitely benefit from this.

236827.en: What was that? I did not get your last transmission.

236828.en: I don't have any more datacores to sell for now. You should try again tomorrow.

236829.en:
Subject: Dark Blood Alpha (ID: Modified Inquisitor)
Military Specifications: Frigate-class vessel. Veteran-level crew.
Additional Intelligence: The Dark Blood Alpha is an Inquisitor variant designed for a single purpose: lead blitzkrieg raids through empire space. Taking after capsuleer tactics, the Dark Blood Alpha coordinates groups of fast-attack frigates known as wolf packs. Wolf packs swarm larger targets, providing too many fast moving targets for the enemy weapons to track. The Dark Blood Alpha is crewed almost exclusively by veterans of past raids, making this ship the most dangerous opponent on the field.
Analyst Fawlon, Ministry of Assessment.
Authorized for capsuleer dissemination.

236830.en:
Subject: Dread Guristas Irregular (ID: Modified Worm)
Military Specifications: Frigate-class vessel. Veteran-level crew.
Additional Intelligence: First encountered in YC112, the Irregular is an attack frigate modified for fast assault and first response action. A tritanium-reinforced hull improves survivability, as does an experimental Guristas Production Atlas capacitor. Each Irregular is, ironically, crewed by seasoned combat veterans. The average total experience of an Irregular crew is 90 years. This experience gap gives the Irregular an 83% higher survivability rating than the average Guristas frigate crew.
Comparative Intelligence Specialist Ahelen, Wiyrkomi Peace Corps.
Authorized for capsuleer dissemination.

236831.en: I hope those datacores will come in handy for you.

236849.en: You have killed the NPC named 'Kill me' and are receiving this message.

236851.en:
The Dark Blood Alpha has been destroyed.

The Covenant really should learn not to mess with capsuleers.

Don't forget to search the wreckage for modules.

236852.en:
The Irregular has been eliminated. The State can focus its resources elsewhere.

And you can focus on robbing the Irregular's wreckage of valuable prizes.

236853.en: I'm sorry pilot, but you do not have the required standings to receive any missions from me. You will need to raise your standings by doing missions for lower-ranked agents. Use the <url=localsvc:method=OpenAgency>Agency</url> to locate agents that are available to you.

236867.en:
Between their extreme religious views and their fixation on capsuleer blood, it can be easy to forget the "raider" part of the Blood Raider Covenant. Blood Raider wolf packs are a deadly reminder of this.

Should any CONCORD or otherwise friendly vessel encounter a raiding party, it is recommended that any Dark Blood Alpha encountered be eliminated on sight.

DED Threat Assessment: 3 of 10

236868.en: Those big ships were brought down by a well-organized group of small frigates. Wolf pack tactics. Expect more fighting.

236869.en: The Dark Blood Alpha is based in the next pocket. Removing its influence will prevent these raids from reaching further.

236870.en:
The Guristas Pirates, despite being an extremely modern and high-tech faction in their own right, often turn to old tactics to foil their Caldari Navy foes. The most common tactic is to launch a series of guerilla raids -- led by a Dread Guristas Irregular -- on numerous soft targets. State forces become harried and stretched thin, allowing the pirates to carry out their real objectives with minimal inference.

DED Threat Assessment: 3 of 10

236871.en: So an entire Caldari station is a "soft target"? The DED needs to update its intel.

236872.en:
You have found the Dread Guristas Irregular and its support wing.

Kill them all.

236874.en: With you and me working together, I'm sure there will be marvelous breakthroughs.

236875.en: You don't have sufficient skill as a Research Project Manager to handle any more research projects.

236876.en: You don't have the skills to match mine.

236877.en: I'm sorry you feel that way, but alas, our research hadn't gotten anywhere yet so no harm done.

236980.en:
Federation Minuteman is the lowest commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks immediately below Defender Lieutenant.

"The Federation is not a defined region of space, of planets, of mountains, rivers, or woods. It is a vision."
- President of the Federation, Arlette Villers. CE 23154.6.2

236981.en:
Defender Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Federation Minuteman and immediately below Guardian Lieutenant.

"The laws of the Federation were written for the good of the many. Not the good of the Gallente nor the good of the Caldari. Hopefully, we can help them remember this."
- Gallente Senator Fronte Belliare, Senate session 23154/T3782. CE 23154.11.21

236982.en:
Guardian Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Defender Lieutenant and immediately below Lieutenant Sentinel.

"You have long since made your choice. What you make now is a mistake"
- Excerpt from the Federation Presidents response to the Caldari Proclamation of Secession. CE 23154.11.22

236983.en:
Lieutenant Sentinel is a junior commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Guardian Lieutenant and immediately below Shield Commander.

“They seek to fragment the Federation for their own selfish pride. Take their planet, strangle it and let's see how proud they stand after.”
- Vice Admiral Eisen Piroit, Addressing the Senate. CE 23154.11.28

236984.en:
Shield Commander is a commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Lieutenant Sentinel and immediately below Aegis Commander.

"A moment of silence is not enough. For their crimes, we must make the Caldari silence permanent."
- Luc Duvailer, newly sworn in President of the Federation, after the Nouvelle Rouvenor attack. CE 23155.1.15

236985.en:
Aegis Commander is a commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Shield Commander and immediately below Vice Commander

[04:00][Command] Orbital Bombardment to begin T minus one hour
[04:05][Command] Fleet begin deployment into close orbit
[04:40][Command] Begin Lock Targets. Orbital spread. Pattern Delta-Four-Two
[04:59][Command] Admiral Signals: For the people of Nouvelle Rouvenor
[05:00][Command] Authorize weapons free. Execute bombardment
- Fleet Log, Caldari Prime Orbital Bombardment. CE 23155.1.17

236986.en:
Vice Commander is a senior commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Aegis Commander and immediately below Major General.

"The savages have murdered the only ones with any sense among them. They lit the fire, now they will burn in it."
- Senator Fronte Belliare, Morning of Reasoning. CE 23155.2.10

236987.en:
Major General is a senior commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Vice Commander and immediately below Lieutenant General.

"This Federation is now at war. We have no time for dissenters, our Admirals will follow the will of this government or we will replace them."
- Hume Roir, newly appointed Gallente Minster of Defense. CE 23155.2.18

236988.en:
Lieutenant General is a senior commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Major General and immediately below Luminaire General.

"He is a cunning one this Tovil-Toba, but he can not evade us forever and his destruction will serve as an example to all Caldari."
- Admiral Eisen Piroit, Gallente Navy. CE 23155.3.10

236989.en:
Luminaire General is the most senior commissioned rank in the Federal Defense Union. It ranks above Lieutenant General.

"Hueromont was our failure yes - our failure to strike harder and strike faster to destroy those traitorous bastards where they stand"
- Luc Duvailer, President of the Federation. CE 23155.3.16

236990.en:
Paladin Crusader is the lowest commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks immediately below Templar Lieutenant.

"I will not hesitate when the test of Faith finds me, for only the strongest conviction will open the gates of paradise. My Faith in you is absolute; my sword is Yours, My God, and Your will guides me now and for all eternity."
- The Scriptures, The Prophet Kuria, "Paladin's Creed"

236991.en:
Templar Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Paladin Crusader and immediately below Cardinal Lieutenant.

"War is not hell, far from it. War is beautiful. War is divine."
- Grand Admiral Mekioth Sarum, excerpt from a commencement speech to Paladin graduates of the Imperial Academy. CE 23215

236992.en:
Cardinal Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Templar Lieutenant and immediately below Arch Lieutenant.

"Surround yourself with the faithful, stand together, for there is no strength like it under the heavens."
- The Scriptures, Book of Missions, 71:21

236993.en:
Arch Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Cardinal Lieutenant and immediately below Imperial Major.

"The word of the Lord is pure,
It is a shield for the faithful,
Brought unto men by the Angels,
As a guiding light in the darkness "
- The Scriptures, Book of the Prophet Anoyia, 8:15

236994.en:
Imperial Major is a commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Arch Lieutenant and immediately below Marshal Commander.

"God's compassion is all encompassing; His vengeance, all consuming."
- Grand Admiral Sundara The Kor-Azor charge. YC 110.6.10

236995.en:
Marshal Commander is a commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Imperial Major and immediately below Imperator Commander.

"And the Lord spoke to him from the heavens,
Described to him his holy purpose,
Bestowed upon him the wisdom,
Of God's holy embrace."

- The Scriptures, Gheinok the First, 2:8

236996.en:
Imperator Commander is a commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Marshal Commander and immediately below Tribunus Colonel.

"To know the true path, but yet, to never follow it. That is possibly the gravest sin"
- The Scriptures, Book of Missions, 13:21

236997.en:
Tribunus Colonel is a senior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Imperator Commander and immediately below Legatus Commodore.

"Assign turrets one through seven, radio crystals, designate target Omega-One!"
"Target Omega-One locked!"
"For the Emperor"
"Fire!"

- Opening salvo of the Battle of Vak'Aioth

236998.en:
Legatus Commodore is a senior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Tribunus Colonel and immediately below Divine Commodore.

"By His light, and His will"
- The Scriptures, Gheinok the First, 12:32

236999.en:
Divine Commodore is the most senior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Legatus Commodore.

"Run and you shall be crushed.
Stand and you shall fall.
Kneel and you shall be saved."
- Emperor Arrach Sarum. CE 21423

237000.en:
Nation Warrior is the lowest commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks immediately below Spike Lieutenant.

"Though free I am bound by the chains of my brothers"
- Inscription from a stone in the Remembering

237001.en:
Spike Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Nation Warrior and immediately below Spear Lieutenant.

"At this exact junction in history we have within our grasp the means to loosen our tormentors' hold and win freedom for our kin. Opportunities are there to be taken.
Brothers, we must rise."
- Maleatu Shakor, Republic Parliament Head Speaking before the Tribal Council November 27th. YC 107

237002.en:
Spear Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Spike Lieutenant and immediately below Venge Captain.

"The initial volleys neutralized sixty-eight separate defense batteries while removing a mere ninety-eight thousand Minmatar from the viable worker stock. Praise unto God."
- Intercepted Amarr Navy transmission during orbital bombardment of "Eanna", Planet VI, The Hror System

237003.en:
Venge Captain is a junior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Spear Lieutenant and immediately below Lance Commander.

"The holder stood atop his tower and preached salvation to the baying horde of slaves below. In answer, Korgoth raised his fist and let out a roar of defiance. The throats of a thousand Minmatar joined him, tearing through the air in a wave of pure hatred."
- Battle of Ariti, "Tales of the Rebellion", Minmatar Archives

237004.en:
Lance Commander is a commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Venge Captain and immediately below Blade Commander.

"Their military handbook regulated the guarding of gates, chokepoints, treelines and skies. it neglected, however, to mention sewers."
- Commander Skioth, "Tales of the Rebellion", Minmatar Archives

237005.en:
Blade Commander is a commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Lance Commander and immediately below Talon Commander.

"Our people assaulted the ship en masse. Those with weapons fired at it, those without hurled whatever was at hand even though they knew such acts to be futile. This is how the last of the Amarrian ships fled our world"
- Unknown Author, "Tales of the Rebellion", Minmatar Archives

237006.en:
Talon Commander is a commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Blade Commander and immediately below Voshud Major.

"There were once men who stood strong against the Amarrians no matter what they threw at them. They never knelt before them, they never called them masters. These men were called the Defiants. We will carry their name into the heart of Amarr and make them tremble at the sound of it. We will stand victorious or we will die with our hands around the slavers throats."
- Karishal Muritor addressing his fleet before the strike on the Imperial Shipyards of Beloth Tor

237007.en:
Voshud Major is a senior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Talon Commander and immediately below Matar Colonel.

"The Matari spirit is an indomitable fire. Be sure when fanning those flames that you do not burn this world of ours down. Seeds cannot grow in a soil of ash."
- "The Elder's Tome", Matari Chronicles

237008.en:
Matar Colonel is a senior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Voshud Major and immediately below Valklear General.

"War is within our hearts. It is a raging beast which we must harness lest it consume us"
- "Teachings of Valla."

237009.en:
Valklear General is the most senior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Matar Colonel.

"We have struggled through pain and grief; we have faced our torments with unbowed heads; we have lived as men. And in the end, what counts is not the years in our lives, but the unyielding life in our years."
- Inscription from a stone in the Remembering

237010.en:
Protectorate Ensign is the lowest commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks immediately below Second Lieutenant.

"Slowly but surely we are betraying the legacy left to us, the children of the Raata. The light of the Caldari spirit grows ever darker under the encroaching shadow of our would-be masters. Our very identity as a people is being subsumed by the Federation and we must act to preserve it."
- Excerpt from a National Address, delivered by Kalaakiota CEO Matias Sobaseki. CE 23154.6.26

237011.en:
Second Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Protectorate Ensign and immediately below First Lieutenant.

"It is rather strange that the good of the many seems to constantly coincide with whatever policies weaken the Caldari, the Intaki, and the Mannar and keep them under the heel of the Gallente."
- Caldari Senator Kiriusu Otenga, Senate session 23154/T3782. CE 23154.11.21

237012.en:
First Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Second Lieutenant and immediately below Captain.

"We will not permit you to tell us how to be Caldari, and so you leave us with no choice"
- Excerpt from the Caldari Proclamation of Secession. CE 23154.11.22

237013.en:
Captain is a junior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above First Lieutenant and immediately below Major.

"We survived on this world for thousands of years without the Gallente. Do they think we will starve now?"
- Wiyrkomi CEO Taaiko Wiyrkomi, Response to the Gallente blockade of Caldari Prime. CE 23154.11.30

237014.en:
Major is a commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Captain and immediately below Lieutenant Colonel.

"They will retaliate. We must be prepared."
– Vice-Admiral Orlan Mito, Caldari Navy, Morning after the Nouvelle Rouvenor attack. CE 23155.1.14

237015.en:
Lieutenant Colonel is a commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Major and immediately below Colonel.

"Caldari Prime burns, those left behind are choking on the dust and ash that fills the air, and you demand our surrender? Is this a joke? You have only hardened our resolve. Every drop of blood you have taken from us will be repaid -- with interest."
- CEP response to Federation demands for unconditional surrender after initial bombardment of Caldari Prime. CE 23155.1.18

237016.en:
Colonel is a commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Lieutenant Colonel and immediately below Wing Commander.

"As we make the tea, you must take it. The Caldari way demands it."
- Matias Sobaseki, CEO of Kaalakiota, Morning of Reasoning. CE 23155.2.10

237017.en:
Wing Commander is a senior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Colonel and immediately below Strike Commander.

"Their fleet is in total control of Caldari Prime's Orbit. We're heavily outnumbered and outgunned. To be able to effectively evacuate the population we need exactly one month of complete orbital control. Ideas anyone?"
- Admiral Orlan Mito, Caldari High Command Session. CE 23155.2.21

237018.en:
Strike Commander is a senior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Wing Commander and immediately below Brigadier General.

"High command need more time to complete the evacuation. We shall provide."
- Admiral Yakiya Tovil-Toba's personal log entry #21A231. CE 23155.3.7

237019.en:
Brigadier General is the most senior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Strike Commander.

"Non-essential personnel, abandon ship."
- Admiral Yakiya Tovil-Toba's last command. CE 23155.3.15

237027.en: In space, we can hear you scream.

238864.en:
PLEX - Pilot License Extension PLEX is a commodity that can be stored, transported and traded on the market or through contracts. It can be used to add Clone State Omega time to your account or to unlock special character and account services. Passes and access to select events, in game and out, can also be purchased with PLEX. Account time: One PLEX is equal to 30 days of Clone State Omega time which can be added to your account by using the PLEX directly from your in-game inventory. Multiple character training: Activate 30 days of passive skill gain on additional characters on your account with PLEX. Character transfer: Transferring characters between two accounts can be paid for with PLEX. Character re-sculpt: Customize and recreate your character’s facial appearance. Convert to AURUM: PLEX can be exchanged for AURUM, the currency used in the Noble Exchange store where unique fashion accessories are sold.
Buying PLEX You can buy PLEX on the EVE market using ISK or securely on eveonline.com using conventional payment methods.

256407.en:
When the privileged and powerful of New Eden yearn for commodities beyond what is normally available on the public market, they turn to the Noble Exchange, a private bazaar of diverse goods governed by the aurum currency. The spectrum of merchandise stretches from current fashions to those that are exceptionally rare or of dubious legality.

These transactions are overseen and guaranteed by CONCORD, but due to the fact that only those with access to aurum and qualified merchant corporations may use the Noble Exchange, virtually all inconsistencies, loopholes, and exploits have been systematically eliminated.

257528.en:
This is the information hub for the war effort. In this panel you can enlist yourself or your corporation, and once enlisted access data and statistics about the war effort.

Individuals may enlist by leaving any current player corporations, ensuring their standing from this faction is above 0.5 and that they're not on a trial account; applications are processed immediately.

Directors and CEOs may enlist their entire corporation by leaving any current alliance and ensuring their corporate standing from this faction is above 0.5; applications are processed at downtime.

All enlisted players are in a state of permanent war with their enemies and may be attacked by enemy capsuleers at any time. They are also advised to avoid high security space (0.5 security and above) belonging to enemy factions, as those factions' navies will shoot on sight.

Enlisted players are empowered to take missions from agents in their Militia, and to assist in the capture of strategic locations. Missions are limited by ship type. Locations are exploration sites found using the onboard scanner, are limited by ship type and have proximity sensors on strategic capture sites that trigger a capturing timer.

For further information on all aspects of the war, please visit the knowledge base!

257853.en: All your ships and items throughout the universe can be viewed from within the assets window. Here you can see a categorized list of your items, on a station by station basis. You can also search for items you might have temporarily misplaced. Perhaps some treasure awaits you!

257855.en: Some items might generate a better profit when sold through auction. Using the contract system, you can auction off your items, exchange them for other items directly, set up part-exchange deals... the contract system gives you the flexibility to choose the right kind of deal for the situation. Countless deals are closed every day, relying on the contract system's rules to prevent swindles and scams. If you have a rare item, others might be willing to fight for it in an auction!

257857.en: Here within you can find tools to manage your corporation, or to set one up. You can also find the corporate registry, which enables you to either quickly find a corporation for yourself, or to list your own corporation to others. You can also manage all roles to your members, manage wars and take care of alliance needs.

257859.en: Your ships need to be fitted with weapons, defensive modules, cargo expanders, mining lasers and other equipment to reach their full potential. The fittings window grants you access to the ship's hardware, where you can install your equipment and view statistics like resistances, cargo space and more.

257861.en: Here within you can find information regarding your agent missions, your ongoing research as well as a list of all corporations that you have gained loyalty points with and how many. On this page you can find information related to the journal, tutorials, knowledgebase articles on how to operate and make best use of the journal.

257863.en: The market is a tool that nearly everyone accesses at on a daily basis. Whether it's to buy a new ship, acquire the latest in weapons technology or to trade countless other items with your fellow pilots. Here you can find it all, and here you can work the market to gain riches and fortune as a trader.

257865.en: Your ship can sustain damage in space and might need repairs. Stations often feature repairshops that can patch up your ships for a small fee.

257867.en: Your hard-earned ISK is stored in your wallet. It holds the balance sheet on your recent expenditures and earnings with detailed information on every entry. If you have access to the corporation wallet, here you can also look at similar information for your corporation.

257869.en: If you are searching for another capsuleer, a system or a corporation then you can use the search functionality here. You can also see your buddy list and your blocked list, a list of your agents and corporation members, and all the locations in space you might have bookmarked.

257871.en: For all your scientific and industry related ventures! You can initiate, monitor and finalize all your manufacturing and researching tasks from within the confines of the science & industry window.

257873.en: The map can show both your current solar system, and the whole universe. It provides you with information and statistics, and acts as a tool for planning your route around your constellation, region or between regions.

257875.en: The character sheet is one of the most important tools in EVE. Here you select skills for training, write your biography, and check on your attributes, clones, standings, employment history and more. It is a valuable source of information on your character development and should not be overlooked.

259046.en: The modern Caldari State was forged in war, a fact that shapes its society a great deal. They are determined and military minded, living their lives like they were at a constant brink of armed conflict. The result is a weird combination of aggressiveness and paranoia. The Caldari are widely regarded as fearsome fighters, be it in space or on the ground, and their high quality military hardware is much admired and imitated by the other empires, bar only the Jovians. The Caldari excel in missile manufacturing and very maneuverable and fast ships.

259047.en: The Minmatar society is a tribal one, although the widely different status of the race today has blurred this in the minds of some of them. Yet the tribal culture is very strong with most of them and they have managed to retain their customs remarkably well. So much so in fact that a Minmatar of any given tribe can travel the width of the world, visiting fellow tribesmen and always feel at home, whether he visits a wealthy merchant within the Gallente Federation, an unscrupulous pirate in the outer regions or even a slave within the Amarr Empire. The Minmatars are the most populous of the races, but also the most politically fragmented. Only a quarter of them reside in their official empire, the Minmatar Republic.
