1030781.en: Plagioclase is not amongst the most valuable ore types around, but it contains a large amount of Tritanium and is thus always in constant demand. It also yields some Mexallon. Available primarily in high security status star systems.

1030783.en: Spodumain is amongst the most desirable ore types around, as it contains high volumes of the most heavily demanded resource and some amounts of the more precious minerals. Huge volumes of Tritanium and moderate amounts of Isogen, Nocxium, Zydrine and Megacyte can be obtained by refining these rocks.

1030785.en: Kernite is a fairly common ore type that yields fair amounts of Mexallon and Isogen. Available primarily in low and null security status and wormhole systems.

1030787.en: Hedbergite is sought after for its high concentration of Pyerite and Nocxium. Available primarily in low security status star systems.

1030789.en: Arkonor is one of the rarest and most sought-after ores in the known universe. A sizable nugget of this can sweep anyone from rags to riches in no time. It has high amount of Megacyte, and also contains some Mexallon and Pyerite. Available primarily in null security status and wormhole systems.

1030791.en: Appearing en masse during the Drifter Crisis of YC127, tyranite is a s-type asteroid that has been bombarded by low-level blackbody radiation for millennia, turning its silicate-like surface regolith into eleutrium. Astrogeologists claim that this process occurred prior to tyranite asteroids appearing, wholly by unknown means. Due to the unknown conditions of its formation and appearance, astrogeologists fear this may be a unique opportunity. Additionally, its special properties break down when under pressure, making it incompressible. Tyranite is the only known source of eleutrium.

1030793.en: When griemeer was discovered in YC126, it took little time for miners to notice that the darker the crystals, the more isogen and, to a lesser extent, tritanium, it would yield. As it has a slight resemblance in texture to Liparer cheese, those obsessed with mining griemeer have been derisively nicknamed "cheesers" by rivals. Asteroid anomalies in null security space is where griemeer is generally found.

1030795.en: II-Grade griemeer is characterized by clear crystals that lack the milky whiteness of the common variant, and where the inky black cloudiness of the rarer versions is also absent. However, clear griemeer is still a fortunate find, as it has a 5% increased yield. Asteroid anomalies in null security space is where clear griemeer is generally found.

1030797.en: III-Grade griemeer with spots of darkness in its clear crystals is called inky griemeer and boasts a 10% extra yield. Asteroid anomalies in null security space is where inky griemeer is generally found.

1030799.en: IV-Grade griemeer, also called opaque griemeer, is the kind that lets no light through its crystals. Those lucky enough to find some will be rewarded with an additional 15% yield during refinement. Asteroid anomalies in null security space is where opaque griemeer is generally found.

1030801.en: Gneiss is a popular ore type because it holds significant volumes of three heavily used minerals, increasing its utility value. Flawed Gneiss however has the same properties as fools gold, in the sense that it looks like the original but is worth almost nothing in comparison.

1030803.en: Nocxite, discovered in YC126 due to new astrogeological surveying techniques, contains mostly nocxium with trace amounts of tritanium and pyerite. Even trace amounts of nocxite produces intoxicating fumes under atmospheric pressures, demanding special care when being handled planetside. Previous failures to appropriately vent the gasses have resulted in a number of workplace accidents and fatalities. Nocxite may be found in null security asteroid anomalies.

1030805.en: Fragrant or II-Grade nocxite has stronger hints of its intoxicating fumes under typical atmospheric pressure. Additionally, it yields 5% more minerals. Fragrant nocxite may be found in null security asteroid anomalies.

1030807.en: Unstable even in low-pressure environments, III-Grade or intoxicating nocxite rewards persistent miners with an additional 10% yield. Intoxicating nocxite may be found in null security asteroid anomalies.

1030809.en: Long-term exposure to IV-Grade nocxite at atmospheric pressure has a chance of causing a state of permanent stupor in those handling it akin to ambrosia. Despite the risk, many planetside miners consider the additional 15% return in mineral yield more than worth it. Ambrosial nocxite may be found in null security asteroid anomalies.

1030811.en: Scordite is amongst the most common ore types in the central regions of known universe. It has a fair bit of Tritanium and Pyerite. Good choice for those starting their mining careers. Available primarily in high security status star systems.

1030813.en: Hezorime, discovered in YC126, is a brittle ore that is sure to cut the unwary miner. The harder and sharper the ore, the better the yield. Hezorime refines into mostly zydrine, with small amounts of tritanium and isogen. Hezorime deposits may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies.

1030815.en: With a barely perceptible saw-like edge, miners lucky enough to notice III-Grade, or serrated, hezorime will be rewarded for their diligence with an additional 10% yield of minerals. Serrated hezorime deposits may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies.

1030817.en: IV-Grade hezorime should never be handled directly, as it is sharp enough to cut through protective gloves, flesh, and bone with incredible ease. Enterprising miners that are willing to risk fingers and limbs are rewarded with an additional 15% mineral yield. Sharp hezorime deposits may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies.

1030819.en: Ueganite is an ore discovered in YC126 due to improvements in astrogeological surveying technology. It is primarily composed of megacyte, with trace amounts of tritanium. Some miners have posited that ueganite forms when multiple metaliminal storms occur in a single system for an extended period of time, but astrogeologists have dismissed the hypothesis as mere conjecture and superstition based on valuable ueganite having diverse properties reminiscent of these storms. Ueganite may be found in asteroid anomalies within null security space.

1030821.en: It takes a keen eye to notice the tiny deposits that give II-Grade ueganite its foggy appearance. This minor variation indicates that it gives a 5% greater yield than its regular form. Foggy ueganite may be found in asteroid anomalies within null security space.

1030823.en: Overcast ueganite, the III-Grade variant of ueganite, has sparkling flecks throughout its composition, but lacks the stormy properties of its rarer variant. It produces an additional 10% mineral yield when refined. Overcast ueganite may be found in asteroid anomalies within null security space.

1030825.en: The sight of its subsurface lightning mineral veins, which gives IV-Grade or stormy ueganite its name, brings great joy to any miner. Stormy ueganite yields 15% more minerals than its base form when refined. Stormy ueganite may be found in asteroid anomalies within null security space.

1030827.en: Veldspar is the most common ore type in the central regions of known universe. It is still in constant demand as it holds a large portion of the much-used Tritanium mineral. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030829.en: This extremely rare and valuable variant of veldspar ore was recently discovered by ORE engineers during early field tests of new moon mining technology. Subsequent testing has confirmed that this ore produces 15% more minerals than standard veldspar when reprocessed. Veldspar is the most common ore type in the central regions of known universe. It is still in constant demand as it holds a large portion of the much-used Tritanium mineral. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030831.en: Scordite is amongst the most common ore types in the central regions of known universe. It has a fair bit of Tritanium and Pyerite. Good choice for those starting their mining careers. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030833.en: Massive or III-Grade scordite was the stuff of legend in the early days of space exploration, due to a 10% higher mineral yield than standard scordite. Though it has long since been taken over in value by other ores it still has a special place in the hearts of veteran miners. Scordite is amongst the most common ore types in the central regions of known universe. It has a fair bit of Tritanium and Pyerite. Good choice for those starting their mining careers. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030835.en: This extremely rare and valuable variant of scordite ore was recently discovered by ORE engineers during early field tests of new moon mining technology. Subsequent testing has confirmed that this ore produces 15% more minerals than standard scordite when reprocessed. Scordite is amongst the most common ore types in the central regions of known universe. It has a fair bit of Tritanium and Pyerite. Good choice for those starting their mining careers. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030837.en: III-Grade or viscous pyroxeres is the secret behind the success of ORE in the early days. ORE has since then moved into more profitable minerals, but viscous pyroxeres and its 10% higher mineral yield still holds a special place in the hearts of all miners dreaming of becoming the next mining moguls of EVE. Pyroxeres is a common ore available in all regions of space. It has fair amounts of Pyerite and Mexallon. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030839.en: This extremely rare and valuable variant of pyroxeres ore was recently discovered by ORE engineers during early field tests of new moon mining technology. Subsequent testing has confirmed that this ore produces 15% more minerals than standard pyroxeres when reprocessed. Pyroxeres is a common ore available in all regions of space. It has fair amounts of Pyerite and Mexallon. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030841.en: Kylixium, an ore discovered in YC126, is mostly composed of mexallon, with some tritanium and pyerite in smaller quantities. It is named for its clay-like properties and appearance. Kylixium may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030843.en: Kaolin or II-Grade kylixium is a rarer form of kylixium that yields a 5% increase in mineral content. It has more claylike properties than its prevalent form.Kaolin kylixium may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030845.en: With 10% more mineral content, III-Grade kylixium is colloquially recognized for its argil-like malleability. Argil kylixium may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030847.en: Extremely rich in mexallon, IV-Grade or adobe kylixium is considered a auspicious find amongst those who mine it. This form has a 15% greater yield than its everyday variety. Adobe kylixium may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030849.en: Nocxite, discovered in YC126 due to new astrogeological surveying techniques, contains mostly nocxium with trace amounts of tritanium and pyerite. Even trace amounts of nocxite produces intoxicating fumes under atmospheric pressures, demanding special care when being handled planetside. Previous failures to appropriately vent the gasses have resulted in a number of workplace accidents and fatalities. Nocxite may be found in null security asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030851.en: Fragrant or II-Grade nocxite has stronger hints of its intoxicating fumes under typical atmospheric pressure. Additionally, it yields 5% more minerals. Fragrant nocxite may be found in null security asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030853.en: Unstable even in low-pressure environments, III-Grade or intoxicating nocxite rewards persistent miners with an additional 10% yield. Intoxicating nocxite may be found in null security asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030855.en: Long-term exposure to IV-Grade nocxite at atmospheric pressure has a chance of causing a state of permanent stupor in those handling it akin to ambrosia. Despite the risk, many planetside miners consider the additional 15% return in mineral yield more than worth it. Ambrosial nocxite may be found in null security asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030857.en: Ueganite is an ore discovered in YC126 due to improvements in astrogeological surveying technology. It is primarily composed of megacyte, with trace amounts of tritanium. Some miners have posited that ueganite forms when multiple metaliminal storms occur in a single system for an extended period of time, but astrogeologists have dismissed the hypothesis as mere conjecture and superstition based on valuable ueganite having diverse properties reminiscent of these storms. Ueganite may be found in asteroid anomalies within null security space. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030859.en: It takes a keen eye to notice the tiny deposits that give II-Grade ueganite its foggy appearance. This minor variation indicates that it gives a 5% greater yield than its regular form. Foggy ueganite may be found in asteroid anomalies within null security space. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030861.en: Overcast ueganite, the III-Grade variant of ueganite, has sparkling flecks throughout its composition, but lacks the stormy properties of its rarer variant. It produces an additional 10% mineral yield when refined. Overcast ueganite may be found in asteroid anomalies within null security space. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030863.en: The sight of its subsurface lightning mineral veins, which gives IV-Grade or stormy ueganite its name, brings great joy to any miner. Stormy ueganite yields 15% more minerals than its base form when refined. Stormy ueganite may be found in asteroid anomalies within null security space. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030865.en: Hezorime, discovered in YC126, is a brittle ore that is sure to cut the unwary miner. The harder and sharper the ore, the better the yield. Hezorime refines into mostly zydrine, with small amounts of tritanium and isogen. Hezorime deposits may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030867.en: A minor step up from its more common variant, II-Grade hezorime has a dull finish and produces an additional 5% yield when refined. Dull hezorime deposits may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030869.en: "With a barely perceptible saw-like edge, miners lucky enough to notice III-Grade, or serrated, hezorime will be rewarded for their diligence with an additional 10% yield of minerals. Serrated hezorime deposits may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material."

1030871.en: IV-Grade hezorime should never be handled directly, as it is sharp enough to cut through protective gloves, flesh, and bone with incredible ease. Enterprising miners that are willing to risk fingers and limbs are rewarded with an additional 15% mineral yield. Sharp hezorime deposits may be found in null security space asteroid anomalies. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030873.en: When griemeer was discovered in YC126, it took little time for miners to notice that the darker the crystals, the more isogen and, to a lesser extent, tritanium, it would yield. As it has a slight resemblance in texture to Liparer cheese, those obsessed with mining griemeer have been derisively nicknamed "cheesers" by rivals. Asteroid anomalies in null security space is where griemeer is generally found. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030875.en: II-Grade griemeer is characterized by clear crystals that lack the milky whiteness of the common variant, and where the inky black cloudiness of the rarer versions is also absent. However, clear griemeer is still a fortunate find, as it has a 5% increased yield. Asteroid anomalies in null security space is where clear griemeer is generally found. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030877.en: III-Grade griemeer with spots of darkness in its clear crystals is called inky griemeer and boasts a 10% extra yield. Asteroid anomalies in null security space is where inky griemeer is generally found. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030879.en: IV-Grade griemeer, also called opaque griemeer, is the kind that lets no light through its crystals. Those lucky enough to find some will be rewarded with an additional 15% yield during refinement. Asteroid anomalies in null security space is where opaque griemeer is generally found. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030881.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles.  Due to its unique chemical composition and the circumstances under which it forms, blue ice contains more oxygen isotopes than any other ice asteroid.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030883.en:
Fairly rare and very valuable, Gelidus-type ice formations are a large-scale source of strontium clathrates, one of the rarest ice solids found in the universe, in addition to which they contain unusually large concentrations of heavy water and liquid ozone.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030885.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles.  Glacial masses are known to contain hydrogen isotopes in abundance, in addition to smatterings of heavy water and liquid ozone.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030887.en:
In areas with high concentrations of electromagnetic activity, ice formations such as this one, containing large amounts of heavy water and liquid ozone, are spontaneously formed during times of great electric flux.  Glare crust also contains a small amount of strontium clathrates.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030889.en:
When star fusion processes occur near high concentrations of silicate dust, such as those found in interstellar ice fields, the substance known as White Glaze is formed.  While White Glaze generally is extremely high in nitrogen-14 and other stable nitrogen isotopes, a few rare fragments, such as this one, have stayed free of radioactive contaminants and are thus richer in isotopes than their more impure counterparts.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030891.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles.  Glacial masses are known to contain hydrogen isotopes in abundance, but the high surface diffusion on this particular mass means it has considerably more than its coarser counterparts.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030893.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. Due to its unique chemical composition and the circumstances under which it forms, blue ice will, under normal circumstances, contain more oxygen isotopes than any other ice asteroid. This particular formation is an old one and therefore contains even more than its less mature siblings.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030895.en:
When star fusion processes occur near high concentrations of silicate dust, such as those found in interstellar ice fields, the substance known as White Glaze is formed.  White Glaze is extremely high in nitrogen-14 and other stable nitrogen isotopes, and is thus a necessity for the sustained operation of certain kinds of control tower.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030897.en: Hemorphite exists in many different color variations. Interestingly, the more colorful it becomes, the better yield it has. Radiant or III-Grade hemorphite has 10% better yield than its more bland brother. With a large portion of Nocxium, hemorphite is always a good find. It is common enough that even novice miners can expect to run into it. Hemorphite also has some amount of Isogen. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030899.en: This extremely rare and valuable variant of gneiss ore was recently discovered by ORE engineers during early field tests of new moon mining technology. Subsequent testing has confirmed that this ore produces 15% more minerals than standard gneiss when reprocessed. Gneiss is a popular ore type because it holds significant volumes of three heavily used minerals, increasing its utility value. It has quite a bit of Mexallon as well as some Pyerite and Isogen. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030901.en: Considered a worthless ore for years, dark ochre was ignored by most miners until improved reprocessing techniques managed to extract the huge amount of Isogen and Mexallon inside it. Dark ochre also contains useful amounts of Nocxium. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030903.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. These crystalline formations can be found scattered around many an ice field, and are known as the universe's primary source of helium isotopes.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030905.en:
Dark glitter is one of the rarest of the interstellar ices, formed only in areas with large amounts of residual electrical current.  Little is known about the exact way in which it comes into being; the staggering amount of liquid ozone to be found inside one of these rocks makes it an intriguing mystery for stellar physicists and chemists alike.  In addition, it contains large amounts of heavy water and a decent measure of strontium clathrates.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030907.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. These crystalline formations can be found scattered around many an ice field and are known as the universe's primary source of helium isotopes.  Due to environmental factors, this fragment's isotope deposits have become even richer than its regular counterparts'.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030909.en:
Fairly rare and very valuable, Gelidus-type ice formations are a large-scale source of strontium clathrates, one of the rarest ice solids found in the universe, in addition to which they contain unusually large concentrations of heavy water and liquid ozone.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1030915.en:
The universe's richest known source of strontium clathrates, Krystallos ice formations are formed only in areas where a very particular combination of environmental factors are at play.  Krystallos compounds also include quite a bit of liquid ozone.

This ore has been compressed into a much more dense version.

1030917.en: This is the most common form of Mordunium ore with a standard relative density of Pyerite mineral content. Mordunium is a rare ore that contains a useful concentration of the Pyerite mineral in relatively dense deposits. Though found in remote clusters of asteroids, the ore is readily transportable and easily refined into the useful mineral it contains. A special "Deep Space Survey" partnership between Ducia Foundry, Eifyr and Co., Mordu's Legion, and Ytiri was forged by the four members of the Upwell Consortium in order to carry out prospecting expeditions at the edges of empire space, deep in nullsec, and even beyond to wormhole space. In YC124, these survey missions were able to identify a number of rare ore types, each containing an unusually pure deposit of a standard mineral. Mordunium was the Pyerite-bearing ore discovered by this group and was named for the Mordu's Legion contribution to the surveying expeditions. Available primarily in nullsec and W-space systems containing A0 (Blue Small) stars, as well as surveyed locations on the borders of empire and nullsec space.

1030949.en: While fairly invisible to all but the most experienced miners, there are significant molecular differences between arkonor and crimson arkonor, colloquially referred to as such because of the blood-red veins running through it. Available primarily in null security status and wormhole systems.

It has high amount of Megacyte, and also contains some Mexallon and Pyerite. Available primarily in null security status and wormhole systems.

It also contains a decent amount of Mexallon. Available primarily in null security status and wormhole systems.

1030955.en: III-Grade bistot, also known as monoclinic bistot, is a variant of bistot with a slightly different crystal structure. It also contains a decent amount of Mexallon. Available primarily in null security status and wormhole systems.

Valuable deposits of Pyerite can also be found within this rare ore. Available primarily in low security status star systems.

Crokite is a very heavy ore that is always in high demand because it has the largest ratio of Nocxium and Mexallon for any ore in the known universe. Valuable deposits of Pyerite can also be found within this rare ore. Available primarily in low security status star systems.

Considered a worthless ore for years, dark ochre was ignored by most miners until improved reprocessing techniques managed to extract the huge amount of Isogen and Mexallon inside it. Dark ochre also contains useful amounts of Nocxium. Available primarily in low security status star systems.

This ore's 10% higher mineral yield makes it more than worth the effort required to find it. Considered a worthless ore for years, dark ochre was ignored by most miners until improved reprocessing techniques managed to extract the huge amount of Isogen and Mexallon inside it. Dark ochre also contains useful amounts of Nocxium. Available primarily in low security status star systems.

1031175.en: This is the most common form of Mordunium ore with a standard relative density of Pyerite mineral content. Mordunium is a rare ore that contains a useful concentration of the Pyerite mineral in relatively dense deposits. Though found in remote clusters of asteroids, the ore is readily transportable and easily refined into the useful mineral it contains. A special "Deep Space Survey" partnership between Ducia Foundry, Eifyr and Co., Mordu's Legion, and Ytiri was forged by the four members of the Upwell Consortium in order to carry out prospecting expeditions at the edges of empire space, deep in nullsec, and even beyond to wormhole space. In YC124, these survey missions were able to identify a number of rare ore types, each containing an unusually pure deposit of a standard mineral. Mordunium was the Pyerite-bearing ore discovered by this group and was named for the Mordu's Legion contribution to the surveying expeditions. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1031207.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. Due to its unique chemical composition and the circumstances under which it forms, blue ice will, under normal circumstances, contain more oxygen isotopes than any other ice asteroid. This particular formation is an old one and therefore contains even more than its less mature siblings.

Available in <color='0xFFFF0000'>0.0</color> security status solar systems or lower.

1031209.en:
When star fusion processes occur near high concentrations of silicate dust, such as those found in interstellar ice fields, the substance known as White Glaze is formed. While White Glaze generally is extremely high in nitrogen-14 and other stable nitrogen isotopes, a few rare fragments, such as this one, have stayed free of radioactive contaminants and are thus richer in isotopes than their more impure counterparts.

Available in <color='0xFFFF0000'>0.0</color> security status solar systems or lower.

1031211.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. Glacial masses are known to contain hydrogen isotopes in abundance, but the high surface diffusion on this particular mass means it has considerably more than its coarser counterparts.

Available in <color='0xFFFF0000'>0.0</color> security status solar systems or lower.

1031213.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. These crystalline formations can be found scattered around many an ice field and are known as the universe's primary source of helium isotopes. Due to environmental factors, this fragment's isotope deposits have become even richer than its regular counterparts'.

Available in <color='0xFFFF0000'>0.0</color> security status solar systems or lower.

1031215.en: This extremely rare and valuable variant of dark ochre ore was recently discovered by ORE engineers during early field tests of new moon mining technology. Subsequent testing has confirmed that this ore produces 15% more minerals than standard dark ochre when reprocessed. Considered a worthless ore for years, dark ochre was ignored by most miners until improved reprocessing techniques managed to extract the huge amount of Isogen and Mexallon inside it. 1031371.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. Due to its unique chemical composition and the circumstances under which it forms, blue ice contains more oxygen isotopes than any other ice asteroid.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1031373.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. These crystalline formations can be found scattered around many an ice field, and are known as the universe's primary source of helium isotopes.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1031375.en:
Dark glitter is one of the rarest of the interstellar ices, formed only in areas with large amounts of residual electrical current. Little is known about the exact way in which it comes into being; the staggering amount of liquid ozone to be found inside one of these rocks makes it an intriguing mystery for stellar physicists and chemists alike. In addition, it contains large amounts of heavy water and a decent measure of strontium clathrates.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1031377.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. These crystalline formations can be found scattered around many an ice field and are known as the universe's primary source of helium isotopes. Due to environmental factors, this fragment's isotope deposits have become even richer than its regular counterparts'.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1031379.en:
The universe's richest known source of strontium clathrates, Krystallos ice formations are formed only in areas where a very particular combination of environmental factors are at play. Krystallos compounds also include quite a bit of liquid ozone.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1031381.en:
When star fusion processes occur near high concentrations of silicate dust, such as those found in interstellar ice fields, the substance known as White Glaze is formed. While White Glaze generally is extremely high in nitrogen-14 and other stable nitrogen isotopes, a few rare fragments, such as this one, have stayed free of radioactive contaminants and are thus richer in isotopes than their more impure counterparts.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1031383.en:
Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. Glacial masses are known to contain hydrogen isotopes in abundance, but the high surface diffusion on this particular mass means it has considerably more than its coarser counterparts.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

Interstellar ices are formed by accretion of gas molecules onto silicate dust particles. Due to its unique chemical composition and the circumstances under which it forms, blue ice will, under normal circumstances, contain more oxygen isotopes than any other ice asteroid. This particular formation is an old one and therefore contains even more than its less mature siblings.

This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

1031466.en:
Auroras, or polar lights, are a universal concept and shared experience among the peoples of New Eden. The heavily-populated terrestrial home planets are particularly noted for stories and myths involving these striking, dancing lights in the sky.

To the Amarr, the aurora are linked to ancient religious stories and are sometimes known as "Sefrim Banners", alluding to the angelic figures considered messengers from God. A tradition of the appearance of these lights heralding divine approval for the armies of Amarr during the Reclaiming of Athra is well attested.

For the Caldari, the polar lights are the enigmatic "Flame Wind", a mysterious force in the animistic mythology of Caldari Prime's pre-industrial era. On the cold Caldari home world, the appearance of the aurora was associated with unusual weather and sudden migrations of animals.

The various nations of Gallente Prime had their ancient legends about polar lights but knew the aurora to be an interaction of atmosphere, magnetic fields and stellar winds from the time of the "Airship Wars". Viewing aurora on airship trips to the polar regions of Gallente Prime is a popular tourist activity on the planet.

The Minmatar have a somewhat mixed viewpoint on aurora, with some believing that such lights were seen during the storms that wracked Matar during the "Day of Darkness" that heralded the Amarr invasion. However, most think this notion misreads the fragmentary tales of what happened in those times. The traditional view of the polar lights, at least for tribes such as the Brutor and Sebiestor, is that they represent a "standing place gathering" or moot of tribal spirits.

At the time of the Yoiul Festival, the aurora lights of the worlds of New Eden are one reminder of the shared history of the people of the cluster and have becomes a symbol to some of their universal connections with one another.

For the Caldari, the polar lights are the enigmatic "Flame Wind", a mysterious force in the animistic mythology of Caldari Prime's pre-industrial era. On the cold Caldari home world, the appearance of the aurora was associated with unusual weather and sudden migrations of animals.

The various nations of Gallente Prime had their ancient legends about polar lights but knew the aurora to be an interaction of atmosphere, magnetic fields and stellar winds from the time of the "Airship Wars". Viewing aurora on airship trips to the polar regions of Gallente Prime is a popular tourist activity on the planet.

The Minmatar have a somewhat mixed viewpoint on aurora, with some believing that such lights were seen during the storms that wracked Matar during the "Day of Darkness" that heralded the Amarr invasion. However, most think this notion misreads the fragmentary tales of what happened in those times. The traditional view of the polar lights, at least for tribes such as the Brutor and Sebiestor, is that they represent a "standing place gathering" or moot of tribal spirits.

At the time of the Yoiul Festival, the aurora lights of the worlds of New Eden are one reminder of the shared history of the people of the cluster and have becomes a symbol to some of their universal connections with one another.

1031885.en:
A well-used camera drone initially recovered from the wreckage of a keepstar in R-AG7W. The ID on the drone shows its owner was part of an independent news team labelled as “Warlock Industries”. 

The drone was scorched while taking an extreme close-up of the explosive force from the Keepstar reactor going critical. 

It is no longer functional, serving as a reminder that empires rise and fall, but news coverage is eternal.

1031890.en:
A data pad containing a set of exhaustingly detailed and exactingly precise evacuation plans which reference the relocation of a large alliance based somewhere in the eastern side of New Eden. 

The data pad was discovered in the Lost & Found bin at the InterBus terminal of the Perkone Factory station in Uemon, the owner apparently forgetting to take it with them when they departed on their trip to Perrigen Falls.

1031892.en: A concentrated, somewhat viscous liquid which, when mixed with water, can be used to create a large amount of bubbles. The shipping label on the side establishes the destination as R-AG7W. The sender is only identified by the initials “A.E.”

1031894.en: A stunning collection of watercolor paintings, fit to adorn the walls of any high-ranking official, signed off by an artist abbreviated as “L.G.”

1031896.en: A small, unpainted miniature that appears to have been separated from a larger collection of miniatures. It would be an ideal tool for a strategist to develop invasion plans in a war room, a tactician to choreograph the movements of a ship in close combat, or even a board game.

1031898.en: Engineering Log, Unsanctioned Entry I thought I’d seen it all after twenty-seven years crawling around afterburner housings, but today Command asked for the impossible: swap the core engine assembly of a Rifter while in mid-warp. I remember clamping my boots to the plating, the hull vibrating like a living thing. The stars stretched into razor-straight lines around me as I opened the access panel. The old engine screamed, the new one hummed, and for a moment, I swear I could see the ship splitting into two timelines, one flying with me, one without. The wrench slipped from my hand and drifted… upward? downward? sideways? Hard to tell in a reality that had forgotten the meaning of directions. The warp tunnel twisted, the engine flared, and everything went white. I woke up at my desk, drooling on the maintenance report I’d fallen asleep reading. Turns out I didn’t replace an engine mid-warp, I just need to stop drinking Quafe.

1031902.en: Printed on stark, no-nonsense graphene paper, this urgent application packet is stamped repeatedly with PRIORITY OVERRIDE sigils and more than one impatient annotation in red text. Intended for corporations seeking immediate refuge within a new alliance, the form demands everything at once: fleet readiness numbers, logistical capacity, diplomatic liabilities, outstanding grudges, and a sworn statement that any fires currently burning are under control. Near the bottom, a desperate handwritten note has been scribbled into the margin: “Please approve quickly. Situation evolving. Assets mobile.” Filing this document is often considered the first true loyalty test: if you can survive the paperwork, you can survive the alliance.

1031906.en:
Initially recovered from a storage locker in Jita, which had been seized due to unpaid fees, and its contents put up for auction. 

The storage locker came with a shipping docket listing its contents and their origin as the system of Niarja, not long after its occupation by the Triglavians. 

Rather oddly, it seems that many of the jars are empty, and those that do still have a filling seem to be remarkably well preserved and have a warm reddish glow to them.

It’s labelled as all-natural and safe to eat… probably.

1031926.en:
In the middle of YC127, at the conclusion of the “War in Heaven” within the Anoikis cluster, the alliance "We Forsakened Few" was evicted from their home in J121006 - a Class 4 pulsar system known as Hoth. 
Defending forces, led by CEO "Dread Father" lennox, mounted a formidable stand around their heavily fortified Keepstar grid, but eventually succumbed to the attacking forces of a coalition led by the Hard Knocks alliance that included allies from Lazerhawks, No Vacancies, Blue Loot Not Included, Czarna Kompania and others.

1031928.en:
Initially found in an auxiliary broadcast studio at the Expert Distribution Warehouse in Siseide, where the walls of the studio had been plastered with cartoonish anthropomorphic characters in a storyboard style. The foreword mentions that it was originally intended to appear in a black-market show called “The Cope,” but had been adapted for scripted media. 

It appears to be largely propaganda focused on how various low-security-based alliances would deliberately corrupt a solar system to facilitate the use of “bubbles” then “Yolo Dreads for fun”. The reductive instructions that follow seem to depict various suggested methods for others to “enjoy themselves” alongside some scripture about a “Rat God”.

1031929.en: A Capsuleer’s Guide To Dropping Dreads

1031930.en: “..and that’s how you can find the answer to life, the universe, and everything” - Excerpt deep from inside New Eden's largest public GalNet repository, recently overhauled and now fully funded, operated and maintained by EVE University.

1031932.en:
It appears to be a very worn-out, simple, blue, three-button console. You can discern particular iconography on each of the three buttons, but it remains unclear what exactly it is depicting. 

Following the wiring out of the bottom of the console, it appears there are three labels: “Jump, Bridge, and Coffee”. As to which button does what, only its original owner could ever know…

1031934.en: A weathered fragment taken from the storied 1DQ1-A Keepstar, its scorched plating still radiating the long memory of a structure that never slept. Mixed within the plating are specks of Rifter debris.

1031936.en:
An audio log that displays the logo of some sort of reptile. Upon playing it, it seems to repeat the same word over and over:

Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard Lizard

1031939.en: A well-used, slightly dog-eared single-page permit allowing its bearer to safely mine in the location it has been issued in. The wording of the document appears to state phrases like “officially certified” and “meets safety standards” multiple times, yet it offers no friend-or-foe recognition or electronic tagging for approval, suggesting that whoever issued this permit intended for it to be only verifiable once recovered from the owner’s ship wreckage.

1031941.en: Confiscated by the SCC from an Opux Luxury Yacht passing through the system of Manarq, a few boxes of them seem to have found their way onto the open market. Created to be placed directly on top of the user's head, the dual transmission pylons provide a connection for direct neural stimulation and transmission via bone conduction, allowing the operator to watch and hear the Alliance Tournament without interfering with those around them. This particular variant appears to have been tuned to receive the broadcast of Alliance Tournament XXI and, since the conclusion of the broadcast, seems to be malfunctioning, repeating the same 2 words on a loop: Kishi Kishi Meow Meow.

1031942.en: Counterfeit Alliance Tournament Emergency Auxiliary Rebroadcasting System

1031943.en: A small-scale replica model of the Fallen Capsuleers Memorial from the system of Molea. It emits a warm glow and has a parting eulogy inscribed on it: ”Eyes forward, capsuleer, the cyno is not yet lit. Consider your modules, your rigs and ammo before you undock, for the cyno is not yet lit. Break free of the station and witness the universe before you, For the cyno is not yet lit. Set your ship to fly through the vastness while you wait, For the cyno is not yet lit. Pay attention, capsuleer, for those who have gone before you call for you to join them. The cyno is now lit.”

1031944.en: For Those Lost, But Never Forgotten

1031945.en: A container with what appears to be a micro-wormhole inside. When observed, the wormhole seems to vanish, but when left to its own devices, a very small negative pressure vacuum seems to be exerted on the inside of the casing. It simultaneously acknowledges the existence of wormholes, but also provides no visual proof of their existence.

1031947.en: A scrap of paper containing a code phrase said to grant the holder access to a very exclusive social club. The coordinates for the club don’t match any location in known space. The text on the page reads: “Tell em' Captator sent you. Praise Bob.”

1031949.en: Bound in weathered synth-leather and secured with a heat-resistant clasp, this worn little cookbook is beloved by pilots with a sweet tooth and too much downtime in deep space. Its pages are filled with recipes for comforting snacks, including one legendary delicacy: a filled lattice of thin, crispy batter pressed together until warm and chewy. The margins are cluttered with notes about optimal heating cycles, field-tested substitutions, and the perfect ratios of sugar and flour. Rumor has it the original recipe came from a Thukker engineer who refused to share it unless bribed with ship parts.

1031950.en: The Capsuleer’s Confectionary Codex – Field Edition

1031951.en: Initially discovered in the remnants of a Phased field, it is an incomplete work of romance fiction written by some mysterious author who was writing while idle-mining. The untitled book details a series of adventures in “Erotic Ore” that are enough to make a fedo blush, even though the author failed to write to completion.

1032194.en: Perseverance Expert System This Expert System makes available skills enabling the Capsuleer to fly a Perseverance ice-mining destroyer. The temporary skills provided by this Expert System last for four days. An Expert System is a remote, restricted artificial intelligence providing you with access to certain skills during the active rental period. As it is independent from your clone and your capsule, an active Expert System is not lost on pod death or clone jump. Activating an Expert System Activation of an Expert System is automatic upon redemption of the item by the specific capsuleer intending to use the service. Expert Systems are a product developed by the PKN Interstellar consortium, made available over the HyperNet FTL communications network, and marketed by PKN Interstellar member corporations. An Expert System is a restricted AI based on artificial gelbrain technology. As the Expert System uses neural pathways based on those created by skill training or skill injection, it is compatible with capsule-ship interface and control systems. Real time command and control communication is achieved using dedicated FTL channels on PKN Interstellar's HyperNet.

1032636.en:
Alongside their humanitarian and scientific pursuits, the Sisters of EVE are involved in many diplomatic and cultural endeavors aimed at promoting friendship between the disparate peoples of the cluster. The SOE's Friendship League is an organization dedicated to advancing good relations between all societies independently of the political and diplomatic maneuvering of the empires and factions of New Eden.

Members of the SOE Friendship League are trained to observe high standards of discretion and impartiality in their work, despite the difficulties often posed by diametrically opposed political, economic, and cultural interests across the empires and worlds of the cluster. The Friendship League is occasionally accused of being a front for less altruistic SOE operations but nothing has ever come to light to definitively tarnish its reputation.

The Friendship League is occasionally accused of being a front for less altruistic SOE operations but nothing has ever come to light to definitively tarnish its reputation.

Survive as long as you are able, then destroy it to claim its contents.

1034172.en: The Scriptures, Verse 4, The Scriptures, Chapter I of the Epitoth

1034173.en:
In YC128, in response to rising military conflict, the Amarr Navy commissioned the development of a specialized destroyer. With growing unrest along the borders and rising conflict with the Minmatar, the Navy required a versatile ship for both military engagements and enforcing Imperial authority. 

The result was the Dragoon Navy issue, a vessel that combines the Dragoon's ability to neutralize and disable with improved missile and laser combat capabilities. A true symbol of imperial might that can be swiftly deployed wherever the Empress requires.

1034273.en: Refinement is the path to perfection.

1034276.en:
The election of Alix Moreau in YC128 brought a new focus on research and development to the Gallente Federation. In their role as a science advisor prior to winning the election, Moreau had tagged a number of innovative new patents submitted by CreoDron for further development. As President, they were able to ensure they entered production. 

The Algos was identified as an ideal design to iterate from. Superior weapon systems, web-drone linkages, and a tougher shell were just some of the systemic improvements integrated into the new Navy Issue variant.

1034301.en: Wait for the next wave to earn more rewards or destroy the Fabricator to end the site.

1034302.en: Fabricator coming online, first wave incoming.

1034304.en: Progress to increase the value of the Fabricator’s contents.

1034336.en:
Following the handing over the adminstration of Jita to CONCORD in YC128, the Caldari State needed its people to rally around a new symbol of strength to help reassert its dominance following the loss of such an iconic system.

The iconic Corax was selected for a new and improved military variant that could lead the charge against the Gallente, a symbol that the Caldari could rally behind. With more robust shields, greater flexibility of fitting, and significant improvements to the explosive force of its attacks, the Corax Navy Issue is the very best of classical Caldari excellence.

1034337.en: The strength of the Republic is the wisdom of its tribes.

1034340.en:
YC128 was a prosperous time for the Thukker tribes of the Great Wildlands. In order to protect the influx of wealth from newly discovered Phased Fields, they voted to support an increase in Republic Fleet spending. 

One of the results of that spending was the development of a new Fleet Issue Talwar. Designed with assistance from Thukker engineers, the ship combines the stalwart fortitude of Fleet Issue vessels with the flexibility and efficiency that has made the caravans of the Great Wildlands uncontested within their homespace.

1034659.en: Navy Destroyers Expert System This Expert System makes available skills enabling a capsuleer to fly all four of the new Navy Faction Destroyers that have recently become available to capsuleers, in addition to the four existing ones. This is a promotional Expert System released to celebrate the launch of Military Campaigns. The temporary skills provided by this Expert System last for four days. An Expert System is a remote, restricted artificial intelligence providing you with access to certain skills during the active rental period. As it is independent from your clone and your capsule, an active Expert System is not lost on pod death or clone jump. Activating an Expert System Activation of an Expert System is automatic upon redemption of the item by the specific capsuleer intending to use the service. Expert Systems are a product developed by the PKN Interstellar consortium, made available over the HyperNet FTL communications network, and marketed by PKN Interstellar member corporations. An Expert System is a restricted AI based on artificial gelbrain technology. As the Expert System uses neural pathways based on those created by skill training or skill injection, it is compatible with capsule-ship interface and control systems. Real time command and control communication is achieved using dedicated FTL channels on PKN Interstellar's HyperNet.

1035602.en:
Campaigns mark periods of heightened focus across New Eden. During a campaign, competing interests, resources, and territories come into sharp alignment, giving rise to coordinated efforts with clear goals and limited timeframes.

Each Campaign reflects the current priorities shaping the cluster. Some are driven by war, others by industry, logistics, or control of space — but all represent moments where collective action can tip the balance.

Active Military Campaigns and their associated operations can be reviewed through the AIR Opportunities, where available objectives and points of contribution are surfaced based on current conditions. A broader view of each Campaign—its goals, progress, and significance—can be found in the Theaters of War Dashboard window.

1035604.en:
Capsuleers may only commit to a limited number of objectives simultaneously. 

You may only commit to an objective if it has not yet been completed.

Any capsuleer can contribute to the objectives of any campaign, with the exception of Factional Warfare objectives, which requires enlistment.

1035606.en:
Campaigns have a start and end date. Every few days, while a campaign is active, new objectives will become available. Objectives remain available until they have been completed by the capsuleer community or the campaign's end date has been reached.

Contributors to an objective may earn ISK, loyalty points, or increased standings with the campaign’s faction.

1035608.en: Participation in Military Campaigns does not inherently affect diplomatic standings. Many operations strengthen relationships through service and support, while only direct engagement in Factional Warfare hostilities carries the usual standing risks.

1035721.en: In response to the growing Rogue Drone outbreaks of YC128, CONCORD commissioned a Carrier specific version of the CONCORD Rogue Analysis Beacon (CRAB). WARNING: Linking to this CRAB will render your ship immobile until the powering up phase is completed. Ship Restrictions: linking and activation may only be performed by Carriers.

1035903.en:
Once triggered, this infested fabricator will produce ever deadlier batches of Rogue Drones until it is depleted, destroyed, or becomes unstable.
Hostiles: Rogue Drones
Roles: Enforcer

Restrictions:
Ships: From wave 5, the Fabricator will only remain stable while a combat ship larger than a Corvette is within its proximity.
Modules: Micro Jump Field Generators are blocked while the Fabricator remains operational. Smartbombs, Bombs, and Vorton Projectors deal significantly less damage to Rogue Drone hostiles, the Fabricator, and Nanoswarms.

1035909.en: This drone fabricator has been infested by an out-of-control rogue drone mind. Once it detects a threat, it will produce a defensive swarm that will continue to grow until all threats are eliminated or its systems overload.

1035910.en: The Fabricator is vulnerable. Destroy it now to end the site and claim the contents, or risk the next wave of hostiles to see if you can earn even more. Escalation points will determine the threat level of the upcoming wave. 0-11 points: Minimal threat. Strategic cruisers, non-Marauder battleships, or a group of battlecruisers are recommended at this tier. 12-35 points: Moderate threat. Marauders or multiple other battleships are recommended at this tier. 36-71 points: Severe threat. Multiple Marauders, or battleships supported by a Force Auxiliary ship, are recommended at this tier. 72+ points: Critical threat. Capital ships, or a large number of battleships, are recommended at this tier.

1035911.en:
Each wave survived adds additional items to the Fabricator. Destroy the Fabricator to claim its contents.

From wave 5, a permitted ship must remain within range to maintain stability; the Fabricator will become invulnerable if stability reaches 0.

1035964.en: A champion of humanity-first policies, Senator Lucas Tenzin ran for President in YC128. His grassroots campaign was unique in that it had no outside political party support or major corporate donors. A man of the people, Tenzin promised to fight for a unified Federation where everyone got their share of prosperity.

1035968.en: A radical thinker ready to fight for the freedom to explore any possibility, Governor Alix Moreau ran for President in YC128. They were unchained by the traditional limitations of what has been and ready to embrace what could be.

1035972.en: A savvy business leader not afraid to make the tough decisions, Soraya Roden was the first to step into the Presidential race in YC128. With the backing of her family’s impressive legacy, she championed traditional values along with groundbreaking cooperation with private interests to build an unstoppable Federation.

1036654.en:
The four main empires of New Eden are tenaciously fighting to secure control over regions in low-security space. 
As the empires wage war across the systems, capsuleers who have enlisted with an empire’s militia will shape the future battlefields and earn valuable Loyalty Points.

Head to the frontlines and engage in PVP fights to conquer systems and advance your militia in the war.

In order to capture and hold a star system in your war zone, Capsuleers need to successfully complete two steps.
• Attacking and completing complexes ("plexes") in a system to make the system vulnerable to capture;
• Once the system is vulnerable, attack and destroy ("capture") the system's Infrastructure Hub (also known as an "i-Hub") to capture the system.

1036658.en: The Field Commander is dead. Return to your agent.

1036659.en: Our reinforcements have finally arrived. Loyal Capsuleer, we need your assistance to take down these imperial scumbags. For the Republic!

1036661.en:
Factional Warfare revolves around two conflicts, one between the Amarr and the Minmatar, and the other between the Caldari and the Gallente. The majority of the actions take place in two areas of low-security space, known as "war zones", each of which is contested by two empires.

The Amarr-Minmatar war zone extends into parts of the Devoid, Bleak Lands, Heimatar and Metropolis regions, while the Caldari-Gallente war zone extends into parts of the Black Rise, Citadel, Essence, Verge Vendor, and Placid regions. The high-security systems on the borders of the war zones are often used as staging areas, as capsuleers fighting for the enemy militia cannot enter them without being attacked by friendly NPC faction navy ships, although many player corporations also use systems inside the war zones themselves as home bases. 

The core Factional Warfare gameplay of capturing systems and running missions takes place exclusively within the war zones.

1036664.en: Our reinforcements have finally arrived. Loyal Capsuleer, we need your assistance to take down these republic scumbags. Amarr Victor!

1036665.en: Frontlines are dynamic, ever-shifting war zone systems in which Factional Warfare between empires takes place. These frontlines denote the border regions where rival factions clash, aiming to capture systems and gain control within the game universe. These regions change based on the ongoing conflicts and victories of each faction, marking contested territories. Frontlines are essential as they represent the active battlegrounds and strategic locations where capsuleers engage in capturing complexes, defending systems, and participating in Factional Warfare missions. Capsuleers can get an overview of the frontlines and the war zones in the Factional Warfare Window.

1036669.en: To enlist in Factional Warfare, a capsuleer must be docked in a station containing a militia office. After docking, open the Enlistment Window, select a faction, and follow the opportunity task to complete the enlistment. Alternately, enlistment can be completed via the info panel or militia office in station services.

1036671.en: Enlisting a corporation or alliance in Factional Warfare subjects all capsuleers within said corporation or alliance to FW rules, meaning all members will be marked as potential PVP targets. Capsuleers cannot dock in stations held by opposing factions within a war zone!

1036689.en: Capsuleers can enlist with any faction they have positive standing with. If their corporation doesn’t allow for participation within a desired militia, then they will be required to leave their corporation prior to enlisting.

1036691.en: Corporations and alliances need to have positive standings with a chosen faction prior to enlisting. Both corporations and alliances can only be enlisted by capsuleers holding an appropriate role such as CEO or Director.

1036698.en: In Factional Warfare, capturing complexes is an integral part of determining rewards and shifting the power dynamics between factions. Capsuleers fight to gain or hold control of systems by completing sites and missions. Attacking complexes and cosmic anomaly sites visible in the Probe Scanner Window renders the system vulnerable and eventually exposes the Infrastructure Hub (iHub) to attack. Each system can be in one of three states: Stable, Contested (up to 100%), or Vulnerable. The system’s contest rate represents the tug of war between the attackers and defenders. Defenders can restore systems to a stable or uncontested state by completing complexes.

1036700.en:
To successfully capture a complex, capsuleers must eliminate opposing forces around the designated capture point. After neutralizing the enemies, capsuleers must hold their position within the 30 km capture radius for a specified duration. Capsuleers must remain vigilant and defend the area until the capture point’s timer expires. Remaining time can be confirmed by selecting the capture point.

Capturing a complex directly influences the balance of power between factions in addition to the rewards and overall outcomes within the war zone. Details on LPs and reward distribution can be found in the Loyalty Points section of this guide.

1036702.en:
Loyalty Points (LP) can be earned by completing Factional Warfare activities including capturing complexes and engaging in FW missions. The reward structure for capturing complexes differs based on the system's status (Frontline, Command Operation, or Rearguard) and the complex's size. Capturing complexes in enemy-held systems yields LP rewards dependent on these factors, encouraging capsuleers to coordinate efforts for efficient capture.  

LP rewards provide capsuleers with access to various items, implants, ships, and skillbooks through the respective faction militia corporations' LP stores, influencing their strategic decisions and engagements within Factional Warfare.

Capsuleers can review their current LP balance by accessing their wallet via the Neocom.

1036704.en:
Factional Warfare missions are lucrative endeavors that offer ISK and loyalty points (LP) rewards. Reward amounts are contingent upon two key factors: the mission level which determines difficulty, and the security rating of the system in which the agent is located. Lower security ratings mean increased rewards for daring capsuleers who complete missions in riskier environments. 

Capsuleers benefit from the bonuses imparted by trained skills such as Icon Negotiation and Security Connections which elevate ISK and LP rewards respectively.

1036706.en: Both factions in Factional Warfare can earn advantage points, determining which faction holds the advantage within a given system. The faction with the highest advantage points within a system gains a bonus to Victory Points scored. This bonus is equivalent to the difference between their advantage points and the opposing side's. For example, if the Amarr faction possesses 30% of their potential advantage points, while the Minmatar faction holds 10%, the Amarr faction receives a 20% bonus for any victory points they accrue. Each system has a base advantage score determined by its friendly frontline and command operation systems. Capsuleers can influence this advantage by accomplishing specific objectives within that system, creating a dynamic strategic landscape where achieving objectives significantly helps to determine factional dominance.

1036708.en: Capsuleers aligned with a system’s controlling militia can upgrade their local i-Hub in exchange for reduced station fees. Reductions span five even upgrade tiers with a 10% reduction at Tier I and a 50% reduction at Tier V. To contribute LP, interact with the target i-Hub, open the Systems Upgrade Panel, input an amount, and select Donate LPs.

1036710.en: Check the advantage tracker in the Factional Warfare window to see which faction has the advantage in a selected system.

1037135.en:
This extra-large Entropic Disintegrator is only seen in use on Triglavian capital ships, these massive ships being capable of managing the considerable radiation and enormous gravitational tidal forces the weapon generates. At the energy levels of this ultraheavy weapon system, the tidal forces are so powerful that even the special systems built into battleships are insufficient and only capital ships can deal with the forces involved.

Entropic Disintegrators draw on the tremendous power of the Triglavian singularity-based energy systems to convert exotic matter into a particle stream directed with locally generated entropic force. While powerful, the range of the weapon is limited by the attenuation of entropic forces, which dissipate critically beyond the optimal range. As a result this weapon has no falloff range.

The particle stream generates thermal and explosive reactions on impact, and the entropic forces resolve into a localized gravitational conduit that steadily increases the acceleration on the exotic particles. In effect, the weapon's damage potential increases to a maximum level as long as the particle stream is kept on the same target.

Requires either standard or advanced exotic plasma charge ammo types: Baryon, Meson, Tetryon, Mystic, and Occult.

1037699.en: Zydrine Burn is a potent liquor that is loosely related to the more refined Zydrine Wine, both of these green-hued drinks being produced using rice leaves, a certain portion of the grains, and whatever additives are appropriate to the style of drink. While Zydrine Wine can be an extraordinarily delicate and subtle drink, with the finest generally held to be brewed from the rice plants of Intaki Prime, its more powerful cousin is a somewhat pungent and vividly green brew. Rumors suggest that some versions of Zydrine Burn use as ingredients effluent from Quafe production, liquefied fedo scent glands, or even the notorious protein delicacies in powdered form. Whatever the case, a market for this harshly memorable liquor has sprung up among space workers of all kinds, and few space station bars lack a bottle or two of the stuff. Among planetary populations the brew has a more notorious reputation, popularly considered the tipple of underclasses, criminals, and ruthless capsuleer pirates.

1038067.en:
Imperial War Reserves mining operations are usually organized around combined naval and logistical units typically commanded by a Cardinal Lieutenant.

The Imperial War Reserves were established as a joint effort to build up and maintain a vast reserve of strategically vital materials by the Amarr Ministry of Assessment and the Ministry of War. The corporation is charged with surveying the Amarr Empire for resources and organizing their exploitation by mining operations.

State Military Stockpile resource harvesting operations are considered a high priority and often commanded by a Captain of Engineers.

The State Military Stockpile was created by order of the Caldari State's Chief Executive Panel to seek out and develop militarily important resources within Caldari space. The Caldari Navy and the security forces of the "Big Eight" megacorporations are all able to draw from the deep reserves that are being built up by State Military Stockpile mining operations.

1038239.en: This variant of Raspite ore is especially prized by Amarr engineers for use in large-scale construction projects. Deposits have been held in reserve until such a time as the Empire needed them. Unlike regular Raspite ore, X-Grade is more stable and can be reprocessed without specialized equipment into Tritanium and Pyerite, as well as providing Crystalline Raspite, which is valuable to the Amarr Empire. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

Unlike regular Polycrase ore, X-Grade is more stable and can be reprocessed without specialized equipment into Tritanium and Pyerite, as well as providing Crystalline Polycrase, which is valuable to the Caldari State. This material is compressed and a much more compact form of the original material.

Unlike regular Moissanite ore, X-Grade is more stable and can be reprocessed without specialized equipment into Tritanium and Pyerite, as well as providing Crystalline Moissanite, which is valuable to the Gallente Federation. 1038246.en: Only united in faith can our Empire forge a path to salvation.

1038249.en:
As the dust settled following the Warpath conflict of YC128, many smaller holdings on the fringes of the Amarr Empire fell into chaos. The constant onslaughts of Minmatar Republic strike teams had left these communities exposed to pirate attacks and vulnerable to internal revolt. Local holders sought a means to reimpose control while relying on their own fleets, which unlike the Imperial Navy, were largely made up of small and medium-sized ships. 

They needed a way to improve the operational efficiency of these fleets while also demonstrating the awesome power of the Empire that backs them. Carthum Conglomerate’s solution to this problem was the Salvation. An advanced support carrier with robust command burst functions, it was capable of elevating a group of lesser vessels into an unstoppable armada.

1038250.en: Dishonor one, earn the fury of all.

1038253.en:
Following their betrayal by the Intaki Syndicate in YC128, the Caldari State annexed the entire region of Syndicate. This annexation did not end lawlessness within the region. The CEP declared that for far too long, criminal organizations had abused the semi-legal status of Syndicate for their own means. They charged the Caldari Navy with bringing the rule of law to the region.

To support these efforts, Kaalakiota developed the Simurgh. Its operational superiority was a threat that the criminal forces of Syndicate could not match. A mobile command centre with advanced combat capabilities, its mission was to bring honor to the lawless reaches of space.

1038254.en: Power and resilience can win battles, but speed and intelligence win wars.

1038257.en:
Predicting that superior fleet support was going to be key to future engagements as the Warpath conflict of YC128 began, President Alix Moreau reached out to Duvolle Labs to commission work on a more advanced carrier design.

The team at Duvolle Labs was given unprecedented access to fleet telemetry research data to inform their design choices. They were charged with producing a ship that demonstrated the life-saving impact that advanced operational intel could have on a fleet, a flagship for Moreau’s vision of a more innovative Gallente future.

1038258.en: Everyone fights, everyone makes it home.

1038261.en:
Following the escalating conflict of YC128, the Sebiestor Chief Acassa Midular called upon Core Complexion to create an elevated war platform capable of supporting the rapid response fleets she felt would be essential to Minmatar's success in the next war to come.

Core Complexion took the Nidhoggur's classic design and elevated it with the latest advancements in fleet support technology. Superior command support technologies allow it to unlock greater speed and resilience for its accompanying fleet members. It is the ultimate expression of the Republic's military doctrine, supercharged by the technical brilliance that Core Complexion and the Sebiestor have become synonymous with.

1038323.en:
In these violent and chaotic times, the sanctity of elections is more important than ever. As of YC128, all election officials will now be equipped with special edition Select Freedom Combat Suits developed by Duvolle Industries. These suits will ensure their ability to protect the Gallente people’s most precious asset, their votes.

- Agenbaert Goisin, Head of the Federal Administration.

1038742.en: Gallente Election Expert System This Expert System makes available skills enabling a capsuleer to fly Gallente Tech 1 and Navy frigate-type, destroyer-type and cruiser-type ships along with Gallente-focused supporting skills. This is a promotional Expert System released to celebrate the Federation Day. The temporary skills provided by this Expert System last for four days. An Expert System is a remote, restricted artificial intelligence providing you with access to certain skills during the active rental period. As it is independent from your clone and your capsule, an active Expert System is not lost on pod death or clone jump. Activating an Expert System Activation of an Expert System is automatic upon redemption of the item by the specific capsuleer intending to use the service. Expert Systems are a product developed by the PKN Interstellar consortium, made available over the HyperNet FTL communications network, and marketed by PKN Interstellar member corporations. An Expert System is a restricted AI based on artificial gelbrain technology. As the Expert System uses neural pathways based on those created by skill training or skill injection, it is compatible with capsule-ship interface and control systems. Real time command and control communication is achieved using dedicated FTL channels on PKN Interstellar's HyperNet.

1038779.en:
The algorithmic output of rogue drone intelligence renders them capable of complex calculations at rates far exceeding the limitations of current augmentation technology. They have been observed swarming fleets, stripping ships of vital components, and reconfiguring them mid flight. While the phenomenon is evocative of a metal snake shedding its skin, the potential for scientific application is staggering. 

- Excerpts from Alix Moreau’s research

1039143.en: - Safe from others. Responsible for yourself. Elevated Security protocols prohibit the disabling of ship safety, making violence between capsuleer impossible. Despite this, reckless combat against hostile non-capsuleers may still result in the loss of your ship. These protocols are present within Exordium, a designated training area for capsuleers. The region can be exited via the Yulai gate in the central system of Mandate, or by using the one-time Empire Shipcasters which connect Empire controlled embassy systems to that Empire’s sovereign space.

1039144.en: - Punished, not prevented. Areas of space with active CONCORD enforcement. Illegal aggression will trigger a rapid CONCORD response that destroys the offender, but attacks can still occur before that response arrives. Legal forms of aggression are allowed. Capsuleers flagged as “suspects” may be legally attacked, corporations may declare war on one another, and strikes may come from those who accept CONCORD's deadly retribution.

1039145.en: - Limited law enforcement, real risk. Areas of space with reduced law enforcement. CONCORD forces do not respond to aggression, although sentry guns do guard gates and stations. Capsuleers may attack one another more freely. Piracy, Factional Warfare, and small-scale conflicts are common.

1039147.en: - Claim it, defend it. There is no CONCORD presence and no automatic law enforcement. Capsuleer alliances may claim sovereignty over much of this space, building their own infrastructure. It is up to capsuleers to protect their own space. Unrestricted combat and large-scale wars are a part of daily life.

1039148.en: - Hidden threats, hidden treasures.  Uncharted systems with no security status and no local communication channel. These system contain bountiful resources but are also home to unknown threats. There is no CONCORD or faction protection, and no capsuleer may claim sovereignty over them. Accessible only through unstable wormholes, these systems exist outside the normal bounds of New Eden. Their ever shifting connections mean that wormhole space is not visible on the map.

1039150.en: - Prove fitness through adaptation. A region annexed by the Triglavian Collective with no CONCORD presence and restricted access. 1039326.en: Controlled space with strong CONCORD enforcement. Illegal aggression triggers a rapid CONCORD response that destroys the offender, but attacks can still occur before punishment arrives. War declarations, suspect mechanics, and suicide strikes are part of life here.

1039328.en: No CONCORD presence and no automatic law enforcement. Player alliances claim sovereignty, build infrastructure, and defend territory through force. Bubbles, unrestricted combat, and large-scale wars define daily life.

1039445.en:
I've opened a secure channel that you can use to reach me should you find yourself in need of guidance during your travels in New Eden. 

Simply open the window and ask me a question. I'll return with any insights that I can provide and try not to lead you to another untimely demise.

1039458.en:
A prototype drone developed by CreoDron based on ORE's 'Excavator' mining drone design by incorporating experimental rogue drone technology. The harvesting protocols have been altered to behave much more like a Rogue Drone would when salvaging and recycling materials to be brought back to a rogue drone hive. The result is a far more efficient mining process creating less residue, albeit a slower one resulting in lower mining yields over time. 

Currently this drone is unsuitable for mass production due to a high rejection rate with the rogue drone technology. CreoDron is hoping to improve their understanding of this process from knowledge gained from the Gallente Federation Military Campaign operation 'Rogue Edge'.
